result.topic: Hip fracture outcomes in younger patients
result.setting: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit Database, multicentre

cycle1.result: Patients aged 50-64 had significantly better survival and function than controls aged 75-89 (n=15,461).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Diabetic foot and soft tissue infection outcomes
result.setting: General Surgical Unit, 37 Military Hospital, Accra

cycle1.result: 80 (8.3%) of 966 surgical patients had diabetic soft tissue infection or foot disease; amputation rate 33.3%, mortality 8.8%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Department of Radiology, Jinnah Hospital, Lahore (tertiary care hospital)
result.standard: American College of Radiology (ACR) recommendations for knee MRI image acquisition

cycle1.result: All three planes acquired; sagittal and coronal slice thickness, gap and coverage appropriate in all. FOV appropriate in 66% axial, 5% sagittal, 0% coronal; adequate axial superior coverage in 13 (66%) and inferior coverage in 16 (80%).

result.intervention: Recommendations (decrease FOV in all planes, increase axial anatomical coverage) presented in departmental meetings.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Obstetric unit (Medical School, Newcastle University affiliation); cases from birth register and incident reports
result.standard: Clinical Negligence Scheme for Trusts (CNST) minimum documentation standards for shoulder dystocia

cycle1.result: All areas 100% documented; brachial plexus injury rate 6.7%.

cycle2.result: Documentation declined: only 65% recorded manoeuvres, timing and stage of delivery; 41% recorded staff attending and time of arrival; sequence of manoeuvres and who performed them not routinely recorded. Brachial plexus injury rate 15.8%.

result.other_findings: McRoberts resolved 50% of cases; suprapubic pressure 14%, entry manoeuvres 18%, posterior arm removal 18%. Authors recommend updating the pro forma and restarting skill drills.

result.setting: Paediatric orthopaedic department, Bristol Royal Children's Hospital (tertiary referral centre); clinic and theatre data

cycle1.result: AFC and fracture clinic follow-up bookings fell by 40% and 48%; patient-initiated follow-up rose from 16% to 75% (AFC) and 12% to 35% (FFO); only 17% of AFC and 39% of FFO patients needed radiographs; on-call referrals and trauma cases fell by 50%; all elective operating cancelled.

result.other_findings: A virtual fracture clinic was implemented with an increasing trend in use.

result.setting: Robert Jones and Agnes Hunt Hospital, Oswestry (orthopaedic surgery)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons COVID-19 consent guidance: all patients informed of COVID-19 risk (in-hospital risk 0.45%)

cycle1.result: COVID-19 risk documented on 44% of consent forms (56% not documented). Of forms without it, 34% completed by consultants, 18% fellows, 48% registrars.

result.other_findings: 6% of patients were suspected of COVID post-operatively and tested; 0% contracted COVID.

result.topic: Spinal imaging provision for trauma and tumour
result.setting: 34 public hospitals in Ireland; Emergency Departments and/or orthopaedic registrars questioned

cycle1.result: 67.64% of centres routinely used a spinal clearance protocol; ED cleared the spine in 87%; CT available in hours in 85.3%, out of hours 47%; MRI available in 50%, out of hours in only two centres.

result.other_findings: Questionnaire-based survey of service provision; all centres participated.

result.setting: Hospital ambulatory care in two public hospitals; records reviewed by two rehabilitation doctors
result.standard: Quality indicators developed from systematic reviews, guidelines and expert criteria (history, examination, diagnosis, treatment)

cycle1.result: 76.3% of records did not meet at least 4 of 10 history criteria; 61.6% did not meet at least 3 of 10 examination criteria; 7.7% had no diagnosis. 96.9% of 98 impingement patients did not meet anti-inflammatory/injection timing criteria; 95.8% of 24 rotator cuff tears not proposed for early surgical evaluation; 86.7% of 15 adhesive capsulitis cases lacked timely exercise instructions.

result.other_findings: Up to 15.3% of impingement patients were not offered physiotherapy or exercise within 4 weeks; poor record quality may explain part of the deficit.

result.setting: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit (national, MSK Audit group)

cycle1.result: Male proportion rose from 22.4% to 29.5% (p < 0.0001); admission from own home rose from 63.9% to 73.1% (p < 0.0001); ASA grade 3 rose from 52.9% to 56.4%.

result.other_findings: Registry report of demographics only; audit discontinued in 2008 and recommenced in 2013.

result.setting: Aintree University Hospital, Liverpool (major trauma centre); image intensifier films reviewed on PACS by at least two blinded observers
result.standard: Reduction criteria published by Pettrone et al.

cycle1.result: Malreduction rate 33%.

result.intervention: Education and reflection between 2013 and 2015; then a change in process in ankle fracture management supported by education between 2015 and 2017.
result.other_findings: Interim 2015 re-audit (68 patients, after education alone) showed malreduction rising to 43.8%. Final major complication rate 0.98%; deep infection 0.5%.

result.setting: Department of Paediatric Orthopaedics, Starship Children's Hospital, Auckland

cycle1.result: MRI correlated well for spinal, congenital, intra-articular and growth plate pathology; 3/10 (30%) foreign body assessments incorrect (sensitivity 0.60, specificity 0.80); 3/20 (15%) could not distinguish oedema/effusion from infection (sensitivity 1.00, specificity 0.73); 4/27 soft tissue tumours did not correlate with histology (sensitivity 0.88, specificity 0.63).

result.other_findings: Retrospective diagnostic accuracy review; MRI accurate for tumour margins and extent.

result.setting: Royal College of Radiologists national audit of NHS MRI services
result.standard: RCR standards for MRI provision: request-to-report times and recommended waiting times for cancer staging and routine orthopaedic examinations

cycle1.result: Request-to-report time did not meet the standard for cancer staging but was within target for routine orthopaedic examinations nationally; mean waiting times longer than recommended for both.

result.intervention: Major investment in MRI capacity: new NHS scanners and, in England, outsourcing of routine MRI to an independent provider.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in waiting times for routine orthopaedic examinations; cancer staging examinations deteriorated.

result.other_findings: Control charts showed underperformance due to common cause variation, needing whole-process improvement from request to report.

result.setting: Single orthopaedic unit (University of Glasgow affiliation); emergency and elective consent forms
result.standard: Best practice for informed consent: patients made aware of risk of contracting COVID-19

cycle1.result: COVID-19 included as a risk in 21/51 (41.2%); elective 10/24 (41.7%), emergency 11/27 (40.7%).

result.intervention: Results circulated to all orthopaedic staff as a poster, with 2 weeks of educational awareness.
result.other_findings: Elective practice remained poor. One patient tested positive pre-operatively and one post-operatively.

result.topic: Tibial stress fracture screening and management
result.setting: Outpatient clinic, US Army setting (Martin Army Community Hospital, Fort Benning)
result.standard: Leg Pain Screening and Referral Tool (LPS&RT) algorithm

cycle1.result: 16 tibial stress fractures diagnosed.

result.intervention: Implementation of the Leg Pain Screening and Referral Tool (LPS&RT) algorithm for lower leg pain.

cycle2.result: 30 tibial stress fractures diagnosed (87.5% increase); provider adherence to LPS&RT 93.3% on chart audit.

result.other_findings: Common treatments were activity restriction, oral medication and specialty referral; 46 patients in total.

result.setting: Surgical Oncology Department, Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital, Lahore

cycle1.result: Pre-operative ASIA grade E in 8 (50%); post-operative grade E in 14 (87.5%); 1 (6.25%) wound infection.

result.other_findings: Breast was the commonest primary (62.5%) and lumbar spine most involved (62.5%).

result.setting: NHS orthopaedic department before and after appointment of a podiatric surgeon

cycle1.result: Questionnaires returned by 56/88 (63.6%) podiatric and 60/88 (68.2%) orthopaedic patients. Satisfaction excellent 63.7%, moderate/good 23.6%, poor 12.7% (podiatric) vs excellent 43.4%, moderate 17%, poor 39.6% (orthopaedic).

result.other_findings: Satisfaction survey with labour force implications; patients matched by OPCS code.

result.setting: District General Orthopaedic Unit, The Ayr Hospital; allograft from primary joint arthroplasty for West of Scotland Blood Transfusion Service

cycle1.result: Allograft not collected from 22/70 suitable patients; 68.6% of suitable bone collected. 29% of donated allograft rejected due to poor patient selection.

result.intervention: Procedural changes to improve the efficiency of allograft collection (not detailed).

cycle2.result: 8/70 allografts discarded due to logistical problems; 88.9% of suitable allograft collected (p = 0.001). Rejection for poor selection fell to 9.4% (p = 0.05).

result.other_findings: Medical contraindications excluded 8/80 in cycle 1 and 28/100 in cycle 2.

result.setting: Emergency department, TUH (Tallaght University Hospital), proximal femoral fractures
result.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standard 1: admission to an orthopaedic ward bed within 4 hours of ED attendance

cycle1.result: Average time to ward 8 hrs 29 mins; 26% of patients reached ward (within standard).

result.intervention: 90-minute multidisciplinary simulation training on the hip fracture pathway for ED staff (32 people; in person and via Zoom), February 2021.

cycle2.result: Not reported in abstract (text truncated); authors conclude improved time to ward and compliance with IHFS 1.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Fracture clinic, district general hospital (Croydon Health Services NHS Trust)
result.standard: British Orthopaedic Association: patients referred to fracture clinic reviewed within 72 hours

cycle1.result: Mean waiting time 10.7 days; 6% seen within 72 hours.

result.intervention: Virtual fracture clinic introduced for all ED referrals to fracture clinic.

cycle2.result: All patients reviewed within 72 hours (mean 1.3 days).

result.other_findings: Achieved with no increase in clinic capacity and negligible cost.

result.topic: Blood cross-match ordering for elective surgery
result.setting: Spinal surgery department, Derriford Hospital, Plymouth; elective lumbar spine operations excluding deformity
result.standard: Evidence-based cross-match tariff (cross-match to transfusion ratio and transfusion index)

cycle1.result: 664 cross-match requests, 40 units transfused; C:T ratio 16.6:1.

result.intervention: New evidence-based cross-match tariff agreed between surgeons, anaesthetists and transfusion department.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: VTE prophylaxis in hip and knee surgery
result.setting: Orthopaedic department, St James's University Hospital, Leeds
result.standard: Departmental thromboembolic prophylaxis policy (TED stockings, subcutaneous low-dose heparin, PEP trial inclusion for fractured neck of femur)

cycle1.result: Subcutaneous heparin given in 43% of primary and 14% of revision hip replacements; all knee replacements received heparin but 75% at incorrect dose. Hip fracture: TED stockings 0% to 70%, heparin 0% to 20%, PEP trial inclusion 0% to 20%.

cycle2.result: Statistically significant improvement in subcutaneous heparin and TED stocking use in arthroplasty and in PEP trial inclusion of hip fracture patients.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Level 1 trauma centre (Aristotelian University of Thessaloniki affiliation)

cycle1.result: 19 unplanned reoperations: missed syndesmotic injury 9/19 (47%), non-anatomic reduction 6/19 (31%), fixation failure 4/19 (21%).

result.other_findings: Fixation type, surgeon experience, sex and age were not correlated with failure.

result.topic: Hip fracture emergency department care standards
result.setting: Emergency Department (University of Nottingham affiliation); ED Information System records
result.standard: Standards from national policies and evidence-based literature: early analgesia, accurate clinical assessment, prompt transfer to orthopaedic ward

cycle1.result: Good performance on medical assessment; shortfalls in pressure-care assessment, timely ward transfer and pain relief (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Authors recommend a care bundle for pain relief, pressure care and fast-tracking.

result.setting: Otolaryngology emergency clinic, Medway Maritime Hospital, Gillingham
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England record-keeping guidelines plus legibility, scored with the ANKLe score

cycle1.result: Baseline ANKLe scores for content and legibility (figures not given in abstract); 20 notes from each of 7 SHOs.

result.intervention: Documentation proforma introduced and handwriting advice given.

cycle2.result: Significant increase in content, legibility and overall ANKLe score.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Orthopaedic department, The Royal Berkshire Hospital, Reading
result.standard: NICE VTE prophylaxis guidance (2010): risk assessment before pharmacological prophylaxis and reassessment at 24 hours

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Risk assessment tool attached to drug charts.

cycle2.result: Re-audit showed attaching the tool to drug charts was workable (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Authors recommend removing 24-hour reassessment from NICE guidance as many patients are high risk.

result.topic: National hip fracture audit and standards
result.setting: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit and national quality assurance authority (national)
result.standard: Scottish evidence-based hip fracture guidelines (1997, updated 2002) and national standards

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Descriptive report of national audit, guidelines and standards (A&E care, pre-operative delay, multidisciplinary care, audit participation) as a clinical governance framework.

result.setting: Regional vascular referral unit, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford

cycle1.result: 53 primary operations; 3 primary amputations (6%); 11 patients had complications including one death; 81% symptom-free at median 6 months follow-up.

result.other_findings: Case series; no late vascular complications.

result.setting: Mona Vale Hospital, metropolitan hospital, Northern Sydney Local Health District
result.standard: Agency for Clinical Innovation (ACI) hip fracture minimum standard 2: pain management

cycle1.result: Hourly pain scores on presentation in 82%; nerve blocks used in 35% in ED; 18% reported severe post-operative pain; neuropathic analgesia used in 14%; inappropriate NSAID use in 10%.

result.other_findings: Analgesia prescribing varied; team developing a standardised pain pathway.

result.setting: Osteoarthritis Healthy Weight For Life community programme database

cycle1.result: Greater weight loss was associated with greater improvement in knee pain and function; baseline BMI had no effect.

result.other_findings: Patients with more severe baseline pain improved more for the same weight loss.

result.setting: University Hospital Waterford DDH ultrasound screening programme
result.standard: Recommended scan within 6 weeks (stated in results)

cycle1.result: 255 (26%) referred to orthopaedic clinic; only two infants referred on for persistent DDH; no baby scanned within the recommended 6 weeks later presented with dislocation or needed tertiary referral.

result.other_findings: Female majority of nearly 3:1 among referrals; most treated with harness or bracing.

result.topic: Ankle injury management in the emergency department
result.setting: Accident and emergency department, North Tyneside General Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: Locally developed ankle injury protocol based on published reports

cycle1.result: 205 (80%) had radiography; 20 ligamentous injuries reviewed; 13 inappropriate fracture clinic referrals.

result.intervention: Introduction of an ankle injury management protocol.

cycle2.result: 186 (70%) had radiography; 66 ligamentous injuries reviewed; 9 inappropriate referrals (53% reduction); protocol completed in 87% of notes.

result.other_findings: 550 patients over four months across both phases.

result.setting: Orthopaedic department, Lokmanya Tilak Municipal Medical College and General Hospital, Mumbai (tertiary care)

cycle1.result: Death rate 0.55 per 100 admissions per year; trauma the commonest cause of admission and death.

result.other_findings: Admissions peaked in the monsoon months (June to August).

result.setting: Department of orthopaedic surgery, Kent and Sussex Hospital, Tunbridge Wells; hip hemi-arthroplasty
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines on surgical documentation (33 parameters)

cycle1.result: Handwritten operation reports scored an average of 58.7%.

result.intervention: Procedure-specific computerised operation report proforma for hip hemi-arthroplasty.

cycle2.result: Scores rose significantly (exact figure truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Computerised proformas reduced variability between reports.

result.setting: Danish National Indicator Project (all clinical units treating six diseases)
result.standard: Disease-specific clinical indicators and standards (stroke, hip fracture, schizophrenia, acute GI surgery, heart failure, lung cancer)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Descriptive paper on mandatory national indicator monitoring with monthly feedback and audit processes.

result.setting: District general hospital (Good Hope Hospital NHS Trust, Birmingham); Austin-Moore hemiarthroplasty

cycle1.result: Re-operation rate 1.4% (3/212) with laminar airflow vs 5.8% (134/223 as printed) in non-laminar theatres.

result.other_findings: Described as a second-cycle audit after introduction of water-impervious gowns and drapes, but reports an outcome comparison only.

result.setting: Single liver transplant centre, Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge

cycle1.result: Incident clinical fractures in 15 (3.5%) patients; mean follow-up 61.4 months; median time to fracture 26 months.

result.other_findings: 5.6% had a prior fracture; spine was the commonest site.

result.topic: Vertebral fragility fracture reporting on CT
result.setting: UK-wide RCR audit (with RCP and Royal Osteoporosis Society) of CT radiology reporting
result.standard: RCR audit standards for reporting incidental vertebral fragility fractures on CT

cycle1.result: Audit standards not achieved.

result.intervention: A series of interventions (not detailed in abstract).

cycle2.result: Generalised improvement in compliance, including a 6-percentage point increase in moderate/severe VFFs reported.

result.other_findings: Paper models potential morbidity, mortality and cost benefits and highlights onward referral pathways.

result.setting: Civil Hospital, Karachi (public sector); surgeons across surgical units

cycle1.result: Of 249 responding surgeons: 98% ordered full blood count, 69.5% urea and creatinine, 92% viral markers, 78.7% blood glucose, 71.5% cardiac fitness tests.

result.other_findings: Questionnaire-based; only 4 (1.60%) respondents were orthopaedic. Authors call for standard pre-operative protocols.

result.topic: Microbiology specimen requesting in orthopaedic infection
result.setting: Department of orthopaedic surgery, University Hospital Nijmegen; prospective review by two consultant microbiologists
result.standard: Consultant microbiologist appraisal and existing protocol for prosthetic joint revision

cycle1.result: Requests definitely appropriate in 67% and 85% of episodes (two reviewers); collection, handling and transport definitely appropriate in 56% and 73% of requests; 20/98 (20%) surgical specimens yielded a relevant organism.

result.other_findings: No request was judged unjustified; similar errors found in compliance with the prosthetic joint revision protocol.

result.setting: Orthopaedic practice with internal Fracture Liaison Service, Southeastern United States
result.standard: Recommended FLS guidelines: referral of patients meeting age criteria with first fragility fracture

cycle1.result: 5% FLS referrals.

result.intervention: Alert button in the electronic health record prompting surgeons to refer eligible patients to FLS.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Dual mobility total hip arthroplasty outcomes
result.setting: Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi

cycle1.result: Mean Harris hip score 33.7 pre-op and 75.9 post-op; one dislocation; mean stay 5.91 days.

result.other_findings: Other complications included wound infection, haematoma and NSTEMI.

result.topic: Pre-operative foot pumps for ankle fractures
result.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Trauma Surgery, Mid-Western Regional Hospital, Limerick

cycle1.result: 64 fractures managed with in-cast AV impulse device vs 73 historical controls: median time to surgery, length of stay and surgical site infections all significantly reduced (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Comparative outcome study of a device.

result.topic: Primary total hip arthroplasty quality indicators
result.setting: Servicio de Cirugía Ortopédica y Traumatología, Hospital Dos de Maig, Consorci Sanitari Integral, Barcelona
result.standard: Management indicators (hospital stay, readmission rate) and clinical practice indicators (dislocation rate, infection rate) for non-traumatic primary THA; no target stated

cycle1.result: Median (range) hospital stay 8 (7-78) days

result.other_findings: 160 patients in total across both audits; readmission, dislocation and infection results are not given in the supplied text. Authors conclude the audit cycle improved quality of care.

result.topic: Bone protection prescribing after hip fracture
result.setting: Southern General Hospital, Glasgow; fractured neck of femur patients with fracture liaison specialist nurse recommendations
result.standard: Discharge prescription should include the secondary prevention medication recommended by the fracture liaison specialist nurse

cycle1.result: Recommended secondary prevention medications included in discharge prescriptions in 50.9%

result.intervention: Fluorescent drug kardex stickers detailing simple treatment recommendations

cycle2.result: Recommended medications prescribed on discharge in 84.6%

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics; orthopaedic trauma wards
result.standard: All patients admitted acutely should have a Hospital Anticipatory Care Plan (HACP) completed within 24 hours

cycle1.result: 37/50 (74%) had HACPs completed; 18/37 (49%) completed within 24 hours; median time to completion 45.3 hours (range 0.4-275.1 hours)

result.intervention: Staff teaching sessions and dissemination of infographic posters
result.other_findings: Carried out during the COVID-19 pandemic; cycle 2 completion within 24 hours is not given in the supplied text.

result.setting: Adult orthopaedic ward, Southern General Hospital, Glasgow

cycle1.result: 3159 bed days in total; 255 bed days (8%) blocked by 46 patients (41 emergency, 5 elective); 236 (93%) of blocked days due to emergency admissions

result.other_findings: Most blocked beds were patients awaiting rehabilitation in a young disabled unit or geriatric rehabilitation ward.

result.topic: Clinical pathway variance in joint arthroplasty
result.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Cairns Base Hospital, Queensland
result.standard: Clinical pathways for total hip and total knee arthroplasty (variance from pathway)

cycle1.result: TKR: 11 serious variances in 8/65 patients (12.3%); THR: 9 serious variances in 7/52 patients (13.5%)

result.other_findings: A surprisingly high number of cardiac events among TKR serious variances; serious variances higher than anticipated.

result.setting: Orthopaedic Department, Royal Bolton Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: Operative intervention within 36 h of admission (Best Practice Tariff / National Hip Fracture Database)

cycle1.result: Mean time to theatre 49±39 h

result.intervention: Two additional morning trauma lists, targeted by analysing Best Practice Tariff achievement by day of admission
result.other_findings: Variation by day of the week of admission was used to identify specific deficiencies in local service provision.

result.setting: Section of Orthopaedics, Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi; patients undergoing Austin Moore hemiarthroplasty

cycle1.result: Preoperative magnification 8%±4% (overestimation of implant size by 4.2±2.3mm); postoperative magnification 13%±4%; fixed 15% scaling correctly estimated implant size in 15 (24%) patients

result.other_findings: Digital pelvic radiographs showed variable and inconsistent magnification on repeat examination.

result.setting: Orthopaedic foot and ankle consultants in the Wessex area (Basingstoke and North Hampshire Hospital)

cycle1.result: Management of acute peroneal tendon tears varied greatly among the nine surgeons

result.other_findings: Questionnaire survey of surgeons; a literature-based protocol was proposed.

result.setting: Middlemore Hospital
result.standard: Guideline-recommended admission from ED within four hours and operative management within 48 hours

cycle1.result: 5.6% admitted from ED within four hours; 51% operated within 48 hours

cycle2.result: 14.2% admitted from ED within four hours; 72.5% operated within 48 hours

result.other_findings: Lack of available theatre space accounted for 51% of delays in 2008 and remains a major cause of delayed surgery.

result.setting: San Diego County trauma system (Medical Audit Committee determinations)

cycle1.result: Errors identified in 4% of all trauma admissions; 5.9% of trauma deaths considered preventable or potentially preventable

result.other_findings: Commonest single error was failure to appropriately evaluate the abdomen; critical care errors had the greatest impact on preventable death.

result.topic: Bone bank allograft use and outcomes
result.setting: Bone bank, Department of Orthopaedics, Odense University Hospital

cycle1.result: 423 femoral heads donated to 300 patients; 7% of transplanted patients reoperated for infection (4% in hip revision group); no disease transmission

result.other_findings: Allografts used mainly for revision hip arthroplasty (34%) and fracture surgery (24%); use shifted from spinal fusion to hip revision and fracture surgery over the decade.

result.topic: Hip fracture analgesia, time to surgery and pressure ulcers
result.setting: Department of Orthopedics, Lund University Hospital
result.standard: Aims: optimise preoperative pain relief, reduce time from admission to operation and reduce pressure ulcers; no target stated

cycle1.result: Close to half waited more than 24 hours for operation; 11% operated within 12 hours; 19% had pressure ulcers at discharge

result.intervention: Quality improvements with attention from all staff (details not given)

cycle2.result: 34% waited more than 24 hours; 24% operated within 12 hours; 4.5% had pressure ulcers at discharge

result.other_findings: Interim 1999 measurement: 36% waited more than 24 hours, 18% operated within 12 hours, 8% pressure ulcers. Patients waiting more than 1 hour for pain relief almost halved.

result.setting: Departments of Orthopaedics and Audit, Princess Margaret Hospital, Swindon
result.standard: Trust maximum surgical blood ordering schedule (MSBOS): 6 units of blood for revision hip arthroplasty

cycle1.result: 80.3% received less than 6 units, 12.2% received 6 units and 7.5% received more than 6 units

result.other_findings: 14 patients had postoperative Hb < 9 g/dl and needed additional units; authors suggest 4 units rather than 6 when pre-operative Hb is 13 g/dl or more.

result.topic: Surgical site infection rates in foot and ankle surgery
result.setting: Nine podiatric surgeons Australia-wide (La Trobe University Podiatry Clinic)
result.standard: Australian Council on Health Care Standards (ACHS) infection definitions; literature benchmark of 0.5-6.5%

cycle1.result: Overall infection rate 3.1%; infection resulting in re-admission 0.25% (1339 admissions, 2387 procedures)

result.other_findings: Authors report rates within accepted industry standards.

result.topic: Cost of surgical site infection after hip fracture
result.setting: Irish healthcare system, national hip fracture clinical audit data

cycle1.result: 16 (0.4%) hip fracture patients developed an SSI; total cost €712,898, mean €44,556 per patient

result.setting: Department of Orthopaedics, Derriford Hospital, Plymouth (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 18 (66.7%) questionnaires returned; 38.9% felt in-patient admission was needed for pain; 67% of those 55 and older vs 11% under 55 (P = 0.04)

result.other_findings: Patient age may predict need for admission after day-case arthroscopic sub-acromial decompression.

result.topic: Emergency department fracture management and referral
result.setting: Accident and Emergency Department, Kings College Hospital, London (teaching hospital)
result.standard: Standard of treatment as determined by fracture clinic doctors; upper limb fracture treatment and referral guidelines

cycle1.result: Some error in 69/215 (32.1%) referrals; 51/215 (23.7%) potentially liable to increased morbidity

cycle2.result: Errors in 14/111 (12.6%); 8 patients (7.2%) at risk of increased morbidity

result.other_findings: Overall improvement 19.5% (95% CI 12.3 to 29.7%); 16.5% (95% CI 9.1 to 23.9%) reduction in potentially more significant errors.

result.topic: Transfusion and preoperative anaemia in lower limb arthroplasty
result.setting: Department of Anaesthesia, Fremantle Hospital, Western Australia

cycle1.result: Overall transfusion 16.0%; primary arthroplasty 11%; revision 44.4%; with preoperative Hb ≤120 g/l transfusion 47.7% vs 7.2% above

result.other_findings: Authors suggest investigating and optimising anaemia when preoperative Hb is 120 g/l or less.

result.setting: Waterford Regional Hospital (regional cancer centre)
result.standard: NICE guidance on metastatic spinal cord compression

cycle1.result: 5 (50%) had MRI within 24 hours; 6 (60%) had full MRI scan; 8 (80%) had corticosteroids before MRI; 6 (60%) had radiotherapy within 24 hours; 4 (40%) referred to orthopaedics

result.other_findings: Number unable to walk increased by 20% up to 14 days after confirmation; authors recommend a fast-track referral pathway and education.

result.setting: University of Texas Medical Branch, Galveston; reconstructive spine surgery

cycle1.result: Autologous red cells made up 87% of blood transfused in sequestration patients (80) and 49% in autotransfusion-only patients (302)

result.other_findings: Sequestration plus salvage was more cost effective than salvage alone and reduced reliance on allogeneic products.

result.setting: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit database

cycle1.result: All case-mix variables strongly associated with post-operative mortality; management variables (including time to surgery) added no significant improvement to the model

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Tertiary care university trauma service, University of California, Irvine

cycle1.result: 25% drank more than recommended and 4% were dependent; 92% found computerised screening easy

result.other_findings: AUDIT here is the Alcohol Use Disorder Identification Test, not a clinical audit.

result.setting: Southampton General Hospital
result.standard: Local guidelines: experienced surgeon responsible for initial management; K-wire stabilisation of type IIB and III fractures; crossed K-wires of adequate thickness (1.6 mm)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Guidelines proposed after the previous four-year review

cycle2.result: Guidelines followed in 52 of 71 cases; no reoperations or malunion when followed; in 19 cases not followed more than one-third needed further operation and six had varus deformity

result.other_findings: Failure to follow guidelines led to an unsatisfactory result in 11 patients; a management protocol was devised.

result.topic: Surgical site infection rates in elective orthopaedics
result.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Southmead Hospital, Bristol

cycle1.result: Early wound infection rate 7.85%

cycle2.result: Early wound infection rate 6.82% (no significant difference)

result.other_findings: 44% of infections occurred after discharge; no difference between theatres with and without laminar air flow; 35 of 53 minor infections had no microbiological specimen.

result.setting: Fracture clinics, Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, West Wales General Hospital, Carmarthen

cycle1.result: Overall discharge rate 38%, differing significantly between consultants

result.other_findings: Re-presentation rates were similar between consultants who discharged aggressively and those who re-reviewed; discharge protocols recommended.

result.setting: Podiatry Outpatients, Repatriation General Hospital, Daw Park, South Australia

cycle1.result: Postoperative infection rate 18.9% after excisional nail matrixectomy

result.other_findings: Rate compared with 0.5%-6.5% for clean foot and ankle surgery; authors raise the case for antibiotic prophylaxis.

result.topic: Modifiable risk factor management in hip and knee osteoarthritis
result.setting: NHS Orthopaedic Interface Service (advanced practitioner-led), Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, South West England
result.standard: Best practice guidance (NHS England 2025) on identifying and acting on modifiable risk factors (weight, smoking, diabetes, psychosocial); aim to increase proportion of applicable consultations with documented action on at least one factor; no numeric target stated

cycle1.dates: January to June 2024 (retrospective audit); August to September 2025 (prospective baseline)
cycle1.result: Retrospective audit: action documented in 11% of consultations. Prospective baseline: documented action in 30% (3/10) in August and 39% (7/18) in September 2025 of applicable consultations; baseline median 34.5%

result.intervention: Three PDSA cycles: audit feedback at team meeting, a one-page clinician handout on thresholds and local options placed in clinic rooms, then an EPIC SmartPhrase with standardised text and signposting links

cycle2.result: Documented action in 78% (14/18) of applicable consultations (30 reviewed); overall 54% (49/90) across August 2025 to January 2026; weight advice or signposting for BMI ≥30 rose from 25% (2/8) in August to 86% (12/14) in January

result.other_findings: Smoking advice documented in 6 of 11 smokers, HbA1c documented in 5 of 13 patients with diabetes, and psychosocial factors documented in only 9 consultations; run chart did not meet formal shift or trend rules.

result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedics, Poole General Hospital, University Hospitals Dorset (district general hospital)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England Good Surgical Practice guidance on operation notes (34-parameter checklist)

cycle1.result: 9.52% of notes typed (90.48% handwritten); 10 important parameters recorded in less than 10% of notes; emergency/elective and time never documented

result.intervention: Findings presented at surgical care group and governance meetings; typed operation note templates with editable fields for common procedures provided in each theatre, a dedicated printer near recovery, and templates designed with the IT team

cycle2.result: 66.67% of notes typed (33.33% handwritten); 3 important parameters still recorded in less than 10% of notes; documentation of 12 parameters improved across the three cycles

result.other_findings: Second cycle (14 to 21 February and 1 to 7 March 2021, n=96) had 57.14% typed notes and 4 parameters below 10%; emergency/elective status was never documented in any cycle and estimated blood loss and antibiotic prophylaxis stayed poor. Consultants were slower to adopt typed templates than registrars.

result.setting: Emergency department and orthopaedic service, Beaumont Hospital, Dublin (tertiary referral centre)
result.standard: BOA/BGS Blue Book standard 1: all hip fracture patients admitted to an acute orthopaedic ward within 4 hours (240 minutes) of presentation

cycle1.result: Compliance 17.00%; mean time to ward 417 minutes; mean time to orthopaedic review 83 minutes

result.intervention: Policy change and protocol: on-call orthopaedic SHOs to review suspected hip fractures after the generic hip fracture alert, before definitive ED referral, with precise documentation of alert, referral, review and admission times

cycle2.result: Compliance 21.70%; mean time to ward 333 minutes (84-minute decrease, p=0.126); mean time to orthopaedic review 76 minutes

result.other_findings: Time to orthopaedic referral fell by 58 minutes (p=0.020) and time to X-ray ordering by 44 minutes (p=0.007), but 12.5% of referrals had no X-ray and 25% no bloods. Time of ward arrival was documented in only 70.5% of cases overall.

result.setting: Trauma and elective orthopaedic theatres, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust (City Hospital)
result.standard: Local surgical pause and imaging pause protocols (in the context of NatSSIPs/LocSSIPs); SMART aim of zero never events within 12 months

cycle1.result: 100% implementation of both surgical and imaging pauses, but uncertainty about when to observe imaging pauses

result.intervention: Clarified timing of imaging and surgical pauses, explained at weekly theatre staff meetings, posters displayed beside the WHO checklist, and pause protocols added to new staff induction

cycle2.result: 100% adherence to surgical and imaging pauses maintained; zero never events since 2017

result.other_findings: Second cycle (June to December 2021) also showed 100% implementation. Data were collected over 29 theatre days in total by staff not in the operating team; never events were 1 in 2013/14 and 2 in 2016/17.

result.topic: VTE prophylaxis after foot and ankle surgery
result.setting: 68 UK centres in the multicentre prospective UK Foot and Ankle Thrombo-Embolism Audit (UK-FATE)

cycle1.result: Among patients not receiving chemical thromboprophylaxis, symptomatic VTE rate was 0.30% (11 cases) with no VTE-related mortality; lower-risk group VTE rate 0.05% (1/1819) versus 0.67% (10/1490), P = .002

result.other_findings: VTE rate was highest in non-operatively managed Achilles tendon ruptures (3.12%); regression identified no single factor associated with VTE risk.

result.topic: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Royal Cornwall Hospital, Truro (district general hospital)
result.standard: BOAST guidance for paediatric supracondylar fractures: documented preoperative neurovascular assessment of radial, ulnar, median and anterior interosseous nerves, radial pulse and capillary refill

cycle1.result: 45.8% (11/24) compliant; capillary refill not documented in 11, radial pulse in 7, AIN in 4, and 3 had only 'NVI'

result.intervention: Results presented at audit and governance meetings, departmental emails, audit results included in resident doctor induction, standardised five-parameter assessment and tick-box neurovascular proformas distributed in ED and orthopaedics
result.other_findings: Of the 10 non-compliant cases in cycle 2, 4 had only 'NVI' documented and 3 lacked ED radial pulse documentation before back slab application.

result.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences Hospital, Lucknow (1,200-bed tertiary care institution)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England Good Surgical Practice guidance on operation notes

cycle1.result: 35.8% of parameters documented; emergency/elective, legibility, complications and extra procedures 0%; patient identification 96%, consultant and anaesthetist 90%

result.intervention: Two-month training programme (questionnaire, classes, awareness sessions) plus a mandatory new RCS-based operation note proforma replacing the progress sheet, and an RCS checklist placed in each file

cycle2.result: 90.2% of parameters documented; date/time 91%, emergency/elective 86%, operative findings 76%, complications 60%

result.other_findings: Complications (60%), incision shape (68%) and weight-bearing protocol (74%) remained the lowest items after the intervention.

result.setting: Inpatient medical and surgical wards (excluding acute medical and surgical wards), Southmead Hospital, North Bristol NHS Trust
result.standard: Resuscitation Council UK ReSPECT guidance (17 criteria); target 100% in all criteria

cycle1.result: Best: CPR recommendation signature and demographics 99.3% (293); worst: mental capacity assessment in notes 15.2% (11/72) and reasoning for lack of capacity 48.6% (35/72); values and fears documented 22%

result.other_findings: Medical wards performed significantly better than surgical wards on reasoning for lack of capacity (p < 0.05); legal proxy documentation was very low on all wards. Education and a re-audit in 6–12 months were planned.

result.topic: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
result.setting: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust, large NHS hospital trust
result.standard: BOAST Standard 1: documented radial pulse, capillary refill time and individual radial, median (AIN) and ulnar nerve function in every child with a supracondylar fracture

cycle1.result: Individual nerve function documented in 4 (9.1%); 40 (90.9%) recorded only as 'neurovascularly intact'. Radial pulse documented in 19 (43%), omitted in 25 (57%). CRT documented in 30 (68%), omitted in 14 (32%). Post-cast X-ray in 29 (66%); 12 (27.3%) discharged in a cast without imaging.

result.other_findings: Single cycle; authors recommend an electronic neurovascular proforma and teaching, with a re-audit planned after an electronic checklist is introduced.

result.setting: Luton and Dunstable Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, district general hospital, A&E department
result.standard: Group and save sample rejection rate of 10% or less (SHOT national haemovigilance guidance and local transfusion policy)

cycle1.result: 64/171 (37.4%) G&S samples rejected; 40 of the rejected samples taken in A&E. Causes: documentation errors 43 (67.1%), sample quality 13 (20.3%), labelling/ordering errors 8 (12.5%). 13 patients needed 2 or more repeat samples.

result.intervention: Training and competency sessions for A&E staff, standardised bedside labelling protocol, and a bedside G&S checklist attached to all blood collection trolleys (implemented April 2025).

cycle2.result: 14/84 (16.6%) samples rejected; 11 of 14 from A&E. Causes: documentation errors 8 (57.1%), sample quality 4 (28.6%), labelling/ordering errors 2 (14.3%).

result.other_findings: Direct cost per rejected sample £12 to £80 (average £30). The 10% target was still not met at re-audit and most rejections remained in A&E.

result.topic: Radiographs at cast removal in distal radius fractures
result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, district general hospital (Dorset County Hospital), virtual fracture clinic referrals
result.standard: BOAST distal radius fracture guidance: no radiograph at removal of immobilisation unless there is clinical concern

cycle1.result: 20/46 (43.5%) had a radiograph at cast removal; none had a documented indication (0:20) and none altered management.

result.intervention: Education: results presented and BOAST guidance highlighted at the departmental morbidity and mortality meeting.

cycle2.result: 12/41 (29.3%) had a radiograph at cast removal (p=0.170); indication documented for 7 of 12 (p<0.001) and 2 altered management.

result.other_findings: Cycle 1 was retrospective and cycle 2 prospective. Number of clinic reviews, time in cast and complications did not differ significantly between cycles.

result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic Department, Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham
result.standard: BOA-endorsed orthoconsent.com complication lists: Consent Form 1 complete if all common, less common and rare complications documented

cycle1.result: Fewer than 50% of forms recorded several complications. Fixation (n=35): pain 6 (17%), catheterisation 2 (6%), altered leg length 4 (11%), avascular necrosis 0, hip stiffness 8 (23%), death 7 (20%). Hemiarthroplasty (n=39): altered wound healing 7 (18%), bone damage 22 (56%), death 8 (21%). THR (n=10): prosthesis wear 4 (40%), bone damage 4 (40%), death 2 (20%).

result.intervention: Results presented at departmental audit meeting; teaching sessions on consent practice and posters listing complications to document (June and July 2024).

cycle2.result: Fixation (n=51): pain 17 (33%), avascular necrosis 8 (16%) (p=0.019), death 10 (20%). Hemiarthroplasty (n=25): altered wound healing 10 (40%) (p=0.051), bone damage 21 (84%) (p=0.022). THR (n=18): prosthesis wear 11 (61%), bone damage 10 (56%), death 4 (22%); no THR change significant.

result.other_findings: Some items fell after the intervention, e.g. fixation blood vessel damage 89% to 80% and THR nerve damage 100% to 72%. Patients who signed Consent Form 4 were excluded.

result.setting: Department of Orthopaedics, tertiary care hospital
result.standard: RCSE and BOA operative note documentation standards (18 parameters in four domains)

cycle1.result: Domain compliance: patient identification 72%, intraoperative findings 65%, postoperative plan 58%, surgeon details 70%; overall adherence 68%.

result.intervention: Staff training programme and a new mandatory standardised operative note template, with laminated guideline cards and documentation mentors (July to October 2023).

cycle2.result: Patient identification 95%, intraoperative findings 95%, postoperative plan 90%, surgeon details 97% (all p<0.001); overall adherence 95% (p<0.001).

result.other_findings: Postoperative plan remained the weakest domain with 10% non-compliance at re-audit. Incident reports related to operative documentation fell by 25%.

result.setting: Orthopaedic trauma unit, William Harvey Hospital, district general hospital, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: RCS England Good Surgical Practice (2014) operation note guidance, modified to 17 parameters; target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: 10/17 parameters above 70% compliance; indication for surgery 45%, tourniquet time 20%, antibiotic prophylaxis 71%, closure technique 62%, detailed postoperative instructions 40%, estimated blood loss 7%.

result.intervention: Results presented at clinical governance meeting; surgeons educated on the typed electronic operation note template through live demonstrations, discussions and recorded videos.

cycle2.result: 14/17 parameters above 70%; indication 75%, tourniquet time 45%, antibiotic prophylaxis 89%, closure technique 86%, postoperative instructions 92%, estimated blood loss 8%. 25% of typed notes fully compliant versus none of the handwritten notes.

result.other_findings: DVT prophylaxis plan documentation regressed and blood loss and tourniquet time stayed below 50%. Mean parameters documented did not differ between typed (14.375) and handwritten (14.080) notes (p=0.449).

result.topic: Surgical site infection prevention in hand trauma
result.setting: International multicentre audit of plastic and orthopaedic units operating on hand trauma, via the Reconstructive Surgery Trials Network
result.standard: WHO global guidelines for the prevention of surgical site infection (e.g. antibiotic prophylaxis within 120 minutes before incision, chlorhexidine-alcohol skin preparation, no shaving, no prolonged prophylaxis)

cycle1.dates: End of November 2023 to end of July 2024 (planned)
cycle1.result: not reported (protocol only; minimum 20 consecutive patients per team)

result.other_findings: Published protocol with no results; secondary outcome is a description of current antimicrobial practice in hand trauma surgery.

result.topic: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
result.setting: Trauma unit, district general hospital, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BOAST guidance for supracondylar fractures in children: individual documentation of sensory and motor function of median, AIN, ulnar and radial nerves, radial pulse and capillary refill

cycle1.result: Full neurovascular documentation at A&E review 19 (39.6%), 'NVI' only 21 (43.7%), none 8 (16.7%). After backslab: full 16 (33.3%), none 24 (50%). Postoperatively (n=42): full 16 (38%), 'NVI' 5 (12%), none 21 (50%).

result.intervention: Supracondylar fracture assessment proforma (paper and electronic) and multidisciplinary teaching for emergency department and trauma staff.

cycle2.result: Full neurovascular documentation at A&E review 5 (19.2%), 'NVI' 18 (69.2%), none 3 (11.6%). After backslab: full 9 (34.6%), none 13 (50%). Postoperatively: full 10 (38.5%), 'NVI' 9 (34.6%), none 7 (26.9%).

result.other_findings: Full neurovascular documentation did not improve and fell at first review; gains were mainly in less incomplete 'NVI' entries. Mean time to surgery 1.3 then 0.96 days.

result.topic: Hip fracture Best Practice Tariff compliance
result.setting: Dedicated trauma unit (Bristol Royal Infirmary)
result.standard: Hip fracture Best Practice Tariff 2016 criteria and NHS Enhanced Recovery Partnership Programme criteria (including day one postoperative osteoporosis bloods)

cycle1.dates: November 2015 to May 2016 (whole audit; initial cycle two months)
cycle1.result: Full BPT met in 38.7% (12/31); no patient had FRAX or NHFS recorded; day one osteoporosis bloods requested in 61.3% (19/31); all other ERP parameters 100%.

result.intervention: Written reminders and M&M presentation on NHFS and FRAX, hip fracture scores added to the hospital smartphone app, and a reminder sticker on the operation note to request day one osteoporosis bloods.

cycle2.result: Full BPT met in 63.3% (19/30); NHFS recorded in 66.7% (20/30); day one osteoporosis bloods 90% (27/30).

result.other_findings: Lost BPT income of £8,265 in cycle 1; projected uplift £18,270 per year for intervention costs of £2.00.

result.setting: Orthopaedic department, District Headquarter Hospital, Rawalpindi, tertiary care training hospital
result.standard: RCS Good Surgical Practice (2014) operative note guidance

cycle1.result: Operative diagnosis 80%, peri-operative findings 72%, anaesthetist name 78%, assistant 88%, operating surgeon 90%, operation type 6%, time 62%, complications 10%, closure technique 12%, DVT prophylaxis 0%, time out 0%, postoperative orders 80%, signature 90%.

result.intervention: New dedicated orthopaedic operation note format based on RCS guidance, introduced July 2019 with staff briefing, posters, short videos and notices.

cycle2.result: Operative diagnosis 100%, findings 96%, anaesthetist 92%, assistant 93%, surgeon 99%, operation type, date and time 100%, complications 94%, closure 93%, DVT prophylaxis 90%, time out 100%, postoperative orders 100%, signature 95% (0.001<P<0.005).

result.other_findings: Text reports a total of 500 notes compared although 215 and 235 are given per cycle. Tissue removed or altered was still only 70% after the change.

result.topic: Marker ball positioning for hip arthroplasty templating
result.setting: York District Hospital (York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust), trauma hip arthroplasty for intracapsular neck of femur fractures
result.standard: Departmental audit standard: 100% of pre-operative pelvic radiographs should contain a correctly positioned marker ball (fully visible, inferior to the pubic symphysis, equidistant between the femora at the level of the greater trochanters)

cycle1.result: Marker ball present and fully visible in 96.2% (50/52). Mean difference between templated and implanted head size 2.82 mm (range −5 to +11 mm); 24 (48%) larger, 18 (36%) smaller, 6 (12%) same size.

result.intervention: Results presented at departmental audit meeting; 30-minute teaching session for radiology staff on marker ball placement and educational posters displayed in the radiology department.

cycle2.result: Marker ball present in 93.0% (40/43); present and fully visible in 86.0% (37/43). Mean difference between templated and implanted head size fell to 1.51 mm (range −4 to +7 mm), p = 0.008; 16 (43%) larger, 12 (32%) smaller, 9 (24%) same size.

result.other_findings: Compliance with a fully visible marker ball fell from 96.2% to 86.0% despite improved templating accuracy. In the second cycle 19% of trauma hip arthroplasties were not templated and were excluded.

result.topic: Early weight bearing after ankle fracture fixation
result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Royal Cornwall Hospital, Truro (district general hospital)
result.standard: BOAST 12: early weight bearing after ankle fracture ORIF unless there is a documented concern about fixation stability or soft tissue condition

cycle1.result: 56/112 (50%) advised early weight bearing; 56 (50%) advised delayed weight bearing without documented contraindications.

result.intervention: Findings presented at the audit meeting; BOAST guidelines disseminated by departmental email, educational posters displayed in clinical areas, and agreement on a structured rehabilitation pathway.

cycle2.result: 40/58 (69%) advised early weight bearing; 18 (31%) delayed. Absolute improvement 19% (95% CI 3.9%–34.1%), chi-square 5.591, p = 0.018; NNT 5.3.

result.other_findings: All cases had clearly documented postoperative weight-bearing instructions. Patient-reported and functional outcomes were not assessed.

result.topic: Distal radius fracture time to fixation
result.setting: Tertiary trauma centre, University Hospitals Dorset (Poole)
result.standard: NICE NG38 and BOAST: intra-articular distal radius fractures fixed within 72 hours and extra-articular within 7 days of presentation; target compliance 80%

cycle1.result: Intra-articular fixed within 72 hours 14/42 (33.3%), mean 6.0 ± 3.2 days; extra-articular fixed within 7 days 11/23 (48%; table gives 42%), mean 9.0 ± 4.1 days. Overall mean time to fixation 6.7 ± 3.7 days.

result.intervention: Appointment of a dedicated hand and wrist consultant and a protected Thursday trauma list for upper limb fractures.

cycle2.result: Intra-articular within 72 hours 23/55 (42%); extra-articular within 7 days 12/19 (63%), mean 6.4 ± 3.0 days. Overall mean time to fixation 5.3 ± 2.8 days (p = 0.03).

result.other_findings: The paper reports conflicting p values for compliance change (p = 0.04 and 0.02 in text; p = 0.38 and 0.27 in Table 3). Both standards remained below the 80% target.

result.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, St James's Hospital, Dublin (inpatient orthopaedic operations)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice (2014) operation note headings

cycle1.dates: April to October 2014 (previous audit of handwritten notes)
cycle1.result: Handwritten notes: tourniquet time 0%, elective/emergency 0%, duration 1.6%, operative diagnosis 74.6%, incision 81.7%, prosthesis named 79.6%, serial numbers 30%; 14% of 57 handwritten notes judged illegible.

result.intervention: Typed operation notes on the standard hospital proforma, with an added tourniquet time heading for orthopaedic notes.

cycle2.result: Typed notes: procedure name, incision, closure, tourniquet time and postoperative instructions 100%; elective/emergency 100%; duration 63.2%; operative diagnosis 80.7%; prosthesis named 98.2%; serial numbers 26.9%; 100% legible.

result.other_findings: Prosthesis serial numbers remained poorly documented (26.9% vs 30%). Postoperative instructions were in the correct place only 30.5% of the time.

result.topic: Orthogeriatric review of older trauma patients
result.setting: Orthopaedic department, Countess of Chester Hospital or Wythenshawe Hospital (not specified); patients aged 65 or over with fragility fractures and stay over 72 hours
result.standard: BOAST care of the older or frail orthopaedic trauma patient: comprehensive geriatric assessment by a geriatrician within 72 hours of injury; physiotherapy on postoperative day 1

cycle1.dates: 8 September 2022 to 8 March 2023 (plus non-hip fracture admissions 8 March to 8 May 2023)
cycle1.result: Geriatrician review within 72 hours in 37/70 (52.9%): hip fracture 31/39 (79.5%) vs non-hip fracture 6/31 (19.3%), p<0.001. Mean geriatrician reviews 15 vs 5 (p<0.001).

result.other_findings: Physiotherapy on day 1 after surgery: 30/36 (83%) hip fracture vs 8/16 (50%) non-hip fracture (p>0.05). No significant difference in length of stay or 30-day mortality.

result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics department, University Hospital Crosshouse, NHS Ayrshire and Arran (elective and emergency cases)
result.standard: GMC Good Medical Practice and RCS Good Surgical Practice operative note parameters; target 100%

cycle1.result: Typed 25 (30%); operative diagnosis 53 (65%); findings 60 (73%); closure 73 (89%); signature 78 (95%); prosthesis identification 60/69 (87%); estimated blood loss 5 (6%); time 12%; trauma/elective 27%.

result.intervention: Theatre posters of documentation standards, encouragement to use typed or templated notes, and a mandatory post-operative checklist before leaving recovery.

cycle2.result: Typed 55 (65%, p<0.001); closure 84 (100%, p=0.038); signature 84 (100%, p=0.040); operative diagnosis 62 (74%); findings 68 (81%); prosthesis identification 47/54 (87%); estimated blood loss 2 (2%).

result.other_findings: Time (11%) and trauma/elective status (24%) stayed poor. Re-audit was only a month after the first cycle.

result.setting: Mental Health and Learning Disabilities division, ABUHB (acute psychiatric wards and psychiatric intensive care unit)
result.standard: NMC guidance on verbal orders (follow-up written instruction by a doctor)

cycle1.result: Round 1 survey of 26 nurses and 27 doctors: e.g. 19% of nurses would request haloperidol without a recent ECG and 8% of doctors would prescribe it; 12% of nurses and 12.5% of doctors would request/prescribe lorazepam above BNF maximum doses.

result.intervention: Verbal orders replaced by a digital order form completed by the ward nurse with prompts (medication, physical health, QTc, vital signs) and emailed back by the doctor; publicised via email, junior doctor forums and induction.

cycle2.result: Round 2 survey of 8 nurses and 8 doctors: 100% of nurses familiar with the digital forms; 75% of nurses said the form puts up barriers and 87.5% found it more time consuming; 6 doctors rated the new system safer.

result.other_findings: Main measurement was an opinion survey rather than compliance data. Nurses were less positive than doctors, with 3 of 8 wishing to revert to verbal orders.

result.setting: Orthopaedic inpatients, St James's Hospital, Dublin (standard handwritten operation sheet)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England Good Surgical Practice (2008) operation note guidelines

cycle1.result: Date and time, surgeon, procedure and signature 100%; operative diagnosis 74.6% (in designated place 63.8%); incision 81.7%; closure 98.3%; postoperative instructions 96.3% (41% in wrong place); tourniquet time 0%; prosthesis serial numbers 30%; elective/emergency 0%.

result.other_findings: 85.7% of notes were written by the registrar although consultants performed 71.4% of procedures. Authors planned re-audit after introduction of electronic notes.

result.setting: Orthopaedic department, Ribat University Hospital, Khartoum (tertiary care hospital)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England Good Surgical Practice (2014) operation note criteria, with added orthopaedic items (19 items)

cycle1.result: Good compliance for date (86%), diagnosis (85%), operating surgeon (90%), assistants (86%), procedure (98%), post-operative instructions (98%), signature (75%). Poor: time 37%, anaesthetist 41%, incision 41%, prosthesis details 15%, drain 7%.

result.intervention: Memory aid placed in the operating theatre for two months (May–June 2019) highlighting poorly documented items.

cycle2.result: Time 56%, anaesthetist 46%, incision 59%, prosthesis size and details 34%, drain documented in correct place 15%.

result.other_findings: Notes written by the operating surgeon fell from 20% to 14%. Some components remained poorly completed.

result.topic: Physical health checks in substance misuse services
result.setting: Gwent Specialist Substance Misuse Services (GSSMS), North Team

cycle1.result: Physical examination by GSSMS 60/121; ECG 37/121 (31%); blood-borne virus screen in last 6 months 62/121. Abnormality found in 77% of those examined, most commonly hypertension (9) and abdominal tenderness (9).

result.other_findings: Physical examination rates were described as having risen from 0% to 50% compared with previous practice, and the team previously had no ECG machine. A front-of-notes checklist and yearly re-audit were recommended.

result.topic: Mental Health Act medical recommendation quality
result.setting: South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust, Wakefield area (section 2 and 3 medical recommendations)
result.standard: Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice and statutory forms; 100% compliance expected on 8 standards

cycle1.dates: Recommendations from January 2025 onwards; data collected August to September 2025
cycle1.result: 100% for stating mental disorder, describing symptoms, nature or degree, own health reasons and why informal admission inappropriate; own safety reasons 62%; protection of others 81%; why community treatment not available 90%.

result.other_findings: Sample contained only section 3 and single recommendations. Feedback to doctors and an agreed template were proposed, with re-audit planned in three to six months.

result.topic: Admission clerking and physical health checks in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Battersea Bridge House Hospital, 22-bed acute mental health facility (three wards)
result.standard: Local and NHS trust admission protocol: clerking, mental state examination, physical examination, ECG and routine bloods all completed within 72 hours of admission

cycle1.result: All five criteria completed within 72 hours in 27 patients (62.8%); delayed in 14 (33.6%); 2 (4.7%) refused blood tests.

result.intervention: Active physical health handover to the physical health nurse and junior doctors, with emphasis on patient rapport.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance for physical health checks increased from 62.4% to 96.6% after intervention; reported 1.76-fold increase in timely protocol completion, 1.39-fold reduction in delays and 4-fold drop in patient refusal.

result.other_findings: Delays were mainly due to patient agitation, refusal of bloods or ECG, delayed consent and slow laboratory results; reasons were not documented for 2 patients.

result.setting: Specialist HPB multidisciplinary team, University Hospitals Plymouth; patients referred locally from Plymouth Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: NHS standard: first definitive treatment within 62 days of urgent GP referral

cycle1.result: Median time from first presentation to surgery 0 days (range 189); to first chemotherapy 81 days (range 231); to palliative decision 23 days (range 77). Delays: presentation to SMDT referral via GP median 9 days (range 17); referral to first discussion median 9 (range 53); first discussion to first biopsy median 31 (range 165).

result.other_findings: Median of 2 SMDT discussions per patient (range 7). Preliminary data suggest patients wait longer than NHS guidelines; proportion meeting the 62-day target not reported.

result.setting: Medical wards, CDU and UTC, Friarage Hospital, Northallerton; patients over 65 referred to psychiatric liaison

cycle1.result: 22/38 (58%) had delirium documented during admission; of these 13 (59%) had delirium documented in the discharge letter and 9 (41%) had no mention. By ward: Romanby 2/8 (25%), Ainderby 5/6 (83%), Rutson 0/1, CDU/UTC 6/7 (86%).

result.intervention: Planned: teaching for Foundation Year doctors, ward posters from 08/01/25, and encouraging documentation of previous delirium at clerking.
result.other_findings: First cycle only; re-audit planned for March 2025 using February 2025 discharges.

result.topic: ADHD in early intervention for psychosis
result.setting: Early intervention for psychosis service, Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 5/174 (2.9%) adult patients had a known ADHD diagnosis; 4 more referred for ADHD assessment.

result.intervention: Development of an integrated clinical pathway and NICE-concordant care plan for ADHD in the EIP service, with the adult ADHD service.
result.other_findings: A previous 2022 audit found 3.6% prevalence of diagnosed ADHD. Adult ADHD assessment waiting list is 18 months to 2 years; 3/5 patients had a history of substance use.

result.setting: Delfryn House, high dependency inpatient mental health rehabilitation unit
result.standard: Safe prescription and administration of psychotropic medication; Mental Health Act 1983 treatment certificate compliance

cycle1.result: Phase I: prescription errors 19%; administration errors 34%; Mental Health Act documentation compliance 77%; patient knowledge of medication 15%.

result.intervention: Medication management committee with PDSA cycles: inpatient depot clinics, daily 10-point nurse self-audit, medication compliance in handovers, monthly prescription, administration and pharmacist audits, patient leaflets and pharmacist sessions, staff policy awareness and monthly MHA certificate audits.

cycle2.result: Phase II: prescription errors 3%; administration errors 11%; Mental Health Act documentation compliance 98%; patient knowledge 32%.

result.other_findings: Acknowledgement of drug interactions and adverse events raised by pharmacists did not improve significantly. Depot errors fell then rose again and the weekly depot clinic was abandoned.

result.topic: Secondary prevention and carotid imaging after minor stroke
result.setting: Stroke ward E58, Sunderland Royal Hospital (South Tyneside and Sunderland Foundation Trust); patients with NIHSS score below 5
result.standard: National Clinical Guideline for Stroke: carotid Doppler ultrasound for TIA or minor anterior stroke (NIHSS below 5), with correct antiplatelet and statin therapy and lifestyle advice

cycle1.result: Cholesterol-lowering therapy about 3 percentage points lower and lifestyle advice 2 points lower than cycle 2; blood pressure commented on in only 3% of cases.

cycle2.result: Correct antiplatelet therapy 100%; cholesterol-lowering therapy 25/30 (83.3%); diet and lifestyle advice 4/30 (13.3%); blood pressure commented on 18/30 (60%). Only one patient had vascular surgery and not within seven days.

result.other_findings: Ultrasound only available Monday to Friday 9:00–17:00, so weekend admissions cannot have a scan within 24 hours. Recommended adding carotid Doppler within 24 hours to ward induction.

result.setting: Hepatobiliary department, University Hospital Southampton (elective and emergency splenectomy)
result.standard: National and local guidelines on post-splenectomy vaccination (Pneumovax, MenACWY, Bexsero, influenza) and antibiotic prophylaxis; 100% compliance expected

cycle1.result: Did not receive: Pneumovax 21%, Bexsero 22%, ACWY 23%, second Bexsero 34%, yearly influenza 30%; 21% received no vaccinations; 1% no prophylactic antibiotics on discharge; 39% of discharge paperwork lacked vaccination timing documentation.

result.other_findings: A follow-up documentation proforma was created and clear discharge documentation recommended, with re-audit planned for 2023. No patients were readmitted with overwhelming infection.

result.setting: 13 rheumatology outpatient departments in Greater Manchester and Lancashire (North West regional audit)
result.standard: NICE, EULAR, BSR and MHRA gout guidelines

cycle1.result: Treat-to-target levels agreed in 49 (57%); cardiovascular risk tool used in 3 (3%); no patient with major cardiovascular disease on febuxostat; 16 (17%) no planned follow-up; 18 (78%) new patients appropriately referred; 15 (75%) started on first-line ULT; 11 (79%) allopurinol started at low dose; 10 (67%) given colchicine prophylaxis.

result.other_findings: None of 12 patients with hypertension without heart failure on diuretics received advice to reduce or stop them. Clinic data would have allowed cardiovascular risk calculation in 13 (14%).

result.topic: Vitamin D supplementation in older adults
result.setting: Acute medical patients over 65, Wexford General Hospital
result.standard: Department of Health guidance 2020: adults over 65 should take 15 micrograms vitamin D daily

cycle1.result: 48% not on any vitamin D supplement; 64% insufficient (32% deficient), of whom 44% not on vitamin D; vitamin D result mentioned in 18% of discharge letters.

result.other_findings: 30% presented with fractures, and 10% of those were not on vitamin D.

result.topic: Excipients in unlicensed paediatric liquid medicines
result.setting: Tertiary paediatric hospital pharmacy
result.standard: European Medicines Agency guidelines on excipients; acceptable daily intake (ADI) of each excipient, assessed with the local New Products Assessment Form

cycle1.result: 14 unlicensed liquid preparations from one manufacturer reviewed: 4/14 (29%) suitable for all age groups; 4/14 (29%) exceeded the ADI for an excipient in neonates (suitable for all other ages); 5/14 (36%) changed to a more appropriate alternative.

result.other_findings: Of the four exceeding ADI in neonates, two were not routinely prescribed in neonates; one preparation was removed from the market. Manufacturer was asked to reformulate where ADI was exceeded.

result.topic: Time to diagnosis in axial spondyloarthritis
result.setting: 54 UK rheumatology departments; national online survey-based audit run by the National Axial Spondyloarthritis Society
result.standard: NASS 'Act on Axial SpA' campaign target to reduce time to diagnosis to 12 months

cycle1.dates: Survey launched October 2022; patients diagnosed January 2021 to September 2024
cycle1.result: Mean total time to diagnosis 8 years (SD 8.91); median 4.7 years (IQR 9.25).

result.other_findings: Preliminary data suggest a trend towards shorter time to diagnosis, apparently from quicker primary care referral and faster rheumatology assessment. Men had shorter time to diagnosis, but improvement between 2021 and 2024 was greater for women.

result.setting: Tertiary centre; paediatric patients (>30 days and <17 years) receiving intravenous vancomycin
result.standard: Local trust guideline (2018) for intravenous vancomycin in children

cycle1.result: Correct frequency 75.9%; correct first dose 58.6%; concentrations taken at correct time 89.7%; therapeutic first concentration 24.1% (70.4% under range); second concentration in range 61.9%.

result.intervention: Significant changes to electronic prescription and concentration report templates; guideline recirculated to all paediatric prescribers.

cycle2.result: Correct frequency 92.6%; correct first dose 71.4%; concentrations taken at correct time 96.2%; therapeutic first concentration 19.2% (65.4% under range); second concentration in range 57.9%.

result.other_findings: Non-compliance with prescribing was due to prescribers following BNFC rather than trust guidance. Therapeutic concentrations were still not achieved in over 80% of patients, prompting a call to re-evaluate the dosing guideline.

result.setting: Community Adult Mental Health Services, Taylor Centre, Southend; outpatient clinics
result.standard: NICE CG178 1.5.8 (offer supported employment to people with psychosis or schizophrenia who wish to work) and NG181 1.8.9 (facilitate alternative educational or occupational activities)

cycle1.result: Supported employment offered to 35% of the non-working sample; alternative educational or occupational options offered to 26%.

cycle2.result: Employment status documented in 97%; supported employment offered to 38%; alternative educational or employment options offered to 47%.

result.other_findings: 64% of those offered supported employment declined; 78% were not actively seeking work. Only 33% were followed up, and employment was most often discussed at follow-up appointments (87%).

result.topic: Physical health monitoring in early intervention in psychosis
result.setting: Mid and North Early Intervention in Psychosis service, Hampshire and Isle of Wight NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Physical health monitoring and intervention standards of the National Audit of Schizophrenia 2021 and National Clinical Audit of Psychosis 2022 (75% standard); Lester UK tool; local target 80% after interventions

cycle1.result: 54/118 identified as high risk. Monitoring of smoking, alcohol, illicit substances, BMI, blood pressure, lipids and glucose exceeded the 75% standard. Acceptance of interventions was low: smoking cessation 18%, alcohol interventions 33%, illicit substance advice 6%, HbA1c-related recommendations 8%, lipid lifestyle advice 10%; 100% accepted interventions for high BMI and hypertension.

result.other_findings: Standards for monitoring were met but not for interventions; an action plan (patient education and team training on Lester tool interventions) was recommended before the next cycle, with re-audit every 6 months.

result.setting: Acute hospitals in the UK and Ireland; national trainee collaborative (protocol)
result.standard: WHO Mastitis Guidelines 2000; GAIN Guidelines 2008; ABM Clinical Protocol #4: Mastitis 2014; NICE Clinical Knowledge Summaries: Mastitis and Breast Abscess

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Protocol only: planned three phases (national practice survey, prospective audit, prospective re-audit) collecting antibiotic prescribing, operative versus radiological management, time to ultrasound, inpatient versus outpatient treatment, length of stay and breast surgeon follow-up.

result.topic: Serious infections in early inflammatory arthritis
result.setting: National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit (NEIAA), England; observational cohort with NHS Digital linkage

cycle1.result: 519 serious infection admissions and 17 deaths; incidence per 100 person-years 3.19 (95% CI 2.93-3.48) for admissions and 0.10 (0.06-0.16) for deaths. MTX-based strategies HR 0.75 and csDMARD combination HR 0.70 versus no DMARD; each 1-unit DAS28 rise HR 1.08.

result.other_findings: Age, smoking, comorbidity, disease activity, symptom burden and disability predicted admissions; corticosteroid association was not significant in fully adjusted models.

result.setting: Old age psychiatry inpatient ward
result.standard: Patients detained under the MHA should have Section 17 leave facilitated as granted by the responsible clinician, with documented discussion and updated risk assessment before leave

cycle1.result: Section 17 form not uploaded to RIO in 25% (7); no documented discussion of leave in 46.42% (13); no evidence whether leave facilitated in 25% (7); 42% (6) of those granted leave off grounds had it facilitated; no updated risk assessment before leave in 83% (5/6).

result.other_findings: All facilitated leave was escorted as specified. Recommendations: discuss leave at ward rounds and one-to-one sessions, document risk assessment and use the pre-leave form; re-audit after 12 months.

result.topic: Tocilizumab approval criteria in giant cell arteritis
result.setting: Bristol and Bath regional GCA multidisciplinary team meeting
result.standard: NHS England criteria (Blueteq) for tocilizumab in refractory or relapsing GCA; MDT discussion required before starting

cycle1.result: 38 cases discussed, 31 approved for tocilizumab; 100% of approved cases met criteria for refractory (n = 11) or relapsing (n = 20) disease.

result.other_findings: High glucocorticoid toxicity burden; 77.4% cranial GCA, 48.4% large vessel, 25.8% ischaemic visual loss. Patients with ocular involvement were referred earlier (478.2 vs 648.1 days).

result.topic: Vitamin D testing in paediatric haematology and oncology
result.setting: Paediatric haematology/oncology; new diagnoses of malignant disease
result.standard: Trust guideline for vitamin D deficiency: 100% tested at diagnosis; 100% of results acted on; 100% given appropriate dose

cycle1.result: 56% tested for vitamin D during admission; 35% of oncology and 83% of haematology patients tested. 6% of haematology and 5% of oncology patients with sufficient levels received treatment not indicated; the 5% of oncology patients with insufficient levels were not treated. Standards not met.

result.other_findings: Recommendations: follow the revised trust guideline, pharmacists to check vitamin D for all new admissions, and build a default test into the new prescribing system.

result.topic: Bone health assessment after inpatient falls
result.setting: Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (Kings Mill Hospital); inpatients who fell, identified via DATIX
result.standard: National Osteoporosis Guideline Group: FRAX to estimate 10-year fracture risk and guide bone protection; NICE CG161; Trust post-fall assessment guidance

cycle1.result: Falls assessment sheet completed in over 80%; FRAX calculated in only 33.3%. Of those with FRAX, 60% intermediate, 20% high and 10% very high risk; only 50% of high-risk patients received oral bisphosphonates. Retrospective FRAX in those not assessed showed 60% very high risk.

result.other_findings: Calcium and vitamin D checks were done more often than FRAX but still below optimal; renal impairment limited bisphosphonate eligibility. Falls Alert Stickers with checkboxes and QR code, a revised post-falls proforma with a bone health section, and clinician education were introduced.

result.setting: Outpatient department, Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore
result.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition) for long-acting injectable antipsychotics

cycle1.result: All patients on fluphenazine decanoate with a concurrent second antipsychotic (100% polypharmacy); 78% informed of side effects; none had post-injection observation; no test doses given; no baseline ECG or physical health assessment; fluphenazine used in rapid tranquillisation.

result.other_findings: Recommendations included staff training on Maudsley guidance, test dose protocols, mandatory baseline ECG, revised rapid tranquillisation protocol and regular re-audit.

result.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit
result.standard: Trust guideline: Labinic probiotic for babies <32 weeks and/or <1.5 kg at birth, at correct dose, given with first feed or within 12 hours of birth

cycle1.result: 76/76 (100%) eligible babies prescribed and given Labinic; 76/76 (100%) correct dose; only 17/76 (22%) received it within the first 12 hours.
