result.other_findings: Poor compliance attributed to lack of awareness of guidance.

result.setting: Acute psychiatric inpatient service, Mount Carmel Hospital
result.standard: American Society of Addiction Medicine Clinical Practice Guideline for Alcohol Withdrawal Management

cycle1.result: Alcohol use documented in 132 (70%); of 36 regular drinkers, duration of dependency and time of last drink documented in 8.3%, CIWA-A in 66.7%, previous withdrawal delirium, seizures and autonomic activation 0%; urine toxicology 63.9%, LFTs 52.8%, INR 27.8%, ethanol 36.11%.

result.intervention: Recommended a locally adapted alcohol assessment guideline and re-audit.
result.other_findings: Comorbidities (100%), other substance use (100%) and suicide risk (91.7%) were well documented.

result.setting: Four inpatient paediatric wards using electronic prescribing
result.standard: Legal prescribing requirements (Medicines Act 1968), trust Medicines Management Policy; ten standards based on RCP Generic Medical Record Keeping Standards 2017

cycle1.result: 100% compliance for most demographics and prescription items and all fluid standards; allergy status 95% (severity 93%); weight 73%; antimicrobial indication 81% and duration 46%.

result.intervention: Results presented locally and emailed to staff; recommended e-prescribing training and compulsory weight and allergy entry.
result.other_findings: Electronic prescribing improved adherence compared with previous paper chart audits.

result.setting: Paediatric wards and prescribing tests for new paediatric doctors
result.standard: Legally and clinically correct CD TTO prescriptions on the CD TTO template

cycle1.result: 67% of prescribers failed the CD TTO test question, mostly dose and frequency errors; 50% of live CD TTOs (two audited) not on the template; average 40 minutes to triage one CD TTO.

result.intervention: Recommended awareness of template location, teaching sessions, adding template to the back of the Child Health chart, and a pocket guide.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: GP referrals to community mental health team
result.setting: Balbriggan Community Mental Health Team, Dublin

cycle1.result: 60 accepted (54.5%) and 50 rejected (45.5%); 16% not receiving psychotherapy, 11% suboptimal medication doses, 9% declined for non-initiation of medication.

result.intervention: Local referral guidelines on appropriate referral, psychotherapy initiation and medication management shared with GPs on 19 August 2024.

cycle2.result: 71 accepted (92.2%) and 6 rejected (7.8%); 14% still not receiving psychotherapy.

result.other_findings: Rejected ADHD/ASD assessment referrals rose from 21% to 33%.

result.setting: Male and female acute inpatient units, Zinnia Centre, Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health Foundation Trust
result.standard: BSMHFT admissions policy: pre-referral MDT assessment including senior doctor, rationale and plan of care, risk assessment, section status and bed type

cycle1.result: Assessed by full MHA team 49%, senior psychiatric doctor 34%; up-to-date assessment summary 67%; risk assessment 82%; detailed plan of care 35%; capacity assessment with outcome 13%; bed type considered 13%.

result.other_findings: Plan of care and bed type were rarely addressed.

result.topic: Pharmacological management of borderline personality disorder
result.setting: not reported
result.standard: NICE CG78 Borderline personality disorder (eight prescribing, indication and review standards)

cycle1.result: >90% compliance for review of effectiveness and tolerability and no medium/long-term antipsychotic use; <79% for single-drug prescribing, agreeing target symptoms and duration, and written information; 80-89% for sedatives <1 week and discontinuing ineffective treatment.

result.intervention: Planned: key cards for clinicians, written information for patients, re-audit in 6 months.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Acute male inpatient psychiatric ward, South London
result.standard: 100% of patients meeting 'Patient-Centred Prescribing' criteria (ward round discussion, written leaflets, informal discussion groups) by March 2021

cycle1.result: 30% of clients answered passively to 'Do you feel involved in your care?' in baseline patient experience data.

result.intervention: Weekly MDT-led medication discussion groups from week 1; rolling rota and posters from week 6; patient information leaflets offered 1:1 from week 14.

cycle2.result: Median 92.86% of patients fulfilled Patient-Centred Prescribing criteria.

result.other_findings: 79.3% of questionnaire responders wanted further sessions and 88% of Blob Tree responses suggested a positive emotional response; COVID-19 affected momentum.

result.setting: Liaison psychiatry, University Hospital of Limerick
result.standard: Checklist of required data items derived from the 2025 redesigned referral form

cycle1.result: Old form showed inconsistent completion of GP details, referring doctor and contact details; cognitive screening items rarely recorded; previous diagnoses, medication and risk often missing.

cycle2.result: Redesigned form improved completeness across nearly all domains, with full compliance for patient identifiers and referrer details; risk documentation among the largest improvements.

result.other_findings: No numerical completion rates given; challenges remain with usability of referral information.

result.topic: Mild cognitive impairment diagnosis and management
result.setting: Eight older adult community mental health teams, Lincolnshire Partnership Foundation Trust
result.standard: Older adult memory assessment and management service protocol, Manchester Consensus recommendations, NICE NG16 and NG97

cycle1.result: Standardised cognitive tool 100%; functional impairment 78%; depression screening 70%; medication review 10%; lifestyle advice 42%; cardiovascular advice in GP letter 21%; no antidementia prescribing; follow-up review 69%.

result.intervention: Findings shared across teams and MAMS how-to guide created with assessment checklist and patient/carer information pack; re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: 21% diagnosis changed to dementia at follow-up; 16% offered research participation; 19% not followed up with no reason recorded.

result.setting: Southampton General Hospital, Major Trauma Centre

cycle1.result: Mean time to surgery 80 hours; surgical delays in 57.4%; 30-day mortality 4.7%.

result.intervention: Additional theatre allocation, dedicated hip fracture team, multidisciplinary medical evaluation, optimised imaging, management of pre-existing conditions and standardised anticoagulation reversal.

cycle2.result: Mean time to surgery 55 hours; delayed surgeries 63.9%; 30-day mortality 3.0% (national average 5.9%).

result.other_findings: Delays correlated with longer length of stay in both cycles; six deaths in each of the non-delayed (5.7%) and delayed (3.2%) groups post-intervention.

result.setting: 14 patch test centres in the UK and Ireland (British Society for Cutaneous Allergy)

cycle1.result: 156/3367 (4.6%) had at least one positive baseline rubber reaction; carba mix 2.6%, thiuram mix 1.9%; 69/612 extended rubber series tests positive.

result.other_findings: Some additives not in the baseline or rubber series were positive, suggesting underdetection; BSCA will update its rubber series.

result.setting: Birmingham Skin Centre, Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust
result.standard: 2018 British Association of Dermatologists and British Photodermatology Group PDT guidelines; clearance ≥ 75%

cycle1.result: All treatments licensed; 3-month clearance 52% (11/21 with recorded assessment); 12-month clearance 50% (2/4); no individual pain plans; patient satisfaction recorded in 9% (3/32).

result.intervention: Planned standardised digital referral and documentation system.
result.other_findings: Ambulatory vs standard PDT was not recorded; clinicians wanted PDT teaching and online referrals.

result.setting: Eastbourne Department of Psychiatry, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: SPFT guidelines: 100% with date of initiation and indication recorded, consultant support for continuation, and indication, duration, dose and reducing regimen communicated to GP

cycle1.result: 12.5% regular and 15% PRN benzodiazepines on discharge; of these 80% on long-term treatment and 40% had documented indication and reducing regimen.

result.intervention: Teaching on benzodiazepine prescribing for residents at the start of rotation.

cycle2.result: 9% regular and 0% PRN on discharge; 100% consultant supported with indication, duration and reducing regimen documented.

result.other_findings: Re-audit covered only the male ward, limiting generalisability.

result.setting: South West community Perinatal Mental Health Team
result.standard: NICE guidance: routine enquiry about alcohol use in all pregnant women

cycle1.result: Alcohol use explored in 16/35 (45.7%); not explored in 19 (54.3%).

result.intervention: Findings presented at MDT meeting in September 2025 with agreed routine enquiry and documentation using the AUDIT screening tool where appropriate.

cycle2.result: Alcohol use explored in 17/22 (77.3%); not explored in 5 (22.7%).

result.other_findings: An information leaflet on alcohol in pregnancy and breastfeeding was then introduced.

result.setting: General adult community mental health team, Pennine Care Foundation Trust
result.standard: PCFT HDAT initiation and monitoring guidelines across 8 domains; 100% compliance required

cycle1.result: Average compliance 60.6% across all domains; HDAT form completion 0%; consultant initiation 83%; 2.13% of patients on HDAT.

result.intervention: Local HDAT register created with biannual review by resident doctors.

cycle2.result: Average compliance 77%; compliance rose in 5 domains with 100% in consent, annual review, side effects and GP notification; HDAT form 67%; consultant initiation 83%; 2.06% of patients on HDAT.

result.other_findings: Blood tests and ECG monitoring fell (25.4% and 75.1% relative reductions); HDAT was discontinued in 50% of the baseline cohort after register review.

result.setting: Acute adult, PICU and specialist inpatient units across 4 boroughs (Warrington, Halton, Knowsley, Wigan), Mersey Care Foundation Trust
result.standard: POMH-UK Quality Improvement Programme 14c: 5 standards (12 criteria) and 3 targets for alcohol detoxification

cycle1.result: Four of twelve criteria (liver function and glucose tests, prescription for acute withdrawal, parenteral thiamine) and all three targets (breath test at admission, relapse prevention, referral to specialist alcohol services) had less than 60% compliance and were below the national sample.

result.intervention: Recommended trust-wide guidance, a junior doctor admission checklist, induction teaching and routine admission bloods.
result.other_findings: Second re-audit in the POMH-UK cycle, compared with 2016; practice varied across the trust.

result.setting: Memory clinic, Prospect Park Hospital
result.standard: NICE recommended dementia blood tests (FBC, U&Es, LFTs, TFTs, HbA1c, calcium, ESR or CRP, B12/folate) within two months of referral

cycle1.result: 11.9% of referrals had all recommended blood tests; 27.1% had none.

result.intervention: Focus groups with the memory clinic team, information update letter and updated referral proforma distributed to primary care clinicians.

cycle2.result: 85.7% of referrals used the proforma; all recommended blood tests in 23.8% overall and in 80% of proforma referrals.

result.other_findings: 101 referrals across both cycles; memory clinic staff will now return referrals lacking up-to-date bloods to primary care.

result.setting: 15 wards, Broadmoor Hospital, high secure forensic psychiatry hospital
result.standard: Local Trust guidelines: vitamin D checked within one month of admission then three-monthly, with prescribing by level

cycle1.result: 76.4% checked within one month of admission; 66.7% checked within the last 3 months; 21.4% prescribed the correct dose, 22.9% under-dosed, 14.3% over-dosed and 41.4% given no dose where indicated.

result.other_findings: Deficiency fell from 43.6% on admission to 14.5% on most recent level.

result.topic: Emergency department management of self-harm in under-18s
result.setting: UK emergency departments, nine medical schools (SPARC student-led national audit)

cycle1.result: Nearly 500 ED records reviewed; 25% of records excluded for data quality issues. Clinical audit results not reported.

result.other_findings: Focus is lessons on student-led audit methods; decentralised peer training gave variable knowledge transfer.

result.setting: 18-bed older adult psychiatric inpatient ward
result.standard: Bowel monitoring with Bristol stool charts and consideration of preventative laxatives for patients on antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Bowel movement recorded on 5 days in total over 2 weeks; 2 bowel charts uploaded.

result.intervention: Bristol stool charts with staff training; charts integrated into MDT discussions with further training; then Norgine risk assessment tool and patient tutorial.

cycle2.result: 151 days recorded, average Norgine score 7.056 and all charts uploaded.

result.other_findings: Second cycle (18 patients) recorded 173 days with 16 charts uploaded; monitoring fell 8.73% from the second to third cycle.

result.topic: Antipsychotic physical health monitoring in CAMHS
result.setting: Child and Family Clinic, tier 3 outpatient CAMHS, Belfast Trust
result.standard: Belfast Trust CAMHS Antipsychotic Medication Monitoring Schedule (2015), based on CAMESA, NICE CG185, CG155 and Maudsley guidelines

cycle1.result: Baseline bloods 92%; baseline ECG 75%; complete monitoring bloods 33%; physical health parameters complete 42%; schedule present and current 42% (0% on PARIS).

result.intervention: Standardised recording using PARIS clinic letters and the schedule at the front of notes; baseline ECG mandatory.

cycle2.result: Baseline bloods 89%; baseline ECG 67%; complete monitoring bloods 44%; physical parameters complete 56%; schedule present and current 38%, present but not current 50% (0% on PARIS).

result.other_findings: Small numbers limit interpretation; initiation checklist, bloods diary and care-pathway booklet proposed.

result.setting: West Lothian Psychiatry, district general hospital (Psychiatric 2222 call)
result.standard: 90% documentation compliance using a new checklist

cycle1.result: Psychiatric team documentation 44%; ward nursing documentation 65%; medical ward doctor documentation 39%; appropriate calls 65%.

result.intervention: Documentation checklist in the electronic records system for completion by the junior doctor, introduced July 2023.

cycle2.result: Documentation 90%; ward nursing documentation 83%; medical ward doctor documentation 57%; appropriate calls 74%.

result.other_findings: Attending doctors staying longer than 10 minutes rose from 47% to 68%.

result.setting: Richmond and Kingston intellectual disability psychiatry caseloads
result.standard: Prolactin measured in the last 12 months for patients on antipsychotics and elevated results managed per current guidelines

cycle1.result: 39 (52.0%) had prolactin measured in the last 12 months; 16 (41.0%) of these were elevated; 81.3% of elevated results discussed and treatment considered.

result.other_findings: 68.8% of those with raised prolactin were on risperidone; uptake of blood tests is the main issue.

result.setting: Rheumatology consultant-delivered ultrasound clinic, Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Known IA (n = 30): 43.3% active on US, 6 of 13 escalated; suspected IA (n = 30): 16.7% had US evidence of IA.

result.other_findings: Sonographic findings were often not followed by a concordant treatment decision.

result.setting: Regional hospital acute psychiatric unit
result.standard: Medication reconciliation as a WHO safety initiative (Accreditation Canada ROP 2020 handbook): documented BPMH with ≥2 information sources

cycle1.result: 21/22 (95%) had a documented admission BPMH; 15/21 (71%) had at least one discrepancy, mostly omissions (10/17, 59%); ≥2 information sources documented in 1/21 (4.8%).

result.intervention: Findings shared with clinicians; DIS MedRec form with pre-populated provincial Drug Information System medication list implemented in late September 2025, with staff education.
result.other_findings: Pre- and post-intervention data collection (June–August 2025 vs November 2025–January 2026) is ongoing.

result.setting: Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists ECT guidelines (consent, vital signs, monitoring of clinical response and cognitive side effects)

cycle1.result: Consent forms completed 100% and ongoing consent checked for all; right to withdraw consent explained to none; vital signs robustly documented; no validated rating scale used; response between sessions assessed in 45%; no documentation of cognitive side-effect assessment.

result.intervention: Recommended updating consent forms to include right to withdraw, culturally validated assessment tools and re-audit in one year.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Broadmoor Hospital, high security psychiatric hospital
result.standard: NICE CG142 Autism spectrum disorder in adults: diagnosis and management

cycle1.result: 13 (76.5%) with confirmed ASD prescribed antipsychotics, nine with comorbid psychotic disorder; none prescribed psychotropics for core ASD symptoms; off-licence antipsychotic use not documented in any relevant participant in the preceding 12 months.

result.other_findings: Suggests forensic-specific prescribing guidance may be needed.

result.setting: Acute adult mental health inpatient unit, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
result.standard: Project aim of 10% improvement in documentation of driving status and driving advice within 8 weeks

cycle1.result: Driving status documented in 48 patients (median 60%); driving advice documented for 10 of 20 drivers (median 50%).

result.intervention: Education session for resident doctors on driving regulations; poster prompt in the resident workspace; mandatory driving status field in the discharge meeting template.

cycle2.result: Driving status documented in 53 patients (median 83%) with a run chart shift; driving advice documented for 17 of 27 drivers (median 80%).

result.other_findings: Driving advice documentation varied widely week to week with several weeks of zero compliance and no run chart shift.

result.topic: Dopamine agonist screening in gambling disorder
result.setting: NHS Northern Gambling Service
result.standard: 100% of initial assessments include a full medication history including dopamine agonists; 100% of patients on dopamine agonists screened by a psychiatrist before treatment allocation

cycle1.result: Full drug history documented in 53% (16/30); 17% (5/30) prescribed a dopamine agonist (all aripiprazole), of whom 1 was referred for psychiatrist screening.

result.intervention: Recommended staff training and discussion with a psychiatrist where appropriate.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Psychotropic prescribing and monitoring in learning disability
result.setting: Learning disability female low secure forensic unit
result.standard: Trust and national prescribing and monitoring guidelines

cycle1.result: 100% compliance for indications on drug chart, care plans for combined or high-dose antipsychotics, consent to treatment forms, annual health check and psychotropic blood monitoring; MHA capacity assessment forms 71%; valproate annual risk acknowledgement forms 0%.

result.intervention: Recommended care plans for all patients on valproate with review dates for risk acknowledgement forms, and consistent filing of results.
result.other_findings: Investigation results were difficult to locate.

result.setting: Hamad Medical Corporation Mental Health Services

cycle1.result: PD diagnosis in 83/171 (48.5%), mostly BPD (65.1%); MDT review 86.7%; crisis plan 61.4%; zero documented individual psychotherapy sessions in 26/48 and zero group sessions in 34/51; antipsychotics 69.9% and benzodiazepines 39.8%.

result.other_findings: No local guideline exists; 59.0% were readmissions and 25.3% had inpatient self-harm.

result.topic: Timeliness of GP letters after assessment
result.setting: CMHT Swords – Orange Team, North Dublin Mental Health Services
result.standard: NHS Standard Contract (2022) and HSE National Clinical Programme for Mental Health (2020): GP letter within 14 days of assessment

cycle1.result: 15 (75%) sent within 7 days, 4 (20%) within 8–14 days and 1 (5%) after 14 days; 95% overall compliance.

result.other_findings: Only patients assessed by the auditor were included.

result.setting: Paediatric inpatients
result.standard: Local paediatric vancomycin guideline: 100% correct starting dose, 90% levels at correct time, 80% third-dose troughs in range (10–15 mg/L), 90% appropriate action for out-of-range levels

cycle1.result: 100% correct starting dose; 90% of levels taken at the correct time; 33% of initial levels in range (a further 31% after dose change); 93% appropriate actions; three of six standards met.

result.intervention: Suggested changing dosing frequency to four times a day or continuous infusion.
result.other_findings: Two standards could not be assessed as no neonates or renal impairment cases; 62 levels reviewed.

result.setting: 59 UK Trusts, procedures under the care of an anaesthetist (national audit)
result.standard: Association of Anaesthetists' 2020 consensus guideline on peri-operative glucocorticoid management

cycle1.result: Of 219 on ≥5 mg prednisolone equivalents, 67 (31%) pre-operatively and 43 (20%) postoperatively supplemented according to guideline; overall compliance 19/219 (9%); 30/219 (14%) no supplementation; 28/58 (48%) on <5 mg received inappropriate supplementation.

result.other_findings: 21,731 operations audited; 45% of anaesthetists reported using the guideline, with adherence in only 27/125 (22%).

result.topic: Mental Health Act assessment on-call doctor involvement
result.setting: Northstaffs Combined Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: Local algorithm for Mental Health Act assessments: one doctor from the care team or on-call consultant in hours and one on-call doctor out of hours

cycle1.result: At least one NSCHT doctor involved in 91% of assessments (92% in the Section 136 suite, 89% out of hours).

result.intervention: Recommended amending the Section 136 form to record the doctor's role; results presented to governance groups.
result.other_findings: 45% detained under section 2 and 35% under section 3; substance misuse featured in 26%.

result.setting: Tri-Borough Perinatal Service (Ealing, Hounslow, Hammersmith and Fulham)
result.standard: Service target non-attendance (DNA) rate of 15% or lower for initial assessments

cycle1.result: Overall DNA rate 35.3% (n=100), exceeding the target.

result.other_findings: DNA rates were higher for physical centre appointments (40.0% vs 20.7% home and 25.9% remote; p=0.035) and with greater deprivation (p<0.001); ethnicity not significant (p=0.062).

result.setting: Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit, Cheshire and Wirral Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice: medical review within 1 hour, 4-hourly until MDT review, twice daily thereafter, with specified content

cycle1.result: 20% seen face-to-face within 1 hour; 75% seen 4-hourly until MDT review; mental health documented 97%, physical health 61%, medication 69%, rationale for continuing seclusion 72%; adverse medication effects and observation level 2%, risk to self 7%.

result.intervention: Planned presentation at junior doctor induction and a quick reference sheet before re-audit.
result.other_findings: 5 seclusion episodes in 4 patients; a previous audit had not led to change.

result.topic: Cardiometabolic assessment clinic attendance and escalation
result.setting: Cardiometabolic Assessment Clinic, community mental health team
result.standard: All invited patients should attend the CMA clinic, and all patients with concerning observations or needing signposting should be appropriately escalated

cycle1.result: DNA rate 52%; 53% of physical health issues managed correctly.

result.intervention: Group and 1:1 staff teaching (primary care invited); information leaflet with each appointment; MEWS-based proforma for GP escalation; staff allowed to contact GP practices directly.

cycle2.result: DNA rate 42%; 90% of physical health issues managed correctly.

result.other_findings: DNA rate remained high; domiciliary visits recommended for repeated non-attenders.

result.setting: Two male and two female general adult inpatient wards, East Midlands
result.standard: Lester Tool: baseline BP, HbA1c/glucose, lipids, lifestyle review and weight within one week of initiation, then weekly weight for six weeks

cycle1.result: Baseline BP 89.5%, HbA1c/glucose 65.8%, lipids 57.9%, lifestyle review 55.3%, weight 36.8%; 5.9% had full weekly weight follow-up and 41.2% none within six weeks.

result.intervention: Recommended awareness of baseline bloods, electronic record alerts for weekly weights and a refusal drop-down, and re-audit.
result.other_findings: Reasons for non-compliance were poorly documented; risperidone most prescribed.

result.topic: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
result.setting: 12 general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE Clinical Guidelines and Trust physical health policy: physical examination and assessment within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Within 24 hours: physical examination 60%, physical observations 86%, BMI 62%, MUST 62%, smoking status 54%, alcohol consumption 65%, comorbidity status 67%.

result.intervention: Recommended greater staff awareness of physical health assessment.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: National Oesophago-Gastric Cancer Audit, England and Wales

cycle1.result: 17 650 patients had surgery; 30-day mortality fell with audit year (OR 0.93, 95% c.i. 0.88 to 0.98) and 90-day mortality (OR 0.94, 0.91 to 0.98), with shorter postoperative stay (IRR 0.98).

result.other_findings: Higher trust volume was also associated with better outcomes; little evidence of earlier diagnosis.

result.setting: Liaison Psychiatry, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Comparison with 2024 local census ethnic composition

cycle1.result: White 90.9% of self-harm and 89.5% of ward referrals vs 91.4% census; Mixed groups absent in self-harm and 0.7% of ward referrals vs 1.3%; Asian 1.7% and 1.5% and African 0.4% and 0.8%, underrepresented.

result.intervention: Recommended better ethnicity data collection, community outreach and cultural competency training.
result.other_findings: 'Other ethnic groups' were slightly overrepresented.

result.setting: Elm Ward, West Park Hospital, Tees, Esk and Wear Valley
result.standard: NICE TA77: zopiclone not exceeding four weeks including tapering

cycle1.result: Mean duration 7.7 weeks (median 8.3); 27% (6/22) within the ≤4-week limit.

result.intervention: Practice changes introduced after the initial audit (not described).

cycle2.result: Mean duration 3.42 weeks, median 1.29 weeks; 83.3% (10/12) within ≤4 weeks; 30% of evaluable cases met indication-specific NICE durations.

result.other_findings: Stop dates, indications, review plans and non-pharmacological interventions remained poorly documented.

result.setting: Older adult psychiatry ward, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: DVLA guidance on fitness to drive

cycle1.result: Driving status documented in 5 (25%) despite 18 (90%) having DVLA-relevant diagnoses; DVLA advice recorded for 3.

result.intervention: Clinician education and prompts in the ward round template.

cycle2.result: Driving status documented in 10 (90.9%); both drivers for whom guidance applied had DVLA advice discussed.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Psychiatry of Old Age service, North-West of Ireland
result.standard: NICE 2014, BNF 2019 and Maudsley 2018: 3-monthly serum lithium and renal tests, thyroid and calcium monitoring

cycle1.result: 78% (n = 14) on track for 3-monthly lithium levels; 39% (n = 7) in therapeutic range; 83% (n = 15) 3-monthly renal tests; thyroid function 89% (n = 16); calcium documented 63%.

result.other_findings: All 18 had abnormal renal function; 56% of those started by the service had renal impairment before initiation.

result.setting: Carseview Centre (3 adult wards, IPCU and learning disability unit), NHS Tayside
result.standard: Local NHS Tayside Emergency Equipment Protocol

cycle1.result: Trolleys lacked ligature packs, masks not by oxygen cylinders, dextro-tablets not readily available; learning disability unit had no resuscitation trolley.

result.intervention: Feedback to wards, multidisciplinary meetings and an updated local protocol (finalised November 2020) with recommendations.

cycle2.result: Trolleys better equipped in line with the updated protocol; missing items varied by ward but none consistent across the site; all recommendations implemented.

result.other_findings: Additional items such as nebuliser and non-rebreather masks were stocked but hard to locate.

result.setting: Lewisham Assessment & Liaison team (Neighbourhoods 1, 3 and 4) and GP practices

cycle1.result: Basic bloods (FBC, U&E, LFTs) in 54% (n = 13); glucose 38% (n = 9); prolactin 13% (n = 3); creatine kinase 0%; 0% completely monitored.

result.other_findings: Data obtained for 24 of 40 patients; audit to be expanded to Neighbourhood 2.

result.setting: Two acute inpatient psychiatric wards
result.standard: BNF minimum standards, NICE CG178 and SIGN 131: side-effect review after initiation and dose titration, at 3 months and annually (gold standard adds 1 month); GASS form completion

cycle1.result: GASS completion rate 7% across both wards; only 1 form valid; one ward had no completed forms

result.intervention: Presentation at ward QI meetings, infographic for staff, highlighting role and importance of the forms; re-audit after 2 months

cycle2.result: Completion rate rose from 7% to 26% (3 to 9 patients); valid forms increased from 1 to 4

result.other_findings: Improvement described as sub-optimal; patient acuity limited completion.

result.setting: Nottingham City Central Local Mental Health Team (community)
result.standard: MHRA guidance that clozapine levels should be monitored in clinical situations where toxicity may be suspected

cycle1.dates: Plasma levels 2006 to 2020; doses from 2018 onwards
cycle1.result: 273 clozapine levels taken; mean interval between levels 10 months 2 weeks (range 2 days to 13 years); 88 levels >600 ug/L and 108 levels <350 ug/L; 32% of levels above recommended range; non-significant positive dose-level trend (R = 0.37)

result.other_findings: No routine clozapine level monitoring found; unclear whether levels were trough levels.

result.topic: Antidepressant indication documentation and medication review
result.setting: Hailsham Early Intervention in Psychosis Service
result.standard: Diagnosis recorded alongside each antidepressant prescription; EIPN guidance that psychotropic medication is reviewed every 6 months

cycle1.result: 33 patients (37%) prescribed an antidepressant; 25 (76%) had a recorded indication; 67 patients (84%) had a medical review within 6 months

result.other_findings: Sertraline was the commonest antidepressant (52%); re-audit planned in 6 months.

result.topic: Raised inflammatory markers of unclear cause
result.setting: Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases, Bath, rheumatology outpatients

cycle1.result: Mean referral to seen time 3.43 weeks; 36% mechanical or non-rheumatological diagnosis, 34% inflammatory arthritis; diagnosis changed in 25% on follow-up; 6 deaths (13% mortality)

result.other_findings: Autoimmune testing in 97% and radiology in 90%; 3 new malignancies diagnosed.

result.topic: Vitamin D testing and replacement in inpatients
result.setting: Becklin Centre, acute adult psychiatric inpatient unit, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust policy that vitamin D is checked in all inpatients and supplementation started where appropriate; target 90% for both

cycle1.result: Vitamin D checked in 79 (56.4%); colecalciferol started in 61 (83.6%) of those insufficient or deficient; target not met

result.intervention: Planned presentation of findings to the Trust medical workforce
result.other_findings: Testing rate differed by ethnicity (Caucasian 64.0% vs non-Caucasian 44.4%, p = 0.032); 51.9% insufficient and 40.5% deficient.

result.setting: Tertiary hepato-pancreato-biliary unit, Manchester Royal Infirmary
result.standard: PACT-UK synoptic reporting template for pancreatic cancer CT; compliance defined as more than 90% of information available

cycle1.result: Compliance 0% for initial presentation scans and 4.2% (n=1) of 24 staging scans; the only compliant scan used the PACT-UK template

result.other_findings: More than 80% of reports lacked pancreatic duct size, predicted tumour type and stage, variant vascular anatomy and arterial/venous involvement.

result.topic: Psychotropic prescribing and physical health monitoring
result.setting: Crisis Team, Fieldhead Hospital, South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines on psychotropic prescribing, baseline investigations, review and physical health monitoring

cycle1.result: 100% for indication, dosage, discussion with patient and side-effect monitoring; of 22 on antipsychotics, 11 had ECG and bloods by Crisis Team, 4 by other parties, 3 bloods but no ECG, 2 no physical health monitoring

result.other_findings: 46 of 50 responded to treatment; physical health monitoring needs improvement.

result.setting: Kilbarrack East Community Mental Health Team, North Dublin Mental Health Services
result.standard: NICE guidelines for lithium monitoring (lithium levels, renal and thyroid function, calcium, BMI)

cycle1.result: 12% (3/25) compliant with all lithium monitoring guidelines; none had calcium or BMI recorded

result.intervention: MDT meeting; green sticker system, lithium monitoring sheet, patient monitoring lists defining responsibilities, lithium blood clinic and new Clinical Nurse Specialist reporting system (March 2025)

cycle2.result: 68% (17/25) compliant; 32% (8/25) had no lithium level; 44% had no U&E or thyroid tests; 8% had calcium tested; no BMI recorded

result.other_findings: Patient education leaflet introduced after the second audit; calcium and BMI stayed poor.

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing audit and feedback in nursing homes
result.setting: Nursing home physicians receiving MyPractice: Long-Term Care reports, Ontario

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Qualitative interview study; professional role and identity influenced antibiotic prescribing and response to the feedback report.

result.setting: ECT service, NHS Grampian
result.standard: NICE guidance on ECT: documented risk/benefit assessment including anaesthetic risk and cognitive impairment, patient information leaflet, consultation of advocate

cycle1.result: Indication documented 100%; RCPsych leaflet received 50%; risk/benefit discussion documented 50%; specific side effects discussed 50%

result.other_findings: Standardised consent form being considered, with re-audit planned after introduction.

result.topic: BMI recording and dietetic referral on admission
result.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards and PICU, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BMI measured and recorded after admission; referral to dietetics if BMI >30 kg/m2, or >28 kg/m2 with weight-related comorbidities

cycle1.result: No BMI measured on admission for 14 of 148; 34 met referral criteria, of whom 4 were not referred and 5 declined

result.other_findings: 74 of 134 with BMI recorded were overweight or obese; need to emphasise BMI recording in the admission physical health screen.

result.setting: General adult psychiatry wards 19 and 20, University Hospital Hairmyres, NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: Scottish Patient Safety Programme and NICE: 95% of medicines reconciled within 24 hours of admission; local medicines reconciliation guidelines

cycle1.result: 70% of forms completed within 24 hours; two sources of information used in 66%

result.intervention: Summary document of latest guidelines and link to an e-learning module distributed to resident doctors and raised at monthly resident doctors' meeting

cycle2.result: 100% of forms completed within 24 hours; two sources used in 100%; improvement in all 12 areas assessed

result.other_findings: Results may reflect individual variability between clerking doctors.

result.setting: North and South Community Mental Health Teams, Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust standard (NHS Standard Contract): 100% of clinic outcomes completed within 24 hours and clinic letters within 7 days

cycle1.result: Clinic entries within 24 hours: South 99%, North 94%; letters within 7 days: South 99%, North 92%; 8% of North letters overdue or missing, some up to 31 days

result.other_findings: Recommended presenting findings, an administrative capacity survey and a 12-week re-audit.

result.setting: Rheumatology department, St George's NHS Foundation Trust, London (tertiary)

cycle1.result: 59 (60%) taking corticosteroids at scan; 39.8% showed active rheumatological disease; 32.6% non-rheumatological abnormalities; 2% new cancer diagnoses

result.other_findings: Incidental findings led to further tests including ultrasound (11 patients) and endoscopy (7 patients).

result.topic: Dual diagnosis substance misuse assessment on admission
result.setting: Redbridge Community Recovery Team West, psychiatric admissions
result.standard: NICE CG120 on co-existing severe mental illness and substance misuse (used to guide recommendations)

cycle1.result: Only 50% with known dual diagnosis had a urine drug screen on admission; 25% of those currently misusing substances were referred to specialist services

result.other_findings: Dual diagnosis patients were more often detained (89% vs 72%), of no fixed abode (28% vs 13%) and non-compliant pre-admission (83% vs 56%).

result.topic: Peri-operative cardiac arrest in cardiology procedures
result.setting: 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) of the Royal College of Anaesthetists

cycle1.result: 54/881 (6.1%) of NAP7 cardiac arrest reports; estimated incidence 1/450 or 0.22 (0.17–0.29)%; ECMO CPR 3/53 (6%)

result.other_findings: Themes included logistics and teamworking in remote locations, cardiogenic shock, late anaesthetic involvement and TAVI.

result.topic: Risk assessment on admission to mixed-sex wards
result.setting: Mixed-sex inpatient psychiatric wards, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust
result.standard: Acute care group standard: patients with known risk to the opposite sex not admitted to mixed-sex wards; comprehensive risk assessment on admission with escalation to MDT

cycle1.result: Full risk assessment documented in 50%; historical risks in 40%; clerkings contained a risk assessment in 70%; 30% had risks to the opposite sex, none escalated to MDT

result.other_findings: Recommended specific guidance and teaching; re-audit scheduled for March 2022.

result.setting: Beech Unit, Torbay, Devon Partnership Trust (inpatient)
result.standard: Trust Inpatient Admissions SOP: capacity to consent to treatment assessed within 24 hours of admission; MCA Code of Practice (decision-specific, four-part functional test, least restrictive, best interests)

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment within 24 hours 100%; MCA template completed in 90% (half within timeframe); decision documented 90%; functional test 90%; least restrictive and best interests 53%

result.other_findings: Recommended using the Trust standardised MCA template and guidance for clerking doctors.

result.setting: 35 acute care hospitals in 7 countries (International Collaboration of Orthopaedic Nursing)
result.standard: 12 internationally accepted nursing quality care indicators for older adults with fragility hip fracture

cycle1.result: 35 hospitals (100%) completed the audit; quality indicators were reflected in the majority of policies, protocols or processes, with variable timing and frequency

result.other_findings: Development and testing of an audit tool; respondents found content relevant and applicable.

result.setting: Peter Bruff Mental Health Assessment Unit
result.standard: NICE NG108 (2018) recommendations 1.4: 100% of admitted patients should have MCA completed during admission clerking

cycle1.result: MCA completed with capacity at clerking and review in 85%; lacked capacity at clerking 3%; capacity at admission but not at review 5%; MCA not completed or unavailable in 7%

result.other_findings: Discrepancy between clerking and later reviews suggests further training needed.

result.setting: Medium secure forensic hospital, Liverpool, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE: all patients with psychosis offered CBTp and complete at least 16 sessions

cycle1.result: 68% (19/28) offered CBTp; 85% (11/13) of these completed 16 sessions

result.other_findings: Barriers to offering were being too unwell (7/9) or in other therapies (2/9); barrier to completion was patient refusal (2/2).

result.topic: Primary care mental health practitioner assessment and referral
result.setting: Community Mental Health Team, Brentwood Resource Centre
result.standard: All new referrals first seen by the Mental Health Practitioner; MHP PCN Consultation V2 assessment template used; target 100%

cycle1.result: Referrals initially assessed 69.2% (82.5%); GP referrals compliant 67.2% (80.2%); MHP assessment template used 100%

result.other_findings: 190 (24.5%) did not engage and 44 (5.7%) had data unavailable.

result.setting: Community secondary mental health service, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 44% (n = 40) smokers; 31 offered smoking cessation advice; NRT offered to 13; 5 referred to smoking cessation services

result.other_findings: Survey: 20/31 smokers wanted to reduce or quit; local GPs did not prescribe NRT and no targeted community service existed.

result.setting: Two care homes, Wakefield (WF9 area)
result.standard: NICE guidance on antipsychotics in dementia: initiation for severe agitation/distress under specialist supervision, monitoring and follow-up

cycle1.result: 24 of 63 with dementia on antipsychotics; blood monitoring 56% (13/24); ECG 50% (12/24); follow-up plan 81% (51/63); reduction plan 8% (2/24)

result.other_findings: 8% (5/95) on antipsychotics without dementia diagnosis; an antipsychotic register was suggested.

result.topic: Mental Health Act detention by ethnicity
result.setting: Andersen Ward Mother and Baby Unit, South Manchester

cycle1.result: Detained: Black 88%, Asian 72.7%, Mixed/other 33.3%, White 28.3% (statistically significant); all 11 with non-English primary language detained

result.other_findings: Length of stay and time to first section 17 leave did not differ by ethnicity.

result.topic: Mortality risk documentation in emergency laparotomy consent
result.setting: West Suffolk Hospital, Bury St Edmunds, emergency general surgery
result.standard: NCEPOD 2011: risk of mortality explicitly discussed and documented on consent forms and in medical records

cycle1.result: Mortality documented in NELA 93%, consent forms 40%, medical notes discussion 35%

result.intervention: Periodic reminders for surgeons during meetings and posters

cycle2.result: Mortality documented in NELA 90%, consent forms 92%, medical notes 51% (consent improvement p < 0.0001)

result.other_findings: Three cycles; second cycle (March to May 2022, 38 cases) showed 92% NELA, 71% consent forms and 42% notes.

result.topic: Eating disorder referral quality in CAMHS
result.setting: West Glasgow CAMHS team, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
result.standard: Junior MARSIPAN guidelines for referral content and physical measures

cycle1.result: Height and weight recorded in 73.1% of referrals

result.intervention: Duty clinicians screened referrals and prompted GPs for physical parameters; weekly board round meeting; weekly physical health monitoring clinic

cycle2.result: Height and weight recorded in 82.1%; 53.8% needed prompting; risk recorded 46.2%, onset 51.3%, body image 56.4% (no change in written content); mean referral to diagnosis 44.1 to 34.2 days

result.other_findings: Staff stress (MHPSS) scores stayed high; a GP referral proforma was recommended.

result.setting: Older adult inpatient units across four localities, Black Country Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE CG183: 100% of drug charts and electronic records (Rio) have allergy status documented

cycle1.result: Paper drug charts 100% (type or severity 70%); EPR allergy status 62% (range 30–100% by ward; Wolverhampton 93%, West Bromwich 100%, Dudley 33%, Walsall 39%)

result.intervention: Allergy status prompt in electronic clerking document, stickers and posters, pharmacy updating EPR allergy status, allergy alert on bed state view
result.other_findings: Second data collection of around 300 patients was under way.

result.setting: Neonatal units
result.standard: Local vancomycin prescribing and therapeutic drug monitoring guidance

cycle1.result: Loading, initial continuous dosing and TDM generally in line with local guidelines; 9% of first levels subtherapeutic; of 298 levels 56% therapeutic, 19% supratherapeutic, 25% subtherapeutic

result.other_findings: A previous audit of intermittent dosing found 50% of first levels subtherapeutic; no vancomycin-specific adverse effects.

result.topic: Driving risk assessment and DVLA advice
result.setting: Adult acute inpatient wards, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local policy: leave risk discussion capturing driving risk before home leave; DVLA advice documented in notes and discharge summaries

cycle1.result: Leave risk discussion compliance 73%; 5% of drivers given written DVLA guidance on discharge letters

cycle2.result: 100% compliance with leave risk discussion; 56% had DVLA advice recorded on discharge summary

result.other_findings: Improvement plan agreed: MDT communication, junior doctor induction and driving advice added to discharge meeting checklist.

result.topic: Community and inpatient team interface during admission
result.setting: Elm Ward (female inpatients), West Park Hospital, Darlington
result.standard: Trust Admission, Transfer and Discharge policy (community team involvement, care plan copy, GP informed within 24 hours of admission)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.dates: Discharges 1 February 2021 to 23 March 2021; data collected May 2021
cycle2.result: Community team invited to meetings in 96%; contact with community team in 100%; GP informed increased to 20%; written care plan copy offered increased but still low; overall amber rating

result.other_findings: Expected length of stay was poorly communicated by care coordinators and responsibility for informing GPs was unclear.

result.topic: Acute upper GI bleeding care bundle
result.setting: Single surgical unit, University Hospital Hairmyres, East Kilbride
result.standard: BSG-led multisociety AUGIB care bundle (2019); target 100% for each step

cycle1.result: All OGDs had consultant supervision; significant gap in applying the care bundle, Glasgow-Blatchford risk scoring and resuscitation and medical management (detailed figures in table, not given in text)

result.other_findings: 30-day mortality 8.0%; 56.7% of OGDs in hours; recommended formal implementation of the bundle from ED to admission unit.

result.setting: Victoria Ward, old age psychiatry, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BMA, BNF and Trust prescription writing standards (GMC number, signature, doctor's name, drug, indication, dose, route, frequency, start date, date, timings)

cycle1.result: Errors found in all parameters except medication timings

result.intervention: Results presented at departmental meeting and re-training on prescription writing

cycle2.result: Errors increased: GMC number errors up 20.33%, doctor's name 16.87%, indication 12.94%, original start date 5%; name of drug improved by 10.88%

result.other_findings: Trust then issued stamps with GMC number and doctor's name to junior doctors; re-audit planned.

result.setting: Adult PICU, Park House Hospital, Greater Manchester Mental Health
result.standard: Local trust seclusion policy (physical health, risk, medication, MSE review; initial medical review within 60 minutes)

cycle1.result: Initiation time and rationale 95%; physical health 75%; risk to others 50%; risk to self 5%; MSE and medication review 50%; initial medical review within 60 minutes 44%

result.other_findings: Policy since changed to 'overall psychiatric health'; risk to self largely undocumented.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Older persons mental health inpatient units, three sites, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: NICE and Department of Health VTE guidelines; target 100%

cycle1.result: East: 6/9 forms filled; Central: 2 of 21 had a form, none filled; West: 3 of 11 had a completed form; no standard proforma in Central or West

result.intervention: Trust-wide VTE risk assessment proforma adapted for psychiatric inpatients planned
result.other_findings: VTE prophylaxis mentioned inconsistently on medication charts.

result.setting: Lithium clinic, Older Person's Mental Health Service, Princess of Wales Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: NICE lithium guidance and GMC Good Medical Practice; 100% of relevant data documented

cycle1.result: Dose, level and renal function over 83.3% (n = 15); psychotropics 61.1%; side effects 50%; mood 77.8%; safety netting 11.1% (n = 2)

result.intervention: Results disseminated to team and lithium clinic proforma introduced, revised after clinician feedback

cycle2.result: Dose, levels, psychotropics and side effects 100% (n = 12); renal function and mood 91.7% (n = 11); safety netting 75% (n = 9)

result.other_findings: Documentation varied between clinicians before the proforma.

result.setting: Psychiatry units, Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore
result.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines in Psychiatry, 13th edition, pre-clozapine assessment

cycle1.result: FBC, LFT, U&E and glucose 100%; ECG 76%; lipids 33%; ESR 19%; troponin 14%; CRP, BNP and physical examination 0%

result.other_findings: Barriers included staff training, prescriber inconsistency and funding and staffing limits.

result.setting: Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust (Trust-wide)
result.standard: National guidance on pre-lithium checks (weight/BMI/waist, TFTs, calcium, eGFR), POMH lithium audit

cycle1.result: Weight/BMI/waist 78%; calcium 80%; TFTs 93%; eGFR 100% before initiation; all above national POMH compliance

result.intervention: Planned Quality Performance Alert to medical and nursing staff and lithium monitoring in junior doctor induction
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust recommendations for high-dose antipsychotic therapy (clozapine considered; baseline and post-increase ECG, BMI, BP, pulse, bloods)

cycle1.result: 21 on combination therapy, 11 on HDAT; clozapine considered in 9 of 11 HDAT; ECG before HDAT 100% but after dose increase 36%; BMI 100%; BP and pulse 91%; HbA1c 91%; prolactin 46%

result.other_findings: HDAT prevalence 9% against 28% in the 2012 POMH audit.

result.topic: Weight and BMI monitoring in learning disability
result.setting: Tower Hamlets Community Learning Disability Service, East London Foundation Trust
result.standard: Project target: up-to-date BMI for 70% or more of service users by September 2024

cycle1.result: 26.7% of 71 service users had an updated weight and BMI

result.intervention: Planned PDSA cycles; weekly MDT meetings with service users; waiting-room machine for weight, height and blood pressure; staff education
result.other_findings: No robust process for weight monitoring across a caseload of 1264.

result.setting: 17-bed functional old age psychiatry ward, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Electronic admission clerking pro forma based on Royal College of Psychiatrists admission guidelines; 90% compliance with each section

cycle1.result: All domains improved from 2019 to 2021 except mental state examination (9.09% decrease, not significant); 4 domains improved significantly; 9 domains still below the 90% standard

result.other_findings: Comparison of pre-pandemic and pandemic periods rather than a pre/post intervention audit; late pandemic better in 10 domains, early pandemic better in 4.

result.topic: Relapse prevention medication in detox referrals
result.setting: The Level Nottingham inpatient detoxification unit (referrals from community addiction services)
result.standard: Referrals mention relapse prevention medications and provide blood test results; target 100% for each

cycle1.result: RPMs not mentioned in 40% of alcohol and 77% of opioid referrals; 48% of referrals had no blood results; median 22 days from blood results to referral and 85 days to admission

result.other_findings: About one-third of referrals did not mention RPMs and were not going to residential rehabilitation; recommended referrer discussions and referral form changes.

result.topic: Controlled drug prescription writing in opioid substitution therapy
result.setting: Substance misuse service issuing methadone and buprenorphine prescriptions
result.standard: Legal requirements for controlled drug prescriptions and Home Office approved instalment wording; internal script record standard terms

cycle1.result: 100% met legal CD requirements; 7 (11%) omitted Home Office wording for pharmacy closure days; 46 (72%) had non-applicable additional wording; 13 different frequency terms used in script record against 6 standard terms

result.other_findings: Frequency of collection left blank on 2 occasions.

result.setting: Rheumatology service, Pennine MSK Partnership, Oldham
result.standard: ACR and EULAR guidance supporting biologic tapering; locally agreed eligibility criteria

cycle1.result: Patients tapered increased from 24 in 2019 to 51 in 2021; tapering failed in 7/116 (6%); estimated saving up to £170,000 per annum

result.intervention: EHR records flagged to prompt shared decision-making discussion at routine appointments
result.other_findings: More patients were eligible than identified by EHR search because of missing coding (787, 61%).

result.topic: Physical health monitoring on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust policy: physical health monitoring within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Within 24 hours: BMI 91%, blood pressure 62%, cholesterol 59%, HbA1c 58%; QRISK calculated in 78% of eligible; NRT offered to 97% of smokers (13% accepted)

result.other_findings: A 24-hour physical health checklist was suggested.

result.setting: General practice, West Midlands
result.standard: BNF annual monitoring of weight, glucose/HbA1c, lipids and blood pressure: 100% with three or more of four monitored; 80% monitored for each measure

cycle1.result: 48% had three or more risk factors monitored; overall monitoring rate 58%; no measure reached 80%

result.intervention: Recommendations from the first cycle (details not reported)

cycle2.result: 60% had three or more risk factors monitored; overall monitoring rate 65% (p = 0.04); no measure reached 80%, three measures improved

result.other_findings: Further recommendations: manual reminders for patients outside SMI checks and phlebotomy access; re-audit planned.

result.topic: Leave and observation documentation in admission plans
result.setting: Out-of-hours psychiatric admissions, NHS Tayside
result.standard: Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003 and local risk protocols: MHA status, leave and observation levels documented

cycle1.result: Observation levels documented 15.4%; leave status documented 1.9% (13.5% failed to mention leave at all); MHA status 82.7%

result.intervention: Posters in resident doctor work areas prompting legal status and safety monitoring plans

cycle2.result: Observation levels 55.2%; leave status 65.5%; MHA status 75.9%

result.other_findings: MHA status documentation stayed roughly the same.

result.setting: Rheumatology, Royal Surrey County Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, Guildford
result.standard: NICE and BSR: DAS28 recorded at least every 6 months for patients with RA on high-cost DMARDs

cycle1.result: 166 (80%) had a documented DAS28; 14 (7%) had DAS28 at least 6-monthly; 152 (73%) did not meet the standard

result.other_findings: Scores were recorded on Blueteq but not in letters; a DAS28 table in the clinic letter template was suggested.

result.topic: Bone protection in giant cell arteritis
result.setting: Rheumatology, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow
result.standard: BSR giant cell arteritis guideline: consider pharmacological bone protection at presentation

cycle1.result: Bisphosphonate consideration documented at diagnosis in 96% overall (TOC 94%, MTX 91%, MONO 100%); compliance for recommended duration 88% overall

result.other_findings: No significant difference between steroid-sparing and monotherapy groups (p = 0.52 and 0.8).

result.setting: Inpatient psychiatric unit, Hampshire and Isle of Wight Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines and local Trust policy on insomnia (non-pharmacological first, CBT-I, documented indication, review and stop dates for hypnotics)

cycle1.result: Insomnia in 30 (66.6%); documented in 23 (76.6%); sleep hygiene in 11/30 (36.6%); CBT-I offered 0%; hypnotics offered to 26/30 (86.6%); 0% met all NICE and Trust criteria

result.other_findings: A standardised insomnia care pathway was recommended.

result.setting: Southern Gambling Service (outpatient gambling disorder service)
result.standard: NICE CG115, Department of Health and Social Care and Royal College of Physicians guidance: full AUDIT if AUDIT-C at least 5, brief intervention for scores 5–10, advice and signposting for 11 or more

cycle1.result: AUDIT-C and EWAC completed 100%; full AUDIT 0%; brief intervention documented in 7% of higher-risk; 1 (25%) possibly dependent patient signposted; none given advice on avoiding abrupt cessation

result.intervention: Recommended: full AUDIT for AUDIT-C 5 or more, staff upskilling in brief intervention, regional alcohol services directory, psychoeducation materials
result.other_findings: 98 patients referred; all with scores of 11 or more had alcohol discussed in formulation and 75% an ICD-11 alcohol diagnosis.

result.topic: Baricitinib dosing in elderly and renal impairment
result.setting: Rheumatology, University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire
result.standard: NICE guidance (2 mg daily if 75 years or older) and BNF (avoid if creatinine clearance <30 ml/min; reduce dose if 30–60 ml/min)

cycle1.result: Of 13 aged 75+ still on baricitinib, 10 on 2 mg and 3 on 4 mg; 4 of 7 started after 75 began on 4 mg; 14 of 16 with creatinine clearance 30–60 ml/min were at some point on 4 mg, 6 still on 4 mg

result.other_findings: Suggested adding age and renal function to the prescription format.

result.setting: Rampton Hospital (high secure hospital)
result.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition) pre-initiation and ongoing monitoring for lithium, valproate and carbamazepine (16 standards)

cycle1.result: Valproate FBC monitoring within 6 months 92% (other 2018 figures not reported)

cycle2.result: Valproate pre-initiation LFT 35.8%, FBC 41.5%, 6-month monitoring 85.7% and 87.5%; lithium pre-initiation ECG 73.1%, TFT 88.5%, U&E 96.2%, monitoring 100%; carbamazepine pre-initiation 50%, monitoring 100%; all standards improved except valproate FBC monitoring

result.other_findings: Only 6 of 16 standards had 100% compliance; pre-initiation monitoring poor for valproate and carbamazepine.

result.setting: Specialist Support Team (Lancashire and Greater Manchester), Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: STOMP prescribing standards: indication and rationale stated, consent, monitoring of response and side effects, review of need for continuation

cycle1.result: Indication and rationale 50%; consent, monitoring and review of continuation each less than 10%

result.other_findings: Early re-audit recommended.

result.setting: Mental Health Liaison Team, Southend Hospital
result.standard: Documented 4AT for patients aged 65 and over referred to the liaison team

cycle1.result: 5 (7.5%) had a documented 4AT score

result.intervention: Educational sessions for MHLT staff and laminated 4AT lanyard prompts
result.other_findings: Recommended integrating the 4AT into assessment forms.

result.setting: Mental Health Inreach Team, HMP Elmley (Category B remand prison)
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists 'Use of licensed medicines for unlicensed applications in psychiatric practice' (2nd edition)

cycle1.result: 82 on off-label quetiapine; 28.1% (23/82) initiated by MHIRT psychiatrists

cycle2.result: 60 on off-label quetiapine; 8.3% (5/60) initiated by MHIRT; licensed drug considered, risks and benefits documented, explained and consent documented 80.0% each; low start dose 100%; baseline physical health 80.0%

result.other_findings: Prescriber could not be determined in 17 patients; most off-label prescriptions were started by other prescribers.

result.setting: High dependency unit and acute ward, Nepean Mental Health Centre, Sydney
result.standard: TGA and Medsafe product information and Therapeutic Guidelines maximum doses: 100% of individual and combined antipsychotic doses within limits

cycle1.result: 13/30 (43.3%) above 100% cumulative maximum; 3 (10%) above maximum for regular antipsychotics; 0/30 for PRN; 18/30 (60%) on 2 antipsychotics, 8/30 (26.6%) on 3, 2/30 (6.6%) on 4

result.other_findings: Recommended review of routine PRN antipsychotics and a vital sign monitoring protocol.

result.setting: South Durham Tier 3 CAMHS
result.standard: National guidelines on ADHD medication initiation, physical health monitoring, follow-up and rating scales

cycle1.result: Pre-medication assessment 100%; regular follow-up 5/7; height and weight plotted 6/7; rating scales returned by parents 0 and schools 3/7

result.intervention: Recommendations from previous audit, including a centralised list of service users and retrieval of rating scales

cycle2.result: Pre-medication assessment 100%; regular follow-up 5/7; physical health check within 3 months 100%; height and weight plotted 6/7; rating scales completed by parents and school 6/7; green compliance

result.other_findings: Waiting time to start medication increased because of staffing issues.

result.topic: Extended VTE prophylaxis after cancer surgery
result.setting: Oesophago-gastric unit, Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Preston
result.standard: NICE: extended pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for 28 days after major abdominal cancer surgery

cycle1.result: Pre-2014: 13/92 (14.1%) discharged with 28-day prophylaxis; post-2014: 423/490 (86.3%) (p<0.05); VTE 0.17%

result.intervention: Trust-wide policy of 28-day extended VTE prophylaxis after discharge adopted in 2014

cycle2.result: 63/68 (92.6%) received prophylaxis (86.3% to 92.6%, p=0.145); VTE 0%; no bleeding readmissions

result.other_findings: No readmissions for bleeding complications in either period.

result.setting: Memory Assessment Service, East North East Older People's Services, Leeds

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Formal MAS appointment pathway with defined admin contact points, displayed on posters in admin and memory nurse rooms

cycle2.result: Positive improvement in attendance rate (figures not reported)

result.other_findings: Admin team had no pathway to guide appointment management before the project.

result.topic: Admission blood tests in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Inpatient adult working age psychiatry unit (excluding PICU), South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: RCPsych guidance: admission blood tests within 24 hours of admission; Trust policy on vitamin D and calcium assessment and management of deficiency

cycle1.result: 79% had bloods within 24 hours; 75% of delays had a reason documented. FBC, U&E and LFTs done in 84%, TFTs and haematinics 79%, lipids and calcium 74%, HbA1c and prolactin 63%, glucose 53%. Vitamin D checked in 68%; all with significant deficiency had loading doses but only 50% with mild deficiency were prescribed vitamin D. Of discharged patients with significant deficiency, 75% had ongoing supplementation and none had a calcium re-check plan on the discharge letter.

result.other_findings: Vitamin D status: 23% sufficient, 31% mild deficiency, 54% significant deficiency. Follow-up after loading dose therapy was poor.

result.topic: Physical health checks in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Pine Ward, 17-bed male low-secure inpatient forensic psychiatric ward, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local Trust guidance: mandatory ALL-Physical Health Assessment on admission and six-monthly thereafter (14 categories)

cycle1.result: 76.4% of patients had an ALL done; 67.2% of completions green, 15.5% amber, 17.2% red. QRISK 70%, alcohol 58%, diet 82%, exercise 70%, diabetic status 58%, smoking 76% documented.

cycle2.result: 15/17 (88%) had an ALL in the last 6 months; 89.9% of completions green, 4.6% amber, 5.5% red. QRISK, alcohol, diet and exercise 100% documented; diabetic status 82%, smoking 88%.

result.other_findings: Some ALL categories were still not completed to the expected standard; authors recommend raising the importance of the assessment with trainees.

result.setting: International pancreatic anastomosis registry (PARANOIA) led from University Hospitals of Birmingham

cycle1.result: 232 surgeons across 56 countries registered 776 cases. 70.5% reported no POPF; 8.4% had CR-POPF. Reduced CR-POPF associated with stent (p=0.008), autologous barrier (p=0.012) and somatostatin analogue (p=0.049).

result.other_findings: Open surgery in 89.7%; end-to-side anastomosis 88.8%, invagination 69% vs duct-to-mucosa 31%; drains used by 97.8%. Surgeons receive risk-adjusted CUSUM plots to benchmark against peers.

result.topic: Polypharmacy and drug interactions in older psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Cherry Ward, old age psychiatric unit, Highbury Hospital, Nottingham
result.standard: King's Fund report criteria for problematic polypharmacy; Medscape and BNF drug interaction tools

cycle1.dates: Admissions in 2018, reviewed January to May 2019
cycle1.result: On discharge 69.7% (30 patients) met criteria for higher risk of polypharmacy. 31/43 had at least one interaction; 18.6% (8 patients) had at least one potentially severe interaction.

result.other_findings: One patient became higher risk during admission and two stepped down. Authors recommend an automated electronic system to flag problematic polypharmacy and severe interactions.

result.topic: Serotonin syndrome risk from prescribing combinations
result.setting: Secondary care pain clinic

cycle1.dates: Patients seen within the last year
cycle1.result: 28 patients (28.8%) had at-risk medication combinations: 5 on SSRI and TCA, 2 on TCA and TeCA, 4 on other antidepressant pairs, 3 on fentanyl patches plus an antidepressant, 14 on an antidepressant plus tramadol.

result.other_findings: None of the patients were diagnosed with serotonin syndrome; it was unclear whether milder symptoms occurred.

result.topic: Resident doctor engagement in quality improvement
result.setting: Quality Improvement and Innovation Team, South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: Psychiatry Silver Guide: trainees supported to be involved in one QI project and/or audit per year

cycle1.result: 42% of respondents not involved in QI projects; of those involved, 65% had no QII team involvement and 35% had QII oversight. 0 resident doctor projects actively progressing on the QII caseload.

result.intervention: Streamline QI cohort programme with bespoke QI teaching and coaching through a group project (refined over 2023-2025), an SpR special interest role to support residents, targeted advertising of QI training, and circulation of trust criteria for QI project endorsement.

cycle2.result: 40% not involved in QI projects; of those involved, 100% had QII oversight. QII caseload had 8 active resident doctor projects and 9 enrolled in Streamline QI.

result.other_findings: Feedback from all three Streamline QI cohorts was unanimously positive. Next change ideas are a monthly QI project idea clinic and QI training at induction.

result.topic: Diabetes care processes in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: General, forensic and learning disability inpatient wards of a mental health hospital
result.standard: JBDS-IP and Royal College of Psychiatrists 2017 guidance: use inpatient psychiatric admission to complete the 9 NICE diabetic care processes, with a named staff member responsible

cycle1.result: None of the 18 diabetic inpatients had a care processes review documented; none had a foot check or urinary albumin during admission; less than 15% had a documented retinal screening plan. One ward had a named responsible staff member. 6/9 care processes were completed in more than 75% of patients.

result.intervention: Posters, teaching at junior and consultant level, documentation templates, and wards nominating a staff member to review care processes. Re-audit organised.
result.other_findings: Diabetic patients made up 14% of inpatients. The centre was not compliant with the guideline.

result.setting: Inpatient wards D15, D17 and D27 referring to liaison psychiatry, City Hospital (Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust)
result.standard: Liaison referral pathway and NHS England guidelines on referral structure to liaison services

cycle1.result: 77.8% (n=14) had insufficient presenting complaint; 22.2% (n=4) no past psychiatric history; 94.4% (n=17) insufficient MSE; 83.3% (n=15) no appropriate risk assessment; 27.8% (n=5) no drug/alcohol history; 22.2% (n=4) patients had not consented to referral.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest a knowledge and confidence gap among non-psychiatric trainees in psychiatric history, risk assessment and MSE.

result.setting: Choice appointments, CAMHS South Edinburgh
result.standard: Standards derived from the CAPA Book and CAMHS South Choice Handbook (12 letter content and process standards, including maximum two sides of A4 and sent within two weeks)

cycle1.result: Current concerns 92%, background 96%, patient goals 40%, clinician impression 62%, choices discussed 22%, choices made 100%, self-help agreed 52%, services required 100%, maximum two sides of A4 50%, copy to patient 88%, copy to referrer 100%, sent within two weeks 72%.

result.intervention: Additional Choice training, electronic canned text for letters and collation of Choice guidance. Re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: 94 different resources were shared, from 0 to 19 per letter, suggesting variable individualisation.

result.setting: Inpatients with bipolar affective disorder, DHQ Hospital, Faisalabad (tertiary care)
result.standard: NICE guidelines on pre-prescription evaluation and treatment monitoring for valproate

cycle1.result: 3/18 (16%) had baseline weight; 6 (33%) had FBC and LFTs during treatment.

result.intervention: Results discussed at departmental meeting; faculty-led presentation and targeted training for residents on monitoring guidelines.

cycle2.result: 20 (80%) had baseline weight; 18 (72%) had recommended blood tests during treatment.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Ethnicity recording in mental health services
result.setting: East Lancashire Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services, all open cases across three localities
result.standard: Original 2020 audit standards: complete ethnicity recording and service users' ethnic composition reflecting the local under-18 population

cycle1.result: Ethnicity recording completeness approximately 78%; Asian service users significantly under-represented.

cycle2.result: Ethnicity recording completeness approximately 88%. Access rates for Asian children about 2-5 vs 12-18 per 1,000 for non-Asian children; observed Asian numbers significantly lower than expected (p < 0.001).

result.other_findings: Improved data quality has not translated into equitable access; Asian children remain under-represented in all localities.

result.setting: Adult community mental health team, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE standards for clinical review and physical health monitoring of ADHD drug treatment

cycle1.result: 17.2% waiting for initiation and 12.7% in initiation phase; annual blood pressure monitoring 62.0%, annual weight 56.7%; longest wait for initiation 330 days; median initiation phase 92 days.

result.intervention: Staff resources reallocated to create a dedicated ADHD clinic with a new process for initiation and shared-care monitoring.

cycle2.result: Keyworker allocated 99.7%, diagnosis recorded 99.1%; 12.5% waiting and 20.8% in initiation phase; annual blood pressure 90.4%, annual weight 80.3%; longest wait 125 days; median initiation phase 62 days.

result.other_findings: Reviews offered to over 90% of monitored patients but not all; 6-monthly monitoring improved less than 12-monthly. Shared-care requests accepted by GPs increased substantially. Data also collected at 3 months.

result.setting: GP eating disorder referrals to CAMHS, East Renfrewshire
result.standard: RCPsych Junior MARSIPAN and NICE eating disorder guidance: GP referrals should contain information allowing risk assessment and prioritisation

cycle1.result: Weight 25%, weight loss 50%, calorie intake 37.5%, fluid intake 12.5%, heart rate 0%, blood pressure 12%, mental health 62%, compensatory behaviours 12.5%, bloods 25%.

result.intervention: Referral pro forma developed and circulated to East Renfrewshire GP practices in August 2021.

cycle2.result: Weight 100%, weight loss 50%, calorie intake 25%, fluid intake 25%, heart rate 25%, blood pressure 50%, mental health 100%, compensatory behaviours 75%, bloods 50%.

result.other_findings: Cumulative percentage of information included rose from 26% to 55%. Calorie intake documentation fell.

result.setting: Forensic inpatient unit, Royal Cornhill Hospital, NHS Grampian
result.standard: National standards: Extended Discharge Document issued within 7-14 days of discharge

cycle1.result: 8/41 eligible discharges had a completed EDD (19.5%); 1 of these (12.5%) was delayed beyond 14 days.

result.intervention: Each EDD assigned to a named doctor at discharge planning, standards reinforced at induction for rotating trainees, and a shared forensic handover template (digital and paper) to track outstanding EDDs.

cycle2.result: 22/27 completed (81.5%); completion above 75% every month and 100% in January. 16/22 (72.7%) issued more than 14 days after discharge.

result.other_findings: Timeliness remained the key concern; early drafting, timeliness checkpoints and automated reminders proposed for the next cycle.

result.setting: Adult inpatient psychiatry ward, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines for monitoring patients on long-term antipsychotics (14 standards: BMI, ECG, blood pressure, lipids, prolactin, U&E at baseline, set time points and dose changes)

cycle1.result: 5 standards attained, 7 not attained, 1 only partially analysable and 1 (12-month monitoring) not analysable due to length of stay.

result.intervention: None reported; recommendations were an admission proforma, a reminder tool for 3, 6 and 12-month rechecks, and regular ECG machine maintenance.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: North Staffordshire Combined Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: Trust Seclusion Policy and Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice

cycle1.result: Incident forms completed in 83%, de-escalation attempted in 87%; NEWS incomplete in 82% at initiation. Doctor notified in all but one case (67% within 30 minutes); 100% had medical review, 39% within one hour and 29% after 120 minutes. Internal and external MDTs in 63% and 72%; 11% had neither. Termination reasons reported in 91%.

result.intervention: None reported yet; recommendations in progress include staff training, policy updates, automated reminders, enhanced documentation, non-touch NEWS and virtual MDT meetings, to be monitored at re-audit.
result.other_findings: Timing of Site Manager notification unclear in 93.5%. Night-time reviews suspended in 14 cases, 10 because the patient was asleep.

result.setting: Outpatient clinics of a mental health service

cycle1.result: 35 (30.7%) had psychiatric diagnoses in the designated place in the ECR (97.4% had them elsewhere in the record); 15 (13.2%) had physical diagnoses. Mean psychiatric diagnoses 0.7±1.4, physical 0.3±0.9.

result.intervention: Project team reviewed and updated psychiatric and physical diagnoses in the ECR, including physical diagnoses taken from GP records.

cycle2.result: Mean psychiatric diagnoses 1.0±1.3 (p<0.001) and physical 1.1±1.4 (p<0.001); physical diagnoses updated in 43 (37.7%). Four-character ICD codes rose from 28.9% to 86.8% (p<0.01).

result.other_findings: Additional psychiatric diagnoses could be entered for 83 (72.8%); 55 physical diagnoses were taken from GP records for 28 (24.6%) patients.

result.topic: Admission physical examination, ECG and bloods in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Park House inpatient unit, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: Local priority: initial physical examination, admission bloods and ECG completed and documented on the PHIT tool in PARIS

cycle1.result: 73% had an initial physical examination, 84% admission bloods and 74% admission ECG; recording on the PHIT tool was 33-42%. Valid refusal reason documented in 63-91% of refusals.

result.intervention: Interventions developed to increase completion and documentation (not detailed); PHIT completion now monitored regularly. Re-audit underway.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Collateral history taking in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Two adult and one functional old age acute inpatient wards, Leicestershire Partnership NHS Trust
result.standard: Collateral history taken within the first 14 days of admission

cycle1.result: 33% had a collateral history within 14 days; where omitted, 10% attempted and 46% planned.

result.intervention: Questionnaire and two junior doctor focus groups to explore barriers; COVID-19 visiting restrictions lifted before re-audit. No practice change reported between cycles.

cycle2.result: 38% had a collateral history within 14 days; where omitted, 13% attempted and 27% planned.
