result.other_findings: Barriers included consent, access to contact details, confidence, unclear responsibility, lack of time and space and documentation. Planned actions: induction and bitesize teaching, a ward crib sheet and re-audit in November 2023.

result.setting: Rheumatology outpatient clinics (general and specialist CTD service), Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BSR national Lupus audit standards (11 standards) based on BSR Lupus guidelines

cycle1.result: 5/11 audit standards met.

result.intervention: Nurse education and urine testing added to the clinic observation form; electronic SLE review form and electronic SLEDAI score introduced.

cycle2.result: 4/11 standards met across all clinics; 9/11 in the specialist clinic. Urine testing rose from 22% (2020) to 90%. When the SLE review form was used, all standards were met apart from lipid testing and pregnancy discussion (79% vs standard 80%).

result.other_findings: Intermediate 2020 cycle (119 patients over 12 months) met 3/11 standards. SLEDAI assessment and lipid monitoring remain focus areas.

result.setting: Inpatients on clozapine across a mental health trust
result.standard: Local trust guidance: bowel habits monitored regularly, at least at every blood (FBC) sampling

cycle1.result: 54.8% (17) had bowel habits monitored at least with every FBC (range 0% to 100% between wards). 87.1% (27) had at least one regular or PRN laxative; 61.2% (19) regular laxatives; 25.8% (8) PRN only, of whom 50% (4) ever used it.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend a standard trust-wide bowel monitoring method and a trust laxative prescribing policy.

result.setting: 14-bed specialist dementia ward for severe BPSD
result.standard: NICE dementia guidance: structured assessment, psychosocial interventions first line, antipsychotics second line for shortest time and reassessed at least every 6 weeks

cycle1.result: Mean psychotropics per patient 2.30 on admission, 2.30 at midpoint and 2.05 at discharge. Mean diazepam equivalent fell from 3.20 mg to 2.10 mg; mean haloperidol equivalent rose from 1.11 mg to 2.27 mg at midpoint then fell to 0.78 mg at discharge.

result.other_findings: 95% were admitted under the Mental Health Act. Patients had structured assessment and regular medicines reconciliation supervised by the team pharmacist.

result.topic: ECT missed seizures and stimulus dosing
result.setting: ECT clinic, Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NHFT ECT protocol: titrate dose per stimulus dosing protocol during seizure-threshold determination; restimulate with 10% dose increase in treatment phase

cycle1.result: Missed seizure rate 12.6%; restimulation rate 67.5%. Correct dosing in seizure-threshold phase 36%; after threshold established 84% received the same or slightly higher dose; 2/3 treatment-phase restimulation doses suboptimally increased.

result.intervention: Staff training, discussions and display of dose charts.

cycle2.result: 210 bilateral ECT treatments to 22 patients. Missed seizure rate 11.6%; restimulation rate 81.5%. Correct dosing in seizure-threshold phase 88%; full compliance with dosing protocol after threshold and with 10% increase for all treatment-phase restimulations.

result.other_findings: Of 27 missed seizures, 19 were in the threshold phase (17 restimulated) and 8 in the treatment phase (5 restimulated). Protocol documentation improved markedly.

result.topic: Driving advice documentation in eating disorders
result.setting: North Yorkshire and York CAMHS Eating Disorder Service, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local audit standards aligned with DVLA/regional guidance: driving status documented at initial assessment, DVLA notification advice and follow-up driving safety advice documented

cycle1.result: Driving status documented at initial assessment in 0/48; any driving safety advice in 33.3% (16/48). Of these, follow-up advice 93.8% (15/16), advice aligned with DVLA/NHS guidance 100% (16/16), explicit DVLA notification advice 43.8% (7/16).

result.intervention: Revised initial assessment pro forma with a structured Driving Status and Advice section and a clinic poster; patient leaflet and updated follow-up template in progress.
result.other_findings: Where advice was documented its quality and follow-up were high.

result.setting: Junior doctor handover, Tyrone and Fermanagh Hospital (multi-site psychiatric inpatient hospital), Northern Ireland

cycle1.result: Password protection used in 69%; other baseline figures not reported.

result.intervention: New handover template with prompts for staff, date and key patient information, emailed to doctors on the rota and highlighted at changeover.

cycle2.result: Staff identification 98% and shift date 99%; password use 91%. Improvements in patient initials (29.4%), health and care number (9.2%), MHO status (15.46%), patient summary (19.76%), working diagnosis (34.91%) and an 88.74% increase in identifying who follows up outstanding tasks.

result.other_findings: Further changes proposed: adjusting template prompts and a secure folder for storing handover.

result.setting: CAMHS services across Lincolnshire
result.standard: National guidelines on melatonin use (audit inspired by the POMH melatonin audit)

cycle1.result: Non-pharmacological measures tried first in 84.6%; target symptom clear in 55.6%; licensed preparation in 46.3%. Efficacy reviewed within 3 months in 86.7% and tolerability in 46.7%; annual review of need in 80.8% and tolerability in 30.8%.

result.other_findings: About half had been on melatonin for over a year; preparation was not clearly documented in most cases.

result.setting: Psychiatry Department, Allied-2 Hospital, Faisalabad
result.standard: Structured checklist based on Royal College of Physicians guidelines; 100% compliance as gold standard

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 47.5%. Admission and discharge dates, final diagnosis, treatment review and discharge medications 100%; patient identifiers 98.75%. Presenting complaint 0%, mental state at discharge 0%, risk assessment 1.25%, counselling 1.25%, typed/legible 0%.

result.intervention: None reported; recommended electronic discharge summaries, standardised templates with mandatory psychiatric sections, counselling protocols and staff training.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Admission physical examination, ECG and bloods in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: 12 general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines and Trust physical health policy: physical examination and assessment within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Within 24 hours: FBC 46%, U&E 45%, LFTs 44%, TFTs 40%, bone profile 44%, B12 38%, folate 37%, prolactin 33%, HbA1c 39%, cholesterol 43%, ECG 47%, urine dipstick 28%, pregnancy test 23% of eligible females, QRISK 2% of applicable patients.

result.other_findings: Authors call for greater medical and nursing awareness of admission physical health investigations.

result.topic: Lifestyle and wellbeing advice in depression
result.setting: Older People's Service North community mental health team, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE depression guidance: advise regular physical activity and a healthy lifestyle to improve wellbeing

cycle1.result: Physical activity advice documented in 35% (11); healthy lifestyle advice in 42% (13).

result.intervention: Action plan including staff education and a patient information leaflet. Re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: Doctors performed worst compared with care coordinators and health support workers.

result.setting: 16 erectile dysfunction services across the North West of England (regional multicentre audit)
result.standard: EAU Guidelines on Male Sexual Dysfunction 2012: detailed medical history and clinical examination in all patients

cycle1.dates: Last 20 new referrals retrospectively from end of 2011
cycle1.result: Diabetes 99.6%, hypertension 41.8%, cardiovascular disease 22.2%, hyperlipidaemia 28.5%, smoking 89.1%, alcohol 83.3%. IIEF 32%, orgasm 39.3%, ejaculation 53.1%. Examination: genitalia 85.4%, blood pressure 74.9%, secondary sexual characteristics 41%, BMI 77.4%, peripheral pulses 56.5%.

result.intervention: None reported; recommended a specific pro forma and dedicated andrology clinics.
result.other_findings: Duration, rigidity, longevity, spontaneous erections, intercourse and libido documented in about 89-97%.

result.topic: Eating disorder management on general psychiatric wards
result.setting: Inpatient general adult psychiatry ward
result.standard: NICE guidelines and MEED (Medical Emergencies in Eating Disorders) guidelines

cycle1.result: Gaps between evidence-based practice and care; a substantial number of patients admitted with eating concerns had no eating disorder diagnosis on discharge, and those with a primary eating disorder had limited specialist inreach support. No compliance percentages reported.

result.other_findings: Audit also gathered qualitative data on MDT perceptions, knowledge and attitudes.

result.setting: 16-bed male medium secure rehabilitation ward, Cumbria Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: E-cigarette and smoking history was not recorded.

result.intervention: Standardised smoking/vaping history and dependence checklists adapted for the setting and used for new admissions; existing patients interviewed retrospectively.

cycle2.result: Both new admissions had a thorough smoking and vaping history documented.

result.other_findings: Of 13 patients assessed, all had smoked, 10/13 had used e-cigarettes (mostly starting in hospital or prison) and eight had high e-cigarette dependence; most had no health concerns about vaping.

result.setting: 7th National Audit Project of the Royal College of Anaesthetists: activity survey and one-year peri-operative cardiac arrest registry across participating UK sites
result.standard: Current guidance: CPR should usually be attempted for cardiac arrest during anaesthesia and pre-existing DNACPR recommendations should be suspended

cycle1.dates: Activity survey over four days per site; one-year case registry
cycle1.result: 595 (3%) of 20,717 adults had a pre-operative DNACPR recommendation, of which 175 (29%) were suspended. Of 881 peri-operative cardiac arrests, 54 (6%) had a pre-operative DNACPR; 25 (46%) of these were formally suspended.

result.other_findings: Of arrest patients with DNACPR, 38 (70%) had clinical frailty scale 5 or more; ROSC achieved in 57% and one in five survived to leave hospital.

result.setting: Head and neck and upper GI cancer pathways, Belfast City Hospital
result.standard: NHS England 62-day referral to treatment standard; NICE: urgent OGD for dysphagia and barium swallow not first line

cycle1.result: Of 348 oesophageal cancers, 14 cervical cases; 9 analysed. 6/9 first referred to ENT. 4/9 had OGD, 5/9 barium swallow (4/5 as first-line) and 7/9 rigid oesophagoscopy. Median GP referral to treatment 108 days vs 62-day standard.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend direct visualisation of the oesophagus for red flag dysphagia regardless of whether assessed by head and neck or upper GI pathway.

result.setting: Rampton Hospital (high secure psychiatric hospital)
result.standard: HDAT monitoring guidelines (CSM/MHRA and Royal College of Psychiatrists): bloods, physical observations and ECG after every dose escalation and every 6 months; consent and reasons for HDAT documented

cycle1.result: Quarterly blood and ECG monitoring 8% to 23%; yearly TFTs 88% and prolactin 72%; quarterly physical observations 77% (regular HDAT) and 77% (including PRN).

cycle2.result: Quarterly bloods about 50-60% and quarterly ECG about 40%; yearly TFTs 100% and prolactin 71%; quarterly physical observations 100% (regular HDAT) and 81% (including PRN). Consent forms completed for all; reasons documented in 85% (regular) and 100% (including PRN).

result.other_findings: 6% of patients received HDAT in 2018. Prescribers were informed of results and a further re-audit was planned for 2021-22.

result.setting: Intensive care unit of a general hospital
result.standard: Trust guidance on delirium screening (CAM-ICU), documentation and management

cycle1.result: 20/81 had delirium. CAM-ICU documentation incorrect in 25% of these; behaviour monitored in 15%; 0% had a complete This is me document; sensory aids unavailable for 50%. Delirium formally diagnosed in 40%, type documented in 15%; 8 had a specific management plan; non-pharmacological management not documented.

result.other_findings: Length of stay 20% longer in patients with delirium; 5 of 10 ICU deaths were in patients with delirium. Authors recommend education and review of haloperidol/lorazepam use in ICU.

result.setting: East Sussex Rehabilitation Pathway community rehabilitation team, Eastbourne, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: SPFT HDAT physical health monitoring policy and RCPsych consensus statement on HDAT monitoring

cycle1.result: Blood tests and weight/physical observations 45%; ECG 27%; GASS offered 27%; HDAT documentation fully up to date 36%.

result.intervention: Findings presented to the MDT and an action plan formulated; re-audit planned in six months.
result.other_findings: HDAT affected about 18% of the caseload; 73% were on two antipsychotics and 27% on three.

result.setting: Two older people's mental health inpatient wards, Auckland Park Hospital

cycle1.result: Choice and dose within recommendations in all cases. Baseline NEWS observations in all; full post-RT observations at correct intervals in 33% (refusals documented). De-escalation documented and post-RT debrief in 100%; medication review post-RT in 66%.

result.other_findings: 33% had a raised NEWS after RT, resolving spontaneously; no documented side effects.

result.topic: Psychotropic prescribing for challenging behaviour in intellectual disability
result.setting: Intellectual disability team, large acute mental health trust
result.standard: NICE and STOMP guidelines for pharmacological management of challenging behaviour in intellectual disability

cycle1.result: Risk assessment 68%; description of target behaviour 74%; metabolic monitoring 0%; documentation of interventions 48%; mental health evaluation 87%, physical health 61%; consent 19%; side-effect discussion 32%; 6-week efficacy review 52%; single drug therapy 19%.

cycle2.result: Risk assessment 100%; description of target behaviour 100%; metabolic monitoring 95%; documentation of interventions 86%; mental health evaluation 60%, physical health 60%; consent 46%; side-effect discussion 50%; 6-week efficacy review 50%; single drug therapy 34%; positive behaviour support plan 75%.

result.other_findings: Intermediate 2014 cycle (n=17): risk assessment 94%, consent 76%, 6-week review 65%. Outpatient-dependent standards were affected by service changes and COVID-19; pharmacy-led reviews suggested.

result.setting: GP monitoring under ADHD shared care, patients due annual structured review with a specialist ADHD team
result.standard: NICE and shared care guidelines: blood pressure, pulse and weight monitored by the GP at least twice a year (every 6 months)

cycle1.dates: Patients due review August and September 2023
cycle1.result: Blood pressure within 6 months 22/22 (100%), within 1 year 19/22 (86%); pulse 20/22 (90%) and 18/22 (81%); weight 21/22 (95%) and 20/22 (90%).

result.intervention: Letter sent to GP practices commending the result and recommending flagging a review for weight loss of 10% or more within 12 months.
result.other_findings: 8 of 22 had a significant blood pressure change as defined by NICE (increase of 2-4 mmHg).

result.topic: Nicotine replacement therapy in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Four Mid-Essex general adult inpatient wards, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: EPUT nicotine prescribing guidelines and British Thoracic Society recommended dual NRT regimen; documentation of smoking status and cessation plans

cycle1.result: 57% were smokers and 72% of smokers used vapes. None were on dual NRT; no cessation plans for anyone using NRT. 75% had a documented discussion about smoking and nicotine use, not all including NRT options.

result.intervention: None reported; recommendations include asking all patients about smoking status, early dual NRT, documenting vaping, cessation plans in physical health checks and a dual NRT prescribing bundle. Follow-up audit in 4-5 months recommended.
result.other_findings: Most patients relied solely on short-acting NRT such as vapes and inhalators; vaping was poorly documented.

result.topic: Depot antipsychotic relapse prevention and side effect monitoring
result.setting: Older adults (over 65) on depot/LAI antipsychotics, pan-trust, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: POMH-UK (relapse prevention) and NICE CG178 (side effect assessment)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Crisis plan in care plan 89.7%; plan for defaulting 34.3%; review of therapeutic response 90.7%; patient involvement in care plan 89.7% (all improved). Care plan accessible 98.3%, relapse signature documented 39.7%, annual review by prescribing team 72.9% (all decreased). Side effects assessed in last 12 months 76.2%; identified side effects followed by change of plan 90%.

result.other_findings: Cycle 2 was pan-trust, which may explain some decreases. EPSE was the most common side effect.

result.setting: General adult psychiatry, Royal Cornhill Hospital

cycle1.result: CDDs: average time saved 13 minutes 13 seconds per case (75.3%). EDDs: average time saved 26 minutes 22 seconds per case (76.7%); largest saving 33 minutes 34 seconds (about 79.9%).

result.intervention: Copilot AI agent used to generate discharge documents compared with manual writing.
result.other_findings: Errors came from incomplete source records and medication changes not reflected in TrakCare; no errors were due to AI hallucination.

result.setting: Weekly MRCPsych core trainee teaching, HPFT

cycle1.result: 50% (n=10) preferred online, 45% (n=9) hybrid, 5% (n=1) in-person. Barriers: parking 70% (n=14), clinical responsibilities 50% (n=10).

result.intervention: Specific neuroscience teaching introduced, small exam-specific study groups encouraged, hybrid format retained.

cycle2.result: 50% (n=11) preferred online, 41% (n=9) and 9% (n=2) other formats as reported. Barriers: parking 64% (n=14), clinical responsibilities 55% (n=12). Neuroscience teaching reported as improved.

result.other_findings: Flexible teaching format continued.

result.topic: Admission physical examination, ECG and bloods in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Samphire ward, acute inpatient unit, Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NSFT Physical Healthcare Policy (C84): baseline bloods, physical examination and ECG within 24 hours of admission; 100% compliance

cycle1.result: Physical examination or documented refusal 34.5%; ECG or refusal 53%; bloods or refusal 68%, correct bloods 4.5%; all three components 0%.

result.intervention: A3 visual aid placed on the ward.

cycle2.result: Physical examination 47%; ECG 61%; bloods 71%, correct bloods 33%; all three components 33%.

result.other_findings: Ward doctors adhered to the standard significantly more than duty doctors. Induction teaching and a wider re-audit (VTE, height/weight, nursing elements) recommended.

result.setting: Rheumatology department, North Bristol NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Mean referral to specialist review 2.7 days; temporal artery biopsy 41%.

result.intervention: Twice-weekly registrar-led hot clinics, ad hoc slots in on-call consultant clinics for GCA referrals, and increased vascular ultrasound capacity during the pandemic.

cycle2.result: Mean referral to specialist review 1.6 days; all had vascular ultrasound; temporal artery biopsy 7.5%. 33% diagnosed and treated as GCA.

result.other_findings: 75% of referrals came from primary care. Planned improvements: steroid advice at referral, updated primary care guideline on urgent ophthalmology input, and a GCA review proforma.

result.setting: Postgraduate psychiatry teaching across three sites in North Wales
result.standard: Deanery/HEIW local teaching requirements and MRCPsych Handbook

cycle1.result: Consistent formal teaching was not provided and the programme did not meet deanery criteria; teaching had worsened over time.

result.intervention: New postgraduate teaching programme developed through PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 31 consultants rated the new programme 4.23/5; 31 non-consultants rated it 3.68/4 and 95% said it covered core trainee requirements.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Intellectual disability services, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
result.standard: NICE and RCPsych ADHD medication prescription guidance; 100% of patients with all audit tool components documented

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Blood pressure/pulse recorded in 84%; height/weight/BMI in 81%; symptom severity, dose, side effects, need for ongoing treatment and review frequency recorded in 97%.

result.other_findings: Significant improvement compared with the previous cycle; physical health monitoring remains the weakest area.

result.topic: CAMHS to adult mental health transition
result.setting: Transition service from CAMHS to adult mental health services

cycle1.result: Good compliance with most NICE standards (coordinated transition plan, named worker, meeting a practitioner from each adult service) except Standard 1 on age at transition planning; most transitioned at 17 years 11 months as a named worker was identified only a month before 18.

result.other_findings: Only 3 needed brief admission; two stayed with CAMHS after 18 as they did not meet adult criteria. Severe anorexia nervosa and possible autism were hardest to engage.

result.setting: National primary care data (ECLIPSE database, 2400 general practices in England)
result.standard: BSR PMR guidelines: glucocorticoids for one to two years with taper; cumulative thresholds 0-6 months >2100mg, 7-12 months >1400mg, 13-18 and 19-24 months >910mg

cycle1.result: A considerable number of patients were prescribed glucocorticoids above recommended levels (figures given in a table not supplied).

result.other_findings: PMR prevalence in over-50s was 0.99% nationally, 1.00% in East of England and 1.5% in Norfolk and Waveney.

result.setting: General adult inpatient units across four localities, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Professional Record Standards Body and RCPsych guidelines on discharge summary availability, timeliness and content

cycle1.result: 28/148 (18.9%) had no completed discharge summary, 14 (9.4%) of whom were out-of-locality patients. Mean time from discharge to summary availability 12.7 days. Most summaries contained all relevant information.

result.intervention: None reported yet; recommendations: bed management to notify parent teams promptly, medical secretaries to monitor admissions register and prompt juniors, and business intelligence monthly reports of missing summaries. Re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: Findings presented to the Trust QI committee to guide a harmonised trust policy.

result.setting: Patients referred for transcranial magnetic stimulation with treatment-resistant depression

cycle1.result: 70% did not follow NICE guidelines for depression management. Mean interval between first and second antidepressant 46 days; mean interval from second antidepressant to TMS about 751 days.

result.other_findings: 21/50 (42%) had comorbid psychiatric disorders. Many remained on ineffective regimens beyond recommended durations in both primary and secondary care.

result.setting: Ritson Outreach drug and alcohol service for general psychiatric wards, Royal Edinburgh Hospital
result.standard: Team-agreed referral criteria and referral detail standards; target 90% of referrals appropriate and containing relevant details by March 2025

cycle1.result: Ward 100%, referrer 100%, contact number 55%, reason for admission 60%, specific request 55%, community addictions input 30%, patient aware 20%, patient's views 40%, drug screen 5%, estimated discharge date 5%; appropriate 55%.

result.intervention: Referral form with criteria and prompts, sent via automatic reply from the referral email address.

cycle2.result: Ward 100%, referrer 100%, contact number 100%, reason for admission 80%, specific request 100%, community addictions input 80%, patient aware 60%, patient's views 60%, drug screen 20%, estimated discharge date 40%; appropriate 80%.

result.other_findings: Only 10% of surveyed staff on the highest-referring ward felt confident about referral criteria before the form. The 90% target was not yet met; posters and induction teaching planned.

result.setting: Liaison psychiatry department, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford (tertiary centre)
result.standard: NCEPOD Treat as One (2017) recommendations for documentation of liaison psychiatry reviews (12-item audit tool)

cycle1.result: Primary diagnosis 77.9%, reason for referral 66.3%, mental capacity 19.8%, need for DoLS 2.3%, risks 27.9%, risk management 7%. Clear numbered plan 61.6%, medication changes 51.4%, useful plan 73%, answered referral question 69.8%, action points assigned 47.7%, non-medical MDT advice 18.6%.

result.intervention: Electronic documentation template based on the NCEPOD recommendations, implemented for all initial liaison reviews. Re-audit planned for March 2020.
result.other_findings: Main areas agreed for improvement: risk documentation, medication changes, assigning action points and advice for non-medical MDT members.

result.topic: Physical health workload of psychiatry trainees
result.setting: The Mount, older adult mental health unit, Leeds

cycle1.result: Foundation doctors and core trainees spent at least half their time on physical health work.

result.other_findings: Trainees sometimes missed MDTs, tribunals and CPAs due to physical health workload. Suggestions included senior GP or geriatric input, phlebotomy support, digital charts and clarity on minimum staffing.

result.topic: Mental health triage proforma use in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department, Royal Cornwall Hospital (patients referred to psychiatric liaison)
result.standard: RCEM recommendation to use a mental health proforma in line with NCEPOD Treat as One; local Mental Health Triage Form

cycle1.result: Mental Health Triage Form used in 44/125 (35%); 15 (12%) had missing ED documentation. Where used, an average 25% increase in information recorded.

result.other_findings: Form use fell from 46% in June 2020 to 35% in June 2021. Triage code questions improved most when the form was used.

result.setting: Local ADHD care pathway, North Staffordshire Combined Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: Local Trust ADHD pathway based on NICE NG87 (2018): eligibility, assessment, outcome measures, medication initiation and ESCA, risk assessment, safety planning and follow-up

cycle1.result: All met eligibility and had a keyworker. Initial ReQoL 64% (50/78); holistic assessment 88% (69/78); care plans 100% but only 49% with DIALOG and Goal-Based Outcomes; risk assessment 99% (77/78); safety plans 76% (59/78). Medication initiated in 76/78 with ESCA sent for 62; all had 6-monthly reviews.

result.other_findings: Deprescribing or medication holiday discussions documented in only three cases; four ESCA requests rejected by the same GP practice.

result.topic: Pregnancy and contraception discussions with women on antipsychotics
result.setting: PATH early intervention in psychosis service, Hertfordshire

cycle1.result: 34/177 (19%) asked about pregnancy plans; 28/177 (16%) given contraception advice. Of 27 with pregnancy plans, 15 (56%) offered perinatal team referral and 12 (44%) given advice on antipsychotic risks in pregnancy.

result.intervention: Pregnancy information added to the service leaflet, pregnancy and contraception prompts embedded in the Trust Physical Health Assessment document, and topics added to PATH physical health training.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Central Aberdeenshire Community Mental Health Team, new GP referrals of older adults
result.standard: Documented intervention to review or mitigate anticholinergic medication when ACB score is 3 or more

cycle1.result: 73% on at least one anticholinergic; 32.7% (N=69) had ACB 3 or more. 75.4% of these had no documented intervention; deprescribing 8.7%, dose reduction 8.7%, medical review suggested 4.4%, switch 2.9%.

result.intervention: None reported yet; recommended routine ACB calculation at assessment, prompted medication review for ACB 3 or more and targeted education. Re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: ACB 3 or more in 63.9% of those on eight or more medicines vs 11.8% on fewer than five. Documented interventions had declined compared with previous local audits.

result.setting: East Lancashire Memory Assessment Service, Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Estimated NHS outpatient non-attendance rate of 7.6% (comparator)

cycle1.result: 4 DNAs among 3 patients out of 99 appointments offered; DNA rate 4%. No DNAs for medication monitoring appointments.

result.other_findings: Telephone reminders 48 hours before appointments were offered to most patients and often led to rescheduling. Recorded reasons for DNA were transport and acute hospital admission.

result.setting: Chorley Mental Health Inpatient Unit, Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust (psychiatric inpatient wards)
result.standard: 20-item list of expected clerking components based on trust guidelines

cycle1.result: Highest completion: clerking within 6 hours, consultant face-to-face review within a week and current medication documentation. Lowest completion: clinical impression, bloods within 24 hours, capacity assessment and smoking/substance history (no percentages given).

result.intervention: Planned: standardised capacity assessment documentation and a clerking checklist; results presented at local teaching and recommendations sent to Site Tutors for local inductions.
result.other_findings: Poorer clerkings were linked to poor patient engagement and transfer from another ward. A survey of 8 trainees found no uniform method for capacity documentation and no official clerking checklist.

result.setting: Psychiatric Liaison Service, Queen's Hospital (NELFT), older adults over 65

cycle1.result: 47% of older adult referrals to PLS had delirium; 87% of delirium referrals needed no further PLS intervention after initial assessment; 31 delirium referrals to the Dementia and Delirium Team.

result.intervention: Simplified PLS referral form with a mandatory 4AT delirium score and mandatory referral to the Dementia and Delirium Team for positive screens (November 2023).

cycle2.result: 35% of referrals had delirium; 58% of delirium referrals needed no further PLS intervention; prior screening and referral to Dementia and Delirium Team rose by 4%; 85 delirium referrals to the Dementia and Delirium Team (174% increase).

result.other_findings: This is the first stage of a multi-phase quality improvement and service development project.

result.setting: Inner city community mental health team (CMHT) outpatient clinics
result.standard: Trust protocol: clinics cancelled only when absolutely necessary and patients informed at least 8 weeks before the appointed clinic

cycle1.result: About 54% of 193 booked clinics were cancelled (68% in September, 30.30% in August). Around 50% of patients were informed 8 weeks in advance. Causes: junior doctor on call 31.58%, annual leave 25%, study leave 21%.

result.other_findings: 72% of cancellations were by junior doctors and 28% by consultants; poor communication between clinicians and the appointment booking team was the main cause.

result.setting: North Tyneside Community Treatment Team, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear Trust
result.standard: NICE and local trust guidelines: 100% of patients on depot antipsychotics have a GASS form yearly; 100% have a GASS ever; completed GASS forms accessible on RiO

cycle1.result: 88% had a GASS in the past year; 97% of GASS recorded on RiO.

cycle2.result: 53% had a GASS completed in the past year (red); 95% had a GASS ever (green); 98% of GASS recorded on RiO (green).

result.other_findings: This was the fourth re-audit; the fall in yearly GASS completion was attributed to COVID-19 disruption of face-to-face reviews. Re-audit planned for 2024/25.

result.setting: Beechcroft, step 5 regional child and adolescent mental health inpatient unit, Belfast
result.standard: 7 criteria of necessary referral information (identifiers, referrer, location, legal status, presenting symptoms, working diagnosis, risks warranting admission)

cycle1.result: Overall 75.2% of criteria met. Identifiers and referrer 100%, presenting symptoms 95%, risks 79%, legal status 74%, location 68%, working diagnosis 11% (2/19).

result.intervention: Planned: in-hours bed manager appointed and a standardised referral proforma to be developed; re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: Working diagnosis was missing in 90% of referrals and risks or legal status missing in up to a quarter.

result.setting: Mental Health Liaison Team, Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Project aim: handover time under 30 minutes within one month and improved handover quality

cycle1.result: Average handover 44 minutes; 7 interruptions; key information available 69%; staff member allocated 80%; review date allocated 83%.

result.intervention: Two PDSA cycles guided by human factors analysis (driver diagram and change ideas), avoiding a rigid handover system; specific changes not detailed.

cycle2.result: Average handover 30 minutes; 2 interruptions; key information 92%; staff member allocated 95%; review date allocated 95%.

result.other_findings: Average patients discussed per handover unchanged (15). Burnout, understaffing and COVID-19 were key human factors; re-audit planned at 6 and 12 months.

result.setting: Three older adult psychiatric inpatient wards
result.standard: Trust Record Management Policy: 80% of entries validated, within 12 hours; GMC Good Medical Practice

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Validated entries improved on all three wards (up to 35% increase on one ward) but overall validation remained below the 80% standard; most validated entries met the 12-hour standard.

result.other_findings: Doctors were more likely to validate entries in normal working hours than out of hours. The cycle led to a wider QI project and trustwide policy change on validation.

result.topic: Timing of cholecystectomy after acute biliary admission
result.setting: Central London tertiary care centre (Guy's and St Thomas' Hospital)
result.standard: AUGIS: laparoscopic cholecystectomy on index admission for acute cholecystitis and gallstone pancreatitis, ideally within 72 hours

cycle1.result: Average waiting time to laparoscopic cholecystectomy 98.2 weeks.

result.intervention: Dedicated e-referral system for patients who did not have cholecystectomy on index admission.

cycle2.result: Average waiting time to laparoscopic cholecystectomy 47.7 weeks.

result.other_findings: Readmissions fell by 23.3% in choledocholithiasis, 17.4% biliary colic, 16.7% ascending cholangitis, 12.8% acute cholecystitis and 8.3% gallstone pancreatitis. 243 patients in total across both years.

result.topic: Dementia diagnostic assessment and post-diagnostic care
result.setting: Community Mental Health Services for Older People, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE 2018 dementia guideline and TEWV 2019 person-centred dementia care pathway

cycle1.result: Consent recorded 80%; prognosis information 47%; dementia and driving information 26%; accessible information leaflets 16%; carer's assessment offered 26%.

result.intervention: Action plans on areas needing improvement (not detailed).

cycle2.result: Consent recorded 65%; prognosis information 80%; dementia and driving 53%; accessible leaflets 50%; carer's assessment offered 18%.

result.other_findings: Carer's assessment stayed below standard in both cycles and consent recording fell. COVID-19 lockdown was thought to have limited leaflet sharing.

result.setting: All wards of a children's hospital (medical and critical care)
result.standard: Local guidelines, 100%: all patients on oxygen have a prescription, target saturations, administration device and nurse signature within last 12 hours

cycle1.result: 0/14 had an oxygen prescription (13 patients receiving oxygen reported).

result.intervention: New paediatric medication chart with an oxygen prescription section and a training package for doctors, nurses and pharmacists; awareness of initial audit results.

cycle2.result: 4/18 had an oxygen prescription (22%), all medical patients; of these target saturations 100%, device 25%, nurse signature within 12 hours 100%.

result.other_findings: No prescribing in critical care (14 patients), which had not engaged with the new chart.

result.setting: Oesophago-Gastric Anastomosis Audit: 137 hospitals in 41 countries (prospective multicentre cohort)

cycle1.result: Anastomotic leak rate 14.2% (n = 319) and conduit necrosis rate 2.7% (n = 60). CN risk score (BMI, ECOG, previous MI, smoking) validated with AUROC 0.775; AL score AUROC 0.618.

result.other_findings: Anastomotic leak was difficult to predict from preoperative factors; external validation of the CN score is needed.

result.setting: Tertiary cancer units, secondary care and community services (National Oesophagogastric Nutrition Audit survey)

cycle1.result: 77% of tertiary surgical units felt able to provide adequate post-operative nutritional care; 52% (diagnostic phase) and 67% (neoadjuvant period) disagreed they could provide adequate dietetic support.

result.other_findings: Barriers were inadequate funding, understaffing and prioritisation of inpatients; wide variation in service structure and staffing.

result.setting: Working-age adult psychiatric inpatient ward
result.standard: MDT-agreed standard for daily progress notes: clear language and information on mental state, medication, meals, physical health, personal care, activities, risks and use of leave

cycle1.result: Accessibility of information scored 1 on average (Likert +3 to -3); language scored 2; personal care information present in 17%.

result.intervention: Standards and a suggested note format emailed to staff, with follow-up meetings with individual staff and the MDT to resolve difficulties.

cycle2.result: Accessibility 3 on average; language 2; all content items increased; meals, medication and physical health present 100%; personal care 89%.

result.other_findings: Largest improvement was in personal care information (17% to 89%).

result.setting: Community Learning Disability Team psychiatry caseload, London
result.standard: Established criteria for genetic testing in unexplained moderate, severe or profound intellectual disability

cycle1.result: 39 had moderate to profound ID; 20.5% had a confirmed genetic diagnosis; genetic testing mentioned in 25.6% of those with moderate or severe ID; only one patient referred for testing by this team.

result.intervention: Planned: targeted education for the team, sharing the Clinical Genetics referral protocol and a prompt in initial assessments.
result.other_findings: Most previous genetic referrals were made under paediatric or child learning disability services.

result.setting: Adult mental health male and female acute inpatient wards, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: TEWV trust policy on regular review of anxiolytics and hypnotics

cycle1.result: Inpatient prescriptions reviewed and documented: 26% (female, 100 prescriptions) and 46% (male, 35); reviewed weekly 6% (female) and 0% (male). Documented discharge plan for benzodiazepine/z-drug review 74% (female) and 91% (male).

result.other_findings: Most prescriptions were reviewed only at discharge (71% female and 22% male discharge prescriptions changed). Weekly MDT reviews and training for doctors in training recommended.

result.setting: Two general adult Community Mental Health Teams (Recovery Team)
result.standard: NICE and Maudsley guidelines: annual FBC, U&E, eGFR, lipids, LFT, HbA1c/glucose and prolactin where required; compliance 80% or above recommended

cycle1.result: U&E 77%, glucose/HbA1c 74%, FBC and LFT ~72% (76 patients), eGFR 60%, prolactin 31% (9 patients); all below 80%.

result.intervention: Recommendations to existing monitoring services and liaison to set up a dedicated physical health clinic (recruitment under way); re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: 66% of blood tests were done in GP surgeries and 25% by mental health services.

result.setting: Paediatric inpatient wards
result.standard: Local Multidisciplinary Guidelines for Acute Pain Management in Children and Young People: all patients on opioids have PRN naloxone with correct directions

cycle1.result: Naloxone prescribed in 17% (7/41); on PRN section 100% (7/7); correct directions 86% (6/7).

result.intervention: Planned: presentation at paediatric and surgical paediatric audit meetings to educate prescribers.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Enfield South Locality Team, Barnet, Enfield and Haringey Mental Health Trust
result.standard: Team-agreed audit standards (95%) on monitoring frequency, time to review and need for referral

cycle1.result: Only 7/30 (23.33%) tested within the last year; 2 (6.667%) new hyperprolactinaemia diagnoses, both reviewed and treated within one month. No audit standards were met.

result.intervention: New risk-stratified hyperprolactinaemia guidance developed; re-audit planned for 2020.
result.other_findings: Reasons for failure included loss to follow-up, tests not requested and missed appointments.

result.topic: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Cedar Ward adult mental health admissions ward, Llandough Hospital
result.standard: NCEPOD 2022 report on physical health care in mental health inpatients

cycle1.result: Physical health plan 100%; bloods 72%; physical examination 79%; ECG 70%; urine dip 15%; nervous system examination 43%; 17% had physical health conditions not updated on PARIS.

result.intervention: Planned: standard proforma for physical health assessment.
result.other_findings: Lack of uniform documentation made data collection difficult; SHOs were the first point of contact for physical health assessment.

result.setting: Inpatient alcohol detox unit, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, East Midlands

cycle1.result: Preparatory work information missing in 72.73% (16/22); written plans 68.18% (15/22); relapse prevention medication mentioned 81.82%; psychological support 59.09%; mental health mentioned 86.36%.

result.intervention: Referral form refined to capture preparatory work and prompt consideration of mental health support.
result.other_findings: 86.36% were out-of-area referrals; 68.42% of those with mental health mentioned had no plan to refer to a local mental health team.

result.setting: Liaison Psychiatry service, Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE guidance and local trust policies: 100% documentation of sexual dysfunction presence/absence and/or advice on sexual side effects at medication initiation

cycle1.result: Consent for psychotropic initiation documented in 64%; sexual side-effect discussion documented in 4%; other side effects discussed in 19%.

result.intervention: Planned: clear documentation and education; re-audit within 8 months.
result.other_findings: 97 of 1214 patients assessed were started on psychotropic medication.

result.topic: Buccal midazolam prescribing and carer training in epilepsy
result.setting: Intellectual disability services, Hertfordshire and Essex mental health services
result.standard: ESNA and ILAE national guidelines for PRN buccal midazolam administration

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Data collection was still under way at the time of the abstract; no results reported.

result.setting: Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust (POMH lithium audit participation)
result.standard: NICE guidelines: six-monthly TFTs, calcium, eGFR and serum lithium in maintenance; weight/BMI/waist circumference within 12 months; compared with POMH national performance

cycle1.result: Six-monthly calcium 64%, TFTs 78%, eGFR 83%, serum lithium 87%; weight/BMI/waist within 12 months 71%.

result.intervention: Planned: Quality Performance Alert to medical and nursing staff and lithium monitoring added to junior doctor induction.
result.other_findings: TFT and weight/BMI monitoring were above the POMH national level; serum lithium, eGFR and calcium were below it.

result.topic: Steroid-induced hyperglycaemia screening in giant cell arteritis
result.setting: Single centre rheumatology service, Leeds
result.standard: British Society for Rheumatology GCA guideline: HbA1c monitoring and documented counselling on steroid-induced hyperglycaemia

cycle1.result: Baseline HbA1c checked in 32/60 (53%); counselling documented 7/60 (12%); hyperglycaemia detected 8/60 (13%).

result.intervention: Results presented at a regional meeting to raise awareness and a GCA clinic was set up.

cycle2.result: Baseline HbA1c checked in 28/30 (93%); counselling documented 9/30 (30%); hyperglycaemia detected 11/30 (36%).

result.other_findings: Those developing hyperglycaemia had higher baseline weight and BMI. Counselling remained poor and was the priority for further work.

result.topic: Core outcome set for breast reconstruction
result.setting: BRAVO study, Delphi survey of patients and professionals

cycle1.result: 303 (51.4 per cent) completed round 1 and 259 (85.5 per cent) round 2; 148 items in 34 domains led to a core outcome set of 11 key outcomes.

result.other_findings: Consensus methodology study, not an audit.

result.topic: Physical assessment of mental health patients in the emergency department
result.setting: Bolton A&E referrals to the Bolton Mental Health Liaison Team
result.standard: Royal College of Emergency Medicine guidelines on physical assessment before mental health referral

cycle1.result: 44% had any physical observations; 37% had full physical assessment before referral; 58% of abnormal observations were acted on.

result.intervention: Recommended: joint guidelines and teaching for A&E and MHLT practitioners.
result.other_findings: 2% near-miss rate, including a missed diabetic ketoacidosis and delayed treatment of a missed overdose; some triage notes said only "mental health".

result.setting: Acute female psychiatric inpatient ward, Greater Manchester Mental Health Trust

cycle1.result: 7/15 (47%) had a documented urine pregnancy test on admission; of 8 untested, only 1 had contraceptive use documented and 7 had no LMP/contraception notes.

result.intervention: Recommended nursing admission checklist recording LMP, contraception and recent unprotected sex when urine is refused; re-audit planned January to June 2022.
result.other_findings: Pregnancy test strips were unavailable on the ward for about a month; one untested patient was later found to be pregnant.

result.setting: Amber Ward (old age dementia ward), Millbrook Mental Health Unit, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: 10 standards from the Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines covert medication pathway

cycle1.result: LPA/best interest discussion 85% (n = 12); pharmacy input 47% (n = 7); administration in drug chart 53% (n = 8); review date 67% (n = 10); MDT discussion 100% (n = 15).

cycle2.dates: Service users initiated January 2021 to June 2022
cycle2.result: LPA/best interest discussion 95% (n = 20); pharmacy input 100% (n = 21); drug chart administration 100% (n = 21); review date 85% (n = 18); MDT discussion 90% (n = 19); 100% compliance in 4 of 10 standards.

result.other_findings: MDT discussion documentation fell; strict use of the existing covert medication initiation form and another re-audit within 2 years recommended.

result.topic: Skin cancer education in organ transplant recipients
result.setting: Two national transplant centres (inpatient wards, outpatient dermatology and transplant clinics), London

cycle1.result: Prior skin cancer education 66% (site A) and 78% (site B); awareness of increased risk 89% (A) and 95% (B); knowledge of monthly self-examination 28% (A) and 49% (B).

result.intervention: Educational poster displayed clinically and distributed online.

cycle2.result: Awareness of increased risk 96% (A) and 100% (B); sun protection confidence 89% (A) and 96% (B); monthly self-examination knowledge 77% (A) and 81% (B); confidence performing skin checks 79% (A) and 86% (B).

result.other_findings: At site A awareness of seeking GP review for suspected skin cancer rose from 47% to 92% and vitamin D advice from 57% to 94%. 158 responses in total (site A 47, site B 111).

result.topic: Blood test rationale for memantine and pregabalin
result.setting: Older People's Mental Health inpatient unit
result.standard: NICE and BNF (no routine blood monitoring for memantine or pregabalin), RCPath renal testing advice and NHS England guidance that all blood tests have a documented rationale

cycle1.result: 92 blood tests in 30 patients; rationale documented for 62% (n=37); renal monitoring for psychotropics was the rationale in 42% (n=24) of these, all with previously normal kidney function.

result.intervention: Recommended: MDT discussion of monitoring rationale and clear documentation for all blood tests.
result.other_findings: 25% (n=23) of tests without rationale may have related to memantine or pregabalin initiation or titration.

result.setting: Torfaen area community services and Talygarn ward, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board
result.standard: BNF: prolactin at baseline, after 6 months and then annually

cycle1.result: 23 of 28 on risperidone/paliperidone never had prolactin measured; 2 of 28 had appropriate monitoring for 2018.

result.intervention: Awareness of baseline prolactin monitoring raised and baseline prolactin added to admission bloods for patients with psychosis or on antipsychotics.
result.other_findings: 150 patients' letters were screened to find 28 on the medications.

result.setting: Three acute psychiatric inpatient units (Wrexham, Rhyl and Bangor), Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: 60 essential criteria derived from the Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry on history taking and mental state examination; 100% target

cycle1.result: Aggregate compliance 50.6%; administrative tasks 84.3%; objective MSE 68.5%; HOPC 26.4%; past psychiatric history 22.9%; risk assessment 58.1% but risk management plan 8.6%.

result.intervention: Planned: training sessions for trainee doctors before re-audit.
result.other_findings: Different clerking proformas were used at the three sites; anxiety symptoms documented in 10.0% and depression in 26.8%.

result.topic: Tissue box availability in clinic rooms
result.setting: Three community outpatient psychiatric bases, Hertfordshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Consensually agreed gold standard of 100% tissue box availability in all clinic rooms

cycle1.result: Location 1: 10/12 rooms (83.4%); location 2: 8/9 (88.9%); location 3: 5/12 (50% as reported).

result.intervention: Results disseminated to site managers with a recommendation to stock all rooms with tissues.

cycle2.result: Location 1 unchanged (83.4%); location 2 unchanged (88.9%); location 3 fell to 41%.

result.other_findings: No trust policy existed; the authors conclude a more robust intervention and trust-wide policy guidance are needed.

result.setting: Psychiatric inpatient seclusion reviews
result.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice, NICE standards and Trust seclusion policy (time of review, reason, diagnosis, MSE, physical health and observations, medication and side effects, risk, plan)

cycle1.result: Above 90% for time of review, record keeping, management plan, risk, MSE and physical health; prescribed medications 60%, medication side effects 40%, physical observations 40%.

result.intervention: Seclusion medical review template designed and incorporated into the existing documentation template, with teaching and training of doctors.

cycle2.result: Quality of seclusion medical review between 95% and 100%; no major concerns identified.

result.other_findings: The project prompted nurses to audit nursing seclusion reviews.

result.setting: Service for Adolescents and Families in Enfield, referrals from North Middlesex and Barnet hospital paediatric wards
result.standard: NICE Self-Harm Quality Standards (QS34): comprehensive psychosocial assessment, assessment within 24 hours if high risk, risk management plan and follow-up

cycle1.result: Comprehensive psychosocial assessment 100%; seen within 24 hours 93%; documented risk assessment 97%; 7-day follow-up review 92%.

result.intervention: Assessment protocol and safety plan, daily liaison with hospitals, paediatric nurses trained in the time to talk programme and a full-time crisis liaison nurse employed; re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: Hospital referrals rose 141% from 2014/15 to 2018/19; 74% were girls and 87% presented with self-harm, suicidal ideation or attempt.

result.setting: 19 UK coronary sinus reducer implanting centres (national audit)
result.standard: Current guideline recommendations for CSR in refractory angina (appropriate patient selection)

cycle1.result: 84% had CCS class ≥3 angina despite ≥2 antianginals in 94%; baseline ischaemia testing 79%; procedural success 95%; periprocedural adverse events 9.2% (46 in 41 patients); 98% stayed ≤1 night.

result.other_findings: At 6 months 75% improved by ≥1 CCS class and 36% by ≥2 classes; MACE and severe adverse events <1%.

result.setting: Inpatient psychiatry department, tertiary care hospital, Faisalabad

cycle1.result: 27% criminal, 14.3% civil and 58.6% departmental cases; commonest diagnoses schizophrenia 27%, depression 23.5%, intellectual disability 18.9%; 14.9% had no psychiatric diagnosis.

result.other_findings: Descriptive case review of referral sources and outcomes; 41.3% referred directly from courts.

result.topic: Early intervention in psychosis waiting times
result.setting: Early Intervention in Psychosis service, Liverpool
result.standard: NICE access and waiting time standard: 60% of people with first episode psychosis treated with an approved care package within two weeks of referral

cycle1.result: Average referral-to-treatment pathway 9.8 days.

result.intervention: Recommendations from the initial audit implemented (not detailed).

cycle2.result: Average pathway 22.5 days, above the NICE standard.

result.other_findings: Main delays were referral assessment, care coordinator allocation and prescriber review; consultants did >50% of prescriber reviews in both periods. Worsening linked to COVID-19 and more referrals.

result.setting: Three adult psychiatric inpatient wards (2 female, 1 male), Warneford Hospital
result.standard: Local Trust guidelines: all adult inpatients offered year-round vitamin D prophylaxis unless osteomalacia symptoms

cycle1.result: 8 (16%) prescribed prophylactic vitamin D; male ward 1 (6%).

result.intervention: Trust guidelines reformatted into a simplified poster and flow chart distributed to ward doctors' offices.

cycle2.result: 16 (31%) prescribed prophylactic vitamin D; male ward 5 (28%).

result.other_findings: Ward populations changed between measurements because of normal admissions and discharges.

result.setting: Women's blended low/medium secure forensic psychiatry inpatient ward
result.standard: CRAMS criteria: 11 points on care plan, risk, activity, mental state and Section 17 leave in daily entries (adopted after CQC Mental Health Act Review)

cycle1.result: 814/1540 (52.9%) CRAMS criteria met: care planning 50.5%, risk 70.7%, activity 54.6%, mental state 49.8%, S17 leave 50.3%.

result.intervention: Findings discussed with the team, an information sheet produced and CRAMS discussed at daily team huddles.

cycle2.dates: One year after the initial cycle
cycle2.result: 1120/1540 (71.6%) met: care planning 72.6%, risk 75.0%, activity 70.7%, mental state 70.5%, S17 leave 70.7%.

result.other_findings: Many entries still did not meet full CRAMS criteria; an electronic template is planned with the new patient record system.

result.setting: Cardiac outpatient clinics, Barts Heart Centre

cycle1.result: Consultant utilisation of the SNOMED-based powerform averaged 60% for 327 new patients.

result.other_findings: Structured summary reports were sent electronically to primary care the same day, replacing dictated letters; batch download of data worked.

result.setting: Inpatient acute psychiatric ward and a rehabilitation centre
result.standard: 13 predefined PRN prescribing standards including generic naming, dose intervals, BNF limits and regular reviews

cycle1.result: Minimum dose interval 64.5%; maximum dose 96.7%; ward round reviews 3.2%; discontinuation of unused PRN 0%; review of regularly used PRN 0%; regular vs PRN use documented 33.3%.

cycle2.result: Minimum dose interval 93.5%; maximum dose 100%; ward round reviews 64.5%; discontinuation of unused PRN 22.2%; review of regularly used PRN 28.5%; regular vs PRN use documented 44.4%.

result.other_findings: Prompted by a serious incident. 100% compliance was sustained for generic naming, routes, BNF limits, indications and rewriting altered prescriptions.

result.topic: Medication chart and consent to treatment documentation
result.setting: Acute mixed psychiatric inpatient unit, South Manchester (GMMH)
result.standard: Local GMMH policy on medication chart documentation

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment form 22 (71%); consent to treatment form 16 (52%); depot route recorded 40%; regular administration date 84% and signature 29%; allergy reaction nature 6/21 (29%).

result.intervention: Planned: recommendations and re-audit in 3–6 months.
result.other_findings: PRN administration details were 100% complete; patient identifiers were not maintained throughout the chart.

result.topic: Admission blood tests on psychiatric wards
result.setting: Norbury House PICU, St George's Hospital, Stafford, Midlands Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: MPFT trust guidelines on routine admission blood tests

cycle1.result: TFTs 71%; glucose 6%; prolactin 77%; calcium 94%; unnecessary tests in 88% of patients (23 tests).

result.intervention: Staff education programme on trust admission blood test guidelines.

cycle2.result: Appropriate admission bloods 69%; TFTs 100%; glucose 69%; prolactin 100%; calcium 92%; unnecessary tests in 21% (3 tests).

result.other_findings: Further re-audit planned for Spring 2022.

result.setting: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit database

cycle1.result: 5193 (3.2%) had predicted mortality ≥50%; 90-day survival 43% (50–59%), 34% (60–69%), 27% (70–79%) and 17% (80+); unplanned return to theatre 11% vs 8% in high-risk patients.

result.other_findings: Median length of stay rose from 26 days (group 50–59) to 35 days (group 80+) versus 17 days for high-risk patients.

result.setting: Community mental health recovery service
result.standard: NICE guidelines: assessment of biological symptoms and discussion of treatment side effects before initiation and at follow-up

cycle1.result: No record of sexual dysfunction as present or absent at initial assessment or follow-up (0%).

result.intervention: Suggested training and recording changes; proposed standard that recording absence of biological symptoms or supplying medicine leaflets is adequate.
result.other_findings: A staff survey showed high confidence and high self-reported discussion of sexual dysfunction despite no documentation.

result.topic: Driving safety discussion in mental health
result.setting: Kingston and Richmond Home Treatment Teams, South West London and St George's NHS Trust
result.standard: DVLA advice on driving and notification during changes in mental health condition

cycle1.result: 17.7% had documented driving discussion.

result.intervention: Findings presented at Trust-wide HTT governance meeting; driving prompt added to the initial assessment proforma and DVLA leaflet added to the welcome pack.
result.other_findings: Three cycles: an interim re-audit at two months showed 33.3%.

result.setting: Three adolescent forensic wards (2 medium secure, 1 low secure), FCAMHS Ardenleigh, Birmingham
result.standard: National Chlamydia Screening Programme: screening of at-risk young people

cycle1.result: 11.5% tested for chlamydia while 36.8% met screening criteria; physical health (Rethink) form completed in 73.7%.

result.intervention: Recommendations from the initial audit (not detailed).
result.other_findings: Physical health forms were no longer in use by the re-audit; including chlamydia screening in admission processes is suggested.

result.setting: One community Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service team
result.standard: Licensed use per Summary of Product Characteristics and NICE, BAP and BNFc guidance

cycle1.result: 177 prescriptions: 25% licensed use; 42% NICE-compatible, 62% BAP-compatible, 67% BNFc-compatible; 12% deviated from all guidance.

result.other_findings: Unsupported prescriptions included melatonin (9), quetiapine (6) and olanzapine (4) and were linked to comorbidity; 88% were supported by licence or guidance.

result.topic: STOMP psychotropic review in learning disability
result.setting: Four adult learning disability teams, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE NG11: documented rationale, likely treatment length and written strategy for reviewing and stopping psychotropics shared with non-specialists

cycle1.result: Rationale documented 102 (92.7%); review strategy 44 (40%); timescale for stopping 32 (29%).

result.intervention: Planned: STOMP awareness, STOMP team involvement, discharge template prompts for review/stop timescale and STOMP pathway GP guidance; re-audit in 6 months.
result.other_findings: 81 patients were prescribed medication for other mental health diagnoses rather than challenging behaviour.

result.setting: Six adult inpatient wards, St Charles Hospital
result.standard: 10 items agreed with community psychiatric colleagues (reason for admission, diagnosis, circumstances, progress, risk, physical health, legal status, medication, plan, contact details)

cycle1.result: 3.3% (1/30) complete for all items; 23.3% (7/30) missing one item; 7/30 had no information; reason for admission recorded in 2/30.

result.other_findings: Four empty summaries were written in progress notes rather than the proforma; reason for admission was often recorded unhelpfully as "in crisis".

result.setting: Three psychiatric units (Heddfan, Ablett, Hergest) and CMHT sites, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: NICE NG53 and CCQI Standards for Community-Based Mental Health Services 2017: 72-hour follow-up with MSE and comprehensive care plan

cycle1.result: 23% did not receive 72-hour follow-up; risk assessment documented 74%; MSE at follow-up 87%; 67% met full follow-up documentation criteria.

result.other_findings: Thorough inpatient assessments in 83%; printouts from the electronic discharge system were often unavailable.

result.setting: Single-centre dermatology phototherapy service

cycle1.result: 72% (n = 26) much better or better on PGA; DLQI reduction in 28% (n = 10); no complications in 94% (n = 34); minor burn in 6% (n = 2).

result.other_findings: Prospective cohort of treatment outcomes, not measured against a standard.

result.setting: Australian and New Zealand Audit of Surgical Mortality (national database)

cycle1.result: 67 deaths; estimated mortality 0.03–0.07 per cent; 27 (40 per cent) precipitated by significant adverse events; 18 (27 per cent) judged preventable.

result.other_findings: Themes: inadequate preoperative assessment, unanticipated intraoperative pitfalls and failure to recognise postoperative complications.

result.setting: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service, Massereene House, Northern Health and Social Care Trust

cycle1.result: 80% rated the help received "a great deal" better and 80% would recommend telephone reviews "a great deal".

result.other_findings: Satisfaction questionnaire; some preferred face-to-face reviews and the reviewing doctor also ran the audit, risking bias.

result.setting: Tier 4 CAMHS inpatient unit
result.standard: NICE: all CAMHS inpatients offered maintenance vitamin D supplementation from November to March

cycle1.result: 1 out of 10 inpatients received vitamin D supplementation; 5 had levels checked in past three months.

result.intervention: 1:1 psychoeducation from a doctor and a clinic room poster promoting opportunistic vitamin D testing and supplementation.

cycle2.result: 9 out of 10 prescribed vitamin D (7 prophylaxis, 2 treatment doses); 5 had levels checked in past three months.

result.other_findings: Three cycles: 9 out of 11 prescribed on 06/01/2025. Vitamin D level monitoring did not improve.

result.setting: Five chronic psychiatric inpatient wards, Mount Carmel Hospital, compared with Saint Vincent De Paule Residence

cycle1.result: Resuscitation form completion 73.47% (MCH) vs 94.90% (SVPR); "Not for CPR" 9.72% (MCH) vs 61.29% (SVPR).

result.other_findings: SVPR patients had more comorbidities (3.50 vs 2.47, p = 0.0002) with similar frailty (5.83 vs 5.48, p = 0.1456). Resuscitation training tailored to psychiatry was introduced.

result.topic: GP registration and medical card status in addiction care plans
result.setting: National Drug Treatment Centre, Dublin (addiction psychiatry)
result.standard: HSE Clinical Guidelines for Opiate Substitution Therapy 2016: care plan based on assessed need for all drug users in treatment

cycle1.result: GP registration on care plan 66%; up-to-date medical card 12%; medical card status unknown 72%; medical card number displayed 25%.

result.intervention: Results discussed at MDT; staff discussed medical card and GP status at every interaction and referred patients to social work for applications and GP registration.

cycle2.result: GP registration on care plan 93%; up-to-date medical card 45%; status unknown 44%; medical card number displayed 55%.

result.other_findings: Still short of 100% compliance; action plan developed.

result.topic: Cancer screening discussion on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Acute adult psychiatric wards (Galleywood, Topaz), Mother and Baby Unit (Rainbow) and PICU (Christopher Unit)

cycle1.result: Cervical screening discussed with 4/43 eligible (9%); breast screening discussed with 1/15 eligible (7%).

result.intervention: Enhanced induction teaching for resident doctors and local academic teaching over 9 months.

cycle2.result: Cervical screening discussed with 5/26 (19%); breast screening with 0/5 eligible.

result.other_findings: Doctors cited lack of time, patients unable to answer and perceived irrelevance; further teaching and reminder posters followed.

result.setting: Stanley Ward, 30-bed acute male psychiatric ward, Wakefield
result.standard: RCPsych CCQI Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services: documentation of capacity, physical health, medications and leave

cycle1.result: Fully documented: capacity 35%, physical health 0%, medications 22%, leave 20%.

result.intervention: Inpatient list for ward doctors with each domain to copy into MDT notes, then an interactive training video of a simulated MDT shown at departmental teaching.

cycle2.result: Fully documented: capacity 45%, physical health 42%, medications 68%, leave 77%.

result.other_findings: Four measurements: late March 2024 capacity 59%, physical 41%, medications 82%, leave 68% full; July 2024 capacity 20%, physical 48%, medications 91%, leave 71% full. Trainee rotation and limited meeting time hindered sustained gains.

result.topic: Baseline physical health checks before antipsychotics in children and young people
result.setting: West Midlands CAMHS consultants (survey of CAMHS consultant group)
result.standard: NICE guidelines on baseline physical and metabolic investigations before prescribing antipsychotics in children and young people with psychosis and schizophrenia

cycle1.result: Indications, record keeping and nutrition/activity assessment 100%; pulse and BP 88.9%; weight and height plotted 77.8%; movement disorder assessment always 44.4%; lipid profile always 44.4%; fasting glucose and HbA1c 33.3% yes, 66.7% never.

result.other_findings: Recommended a physical/metabolic health check proforma and re-audit after its introduction. Data were collected by questionnaire of nine consultants.

result.topic: Annual psychiatrist review of patients on depot antipsychotics
result.setting: General adult community mental health service, North Norfolk
result.standard: Maudsley prescribing guidelines: all patients on long-term antipsychotics seen by responsible psychiatrist at least once a year; target 100%

cycle1.result: 28/47 (approximately 60%) reviewed by a psychiatrist in the last year; 19 (approximately 40%) not reviewed.

result.other_findings: Of the 19 not reviewed, only 8 had been offered an appointment. Findings discussed with the community team manager to arrange prompt reviews.

result.setting: Regional women's medium secure unit
result.standard: Recording of the 15 criteria of the Ligature Assessment Tool in ligature incident reports

cycle1.dates: Previous (third) audit, about two and a half years earlier
cycle1.result: 19% of reports recorded 11 or more criteria.

result.intervention: No specific intervention (such as education or promotion) between the third and fourth cycles; the Ligature Assessment Tool had been introduced in 2020.

cycle2.result: 37% of reports recorded 11 or more criteria; 19 (35%) recorded all 15 criteria.

result.other_findings: This was the fourth audit cycle since the tool was introduced in 2020. Plan to integrate the tool into the Trust incident reporting system.

result.setting: Auckland City Hospital, Orthopaedics and Older People's Health

cycle1.result: 24% had surgery within 24 hours of admission; of those not operated within 24 hours, 39% were awaiting theatre availability. Inpatient mortality 5%; median length of stay 27 days; 84% transferred to Older People's Health.

result.other_findings: Fast-tracked patients (n=43) had median length of stay 23 days vs 28 days with usual care. 35% were discharged to a higher level of care; 44% walked unaided before fracture but only 1% at discharge.

result.topic: Cholecystectomy after ERCP for bile duct stones
result.setting: Single centre, Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle upon Tyne
result.standard: NICE CG188: bile duct clearance and cholecystectomy offered for bile duct calculi, or documented reason if declined

cycle1.result: 45/82 (55%) had a cholecystectomy after ERCP; of the 37 without cholecystectomy, 20 (54%) had no documented justification.

result.other_findings: Robust follow-up and documentation measures have since been put in place and a follow-up audit is under way.

result.setting: Wolverhampton Older Adult Enhanced Community Mental Health Teams, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BCHFT standard operating procedure: 15 standards for depot prescription writing

cycle1.result: Standard 3 (signed, dated, name printed) 75%; Standard 7 (interval using the word 'every') 19%.

result.intervention: Memory aid for prescribers placed at the front of depot card folders.

cycle2.result: 6 of 15 standards 100%; Standard 3 fell to 15%; Standard 7 improved to 31%.

result.other_findings: Standard 3 non-compliance was mainly due to no space for printing prescriber's name; depot cards to be revised to include signature and name columns.

result.setting: Single-centre biologic registry, The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 78/191 (40.8%) met EULAR criteria for difficult-to-treat RA; erosive disease was the only multivariate predictor.

result.other_findings: Univariate associations included erosive disease, coexistent osteoarthritis and lack of concurrent csDMARD use.

result.setting: Phototherapy unit, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: BAD phototherapy guidelines: urgent referrals to start treatment within 3 weeks of referral; local guidelines on documenting severity scores

cycle1.result: Time from referral to treatment start was 12 months; only 26% of referrals had documented disease severity scores.

result.other_findings: A pre-pandemic audit (March 2021) found a 6-week wait. 73% of urgent referrals were for eczema, 16% psoriasis.

result.setting: Assertive Outreach Team, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust guidance on HDAT monitoring (HDAT monitoring form plus physical health assessment)

cycle1.result: 4 patients on HDAT (117-150% BNF maximum); only one had an HDAT form, which was out of date. 39/52 (75%) had a physical health assessment in the past 12 months.

result.other_findings: Barriers identified: lack of team awareness of HDAT, no reliable system to flag physical health checks and insufficient equipment.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring on psychiatric wards
result.setting: Working-age general adult acute psychiatric inpatient ward
result.standard: Completion and timeliness of physical health checks (examination, observations, height/weight, ECG, bloods, cardiometabolic checklist)

cycle1.result: Physical examinations completed in 93%.

result.intervention: Daily MDT reviews, job list integration and master list; then a whiteboard with colour coding for task tracking, post-MDT reviews, staff reminders and induction sessions.

cycle2.result: Physical examinations 100%; physical observations maintained at 100%; reduced delays and more BMI measurements completed.

result.other_findings: Barriers included gender-based refusal of ECGs and reluctance of patients with eating disorders to have BMI measured.

result.topic: Follow-up after antidepressant initiation in young adults
result.setting: Primary care practice
result.standard: NICE: patients aged 18-25 reviewed within one week of antidepressant initiation or dose increase and again within four weeks

cycle1.result: 3/55 (5.5%) fully compliant; 4/55 (7.3%) reviewed within one week; 8/55 (14.5%) within four weeks.

result.other_findings: 12 patients had no documented follow-up; most reviews were by telephone. Suggested automatic booking of a 1-week telephone review.

result.topic: Folate and vitamin B12 testing and treatment
result.setting: CAMHS Transition service, Oldham
result.standard: BSH guidelines and NICE clinical summaries on diagnosis and treatment of folate and cobalamin deficiency; target 100% for all standards

cycle1.result: Standards 1, 2 and 5 were 100%; standards 3 and 6 (treatment per BNF) were 0%; standard 4 not applicable.

result.intervention: Results shared with the MDT and an algorithm created and circulated.
result.other_findings: Re-audit sample was small, so a further cycle was suggested.

result.topic: ECG on admission to psychiatric wards
result.setting: General adult inpatient wards, Clock View Hospital, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Mersey Care physical health policy: ECG within 24 hours of admission; NICE and RCP guidance

cycle1.result: 31/60 had an ECG within 24 hours; of the other 29, reason documented in 16. 13 abnormal ECGs, only 3 referred for further investigation.

result.other_findings: No documentation of the ECG report in one third of cases. Recommended induction teaching and training ward nurses to perform ECGs.

result.setting: High-volume primary care practice (population over 15,000)
result.standard: NICE NG198: oral lymecycline with a topical agent for a maximum of 12 weeks then reassessment, avoiding concurrent oral and topical antibiotics

cycle1.result: 22% fully adherent; 54% received a topical treatment; 13% had concurrent oral and topical antibiotics; median continuous duration 4 months (range 1 month to 7.5 years).

result.other_findings: Recommended clinician education, integrating NICE guidance into clinical systems and structured treatment reviews.

result.topic: Physical health investigations on admission to psychiatric wards
result.setting: Nine general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust physical health policy: admission blood tests and ECG within 24 hours

cycle1.result: FBC 89 (56%); U&E 90 (56%); LFT 93 (58%); TFT 90 (56%); HbA1c 83 (52%); lipids 89 (56%); ECG 86 (54%); urine pregnancy test 15/69 women (22%); urine drug screen 31 (19%).

result.other_findings: Recommended induction teaching, nursing awareness of pregnancy testing and daily review of patients declining investigations.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment in mental health inpatients
result.setting: 23 inpatient wards, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE NG89: VTE risk assessment on admission or first consultant review, reassessment, and prophylaxis where indicated

cycle1.result: 30 (59.2%) risk assessed within 24 hours; 2% reassessed during admission; all 3 at-risk patients (6.1%) given prophylaxis but none reassessed for continued need.

result.other_findings: Recommended VTE teaching at junior doctor induction and a Trust VTE policy including mental health risk factors.

result.topic: Time to ERCP for acute gallstone cholangitis
result.setting: District general hospital, Princess Alexandra Hospital, Harlow
result.standard: NICE: ERCP within 72 hours of diagnosis of acute gallstone cholangitis

cycle1.result: Median time to ERCP 10 days (5-24); moderate-severe 8 days (5-19), mild 28 days (9-46).

result.intervention: Additional referral pathways to three nearby tertiary centres for ERCP; results presented to surgical MDT.

cycle2.result: Median time to ERCP 6 days (4-9); moderate-severe 6 days (6-8), mild 4 days (4-25).

result.other_findings: 41 patients across both cycles. Median length of stay fell from 8 (6-13) to 7 days (4-10).

result.topic: Resuscitation futility in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
result.setting: Emergency Department, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh

cycle1.result: 202 (71.4%) low, 46 (16.3%) intermediate and 35 (12.4%) high risk of CPR futility by SPICT score.

result.other_findings: 27.7% of low-risk patients survived to discharge vs 2.17% intermediate and 2.86% high risk; suggests community DNACPR implementation is suboptimal.

result.setting: Approved Centre (acute psychiatric unit), Tallaght University Hospital
result.standard: Mental Health Commission rules governing the use of seclusion (13 rules)

cycle1.dates: Before introduction of the Integrated Care Pathway (2012)
cycle1.result: Compliance across the 13 MHC rules ranged from 3% to 100%.

result.intervention: Seclusion Integrated Care Pathway introduced in 2012 to record and monitor each seclusion episode.

cycle2.result: Compliance ranged from 69% to 100%; 100% compliance with five of the 13 rules.

result.other_findings: Improvements in medical and nursing reviews, informing patients of reasons and likely duration of seclusion, and informing next of kin. An audit immediately after ICP introduction was also done.

result.topic: Alcohol use disorder assessment on psychiatric admission
