result.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Assessment and management of alcohol use disorders following admission (alcohol history, weekly quantity, CIWA-R, bloods, referral)

cycle1.result: Alcohol history documented 45%; weekly quantity 22%; CIWA-R on admission 0.7%; referral to community alcohol services 3%.

result.intervention: Recommendations from the original audit implemented (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Alcohol history documented 81%; weekly quantity 8%; CIWA-R 4.0%; referral to community alcohol services 7%.

result.other_findings: Gamma GT and magnesium checks on admission improved. Further recommendations: induction teaching, CIWA-R training and a ward flow chart.

result.topic: Mental health risk assessment in paediatric emergency department
result.setting: Paediatric Emergency Department, Leicester
result.standard: NICE NG225: completion of ED mental health risk assessment tool and ED mental health form

cycle1.result: Risk assessment tool completed 7/59 (11.9%); ED mental health form opened 37/59 (62.7%); mental state examination completed 16/37 (43.2%); DPS score assigned 29/37 (78.4%).

result.other_findings: The tool may be unsuitable for children (capacity rather than competence) and overlaps with the form. Plan to revise tools and add education.

result.topic: PPI cover with SSRIs in older adults
result.setting: Older adult community mental health team
result.standard: Maudsley Guidelines: PPI prescribed if SSRIs cannot be avoided in patients at high bleeding risk

cycle1.result: 56.5% of patients on SSRIs prescribed a PPI.

result.intervention: Results presented to prescribers within the team.

cycle2.result: 64.7% of patients on SSRIs prescribed a PPI.

result.other_findings: Only 1 patient had bleeding risk explicitly documented. Many PPIs were started before the SSRI, possibly inflating results.

result.topic: Mental Health Act medical recommendation quality
result.setting: Derby inpatient psychiatric units
result.standard: Mental Health Act 1983 criteria for Section 2 and 3 medical recommendations, using the Mason et al. (2012) audit tool

cycle1.result: Mental disorder and nature/degree well documented; justification of risk to health, safety or others poorly documented, lowest for health.

result.other_findings: Recommenders often did not identify which of the three risk categories applied. Results presented at teaching and inclusion in junior doctor induction recommended.

result.topic: Baseline physical health checks before antipsychotic initiation
result.setting: Intensive Home Treatment Team, Bradford District Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BDCFT Antipsychotic Physical Health Monitoring Shared Care Guidelines

cycle1.result: 32% had a full physical health check before antipsychotic initiation; 56% incomplete; no individual investigation fully compliant; 40% had checks reviewed by a professional.

result.other_findings: BMI/weight was least often completed and HbA1c was the least completed blood test.

result.topic: Menstrual health screening on psychiatric wards
result.setting: Female inpatient psychiatric wards, Lambeth Hospital, South London and Maudsley
result.standard: Active screening for menstrual and menopausal health on admission

cycle1.result: 3/44 (7%) actively screened; 8/44 (18%) had appropriate menstrual health intervention.

result.intervention: Staff training, patient information materials and updated clerking prompts.

cycle2.result: 28/45 (62%) actively screened; 33/45 (73%) had appropriate menstrual health intervention.

result.other_findings: Menstrual symptoms were identified more consistently after the changes, leading to counselling, products and leaflets.

result.setting: Mental health liaison service, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board acute hospitals
result.standard: RCPsych PLAN quality standards: 100% essential, 80% expected and 60% desirable standards met

cycle1.result: 30% of essential standards not met and 21% somewhat met; 36% of expected standards met, 41% not met; 89% of desirable standards not met.

result.other_findings: Weak domains included policies, urgent care, governance, induction and teaching. A business case for a consultant-led MDT is being developed.

result.setting: Older Persons Community Mental Health Team
result.standard: NICE guideline on antipsychotics for behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia; local CAIR form

cycle1.result: CAIR form present in 73% of notes (37% the new shorter version); 63% of forms fully completed; 100% had assessment of causes, non-drug interventions first, target symptoms and review within 3 months.

result.other_findings: Risk-benefit discussions were documented vaguely. Teaching held, leaflet to be provided, team to revert to original CAIR form and re-audit in 6 months.

result.setting: Holywell Hospital (psychiatric hospital)
result.standard: 100% of digital handover records completed by doctors at end of shifts

cycle1.result: 5.36% of digital handovers completed.

result.intervention: PDSA cycle August 2022 to January 2023: information sharing, teaching at changeover inductions, administrative help with shared drive access, and regular audit and feedback.

cycle2.result: 91.94% of digital handovers completed (88.71% in December 2022).

result.other_findings: 35.00% in April 2022 and 25.81% in August 2022; access for outside locums remains a problem.

result.topic: Admission checklist for borderline personality disorder
result.setting: Nine acute care wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust BPD admission checklist completed at admission

cycle1.result: 0/60 admissions had a completed BPD checklist.

result.other_findings: 40% of admissions were out of hours, with more use of the MHA; 40% of ST doctors could not find the checklist. Training and re-audit in 6 months planned.

result.topic: Glucocorticoid adherence in giant cell arteritis
result.setting: Single rheumatology department, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre, Oxford

cycle1.result: 22% (last 7 days) and 40% (last 6 months) were not following their original recommended steroid regimen.

result.other_findings: Most non-adherence was due to medical advice; others were forgetting, fear of side effects or confusion about preparations.

result.topic: Early onset colorectal cancer presentation and management
result.setting: Prospective multicentre cohort, 11 hospitals in extended Northwestern Switzerland

cycle1.result: 38 (10.8%) had early onset colorectal cancer; diagnostic delay 6.5 weeks longer than late onset; adjuvant chemotherapy 55.6% vs 28.6%.

result.other_findings: Rectal bleeding was the main symptom in both groups (60.5% vs 37.0%); more early onset patients received an ostomy.

result.topic: Naloxone provision for patients on opioid substitution treatment
result.setting: CGL drug and alcohol service, East Sussex
result.standard: UK guidelines on clinical management of drug misuse and dependence: 100% of clients prescribed OST offered naloxone

cycle1.result: 65/748 (8.7%) did not have naloxone, all of whom (100%) had been offered it and declined; 60 had expired naloxone; 54 had naloxone given but not coded on the opiate report.

result.other_findings: Most common reason for declining was no longer injecting and no contacts using opiates (57%); stigma was also cited.

result.topic: Citalopram and escitalopram dosing and QTc in older adults
result.setting: Older adult community mental health services, Wolverhampton
result.standard: MHRA 2014 guidance: maximum citalopram 20 mg and escitalopram 10 mg daily in older adults

cycle1.result: One patient on citalopram above the recommended dose (30 mg); escitalopram within limits; QTc risk documented in 2 (11.8%); ECG review at initiation or adjustment in 1 patient.

result.other_findings: 6 (35.3%) were on concurrent QTc-prolonging medication, all antipsychotics.

result.setting: Enhanced Teams, Folly Hall Community Mental Health Team
result.standard: NICE NG181 and local standards: serum lithium every 3 months; renal, thyroid and calcium every 6 months; side effect monitoring; fully met 91-100%

cycle1.result: Lithium levels every 3 months 44.4%; renal function 94.4%; thyroid function 88.9%; calcium 61.1%; side effect monitoring 100%.

result.other_findings: No action taken for one patient with out-of-range lithium. Recommended reminders, a lithium registry, business meeting discussion and a lithium champion; re-audit planned.

result.setting: Working-age adult inpatient wards, Farnham Road Hospital
result.standard: Trust guideline: GASS-C completed at 30 days after clozapine titration

cycle1.result: GASS-C completed at 30 days in 3/8 (37.5%).

result.other_findings: Constipation documented in clinical notes in 6 (75%) and laxatives prescribed in 7 (87.5%). Embedding GASS-C into titration workflow proposed with re-audit.

result.topic: Risk assessment documentation at psychiatric admission
result.setting: Two acute mental health wards (male and female)
result.standard: Documented risk assessment (risk to self, others, property) in junior doctor admission clerking

cycle1.result: 12/30 (40%) had a junior doctor risk assessment in the clerking; 14 (47%) had no mention of risk on admission.

result.other_findings: Of 12 assessments all covered self-harm and violence, but only 1 absconding. Teaching and a risk assessment template introduced, with re-audit under way.

result.topic: Staff knowledge of transgender patient care
result.setting: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust (survey of medical staff)

cycle1.result: 83.7% had cared for transgender patients; 58.1% not confident; 86% had no training; 79.1% unaware of guidelines or policies.

result.other_findings: 60.5% were unaware of UK gender reassignment processes; staff requested training on pronouns and legal frameworks.

result.setting: Eight acute adult inpatient wards, Nottingham Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE and local guidance on prolactin monitoring and management of hyperprolactinaemia

cycle1.result: 19 patients had no prolactin assay during admission; 44.4% of antipsychotic-naive patients had baseline prolactin; 9.1% with hyperprolactinaemia had symptoms assessed; 27.3% had actions taken.

result.other_findings: Hyperprolactinaemia identified in 9 patients.

result.topic: Mental Health Act Section 5(2) form completion
result.setting: Large acute NHS hospital, adult and paediatric medicine
result.standard: Proforma of 12 criteria for correct completion of Section 5(2) forms

cycle1.result: 84% of criteria met (202/240); 100% legally valid; 70% identified risks; 55% correct status deletions; 55% contained abbreviations; 40% stated detention was needed to allow MHA assessment.

result.other_findings: Hospital revising Section 5(2) guidance and preparing example templates; re-audit planned.

result.topic: Physical health assessment in crisis home treatment teams
result.setting: South Cambridgeshire Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: HTAS standards: physical health assessment and medical review for 100% of service users

cycle1.result: Physical health assessment criteria met in 70.12%; medical review criteria met in 94.80%.

result.other_findings: 1232 referrals screened to find 77 eligible service users.

result.topic: Dementia diagnosis and treatment in memory services
result.setting: 15 memory services, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE NG97 (2018) and TEWV Dementia Pathway: diagnostic work-up, subtype diagnosis, cholinesterase inhibitors/memantine and cognitive stimulation therapy

cycle1.result: Dementia subtype given in 100%; medication offered when indicated in 96% (10 of 15 services 100%).

result.other_findings: Only 2 services offered cognitive stimulation therapy to all suitable patients; 10 teams scored below 40%.

result.setting: Specialist addictions service (three hubs), Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Attendance at an addictions prescriber review within the last 3 months for patients on OST

cycle1.result: 170/343 (50%) attended a prescriber review in the last 3 months (Hub 1 55%, Hub 2 34%, Hub 3 65%).

result.intervention: Quality improvement plan then enhanced plan: new appointment letter, text confirmation and reminder, keyworker reminder, prescriber call to persistent non-attenders, and medication safety review for non-attenders.
result.other_findings: After the enhanced plan in December 2018 attendance was 258/339 (76%) across all hubs; Hub 1 dipped to 51% in October 2018 after the first plan.

result.setting: Inpatient services, Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust seclusion policy based on the Mental Health Act Code of Practice (review content and timing: within first hour, then 4-hourly until MDT)

cycle1.result: Above 80%: timing of review, record keeping, plan for continuing seclusion, risk to self and others, mental state examination. Below 60%: prescribed medications, medication side effects and physical observations.

result.other_findings: A seclusion medical review template was developed and teaching delivered; re-audit planned in 1 year.

result.setting: Two adult acute psychiatric wards
result.standard: Trust policy for drug screening on admission

cycle1.result: Documentation about drug screening in 23/40 (57.5%); test offered to 21/40 (52.5%); 15/21 (71.4%) completed; 5/8 positive results referred to substance misuse services.

result.other_findings: Reasons for refusal (6, 28.6%) were not documented; re-audit planned after 3 months.

result.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Mersey Care Nutrition and Hydration Policy: MUST within 72 hours of admission and Nutrition Screening Tool Care Plan completed

cycle1.result: 36 (90%) had MUST completed within 72 hours; 31 (79%) had every element of the care plan completed; 3/5 (60%) high-risk MUST patients fully compliant.

result.other_findings: Described as a re-audit but earlier results are not given. Dietitian referrals were not made consistently.

result.topic: Follow-up after cervical spine fracture in older adults
result.setting: Major Trauma Centre, Cork University Hospital
result.standard: Outpatient neurosurgical appointments arranged for patients aged 65 and over with documented follow-up plans at discharge

cycle1.result: 28/38 (74%) eligible patients had appointments arranged; 26% without planned specialist review.

result.intervention: Findings presented to Neurosurgery; consultants' secretaries reviewed every discharge summary and booked outpatient appointments.
result.other_findings: Initial cycle 57 patients, median LOS 13 days, in-hospital mortality 12%; re-audit 14 patients, median LOS 9 days, no deaths.

result.topic: NELA risk assessment in emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Single centre, University Hospital Hairmyres, NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: NELA guidelines for risk assessment and documentation in emergency laparotomy

cycle1.result: About 21% of CEPOD booking forms had a recorded NELA score; NELA form or risk score missing in up to 97% of files and operation notes.

result.other_findings: Mortality was 21% for NELA score over 20%; 48% stayed longer than 10 days.

result.setting: Prospect Park Hospital (psychiatric hospital), Berkshire
result.standard: Local Trust policy and Resuscitation Council UK standards for resuscitation equipment and weekly checklists

cycle1.result: 7/10 locations did not meet standards (missing or expired adrenaline, suction, oxygen masks); 4/10 wards had not completed the weekly checklist; 70% of staff-completed checklists were incorrect.

result.intervention: Updated, more detailed checklist, standardised procedure for ward managers, regular audits and extra Resuscitation team staffing.
result.other_findings: A re-audit was done and changes are being rolled out Trust-wide, but re-audit results are not reported.

result.setting: Seclusion areas across Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Defined checklist of seclusion room recommendations

cycle1.result: No audited area was 100% compliant; no rooms had a bed; problems with blind spots, bedding, lighting and heating.

result.other_findings: Four wards had no dedicated seclusion room, and patients were secluded in general areas on three of them.

result.topic: Physical health information on transfer to secure wards
result.setting: Male forensic secure rehabilitation ward
result.standard: Complete physical health notes on transfer (consultation records, prior physical history, complete prescription with allergies)

cycle1.result: 7/12 patients transferred with complete physical health notes; no formal verbal or written physical health handover.

result.other_findings: A proforma for preadmission meetings is being introduced from February 2024 with re-audit in February 2025.

result.topic: ECG monitoring for patients on antipsychotics
result.setting: Acute Mental Health Inpatient Centre (5 wards), Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
result.standard: Maudsley prescribing guidelines: ECG on admission and before discharge if antipsychotic regimen changed

cycle1.result: 0% had a discharge ECG; 7/34 (20.59%) had no ECG during admission; 17/34 (50%) did not have an ECG within 7 days of admission.

result.other_findings: Teaching session and reminder posters arranged, with a PDSA approach planned.

result.setting: Acute psychiatric inpatient unit, The Orchard
result.standard: Standards in the New Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry for components of the psychiatric history

cycle1.result: Only patient ID and presenting complaint in 100%; medical history 72%; forensic history 44%; social history 39%.

result.intervention: Clerking proforma created and distributed to junior doctors.

cycle2.result: ID, PC, HPC, psychiatric history and MSE 100%; forensic history 73% (p = 0.015); social history 78% (p = 0.018); premorbid personality 89% (p = 0.005); medical history 94%.

result.other_findings: Personal history (39% to 56%) and family history (39% to 61%) improved but not significantly.

result.setting: 7 psychiatry wards, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: 80% completion of ward review documentation questions considered satisfactory

cycle1.result: Most questions did not meet the 80% standard; 'Responsible clinician' completed in 23.3%.

result.intervention: Strategies to improve record keeping, including automation of some fields, junior doctor induction teaching and awareness posters.

cycle2.result: 9 questions satisfactory (at least 80%); 7 above 45%; 17 low; 'Responsible clinician' 99.5% after automation.

result.other_findings: Effectiveness of non-automated strategies was limited; making fields mandatory or auto-complete worked best.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring in eating disorder day care
result.setting: Adult Eating Disorder Service day-care, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines and MEED guidance: weight, height, BMI, pulse, sitting/standing BP and temperature every attendance; bloods and ECG by BMI schedule

cycle1.result: Average day-care admission 5.5 months; other results not reported.

cycle2.result: 100% monitoring of BMI, weight, BP and pulse at admission and last assessment; temperature monitoring fell by 11.1%; ECG and bloods fell by 11.1% at all points; one patient lacked BMI, BP and pulse at midpoint.

result.other_findings: Average admission fell to 3.5 months. Faulty thermometer and COVID-related difficulty accessing primary care affected monitoring.

result.setting: Women's secure services, Ardenleigh, Birmingham
result.standard: Trust guidelines for management of vitamin D deficiency

cycle1.result: 89% had vitamin D checked during admission; 25% of those tested within 1 week of admission; 89% needing treatment were prescribed supplementation, 94% at correct dose and duration.

result.other_findings: Only 25% of those tested had adequate levels; recommended vitamin D as a routine admission blood test.

result.setting: Inpatient units, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 28 reports of unavailable ECG machines; 490 minutes spent searching (median 10 minutes, longest 120); 4 ECGs not done; 46% missing and 54% faulty machines.

result.intervention: Escalation to senior leadership and more ECG machines sourced during the audit period.
result.other_findings: Plan to develop instructional flowcharts for escalating faulty machines.

result.setting: Inpatient wards, Lincolnshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Restraint practice: documentation, de-escalation, post-incident debrief and reflection, care planning

cycle1.result: 100% documentation of type and outcome of restraint; 20-30% of restraints without de-escalation, debrief or MDT reflection; 12% involved patients in post-incident reflection.

result.intervention: PDSA 2021-2022: PMVA de-escalation training, sharing practice via MDT, monthly restrictive practice hub meetings and root cause analysis.

cycle2.result: Patient involvement in post-incident reflection increased by 60%; care planning and de-escalation improved by 10-15%.

result.other_findings: Restraints fell by 10-30% on eleven wards from 2020 to 2022.

result.setting: Irish National Audit of Stroke (national)

cycle1.result: 21 international stroke registries identified; core minimum dataset for acute stroke care agreed.

result.other_findings: Later phases address non-acute care datasets, PROMs and implementation.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment in mental health inpatients
result.setting: 16 inpatient wards, Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE VTE in over-16s guideline: risk assessment on admission or by first consultant review, and reassessment at consultant review

cycle1.result: 153 (63%) had a signed and dated VTE assessment on admission; 154 (63%) within 24 hours; 242 (99%) had no reassessment at consultant review.

result.other_findings: 13 (5%) assessments unsigned or undated; recommended induction teaching and making the VTE section a required field.

result.topic: VTE prophylaxis in lower limb immobilisation
result.setting: Emergency Department, Stockport NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE recommendation for VTE risk assessment in lower limb immobilisation, RCEM GEMNet guidance and local policy

cycle1.result: 20/62 (32%) had a documented VTE risk assessment; none received thromboprophylaxis per local policy.

result.intervention: Pathway redesigned to GEMNet guidance, local education and launch, electronic discharge prompt/block and orthopaedic engagement.

cycle2.result: 54/58 (93.1%) had a documented risk assessment; 25/58 (43%) high risk and prescribed thromboprophylaxis.

result.other_findings: 40% at baseline would have been eligible under GEMNet; no short-term complications on chart review.

result.setting: Six community mental health teams (9 general adult consultants), east side of North Wales (Wrexham and Flintshire), BETSI Health Board
result.standard: NICE ADHD guidance (adapted ADHD audit support tool)

cycle1.result: Good compliance with NICE guidance for assessment and treatment and in documenting diagnostic criteria (DSM-IV and/or ICD-10); deficiencies in recommended physical examination and side-effect monitoring; antipsychotics used in some patients. No numbers reported.

result.other_findings: Case notes of 20 patients per consultant were audited. Recommendations included clinician education, local ADHD clinics and joining the POMH-UK ADHD prescribing QIP.

result.topic: Radical cystectomy practice and case volume
result.setting: British Association of Urological Surgeons audit and data platform; 84 centres, 161 surgeons in England

cycle1.result: Ileal conduit 85.2%; open cystectomy 67.8%, robotic 20.6%, laparoscopic 9.1%; lymph node dissection rates 79.5% to 90.3%; median LOS 7–9 days minimally invasive vs 11–12 days open.

result.other_findings: Robotic cystectomy was more likely in high-volume surgeons and centres; transfusion rates trended higher as centre volume fell; high-grade complications appeared under-reported.

result.setting: Four general adult acute psychiatric wards, Aneurin Bevan Health Board
result.standard: Smoking status asked on admission and cessation advice or nicotine replacement therapy offered (target not reported)

cycle1.result: Smoking status asked in 68%; not asked n = 11 (32%); smoker not given advice n = 13 (38%); smoker given advice n = 4 (12%); advice or NRT given to only 14% of potential smokers.

result.other_findings: Asking about smoking varied between wards and there was a lack of smoking cessation literature on the wards.

result.setting: Dermatology department, Barts Health NHS Trust, London
result.standard: British Association of Dermatologists 2020 guidelines: TB screening questions, chest X-ray and IGRA before biologics

cycle1.result: CXR performed in 74 (96%); IGRA in 72 (94%); 3 (4%) had latent TB on positive IGRA with normal CXR; no IGRA-negative patient had a positive CXR.

result.other_findings: Authors propose CXR only for patients symptomatic for TB or with a positive IGRA.

result.topic: Implementation of perinatal audit improvement objectives
result.setting: All 11 perinatal cooperation groups in the northern region of the Netherlands

cycle1.result: Knowledge and skills scores rose from mean 2.53 to 3.70 on a 1–5 Likert scale (p<0.001); 98 improvement objectives addressed, 46 (47%) fully implemented and secured.

result.intervention: ACTion method: 7-step PDCA cycle with interactive learning, training and coaching in implementation and behaviour change
result.other_findings: 86% of 93 team members completed training; implementation per team ranged from 14% to 67%. Barriers were limited time, manpower and commitment.

result.setting: High secure forensic psychiatry hospital
result.standard: Public Health England national COVID-19 guidance

cycle1.result: SARS-CoV-2 detected in 1 patient; practice consistent with national guidance.

cycle2.dates: Third cycle, later wave of COVID-19, 2020
cycle2.result: SARS-CoV-2 detected in 12 patients; identification of suspected cases and management of confirmed cases consistent with national guidance.

result.other_findings: Three cycles, one per wave; cycle 2 had 12 patients. All patients recovered; three needed oral antibiotics and dexamethasone and one was admitted to a general hospital for oxygen.

result.topic: Physical health appointment attendance in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Psychiatric care setting

cycle1.result: Attendance 68.5% of 89 appointments; missed rate 25.8%.

result.intervention: Measures addressing patient transfers, leave protocols and transport problems

cycle2.result: Attendance 71.8% of 39 appointments; missed rate 28.2%; chi-square 2.2893, p = 0.3183 (not significant).

result.other_findings: Missed appointments in phase 2 were due to patient leave, ward cancellations and transport problems.

result.setting: Stanley Treatment and Intervention Team, community mental health, Derwent Clinic
result.standard: General Medical Council professional standards for prescribing unlicensed medicines

cycle1.result: 2/27 initiated on unlicensed medication; both (2/2) had documented discussion, rationale, risk-benefit, accurate records and information given; 100% compliant.

result.other_findings: Better than a previous inpatient ward audit. A set proforma for unlicensed prescribing was suggested.

result.setting: Large teaching hospital, Kellgren Centre for Rheumatology, Manchester Royal Infirmary
result.standard: GIRFT guidance on broad MDT input (rheumatology, haematology, infectious diseases, critical care) and local HLH guidelines

cycle1.result: MDT discussion in 26/34; 1/26 (4%) met guideline standards; 13/26 (50%) single-specialty discussions; median 10 days admission to MDT, 19/26 (73%) within 14 days.

result.other_findings: Mortality 6/26 (23%) with MDT discussion vs 5/8 (63%) without; organ support 14/26 (54%) vs 5/8 (63%). Overall mortality 11/34 (32%).

result.setting: Community mental health team, Glasgow, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
result.standard: NICE: weight, blood pressure and heart rate monitored every 6 months on ADHD medication

cycle1.result: Weight recorded 15%, heart rate 8%, blood pressure 19%.

result.intervention: Results presented at a local meeting with relevant clinicians in May 2021

cycle2.result: Weight recorded 45%, heart rate 40%, blood pressure 50%.

result.other_findings: 30 patients identified, 10 excluded for non-engagement. Still not meeting NICE guidance; COVID-19 reduced face-to-face reviews.

result.setting: Wards 6 and 7 (old age psychiatry), Harplands Hospital
result.standard: Trust NEWS2 standards, SOP 1.62a and Physical Health policy

cycle1.result: 37/39 charts completed at admission; 9 lacked demographics, 13 missing date/time, 6 missing signatures, 9 illegible entries, 12 incomplete sections; GCS issues in 2 charts.

result.intervention: Printed patient information labels, targeted education sessions for ward teams and discussion with ward management
result.other_findings: Scores 1–4 were often escalated to a registered nurse first and scores >4 directly to medics; electronic versions of charts were often left unfilled. Re-audit planned.

result.setting: Six wards (three geriatric, two medical, one surgical), district general hospital
result.standard: Local mental health trust rapid tranquillisation guidance

cycle1.result: 13/297 (4.3%) received RT; indication documented in 50%; maximum frequency not indicated; no psychiatric liaison or dementia team involvement evident; post-RT monitoring not evident.

cycle2.result: 9/172 (5.2%) received RT; indication documented in 88.8%; maximum frequency indicated in 55.5%; almost 100% documentation of RT administration; liaison or dementia team involvement around 33%; post-sedation monitoring still not evident.

result.other_findings: PRN and intramuscular remained most common. A new RT policy with teaching and training has since been approved, with re-audit planned in 6–12 months.

result.setting: Trent Oesophago-Gastric Unit, Nottingham University Hospitals (high-volume UGI cancer unit)
result.standard: NICE: PET-CT for all oesophageal and OGJ cancers except T1a

cycle1.result: Mean wait for PET-CT 17 (1–57) days; 14 (32%) had CT/PET-CT discrepancy; 5 (11%) distant metastasis on PET-CT; 9 (20%) incidental uptake; further investigations added mean 15 (1–28) days delay.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend timely PET-CT scanning and reporting, e.g. during pre-MDT triage.

result.setting: Middlesbrough Memory Service
result.standard: NICE NG97 (1.5): consider memantine with acetylcholinesterase inhibitor in moderate to severe Alzheimer's dementia; Trust guidelines

cycle1.result: Severity documented in only 7% (all moderate), 93% generic diagnosis; 46/60 on medication, all on monotherapy; 46 completed the diagnostic pathway.

result.other_findings: Mixed dementia 40%, Alzheimer's 39%, Lewy body 8% of diagnoses. Combination therapy not yet considered at diagnosis.

result.setting: Frailty admission unit, Mid Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust (large district general)
result.standard: NICE CG103 and SIGN 157: delirium diagnosis with CAM or 4AT and management with care plan

cycle1.result: CAM or 4AT used in 32.5%; delirium care plan in 20%.

result.intervention: Delirium care checklist sticker, brief education sessions for ward doctors and reminder emails over 6 weeks

cycle2.result: Sticker use fell from 57% in week 1 to 0% in week 6; 4AT 57%, 50%, 100% in first 3 weeks then 40%, 4.2%, 1.3%; care plan 42% and 37% in first 2 weeks, 0% by week 6.

result.other_findings: Barriers were lapse of education sessions due to registrar on-calls, junior doctor changeover, time to complete and unclear ownership between medical and nursing teams.

result.topic: COVID-19 infection and mortality after surgery
result.setting: 43 centres in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland (multicentre national audit)

cycle1.result: COVID-19 in 0.52% (n=35); overall 30-day mortality 0.41%; mortality 25.71% (n=9) with COVID-19; adjusted OR 11.71 (95% CI 1.55 to 88.74, p=0.017).

result.other_findings: Mortality 75% (n=3) in diabetic foot surgery patients with COVID-19; post-lockdown infection rate 0.15% with no COVID deaths; complications and infection rates unchanged.

result.setting: 15 memory services, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: National benchmark of diagnosis within six weeks (42 days) of referral; National Audit of Dementia

cycle1.result: Access times 30–207 days, diagnostic waits 3–147 days, overall waits 92–323 days; no service met the six-week benchmark; 25% of services diagnosed within 6–18 weeks, 75% within 18–52 weeks.

result.other_findings: Trust average waits exceeded national averages; the best service was at 92 days.

result.topic: STOMP/STAMP psychotropic prescribing and physical health monitoring
result.setting: Leeds Community Healthcare Learning Disability Clinic (children and young people)

cycle1.result: Annual health check 70%; drug names and doses 100%; indication 85%; side-effect discussion at initiation 73%; side-effect enquiry at follow-up 77%.

cycle2.result: Annual health check 80%; drug names and doses 100%; indication 93%; side-effect discussion at initiation 38%; side-effect enquiry at follow-up 54%.

result.other_findings: Criteria were changed in cycle 2 (follow-up definition and age >14 for health checks), which may explain differences. Side-effect discussion was often missing for melatonin or ADHD medication.

result.topic: Physical health equipment on psychiatric wards
result.setting: Seven inpatient wards (acute adult, older adult, forensic), The Redwoods Centre, Midlands Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: RCPsych Physical Health in Mental Health (2009) equipment checklist; compliance standard 100%

cycle1.result: All wards >80% compliant; overall compliance 87%; neurological testing pins absent on most wards; alcometers, Snellen charts, ophthalmoscopes and otoscopes borrowed between wards.

result.intervention: Formal equipment-sharing arrangements confirmed and procurement of missing equipment planned
result.other_findings: Re-audit planned 6 months after the first cycle.

result.setting: Specialist community rehabilitation team, Sheffield Health Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists standards for community rehabilitation services

cycle1.result: Only 3/50 (6%) service users had formally recorded carers; survey response 24% (14/58); 93% had emergency contact information, 78% felt supported, 64% felt involved, 50% aware of carers groups, 14% given written information.

result.intervention: Bimonthly family, friends and carers support group set up, written carers pack reviewed and definition of carer broadened
result.other_findings: All 14 respondents identified as carers, suggesting significant under-recording; EPR limits formal recording of carer status.

result.setting: Three psychiatric units across three sites, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: RCPsych and PRSB recommendations for letters to GPs

cycle1.result: Missing care coordinator details 91.7%, medical comorbidities 61.22%, non-psychiatric diagnosis 79.59%, actions for GP 71.43%; psychiatric diagnosis 83.47%, psychiatric medications and follow-up plan 80.17%.

result.intervention: Local guidelines and letter template with recommended headings, and formal teaching for junior doctors

cycle2.result: Psychiatric diagnosis 97.1% (previously 83.5%), psychiatric medication 91.4% (80.17%), follow-up plan 98.6% (80.2%); medical comorbidity 28.6% vs 31.4%, non-psychiatric medication 65.7% vs 34.7%, care coordinator 54.3% vs 8.3%, action for GP 27.1% vs 44.6%.

result.other_findings: Two headings declined and change varied between sites. Barriers were template not used, lack of junior training and psychiatrist workload.

result.setting: Psychiatry clinics, TEWV NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on GP letters (January 2021), 10 domains

cycle1.dates: Letters September to December 2023; audited December 2023 to January 2024
cycle1.result: 100% for contact details, review date, consultation, participants and plan; venue and diagnosis 97%; medications 93%; care coordinator 60%; MSE 70%; risk 50%; user-friendly information 23%; allergies 13%; service users copied in 3%.

result.intervention: Updated GP letter template with sections for allergies, risk, user-friendly information and copying patients; dissemination via huddles, trainee handovers, laminated copies and email
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Major trauma centre, Cambridge University Hospitals

cycle1.result: BOAST compliance result not reported; FUSION vs ORIF showed no significant difference in EQ-5D-5L (P = 0.13), FAAM-ADL (P = 0.20), FAAM-Sport (P = 0.34), infection (P = 0.55), surgical time (P = 0.91) or time to weight bearing (P = 0.39).

result.other_findings: 15 open talus fractures in 14 patients: 7 ORIF, 5 fusion; mean follow-up four years and one month.

result.topic: Antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring in learning disability
result.setting: CAMHS services, Surrey (children and young people with learning disability)
result.standard: NICE guidelines on antipsychotic prescribing (tool based on an RCPsych audit)

cycle1.result: 5 prescribed antipsychotics, all with documented reason for starting; for 4 started more than 12 months ago, side effects, EPSE, weight, BP, glycaemic control and lipids not documented; 1 had no review in 6 months; 3 reviews did not consider dose reduction or stopping.

result.other_findings: One patient transferred to primary care with clear transfer of prescribing responsibility and written guidance.

result.topic: COVID-19 vaccination offer and uptake in inpatients
result.setting: Acute adult psychiatric wards (male, female, PICU), Highbury Hospital, Nottingham
result.standard: Trust policy: all eligible patients offered COVID-19 vaccine

cycle1.result: 105 (31%) vaccinated or planned before admission; 100/234 (43%) offered; 59% (n = 59) accepted; 92% (n = 55) of acceptors received vaccine.

result.other_findings: Sectioned patients and those in psychotic clusters more often refused; acceptance 59% was below national 80%. Offering in rounds may have missed patients.

result.setting: Derbyshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust seclusion policy in line with Mental Health Act Code of Practice 2015: 1-hour and 4-hourly medical reviews, MDT within 12 hours, documented review content

cycle1.result: Reviewed within 1 hour 34%; 4-hourly 41%; internal MDT 47%; review documented 57%; ongoing concerns 50%; MSE 47%; physical health 42%; medication 44%; risk 44%; need for seclusion 58%; intervention 52%.

result.other_findings: 107 seclusion episodes in 61 patients; the seclusion review template was poorly used by medics.

result.setting: Inner city hospital psychiatric ward
result.standard: Mental Health Commission Judgment Support Framework version 5; target 100% physical examination on admission

cycle1.result: 3/13 had physical examination on admission (23% compliance); 6 had examination in ED before admission.

result.intervention: Results presented to MDT and NCHDs; colour-coded physical examination proforma developed and briefed to all staff

cycle2.result: 7 examined on admission, 2 refusals documented; 100% compliance (examination done or reason documented).

result.other_findings: Proforma to be audited every 6 months.

result.topic: Admission blood tests in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Psychiatric intensive care unit, KMPT trust
result.standard: RCPsych Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services: bloods within 24 hours of admission; standardised PICU blood panel

cycle1.result: 30% bloods within 24 hours, 10% on previous ward, 40% declined/unsafe, 20% not done in timeframe; 69% of direct admissions had all relevant tests, 23% some.

result.intervention: Standardised PICU guideline with pre-filled blood test request form

cycle2.result: Only 6% not done within 24 hours; all consenting direct admissions (89%) had all standardised tests; conclusion reports 77% to 100% for full tests and 80% to 94% within 24 hours.

result.other_findings: Completion remained lower for patients transferred from other wards. Plan to roll out pre-filled forms across all trust wards.

result.setting: Alcohol service, Lorraine Hewitt House drug and addiction service
result.standard: NICE recommendation for fibroscanning (target not reported)

cycle1.result: 37% normal; 16% liver stiffness >10kPa, 15 referred to liver clinic; steatosis stage 1 13%, stage 2 18%, stage 3 29%; 10/15 (66.7%) attended liver clinic.

result.other_findings: Scans covered about one third of clients with alcohol as primary substance; all had results discussed with lifestyle advice.

result.setting: Low secure services unit, Northern England, South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust standards for completion of the Formulation Information Risk Management (FIRM) assessment

cycle1.result: Current/historical risks 100%; formulation 89%; Staying Safe/Staying Well care plan 73%; service user involved 16%; updated since last CPA 70%.

result.intervention: Findings presented at local academic meeting and distributed to staff
result.other_findings: Formulation and care plan completion improved compared with earlier auditing in October 2021 (figures not reported). Patient involvement was low, often because FIRM was completed at night.

result.setting: Four old age psychiatry wards, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board, South Wales
result.standard: All-Wales DNACPR policy for adults (2015, revised 2024)

cycle1.result: Decision date missing in 2 forms; not signed with date and time in 1; not documented in clinical notes in 10; discussion with patient in 9; discussion with IMCA/attorney or family in 20; appropriate signatures in 17; 7 not countersigned in section 6.

result.other_findings: Different versions of the DNACPR form were in use. Recommended a unified form and adding DNACPR and treatment escalation status to the ward round proforma.

result.setting: Dublin North City and County CAMHS team
result.standard: Established ICP policy: every service user to have an individual care plan with key worker, formulation, goals, action plan, copy to family, review and discharge dates

cycle1.result: Overall ICP compliance 62%.

result.intervention: Findings and intervention discussed at multidisciplinary team meeting and wider CAMHS academic meeting
result.other_findings: Re-audit every three months recommended.

result.topic: GP referral quality to memory services
result.setting: Memory Clinic, South Sefton Neighbourhood Centre, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: 100% completeness of referral information (green ≥95%, yellow 75–94%, red <75%)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: History of memory loss 86%; duration of memory loss 46%; 8% reduction in documentation of impact on ADLs compared with 2019; about a quarter accepted on first referral; 70 inappropriate or declined.

result.other_findings: 17 initially rejected referrals were accepted after GPs gave further details. A new referral proforma has since been designed with the local ICB.

result.setting: Oxted Health Centre, semi-rural general practice with 16,300 patients
result.standard: NICE guidance on anti-resorptive or anabolic treatment after osteoporotic fragility fracture

cycle1.result: 51% not on any fracture prevention medication (reasons explained in 40%); 39% taking bisphosphonates; 10% prescribed but not taking oral bisphosphonates.

result.intervention: Dedicated clinics (telephone or face to face) to discuss management and start medication

cycle2.result: 49% started on medication; 9% refused; 17% deemed inappropriate; 25% had died or left the practice.

result.other_findings: Only direct consultation led to discussion and treatment.

result.setting: Paediatric intensive care unit

cycle1.result: Unit mean error rate 12.5%.

result.intervention: Automated Excel spreadsheet producing individual prescriber feedback forms, plus posters and discussion at clinical governance meetings

cycle2.result: Unit mean error rate 13.0%; in 7 prescribers with at least 5 items in both cycles, mean error rate fell from 15.3 (SD 14.6) to 9.4 (SD 7.3), p=0.29.

result.other_findings: Limited by few data per prescriber and variable prescribing volume.

result.setting: CMHT Inverness Sector A outpatient service, NHS Highland
result.standard: First appointment within 12 weeks of referral

cycle1.result: 140 (87.5%) given an appointment; mean wait 12 weeks for 103 (64%); 57 (36%) waited longer than 13 weeks; 20 (12.5%) referrals inadequate.

result.other_findings: Delays due to DNAs, cancellations and postponement awaiting information. Plans to flag the 12-week deadline in a database and improve referral information.

result.setting: Somerset NHS Foundation Trust (Severn Deanery), psychiatry placements
result.standard: Severn Deanery and Trust recommendation of one hour of supervision per week for psychiatry trainees

cycle1.result: Response rate 63%; 17% met supervisor only sometimes; WPBAs completed 89%; QI/audit discussed 66%; psychotherapy competencies partly discussed 42%.

result.intervention: Results highlighted in local teaching and audit meetings

cycle2.result: 9/27 responded (33%); 11% met supervisor only sometimes; WPBAs 88%; QI/audit discussed 60%; psychotherapy competencies discussed 75%.

result.other_findings: Most trainees were satisfied, but supervision needed protecting from clinical work.

result.setting: Ward 3 old age psychiatry inpatient ward, Wishaw General Hospital, NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists standards for ward rounds

cycle1.result: No up-to-date MDT checklist information; 10% individual food and fluid charts; 0% in folders.

result.intervention: Structured MDT ward round checklist developed through PDSA cycles, and food, fluid and weight charts kept in separate folders

cycle2.result: 44% up-to-date MDT checklist items; 100% food and fluid charts in folders.

result.other_findings: November 2021 showed a 73% increase in up-to-date checklist items; the January fall was attributed to Omicron staff sickness.

result.setting: Three hospitals contributing to the Australian and New Zealand Hip Fracture Registry

cycle1.result: Overall data agreement 82.3%; data completeness 95.6%.

result.other_findings: Half of disagreements were information discrepancies, a quarter missing data and a quarter time/date/number; transcription caused 1 in 50. A generic data quality audit framework is proposed.

result.setting: Department of general surgery, Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE and Good Medical Practice: written and verbal information for people with pancreatitis and families

cycle1.result: 60% not satisfied with information; none given written information; more than 90% not shown a diagram; not informed about investigations 40%, treatment 60%, verbal information 26%, alcohol as cause 27%.

result.intervention: Results shared with surgical team and patient information leaflet designed and given to every patient

cycle2.result: Improvement in almost all areas; overall satisfaction improved from 60% to 92%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Inpatient adult intellectual disability assessment and treatment unit, NHS Highland
result.standard: NHS Highland Seclusion Policy: 15-minute monitoring, reviews at 2 and 4 hours, Datix on commencement

cycle1.result: Anxiolytic use before seclusion, respiration rate and appearance at 15-minute checks, plans to end seclusion at 2 hours and informing duty consultant at 4 hours often missing; Datix not always submitted. No figures reported.

result.intervention: Results shared via Seclusion Policy Short Life Working Group, internal teaching, clinical governance forum and trainee induction; protocol drafts updated
result.other_findings: Commonest reason for seclusion was increasing agitation and aggression. Re-audit planned.

result.setting: CAMHS, West Glasgow
result.standard: NICE: height, weight, blood pressure, heart rate with centiles and growth charts for children on ADHD medication

cycle1.result: Height and weight 97%; BP and HR 100%; height/weight centiles and growth charts 85%; BP centiles 10%; HR centiles 0%.

result.intervention: Results presented at local department meeting and posters of NICE guidelines distributed

cycle2.result: Height, weight, their centiles, HR, BP and growth charts 100%; BP centiles 2%; HR centiles 0%.

result.other_findings: The electronic record cannot convert BP and HR to centiles, limiting compliance.

result.topic: Physical health equipment on psychiatric wards
result.setting: Four old age psychiatric wards, the Mount hospital
result.standard: CQC physical health recommended equipment list and equipment needed for NICE antipsychotic monitoring

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Recommendations from the first audit (details not reported)

cycle2.result: No ward had all equipment; 17.5–35% of recommended items unavailable; alcometer, Snellen chart, BMI chart and tuning fork missing on all wards; expired blood bottles and urinalysis sticks; only otoscope and ophthalmoscope not working.

result.other_findings: No significant improvement from the first cycle; variable ECG machine function means QT monitoring is unreliable.

result.topic: Handover between emergency department and psychiatric wards
result.setting: 9 mental health inpatient wards across 3 locations in one trust

cycle1.result: 28 (62%) had no SBAR handover documented; 8 (28%) no discharge summary; 5 had neither; 25 (56%) returned with ward actions, 5 (20%) of which were delayed.

result.other_findings: Extension of an earlier single-ward audit, showing improvement on previous findings (figures not reported). All but one ward identified handover problems.

result.topic: Delirium and dementia assessment in older inpatients
result.setting: Psychiatric liaison service, busy district general hospital
result.standard: Local and national delirium and dementia guidelines (4AT, PINCH ME)

cycle1.result: 51.3% referred to Delirium and Dementia team; PINCH ME used by referring team in 28.2% and by liaison in 10.2%; antipsychotics in 30.7%; follow-up arranged in 82.1%; 35% referred to memory clinic.

result.intervention: Educational initiatives and closer collaboration with the Delirium and Dementia team
result.other_findings: 43.6% had pre-existing dementia and 28.2% were admitted with acute confusion.

result.setting: Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust (trust-wide)
result.standard: CNTW seclusion policy: independent seclusion review must include an Approved Clinician

cycle1.result: Senior clinicians at ISR: 83% medical, 11% non-medical AC, 6% neither; 68% of medical clinicians not AC grade; 0% of non-AC medical ISRs documented discussion with an AC; 29% out of hours.

result.intervention: Seclusion policy changed so ISRs must be done by an AC except in extreme circumstances, when discussed with an AC
result.other_findings: 96 of 260 seclusion episodes triggered an ISR; 72% of non-AC doctors were SHO grade.

result.setting: Ten national hip fracture audits (international comparison)
result.standard: Fragility Fracture Network 2014 minimum common dataset (32 questions)

cycle1.result: 215 questions tabulated; 72 (34%) used in >1 audit, 32 (15%) by more than half; 21/32 (65%) MCD fields used by the majority; only three used by all ten audits.

result.other_findings: A revised minimum common dataset was developed with international feedback.

result.setting: Mental Health of Learning Disabilities team, Kent and Medway
result.standard: NICE guidance on ADHD medication monitoring in the past 6 months

cycle1.result: Weight measured in last 6 months 83%; pulse 76.5%; blood pressure 64%.

result.other_findings: 15% (N=97) of 629 MHLD patients had confirmed ADHD; 43% (N=42) of these were on medication, mostly methylphenidate (62%).

result.setting: Rheumatology department, South Eastern Health and Social Care Trust (Ulster Hospital)

cycle1.result: All had ESR and CRP; ANCA in 43 (3 positive); CT brain in 40; TA ultrasound once; CT-PET in 6; 70 TAB with 12 positive and 4 suggestive.

result.intervention: Rapid access GCA pathway being designed
result.other_findings: Temporal artery ultrasound and CT-PET were under-used.

result.topic: Eating disorder assessment and risk monitoring
result.setting: Tier 3 community CAMHS, South Lanarkshire, NHS Lanarkshire

cycle1.result: Recording: weight change 40%, hydration 40%, temperature 5%, over-exercising 85%, purging 75%, self-harm 85%, BP/HR 80%, ECG 75%, engagement 75%.

cycle2.result: Weight change 80%, hydration 70%, temperature 30%, over-exercising 90%, purging 85%, self-harm 90%, BP/HR 50%, ECG 40%, engagement 60%.

result.other_findings: Mean time to initial assessment 63 days (40% within 4 weeks); 15% received no intervention. Standard remains inadequate.

result.topic: STOMP/STAMP psychotropic prescribing and physical health monitoring
result.setting: Alders Warrington CAMHS, Mersey Care NHS
result.standard: RCPsych Position Statement PS05/21 (STOMP) and Mersey Care Consent to Examination and Treatment Policy SD06; 14 compliance standards

cycle1.result: Overall STOMP compliance 98% (significant assurance); indication documented for all; 1 (6%) had no behavioural support plan before medication; all had MDT before prescribing, 3-monthly reviews, specialist prescriber and capacity documented.

result.other_findings: Three criteria were not met. 3 (17%) had medication indicated for behavioural problems.

result.topic: Time to first appointment after referral
result.setting: Older People's Service CMHT, North Leeds, LYPFT
result.standard: LYPFT guidance: seen within 15 working days of referral (trust standard 80%); electronic documentation within 24 hours; GP letter within 2 weeks

cycle1.result: 70% seen within 15 working days; reason for delay documented 33%; electronic documentation 100%, within 24 hours 73%; GP letter sent 87%, within 2 weeks 33%.

result.intervention: Resident doctors added to gatekeeping assessment rota; reminders to document reasons for delay; record of patients not accepted with admin reminders to complete GP letters within 2 weeks

cycle2.result: 87% seen within 15 working days; reason for delay documented 40%; electronic documentation 97%, within 24 hours 61%; GP letter sent 79%, within 2 weeks 41%.

result.other_findings: Referrals rose from 80 to 100. Documentation timeliness gave mixed results under greater service pressure.

result.topic: Braun procedure for bile reflux after OAGB
result.setting: Single bariatric centre

cycle1.result: 35/1024 (3.4%) OAGB patients needed surgery for bile reflux; 31 had Braun procedure, 27/31 (88%) immediate resolution and 23 (74%) at 2 years; 4/31 (13%) failed and converted to RYGB.

result.other_findings: All 8 RYGB conversions had resolution at 1 year; Braun was a day case vs 2-day stay for RYGB.

result.topic: Methadone dosing in opioid substitution therapy
result.setting: Newcastle Treatment and Recovery (addictions service)
result.standard: Clinical guidance of therapeutic methadone dose 60–120mg; documented reason for sub-therapeutic dosing and evidence of instability

cycle1.result: 54% undergoing dose change; 46% maintained below 60mg (8 declined advised change, 15 no advice recorded); of 8 using illicit opioids, 63% advised increase but declined and 25% not advised; of 21 using other substances, 48% had no OST change considered.

result.other_findings: 285 patients were on <60mg. Recommendations were further training and at least 6-monthly strategic care plan reviews.

result.setting: Chesterfield Mental Health Liaison Team, acute hospital, Derbyshire Healthcare Foundation Trust
result.standard: 100% documentation of capacity assessment; minimum Grade 2 detail for all four functional stages

cycle1.result: Broad capacity assessment recorded in 90%; specific decision documented in 37%; no evidence (Grade 0) for Understanding and Communicating in 50%, and for Weighing-up in 40%.

result.intervention: Recommended mandatory MCA forms in the core electronic assessment template
result.other_findings: Re-audit planned in six months.

result.setting: Rathbone Rehabilitation Centre, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Smoking status recorded 47 (92%); 26/28 (93%) smokers offered support on admission; 24/31 (77%) offered support at regular intervals; 20/28 (71%) offered NRT; 5/31 referred to Nicotine Dependence Treatment Advisor.

result.intervention: Action plan: reminders via team meetings and emails, completion of physical health nursing proforma, and posters on the referral pathway
result.other_findings: 3 patients started smoking during admission.

result.topic: Handover information on transfer to emergency department
result.setting: Peter Bruff Mental Health Assessment Unit and Ardleigh Acute Inpatient Ward, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: PRSB Ambulance handover to emergency care standard V1.0: 100% of transfers with a doctor's support letter

cycle1.result: Peter Bruff: support letter in 1 of 6 transfers (17%); Ardleigh: 2 of 5 (40%).

result.intervention: Template care summary and handover letter created
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Rheumatology department, Glasgow Royal Infirmary, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde

cycle1.result: 30.89% lacked examination findings; 69.10% no further investigations documented beyond haematological/radiological; 53.65% had no differential diagnosis documented.

result.other_findings: 38.2% requested advice, 60.16% review and 1.63% takeover; ongoing education for resident doctors recommended.

result.setting: Acute old age psychiatry inpatient wards, Royal Edinburgh Hospital, NHS Lothian
result.standard: All inpatient deaths reported via DATIX

cycle1.result: 7/14 deaths reported on DATIX (all 3 unexpected, 4 expected); 50% not reported.

result.intervention: MCCD issuing made electronic and senior management informed all teams of the need to report every death
result.other_findings: Expected deaths in particular were not reported consistently.

result.topic: Coeliac testing in irritable bowel syndrome
result.setting: St Johns Surgery, large semi-rural general practice (11,250 patients), Bromsgrove
result.standard: NICE guidance: test for coeliac disease in patients with IBS symptoms

cycle1.result: 65/250 tested for coeliac disease; 185 not tested.

result.other_findings: No significant difference in poverty or depression between tested and untested patients; 137 untested had no further investigations.

result.setting: 15 UK centres; national, trainee-led, retrospective multicentre study

cycle1.result: 183 patients (34 primary, 149 secondary angiosarcoma); only 78.9% discussed at a sarcoma MDT meeting; recurrence at 5 years 14/28 (50%) primary and 80/124 (64.5%) secondary; median survival 5 years in both groups.

result.other_findings: Median latency from breast cancer to secondary angiosarcoma was 6 years; 94 recurrences in 162 patients (58.0%). Median 10-year PREDICT survival 69.6% versus 54.0% observed.

result.setting: HMP Birmingham (prison healthcare)
result.standard: NICE and Maudsley prescribing guidelines for physical health monitoring on antipsychotics (pre-prescription, 12-weekly and annual checks)

cycle1.result: Pre-prescription, 12-weekly and annual physical health checks had poor compliance (no figures given); checks that met NICE and Maudsley guidance were done by coincidence at diabetic reviews.

result.intervention: Planned: improved computer reminders and training of existing and new team members, with re-audit in 6 months.
result.other_findings: Antipsychotics were initiated by both GPs and psychiatrists; some were prescribed for unlicensed indications and some lacked documented diagnosis or indication. Average BMI was in the overweight range, up to 45.

result.setting: Multinational audit of elective curative oesophageal cancer surgery (TUGS)

cycle1.result: 318 (51%) had postoperative complications within 90 days; 31 (5%) intraoperative complications; reoperation rate 9.3%; 34 (11%) died because of a surgical complication.

result.other_findings: McKeown had more infective complications than Ivor Lewis (19% vs 11%, p=0.007); robotic-assisted oesophagectomy had the lowest complication, reoperation and mortality rates.

result.setting: Working-age adult acute inpatient psychiatric ward, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Trust
result.standard: DVLA guidance: patients admitted for serious mental illness should not drive for 3 months after stabilisation and should inform the DVLA

cycle1.result: Driving status explored 25%; of these 67% given DVLA advice and 67% told to inform the DVLA.

result.intervention: Added a 'driving status' field to the electronic ward round template to standardise screening at ward reviews.

cycle2.result: Driving status explored 85%; of drivers 86% given DVLA advice (from 67%) and 71% advised to contact the DVLA (from 67%).

result.other_findings: Further planned actions were ward posters, gathering information on MDT awareness and extending the audit to other wards.

result.topic: Osteoporosis specialist referral in rheumatoid arthritis
result.setting: Rheumatoid arthritis patients referred for DEXA, Barnet Hospital (Royal Free NHS Foundation Trust) and St George's Hospital
result.standard: NOGG 2022 guidance on specialist referral based on FRAX and other risk factors

cycle1.result: Mean major osteoporotic fracture risk 15.6 and hip fracture risk 4.7 over 10 years; 31.6% had previous fracture; 26.3% on steroids (10.5% high dose); 5% had received parenteral treatment. A significant number would need specialist referral under NOGG 2022 (number not given).

result.other_findings: 90% were female, mean age 63.2 years; 8% had recent fracture and 8% vertebral fractures.

result.topic: Teledermatology versus face-to-face skin cancer triage
result.setting: 2-week-wait suspected skin cancer clinics, tertiary dermatology department, Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital

cycle1.result: Follow-up needed in 11% (7/63) teledermatology and 11% (7/63) face-to-face; discharge 21% (13/63) vs 24% (15/63); surgical management 63% (45/71 lesions) vs 64% (44/69), P = 0.96.

result.other_findings: Only 2% (1/63) of teledermatology patients needed later in-person review and 2% (1/63) had a change in management.

result.setting: UK anaesthesia departments reporting to the 7th National Audit Project (NAP7)

cycle1.result: 52/197 (26%) departments employed anaesthesia associates; 71 of 10,009 respondents (<1%) were anaesthesia associates. Of 24,172 cases, anaesthesia associates attended 432 (2%) and were senior provider in 63 (<1%), with indirect supervision in 27 (43%).

result.other_findings: Anaesthesia associates reported less training and confidence in managing peri-operative cardiac arrest; 33 (47%) worked nights or weekends.

result.topic: Inpatient physical examination, chaperone and capacity documentation
result.setting: Rotherham psychiatric inpatient wards (acute adult, rehabilitation, PICU, older adult), RDaSH NHS Trust
result.standard: Trust standards: initial medical examination within 24 hours of admission, documented capacity to consent, chaperone for examinations beyond appearance, pulse or blood pressure, and chaperone gender preference offered

cycle1.result: Good results for examination within 24 hours and capacity consideration; inadequate results for chaperone presence and chaperone gender preference (no figures given).

result.intervention: Recommendations from the 2021 Trust-wide audit (not described).

cycle2.result: Nearly 90% examined by a doctor within 24 hours; chaperone documented in only 14%; no patient offered choice of chaperone gender; capacity documented in one third.

result.other_findings: Older adult wards performed better. Planned next step is teaching at junior doctor induction and a further re-audit.

result.topic: ECG on admission to psychiatric wards
result.setting: Three general adult inpatient wards, Clock View Hospital, Liverpool, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: ECG within 24 hours of admission, documented ECG report, and further investigation of abnormal ECGs

cycle1.result: 52% had ECG within 24 hours; no documented ECG report in 35%; 23% of abnormal ECGs further investigated.

result.intervention: Recommendations from the original audit (not described).

cycle2.result: 57 (62%) had ECG within 24 hours; 16 (17%) after 24 hours; 19 (21%) never; no documented report in 13%; abnormal ECGs further investigated in 9/16 (56%).

result.other_findings: Reason for not doing an ECG was documented for 32 (91%). Recommended an electronic alert if no ECG within 24 hours and copying reports to the ward clerk or consultant PA.

result.setting: CAMHS outpatient services in Rotherham, Doncaster and Scunthorpe, RDaSH NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust Promise 16: collate and compare outcomes; audit standards on use of outcome measures

cycle1.dates: November 2023 (discharges in the three months to September 2023)
cycle1.result: 11/15 young people had an outcome measure completed at some point; Scunthorpe 5/5 (usually only at the start), Doncaster 4/5, Rotherham 2/5.

result.intervention: Planned: use SystmOne to send outcome measures to patients' mobile devices and inform staff of expected use; re-audit in 2024.
result.other_findings: RCADS was the most used measure, followed by SDQ; type and frequency of use were not standardised.

result.setting: Dermatology department patch test clinic, Glan Clwyd Hospital, Bodelwyddan

cycle1.result: Positive reactions in 75.7% (n = 171); mean wait to patch testing 237 days (range 4–1706); allergic contact dermatitis diagnosed in 64.6% (n = 146).

result.other_findings: Commonest allergens were nickel (21.7%), fragrance mix I/II (15.5%) and limonene (13.7%). Re-presentation among patients on SOS or PIFU was 20%.

result.topic: Dementia with Lewy bodies diagnosis rates
result.setting: Memory Assessment and Treatment Services (MATS) Central, North and South, Manchester
result.standard: National benchmarks for dementia subtype diagnosis: DLB 5–15%, Alzheimer's 50–75%, vascular ≤20%, mixed 10%

cycle1.result: DLB diagnosis rate 2% (2/121).

result.intervention: Recommendations for greater awareness and potential use of the DIAMOND Lewy Toolkit.

cycle2.result: DLB diagnosis rate 2.85% (9/315); MATS Central 5% (7/133), North 1.5% (2/129), South 0%.

result.other_findings: Alzheimer's 30.7% (lower than expected); vascular 22%, mixed 28% and unspecified 16% (higher than expected). The toolkit was used only when DLB was already suspected.

result.topic: Geriatrician input for older emergency laparotomy patients
result.setting: Great Western Hospital, Swindon (district general hospital), emergency laparotomy patients aged over 70
result.standard: NCEPOD 2010 'An Age Old Problem': routine daily geriatric input for older surgical patients

cycle1.result: Mean length of stay 22.5 days; inpatient mortality 8.9%.

result.intervention: New geriatrician service: 4 hours per week consultant geriatrician and 2.5 days per week Clinical Innovation Fellow, with twice-weekly consultant-led ward rounds.

cycle2.result: Mean length of stay 17.8 days (4.7 days saved per patient); inpatient mortality 8.8%.

result.other_findings: 6.6% had a new medical diagnosis and 24.4% were followed up; estimated saving about £52,875 over six months.

result.setting: Male inpatient wards, St George's Park Hospital, CNTW NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE CG120 Coexisting severe mental illness (psychosis) and substance misuse

cycle1.result: 88.8% assessed for substance use in first week; 62.06% had specialist drug and alcohol service involvement on admission; 87.5% had ward policies followed; 42.8% had specialist involvement on discharge.

result.intervention: Planned: service evaluation of barriers to specialist service involvement and an educational programme for staff, especially nurses; re-audit in 6 months.
result.other_findings: Involvement of specialist substance misuse services at admission and discharge remained the weakest area.

result.topic: National anaesthetic workload and case mix
result.setting: 352 UK hospital sites delivering anaesthesia (NAP7 activity survey)

cycle1.result: Compared with NAP5 (2013), median age rose from 50.5 to 52.8 years, median BMI from 24.9 to 26.7 kg.m-2, ASA 1 fell from 37% to 24% and TIVA use rose from 8% to 26% of general anaesthetics.

result.other_findings: 352 of 416 invited sites (85%) took part; confirmed COVID-19 accounted for 149 (1%) cases.

result.topic: Physical healthcare equipment on psychiatric wards
result.setting: Forensic inpatient wards (low, medium, high and secure LD), Mersey Care secure division
result.standard: CQC 2019 'Brief Guide: Physical Healthcare in Mental Health Settings' recommended equipment

cycle1.result: Mean equipment availability 66% (range 50.9%–88.9%) in secure wards versus 75% (61.1%–88.9%) in non-secure control wards.

result.intervention: Findings presented and physical health equipment boxes placed in ward clinic rooms.
result.other_findings: Gloves, pulse oximeters, sphygmomanometers, thermometers and stethoscopes became available on all wards, but secure wards still lagged the non-secure controls; further re-audit planned.

result.topic: Early warning score accuracy and emergency team activation
result.setting: General medicine and surgery admissions, Wellington Regional Hospital
result.standard: New Zealand early warning score (NZEWS) calculation and MET callout criteria

cycle1.result: NZEWS correctly calculated and documented in 75.8%; 46.8% of 47 NZEWS instances mandating MET activation led to a callout; 20 of 23 patients meeting MET criteria had a callout.

result.other_findings: Only 12.8% of MET-mandating instances had a documented, accurately calculated NZEWS; mean nurse minus audit difference -0.19 (limits of agreement -3.64 to 3.26). 491 admissions were screened.

result.topic: Clozapine documentation in primary care records
result.setting: North Cornwall Community Mental Health Team, Cornwall Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Cornwall Partnership NHS Foundation Trust 'Procedure and Guidance for the Use of Clozapine' (MM/032/22)

cycle1.result: Clozapine on GP repeat prescription 93%; accurate dose and frequency documented 33%.

result.intervention: Dissemination of findings and targeted liaison with GP practices.

cycle2.result: Clozapine on repeat prescription 93%; accurate dose and frequency 80%.

result.other_findings: Residual inaccuracies persisted in a minority of cases.

result.setting: CMHT outpatient clinic, EPUT, with local GP surgeries
result.standard: MHRA guidance: women and girls of childbearing potential on valproate must be on a Pregnancy Prevention Programme; target 50% reduction in valproate prescriptions in this group

cycle1.result: 4/25 registered on the Pregnancy Prevention Programme; overall non-compliance 86%.

result.intervention: Planned: electronic alert to prompt registration and yearly reminder for the annual risk acknowledgement form (under discussion).
result.other_findings: Only 10 of 50 GP surgeries responded. A previous inpatient audit found none of 35 women of childbearing age on a pregnancy prevention plan.

result.topic: Suicide and self-harm risk assessment in depression
result.setting: Reedyford Healthcare Group primary care practice, Nelson
result.standard: NICE depression in adults: all patients asked directly about suicidal ideation and intent (100%); same-day specialist referral for significant risk (100%)

cycle1.result: 42 patients asked direct questions about self-harm and suicide; 2 patients at immediate risk urgently referred to specialist services.

result.other_findings: All patients at increased risk were given increased practice support.

result.setting: Realist synthesis of published and grey literature

cycle1.result: 69 articles included; four context-mechanism-outcome configurations identified: generating trustworthy data, encouraging audit participation, ensuring audit sustainability and facilitating audit cycle completion.

result.other_findings: Highlights balancing reliability with pragmatism, protecting human capital, fair and credible leadership and prioritising change facilitation.

result.setting: Older Adult CMHT receiving GP referrals for memory problems
result.standard: NICE-recommended eight dementia screening blood tests within the preceding 6 months; target 95%

cycle1.result: 15 (48%) had all 8 blood tests, 13 (42%) some, 3 (10%) none; mean 76.6% of recommended bloods completed; glucose most often omitted.

result.intervention: Business-card sized aide-memoires sent to all local GPs with a letter outlining the audit findings.

cycle2.result: 10 (50%) had all tests, 8 (40%) some, 2 (10%) none; mean 76% completed.

result.other_findings: Completion of glucose and liver function tests improved; practice still did not meet the standard and a third cycle was suggested.

result.topic: Patient experience of psychiatric ward rounds
result.setting: Acute adult, psychiatric intensive care and perinatal psychiatry inpatient units
result.standard: NICE CG136 and Trust policies on service user experience

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: More patients had weekly consultant reviews, felt comfortable speaking and felt physical health was attended to; but understanding of discussions, communication of schedule changes, satisfaction with environment and feeling involved worsened (no figures given).

result.other_findings: Data were collected by face-to-face questionnaire interviews using a modified Likert scale; a root cause analysis and improvement plan were proposed.

result.setting: NHS Northern Gambling Service, first assessment appointments

cycle1.result: Overall attendance 77% (299 attended, 87 DNA); DNA rates face-to-face 24%, virtual 22%, telephone 23%; chi-square 0.92 (critical value 5.99), no significant difference.

result.intervention: Supportive reminder letter for patients between referral and first assessment (implemented).
result.other_findings: No demographic data were collected, so confounders such as location could not be assessed.

result.setting: General paediatric dermatology department, St John's Institute of Dermatology, Guy's and St Thomas' Hospital, London
result.standard: BAD guidelines for methotrexate prescribing and monitoring

cycle1.result: Patient information leaflets 94%; baseline severity score (EASI/PASI) recorded 14%; baseline bloods 100%; week-4 nurse specialist review 86% (2018 figures). 57 patients across both cycles.

result.intervention: Local clinical guideline and standardised electronic initiation template, led by a clinical nurse specialist, introduced in 2022.

cycle2.result: Information leaflets 100%; baseline severity score 86%; baseline bloods 100%; week-4 review 100% (2025 figures).

result.other_findings: Pregnancy counselling documentation improved; test doses were discontinued by 2024–2025; dosing varied (0.19–0.40 mg/kg) in both cycles; telephone review helped week-4 monitoring.

result.setting: Four Community Learning Disabilities locality teams, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NHS England STOMP (Stopping Overmedication of People with a Learning Disability, Autism or Both) recommendations

cycle1.result: Good evidence of capacity, consent, best interests, MDT input and regular review of medication, side effects and response (no figures given); rationale for off-label use could be recorded more clearly.

result.other_findings: Twenty patients were randomly selected per team, excluding those not on psychotropics. Psychotropics still play a significant role in managing behavioural problems.

result.setting: Section 136 Mental Health Act assessments, Doncaster locality, RDaSH NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: GMC Good Medical Practice (clear, contemporaneous records by each doctor) and Mental Health Act Code of Practice 2015

cycle1.result: Documentation took over 1 day in 61% (14/23); within 4 hours in 26% (6/23); neither doctor documented in 70% (16/23); letter to GP by an assessing doctor in 22% (5/23).

result.other_findings: 9% (2/23) had no AMHP report or documentation. Nineteen assessments did not result in detention.

result.setting: Psychiatry of old age community services, North Dublin Mental Health Services for Older People
result.standard: NICE and Maudsley lithium monitoring guidelines

cycle1.result: Deficiencies in documenting side effects and interactions and in regular monitoring of eGFR and physical health (no figures given).

result.intervention: Lithium flowsheets for 3-monthly bloods, lithium stickers for nursing documentation, a two-page tick-box assessment form, a GP template prompting blood tests and a formal lithium policy.

cycle2.result: Significant improvements in lithium monitoring and documentation reported (no figures given).

result.other_findings: Patient education and documentation of side effects improved.

result.setting: Dartford, Gravesham and Swanley CMHT, Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: Trust guidelines: starting dose 2.5mg, review every 3–4 months, attempted withdrawal after 3 months

cycle1.result: 14/36 (39%) on regular procyclidine; 93% had recorded reviews; 0% on recommended starting regimen; no withdrawal plans documented.

result.intervention: Team-wide dissemination of findings and standardised prompts for dose-reduction discussions at reviews.

cycle2.result: 18/100 (18%) on procyclidine; dose reduced in 3/18 (17%) and reduction discussed in 4/18 (22%); 44% received active de-prescribing intervention or discussion.

result.other_findings: Project followed a fatal procyclidine overdose; 1/18 (6%) needed a dose increase.

result.setting: Rathbone Rehabilitation Centre (mental health rehabilitation unit)
result.standard: DVLA guidance on driving with psychiatric disorders

cycle1.result: Driving status documented in 9 (18%); vehicle type 0%; of 3 drivers, 2 (67%) advised on restrictions and 67% told of duty to inform the DVLA.

result.intervention: Action plan: record driving status and vehicle type on the Rio admission clerking proforma, inform patients at first ward review, and consider driving in risk assessment.
result.other_findings: All 51 (100%) had a mental health diagnosis documented.

result.topic: Lying and standing blood pressure measurement
result.setting: Geriatrics and other wards, Queen Elizabeth Hospital King's Lynn (secondary care)
result.standard: RCP guidance on orthostatic (lying/standing) blood pressure measurement

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Laminated copy of the RCP method placed in all Early Warning Score observation folders, with a dedicated lying/standing BP recording sheet.

cycle2.result: RCP guideline compliance 93.33%; symptom identification and documentation 100%.

result.other_findings: A 2018 re-audit showed marked improvement but still fell short of the RCP standard; the 2019 loop used a larger sample across more wards.
