result.topic: Anaesthetic technique and unplanned ICU admission after lung resection
result.setting: 16 UK thoracic surgical centres (ACTACC national audit)

cycle1.result: 253/11,208 had unplanned ICU admission (2.3%, 95% CI 2.0–2.6%); TIVA OR 0.50 (0.34–0.70) and epidural OR 0.56 (0.41–0.78) for ICU admission.

result.other_findings: Unplanned ICU admission was linked to higher mortality (29.00% vs 0.03%) and longer stay (26 vs 6 days).

result.topic: Advanced life support in intra-operative cardiac arrest
result.setting: UK hospitals reporting to the 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) registry

cycle1.result: Sustained ROSC in 425 (78%); 338 (62%) alive at reporting; in 365 with PEA or bradycardia, adrenaline given as 1 mg bolus in 237 (65%).

result.other_findings: Calcium given to 51 (9%) and sodium bicarbonate to 25 (5%), with specific indications in under half; precordial thump used in 14 (3%).

result.topic: Physical and cognitive assessment in alcohol detoxification
result.setting: Bridge House inpatient alcohol detoxification unit
result.standard: NICE guidelines and Trust policy: physical examination on admission and cognitive assessment before discharge

cycle1.result: Physical examination done in 98%; cognitive assessment before discharge in 7%.

result.other_findings: About 30% had cognitive assessment in the admission plan but it was not actioned before discharge; mean stay about 14 days.

result.setting: Rheumatology department, Manchester Royal Infirmary
result.standard: NHS England PIFU guidance: stable inflammatory arthritis, face-to-face review within 2–4 weeks of contact, around 5% of patients on PIFU

cycle1.result: Only 22 (17%) met NHS England criteria; 0% seen within the recommended time after contact; 1.5% of department patients on PIFU (target 5%).

result.other_findings: Three patients made contact (median 60 days after starting PIFU), two needing face-to-face review; one was seen at 6 weeks and one had no appointment 8 weeks after contact.

result.setting: Medium and low secure learning disability wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust policy SD28 'The use of seclusion and long-term segregation' and Mental Health Act Code of Practice 2015 chapter 26

cycle1.result: Initial medical review within first hour 34%; on-call consultant informed 50%; 4-hourly reviews 50%; responsible clinician present 67%; risk assessment 48%; medications commented on 20%.

result.intervention: Education of colleagues working in secure services.

cycle2.dates: One month, three months after actions
cycle2.result: Initial medical review within first hour 66%; on-call consultant informed 60%; 4-hourly reviews 66%; responsible clinician present 100%; risk assessment 89%; medications commented on 72%.

result.other_findings: Physical health reviewed in 100% in both cycles; 34% of MDT reviews still had only 2 MDT members; comment on reducing restriction rose from 59% to 84%.

result.setting: Two community mental health teams
result.standard: NICE guidelines and Trust policy on monitoring antipsychotic side effects using rating scales (GASS, LUNSERS, SESCAM) at three months and one year

cycle1.result: No rating scale used (0%); side effects documented informally in case notes in 96%.

result.other_findings: Extrapyramidal side effects were the most documented in both cycles.

result.topic: Vitamin D testing in alcohol and substance detoxification
result.setting: Bridge House Detoxification Unit (inpatient)
result.standard: NICE PH56: test and replace vitamin D in adults at high risk of deficiency

cycle1.result: No patient had vitamin D tested (0%).

result.intervention: Pre-populated admission blood form including vitamin D, used on the first day of admission.

cycle2.result: Compliance maintained at 90% in the third round.

result.other_findings: Three rounds with 76 patients in total; round two achieved 86.67%. Of 44 tested after the change, 30 (68.18%) were deficient or inadequate.

result.topic: SSRI monitoring in children and adolescents
result.setting: CAMHS
result.standard: NICE and Maudsley guidelines: review at one week and every 4–6 weeks after starting an SSRI, with monitoring of response and adverse effects

cycle1.result: Follow-up in 17/18; none within a week; median follow-up 42 days; improvement monitored in 88%; adverse effects monitored in 36%, not documented in 53%.

result.intervention: Recommendations: inform patients of side effects before starting, follow up within 4–6 weeks, discuss and document adverse events and response; re-audit.
result.other_findings: Dose was increased in 22% without clear documentation of adverse effect monitoring; one-week follow-up was judged impractical.

result.setting: Mental Health Service for the Elderly team, County Monaghan (Cavan and Monaghan Mental Health Service)
result.standard: NICE guidelines for lithium prescribing and monitoring

cycle1.result: All 3-monthly lithium levels completed; 100% given information booklets, record books and BMI recorded; 60% of six-monthly lithium levels completed; 20% of six-monthly bloods done but not documented.

cycle2.result: 100% completed three- and six-monthly lithium levels, with 100% documentation.

result.other_findings: Recommended a lithium clinic with blood pathways, reminder letters, recording tables, alert cards and written information.

result.topic: Mental Health Act assessment and bed delays for court diversion
result.setting: Liaison and Diversion Service at Willesden Magistrates Court, North West London
result.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice: up to 14 days from medical recommendation to conveyance; local standard of same-day admission for defendants liable to detention

cycle1.result: Referral to assessment time (available in 25/42) ranged from 1.5 to 22 hours; 2 defendants remanded overnight because assessment was not same day; of 25 Section 2 applications, no same-day bed in 7, with 4 remanded to prison.

result.other_findings: Medical recommendations were completed within 5 days and admissions within 14 days, but defendants were still remanded to custody; data were missing for some referrals.

result.topic: Prescribing safety in alcohol and opioid use disorder
result.setting: Umm Slal Treatment and Rehabilitation Center (mandated inpatient addiction rehabilitation)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Indication documented AUD 72%, OUD 78.9%; dose titration and adjustment 98–100%; missing liver or renal baseline results in 8.7% AUD and 10.5% OUD; ADRs documented in 18% AUD and 5.3% OUD.

result.other_findings: Drug interactions in about one-third of prescriptions, 25–29% higher-risk; documentation gaps and limited multidisciplinary ADR reporting persisted.

result.setting: South Gloucestershire Later Life Community Mental Health Team
result.standard: Nine standards from NICE and Trust guidelines (e.g. lithium level 3-monthly, kidney function 3–6-monthly, calcium 6-monthly); target 100%

cycle1.result: Average compliance 57%; six of eight standards below 60%, including lithium levels, kidney function and calcium.

result.intervention: Physical health nursing team took over investigations from primary care using a bespoke database, plus a staff education session (PDSA).

cycle2.result: Average compliance 94%; lithium level, kidney function and calcium monitoring 100%.

result.other_findings: Weight/BMI every 6 months and documented action plans for out-of-range results remained weak; a second PDSA cycle is planned.

result.topic: DNACPR discussions with patients and relatives
result.setting: Geriatric ward, Stafford County Hospital, University Hospitals of North Midlands

cycle1.result: 86% knew the implications of DNACPR; 50% knew it would not limit other treatment; 66% felt too little information was given.

result.intervention: Data presented and doctors taught effective DNACPR discussions using video demonstrations at weekly journal clubs; information leaflets distributed.

cycle2.result: 80% understood the DNACPR discussion; 76% knew it does not limit other treatment; 76% satisfied; 11/30 received leaflets.

result.other_findings: Of 35 doctors surveyed, 95% knew what a DNACPR discussion should include; barriers were not considering it, discomfort making the decision and fear of distress.

result.topic: Clozapine levels after change in smoking status
result.setting: East and West Hull community mental health teams
result.standard: MHRA Drug Safety Update August 2020: check clozapine levels when smoking status changes

cycle1.result: Clozapine level checked after smoking change in 42.86%; medical review after change in 19%.

result.intervention: Recommended: clozapine level within a week and medical review within two weeks of a change, and a smoking status section on the electronic clozapine monitoring form.
result.other_findings: 58 smokers on clozapine were identified, with 21 documented changes in smoking status.

result.topic: Preadmission handover for secure ward transfers
result.setting: Medium secure rehabilitation ward
result.standard: NICE NG53 1.2.7, Trust handover policy and QNFMHS transfer handover standard

cycle1.result: Lack of a structured approach to preparing for preadmission meetings (no figures given).

cycle2.result: No difference in overall information sought before and after; updates still needed on physical and mental health and third-party safeguarding.

result.other_findings: Using the checklist helped identify information gaps before the meeting so requests could be made in time.

result.setting: Havering Community Recovery Team, NELFT
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists consensus on high-dose antipsychotics as a time-limited trial with regular review and safety monitoring

cycle1.result: 16 (4.58%) on high-dose antipsychotics; 0/16 had the monitoring form; 12 (75%) had documented review, 4 (25%) none.

result.intervention: Recommended: staff education, better care plan documentation and wider availability of HDAP monitoring forms with pharmacy.
result.other_findings: First community audit of this topic in the Trust after yearly inpatient audits following a 2014 CQC inspection.

result.topic: Evaluation of national stroke audit programme
result.setting: Australian National Stroke Audit programme; national surveys and interviews

cycle1.result: 106 survey participants plus 14 clinician and 5 administrator interviews; audit valued for benchmarking but mixed views on local QI; data entry time was the main barrier (88%).

result.other_findings: Suggested improvements were refining questions, automatic export from electronic records and better data for inter-hospital transfers; 47 Australian data programmes were mapped.

result.topic: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Mill Lodge Tier 4 CAMHS inpatient unit, York
result.standard: Tier 4 CAMHS service specification 2.6.3: assessment, care plan and physical examination within 24 hours of admission (100%)

cycle1.result: Within 24 hours (excluding refusals): physical examination 85%, bloods 82%, ECG 84%; during admission bloods and ECG 100%, examination 90%.

result.intervention: Planned support for ward staff and on-call junior doctors; re-audit in twelve months.
result.other_findings: No reason documented for several missed procedures (3 examinations, 2 bloods, 3 ECGs); one blood test delayed by lack of blood tubes.

result.setting: ECT service, University Hospital Wishaw
result.standard: NICE ECT guidance on valid consent and Mental Health Act (Scotland) forms T2, T3A and T4

cycle1.result: Over 30% of cases lacked the documentation proposed by NICE; of cases with complete documentation, 25% were informal and 75% under the Mental Health Act.

result.intervention: Planned: dissemination to prescribing consultants and redesign of the ECT booklet to include required documents.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Acute medical wards, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (liaison psychiatry)
result.standard: Health board antipsychotic policy for delirium, based on NICE guidelines

cycle1.result: Antipsychotics prescribed in 57%; 100% compliance for appropriate drug, maximum dose and investigations (except chest X-ray and CT); antipsychotic stopped before discharge in only 54%.

result.intervention: Planned: periodic training for liaison practitioners and medical ward staff on delirium diagnosis and antipsychotic prescribing; re-audit after 6 months.
result.other_findings: Cause of delirium documented in 55%; 57.4% diagnosed by liaison psychiatry. Monitoring was assigned to the GP in 23% and the treating team in 23%.

result.setting: NHS Grampian CAMHS (Aberdeen City, Aberdeenshire and Moray)

cycle1.result: Referrals 3.19% of SIMD decile one versus 1.74% of decile ten; referral rejection 33% in decile one versus 21% in decile ten.

result.other_findings: Young people from the most deprived areas were 3 times more likely to need tier 4 care relative to population share; findings to be shared with multiagency stakeholders.

result.setting: Adult acute inpatient female psychiatric ward
result.standard: NICE guidance on PRN prescribing and local Trust policy

cycle1.result: PRN reviewed in last 7 days 25%; oral and IM grouped 7.2%; minimum dose documented 10.7%; maximum 24-hour dose 100%; indication 100%.

result.intervention: Guidelines added to junior doctor induction, weekly discussion with team pharmacist, prompts on the medication chart and weekly PRN review in ward MDT.

cycle2.result: PRN reviewed in last 7 days 56%; oral and IM grouped 28%; minimum dose 24%; maximum 24-hour dose 100%; indication 96%.

result.other_findings: Improvements did not reach the 100% standard.

result.topic: Frailty in emergency general surgery admissions
result.setting: Emergency general surgery admissions over 60 years in eight Irish hospitals

cycle1.dates: Fourteen consecutive days within a two-month period
cycle1.result: 52% (135/258 screened) had Clinical Frailty Score ≥4.

result.other_findings: Frailty was linked to more complications, MDT input, inpatient mortality (p=0.033) and 30-day readmission (p=0.020), and less discharge home.

result.topic: Prolactin, HbA1c and vitamin D monitoring on antipsychotics
result.setting: Five in-patient secure wards (medium and low secure, including Northside House)
result.standard: Best practice: at least annual HbA1c and prolactin for all; vitamin D only if symptomatic of deficiency

cycle1.result: 100% tested on the medium secure unit, but vitamin D tested without documented clinical indication; on the other units prolactin and HbA1c were least measured (18% male LSU, 23% female ward); vitamin D testing 38% female ward and 18% male ward.

result.intervention: Recommended adding prolactin and HbA1c to pre-CPA physical screens and stopping vitamin D testing without symptoms.
result.other_findings: The unit with a dedicated physical health team scored 100%; prolactin levels were highest on male medium secure wards.

result.setting: CAMHS consultant outpatient clinics, Black Country Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on writing clinic letters

cycle1.result: ICD-10 diagnosis 80%; medication indications 32.5%; physical measurements 55%; mental state 60%; risk assessment 70%; current medication 100%; allergies 27.5%; useful links 7.5%.

cycle2.result: ICD-10 diagnosis 100%; medication indications 56.6%; physical measurements 80%; mental state 88.3%; risk assessment 86.6%; current medication 90%; allergies 3.3%; useful links 13.3%.

result.other_findings: Copying patients or carers into letters fell from 100% to 86.6%. A QI project to collate useful links was proposed.

result.setting: General adult, old age and CAMHS acute mental health wards, Luton and Bedfordshire (East London NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Guidelines on PRN prescribing and regular review and discontinuation

cycle1.result: 84% prescribed PRN; 5 of 21 had PRN no longer clinically indicated but still active; PRN protocols not updated after legal status change in 2 patients; oral offered before IM as per guidance.

result.intervention: Recommended regular PRN review at ward rounds, discontinuing unused PRN, updating protocols after legal status change and MDT review for frequent PRN use.
result.other_findings: 10 of 21 were prescribed both promethazine and lorazepam; 6 of 21 needed more than 20 PRN doses since admission.

result.topic: Emergency department management of self-harm in young people
result.setting: Emergency departments of teaching hospitals linked to nine medical schools in England, Wales and Scotland
result.standard: NICE self-harm guideline (updated September 2022) for young people aged 8 and over

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: 82.0% were female and mean age was 14.7 years; the compliance table was not reproduced in the supplied text and some criteria may have been met but not documented.

result.setting: Tower Ward, Landermere Centre, Clacton on Sea, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Psychiatry Ward Review Safety Checklist items; 80% completion

cycle1.result: Legal status 93%; resuscitation status 39%; capacity 14%; deteriorating health 64%; physical health concerns 69%; medication review 81%.

cycle2.result: Legal status 88–100%; resuscitation status 42–53%; capacity 67–92%; deteriorating health 100%; physical health 88–92%; medication review 75–88% (across first-week, mid-point and pre-discharge reviews).

result.other_findings: The electronic checklist was introduced in 2018; all items were over 80% except resuscitation status (40–50%).

result.setting: Memory clinic (outpatient)
result.standard: Notification of diagnosis form completed for patients diagnosed with MCI or dementia; target 50% within 3 months

cycle1.result: 12/40 (30%) diagnosed patients were on the dementia register.

result.intervention: Raised awareness of the process and placed the notification form in all new patients' notes.

cycle2.result: Form completion 75% in November, 66.7% in December and 50% in January 2021.

result.other_findings: Completion declined over three months as forms stopped being placed in notes consistently.

result.topic: Timeliness of inpatient MDT formulation meetings
result.setting: Maple Ward, adult mental health inpatient ward, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: TEWV NHS Foundation Trust standard: formulation meeting within 72 hours of admission with full MDT participation

cycle1.result: 27% of cases met the 72-hour standard; mean interval admission to formulation 4.9 days (median 4; range 1–10 days).

result.other_findings: Psychologists (13%) and occupational therapists (25%) attended infrequently and carers were present in 46%; documentation gaps included missing capacity assessment (91%), legal status (55%) and clinical impression (49%). Recommendations included scheduling triggers, protected daily slots and a standard documentation template.

result.setting: Rheumatology Department, Salford Royal Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Ophthalmologists 2018 guidelines on hydroxychloroquine dosing and retinopathy screening

cycle1.dates: Patients starting HCQ April 2013 to November 2014, followed to 30 November 2019; screening 1 November 2018 to 30 June 2019
cycle1.result: Of 86 eligible patients, 23% were prescribed a dose of >5mg/kg/day; 10% had eGFR <60; none on tamoxifen. 29 patients attended screening and none had HCQ retinopathy.

result.other_findings: Of 207 patients who started HCQ, 43% remained on the drug at 5 years. A disproportionately high number of 'lost referrals' was being investigated, possibly due to IT issues or the paused screening service.

result.topic: Physical health assessment in alcohol use disorder
result.setting: Drug and alcohol treatment service
result.standard: Recent blood tests, FIB-4 scoring and FibroScan for clients with alcohol use disorder

cycle1.result: 175 (87.5%) had recent blood tests; 134 (67%) had all components to calculate FIB-4; 90 (40%) had undergone FibroScan.

result.intervention: Targeted clinician training, updated blood test request protocols to include all FIB-4 components, and revised guidelines to reoffer FibroScan to clients with abnormal liver function tests.
result.other_findings: AST was not routinely measured unless specifically requested, which not all staff knew. A follow-up audit was planned in six months.

result.setting: NHS Borders Mental Health for Older Adults Service memory assessment clinic
result.standard: All patients with suspected dementia should have a documented decision and rationale about neuroimaging, and the majority should be imaged unless clinical justification is recorded (NICE and SIGN guidance)

cycle1.result: Documented consideration of neuroimaging 59%; neuroimaging performed in 18%.

cycle2.dates: Referrals January to March 2024; reviewed February to August 2025
cycle2.result: Documented consideration of neuroimaging in 45 patients (88.2%); neuroimaging performed in 27 patients (53%).

result.other_findings: Of the 24 not imaged, eight (33%) had neuroimaging in the preceding two years; the commonest rationale for not imaging was that the diagnosis was already clear.

result.setting: Tertiary dermatology centre
result.standard: Consent documentation and governance standards for clinical photography (General Data Protection Regulation)

cycle1.result: Documented consent present in 75 of 200 (37.5%); 125 of 200 (62.5%) had no documented consent. Of documented consent, 55 of 75 (73%) on consent forms and 20 of 75 (27%) in clinical notes.

result.intervention: Development of CliniSnap, a secure digital photography workflow with patient identifier verification, in-app consent confirmation, no camera-roll storage and direct upload to the electronic record.
result.other_findings: Eleven of 211 image sets (5.2%) could not be matched to a patient encounter, highlighting traceability risks. Pilot and re-audit were planned.

result.setting: North West based primary care practice
result.standard: NICE: patients aged 18–25 started on antidepressants reviewed at 1 week; all others within 2 weeks

cycle1.result: Aged 18–25: median first follow-up 3 weeks, 8% compliance. Aged >25: median 4 weeks, 19% compliance.

result.other_findings: 58% had a mental health practitioner appointment mentioning medication within 4 weeks. A practice meeting, an MHP medication pro-forma and a re-audit in 6 months were planned.

result.setting: Inpatient forensic and rehabilitation psychiatry services, NHS Ayrshire & Arran
result.standard: Scottish Government 2017 National Standard for Monitoring the Physical Health of People Being Treated with Clozapine

cycle1.result: Fasting glucose in 10/18 and lipid profile in 12/18 in preceding 6 months; LFTs in 18/18 in last year; BMI, heart rate and blood pressure documented in all; ECG in 12/18 in last year.

result.intervention: Physical health monitoring checklist planned for forensic wards.
result.other_findings: The rehabilitation ward, which already used a monitoring checklist, achieved 100% adherence. Re-audit was planned in 6 months.

result.setting: Eight hospitals, emergency general surgery admissions (Irish Surgical Research Collaborative)

cycle1.result: 52% were frail (135/269); frailty was associated with more complications (p<0.001), longer stay (p=0.002) and higher one-year mortality (20% vs 8%, p=0.006). Only 16% of frail patients were seen by a geriatrician (20/122).

result.other_findings: Of 21 laparotomies, one patient was seen by a geriatrician.

result.setting: 19 of 39 inpatient and outpatient psychiatric units across North Wales
result.standard: Public Health England guidance on personal protective equipment

cycle1.result: About 50% of staff donned PPE as per guidance (Central 85%, West 22%); only 21% doffed as per guidance.

result.intervention: Planned designated donning and doffing areas, staff teaching sessions and reminders.
result.other_findings: There were no designated donning and doffing areas in outpatient units, and staff often did not wear masks within 2 metres of other staff.

result.setting: Seven CAMHS teams, south region of Derbyshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Locally agreed protocol for recording medication history in the specified section of PARIS

cycle1.result: 13% had medication recorded in the correct section of PARIS.

result.intervention: Teaching delivered to teams following the 2017 audit.

cycle2.result: 74% (n = 58) had medication recorded in the correct section of PARIS; of these, 86% had drug names correct, 79% correct dose, 71% correct frequency and 81% regular/PRN recorded.

result.other_findings: Compliance varied between teams from 0% to 100%. Further teaching was delivered and a move to combined documentation and e-prescribing (SystmOne) was supported.

result.topic: Physical observations documentation and NEWS escalation
result.setting: Mental health services for older people (MHSOP) inpatient wards
result.standard: Local and national guidance on recording physical (NEWS) and psychiatric observations

cycle1.result: Paper documentation: NEWS scores correctly documented 87%; raised NEWS scores escalated and reviewed 0%.

result.intervention: Introduction of Nervecentre electronic observation recording, which prompts when observations are due, calculates scores and allows direct escalation.

cycle2.result: NEWS scores correctly documented 100%; raised NEWS scores escalated to a senior and reviewed 80%.

result.other_findings: Improvement was seen in almost all physical observation domains, but psychiatric observations (still on paper) did not meet local or national guidance.

result.topic: Dementia referral pathway in intellectual disability
result.setting: East and West Kent Mental Health of Learning Disability (MHLD) teams, Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE NG54: refer people with learning disabilities and suspected dementia to a specialist psychiatrist

cycle1.result: 48% of dementia-related referrals accepted (82% East vs 25% West); psychiatric input in 84%; 77% redirected to MAS or CLDT; no confirmed diagnoses at initial or three-month follow-up.

result.other_findings: In a staff survey (n=18), 83% supported a formalised pathway and confidence gaps in diagnosis and prescribing were reported. 59% of referrals had Down's syndrome.

result.topic: Sliding hip screw versus intramedullary nail outcomes
result.setting: Scottish hospitals, Scottish Hip Fracture Audit data

cycle1.result: 9867 (72%) received SHS. No difference in 30 or 60-day survival; IMN had lower early mobilisation (OR 0.64, 95%CI 0.59–0.70; p<0.001) and lower discharge to domicile by day 30 (OR 0.77, 95%CI 0.71–0.84; p<0.001). Acute and overall LOS lower for SHS (11 vs 12 and 20 vs 24 days; p<0.001).

result.other_findings: Findings were similar in a subgroup of 559 AO A1/A2 fractures; LOS differences potentially increase cost by £1230 per patient with IMN.

result.setting: National Swiss federal statistics office (BFS) database

cycle1.result: Proportion operated in smaller hospitals fell from 38% to less than 20%; large cantonal hospitals rose from 50% to 71%. Only three centres performed a median of more than 100 resections per year.

result.other_findings: 6.7% of resections were in patients under 50, a 30% absolute increase over the period, with a late trend towards robotic access.

result.topic: Staff life support training on psychiatric wards
result.setting: Three acute inpatient psychiatric wards, Stepping Hill Hospital, Stockport
result.standard: NICE Clinical Guideline 25 (2005) and NPSA Rapid Response Report 2008/RRR010 on staff ability to respond to medical emergencies

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Nursing staff training met standards except for staff new to the wards or returning from prolonged leave; gaps found for other staff groups and for the remaining standards.

result.other_findings: Gaps were attributed mainly to new or bank staff covering wards without training or orientation to equipment and policies.

result.setting: Wards of Wrexham Maelor Hospital, general hospital
result.standard: Health board policy NU16 for alcohol withdrawal syndrome management, based on NICE guidelines

cycle1.result: Complete drinking history 4%; physical examination 84%; Wernicke's signs documented 20%; CIWA-Ar applied 44%, correctly scored 24%; benzodiazepines prescribed 38%; oral thiamine 58%; alcohol liaison opinion 16%.

result.intervention: Training programmes on alcohol withdrawal management by the alcohol liaison team for all clinical staff.
result.other_findings: Laboratory investigation compliance ranged from 16% for GGT to 84% for full blood count; 42% had IV Pabrinex two pairs three times daily.

result.setting: Two inpatient rehabilitation wards and one Day Hospital, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: International and European clinical practice guidelines on sarcopenia (screening, strength assessment, muscle quantity, physical performance measures, progressive resistance training and protein-rich diet)

cycle1.result: 0% screened with a validated tool; validated strength assessment 83.3% (15) DH and 33.3% (4) inpatients; 0% muscle quantity analysis; PPMs 66.6% DH and 33.3% inpatients; PRT prescribed 94% DH and 50% inpatients.

result.intervention: A multidisciplinary sarcopenia management pathway being implemented.
result.other_findings: Referral for nutritional assessment was 16.6% in DH and 75% of inpatients; all nine patients seen by clinical nutrition received a high-protein/high-calorie diet. Re-audit was planned.

result.setting: International multicentre Oesophago-Gastric Anastomosis Audit (OGAA) cohort

cycle1.result: AL/CN rates 19.3% handsewn, 14.0% linear stapled, 12.1% circular stapled (p<0.001); OR 0.63 (95% CI 0.46–0.86) for circular stapled vs handsewn.

result.other_findings: The effect was mainly in neck anastomoses (23.2% vs 14.6% vs 5.9%); chest anastomosis failure rates were similar across techniques.

result.topic: Mental health liaison one-hour response breach documentation
result.setting: Mental Health Liaison Team, A&E of a medium-sized district general hospital, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Core-24 one-hour response target with documented reasons for breaches

cycle1.result: 32 of 97 referrals breached the one-hour target (33%); 10 recorded a breach reason (30%).

result.intervention: Team agreed breach codes; the A&E assessment proforma was amended and emailed to all staff, with posters in the office as reminders.

cycle2.result: 20 of 44 referrals breached (45.5%); 9 recorded reasons (45%): staffing 6 (67%), multiple referrals 1 (11%), patient left 1 (11%), other 1 (11%).

result.other_findings: Documentation remained low; 50% fewer referrals were accepted during the re-audit, possibly due to the Christmas period.

result.topic: Absent without leave management in inpatient psychiatry
result.setting: Nile ward, 14-bed male psychiatric intensive care unit
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists' Quality Network for PICUs standards on leave planning, AWOL actions and carer involvement (eight criteria)

cycle1.result: All cases met six of eight criteria; carer involvement in 5 of 6; no patient had documented provision of crisis numbers before leave.

result.other_findings: Possible AWOL risk factors were disagreement between patient and team on the care plan and concerns about mental state. A QI intervention on crisis cards was planned.

result.setting: Bryngofal ward, adult general psychiatry inpatient ward, Hywel Dda Health Board
result.standard: Cycle 1: NICE review within 7 days for all and within 48 hours if at risk of suicide; cycle 2: RCPsych core standard of review within 3 days for all

cycle1.result: 42 of 44 (95%) followed up within NICE-recommended timeframes.

result.intervention: Staff education, reinforcement of discharge risk documentation and clarification of local follow-up standards (adoption of the 3-day RCPsych standard).
result.other_findings: Cycle 1 non-compliance related to transfer of care to another health board and incomplete discharge risk documentation; the single cycle 2 delay was due to a ward–community communication lapse.

result.setting: Rowan View medium secure hospital
result.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines 14th edition and Synnovis guidance: clozapine level taken 12 hours post dose

cycle1.result: Samples >15 hours post dose: OD 56.3% (31/55), BD pm evening/night 25% (3/12), TDS 16.7% (2/12), BD am/nocte 12.9% (9/62). Samples >12 hours: OD 63.6%, BD am/nocte 51.6%, BD pm 75%, TDS 41.7%.

result.intervention: Planned: informing teams of recent samples >15 hours post dose, service education and guideline change with pharmacy support.
result.other_findings: Timing inaccuracy was greatest with bespoke regimes; Maudsley guidance does not address bespoke dose timings. Re-audit planned in 12 months.

result.topic: Blood test requesting in mental health services
result.setting: Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team North East Kent
result.standard: Trust protocol for requesting blood tests, with documented clinical indication when deviating

cycle1.result: Trust policy not followed in 33.3% of cases, mostly TFT, folate and B12 requested without documented indication.

result.intervention: Trust policy poster made accessible in clinical areas, prescriber awareness of the policy, and documentation of indication when deviating from policy.

cycle2.result: Only 13.3% of cases did not follow the policy; documentation of rationale improved.

result.other_findings: Deviation from policy remained mostly requests for TFT, B12 and folate, though less frequent.

result.topic: Mental Health Tribunal report quality and timeliness
result.setting: The Cove CAMHS inpatient unit, Lancaster and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: 27 mandatory standards from the Mental Health Act Code of Practice, including timely report submission

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 94.4%; timely submission 64.3%; documented patient discussions 28.6%.

result.intervention: New administrative tracking system for legal deadlines and a clearer clinical pathway for recording patient discussions.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 97.1%; timely submission 100%; documented patient discussions 64.3%.

result.other_findings: 28 reports were reviewed across both years. A new digital template lacking prompts was linked to a compliance dip (85.2%), with omission of patient strengths and detention justifications.

result.setting: Gerontology wards, acute London trust
result.standard: National guidance on advance care planning

cycle1.result: Preferred place of death documented 24%; treatment escalation plan 41%; preferred place of care 59%; CPR recommendations most discussed.

result.intervention: New ACP toolkit, training programme and electronic ACP flowsheet in the patient record system, via PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Preferred place of death 60% (p 0.011); treatment escalation plan 75% (p 0.014); preferred place of care 71% (p 0.066).

result.other_findings: Spiritual needs, information needs, prognostic discussion, broader social needs and what mattered most to the patient did not improve significantly.

result.setting: On-call rooms, psychiatric services in Aneurin Bevan and Cwm Taf Morgannwg health boards and Elysium Healthcare, Wales

cycle1.result: On-call rooms frequently unclean, insect-infested, lacking bed linen and used as day offices. 626.3 miles driven in total, 247.4 miles home after on-call; doctors unsure or unable to drive home safely after 20 of 38 shifts.

result.other_findings: Doctors reported feeling frequently tired on 17 shifts and very frequently tired on 15 shifts when driving; kitchens lacked water access and lighting was poor.

result.setting: University Hospital Southampton patients managed in primary care
result.standard: Guidance recommending transition to an alternative osteoporosis therapy when denosumab is stopped, and pre-injection calcium and renal function checks

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: 19 (38%) had died. Of 15 no longer on denosumab, 9 (60%) had no alternative bone protection and 3 (20%) were on alternative therapy. Of 16 still on denosumab, 13 (81%) had pre-injection calcium and 12 (75%) renal function checks.

result.other_findings: Findings suggest inappropriate widespread discontinuation of denosumab without follow-on therapy, so targeted education of primary care physicians was recommended.

result.topic: Usability of audit and feedback reports
result.setting: General practitioners receiving the insurers' Primary Care Practice Report

cycle1.result: Qualitative study: GPs found the report poorly usable (not clinically meaningful, not recent, individual or reliable, unclear comparators and visuals) and were minimally motivated to change.

result.other_findings: GPs said well-designed feedback could motivate improvement but they receive many audit and feedback reports they hardly use.

result.setting: 51 UK rheumatology units, outpatient clinics
result.standard: BSR 2018 guideline for management of adults with SLE, NICE technology appraisal for belimumab and NHS England commissioning policy for rituximab

cycle1.dates: Any 4-week period between February and June 2018
cycle1.result: 1021 episodes of care audited; low documented compliance (<60% of visits) for formal disease-activity assessment, reduction of drug toxicity and protection against comorbidities; prednisolone recorded in 497 (49%) visits, including 28.5% of visits with inactive disease.

result.other_findings: Dedicated clinics had better urine protein quantification (85.1% vs 78.1%) and specialised centres better BILAG Biologics Register recruitment (89.4% vs 44.4%) and blood pressure recording (95.3% vs 84.1%). 286 (28.5%) had active disease.

result.setting: General adult psychiatry wards 1, 2 and 3, Mental Health Unit, Forth Valley Royal Hospital
result.standard: NICE 2016 guidance and local discharge policy: follow-up within 7 days of discharge

cycle1.result: 26 of 41 (64%) followed up within 7 days.

result.intervention: New discharge policy (April 2019), a 'Discharge Pause' sticker later made an electronic form, reminders to community mental health teams and a flowchart on who provides follow-up.
result.other_findings: An interim audit in May 2019 found 39 of 46 (84%) followed up within 7 days.

result.topic: Delirium screening in older surgical patients
result.setting: Surgical Assessment Unit, University Hospitals of Derby and Burton
result.standard: 4AT delirium screening of patients aged over 65 on arrival and at 48 hours

cycle1.result: 36% likely to have delirium on 4AT; 5% coded as delirium and 19% had delirium documented in notes; average 4AT completion 40%.

result.intervention: PDSA cycles introducing 4AT and delirium sections in care plans, plus teaching and supporting materials around the PINCHME acronym for SAU staff.

cycle2.result: Average 4AT completion rose from 40% to 64%, reaching 100% after interventions but falling back between them.

result.other_findings: Staff knowledge scores improved from 43% to 92% after teaching; length of stay was 10 days with delirium vs 5.3 days without. Improvements were not sustained and delirium champions were being explored.

result.setting: Early Intervention Service first episode psychosis team
result.standard: NICE guidelines on yearly physical health monitoring for patients on antipsychotics (BMI, BP, ECG, bloods, alcohol and smoking status); target 100%

cycle1.result: BMI recorded 91.67% (33); blood pressure 86.11% (31); substance use recorded 97.22% (35); ECG not recorded in 72.22% (26); full bloods up to date 75% (27); QRISK not collected in 22.73% (5/22) of eligible.

result.intervention: Planned presentation to team and physical health check clinics.
result.other_findings: Of 14 overweight or obese patients, 85.71% (12) received diet or exercise advice. Re-audit was planned at 3 months.

result.setting: Ty Llywelyn Medium Secure Unit
result.standard: BCUHB guidelines for physical health monitoring of adults prescribed antipsychotic therapy

cycle1.result: Waist circumference was not measured on patients in the previous audit.

cycle2.result: Waist circumference measured in 17 of 18; HbA1c showed 6 of 18 diabetic.

result.other_findings: By waist circumference 13 of 17 were obese and 3 overweight; by weight 11 obese, 4 severely obese and 1 overweight.

result.topic: Emergency laparotomy outcomes in older patients
result.setting: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) hospitals in England and Wales

cycle1.result: Patients ≥65 had higher 30-day (15.3 vs 4.9%) and 90-day mortality (20.4 vs 7.2%), longer LOS and more discharge to care homes (6.7 vs 1.9%); post-operative geriatrician review increased from 8.5 to 16.5%.

result.other_findings: Post-operative geriatrician review was associated with lower 30-day mortality (OR 0.38, CI 0.35–0.42) and 90-day mortality (OR 0.6, CI 0.56–0.65).

result.setting: Functional old age psychiatry Wards 3 and 4, The Mount, Leeds
result.standard: Discharge summary completed within 7 days of discharge

cycle1.result: Ward 3: 0 of 11 completed within 7 days; Ward 4: 23% of 13 met the target.

result.intervention: Proposed dedicated 4-hour weekly slot for junior doctors, assigning a responsible doctor at discharge and a quiet onsite workspace.
result.other_findings: Nine barriers were identified; lack of uninterrupted time and delayed doctor allocation were prioritised. The target was extended to 14 days.

result.setting: Memory clinic, Watermill resource centre, Berrywood Hospital
result.standard: GMC guidance on fitness to drive and DVLA reporting, and Driving with Dementia or Mild Cognitive Impairment Consensus Guidelines

cycle1.result: Informed to report to DVLA 73%; informed to report to insurer 45%.

cycle2.result: Informed to report to DVLA 80% (4 of 5 drivers); informed to report to insurer 0% overall (1 of 5 drivers, 20%). Risk assessment recorded in 34 of 40.

result.other_findings: No documentation of advice on the consequences of not reporting; 3 patients were referred to occupational therapy for driving assessment. Use of a standard template was recommended.

result.setting: Psychiatry ward, Allied Hospital 2, Faisalabad, tertiary care hospital

cycle1.result: 156 charts with 624 prescriptions showed severe discrepancies, including missing dose, frequency, strength and start/end dates.

result.intervention: Faculty-led workshop and mandatory teaching sessions for residents on prescription documentation.

cycle2.dates: About three months later (dates not reported)
cycle2.result: 200 charts with 650 prescriptions showed much improvement in all highlighted areas (figures not reported).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Management of missed appointments in community mental health
result.setting: West Essex community mental health teams
result.standard: Trust policy on non-attendance (DNA) and disengagement

cycle1.result: 98.1% notified adequately with letters to patient and GP; risk assessment completed in 50.9%; risk assessment updated in 25%; contingency plan reviewed for 26 patients; family contacted for 3.

result.other_findings: Police/welfare checks were done for 4 patients and 31 were discharged after not responding. Risk assessment updates, crisis plan review and welfare checks fell short of policy.

result.setting: Mid Essex ECT clinic, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Legal status documented 5%; written consent/Form 5 95%; Mini-ACE 5%; MADRS 0%.

result.intervention: Checklists and assessments introduced after an earlier QIP, then ECT discharge summaries generated for every patient from November 2021.

cycle2.result: Legal status, written consent/Form 5, Mini-ACE and MADRS all 100% (excluding patients who did not complete treatment).

result.other_findings: Discharge summaries improved communication with referring clinicians and patient and carer satisfaction.

result.topic: Carbon footprint of shoulder dislocation pathways
result.setting: Emergency department of a major trauma centre

cycle1.result: 13 actions identified with potential saving of 86.4 kgCO2e per patient; estimated 2666 tonnes CO2e across England for 2022/2023.

result.other_findings: Traumatic dislocation without fracture made up 68.2%; 59.7% were aged 15–34 and 70.8% were male.

result.setting: Tertiary paediatric hospital, paediatric and surgical teams, Sydney Children's Hospital Randwick
result.standard: Evidence-based guideline for timely intravenous-to-oral antibiotic switch within 24 hours of eligibility

cycle1.dates: Baseline, before guideline launch (dates not reported)
cycle1.result: 32/50 (64%) switched within 24 hours of eligibility; median time to switch 15 hours 42 min.

result.intervention: Guideline launch with team-based education, audit and feedback.

cycle2.dates: Post-implementation within a 12-month project (dates not reported)
cycle2.result: 203/249 (82%) switched within 24 hours (p=0.006); median time to switch 4 hours 20 min (p=0.0006).

result.other_findings: Median hospital stay fell by 14 hours (p=0.008); readmission and restarting IV therapy did not change significantly.

result.setting: Community mental health team
result.standard: NICE: lipids at baseline, 3 months after starting a new antipsychotic, then annually; lifestyle advice and QRISK3 assessment

cycle1.result: 36 of 39 (92%) had lipids checked in last 12 months; 21 of 39 (54%) had cholesterol over 5.0; 9 of 39 (23%) had documented lifestyle discussion; 0 of 39 (0%) had QRISK3 assessment.

result.intervention: Planned presentation to the CMHT and teaching on lifestyle advice and QRISK3.
result.other_findings: 17 of 56 clozapine patients were excluded as already on cholesterol-lowering medication.

result.setting: Non-critical care internal medicine resident wards, DHR Health, Edinburg, Texas
result.standard: Inpatient hyperglycaemia guidelines; aim to reduce glucose values above 180 mg/dL by 30%

cycle1.result: 25.1% of glucose values were above 180 mg/dL.

result.intervention: Three PDSA cycles of resident education plus a pharmacy and resident audit and feedback process.

cycle2.result: 23.0% of glucose values above 180 mg/dL (p<0.05); 1045 audits of 16 095 accu-checks, mostly compliant with guidelines.

result.other_findings: The 30% reduction aim was not met, suggesting prescribing behaviour was not the key driver of hyperglycaemia; the intervention was well accepted by residents.

result.setting: Springs Centre, 17-bed male locked secure rehabilitation ward for autism and learning disability
result.standard: NICE guideline recommendations on monitoring metabolic side effects of antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Blood pressure, BMI and HbA1c recorded in 100%; lipid profile 86.6%; waist circumference 60%.

result.other_findings: 79% had excess central adiposity, about 40% were obese and 20% of males had type 2 diabetes and smoked.

result.setting: Two mental health inpatient wards (one male, one female)
result.standard: Local and national clinical coding guidelines

cycle1.result: 5 (25%) had coding completed during admission; 1 of 4 (25%) updated after diagnosis change; 3 of 9 (33%) physical health diagnoses coded; 16 (89%) coded on last discharge.

result.intervention: Doctors informed about clinical coding, how to access the form and its importance through teaching sessions and doctor communication groups.

cycle2.result: 10 (50%) had coding completed during admission; 3 of 4 (75%) updated after diagnosis change; 2 of 7 (29%) physical health conditions coded; 12 (75%) coded on last discharge.

result.other_findings: Physical health coding remained poor; posters and regular reminders were suggested.

result.topic: Work impact of early inflammatory arthritis
result.setting: National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit

cycle1.result: 5999 (47%) in paid work ≥20 hours/week; of 2793 WPAI completers at diagnosis, 200 (7.2%) had stopped work and 344 (12.3%) changed jobs; absenteeism 30% and presenteeism 40%.

result.other_findings: During follow-up 9.4% stopped work and 14.6% changed roles, with work drop-out almost entirely among routine (manual) occupations.

result.topic: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Old age psychiatric inpatient unit, Wrexham, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: Local Health Board acute inpatient admission policy: clerking and physical examination within 12 hours, bloods and medication chart within 2 hours, ECG at admission

cycle1.result: Clerking within 12 hours 67%; physical examination 52%; bloods within 2 hours 24%; ECG at admission 14%; medication chart within 2 hours 90%.

result.other_findings: Barriers included patient agitation, poor inter-team communication, no online handover system and junior doctor workload; recommendations included handover, training nurses and HCAs in phlebotomy and ECG, and ward-based doctor cover.

result.setting: Psychiatric inpatient wards using EPMA in an NHS trust
result.standard: Trust guidelines on safe deprescribing (name and row crossed, ID, reason code, stop date)

cycle1.result: Less than 33.88% of deprescribed medications met the standards on paper Kardex.

result.intervention: Transition from paper Kardex to an electronic prescribing and medicines administration (EPMA) system.

cycle2.result: 100% compliance with the previously measured standards; reason stated for 'other' option in 94.5%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Irish university teaching hospital, University Hospital Limerick
result.standard: Irish Heart Foundation Council for Stroke 2015: alteplase 0.9 mg/kg up to 90 mg

cycle1.result: Weights available in 92/107; 21% (19/92) received the correct 0.9 mg/kg dose, 54% (50/92) within ±10%, 25% outside ±10% (11% under- and 14% over-thrombolysed).

result.other_findings: 17/92 had intracranial haemorrhage, of whom 35% (6/17) had received a dose >10% higher. Weight was not documented in 15 (9 by omission).

result.setting: European Pediatric Surgical Audit (EPSA) Delphi panel, 59 hospitals in 17 countries

cycle1.result: Delphi of 96 professionals and 8 patient representatives (response rate 73%) agreed a core set of 11 baseline characteristics, 5 outcome, 2 structure and 7 process indicators.

result.other_findings: Six indicators were universally prioritised; the indicators are to be implemented in EPSA.

result.setting: Tertiary care psychiatric facility
result.standard: Rapid tranquillisation protocol for psychiatric emergencies (stepwise de-escalation, oral then IM medication, post-administration monitoring)

cycle1.result: Only 60% adhered to recommended protocol steps; 68% bypassed oral medication or de-escalation; vital sign monitoring after administration not recorded in 30%.

result.other_findings: 12% needed a second injection, with the interval undocumented in 15% of these; medication unavailability affected 8% of aggressive cases, and ECG before haloperidol was omitted.

result.setting: Working-age adult outpatients, 8 sector teams, Dudley mental health services
result.standard: NICE CG185; locally agreed 3-monthly lithium levels, 6-monthly U&Es and TFTs, and lithium results reviewed and documented at every outpatient review

cycle1.result: 3-monthly lithium monitoring 10%; 4 or more lithium tests in 12 months 17.5%; mean 2.67 tests per patient; results documented at clinic review 67.5%.

cycle2.result: 3-monthly lithium monitoring 17.5%; 4 or more tests 32.5%; mean 3.3 tests per patient; results documented at clinic review 62.5%; U&Es 6-monthly 90%; TFTs 6-monthly 85%.

result.other_findings: A lithium blood monitoring clinic was proposed to improve compliance.

result.topic: Cervical spine imaging in older head injury
result.setting: Emergency Department, Stoke Mandeville Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Trust guidelines based on the Canadian Cervical Spine Rule for c-spine imaging in patients over 65

cycle1.result: 16% had CT c-spine in addition to CT head; c-spine examination documented in 16% of those without CT c-spine.

result.intervention: Results presented at an ED education meeting and posters of CT c-spine indications displayed around the ED.

cycle2.result: 38% had CT c-spine; documented c-spine examination in those not imaged remained 16%.

result.other_findings: An older person's trauma team with age-appropriate triage was proposed.

result.topic: Young onset dementia assessment and support
result.setting: Shepway Community Mental Health Service for Older People
result.standard: NICE dementia guidelines and Royal College of Psychiatrists recommendations for young onset dementia service provision

cycle1.dates: Patients open within the last 2 years (dates not reported)
cycle1.result: Mood considered in all; young onset bloods when indicated 89%; physical examination 43%; all had imaging; named practitioner in half; cognitive stimulation therapy and post-diagnostic support offered to 79%.

result.other_findings: There was no named lead for young onset dementia; referral to diagnosis took 6 months for Down syndrome dementia and 5.5 months for other types.

result.topic: Physical health information in psychiatric discharge letters
result.setting: Male and female inpatient wards, Foss Park Hospital, York
result.standard: 100% of Lester Tool data (smoking status, BMI, ECG, blood pressure, blood results) included in discharge documents

cycle1.result: No discharge had 100% compliance; on average 23% of Lester Tool information included; no cholesterol ratios recorded; BMI 50%; smoking status 27%.

result.other_findings: 40% of female ward and 15% of male ward discharges had none of the data recorded.

result.setting: Adult community mental health team
result.standard: NICE: baseline height, weight, pulse, blood pressure and cardiovascular assessment before stimulant treatment, then 6-monthly weight, blood pressure and pulse

cycle1.result: Baseline blood pressure 57% (19); pulse 39% (13); weight 51% (17); cardiovascular assessment 6% (2). At 6-month follow-up (10 patients), 0% had blood pressure, pulse or weight documented.

result.intervention: New proforma for baseline and 6-monthly physical health monitoring to be placed in case notes; results presented at CMHT meeting.
result.other_findings: Re-audit was planned for March 2023.

result.topic: Pulmonary rehabilitation enrolment and completion inequalities
result.setting: National Respiratory Audit Programme pulmonary rehabilitation services, England and Wales

cycle1.result: 72 085 (82%) enrolled and 52 669 (60%) completed; lower odds of enrolment and completion with age <60, female gender, MRC 5 and most deprived IMD quintile.

result.other_findings: Black ethnicity had higher odds of enrolment (OR 2.16) and completion (OR 1.50) than White ethnicity.

result.setting: General surgery department, University Hospital Hairmyres
result.standard: RCSEng guidelines on operation note content

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Departmental education presentation and posters in theatres as reminders.

cycle2.result: Improved documentation of elective/emergency, time, anaesthesia type, indication, position, findings, tissue removed, blood loss, antibiotics and DVT prophylaxis; figures not reported in the abstract.

result.other_findings: Documentation of date, assistant name, incision, closure and signature worsened; 193 of 239 notes were handwritten. Extra headings on the op-note and digital operation notes were suggested.

result.topic: Memantine prescribing and renal function checks
result.setting: Old age psychiatry outpatient clinic, Ribchester Centre, Bury
result.standard: NICE guidelines on memantine indications and renal function review before prescribing

cycle1.result: Only 3 of 12 memantine prescriptions had a NICE diagnostic indication documented; all had eGFR and renal function documented in GM records, but 7 did not have these in clinic correspondence.

result.other_findings: 395 dementia patients were screened; memantine was used as adjunct in two cases and for severe Alzheimer's disease in one.

result.topic: Withholding antihypertensives after hip fracture surgery
result.setting: Orthogeriatric ward, Lister Hospital, East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust
result.standard: Pre-emptive holding of ACE inhibitors and calcium channel blockers for 48 hours after neck of femur fracture surgery

cycle1.result: Antihypertensives appropriately held in 40% of cases; mean days with severe hypotension 0.62.

result.intervention: Induction teaching for resident doctors and a revised post-operative proforma prompting holding of ACE inhibitors and CCBs.

cycle2.result: Antihypertensives appropriately held in 88% (p = 0.04); mean days with severe hypotension 0.28 (p = 0.03); hypotension incidence fell from 35% to 28% (p = 0.01).

result.other_findings: 75% were on at least one antihypertensive on admission; in cycle 1, holding was associated with fewer days of severe hypotension (0.36 vs 0.64, p = 0.03).

result.setting: University Hospital Galway, Emergency Department and ward consults (Liaison Psychiatry/on-call Psychiatry)

cycle1.result: 28 presentations; 23 (82.1%) seen in ED; 19 (67.9%) needed an interpreter; 16 (57.1%) related to low mood with or without suicidal ideation; 16 (57.1%) referred to a Community Mental Health Team.

result.other_findings: Descriptive service review with no standard; suggests translated patient information documents to improve care.

result.topic: Low FODMAP diet response in IBS
result.setting: St Mary's Hospital, London (dietetic service)

cycle1.result: Of 80 treated, 46 had follow-up data; at least 70% improved for each symptom; bloating 93% improved, flatulence 92% improved; mean stool consistency 5.21 to 4.16 (Bristol); mean stool frequency 3.87 to 1.56 per day.

result.other_findings: 27 of 80 did not attend follow-up and 7 were awaiting follow-up; use of the diet increased each year since 2009.

result.setting: Dorset Healthcare Liaison Psychiatry services
result.standard: NICE NG225: comprehensive biopsychosocial assessment for self-harm or suicidal ideation, using standardised template headings

cycle1.result: Presenting Situation 100%; Mental State Examination 98%; Risk Summary 98%; Psychiatric Formulation 92%; Social Situation 81%; Physical Health History 75%; Safeguarding Concerns 71%; Carer/Parent's Understanding 40%.

result.other_findings: Psychiatric headings well completed but social aspects, especially family understanding, poorly assessed; qualitative work on barriers planned.

result.topic: DNAR and ceilings of care documentation
result.setting: Sligo University Hospital, Model 3 hospital, adult medical inpatients
result.standard: Irish Health Service Executive (HSE) national DNAR guidelines

cycle1.result: DNAR status documented in medical notes 35%; reasoning 32%; patient discussion 45%; reasons if patient discussion excluded 41%; relatives' discussion 48%; reasons if relatives excluded 18%.

result.intervention: Two education sessions for NCHDs and consultants.

cycle2.result: DNAR status 35% and reasoning 32% (unchanged); patient discussion 61%; reasons if excluded 66%; relatives' discussion 48% (unchanged); reasons if relatives excluded 25%; ceilings of care documentation increased (ICU three-fold, intubation two-fold) but still under 15%.

result.other_findings: Ceilings of care documentation remained under 15%; authors propose a Ceilings of Care document.

result.setting: Specialist Geriatric Ward, Connolly Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Irish National Audit of Dementia-2 (INAD-2) recommendations and National Clinical Guideline 21 dementia care standards

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 69%; delirium recognition 53%; nutritional care 84%; food within reach 38%; safe mobility 80%; pain assessment 0%; personal preferences documented 40%.

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary Dementia/Delirium Care Bundle: staff training, bedside identifiers, personalised care plans and environmental changes (orientation boards, activity resources, dementia signage).

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 87%; delirium recognition 89%; nutritional care 95%; food within reach 100%; safe mobility 100%; pain assessment 100%; personal preferences 88%; antipsychotic prescribing practices improved by 37%.

result.other_findings: 27 patients across pre- and post-implementation audits; documentation gaps remain and sustainability work is needed.

result.setting: Nottingham University Hospitals, high-volume oesophago-gastric resection unit
result.standard: Trust ERAS protocol for oesophagectomy and gastrectomy (oral intake, drain, catheter and epidural removal, mobilisation, discharge medications)

cycle1.result: Oral diet started on time 85%; epidural removal 52.6% (95% within 24 h); catheter 55% (90%); apical drain 55.6% (100%); basal drain 53.8% (85.7%); abdominal drain 81.8% (90.9%); daily mobilisation 65%; VTE prophylaxis 100%; discharge medications 86.7% to 100%.

result.other_findings: All mobilised within four days; mean stay 9 days post-oesophagectomy; 3.2% emergency department return rate.

result.setting: Geriatric wards, Royal Glamorgan Hospital, district general hospital, South Wales

cycle1.result: Baseline cognition, falls history, memory loss and personality changes each documented in fewer than 40% of patients.

result.intervention: Concise collateral history proforma introduced (PDSA 1), then refined after staff feedback (PDSA 2).

cycle2.result: After second PDSA cycle: falls documented in all patients; memory loss, mood and personality changes each over 75%; smoking, alcohol and finances consistently captured.

result.other_findings: First PDSA re-audit (30 patients, 2 months) showed falls and baseline cognition over 70% and mood, memory and personality coverage more than doubled.

result.topic: Missing person rapid risk assessment completion
result.setting: Royal Cornhill Hospital, NHS Grampian, general adult, older adult and learning disability wards
result.standard: Missing Person Protocol Rapid Risk Assessment proforma completion, in line with the National Framework for Missing Persons

cycle1.result: Previous audit figures not given; first audit in 2017.

result.intervention: Teaching around the RRA and weekly review of the RRA at MDT meetings.

cycle2.result: 100% of notes contained the RRA proforma; average completion of all sections 87.5%; 14.5% improvement compared with previous audit and 21% since 2017.

result.other_findings: Brief Admission Details poorly completed and no ward had completed the Return to Ward Questionnaire; completion best in learning disabilities and worst in general adult wards.

result.setting: Single centre, Kingston, Ontario

cycle1.result: Appropriate albumin use by indication 30%; about 800 vials per month.

result.intervention: Dissemination of evidence-based recommendations, new electronic order set, education, prescriber interviews and a return policy change to reduce wastage.

cycle2.result: Appropriate use 50% (p<0.0001); usage fell to 450 vials per month, mainly less 5% albumin (p<0.0001); less wastage (p=0.017).

result.other_findings: Mortality, length of stay and new kidney replacement starts unchanged; estimated annual saving CAN $300 000.

result.topic: Antipsychotic high-dose and PRN prescribing governance
result.setting: Early Intervention in Psychosis service, Leicester
result.standard: BNF dose limits, PRN governance (instructions, review, benzodiazepine PRN 4 weeks or less) and HDAT form completion

cycle1.result: Exceeding BNF maxima 1%; polypharmacy 5.6%; PRN not reviewed 1.9%; PRN instruction missing 1.1%; benzodiazepine PRN over 4 weeks 0.26%; HDAT forms completed 1/378 (0.002%).

cycle2.result: Exceeding BNF maxima 2.9%; polypharmacy 10.4%; PRN not reviewed 1.45%; PRN instruction missing 2.1%; benzodiazepine PRN over 4 weeks 2.70%; HDAT forms 3/482 (0.62%).

result.other_findings: Most measures worsened; recommends EHR hard-stops, automated benzodiazepine review prompts, a polypharmacy proforma and HDAT training, with a third cycle.

result.setting: Galway University Hospital, tertiary acute stroke centre
result.standard: Practice compared with the intervention arms of the RESTART and SO-START trials (no guideline stated)

cycle1.result: 42 (75%) survived to discharge; 25% of those on antiplatelets restarted at one year (mean 20 weeks to restart); 70% of those on oral anticoagulation restarted at one year (mean 14 weeks); none with MRI-confirmed amyloid angiopathy (n=5) restarted (p<0.01).

result.other_findings: Fewer patients restarted antiplatelets than anticoagulants despite trial evidence supporting both.

result.setting: 28 centres, cardiology and cardiac surgical patients under anaesthesia, ACTACC national audit

cycle1.result: 17 major complications (palatal injury or gastro-oesophageal disruption), incidence 0.08% (95% CI 0.05-0.13%), about 1:1300; 7 deaths, 0.03% (95% CI 0.01-0.07%), about 1:3000.

result.other_findings: About 40% of patients with a complication died; most complications occurred in patients without known risk factors.

result.setting: Teiripe sa Bhaile integrated early supported discharge programme, St James's Hospital and The Meath Community Unit, Dublin
result.standard: Chartered Society of Physiotherapy hip fracture rehabilitation: start within 72 hours of discharge and two hours of rehabilitation per week until goals met, with an outcome measure

cycle1.result: All patients seen within 72 hours of referral and received on average 3 hours per week of rehabilitation; mean FIM improvement 36.35; mean hospital LOS 14.8 days with TsaB versus 54 days.

result.other_findings: Rockwood frailty score improved from 5.6 to 3.14; no 30-day readmissions; about 4 bed days saved per week.

result.topic: Antipsychotic side-effect monitoring (GASS) for depot patients
result.setting: Swale Community Mental Health Team, Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: Trust and NICE guidance: GASS at one month after starting depot and at least every six months thereafter

cycle1.dates: 1 Nov 2023 to 30 Jan 2024 (monitoring reviewed Jan 2022 to Oct 2023)
cycle1.result: 5% (1/20) had six-monthly GASS assessments.

result.intervention: Staffing improvements including a new pharmacy team and increased awareness of guidelines.

cycle2.dates: 15 Jan 2025 to 30 March 2025 (monitoring reviewed Jan 2024 to Dec 2024)

result.other_findings: Reasons for missed assessments were often undocumented; patient refusals persisted.

result.topic: Peri-operative cardiac arrest in frail older patients
result.setting: Royal College of Anaesthetists 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) activity survey and cardiac arrest registry

cycle1.result: 1676 (26%) of 6466 patients over 65 were frail (CFS 5 or more); 156 (18%) of 881 cardiac arrests were in frail over-65s, incidence 1 in 1204 and mortality 1 in 2020, about 2.6-fold higher than non-frail.

result.other_findings: Hip fracture, emergency laparotomy, emergency vascular and urological surgery were the commonest procedures in frail patients who arrested.

result.topic: Blood test result actioning and communication
result.setting: 57 general practices across all four UK nations (Primary care Academic CollaboraTive)

cycle1.result: Auditors agreed with actioning in 89.9% (n=2311); specified action carried out in 89.7% (1015/1132); no evidence of result communication in 47% (n=1210), and in 30.6% (360/1176) with abnormal results.

result.other_findings: Of 117 unactioned results, 2 were high risk and 1 came to harm; large variation between practices; practices received benchmarked reports.

result.setting: Medical gerontology rehabilitation ward, Tallaght University Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians National Audit of Continence Care (NACC) standard

cycle1.result: 26 (83.9%) wore incontinence wear, 21 (80.8%) by choice; urinary incontinence documented in 13 (41.9%).

result.intervention: Continence added to NCHD teaching schedule and MDT proforma adjusted to include a patient-specific continence record.

cycle2.result: 27 (67.5%) wore incontinence wear, 19 (70%) by choice; urinary incontinence documented in 18 (45.7%).

result.other_findings: Prevalence of incontinence unchanged; many patients preferred incontinence wear, so future work should engage patients.

result.topic: Fracture liaison service falls assessment and exercise referral
result.setting: Irish Fracture Liaison Services, national FLS Database and Facilities Audit
result.standard: IOF Capture the Fracture KPIs: falls risk assessment and strength and balance exercise referral

cycle1.result: 51% of 3,770 fragility fractures assessed for falls risk (range 2-90%); one third of these referred or advised to self-refer to strength and balance programmes; at 16 weeks 56% contactable, of whom 21% had started a programme.

result.other_findings: Five of six Dublin hospitals reported access to programmes versus none outside Dublin; four hospitals reported no patient exercise participation at 16 weeks.

result.setting: Luton & Dunstable University Hospital, general surgery
result.standard: NICE guidance: liver function tests and ultrasound first line for suspected gallstones, MRCP/EUS if not detected

cycle1.result: 44 CT scans; CTAP as first scan in 38 patients.

result.intervention: Findings presented at local general surgery clinical governance meeting and communicated to hospital doctors.

cycle2.result: 31 CT scans (30% decrease); CTAP as first scan in 21 patients (45% drop).

result.other_findings: Ultrasound still not always first line owing to clinical judgement, different requesting specialties, unawareness of NICE guidance and ultrasound delays.

result.setting: Four Black Country Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Teams (Dudley, Walsall, Sandwell, Wolverhampton)
result.standard: All patients discharged from CRHT should receive planned follow-up within 3 months of discharge

cycle1.result: Wolverhampton: all had 72-hour follow-up but 12% lost to long-term follow-up or in crisis first; Dudley 51% and Sandwell 47% followed up within 3 months; Walsall followed up all unless discharged to GP.

result.other_findings: 30 patients went into crisis before planned follow-up; one patient died by suicide 4 months after discharge without follow-up.

result.setting: Southmead Hospital, North Bristol NHS Trust, emergency laparotomy patients aged 70 and over
result.standard: NELA standard: geriatrician review of all patients aged 70 or over, target 80%

cycle1.result: Geriatrician review 16% (n=5); inpatient mortality 23% (n=7); discharge home 68% (n=21); mean LOS 17.6 days.

result.intervention: Dedicated gastrointestinal surgery geriatric liaison service established in August 2018 replacing ad hoc reviews.

cycle2.result: Geriatrician review 86% (n=43); inpatient mortality 14% (n=7); discharge home 76% (n=38); mean LOS 17.9 days.

result.other_findings: National compliance with this standard was 23%; one patient in each cohort newly discharged to a nursing home.

result.topic: Bone protection first dose before discharge in orthogeriatric patients
result.setting: Ageing and Complex Medicine orthogeriatric service, Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NHFD and NOGG: bone health plan and first dose of bone protection during hospital stay

cycle1.result: 90% had a bone health plan; only 33% of these received first dose before discharge; treatment delayed in 56% and not given in 10%.

result.intervention: Teaching session, new trust guidelines, redesigned electronic note for documentation and inclusion in orthogeriatric induction.

cycle2.result: 100% had a bone health plan; 81.25% given first dose of IV bisphosphonate before discharge (48.25% improvement).

result.other_findings: Barriers included unclear documentation, inadequate vitamin D/calcium replacement and not obtaining consent during admission.

result.setting: Paediatric dermatology clinics, Birmingham Children's Hospital
result.standard: Dedicated consultant clinic slot directly bookable by ED (local booking rules)

cycle1.result: Only 85 (41.1%) of slots used by ED referrals; 92 (44.4%) GP, 15 (7.2%) internal, 9 (4.3%) external, 6 (2.9%) own department; median wait 2 weeks; attendance 84.7%.

result.other_findings: ED treatment appropriate in 56% and not assessable in 28%; problem resolved by appointment in 20%; plans to reinforce booking rules and reinstate dermatology teaching in ED.

result.setting: Specialist NHS drug service, West London
result.standard: Best practice recommendations for initiation and monitoring of naltrexone

cycle1.result: All patients had keyworker involvement and physical health checks; 18 of 28 took naltrexone over one week; 16 reported reduced cravings; 6 abstinent and 10 partial response; 9 of 18 had side effects.

result.other_findings: Diagnostic coding and recording of the offer of written information need improvement.

result.setting: Ipswich Hospital, UK district general hospital
result.standard: Comparison with the PANC study; Royal College of Radiologists guidance on CT use

cycle1.result: Gallstones 45% (PANC 50.6%), idiopathic 33% (PANC 22.4%), alcohol 18%; 45% of idiopathic cases had further screen and 10% EUS; CT used in 51% (PANC 53%); antibiotics within 48 hours in 55% (PANC 34.6%).

result.other_findings: 33% of patients with diagnostic amylase had a CT, suggesting CT overuse against RCR guidance.

result.setting: Geriatric service, Beaumont Hospital, Dublin, tertiary hospital
result.standard: HIQA National Standard for Patient Discharge Summary Information (25 variables), 80% completeness per variable

cycle1.result: 17 of 25 variables 100% complete (automatically included); discharge medication and follow-up over 80%; allergy status 27%; blood and radiological investigations 49%.

result.other_findings: Automated fields achieved 100%; recommends automatic inclusion of investigation reports.

result.topic: Lifestyle factor documentation in psychosis clinic letters
result.setting: Leicestershire Early Intervention in Psychosis team
result.standard: Gold standard: all seven pillars of lifestyle medicine explored at each medical review

cycle1.result: For all domains 'not mentioned' was most common, ranging from 48.6% to 70.8%.

result.intervention: Findings shared with team, educational poster created and electronic system being adapted to record lifestyle factors (re-audit planned in 12 months).
result.other_findings: Second commonest finding was 'mentioned with no further details' for all domains except refraining from toxins.

result.setting: Five residential psychiatric rehabilitation units
result.standard: NICE, IDF and WHO: metabolic screening every 6 months for patients on long-term psychotropics

cycle1.result: 15.15% had complete screening within six months; 30.30% incomplete; 54.55% missing data.

result.intervention: Structured metabolic screening tool, GP coordination and staff education.

cycle2.result: 66.67% screened within six months; 33.33% not screened within six months.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Mental Health Act T3 medication authorisation compliance
result.setting: 16-bed Old Age Psychiatry ward, Hollins Park Hospital
result.standard: Mental Health Act medication authorisation (T3) forms: zero administrations outside authorised route or frequency

cycle1.result: Four off-T3 medication incidents; mean staff knowledge score 58%; confidence 3.7/5.

result.intervention: Visual whiteboard above the drug trolley identifying patients with active T3 forms, plus targeted teaching using real incidents.

cycle2.result: Zero off-T3 incidents for four consecutive months; knowledge score 71%; confidence 4.3/5.

result.other_findings: Staff reported the visual prompt aided adherence.

result.setting: Southland Hospital, Invercargill, orthopaedic and geriatric shared care

cycle1.result: Orthopaedic ward LOS 9.8 days; rehabilitation ward LOS 19.9 days; patients with a complication 71.6%.

result.intervention: Collaborative orthopaedic and geriatric shared care model introduced in 2012.

cycle2.result: Orthopaedic ward LOS 7.5 days (p=0.138); rehabilitation ward LOS 9 days (p<0.001); patients with a complication 57% (p=0.045).

result.other_findings: Adjusted odds of complication reduced by 12% (p<0.001); no difference in mortality.

result.setting: Ely Neighbourhood Team, Old Age Community Mental Health Team, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE guidance on routine antipsychotic monitoring (BMI, ECG, bloods, lipids, HbA1c, pulse and BP, LFT, EPSE) over 12 months

cycle1.result: All offered monitoring (1 declined); blood monitoring 94%; pulse and BP 100%; 29% (5) lacked an ECG despite needing one; 65% (11) not asked about EPSE/movement disorders.

result.other_findings: Recommends closer collaboration with GPs to improve ECG and movement disorder monitoring.

result.topic: CAMHS to adult mental health transition
result.setting: North Devon Liaison and Home Treatment Teams, Devon Partnership NHS Trust
result.standard: Devon Partnership NHS Trust transfer of care SOP (8 core transition standards), target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: 100% of specialist CAMHS users secured AMHS input; 57% had a care plan with defined exit; 14% given explanation why services could not be offered; 14% allocated a doctor on transfer; 29% had a documented joint CAMHS-AMHS meeting.

result.other_findings: Of 51 young people, 28 were formerly known to CAMHS and 12 underwent transfer; re-audit planned after change.

result.setting: 18 UK district general hospitals, children with suspected appendicitis (PAPAYA study)

cycle1.result: Negative appendicectomy rate 21%; PAS not correlated with histological appendicitis (rho=0.004, p=0.951); ultrasound findings not associated (p=0.336); 87% with non-visualised or equivocal ultrasound had appendicectomy with normal histology.

result.other_findings: Retrospective cohort study showing wide variation in diagnostic pathways.

result.setting: Medical gerontology ward, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: HIQA National Standard for Patient Discharge Summary Information

cycle1.result: 97% (30/31) had discharge summaries; patient identifiers, dates, clinical course, investigations, medications and author 100%; referral source 20%; dietary interventions 13%; immunisation 0%; follow-up guidance 77%; social care actions 27%; advice and future plans 20%; information given to patient/carer 10%.

result.other_findings: Ward doctors now receiving education on documenting functional status, social care and diet; mandatory electronic fields suggested.

result.setting: University Hospital Waterford trauma unit and pilot six-bed rehabilitation unit at Kilcreene Regional Orthopaedic Hospital

cycle1.result: Median wait for off-site rehabilitation across the south-east was six days.

result.intervention: Pilot six-bed hip fracture rehabilitation unit with orthogeriatric-led weekly MDT meetings and ward rounds.

cycle2.result: 15 of 17 transferred same day or day after being rehabilitation ready; longest wait three days (two patients).

result.other_findings: Hospital average hip fracture LOS 17 days (19 days awaiting off-site rehab) versus national average 12 days.

result.setting: Pain clinic, Sunnybrook Health Science Centre, tertiary teaching hospital, Toronto

cycle1.result: 174 completed follow-up; 55 (31.6%) had no benefit; 119 (68.4%) had good (>50%) to excellent (>80%) pain relief lasting 6 to 24 months.
