result.other_findings: 35 patients lost to follow-up or had incomplete data.

result.setting: South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust, trust-wide
result.standard: NICE guidance on EUPD: no drug treatment specifically for EUPD, time-limited crisis prescribing only, regular reviews and written information

cycle1.result: 81.6% (71) prescribed medication; 39.4% (28) consistent with time-limited prescribing; 57.7% (41) had timely reviews; 4.2% (3) had evidence of written information.

result.other_findings: Results presented to the Clinical Reference Group and a working group formed to improve prescribing and written information.

result.setting: Adult inpatients of a general psychiatric hospital
result.standard: NICE: prolactin checked 6 months after starting then every 12 months, with enquiry about symptoms (not required for aripiprazole, clozapine, quetiapine, olanzapine under 20 mg)

cycle1.result: Prolactin measured in 80.6% (25/31) in last year; 48% (12/25) hyperprolactinaemic, with action in 5 (41.7%); of 9 on drugs needing monitoring for a year, 8 (88.9%) measured, 5 elevated, action in 3 (60%).

result.other_findings: Hyperprolactinaemia in 58.3% of women and 38.5% of men; 25.8% on two antipsychotics.

result.setting: Orthogeriatric care, Forth Valley Royal Hospital
result.standard: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit 2023 and 2024 recommendations: timely vitamin D and IV zoledronic acid

cycle1.result: Vitamin D administration 14.71%; IV zoledronic acid 12.12%.

result.intervention: Staff education, process standardisation, Bone Health stickers and whiteboards, formal referral pathways and decision-making protocols.

cycle2.result: Vitamin D administration 100%; IV zoledronic acid 95.45%.

result.other_findings: 165 records analysed November 2023 to May 2024; initial data capture inaccurate owing to inconsistent referral system use.

result.setting: General adult community mental health service, HSE North Dublin Mental Health Services
result.standard: NICE: 6-monthly TFTs and U&Es, documented lithium levels, clinical review of results and structured follow-up

cycle1.result: Fell short across all standards, with deviations of 21% to 36%.

result.intervention: Nurse-led lithium monitoring clinic (January 2025) with structured appointments, reminders, GP collaboration and systematic documentation, plus team psychoeducation.

cycle2.result: All parameters over 85% compliance; largest gain in documentation and clinical sign-off of investigations (+29.2%).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Mossley Hill older adult inpatient and outpatient service, Liverpool
result.standard: NICE NG97 and BNF/SPC renal function (eGFR) recommendations, with GP communication

cycle1.result: Renal function documented in 68%; GP informed of medication change in 86%; initiation mostly in line with NICE.

result.other_findings: Recommends an electronic memantine prescribing checklist.

result.topic: Antipsychotic use for non-cognitive symptoms of dementia
result.setting: Acute care older adult ward, Cork University Hospital

cycle1.result: Median 14 patients per month on an antipsychotic (range 7-18); median 5 on PRN antipsychotics (3-12); median 2 given IM injection (1-3).

result.intervention: Multicomponent PDSA intervention: antipsychotic decision algorithm, CNS-led review, behaviour charts, staff education and coaching, 'Get-to-Know-Me' document and distraction resources.
result.other_findings: Some evidence of reduced PRN and IM use in new admissions, but long-stay patients had high antipsychotic use; reasons for PRN often undocumented.

result.setting: UK tertiary referral centre (Southmead Hospital, Bristol)
result.standard: Melanoma Focus standards for ano-uro-genital mucosal melanoma

cycle1.result: 83% first assessed in gynaecology urgent suspected cancer clinic; 83% biopsied before resection; staging CT 93%; lateral margins involved in 53%; no patient had formal quality-of-life assessment.

result.other_findings: 28% had died; local standard operating procedure developed.

result.setting: CAMHS, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, trust-wide
result.standard: NICE guidelines on prescribing for children with autism spectrum disorder

cycle1.result: 44% had alternative interventions before medication; consent documented in 62%; psychotropics started at minimum effective dose; follow-up within 3-4 weeks in 70%; 77% on sleep medication, 55.5% of whom had alternatives first.

result.other_findings: Marked variation between localities.

result.topic: Pre-operative fluid fasting in hip fracture
result.setting: Tertiary university hospital, Cork University Hospital, operative hip fracture patients
result.standard: Fasting 6 hours for solids and 2 hours for clear fluids; SipTilSend clear fluids until transfer to theatre

cycle1.result: Previous PDSA cycle average fluid fasting 3 h 45 min.

result.intervention: Reinforcement through staff education, ward prompts and MDT engagement with nursing, orthogeriatric and anaesthetic teams.

cycle2.result: Mean fluid fasting 11.2 hours (median 9.75 hours, range 0-36 hours), worse than previous cycle.

result.other_findings: No peri-operative aspiration events; compliance with SipTilSend deteriorated over time.

result.topic: COVID-19 impact on foot and ankle surgery
result.setting: 43 centres in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland (FAlCoN national audit)

cycle1.result: COVID-19 infection 0.53% (n=35), highest in lockdown 2.11% and lowest after 0.16%; lockdown activity 24.44% of pre-lockdown; elective activity 1.73% in lockdown and 10.72% after.

result.other_findings: Highest regional infection rate in South East England (3.21%); national peak 1.37% in final week of lockdown.

result.setting: General medical and surgical wards, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin, patients over 65
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians National Audit of Continence Care (NACC) standard

cycle1.dates: Three-day period at start of continence awareness month
cycle1.result: All had documented continence status; of 44 continent pre-admission, 12 had incontinence wear as inpatients.

cycle2.result: All had documented continence status; of 40 continent pre-admission, 14 had incontinence wear as inpatients.

result.other_findings: Rationale for incontinence wear varied and was sometimes undocumented; use increased between audits.

result.setting: Psychiatry of Old Age service, Sligo Leitrim Mental Health Service
result.standard: Developing national Model of Care for Dementia in Ireland and best practice

cycle1.result: Lack of standardised memory assessment, delays in neuroimaging and laboratory results, and gaps in staff training (no figures reported).

result.intervention: Care pathway document, staff training with standardised assessment scales, improved laboratory/radiology booking and an OT cognitive remediation group.
result.other_findings: Preliminary data show improved satisfaction in the cognitive remediation group; equipment audit led to improvements.

result.topic: Adjuvant chemotherapy outcomes in pancreatic cancer
result.setting: Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma

cycle1.result: 209 (69%) had adjuvant chemotherapy; median OS gemcitabine 21.6 months (ESPAC 4 25.5), gemcitabine-capecitabine 25.2 months (ESPAC 4 28), FOLFIRINOX 19.9 months (PRODIGE 24 54.4).

result.other_findings: FOLFIRINOX completion rate 17%.

result.setting: Bournville Ward, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, geriatrics
result.standard: Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham guidelines: conservative measures (fluid, fibre, exercise) before laxatives

cycle1.result: Constipation recognised in 57%; 64% of these developed it in hospital; 20% had complications.

result.intervention: Teaching sessions for ward staff and weekly MDT discussion of constipated patients, with early non-laxative measures if bowels not opened for over 2 days.

cycle2.result: Patient education up 19%, cause recognition up 27%, non-laxative methods up 30%; inpatient-developed constipation down 6% and complications down 4%.

result.other_findings: Only a small impact on constipation prevalence and complications.

result.topic: Psychotropic prescribing audit tool in residential care
result.setting: Single residential care facility, Cork

cycle1.result: Pilot of audit tool acceptability: all 15 auditors found the audit relevant and training and manual useful; some needed extra support.

result.other_findings: Difficulties included reading handwriting, locating information and prescribing inconsistencies; suggestions to shorten manual and add glossary.

result.setting: Acute Frailty Unit and two Elderly Care wards, Maidstone General Hospital
result.standard: European Society of Cardiology heart failure guidelines 2023

cycle1.result: Phenotype in clerking 18% (5/28) and discharge notes 39% (11); iron deficiency investigated 43%; iron infusion 5/12 (42%); SGLT2i 10/22 (45%); ACE/ARB/ARNI 3/9 (33%); MRA 3/9 (33%).

result.intervention: Departmental teaching, discussing HF phenotype at board rounds, ward round teaching, governance presentation and posters.

cycle2.result: Phenotype in clerking 23/42 (54.7%) and discharge notes 27/42 (64.3%); iron deficiency investigated 69%; iron infusion 14/15 (93%); SGLT2i 22/28 (79%); ACE/ARB/ARNI 17/18 (94%); MRA 13/13 (100%).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Heddfan Psychiatric Unit, Wrexham, general adult inpatients, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: Core psychiatry trainee competencies, NICE guidelines, local BCUHB physical health policy and Department of Health VTE guidance

cycle1.result: Baseline audit showed incomplete vital data at clerking (figures not reported).

result.intervention: New admission clerking proforma developed using fishbone and driver diagrams and PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Repeat audits over one year showed improved completion of medication, allergy, legal and forensic status, MSE, risk, VTE assessment and investigations (figures not reported).

result.other_findings: Barriers included no ECG machine and investigations done but not documented.

result.setting: NELA Leads at hospitals across England and Wales (national survey)

cycle1.result: 166/289 leads (57.4%) and 117/167 hospitals (70.1%) responded; pre-operative nutritional screening 39.2% and assessment 45.8%; albumin still used for malnutrition risk 73.5%; post-operative pathways 71.7%.

result.other_findings: 71.2% said nutrition risk is an important missing NELA data item; barriers were time, training, organisational support and ownership.

result.setting: National Office of Clinical Audit Orthogeriatric Network multidisciplinary workshop

cycle1.result: Strong consensus on including nutritional assessment and monitoring in CGA; barriers included limited dietetic support, portion sizes, modified diets and repeated fasting.

result.other_findings: Facilitators included dietetic access, protected meal times, red trays, protein supplements and 'sip til send'; national guidance in development.

result.topic: Antidepressant prescribing in children and adolescents
result.setting: Tonteg Hospital, Taf Ely area, Rhondda Cynon Taf, child and adolescent services
result.standard: NICE guidelines for depression in children and young people: psychological therapy before antidepressants

cycle1.result: Psychological therapy before antidepressants 63% (29/46); single antidepressant 100%.

result.intervention: Recommendation that psychotherapy be considered before starting antidepressants and that this be included in GP letters.

cycle2.result: Psychological therapy before antidepressants 82% (9/11); single antidepressant 100%.

result.other_findings: Comorbid diagnoses 82.6% (38/46) initially and 54.5% (6/11) at re-audit; only fluoxetine and sertraline used.

result.topic: VTE after foot and ankle surgery
result.setting: National multicentre prospective audit (UK-FATE)

cycle1.result: 99 symptomatic VTE within 90 days (0.87%); 3 VTE-related deaths (0.03%).

result.other_findings: Independent predictors were Achilles rupture (OR 11.62 operative, 14.41 non-operative) and ASA III/IV (OR 3.64).

result.setting: Inpatient psychiatric units in North Wales (Heddfan, Ablett, Hergest), Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: RCPsych Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services (2014) and PRSB Mental Health Discharge guidelines (2018)

cycle1.result: Allergy status not mentioned in 96% at Hergest; same-day GP receipt 13% Ablett, 0% Hergest, 100% Heddfan; risk history 0% Hergest and Heddfan, 12% Ablett; crisis contacts 0% across sites.

result.other_findings: In 49% of Ablett summaries medication was the only field completed; care coordinator details 0% at Heddfan and Ablett.

result.topic: Contacting the on-call doctor via switchboard
result.setting: Abraham Cowley Unit, four-ward inpatient psychiatric unit
result.standard: Trust protocol: duty doctor contacted via switchboard, target 80% of calls

cycle1.result: 25% (5/20) of calls via switchboard.

result.intervention: Posters above ward telephones and assessment suite telephone, and direct handover of policy to nurses in charge.

cycle2.result: 88% (7/8) of calls via switchboard; 80% standard met.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Four early intervention service hubs, Birmingham
result.standard: POMH-UK quality improvement programme standards for valproate prescribing

cycle1.result: Target symptoms documented in all; 94% started as inpatients; 55% on off-licence preparation, 93% of these without documented rationale and 93% without discussion with patient; adequate community monitoring 74%.

result.other_findings: Semi-sodium and sodium valproate used interchangeably despite not being bioequivalent; limited side-effect screening documented.

result.topic: Secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome
result.setting: All hospitals admitting ACS patients in Australia and New Zealand; bi-national prospective audit
result.standard: Optimal in-hospital preventive care: lifestyle advice, referral to rehabilitation and prescription of secondary prevention pharmacotherapies

cycle1.result: 46% referred to rehabilitation; 65% discharged on sufficient preventive medications; 27% received optimal preventive care.

result.other_findings: STEMI (OR 2.64), NSTEMI (OR 1.99), PCI (OR 4.71), CABG (OR 2.10) and hypertension were associated with more preventive care; age over 70 (OR 0.53) and private hospital admission (OR 0.59) with less.

result.setting: Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Trust; patients presented at Personality Disorder forums
result.standard: NICE guidance on drug treatment in borderline personality disorder; two audit standards and four treatment targets from the POMH-UK audit; Trust 'Guidance for Prescribing in Personality Disorder' (Dec 2020)

cycle1.result: Crisis plan documented 87%; clinical reason for antipsychotic documented 43%; antipsychotics >4 weeks without psychosis 86%; Z-hypnotics >4 weeks 13%; benzodiazepines >4 weeks 28%; medication reviews 90%.

result.intervention: Trust 'Guidance for Prescribing in Personality Disorder' published and circulated across the Trust in December 2020.

cycle2.result: Crisis plan documented 79%; clinical reason for antipsychotic documented 69%; antipsychotics >4 weeks without psychosis 91%; Z-hypnotics >4 weeks 37.5%; benzodiazepines >4 weeks 38%; medication reviews 100% of eligible patients.

result.other_findings: Quality of medication reviews remained similar to 2017; POMH-UK national audits were done in 2012 and 2014. Findings to be presented with re-emphasis on guidelines and re-audit in 2 years.

result.topic: Did not attend follow-up actions in outpatient clinics
result.setting: Learning disability outpatient mental health service, BCHFT
result.standard: Trust DNA policy: ring patient after DNA, check awareness of appointment, discuss barriers and document

cycle1.result: 35/117 (29%) appointments were DNA. Staff telephoned 34% after the DNA but no policy-aligned details were documented; no contact for 57%; no documentation for 9%. 83% offered another appointment, 17% discharged to GP.

result.other_findings: DNA was associated with male gender, living with family and neuropsychiatric comorbidity. Recommendations: adapt DNA policy for this group and raise awareness at induction.

result.setting: Acute general surgery department, University Hospital Hairmyres, East Kilbride; single centre retrospective audit
result.standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021: lactate measured within 3 hours of admission and repeated within 4–6 hours if ≥2 mmol

cycle1.result: Surgical ward: lactate repeated in 16 (28.6%) patients with high lactate, 9 (56%) of these at ≥8 hours. HDU/ICU: 12 (92%) had lactate repeated in the target time.

result.other_findings: Standards were not achieved on the ward, attributed to unawareness of recommendations and time pressure.

result.setting: AIC Kijabe Hospital, tertiary training hospital

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes a five-category mortality classification system for low-resource settings used to drive trainee, departmental and system learning.

result.topic: JAK inhibitor prescribing for alopecia areata
result.setting: Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, North Wales; regional retrospective audit
result.standard: BAD guidance on ritlecitinib: eligibility, safety screening, outcome monitoring and psychological support

cycle1.result: Baseline SALT ≥50 in 94% (n=16); psychological screening documented 65% (n=11); referred for psychological support 29% (n=5); wig services 82% (n=14); counselling on long-term treatment 47% (n=8); pharmacovigilance registry enrolment 0%.

result.other_findings: At 36 weeks 12% (n=2) achieved SALT ≤20; 5 (29%) did not reach week 36. A standardised regional pathway was recommended.

result.setting: Two acute hospitals in one UK health board (NHS Lanarkshire); biliary stone pathway database
result.standard: UK legal and professional (GMC) standards: documentation of material risks and reasonable alternatives (options-based shared decision-making) before ERCP

cycle1.result: Options-based SDM documented in 73/356 (20.5%) ERCP episodes: low risk 19/78 (24.4%), medium 21/141 (14.9%), high 33/137 (24.1%) (p=0.105). Increased from 12.5% (2023Q4) to 31.8% (2024Q4) (p=0.160). LCBDE 38/38 (100%).

result.other_findings: ERCP 30- and 90-day mortality 1.4% (5/355) and 2.5% (9/355). An options-led consent template was proposed.

result.topic: Shared care transfer of antipsychotic depot prescribing
result.setting: Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton community mental health team depot clinics
result.standard: GMMMG Shared Care Pathway: prescribing of depots for stable patients transferred to GP; target 100%

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 83%.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 96%; first generation antipsychotics 98%; paliperidone and risperidone 94%; aripiprazole 91%.

result.other_findings: One team was 99% compliant overall. The 100% target was still not met; transfers between teams were a weak point.

result.topic: Mental health admissions to paediatric assessment unit
result.setting: Paediatric Assessment Unit, Royal Aberdeen Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: 98/4898 (2%) PAU admissions were for mental health; 87% received a psychiatry review; mean stay 2.1 days (1–20).

result.other_findings: 27% needed treatment for paracetamol overdose and 7% for anorexia; 75% followed up by CAMHS, 22% had no follow-up.

result.topic: Heart failure discharge key performance measures
result.setting: 185 hospitals in England and Wales; National Heart Failure Audit
result.standard: Three key performance measures: ACE-I/ARB on discharge, beta-blocker on discharge, referral to specialist follow-up

cycle1.result: Composite KPM adherence by hospital ranged 50% to 97% (median 79%); referral to specialist follow-up median 81% (range 20% to 100%).

result.other_findings: Only 8% of composite variation (7% ACE-I/ARB, 6% beta-blocker) was attributable to hospital features, versus 26% for specialist referral.

result.setting: 11 specialist Parkinson's disease services (geriatrician- or neurologist-led); national audit
result.standard: De novo audit tool based on international standards, guidelines and audit tools

cycle1.result: 16.8% seen less than annually; motor and mobility assessment >75%; cognition 70%; pain 64%; saliva management 50%; bone density 18%; PD nurse access 65%; physiotherapy 69%; SLT 53%; OT 50%; written information after diagnosis 24%.

result.other_findings: Geriatric-led services screened more for malnutrition (99% v 78%) and orthostatic hypotension (94% v 52%). Carer communication poorly documented (financial support 12%).

result.topic: Mental Health Act consent to treatment documentation
result.setting: Adult acute and rehab wards, Roseberry Park Hospital
result.standard: MHA documentation for section 3 patients staying 90 days or more: MCA1 capacity assessment at admission and 3 months, T2 form, SOAD request and T3 authorisation

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment documented 80% at admission and 60% at 3 months; T2 completed in all consenting patients; SOAD request sent in 7 (78%) but recorded in 5 (56%); T3 documented in 4 (45%), discussed with patient in 1 (11%).

cycle2.result: Capacity assessment 80% at admission and 60% at 3 months; T2 completed in all consenting patients; SOAD request recorded in 1 (25%); T3 not documented or discussed for any patient.

result.other_findings: Rehab ward closed in February 2020 so re-audit covered acute wards only. No change between cycles was described.

result.topic: Crisis safety plans for high intensity users
result.setting: Acute mental health services (s136 suite, liaison and inpatient wards)
result.standard: Safety plan in place containing person-centred, specific recommendations to avert and manage crisis

cycle1.result: >80% had a safety plan, but these lacked sufficient detail to avert crisis or guide treatment.

result.intervention: HIU response plan template, best practice example for care coordinators and process for flagging HIUs to community teams, developed through process mapping, driver diagram and focus groups.

cycle2.result: HIU response plans incorporated into the safety plans of 20/26 HIUs.

result.other_findings: Most frequent diagnosis was EUPD (77%); 93% on CPA. PDSA cycles ongoing.

result.topic: Management of behavioural symptoms in dementia
result.setting: Humber Older People's Mental Health Services
result.standard: NICE: non-pharmacological before pharmacological management; antipsychotics started low and slow; follow-up at least 6 weeks after starting

cycle1.result: About 24% started on medication without trial of non-pharmacological methods; those started on medication were properly followed up; overall adherence around 75%.

result.other_findings: Risperidone was the commonest medication (37%). Re-audit suggested in 12 to 24 months.

result.setting: General medical ward and specialist geriatric medicine ward, city centre teaching hospital (Mercy University Hospital, Cork)
result.standard: Audit tool adapted from the RCP National Continence Audit tool and the hospital elimination documentation pathway

cycle1.result: 4 patients had no continence status documented; of over-65s with documented incontinence (42%), only 40% had the nursing elimination section fully completed; 6 had symptoms/type documented; catheter indications documented in both catheterised patients.

result.other_findings: An assessment tool and education programme were planned for the geriatric ward.

result.setting: 30-bed independent care home intermediate care unit with NHS trust MDT (SEHSCT, Dundonald)

cycle1.result: Baseline nursing confidence in handover assessed by semi-structured interviews and weighted questionnaire.

result.intervention: Care-home-specific electronic nursing handover template based on National Audit of Intermediate Care quality indicators, four iterations.

cycle2.result: 70% reported increased or slightly increased confidence in addressing questions from residents or relatives, responding to change in health status and giving handover.

result.other_findings: Measured staff confidence rather than compliance with a standard.

result.setting: Memory clinic, Stockton Mental Health Services for Older People
result.standard: Trust and NICE standards: minimum body of key information recorded in electronic records within 24 hours of diagnostic assessment

cycle1.result: Minimum body of information recorded in 90–100% of cases.

result.intervention: All diagnosing clinicians informed about the project and expected improvements.

cycle2.result: Minimum body of information recorded in 95–100% of records; documentation within 24 hours in all but one applicable record.

result.other_findings: Prognostic information was not consistently discussed.

result.topic: Smoking cessation and nicotine replacement on admission
result.setting: Four older adult psychiatric inpatient wards (Lancashire and South Cumbria Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Trust Smoke-Free standards: smoking status documented on admission; tobacco dependence treatment within 30 minutes; regular MDT review; referral to Tobacco Dependency Team within 24 hours

cycle1.result: Smoking status documented 31% (16/53); treatment within 30 minutes 0%; 83% of smokers eventually prescribed NRT, all >5 hours after admission; MDT review 0%; referral within 24 hours 17%.

result.other_findings: Only 6 patients had documented tobacco dependence. Re-audit planned after interventions.

result.setting: Four post-acute rehabilitation hospitals; multi-site retrospective audit

cycle1.result: Mean acute stay 11.8 days, rehabilitation stay 37.6 days; 90.2% (n=333) discharged home; 82.2% (n=256) independently mobile at discharge.

result.other_findings: Significant between-site differences in acute (median 8–13 days) and rehabilitation length of stay (median 16–39 days).

result.setting: Emergency theatre list, tertiary general surgical unit (Oxford University Hospitals)

cycle1.result: Over 18% of patients hypothermic at knife-to-skin.

result.intervention: Forced-air warming gowns for 45 minutes preoperatively, through induction and intraoperatively (prospective trial).

cycle2.result: 100% normothermic at knife-to-skin; mean core temperature significantly higher (p=0.012).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Stroke Unit, Manchester Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Five standards from NICE (2012) and RCP (2016) stroke guidelines on continence identification and management

cycle1.result: Continence status identified by nursing 100% and medical team 41%; care planning 22%; MDT input 11%; interventions 11%.

result.intervention: After cycle 1: awareness training and MDT prompt sheet. After cycle 2: individualised assessment within 7 days by the advanced nurse practitioner.

cycle2.result: Cycle 3 showed improvement in all five standards; nursing and medical identification 100% and 91% (abstract truncated).

result.other_findings: Cycle 2: medical identification 82%, MDT discussion 100%, continence interventions 66%, care planning fell from 22% to 0%. Three cycles, 66 patients over four months.

result.setting: Wirral University Teaching Hospital NHS Trust
result.standard: WSES 2020 guidelines: post-operative antibiotic use and duration, intra-operative documentation of severity and contamination, microbiological sampling

cycle1.result: Mean antibiotic duration in complicated appendicitis 9.2 days.

result.intervention: Consultant-led education and a revised electronic laparoscopic appendicectomy theatre note with guideline prompts.

cycle2.result: Antibiotic duration in complicated appendicitis fell to 8.4 days.

result.other_findings: Variation persisted in prescribing for uncomplicated appendicitis; negative appendicectomy rate 6.5%.

result.topic: Skin cancer surveillance in transplant recipients
result.setting: Tertiary dermatology department, Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: SUNTRAC and US Delphi consensus guidelines on skin surveillance

cycle1.result: Mean time to first dermatology review 5.76 years post-transplant; medium-risk patients seen at 6.5 years, very high risk within 12 months; 60% had skin cancer.

result.other_findings: Under-35 recipients (mainly thoracic) waited a mean 8.5 years for first review. A QI project is underway.

result.topic: Urgent GP referrals to mental health services
result.setting: Community mental health duty team, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: Trust policy: all urgent GP referrals contacted within 48 hours by the duty team

cycle1.result: Only 13/124 urgent referrals were deemed urgent after telephone assessment; 53 referred to primary care mental health, 24 to secondary CMHT, 20 to older adults, 10 discharged to GP.

result.other_findings: Recommendations: GP surgery visits to raise awareness and a brief risk assessment to justify urgent referral. Compliance with 48-hour contact was not reported.

result.setting: Contact Dermatitis Unit, University Hospitals of Leicester

cycle1.result: 65 (26.7%) self-reported nickel allergy; 49 (20.2%) patch test positive; sensitivity 63.3%, specificity 82.4%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Emergency department, Australian Major Trauma Centre; prospective interventional cohort with online airway registry

cycle1.result: First-attempt success rate 88.5%; hypoxia 8.3%; hypotension 8.3%; any complication 27.4%.

result.intervention: Bundle of monthly audit, monthly airway management education and an airway management checklist.

cycle2.result: First-attempt success rate 94.6% (RR 1.07, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.14, p=0.014); hypoxia 8.9%; hypotension 7.0%; any complication 23.6%.

result.other_findings: Success rose by 13.4% (p=0.006) in the first month with a monthly trend increase of 1.71% (p<0.001); adverse event rates did not change significantly.

result.setting: All UK hospitals offering anaesthetic services; 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) of the Royal College of Anaesthetists

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Methods paper describing baseline surveys, a 4-day activity survey and a 1-year case registry of peri-operative cardiac arrest.

result.setting: HPB surgery, Sheffield Teaching Hospitals
result.standard: RCS England recommendation (following NHSBT amber alert): tranexamic acid for all adult surgical patients where more than 500 ml blood loss is likely

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Prompt for TXA added to the WHO timeout pre-operative checklist.

cycle2.result: The prompt did not increase the likelihood of a pre-operative TXA dose; change in haemoglobin and transfusion rates were similar between groups.

result.other_findings: Numerical TXA administration rates were not given in the abstract.

result.setting: Pathfinder service (National Ambulance Service and University Limerick Hospital Group), patients who fell at home without admission
result.standard: 2022 World Guidelines for falls prevention and management; target 100% documentation of eight key assessments

cycle1.result: Falls risk stratification 12.5%; other domains not given individually.

result.intervention: Eight practice changes aligned with the World Falls Guidelines (delirium screen, lying/standing BP, ECG, standardised balance and gait, ADL and environmental assessments, risk stratification, 3 key questions).

cycle2.result: Implementation increased by 34% to 71% on average; 3 key questions increased by 72%; falls risk stratification 79%; standardised mobility assessment compliance doubled.

result.other_findings: Further improvements being embedded in team education and patient information.

result.setting: Department of Plastic Surgery, major trauma centre (St Mary's Hospital, Imperial College NHS Trust)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons guidance on timely, accurate and accessible operation notes

cycle1.result: 56% of operation notes accessible to nursing staff on the electronic medical record.

result.intervention: Bespoke online pop-up reminder to upload operation notes to the electronic medical record.

cycle2.result: 83% of operation notes accessible to nursing staff (p<0.05).

result.other_findings: Accessibility was not correlated with case type, surgeon grade or number of surgeons; performance remained below the expected standard.

result.setting: General surgery, Birmingham Heartlands Hospital (NHS Trust in West Midlands)
result.standard: GIRFT and RCS England recommendations for documentation of laparoscopic cholecystectomy

cycle1.result: Indication, consent, WHO checklist and surgeon details documented in all cases. Omissions: pneumoperitoneum technique 19%, intraoperative drugs 54%, intra-abdominal pressure 95%, number of clips 66%, retrieval method/port 38%, port removal under vision 32%, haemostasis 12%, fascial closure 26%, critical view of safety 49%, anaesthetist names 62%, first surgeon signature 41%.

result.intervention: Planned: teaching presentations and an electronic documentation template.
result.other_findings: Re-audit was planned for July 2023.

result.setting: Square Medical Practice, Dundalk (primary care) with secondary care correspondence
result.standard: Secondary care letters state indication and duration of DAPT; stop date on prescription; DAPT for correct duration

cycle1.result: 12% of secondary care letters did not specify duration; 43% had no stop date on prescription; 19% on DAPT for incorrect duration; 15% serious medication error.

result.intervention: Clinical system warnings for DAPT time limits, switching of less appropriate PPIs and reminders to secondary care colleagues.
result.other_findings: 14.8% were not prescribed a PPI and 4.9% were admitted with GI bleeding; 24.7% were on omeprazole/esomeprazole with clopidogrel.

result.setting: Advanced Nurse Practitioner-led frailty outreach clinic (HSE ICPOP, Sligo)

cycle1.result: 30 patients (31.5%) re-presented to the emergency department after initial assessment.

result.other_findings: Cognitive impairment and polypharmacy were the most frequent referral concerns.

result.topic: Suspected cauda equina syndrome MRI pathway
result.setting: Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board West (Ysbyty Gwynedd)
result.standard: SBNS/BASS guidelines for urgent MRI in suspected cauda equina syndrome

cycle1.result: 99% scanned in compliance with SBNS/BASS standards; CES found on imaging in 18%.

result.other_findings: 33% of scans were out of hours and 4% had repeat scans within 6 months; referrals rose from 2.5 to 3.5 per week during the COVID-19 peak.

result.setting: North Kirklees Community Mental Health Team, Older people services (South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: SWYPFT Trust standards, NICE guidelines and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition); target 100% prolactin monitoring

cycle1.result: Prolactin monitored in 41%.

cycle2.result: Prolactin monitored in 22/43 (51%): first-time users 5/15, long-acting injection 6/8, oral 11/20.

result.other_findings: 78 patients on antipsychotics; 35 on drugs not needing monitoring. No intervention between audits was described.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring in severe mental illness
result.setting: Community mental health clinic
result.standard: National and local guidelines on routine physical health monitoring; target 100% compliance within 8 weeks

cycle1.result: Baseline: 140 outstanding blood test results and 16 pending ECG results.

result.intervention: PDSA cycles: staff training on Kardia ECG interpretation; weekly logging and mop-up of outstanding ECG and blood results; improved cover and swaps during annual leave.

cycle2.result: Outstanding blood results fell to 24 and pending ECGs to 1 in four weeks; 100% compliance by eight weeks.

result.other_findings: The weekly mop-up was the most effective intervention.

result.setting: Prehabilitation service, Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Physical activity scores improved significantly in hospital gym (54.4 to 216.7) and community gym (180.5 to 362.0) groups (p<0.001).

result.other_findings: Colon surgery patients completing prehabilitation (n=37) had median LoS 5.2 days v 5.6 days for those not in the programme (n=567), p<0.05.

result.setting: Community mental health teams in Halton, Mersey Care NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE-BNF prescription writing guidance and Trust policy on FP10 prescriptions

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 97%; Appendix 3 completion 83%; scanning/documenting FP10s in records 87%; storage and prescription writing 100%.

result.intervention: Column added to Appendix 3 for NHS numbers and an information/prompt sheet inserted in the FP10 bundle.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 99%; Appendix 3 completion 100%; documentation in records 97%; storage and prescription writing 100%.

result.other_findings: The community FP10 management procedure was reviewed and rewritten.

result.setting: Hospital psychiatric liaison team
result.standard: Psychiatric Liaison Accreditation Network (PLAN) standards for documentation of assessments

cycle1.result: Collateral history 23%; past medical history 30%; patient/carer perspective 46%; written correspondence offered to patients 0%.

result.intervention: Presentation of results to team, emailed instructions to create a PLAN-based assessment template, and lobbying for Cerner access at the liaison office.

cycle2.result: Collateral history 67%; past medical history 70%; patient/carer perspective 74%; written correspondence offered 20%.

result.other_findings: Staff were positive about writing to patients but cited workload as a barrier.

result.topic: Smoking cessation and nicotine replacement on admission
result.setting: Adult psychiatry inpatient wards, North Wales
result.standard: Smoking status documented; NRT within four hours of admission; contraindications documented; drug interactions considered

cycle1.result: Smoking status assessed 79%; NRT within four hours 59%; contraindications and drug interactions considered 14%.

result.other_findings: Recommendations: clinician training and a standardised NRT tool.

result.setting: Independent sector hospitals; 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) of the Royal College of Anaesthetists

cycle1.result: 174/442 (39%) independent hospitals participated; preparedness survey response 23 (13%); activity survey (1912 responses) suggested suboptimal compliance with monitoring recommendations; 17 cardiac arrest reports (2% of NAP7).

result.other_findings: Outcomes were similar to the NHS despite lower-risk case mix; quality of care was less often rated favourable than NHS reports.

result.setting: Royal Blackburn Hospital, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Sustained virological response in 264 (60.41%); 43 (9.84%) non-responders; 49 (11.21%) did not complete treatment.

result.other_findings: Patient feedback on the nurse-led service was very positive.

result.setting: Hospitals reporting to the Irish National Audit of Stroke (INAS); online survey of audit co-ordinators

cycle1.result: Responses from 11/34 audit co-ordinators (10/24 hospitals); variability in data points chosen for hospital arrival time, team time and brain imaging time.

result.other_findings: Thrombolysis and thrombolysis time showed less variability in interpretation.

result.setting: Level four hospital (University Hospital Waterford); medical, surgical and orthopaedic admissions
result.standard: Correct and timely prescription and administration of Parkinson's disease medication

cycle1.result: 86% did not receive appropriate PD medication in ED; 21% had prescribing errors on admission; 75% missed at least one levodopa dose (83 missed doses); 64% had doses delayed by more than 1 hour; 18% received antidopaminergic drugs.

result.intervention: Hospital guideline for managing PD patients who are nil by mouth, approved by the Medications and Therapeutics committee, with education sessions at changeover.
result.other_findings: 40% of missed doses were due to nil by mouth and 21% had no reason documented; over 80% of delays were perioperative. Re-audit planned after 6 months.

result.setting: Health Care of the Older Person ward, Lincoln County Hospital
result.standard: Structured medication review supported by STOPP/START and Beers criteria for patients ≥65 on ≥5 regular medications

cycle1.result: SMR completed 80%; documentation 80%; PIMs prescribed in 40%; changes communicated to GP via EDD 100%.

result.intervention: Staff education sessions, e-mail reminders and ward posters.

cycle2.result: SMR completed 100%; documentation 100%; PIMs prescribed in 70%; changes communicated to GP 100%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Geriatric Emergency Medicine Unit, University Hospital Limerick
result.standard: 11-standard audit tool based on the World Guidelines for Falls Prevention and Management (2022) and ESC syncope guidelines (2018)

cycle1.result: Compliance ranged 15-100% across 11 standards; composite compliance 65%; careful history 55%; ECG 60%; lying and standing BP 25%.

result.intervention: Team-based education on assessment practices and a 'falls from a standing height checklist'.

cycle2.result: Composite compliance 90%; careful history 100%; ECG 90%; lying and standing BP 65%.

result.other_findings: Three cycles: re-audits in Q2 2024 and Q1 2025.

result.topic: Frailty and survival after emergency laparotomy
result.setting: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit data linked to ONS mortality

cycle1.result: Beyond 90 days, adjusted hazard ratios versus CFS 1–3: CFS 4 1.52, CFS 5 1.69, CFS 6 2.14, CFS 7 2.97, CFS 8 4.24, CFS 9 3.34.

result.other_findings: Frailty was strongly associated with death within 90 days and the association persisted afterwards.

result.setting: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit; 15 geographic regions
result.standard: NELA process standards (critical care admission, CT imaging, data completeness, elderly assessment)

cycle1.result: Mortality fell from 11.36% (2016) to 8.15% (2025); regional mortality ranged 5.4% (London South West) to 11.3% (Yorkshire & Humber).

result.other_findings: Critical care admission stable (78% to 77.5%); CT imaging declined (65% to 54%); data capture decreased (91% to 83%).

result.setting: Three rehabilitation wards, St Mary's Hospital, Phoenix Park, Dublin
result.standard: NICE: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission; HSE VTE Prevention Programme template

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment on admission 0%; therapeutic anticoagulation continued 23 (56%); appropriate prophylaxis started 3 (7%); 8 eligible at-risk patients had no prophylaxis.

result.intervention: VTE Prophylaxis Protocol based on the HSE template incorporated into the admission booklet on 3 pilot wards (February 2024).

cycle2.result: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours 10 (40%); anticoagulation continued 9 (36%); appropriate prophylaxis 5 (20%); 3 at-risk patients had no prophylaxis; 1 inappropriately received prophylaxis.

result.other_findings: No association between prophylaxis prescribing and protocol use was shown in this small sample.

result.setting: West Suffolk Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: National confidential enquiry into PEG outcomes (patient selection); PEG indication, antibiotic prophylaxis documentation and MDT review

cycle1.result: Antibiotic prophylaxis documented 80%; 7 patients had no MDT discussion; 3 deaths within 30 days.

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary nutrition team approach and PEG referral proforma.

cycle2.result: Antibiotic prophylaxis documented 83%; all patients had MDT discussion; 2 immediate complications; no deaths at 30 days.

result.other_findings: Dysphagia after stroke as indication fell from 56% to 39%.

result.topic: Staging bone scans in prostate cancer
result.setting: BAUS radical prostatectomy database; UK nationwide audit
result.standard: Guidelines to avoid staging bone scans in low-risk prostate cancer

cycle1.result: Proportion of low-risk patients having bone scan fell to less than 1% in 2016; intermediate-risk proportion remained stable; no staging scan before RP 3.66% in 2016.

result.other_findings: Data quality improved from 2011 and 13 of 15 regions improved data completeness.

result.setting: East Surrey Hospital, single NHS Trust in England
result.standard: 2021 ESGAR guidance on management of gallbladder polyps

cycle1.result: 35 (36%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy, including all with polyp >10mm; histology cholecystitis 69%, true gallbladder polyp 6%; 47% of symptomatic patients had two ultrasounds and two clinic appointments. Adherence to ESGAR was inconsistent.

result.other_findings: 74% (26/35) of cholecystectomy patients had biliary symptoms and 77% (20/26) of these had cholecystitis on histology.

result.setting: General surgical department (South Tyneside and Sunderland, Royal Marsden, Northumbria and North Tees affiliations)
result.standard: European Hernia Society guidelines: perioperative antibiotics only for high-risk hernia repairs

cycle1.result: Perioperative antibiotics given in 87.8% overall: 89% elective groin, 85% elective ventral/umbilical, 80% emergency repairs.

result.intervention: Departmental standardised 'high-risk criteria' defining when antibiotics are indicated, with departmental education.
result.other_findings: Postoperative complication rates stayed low and did not increase.

result.setting: Early Intervention for Psychosis team, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: DVLA guidance: documentation of diagnosis, driving status, vehicle type, advice on effect on driving, restrictions and legal duty to inform DVLA

cycle1.result: Diagnosis documented 95% (38); driving status 67.5% (27); vehicle type 33% (5) of drivers; told condition may affect driving 33% (5); driving restrictions advice 67% (10); legal duty to inform DVLA 47% (7).

result.other_findings: Recommendations: training, team meetings, adding driving to structured initial assessments and patient leaflets.

result.setting: Section 136 suite, Fieldhead Hospital, Wakefield (South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Local s136 standard operating procedures: timeliness of MHA assessment, IHBTT involvement, documentation and GP communication

cycle1.result: 60% assessed within four hours and 90% within twelve hours; IHBTT face-to-face input 45%; 99% of assessments documented by Section 12 doctors; over 70% of discharged patients lacked documented GP correspondence.

result.other_findings: 60% of presentations were out of hours and 55% were known to CMHTs.

result.setting: Virtual fracture clinic, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff (CAVUHB)
result.standard: Appropriate VFC referrals, compared with established VFCs in England

cycle1.result: Inappropriate referrals for soft tissue knee and shoulder injuries 15.1% (n=50).

cycle2.result: Average 19% improvement in referral quality; inappropriate soft tissue referrals 4.5% (n=15); fracture clinic appointments rose by 8% to 74.4% (n=247).

result.other_findings: 64% (n=27) of radial head fractures were still seen in clinic after VFC referral; the rise in clinic appointments was mainly from nurse practitioner referrals.

result.setting: Tertiary dermatology centre, Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Of 52 tests with results, 11 (21%) found a pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant, 4 (8%) a VUS and 37 (71%) no pathogenic variant.

result.other_findings: Yield was 43% for mosaic skin disorders, 60% for ichthyosis and keratoderma and 0% for familial melanoma.

result.setting: Four surgical wards, Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: CPOC and BGS guideline for perioperative care for people living with frailty: 4AT delirium screening in surgical inpatients over 65

cycle1.result: Baseline 4AT documented preoperatively 25% (n=9); 4AT documented during admission 33% (n=11).

result.intervention: Educational sessions for ward-based medical, nursing and allied health staff.

cycle2.result: Baseline 4AT documented preoperatively 35% (n=19); 4AT documented during admission 47.3% (n=26).

result.other_findings: Delirium incidence 14.5% (8 patients with 4AT >4); all patients had ≥2 risk factors.

result.setting: Geriatric medicine service, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: HIQA National Standard for Discharge Summary Information (2013)

cycle1.result: Clinical course 40%; primary diagnosis 85%; stopped medications 40%; future plans 85%; ideal summaries 20%.

result.intervention: NCHD-designed flowchart, targeted education sessions and weekly reports on outstanding summaries to consultants.

cycle2.result: Clinical course 75% (p=0.004); primary diagnosis 100% (p=0.002); stopped medications 70% (p=0.016); future plans 97% (p=0.062); ideal summaries 40% (p=0.104); composite score 0.63 points higher (p=0.022).

result.other_findings: Four cycles over three years, 20 patients each. New or changed medications (85%-75%), complications (80%-85%) and complete discharge medications (57%-60%) did not improve.

result.setting: Model 2 hospital (University Hospital Limerick affiliation), inpatients
result.standard: Adapted MediDocQ patient safety instrument for prescribing and transcribing documentation

cycle1.result: As-required prescribing completeness 35%; discontinuation completeness 21%; allergy status documented 90%; nature of reaction documented 43%.

cycle2.result: As-required prescribing completeness 33%; discontinuation completeness 31%; allergy status 100%; nature of reaction 31%.

result.other_findings: No convincing or consistent improvement; polypharmacy 76% and hyperpolypharmacy 46%.

result.setting: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust; patients starting clozapine
result.standard: Cardiac monitoring during clozapine initiation: baseline ECG and weekly troponin and CRP in the first 4 weeks (no standardised framework stated)

cycle1.result: Of 219 patients, 180 had complete data. Baseline ECG completed in 80%. No routine troponin monitoring identified; CRP testing infrequent.

result.other_findings: Tachycardia occurred in more than 40%; 15 referred to cardiology before initiation, 6 in the first 4 weeks and 5 thereafter; 12 (7%) discontinued clozapine early, mainly owing to tachycardia. Authors propose adding weekly troponin and CRP to mandatory blood tests.

result.setting: Scottish pre-hospital trauma teams and receiving hospitals with Code Red policy; national audit
result.standard: Recommendations of the Scottish Transfusion and Laboratory Support in Trauma (TLST) group from the previous Code Red audit

cycle1.result: Previous audit: median time from 999 call to Code Red activation 70 minutes; 70% received pre-hospital TXA; survival to discharge 63%.

result.intervention: Recommendations from the previous audit adopted to optimise transfusion support in major trauma

cycle2.result: 66 activations; 93% received blood components; pre-hospital transfusion in 48 patients (73%), a 300% increase; median time from 999 call to Code Red activation 37 minutes; 78% received pre-hospital TXA; CRC:FFP ratios improved; survival to discharge 66%.

result.other_findings: Survival improved despite increased ISS; further improvement needed in TXA administration and time to blood products.

result.topic: Psychotropic prescribing in children with neurodevelopmental disorders
result.setting: Barnet Service for Children and Adolescents with Neurodevelopmental disorders (SCAN), Holly Oak Unit, Edgware Hospital
result.standard: NICE guidelines and the STOMP and STAMP pledges

cycle1.result: 19% of young people prescribed psychotropics (2020); 50% offered therapeutic interventions.

result.intervention: Positive Behavioural Support (PBS) workshops introduced in SCAN

cycle2.result: 88/161 (55%) on psychiatric medication; clients offered therapeutic interventions rose from 50% to 91%; prescribing of psychotropics rose (19% in 2020 vs 24%).

result.other_findings: Of those on medication, 55% had ADHD, 77% ASD and 45% both; authors attribute the rise in prescribing to post-COVID case acuity.

result.setting: Geriatric ambulatory care day hospital, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Weaning guidance for benzodiazepines and Z-drugs from the Canadian National Pain Centre

cycle1.result: 11/59 (19%) had a benzodiazepine or Z-drug on repeat prescription (benzodiazepine 5, Z-drug 5, both 1); none of those on benzodiazepines were being weaned.

result.intervention: Notices placed in the consult room in the registrar's line of sight reminding them to consider weaning, with side effects and weaning guidance

cycle2.result: No change in benzodiazepine prescribing (5/59); non-significant increase in Z-drugs (9/59, p=0.26).

result.other_findings: Of those on benzodiazepines, 4 of 6 had a documented psychiatric diagnosis and 1 of 6 was attending psychiatric services.

result.setting: Healthcare for older people wards, Queens Medical Centre, Nottingham
result.standard: NICE: reassess anticoagulation for patients on warfarin with poor control (2 INR values <1.5 or >5, or 1 INR >8, in past 6 months; or TTR <65%)

cycle1.result: Warfarin correctly continued in 7/38 (18%); 26/32 (81%) with unstable INRs discharged on warfarin.

cycle2.result: Warfarin correctly continued in 9/28 (32%); 10/24 (42%) with unstable INRs discharged on warfarin (p = 0.0043, Fisher exact test).

result.other_findings: Overall NICE compliance remained poor despite the trend to improvement; median age 87.5 vs 83 in the first audit.

result.setting: Teledermatology service including GP referrals and a 2-week-wait cancer pathway, Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: 68% received a definitive outcome without clinic attendance, 27% referred to clinic; lesion-based referrals (n = 5781) 71% definitive; 2WW TD-only pathway (n = 2889) 79% definitive; inflammatory referrals 55% definitive, 42% clinic.

result.other_findings: Progressive statistically significant improvements across audit cycles, attributed to medical photographers' image quality, consultant experience and direct-to-biopsy referrals.

result.setting: Seven surgical wards, district general hospital
result.standard: Francis Inquiry Report (2013) Recommendation 236: all inpatients should have a nominated responsible clinician

cycle1.result: 71% did not know their surgeon's name and 62% did not know their nurse's name; 76% of ward whiteboards had correct nominated staff information; 2% of bed-headboards had the surgeon's details.

result.intervention: Junior doctor education to encourage communication with patients about their responsible care team

cycle2.result: 14% improvement in awareness of surgeon's name; whiteboards correct 95%; bed-headboards with surgeon's details 24%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Single instillation intravesical chemotherapy after TURBT
result.setting: 232 hospitals globally (RESECT study data); primary curative TURBT
result.standard: Guideline-recommended single instillation intravesical chemotherapy (SI-IVC) after TURBT for NMIBC

cycle1.result: SI-IVC given in 3075 (39%) cases (low grade 48%, high grade 32%). In low grade cases, reasons for non-administration: surgeon did not request it (68%), requested but not given (7%), never given at the hospital (25%).

result.other_findings: Of 3566 not requested, 42% surgeon thought not indicated, 14.4% potential contraindications, 34% no reason; 837 (31%) of 2707 without documented contraindication had low grade disease and likely would have benefitted.

result.topic: Calcium and vitamin D monitoring in sarcoidosis
result.setting: King's College Hospital sarcoidosis database with community primary care records
result.standard: Monitoring of serum calcium and vitamin D in sarcoidosis patients on calcium and/or vitamin D supplementation

cycle1.result: 46/102 (45%) had serum calcium and vitamin D measured in the community in the last 12 months.

result.other_findings: One patient on vitamin D had hypercalcaemia; a CCG-wide prescribing alert was implemented afterwards.

result.setting: Two acute psychiatric wards, Briary Wing, Harrogate District Hospital
result.standard: Local and national research and development standards for approaching inpatients about research

cycle1.result: Only one ward implemented local guidance; 13/14 noted as approached, but only 3 remembered a research leaflet and none were verbally informed; documentation present in 9 and nonspecific.

result.other_findings: No process for re-approaching initially unwell patients or following up at discharge; an action plan with flow charts was proposed.

result.setting: 51 UK rheumatology centres; British Society for Rheumatology multicentre SLE audit data
result.standard: BSR risk stratification guidance and scoring grid for shielding (used to classify, not audited against)

cycle1.result: 344 (34.3%) had a shielding score of 3 or more and would have been advised to shield.

result.other_findings: Previous or current lupus nephritis 2.6 (1.9–3.4) times more likely to shield; Black 1.9 (1.3–2.8) and Asian 1.9 (1.3–2.7) times more likely than White people, persisting after controlling for nephritis.

result.setting: Two UK centres; adults undergoing emergency laparotomy

cycle1.result: 1, 3 and 5-year survival 76%, 67% and 61%. NELA and ACS-NSQIP 30-day predicted mortality correlated with 1-year mortality (R²=1); at 3 years only NELA (R²=0.23, p<0.05); at 5 years NELA R²=0.61, p<0.001 and ACS-NSQIP R²=0.31, p<0.05.

result.other_findings: Median age 70 years; NELA showed the stronger correlation.

result.setting: Cardiothoracic surgery wards, large cardiothoracic surgery department
result.standard: Complete stocking of emergency chest drain boxes (target date June 2022)

cycle1.result: Missing equipment prevalent in emergency chest drain boxes (baseline number of missing items not stated).

result.intervention: Revised stock checklist produced with the project champion, thoracic audit lead and procedural document team, introduced over two PDSA cycles

cycle2.result: 81% reduction in the 3-month average number of reported missing items; 92% increase in perceived confidence that the box will be correctly stocked.

result.other_findings: A third PDSA cycle is introducing a single-use pre-packed chest drain insertion pack.

result.topic: Chest physiotherapy after open liver surgery
result.setting: Open liver surgery patients, Hampshire Hospitals Foundation Trust, Basingstoke
result.standard: Early postoperative chest physiotherapy as part of the enhanced recovery protocol

cycle1.result: 18/50 (36%) received chest physiotherapy on POD1; 16 (32%) received none; PPCs 20%.

result.intervention: Intensive preoperative patient education, poster campaign and increased engagement with physiotherapists about timely chest physiotherapy

cycle2.result: 20/36 (57%) received chest physiotherapy on POD1 (p=0.07); 7 (19%) received none (p=0.19); PPCs 8% (p=0.13).

result.other_findings: Wards with higher physiotherapist:patient ratios delivered more POD1 physiotherapy (C1 63% vs 20%, p=0.001; C2 93% vs 30%, p=0.0001); median stay unchanged at 4 days.

result.setting: Major Trauma Centre, University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire
result.standard: No national guideline on routine post-operative pelvic radiographs after hemiarthroplasty

cycle1.result: Post-operative pelvic radiographs performed in 98% at mean 2.71 days; only 8.2% had a documented clinical indication; positive findings in 3.1% (one dislocation, two leg-length discrepancies).

result.other_findings: 90.8% mobilised before imaging; 32% of documentation lacked reviewer attribution. An electronic proforma for targeted imaging is recommended.

result.setting: Dova Unit, Dane Garth (inpatient unit)
result.standard: Completion of the VTE prophylaxis admission assessment

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 35%; VTE risk assessment completed 50%; 'active VTE on admission' 30%; 'active VTE at 72 hours' 20%; 'risk assessment for VTE' form 40%.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 50%; VTE risk assessment 60%; 'active VTE on admission' 40%; 'active VTE at 72 hours' 40%; 'risk assessment for VTE' form 60%.

result.other_findings: Further work with junior doctors planned to improve completion.

result.topic: Indeterminate FDG-PET brain reports in memory clinic
result.setting: Memory clinic, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust

cycle1.result: Of 134 scans, 22 definitively indeterminate; all had further outpatient follow-up; 20 developed dementia (11/20 parietal z scores >2) and 2 had mild cognitive impairment.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend follow-up of indeterminate scans, particularly with parietal z scores above 2.

result.topic: HbA1c monitoring in vascular surgery inpatients
result.setting: Vascular surgery department, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary (tertiary centre)

cycle1.result: Appropriate HbA1c re-checks on indicated admissions 25%; repeat HbA1c required in 38%; mean staff knowledge score 56%.

result.intervention: Educational teaching programme on diabetes management for clinical staff

cycle2.result: Appropriate HbA1c re-checks on indicated admissions 86%; repeat HbA1c required in 50%; mean knowledge score 77%.

result.other_findings: Mean pre-admission HbA1c was high (78.6 and 73.6 mmol/mol); referral for multidisciplinary diabetes optimisation is a further focus.

result.topic: VTE prophylaxis prescribing in older inpatients
result.setting: Medicine for the elderly service, Connolly Hospital, Dublin (level 3 hospital)
result.standard: Prophylactic anticoagulation for all hospitalised older adults unless contraindicated; target 95%

cycle1.result: 80% of older adults admitted were receiving prophylactic anticoagulation.

result.intervention: Cause and effect analysis then small tests of change over 4 PDSA cycles addressing history taking, clinician education, documentation, handover, medication reconciliation and pharmacy support

cycle2.result: 98.1% (104/106) receiving prophylactic anticoagulation; 83% after one month.

result.other_findings: Only 2 patients lacked documentation of a reason for not prescribing.

result.setting: Two general medical wards, Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth

cycle1.result: 25/55 patients at risk; documented next of kin discussion in 74%; treatment plan discussions 81%.

result.intervention: Education of the medical team and a written prompt in the patient's notes

cycle2.result: 39/71 patients at risk; documented next of kin discussion 82%; treatment plan discussions 97%.

result.other_findings: Discussions on escalation, DoLS, capacity and Mental Health Act slightly decreased; consent for data sharing rarely documented.

result.setting: General adult psychiatry inpatient ward, Heddfan Adult Mental Health Unit, BCUHB, north Wales
result.standard: Questionnaire based on Royal College of Psychiatrists core training learning outcomes and textbooks; target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: GMC number recorded 30%; route of admission 4%; consultant name 8%; no personal history or formulation; nursing observation level 20%; many other items missing.

result.other_findings: A clerking and physical health proforma is planned before re-audit.

result.setting: Mental Health Service for Older Persons, Dublin North City Central (community)
result.standard: Irish Medication Safety Network (IMSN) guidance for prescribing and monitoring lithium therapy

cycle1.result: Poor compliance with lithium monitoring against the standard (figures not stated).

result.intervention: Lithium monitoring pack inserted into patient files to prompt standardised monitoring

cycle2.result: Improvement in recording of blood monitoring (figures not stated).

result.other_findings: A formal lithium clinic was recommended; the pack will be added to NCHD induction and MDT teaching.

result.setting: Gerontological inpatient rehabilitation ward, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate medications

cycle1.result: 38 potentially inappropriate medications identified (10% of all prescriptions); 12 deprescribing opportunities taken, one a dose reduction.

result.other_findings: Commonest PIMs were full-dose PPI (n=12), hypnotics (n=7) and inappropriate opioids (n=4) in high-risk groups; mean 11 medications per patient.

result.setting: General surgery and ageing and complex medicine teams, Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh NHS Teaching Trust
result.standard: NELA best practice tariff KPI: geriatrician input for all patients over 80 and those over 65 with frailty

cycle1.result: 0 NELA referrals to ageing and complex medicine; 8% received geriatrician-led CGA in 2019–2020 (national average 27%).

result.intervention: Standardised referral proforma and pathway, then a dedicated NELA nurse and an electronic referral order in a digital acute abdomen pathway with mandatory frailty scoring (three cycles)

cycle2.result: 18 NELA referrals received and completed (6 in March–June 2024 after the proforma); geriatrician review rose from 40% in March 2024 to 100% for November 2024 to January 2025 in NELA audit figures.

result.other_findings: Geriatricians on the frailty session completed CGAs for all referred patients.

result.setting: Single tertiary centre in Romania; adults undergoing emergency laparotomy

cycle1.result: Actual 30-day mortality 31.4% vs NELA predicted 5.78% (1.84;21.48) and ACS-NSQIP 5.5% (1.2;24.2); correlation with actual mortality R²=0.33 and R²=0.41 (both p<0.0001).

result.other_findings: Both calculators underpredicted 30-day mortality despite strong correlation with each other (R²=0.88).

result.setting: Healthcare professionals reviewing images, Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Initial diagnostic accuracy 65%; higher among consultants and with CT (P < 0.01).

result.intervention: Teaching on four key distinguishing imaging features

cycle2.result: Accuracy improved to 81%, with carotid body tumours better identified (P < 0.05).

result.other_findings: MRI and non-consultant reviewers were associated with lower confidence.

result.setting: Cardiff Health Access Practice, primary care for refugees and asylum seekers
result.standard: All Wales pharmacological PTSD prescribing algorithm (Cardiff and Vale Traumatic Stress Service, based on NICE and ISTSS guidelines)

cycle1.result: Only 10/130 initiated on a first-line medication; 117 started on a fourth-line medication; none on second- or third-line medications.

result.other_findings: The algorithm had not yet been fully introduced; teaching on the algorithm followed the audit.

result.setting: Surgical unit 1, Holy Family Hospital, Rawalpindi Medical University
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Documentation Checklist (23 elements)

cycle1.result: Five elements absent in all notes (estimated blood loss, antibiotic prophylaxis, time-in, complications, nature of surgery: 0%); operative diagnosis 30%, OT staff names 43%, anaesthetist details 73%, incision 70%, DVT prophylaxis 3/37 (8.1%).

result.intervention: Revised RCS-based operation note template, real-time theatre reminders and staff feedback at morning meetings

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in 22/23 elements: complications 98%, time-in 89%, estimated blood loss 96%, antibiotic prophylaxis 83%, DVT prophylaxis 80%; OT staff names least compliant (71%).

result.other_findings: Surgeon name, findings, postoperative instructions, assistant, procedure name and time out were already >95%.

result.topic: Epilepsy aetiology investigation in learning disability
result.setting: Epilepsy Service, Bromley Community Learning Disability Team, Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE and ILAE: 100% of patients should have sufficient aetiological investigation (dysmorphism assessment, neuroimaging and genomics as appropriate)

cycle1.result: Aetiology structural 42%, genetic 13%, infectious 5%, unknown 41% (n=31); 58% (n=18) of unknown had outstanding investigations, 72% (n=13) with no apparent reason.

result.other_findings: Genomics was the commonest outstanding investigation (70%); 40% (n=12) newly eligible for whole genome sequencing.

result.topic: Modified Barthel Index as functional outcome measure
result.setting: Stroke rehabilitation unit, St Columcille's Hospital, Loughlinstown, Dublin

cycle1.result: MBI scores increased from 41 to 63/100, average increase 22% (up to 49%); predicted 'unlikely to return home' fell from 56% to 38%.

result.other_findings: No significant correlation between MBI and Shah's predicted outcomes.

result.topic: Airway and respiratory complications during anaesthesia
result.setting: 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) of the Royal College of Anaesthetists; national survey and case reports

cycle1.result: Among 24,721 surveyed cases, 421 airway and 264 respiratory complications; commonest airway complications laryngospasm 157 (37%), airway failure 125 (30%), aspiration 27 (6%); emergency front of neck airway 1 in 8370.

result.other_findings: Of 881 cardiac arrest reports, airway and respiratory complications accounted for 113 (13%) arrests and 32 (9%) deaths, hypoxaemia the commonest cause; six unrecognised oesophageal intubations, three causing arrest, with capnography misinterpretation recurrent.

result.setting: Major trauma centre, Lancashire Teaching Hospitals, Preston; patients aged 65 and over
result.standard: NHFD key performance indicators: orthogeriatric review within 72 hours, surgery within 36 hours, post-operative weight bearing, confusion assessment, discharge home

cycle1.result: Orthogeriatric review within 72 hours 84%; surgery within 36 hours 32% (over 36 hours in 92% of peri-prosthetic fractures); 37% not advised to fully weight bear; confusion assessment 84%; 61% discharged to prior place of living.

result.other_findings: Care for non-hip femoral fractures fell short of hip fracture standards, especially time to surgery in peri-prosthetic fractures.

result.setting: Auckland City Hospital surgical patients

cycle1.result: 90-day mortality 395/9475 (4%).

cycle2.result: 90-day mortality 362/10,589 (3%), OR 0.93 (0.80–1.09), p = 0.4; days alive and out of hospital 1.0 (0.4–1.6) days longer, p < 0.001.

result.other_findings: Changes were indistinguishable from longer-term trends over 2004–2013 (57,577 patients); Māori had worse outcomes than non-Māori.

result.setting: Range of wards caring for older patients, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE and AMRC guidance on discharge summary content

cycle1.result: 13% of discharge summaries scored 'good' across the four main components (follow-up actions, medicines, clinical summary, functional assessment).

result.intervention: Monthly audit with a live-feedback system to ward teams from February 2018 (suspended April to September 2019 due to staffing, then restarted)

cycle2.result: 31% scored 'good' (40% in March 2019, falling to 20% in July 2019 while feedback was suspended).

result.other_findings: Quality deteriorated when feedback stopped and recovered quickly when it restarted.

result.topic: Bone health assessment in Parkinson's disease
result.setting: Weekly Parkinson's Disease Interdisciplinary Clinic, age-related day hospital, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 36% had known osteoporosis, of whom 33% were not on treatment; 27% had a previous fragility fracture, 33% of these not on treatment; 27% had a DXA scan.

result.intervention: 'Bone health' section added to the clinic proforma

cycle2.result: Suboptimal bone health management warranting intervention identified in 50%; 25% started calcium/cholecalciferol; 8.3% restarted denosumab; 8.3% counselled on denosumab; 8.3% repeat DXA booked; 33% had a DXA.

result.other_findings: 42% were unsure of their osteoporosis diagnosis in cycle 2; over 66% had a history of falls.

result.setting: Assisted conception unit, Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local project targets for total cycle time and data administration time

cycle1.result: Average total cycle time for administrative steps around 17 days; data administration time around 30 min per patient.

result.intervention: Real-time data entry into a single data system (IDEAS) as part of clinical jobs, over five PDSA cycles plus two sustainability cycles

cycle2.result: Total cycle time cut to 0 or 1 days and data administration time to around 18 min; all metrics reliably within targets.

result.other_findings: Paper and spreadsheets removed, and a 2-yearly storage tank audit replaced by a rolling audit.

result.setting: Irish Hip Fracture Database (national clinical audit); realist evaluation protocol

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Protocol for a realist evaluation using literature review, qualitative interviews and an expert panel to develop programme theories on how a national audit generates impact; no results reported.

result.topic: Perineural catheter analgesia in hip fracture
result.setting: Acute pain team, Cork University Hospital (tertiary hospital)
result.standard: ESRA recommendation of regional analgesia (femoral or PENG block) for hip fracture

cycle1.result: Early catheter removal (<72 hours) in 23 cases (59%), 15 removed by patients with delirium.

result.other_findings: Pre-existing cognitive impairment in 18 (40%) and postoperative delirium in 21 (49%); 16 (90%) of the cognitively impaired developed delirium. Practice under review.

result.topic: Secondary prevention prescribing in vascular patients
result.setting: Vascular surgery department, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary (tertiary centre)
result.standard: Guidance-based secondary prevention with antiplatelets and statins

cycle1.result: Antiplatelets started by discharge in 36% of those admitted without antiplatelet or anticoagulant; statins started in 20% of those without lipid-lowering therapy; 15% discharged on no secondary prevention.

result.intervention: Education on guidance-based secondary prevention and modification of the daily handover proforma to monitor prescribing

cycle2.result: Antiplatelet initiation 55% and statin initiation 41% in eligible patients; 13% discharged on no secondary prevention.

result.other_findings: On admission 70% (pre) and 49% (post) were already on antithrombotic plus statin therapy.

result.topic: COVID-19 green pathways in elective surgery
result.setting: 46 centres in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; UK-FALCON national audit of foot and ankle surgery

cycle1.result: No significant difference in perioperative COVID-19 infection between blue and green pathways in phase 1 (p = .109, .923, .577).

cycle2.result: Significant reduction in infection on the green pathway pre-lockdown (p < .001) and during lockdown (p < .001). Overall infection 1.07% (69/6,470) blue vs 0.21% (9/4,280) green.

result.other_findings: No significant difference in COVID-19 related mortality between pathways; 10,846 patients in total.

result.setting: Orthopaedic service and fracture liaison service, Letterkenny University Hospital, Co. Donegal
result.standard: Fifth Irish Hip Fracture Standard (bone health assessment) and British Geriatrics Society guidance on IV zoledronate after hip fracture

cycle1.result: 100% reviewed by the fracture liaison service; bone protection recommended for 46 (60%) via GP letter; only 7/46 (15.2%) had started treatment at follow-up.

result.other_findings: An IV zoledronate clinic for patients after hip fracture is being established.

result.setting: Four extended care units for residents over 65, Our Lady's Hospice and Care Services, Dublin
result.standard: Two HSE standards for documentation of indication and duration on antimicrobial prescriptions

cycle1.result: Of 136 antimicrobial prescriptions, 63.24% had indication, 66.18% duration and 55.88% both documented; 55/84 residents (65.5%) had at least one antimicrobial.

result.other_findings: Oral/enteral prescriptions had highest adherence (88.90%) vs topical 49.5%; no prophylactic prescriptions (n = 32) had indication or duration recorded.

result.setting: Emergency department and geriatric ward, large teaching hospital, Cork
result.standard: National dementia care standards and local hospital group KPIs, including 4AT delirium screening

cycle1.result: 85% compliance with the 4AT tool; 17/20 charts had complete 4AT scores.

cycle2.result: 4AT compliance fell to 40%; 11/20 charts had scores recorded, only 8 fully completed.

result.other_findings: Environmental audit showed poor dementia-friendly compliance (signage, clutter, bedroom colour contrast); all ward staff trained in the Sunflower life story tool.

result.topic: Routine preoperative ECG before cataract surgery
result.setting: Low-risk ophthalmic surgery under sedation, Singapore General Hospital
result.standard: International guidelines advising against routine preoperative ECG in low-risk ophthalmic surgery

cycle1.result: Cancellations 3%; 275 cardiology referrals.

result.intervention: Phased removal of routine preoperative ECGs: randomised pilot (1,000 patients), then all cataract surgery under sedation, then all low-risk ophthalmic surgery under sedation

cycle2.result: 67 cancellations (0.65%); cardiology referrals fell 57% (275 to 116, p<0.0001); estimated savings SGD 733,738.

result.other_findings: Phase three (9,955 cases) achieved an 83% reduction in ECG use with no preventable perioperative events; phase one showed no difference in events (4.0% vs 3.2%, p=0.79).

result.setting: International multicentre cohort from the Oesophagogastric Anastomosis Audit (OGAA)

cycle1.result: Pulmonary complications lower after totally MIE than open and hybrid (31% vs 38% vs 39%, p=0.002; adjusted OR vs open 0.57).

result.other_findings: MIE had higher anastomotic leak (16% vs 11% vs 11%, p=0.026) but similar 90-day mortality (3% vs 4% vs 3%).

result.topic: GP referrals to perinatal mental health
result.setting: Perinatal Mental Health Service, four localities

cycle1.result: 66% used the referral proforma and 20% a letter; 25% did not state antenatal or postnatal status; medication stopped in 10%, and 64% of those proformas were incomplete.

result.other_findings: Reason for referral was mostly unclear and some referrals were illegible; discussions with GP practices and a re-audit are planned.

result.setting: Edisford and Hyndburn psychiatric inpatient wards, Royal Blackburn Hospital
result.standard: DVLA and GMC standards: advise patients when mental state or medication may affect driving, inform them of duty to notify the DVLA, and document this

cycle1.result: 19 (95%) on psychotropics that may impair driving; only 1 had documented driving advice at discharge; no documented DVLA contact by clinicians.

result.other_findings: Ward education on DVLA and GMC standards and a re-audit after 1 month are recommended.

result.topic: Osteoporosis assessment in inflammatory bowel disease
result.setting: Inflammatory bowel disease outpatient clinic, Midlands Regional Hospital Mullingar
result.standard: European Crohn's and Colitis Organisation (ECCO) recommendations on bone protection in IBD

cycle1.result: All had >3 months systemic steroids; FRAX assessment in 2 (2%); DEXA ordered in 22 (21%), 7 (7%) by the IBD clinic; bone protection in 21 (20%).

result.other_findings: 39 of 150 charts lacked essential data, so FRAX scores could not be calculated; an intervention tool is being designed before re-audit.

result.topic: Paediatric forearm fracture manipulation in the emergency department
