result.setting: 51 hospitals across Great Britain; national trainee-led collaborative audit (CURFFED)
result.standard: BOAST standards for the early management of the paediatric forearm fracture

cycle1.result: Overall compliance with BOAST standards 63%; of 577 eligible for ED manipulation, 424 (73%) managed in ED and 89 (21%) needed later theatre manipulation; IV sedation in 28% (n=120).

result.other_findings: Survey of 683 clinicians: barriers to ED manipulation were staff availability (65.7%) and physical space (50.4%); orthopaedic consultants more likely than registrars to favour theatre reduction (OR 1.9).

result.setting: Large tertiary referral hospital, St James's Hospital, Dublin; patients with dementia who died in hospital
result.standard: NICE guidance that people with dementia should have every opportunity to discuss future care wishes

cycle1.result: Only 14% had an advance care plan; 22% had resuscitation status recorded on admission; palliative care involved in 40%.

result.other_findings: Resuscitation status was mostly documented about 15 days before death; 2 patients had no status documented and 3 received CPR.

result.setting: 12 UK cardiac surgical centres; Association of Cardiothoracic Anaesthetists national audit

cycle1.result: 5895 (31%) had preoperative anaemia (centre range 23% to 45%); anaemia independently associated with transfusion (OR 2.75), mortality (OR 1.42) and longer stay.

result.other_findings: Regional variation remained after adjustment (p < 0.001); each 10 g/l fall in haemoglobin raised odds of transfusion by 43% and mortality by 16%.

result.setting: Tier 4 specialist eating disorder inpatient unit
result.standard: Six standards from NICE guidelines: DEXA after 9–12 months of anorexia nervosa, repeat every two years, professional interpretation and patient education

cycle1.result: 30% of eligible patients scanned; 6% had results explained by professionals; patient education documented in 50%.

result.intervention: Structured recommendations: DEXA integrated into admission protocols, improved documentation and multidisciplinary interpretation and patient education

cycle2.result: 62.5% of eligible patients scanned; 80% had results interpreted and explained; education documented in 80%; scanning interval adherence 100%.

result.other_findings: No documentation of hormonal treatments or discussion of scan utility before use.

result.setting: Liaison psychiatry service, acute hospital, West London NHS
result.standard: GMC and DVLA guidance: assess driving status, advise and document

cycle1.result: Driving status documented in 5%; no documented DVLA advice when indicated.

result.intervention: Driving status and DVLA advice prompt added to the assessment template, verbal and email reminders, sharing case learning and visual prompts in the team office (PDSA cycles)

cycle2.result: Driving status documented in 50% by week three; DVLA advice provided in 13.6%.

result.other_findings: Gaps persisted in giving DVLA advice once driving status was confirmed.

result.topic: Index admission cholecystectomy for gallstone pancreatitis
result.setting: Single surgical unit, University Hospital Hairmyres, NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: AUGIS guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy during index admission or within two weeks for surgically fit patients with mild to moderate gallstone pancreatitis

cycle1.result: 19 (16.5%) had inpatient cholecystectomy, 42 (36.5%) outpatient cholecystectomy, 4 (3.5%) declined, 10 (8.7%) unfit; no documented reason in 40 (34.8%).

result.other_findings: Median length of stay 5.8 days; median Charlson index 4.5 in those with no documented reason.

result.setting: UK hospitals; 12-month registry phase of the 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) of the Royal College of Anaesthetists

cycle1.result: Initial rhythm non-shockable in 723 (82%); 665 (75%) survived the initial event and 384 (52%) survived to discharge; favourable functional outcome in 249 (88%) survivors.

result.other_findings: Care rated good in 464 (53%) and poor in 18 (2%), with poor elements in a further 245 (28%); care before arrest most often poor (92, 11%).

result.topic: Perioperative practice in deceased donor kidney transplantation
result.setting: 14 UK transplant centres; National Transplant Access to Theatre (NTACT) prospective audit

cycle1.result: Pre-operative antibiotics 98.4%; consultant surgeon led 91.7% (n=409), consultant anaesthetist 61.4%; central lines 67.7%, arterial lines 44.2%, advanced haemodynamic monitoring 27.6%; goal-directed fluid therapy 71.7%.

result.other_findings: Post-operatively 76.9% went to a transplant ward, 9.4% ICU and 10.8% HDU; significant variation in practice.

result.setting: Rapid Access Frailty Assessment Unit, Midland Regional Hospital Tullamore
result.standard: NICE guidelines on PPI prescribing indications

cycle1.result: 63 (52.5%) prescribed a PPI; only 15 (23.8%) had a documented indication in line with NICE.

result.other_findings: Only one record mentioned PPI for iatrogenic gastritis despite gastro-erosive drugs; no records mentioned deprescribing.

result.setting: Two UK centres; adults undergoing emergency laparotomy

cycle1.result: Actual 30-day mortality 9.74% vs NELA predicted 9.8% and ACS-NSQIP 6.59%; only NELA correlated strongly with actual mortality (R²=0.31, p<0.0001).

result.other_findings: Under 70s: actual 5.78%, NELA 5.53%, ACS-NSQIP 3.41%; over 70s: actual 13.96%, NELA 14.02%, ACS-NSQIP 9.76%, with weak correlation.

result.topic: Anticholinergic burden review in cognitive impairment
result.setting: East Hub Older Adult Community Mental Health Team, BSMHFT
result.standard: NICE guidelines on assessing and optimising anticholinergic burden

cycle1.result: 24% of patients with an ACB score greater than 3 had no documented assessment of anticholinergic burden or medication optimisation.

result.other_findings: Findings disseminated Trust-wide and an ACB calculator (medichec.com) adopted before re-audit.

result.setting: Older people's inpatient ward, Kingfisher Court, Hertfordshire
result.standard: Trust protocol for admission blood tests including fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c

cycle1.result: 23 (57.5%) had HbA1c or plasma glucose on admission; only 6 (15%) had plasma glucose, not specified as fasted; 17 (42.5%) had neither.

result.other_findings: One patient with diet-controlled diabetes (HbA1c 55 mmol/mol) was started on metformin; clerking proforma and induction changes proposed.

result.setting: Foundation Year 1 and 2 doctors across the Yorkshire and the Humber deanery (district general and tertiary hospitals)
result.standard: Audit standards derived from RCS England, GMC National Training Survey 2024 and GIRFT productivity guidance

cycle1.result: 82 responses (F1 n=51, F2 n=31); 42% had consistent theatre access, 25.9% assisted in surgical procedures, 11% received regular feedback, 20.5% reported career guidance and 8% felt prepared for CST.

result.other_findings: Quality ratings clustered at 1–2 of 5 and DGH vs tertiary differences were small; barriers included rota gaps, list cancellations and lack of protected time.

result.topic: Obesity identification and weight management referral in mental illness
result.setting: Three general practice surgeries (SMI and depression registers)

cycle1.result: 189 (32%) patients met the criteria for referral to weight management; 154 (81%) accepted and 35 (18%) declined.

result.intervention: Patients meeting obesity criteria at their twice-yearly mental health and medication review were offered referral to a 12-week local authority weight management programme.
result.other_findings: A review of BMI change at 6 and 12 months after referral is planned.

result.setting: Dedicated acute stroke ward, model 4 tertiary teaching hospital (Cork University Hospital)
result.standard: High-intensity statin (SPARCL trial) and Medicines Management Programme recommendation of atorvastatin as preferred drug

cycle1.result: 19 of 21 patients on a statin at data collection (13 before admission); 76% had a change in statin type or dose during admission; 95% were prescribed their statin at night.

result.intervention: Planned education session with pharmacy on atorvastatin/rosuvastatin prescribing timing, with re-audit to follow.
result.other_findings: Point prevalence audit; authors hypothesise morning administration with other medicines would improve adherence.

result.setting: Single institution (East Cheshire NHS Trust), NELA patients

cycle1.result: Direct ITU (n=445), indirect ITU (n=40), non-ITU (n=589); 90-day mortality 74, 16 and 41 respectively; 1-year survival 75.6%, 57.3% and 88.6% (logrank p<0.0001).

result.other_findings: Indirect ITU patients had higher INARC mortality (26.2% vs 14.6%) and poorer survival; authors suggest NELA risk >10% should prompt direct ITU admission.

result.setting: Adult and paediatric tonsillectomy patients, The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust
result.standard: National Prospective Tonsillectomy Audit and ENT UK Tonsillectomy Commissioning standards: overall readmission <15%, pain readmission <1%, return to theatre <1%

cycle1.result: Overall readmissions 15.5%, pain readmissions 1.4% (n=1), return to theatre 2.8%; documentation of analgesia instruction and discharge medication 83%.

result.intervention: Departmental education and dissemination of post-operative verbal/written patient education.

cycle2.result: Overall readmissions 9.3%, pain readmissions 2.3% (n=1), return to theatre 0%; documentation of analgesia instruction and discharge medication 98%.

result.other_findings: Length of stay compliant throughout (0.2, 0.1 days); pain readmission remained above standard; a pharmacist-led pain protocol and discharge analgesia pack are planned.

result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic unit, Craigavon Area Hospital (Southern Health and Social Care Trust)
result.standard: Completion of NHFD V13.0 theatre collection sheet by the operating surgeon >80%, with improved accuracy

cycle1.result: 56% (n=14) had a completed V13.0 form; of these 21% (n=3) were 100% accurate.

result.intervention: Results presented with education on V13.0 at the monthly trust audit meeting, and a sticker added to the hip fracture pre-operative checklist (time of admission and reason for delay).

cycle2.result: 81% (n=25) had a completed form; accuracy increased to 56% (n=14).

result.other_findings: 100% accuracy was not achieved.

result.setting: Medical, surgical and orthopaedic admissions, level four hospital (University Hospital Waterford)

cycle1.result: PD documented in 97% in ED, of whom 11% received PD medications in ED; 78% had a history of falls but only 20% had lying and standing BP; medications held in 71% of procedures; 69% of discharge summaries readily available.

result.intervention: Planned education sessions for staff, review of ED pathways and PD medication management; re-audit in 6 months.
result.other_findings: Median LoS 15.5 days; 38% had delirium; 42% made nil by mouth (87% for peri-procedural fasting); 20% readmitted within 3 months.

result.setting: Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, day surgery unit, Northampton General Hospital
result.standard: GIRFT national median day case rate of 60%

cycle1.result: Day case rate 64% (55/86), exceeding the national median of 60%.

result.intervention: Business case to extend DSU recovery staffing and hours from 6pm to 9pm; coding team asked to separate elective from hot list cases.
result.other_findings: Unplanned admissions mainly for observation monitoring (46%), late afternoon extubation (29%) and intra-operative concerns (18%); estimated cost over £12,000; GIRFT discrepancy due to inclusion of hot list cases.

result.setting: East community learning disability team psychiatry clinic
result.standard: BNF: prolactin at baseline, 6 months and then annually; all patients on risperidone or paliperidone should have prolactin checked at least once a year

cycle1.result: 8 of 27 (29.6%) had no prolactin check within the last year; 8 of 19 (42.4%) checked had not been checked annually previously; approximately 60% not receiving regular monitoring.

result.intervention: Proposed: recommendation in clinic letters to GPs to include prolactin in annual health check bloods, symptom monitoring in clinic and caregiver education.
result.other_findings: 27 of 106 patients (25.4%) were on risperidone.

result.setting: Department for Older Persons Services, Mercy University Hospital, Cork
result.standard: Oxford Audit Assessment Tool for Care of the Dying (1–5 point scale)

cycle1.result: Greater than 90% of patients had satisfactory, good or excellent end-of-life documentation.

result.other_findings: One-third of deaths were acutely unwell, one-fifth followed a dwindling trajectory, 15% had known specialist palliative care needs and about 10% had an unexpected cardiac arrest.

result.setting: National Heart Failure Audit, hospitals in England and Wales

cycle1.result: Ten-variable model predicting 30-day mortality had C-statistic 0.80 (95% CI 0.79 to 0.81), calibration slope 1.00 (95% CI 0.97 to 1.03).

result.other_findings: Temporal validation in 43 942 patients (2018–2019) and 2021–2024 data, and geographical validation, showed similar performance.

result.topic: Opioid co-prescribing of laxatives, antiemetics and naloxone
result.setting: Nine surgical departments, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham
result.standard: UHB safe opioid prescribing guidelines: co-prescription of laxatives, anti-emetics and naloxone

cycle1.result: 80-90% of inpatients on strong opioids; concurrent prescribing rates below 50% in several departments.

result.intervention: Clinical staff education, educational posters and weekly team reminders.

cycle2.result: Antiemetic co-prescribing exceeded 75% across all cycles in all 9 departments; laxative and naloxone prescribing improved progressively with several departments >70%.

result.other_findings: Multiple cycles; laxative co-prescribing remained suboptimal in Colorectal (33%) and General Surgery (40%).

result.setting: Tertiary care orthopaedic unit (National Hospital of Sri Lanka)
result.standard: CDC and AHRQ CAUTI-prevention guidelines: securement device at insertion and throughout use; target ≥90% appropriate securement

cycle1.result: Only 10.4% had appropriately secured catheters (6.9% done intraoperatively, the rest in ICU); most ward-inserted catheters had no securement.

result.intervention: Structured teaching for nursing and junior medical staff and a catheter care checklist with securement as a mandatory item.

cycle2.result: Appropriate securement improved to 40.7%, a near 4-fold increase but below the ≥90% benchmark.

result.other_findings: Lack of staff awareness of the importance of securement was the main reason for poor practice.

result.setting: Wards with predominantly >80-year-old patients, Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital, Drogheda
result.standard: HSE National Consent policy and local guideline: DNAR orders clearly documented in records and communicated at nursing handover and clinical rounds

cycle1.result: 33% of patients with signed DNAR forms did not have DNAR status on the nursing handover sheet; 89% of forms at front of chart, 7% with admission note, 4% unfiled; 6% of staff very confident of DNAR status without notes (24% with access).

result.intervention: Recommended: keep only original coloured DNAR forms on the ward, file forms at front of charts, add a DNAR status column to medical and nursing handover sheets.
result.other_findings: 33 staff survey responses; 82% said the coloured DNAR form (used 56% of the time) was much easier to locate than a photocopy.

result.topic: Psychotropic medication review in learning disability and autism
result.setting: Scottish GP practice (NHS Tayside)
result.standard: Annual medication review of antipsychotics and antidepressants in patients with learning disability, autism or both

cycle1.result: 10 of 12 patients on an antipsychotic and 19 of 20 on an antidepressant had a medication review within the last 12 months.

result.other_findings: Further audit of annual blood tests (cholesterol) suggested.

result.setting: Stroke and Acute Internal Geriatric Medicine services, Cork University Hospital
result.standard: BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care 'Guidance for completing End of Life Structured Judgement Review' quality indicators

cycle1.result: Stroke vs AIGM: recognition of dying 92.9% (26/28) vs 94.1% (16/17); DNAR 100% vs 100%; escalation plan 84.6% vs 75%; risk of dying communicated to family 75% vs 59%; anticipatory medicines prescribed 94.1% vs 92.9%; spirituality documented 17.9% vs 5.9%; patient wishes 7.1% vs 0%.

result.other_findings: Communication of risk of dying to the patient was 3.6% vs 0%; palliative care consulted in 14.3% vs 29.4%.

result.topic: End PJ paralysis (patients up and dressed)
result.setting: Medical gerontology ward, Tallaght University Hospital

cycle1.result: Breakfast: 38.5% sat out, 25.6% own clothes, 69.2% pyjamas, 5.1% hospital gowns. Lunch (n=38): 84.2% sat out, 78.9% own clothes, 2.6% gown.

result.intervention: Staff education on PJ paralysis, promoting day room use at lunchtime, communication with patients/relatives about personal clothes and footwear, and a clothing donation drive.

cycle2.result: Breakfast: 56.8% sat out, 18.2% own clothes, 81.8% pyjamas. Lunch: 81.8% sat out, 75% own clothes, 25% pyjamas; no hospital gowns.

result.other_findings: Most patients still wore pyjamas at breakfast; further MDT education, posters, leaflets and re-audit planned.

result.topic: Frailty identification and Clinical Frailty Scale use
result.setting: Inpatient, Emergency Department, Ambulatory Hub and primary care sites, Cavan

cycle1.result: Frailty identified in 20% of ED charts and 26% of inpatient charts (mostly by the Frailty Intervention Team); CFS used in all Ambulatory Hub notes.

result.other_findings: Staff survey (n=115): frailty awareness 92–100%; competence in CFS 25% ED, 12% acute, 33% primary care, 54% Ambulatory Hub.

result.setting: Emergency Surgical Unit, Northwick Park Hospital
result.standard: National guidelines: all surgical admissions risk assessed for VTE within 24 hours

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment complete 54%; LMWH prescribed 57%, TEDs prescribed 37%; 26% wearing TEDs.

result.intervention: Three PDSA cycles: educational poster; VTE e-learning module and inter-professional tutorials; patient information leaflet distributed with TEDs.

cycle2.result: Patient adherence to TEDs 64%, with sustained improvement in all other parameters.

result.other_findings: After cycle 1 (October 2020, n=68) VTERA 73.5%, LMWH 75%, TEDs 53%; after cycle 2 (November 2020, n=55) all parameters improved except TED wearing (31%).

result.topic: Prescribing for dying patients with Parkinson's disease
result.setting: Acute hospital, Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Anti-dopaminergic medications prescribed for 47% of patients recognised as dying; agitation noted in 52%.

result.intervention: After round 1 a medicines information leaflet on prescribing for dying PD patients; after round 2 an EoL symptom management PowerPlan in electronic prescribing.

cycle2.result: Anti-dopaminergic prescribing 50%, essentially unchanged from baseline; agitation noted in 42%.

result.other_findings: 74 patients over 3 rounds; round 2 anti-dopaminergic prescribing fell to 7%; 41% prescribed rotigotine and dose adjustment made in only 3 cases.

result.setting: 84 UK hospitals, multicentre collaborative audit

cycle1.result: Immediate weight-bearing allowed in 15543 (95.7%) hip fracture and 1071 (32.3%) non-hip fracture patients; unrestricted weight-bearing after femoral shaft 47.8% and distal femur 64.6% fixation.

result.other_findings: 45.6% of distal femur and 44.2% of femoral shaft fractures were periprosthetic vs 2.2% of proximal femur; foot and ankle was the commonest non-hip fracture (45.1%).

result.setting: General Surgery operations, Southend University Hospital
result.standard: Local surgical antibiotic prophylaxis guideline: correct antibiotic choice, dose and timing (≤30 minutes pre-incision)

cycle1.result: Correct antibiotic choice 50.4%, correct dose 44.1%, correct timing 58.5%.

result.intervention: Targeted teaching, QR-enabled guideline posters at point of care, and 'antibiotic dose and timing confirmed?' added to the WHO time-out checklist.

cycle2.result: Improvements in antibiotic selection, weight-based gentamicin dosing and timing (figures not stated).

result.other_findings: Documentation of administration time remained poor despite verbal confirmation.

result.topic: Community specialist team for older people service profile
result.setting: Community Specialist Team for older persons (ambulatory hub and home visits), Wicklow
result.standard: NICPOP framework; target length of stay six weeks

cycle1.result: 80% frail (CFS ≥5); average length of stay 10 weeks, exceeding the six-week target.

result.other_findings: Commonest referral reason was functional decline (77%); 23% lived alone.

result.setting: Australia and New Zealand Emergency Laparotomy Audit–Quality Improvement (ANZELA-QI)

cycle1.result: Lower early (within 72 h) mortality after emergency laparotomy than in overseas studies, persisting to 30 days with a relative increase after 14 days.

result.other_findings: Australian patients had fewer high-risk characteristics than NELA patients; the late rise likely reflects known poor compliance with care standards.

result.topic: ITU care after colorectal cancer resection
result.setting: Single institution (East Cheshire NHS Trust), colorectal cancer resections

cycle1.result: Direct ITU (n=392), indirect ITU (n=76), non-ITU (n=1525); 90-day mortality 44, 16 and 59; INARC mortality 8.6% vs 17.5% (direct vs indirect, p<0.0001).

result.other_findings: ITU support in 23.5% of resections (83.8% direct, 16.2% indirect); indirect transfers associated with more complications and mortality.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis in hip fracture arthroplasty
result.setting: Arthroplasty after neck of femur fracture, St Richard's and Worthing Hospitals (University Hospitals Sussex)
result.standard: Local antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines (NICE advises prophylaxis for all arthroplasty)

cycle1.result: 90% received some antibiotic prophylaxis; 78% received appropriate prophylaxis per local guidelines.

result.intervention: Findings presented at the local orthopaedic clinical governance meeting to educate team members.

cycle2.result: 100% received some prophylaxis; 83% received appropriate prophylaxis per local guidelines.

result.other_findings: More incomplete prophylaxis in cycle 2: 5% on concurrent antibiotics without full prophylaxis, 5% under-dosed gentamicin, 3% without full 24 hours of flucloxacillin; no joint infections at 6 months.

result.setting: Physiotherapy initial assessments across 6 Primary Care teams, HSE Galway
result.standard: World Guidelines for Falls Prevention 2022: all adults ≥65 asked the 3 Key Questions, with assessment and referral if any answer is yes

cycle1.result: Compliance 70% for Question 1, 36.7% for Question 2 and 23.3% for Question 3; 66.7% documented follow-up actions based on responses.

result.intervention: 3KQ added to physiotherapy assessment forms, risk stratification algorithm displayed in treatment rooms and staff guidance on referral.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 352 UK hospital sites, 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) activity survey

cycle1.result: 1705 potentially serious complications in 1150 (5%) non-obstetric cases; circulatory 616 (36%), airway 418 (25%), metabolic 264 (15%), breathing 259 (15%), neurological 41 (2%).

result.other_findings: Emergency surgery was 16% of cases but 42% of complications; complications associated with younger age, higher ASA, male sex, frailty, urgency and extent of surgery, day and time.

result.topic: Colonic evaluation after appendicectomy in over-40s
result.setting: District general hospital (Broomfield Hospital, Mid and South Essex)
result.standard: Local guideline: postoperative outpatient colonoscopy or CT colonography for patients aged ≥40 after appendicectomy

cycle1.result: 25 patients (37.3%) referred for postoperative colonic evaluation.

result.intervention: Educational email with supporting evidence sent to surgical teams.

cycle2.result: 28 patients (62.2%) received appropriate postoperative colonic evaluation.

result.other_findings: No lesions found in cycle 1; in cycle 2 two patients had proximal ascending colon polyps, one with high-grade dysplasia.

result.topic: Delirium screening (4AT) in older surgical inpatients
result.setting: Three surgical wards, Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: CPOC and BGS guideline for Perioperative Care for People Living with Frailty undergoing Elective and Emergency Surgery

cycle1.result: 33% had a 4AT documented at any stage and 25% had a baseline preoperative 4AT.

result.intervention: Interdisciplinary educational sessions planned, with re-audit in 6 months.
result.other_findings: 50% were orthopaedic patients; delirium incidence 18.7%; surgical risk factors for delirium in 69%.

result.topic: Online information on periodontitis and cardiovascular disease
result.setting: Ninety English-language websites of ageing, cardiovascular and general health organisations
result.standard: 2019 EFP/WHF consensus report on periodontal disease and cardiovascular disease

cycle1.result: Only 8 (8.8%) sites had information on the PD-CVD link within five years, of which 5 (5.5%) gave actionable oral health guidance.

result.other_findings: A further 9 sites (10%) had the information but it was older than five years.

result.topic: Audit and feedback of primary care physician practice
result.setting: Primary healthcare clinics, SINA Health Education and Welfare Trust, Karachi
result.standard: Clinical protocols for consultation and management (not specified)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Structured feedback sessions to physicians after on-site and EMR audits.

cycle2.result: Significant improvements in consultation skills, history taking, provisional diagnosis and protocol adherence (figures not stated).

result.other_findings: Management of fever, respiratory, dermatological and gastrointestinal conditions also improved.

result.setting: District general hospital (The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust), laparoscopic appendicectomy
result.standard: GIRFT and Royal College of Surgeons of England operative documentation standards (27 criteria)

cycle1.result: 7% (4/56) of operative notes achieved 100% compliance.

result.intervention: Standardised procedure-specific operative note template, targeted teaching and workflow reinforcement.

cycle2.result: 85% (23/27) of template operative notes achieved 100% compliance; template notes met 100% in 22 and >95% in 5 criteria.

result.other_findings: None of the handwritten or self-made notes in cycle 2 achieved full compliance.

result.setting: Single institution (East Cheshire NHS Trust), NELA patients

cycle1.result: RCS-1 (n=415) vs RCS-2 (n=634): 90-day mortality 61 vs 69 (NS); 1-year survival 81.0% vs 82.1% (NS).

result.other_findings: RCS-1 patients had worse pre-operative markers (lactate, CRP, NELA mortality score) but identical clinical outcomes.

result.setting: Assertive Outreach Team, Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE: annual physical health monitoring for patients on antipsychotics (BMI, BP, ECG, FBC, LFTs, lipids, HbA1c, U&Es); target 100%

cycle1.result: Only 18% received all recommended monitoring; 41% of non-compliant cases missed three or more investigations.

result.intervention: Recommended: structured consultation checklists, electronic reminders and regular staff education; re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: BMI and ECG were the most frequently omitted measures.

result.topic: Psychotropic medication monitoring in mother and baby unit
result.setting: Uned Gobaith Mother and Baby Unit, Swansea Bay University Health Board
result.standard: Perinatal Quality Network standards for pharmacological management; target 90% or more

cycle1.result: Therapeutic response monitoring 69.1%, safety assessment 44.9%, side-effect discussion 22.4%, adherence recording 78.5%, weekly PRN review 36.7%.

result.intervention: MDT changes to the weekly review and ward documentation.

cycle2.result: Therapeutic response monitoring 93.6%, safety assessment 92%, side-effect discussion 98%, adherence recording 96%, weekly PRN review 67.5%.

result.other_findings: No new medication reviews in cycle 1; in cycle 2 treatment goal, risks and benefits were discussed in all but timescale was not specified in any of three reviews.

result.setting: Emergency medical admissions, acute hospital (Our Lady's Hospital, Navan)
result.standard: HSE best practice guidelines: all patients over 65 asked whether they have fallen in the past year, with frequency, context and characteristics

cycle1.result: Only 3 (25%) patients were screened for falls at admission.

result.intervention: New admission proforma containing a falls screening questionnaire, with an information session on its use.

cycle2.result: 58% of admissions screened for falls; 40% of those screened had fallen in the last year.

result.other_findings: Of falls identified in the re-audit, 75% were mechanical and 25% due to other causes.

result.topic: Prescription documentation in community learning disability team
result.setting: Community Learning Disability Team, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local prescribing documentation standards (upload to Care Director, clinic register entry, case note documentation)

cycle1.result: 65% (208/319) of prescriptions uploaded to Care Director; 19% (58/300, clozapine excluded) entered in clinic register; documented elsewhere in 98% (314/319).

result.intervention: Standard Operating Procedure: scan-first requirement, legibility standards, mandatory case-note entry of medication and dose, centralised electronic tracking register, quarterly monitoring and data protection guidance.
result.other_findings: 319 prescriptions to 147 patients from 297 records reviewed; documentation was frequent but inconsistent in format, location and completeness; re-audit recommended at 6–12 months.

result.topic: Postoperative anaemia and iron deficiency management after hip fracture
result.setting: Patients over 60 with operatively managed neck of femur fracture, University Hospital Waterford
result.standard: International consensus statement on postoperative anaemia and iron deficiency

cycle1.result: All had postoperative haemoglobin; 15 (30%) met criteria for postoperative iron deficiency but only 4/15 received IV iron; 4 received transfusion despite Hb >8g/dL.

result.intervention: A local protocol for postoperative iron deficiency management is to be developed.
result.other_findings: Four patients without iron deficiency received IV iron; two with Hb 7-8g/dL appropriately received transfusion.

result.setting: Psychiatry outpatient department, Benazir Bhutto Hospital (tertiary care)

cycle1.result: 78% had significant perimenopausal symptoms on the Greene Climacteric Scale that were initially overlooked; 65% had substantial quality of life impact on MENQOL.

result.other_findings: 82% treated with antidepressants, 8% psychological counselling, 10% lifestyle/non-hormonal advice; only 45% reported satisfactory symptom management.

result.setting: Children's hospital, University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Across 41 cases, all patients received IVIG and aspirin and were referred to cardiology; 23 were atypical; one 4-month-old died of untreated atypical Kawasaki disease diagnosed at autopsy.

result.topic: ASA grading accuracy in hip fracture
result.setting: Orthogeriatrics, UK district general hospital (The Hillingdon Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Accurate ASA grading for NHFD casemix adjustment, compared with revised ASA using comorbidities, baseline function and Clinical Frailty Scale

cycle1.result: Audit cycle 2 (baseline comparator): ASA underestimated in 33 patients (25.6%).

cycle2.result: Audit cycle 3: ASA underestimated in 17 patients (14.9%), with no overestimation.

result.other_findings: Three audit cycles in total; the commonest discrepancy was ASA 3 revised to ASA 4 and prospective CFS documentation was absent throughout.

result.setting: General surgery inpatients, district general hospital (East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: British Society for Haematology guideline on administration of blood components and local trust guidelines

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Discussion with junior doctors to raise awareness of transfusion guidelines.

cycle2.result: Adherence above 80% in most criteria that needed improvement in cycle 1.

result.other_findings: Criteria covered decision to transfuse, consent, post-transfusion effect and discharge notes; posters and re-audit in December 2023 planned.

result.setting: Acute psychiatric inpatient ward, Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: International consensus guidelines recommending metformin to prevent antipsychotic-induced weight gain in high-risk patients

cycle1.result: 60% (27/48) met criteria for preventative metformin; only one had a documented discussion and one was started on treatment.

cycle2.result: 64% (32/57) met criteria; documented discussions 34% (11/32) and initiation 9% (3/32).

result.other_findings: 94% (16/17) of clinicians surveyed did not routinely prescribe preventative metformin; barriers were no local guideline (78%), polypharmacy concerns (56%) and primary care reluctance (33%).

result.topic: Bone health assessment after falls and fragility fracture
result.setting: Sheffield Frailty Unit, Northern General Hospital
result.standard: NICE and NOGG guidance on fracture risk evaluation (FRAX) and osteoporosis treatment

cycle1.result: 0% of patients presenting with a fall had a FRAX score; 40% of new fragility fractures managed according to guidelines.

result.intervention: Pathway with Metabolic Bone Centre including flow chart, guidelines and staff education; after May 2019, a tick box prompt added to post-take ward round documentation.

cycle2.result: 86% had a FRAX score calculated appropriately; 100% of fragility fractures managed according to guidelines.

result.other_findings: Interim re-audit May 2019: FRAX 18% and fragility fracture management 100%; 100% of FRAX scores acted on appropriately in both re-audits.

result.topic: Analgesia for distal radius fracture manipulation
result.setting: Two tertiary centres, emergency departments
result.standard: 2018 BSSH guidelines: intravenous regional anaesthesia and haematoma blocks for manipulation of distal radius fractures

cycle1.result: 87.88% received methoxyflurane (Penthrox) and the remainder lidocaine haematoma block; guidelines not being followed.

result.other_findings: Pain increased during manipulation in 64.29% (median +7) and decreased afterwards in 87.10% (median −16); 27.27% needed further manipulation and 21.21% operative fixation.

result.setting: Dedicated geriatric ward, tertiary hospital (Beaumont Hospital, Dublin)
result.standard: HSE guidelines on indications for urinary catheterisation

cycle1.result: Catheters inserted in 45.2% (n=14); insertion warranted per guidelines in only 42.85% (n=6).

result.intervention: Ward-level and NCHD education recommended with re-audit.
result.other_findings: Urinary incontinence (25.8%) was documented in admission notes in only 6.5%; healthcare associated infection in 6.5%.

result.setting: Upper limb trauma, tertiary plastic surgery trauma centre (Sheffield Teaching Hospitals)
result.standard: BOAST/BSSH (2021) guidance on safe use and documentation of intraoperative upper limb tourniquets

cycle1.result: Pre-operative skin condition documented 33%, post-operative assessment 0%, skin isolation method 80%, safe tourniquet pressure 94%.

result.intervention: Departmental teaching, circulation of guideline material, laminated reminders on tourniquet machines and an electronic documentation template.

cycle2.result: Pre-operative skin condition 50%, post-operative assessment 50%, skin isolation method 100%, safe tourniquet pressure 100%.

result.other_findings: Tourniquet time recording unchanged with 4% lacking clear documentation; no tourniquet burns in either cycle.

result.setting: Orthogeriatric service, Cork University Hospital
result.standard: HIQA standards for safe information transfer (51 data points across seven key areas)

cycle1.result: Clinical narrative appropriate in 8/10; discharge medications included for 3 and medication change details for 1; admission, discharge, patient, GP and author details met standards in all.

result.intervention: Discharge summary template and education sessions for orthopaedic NCHDs.

cycle2.result: Clinical narrative appropriate in all; discharge medications included for 8 and medication change details for 7; living circumstances documentation improved by 70% and functional state by 90%.

result.other_findings: Future management details improved in 5, 7 and 3 summaries for hospital, GP and community actions respectively.

result.setting: 69 hospitals in the UK and Ireland, multicentre prospective audit (MAMMA)

cycle1.result: Incision and drainage rate 21.0 per cent; ultrasound-guided aspiration of abscesses 61.0 per cent; 22.5 per cent admitted, of whom 72.9 per cent received intravenous antibiotics.

result.other_findings: Wide unit variation in incision and drainage (0–100 per cent) and aspiration (12.5–100 per cent); weekend presentation increased odds of incision and drainage or admission; breast specialists reviewed only 40.9 per cent directly.

result.setting: Level 4 hospital, University Hospital Waterford
result.standard: Target blood pressure ≤140 mmHg within 2 hours of diagnosis; stroke unit admission

cycle1.result: 3/8 (38%) with arrival systolic BP 150-220 mmHg achieved ≤140 mmHg at 2 hours; 5/11 (45%) who died were admitted to the stroke unit; 3 of 5 anticoagulated patients received a reversal agent.

result.other_findings: 30-day mortality 37.9% (11/29); mean age 80.9 years; median ICH score 3; mean volume 45.6 mls.

result.topic: Rib fracture risk stratification in older adults
result.setting: District general hospital, peri-operative medicine (Maidstone and Tunbridge Wells NHS Trust)
result.standard: Use of rib fracture risk stratification scores (Battle score) with anaesthetist assessment within 48 hours for high-risk patients; NICE: NSAIDs should not be prescribed

cycle1.result: No patients had a documented risk stratification score; 39.3% (11/28) prescribed NSAIDs; 21.4% (6/28) reviewed by an anaesthetist within 48 hours.

result.other_findings: Ten patients (37.5%) developed rib fracture complications, of whom 20% (2/10) had anaesthetic review within 48 hours; 14.3% (4/28) died.

result.topic: Preoperative clear fluid fasting (Sip Til Send)
result.setting: Surgical patients and nurses, London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Before assessment 20% of patients received no fasting instructions and 80% believed only water was a clear fluid; after assessment >50% remained unsure whether they could drink clear fluids.

result.other_findings: Of 20 nurses, 70% had only 'maybe' heard of the programme, with misconceptions such as 'sips of water only' and low education ratings.

result.setting: General surgery inpatients, district general hospital (East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: British Society for Haematology guideline on administration of blood components and local trust guidelines

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Discussion with junior doctors to raise awareness of transfusion guidelines.

cycle2.result: Adherence above 80% in most criteria that needed improvement in cycle 1.

result.other_findings: Criteria covered decision to transfuse, consent, post-transfusion effect and discharge notes; posters and re-audit in December 2023 planned.

result.topic: Oncological quality of emergency colon cancer resection
result.setting: Colonic resections for cancer, North Tees and Hartlepool, South Tees and Gateshead NHS Foundation Trusts
result.standard: ESMO and RCPath standards: R0 resection, lymph node yield >15, no conversion

cycle1.result: Emergency vs elective: R0 96.97% vs 100%; lymph node yield >15 94.74% vs 98.99% (p = 0.2973); no conversion 89.47% vs 97.98% (p = 0.1211); overall compliance 84.21% vs 94.95%.

result.other_findings: No statistically significant differences between groups; small retrospective cohort.

result.topic: Distal radius fracture management in CRPS
result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics and hand therapy, UL Hospitals Group, Limerick
result.standard: BSSH guidelines: surgery within 72 hours for intra-articular fractures; 4 weeks of immobilisation

cycle1.result: Intra-articular fractures had surgery on average 6 days after injury; average casting and post-operative immobilisation 6 weeks.

result.other_findings: All patients female; average time from casting to physiotherapy 54 days vs 35 days after surgery.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring on mood stabilisers
result.setting: Community Learning Disability Team, Wrexham
result.standard: NICE guidelines on physical health monitoring for mood stabilisers

cycle1.result: Monitoring largely consistent with guidelines; thyroid function not monitored 6-monthly on lithium and carbamazepine levels not monitored as per guidelines (1 patient had no bloods).

result.intervention: Monitoring proforma attached to case notes and an online database with reminders.
result.other_findings: Monitoring results were not readily available to the team, requiring GP contact.

result.topic: DOAC dosing after stroke in atrial fibrillation
result.setting: Irish teaching hospital stroke service (Galway University Hospital)
result.standard: Correct DOAC dosing for non-valvular atrial fibrillation

cycle1.result: 54/68 (79%) correctly anticoagulated; 21% incorrectly dosed, of whom 13/14 (93%) were under-dosed.

result.other_findings: Incorrectly dosed patients were older and more likely to be on 5 or more medications; renal function did not differ.

result.setting: Two general medical wards, Model 3 hospital (Naas General Hospital)
result.standard: National guidelines: routine cognitive screening (4AT within 24 hours) and non-pharmacological management (PINCH-ME)

cycle1.result: 4AT within 24 hours 34%; delirium formally diagnosed 8.5%; risk factors identified 8.5%; risk factor management and non-pharmacological strategies documented 8.5%.

result.intervention: Bedside 'Delirium Tool' incorporating 4AT and PINCH-ME prompts, with regular education sessions.

cycle2.result: 4AT within 24 hours 44%; delirium diagnosed 25%; risk factors identified 21%; risk factor management and non-pharmacological strategies 17%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Senior review within 48 hours of psychiatric admission
result.setting: Five mental health wards, Forth Valley Royal Hospital
result.standard: NHS Forth Valley Psychiatry Emergency plan 2023: senior review (ST4-6 or consultant) within 48 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Overall average compliance 97%; one ward 78%.

result.other_findings: Biannual cycles: the low-compliance ward improved to 89% (February 2024), 90% (August 2024) and 100% in 2025; the IPCU was fully compliant in all cycles since 2021.

result.setting: Old age psychiatry inpatient wards 6 and 7, Harplands Hospital (North Staffs Combined Healthcare NHS Trust)
result.standard: Trust Standard Operating Procedure and Physical Health Policy for NEWS2 assessment, recording and escalation, aligned with NICE standards

cycle1.result: NEWS2 chart completed on admission for 37/39; 12 charts incomplete, 9 with illegible entries, 6 missing signatures, 12 incomplete sections, 9 lacking demographics, 13 missing date/time; GCS incomplete in two charts; NEWS 1–4 inconsistently reviewed.

result.intervention: Standardisation of NEWS2 recording and increased electronic recording, following recommendations from the initial audit.

cycle2.result: NEWS2 chart completed on admission for 33/35; demographics, date, time and assessor name 100%; all observations and NEWS scores correct; weekly NEWS in 31/35 (rest had documented justification); NEWS 1–4 reviewed by nursing staff in 20/21; all scores >4 escalated to medical staff.

result.other_findings: All 35 patients had electronic charts and 12 also had paper charts. Authors report performance improved across all domains, meeting Trust and national standards.

result.topic: Menopause and HRT documentation in rheumatology
result.setting: Rheumatology clinics, Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases, Royal United Hospitals Bath; linked primary care records

cycle1.result: Menopause status documented in 10/90 (11.1%) clinic letters; menopause discussed in 4/16 (25%) new patient appointments; HRT documentation accurate and concordant in 83/90 (92.2%); rheumatological diagnosis accurately coded in primary care record in 68/90 (75.6%).

result.other_findings: Of 10/90 patients with APLS or SLE, 3/10 (30%) had a documented menopause discussion, 9/10 (90%) had the diagnosis accurately coded in primary care and 4/10 (40%) were prescribed HRT. Authors identified an educational need and plan a multicentre UK service evaluation.

result.setting: YCC community mental health team, adult ADHD patients (Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board)
result.standard: NICE: blood pressure, heart rate and weight before starting ADHD medication and at least six-monthly, with structured side-effect reviews

cycle1.result: Physical health observations recorded for 174 (84.1%), often incomplete; monitoring within NICE intervals in 30.9%, 6–12 months in 28.5%, beyond 12 months in 24.6% and no monitoring in 15.9%.

result.other_findings: No standardised monitoring tool was used; barriers included limited access to monitoring equipment and continued prescribing despite non-attendance. Electronic prompts and standardised monitoring templates were recommended.

result.topic: Rheumatology nurse advice line response times
result.setting: Rheumatology nurse advice line, Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases, Bath

cycle1.result: Multiple attempts needed to return the call in 19/97 (19.6%), of which 13/19 (68.4%) needed ≥2 nurses; first return attempt average 7.6 hours (range 0.1–27.7); time to conclude call average 12.7 hours (range 0.1–142.6); doctor advice needed in 18/97 (18.5%).

result.other_findings: Average 653 calls per month; 67% of staff felt the line was a good service but 67% found it hard to manage. Planned changes: live answering by an administrator with call-back times, a named doctor contact and a nurse rota, with a repeat audit.

result.setting: Older Adult Community Mental Health Team, South Wales
result.standard: NICE and Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on physical health monitoring for antipsychotic prescribing

cycle1.result: Lifestyle advice 0%, physical observations 3%, blood tests 3%, ECG 3% of eligible patients; 0% had full monitoring as per guidance; mean overall compliance per patient 9%.

result.intervention: Local protocol, staff education, a junior-doctor-led virtual physical health monitoring clinic and a phlebotomy/ECG pathway.

cycle2.result: Mean overall compliance per patient 69% (vs 9% baseline); complete monitoring as per guidance reached 50% in January 2023; bloods and ECG done in 67%; trained staff 100%.

result.other_findings: Pareto analysis found no clear pathway and lack of prescriber awareness caused >95% of poor performance. GPs declined responsibility for monitoring in the first 12 months; results are preliminary.

result.setting: Central Norfolk Older Adult Inpatient Unit, Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE (2012): fracture risk assessment with FRAX or QFracture for women ≥65 and men ≥75, with appropriate management of high-risk patients

cycle1.result: 0% had documented FRAX/QFracture assessment or DEXA scan; only 19% were treated with bone-protecting medication despite over 90% being at intermediate or high risk.

result.other_findings: Titled a re-audit but no earlier results are given. 60% had secondary risk factors, about 70% had a history of falls and 57% previous fractures; prescribing responsibility rested with GPs.

result.topic: Psychiatry trainee exposure to liaison referrals
result.setting: Liaison psychiatry services across multiple sites of a large NHS mental health trust (Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: Trainee questionnaire: most reported limited or infrequent exposure to ED and acute hospital referrals; a significant minority felt under-supervised; only a modest proportion were confident of achieving competency (no figures given).

result.intervention: Trust approved a mandatory one-month liaison shadowing period for new trainees and structured, supervised trainee involvement in ED and acute ward referrals.
result.other_findings: Feedback from 7 liaison consultants identified barriers including workload, ward prioritisation on call, rota structure, nurse-led triage and role ambiguity. A second cycle is planned.

result.topic: Glucocorticoid tapering with avacopan in ANCA vasculitis
result.setting: Tertiary rheumatology centre, University Hospitals Bristol and Weston
result.standard: PEXIVAS glucocorticoid tapering protocol and local guideline (twice the PEXIVAS tapering rate)

cycle1.result: 50% tapered glucocorticoids in line with PEXIVAS; none followed the accelerated local guideline rate.

result.other_findings: At six months 5 (62.5%) were in remission, 80% of whom remained on glucocorticoids; 3 (37.5%) had infections and one patient died of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

result.topic: Bone protection adherence after fragility fracture
result.setting: Fracture Liaison Service, Royal United Hospitals Bath

cycle1.result: 65/169 (38%) were prescribed or re-prescribed bone protection after the poor-adherence letter to the GP; treatment ongoing in 40 (24%).

result.other_findings: 1164 questionnaires sent, 684 (59%) returned; 257 (38%) reported poor adherence. Authors concluded GP letters are only partially effective.

result.setting: Dermatological surgery across three hospital sites, NHS Lothian

cycle1.result: Over 11 000 procedures; 256 patients reported 331 complications: 124 suspected infections (37.5%), 63 pain (19.0%), 62 bleeding (18.7%), 52 dehiscence (15.7%), 30 other (9.1%).

result.other_findings: 41% of complications were on the head and neck and 72% of positive swabs grew Staphylococcus aureus. A departmental complications proforma was used to collect data and inform consent.

result.setting: Dedicated 10-bed inpatient de-addiction ward ('Vimukthi') attached to a general hospital, Kerala
result.standard: ASAM, NICE and Government of India guidelines: long-acting benzodiazepines with fixed-dose, symptom-triggered or front-loading regimens according to setting and risk

cycle1.result: Fixed-dose regimen of short-acting lorazepam used for all patients; no documentation of risk profiling.

result.intervention: Standard operating procedure with risk profiling, symptom-triggered regimen using nurse-administered CIWA-Ar and front-loading for high risk, introduced after team discussion and training in October 2023.

cycle2.result: Risk stratification documented (34% low, 52% intermediate, 14% high risk); symptom-triggered regimen given to all patients with front-loading for all high-risk patients; oral lorazepam fell from 3324 mg for 63 patients (Oct–Dec 2022) to 10 mg for 39 patients.

result.other_findings: Injectable lorazepam use rose by 25% (0.8 mg to 1 mg per patient) and oral diazepam rose from nil to 170 mg. Staff and patients reported satisfaction with the new protocol.

result.setting: Home Treatment Team, psychiatric patients
result.standard: DVLA 'Assessing fitness to drive: a guide for medical professionals' – driving advice given and documented

cycle1.result: Driving advice documented in 25/86 (29.1%); not documented in 61/86 (70.9%).

result.intervention: MDT checklist prompt on driving status and advice, patient information leaflet on DVLA advice, presentation at a Learning-From-Excellence meeting, and staff education leaflet and teaching.

cycle2.result: Driving advice documented in 76/93 (81.7%); absolute improvement of 52.6%.

result.other_findings: Where advice was applicable (54/93), it was documented in 29/36 female (80.6%) and 14/18 male (77.8%) patients. Future work will assess the quality of advice given.

result.topic: Antipsychotic prescribing for behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia
result.setting: Newark and Sherwood Older Adult Community Mental Health Team, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Nottingham Area Prescribing Committee guidance EG019 and NICE NG97

cycle1.result: Target symptoms identified in 100%; delirium considered in 83%; risk of harm documented in 67%; risk-benefit discussion in 83%; review at or before six weeks in 80%; rationale for continuation in 60%; deprescribing considered in 60%; Trust Antipsychotics in Dementia Assessment and Monitoring Form completed in 0%.

result.other_findings: 114 records were screened and only six met inclusion criteria. Education, better induction and system changes were recommended, with a re-audit planned including baseline physical health monitoring.

result.setting: Cedar ward, acute adult psychiatric inpatient unit, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust Alcohol Dependence Guidelines for assessment and management of alcohol withdrawal

cycle1.result: SADQ/weekly alcohol intake documented in 44.4%; regular chlordiazepoxide prescribed per guideline in 55.6% (lower for as-required); escalation for clinical review documented in 25%; CIWA-Ar completed in 23.97%.

result.intervention: Teaching for nursing staff and resident doctors, alcohol-withdrawal guidance in nursing induction, electronic prescribing prompts for CIWA-Ar, CIWA-Ar and SADQ tools in the electronic record, and guideline review with the Area Prescribing Committee, via PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Authors report improved clinician confidence, recognition and documentation of withdrawal symptoms; no figures given.

result.other_findings: A resident doctor survey found gaps in awareness and process problems on the ward.

result.setting: Paediatric rheumatology centre, Lucy Wade Unit, Nottingham Children's Hospital
result.standard: BSPAR consensus guidance: check varicella immunity before methotrexate and immunise if non-immune; consider measles status and TB testing in high-risk patients

cycle1.result: Varicella status checked before methotrexate in 91 (89%), after starting in 7 and not checked in 4; 20 non-immune, of whom 16 were vaccinated; measles serology checked in 57 (31 before methotrexate); TB Quantiferon checked in 35 before and 39 after starting.

result.other_findings: Practice for measles, hepatitis and TB screening varied; 6 (8%) TB tests were indeterminate. An updated guideline was suggested to streamline pre-DMARD screening.

result.setting: Psychiatry posts across NHS trusts in the West Midlands; intellectual disability psychiatry, Birmingham Community Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Induction provides new trainees with timely IT access and clear understanding of MDT roles and referral confidence

cycle1.result: Clear pre-induction information 61%; induction rated good by 64% and poor by 21%; laptop on day one 61%, 22% waited two weeks; administrative issues in first week 57%; 93% felt welcomed. In BCHC MDT survey (n=9), 78% confident in the MDT but only 23% confident making timely referrals.

result.intervention: MDT guide and teaching session for new trainees at BCHC (February 2026 intake).
result.other_findings: Referral confidence varied: 56% for physiotherapy versus 44% for psychology and OT; 67% hesitated to refer. The MDT confidence survey will be repeated six weeks after the intervention.

result.topic: NOAC renal function monitoring and dosing
result.setting: Two GP practices, Bognor Regis (Western Sussex Hospitals NHS Trust)
result.standard: NICE: regular renal function testing for patients on NOACs with dose adjustment by creatinine clearance; target 100% monitored at correct frequency

cycle1.result: Renal function tested in last 12 months in 84.5%; weight checked in last 12 months in 49%; accurate CrCl calculable in 46% (81/176); all apixaban and dabigatran doses correct but only 81% (59/73) of rivaroxaban doses correct.

result.other_findings: 12 patients with CrCl <50 received the higher dose and 2 were under-anticoagulated; patients with CrCl <60 were not monitored more often. Findings were presented at practice meetings and incorrect doses corrected.

result.topic: Cognitive screening of older patients on admission
result.setting: Surgical assessment unit, acute general surgical pathway (Sheffield Teaching Hospitals)
result.standard: Trust standard: all patients aged ≥60 have a cognitive screen completed on presentation to the surgical assessment unit

cycle1.result: Cognitive screen documented in 38 (45%); not documented in 37 (44%); clerking documentation missing in 9 (11%).

result.other_findings: Of those screened, 19 (50%) had an operation within seven days, compared with 8/37 (22%) without a screen. Further work on barriers and targeted education was recommended.

result.setting: Emergency department admissions, tertiary paediatric hospital
result.standard: Local antimicrobial guidelines: ≥90% of children admitted via ED and started on antibiotics have a documented indication and guideline-compliant choice

cycle1.result: Documentation of indication and guideline compliance median 30%.

result.intervention: Weekly audit feedback with run charts, antibiotic discussion at Monday handover, prescriber spot quiz, updated guidelines and prescribing app, ID badge guideline cards, and reminders at point of prescribing in ED.

cycle2.result: Documentation of indication and guideline compliance 100% consistently.

result.other_findings: Weekly audits sampled the first ten children admitted via ED on antibiotics; improvement persisted through three NCHD changeovers. Antimicrobial expenditure fell by €101,078.44 from 2014 to 2015.

result.topic: Senior medical review in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Four acute psychiatric inpatient wards, Roseberry Park Hospital (Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Trust)
result.standard: RCPsych Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services, 4th edition (2022) and NHS England guidance on acute inpatient mental health care

cycle1.result: Senior medic assessment within 24 hours 86%; reviews at expected intervals 76%; senior review clearly documented 80%; clinical entries complete 97%; medication adherence and side-effect monitoring 83%; discharge planning 97%; MDT presence, risk documentation and statutory requirements 100%.

result.other_findings: No criteria fell below the red compliance threshold. Recommended administrative monitoring and structured review checklists.

result.setting: Tertiary referral centre, Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (rheumatology, medical ophthalmology, immunology and infectious diseases)
result.standard: EULAR guidelines and National Centres of Excellence guidelines for Behçet's disease (escalation and de-escalation of treatment)

cycle1.result: 26/50 had used anti-TNFalpha therapy and 9/50 IV cyclophosphamide; EULAR guideline followed least well by rheumatology; low adherence to the national guideline due to methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine use in less severe disease and failure to switch from IV to subcutaneous anti-TNFalpha (adherence figures given in a table only).

result.other_findings: Deviations in severe disease related to first-line IV cyclophosphamide for organ- or sight-threatening disease. A national audit was proposed to see whether local practice is an anomaly.

result.setting: Leeds Child and Young Person Mental Health Service Learning Disability Psychiatry Clinic

cycle1.result: 83% of appointments attended; afternoon 94% vs morning 81%; 91% in 17-year-olds vs 67% in 9-year-olds; home visits 100%, school visits 85%, virtual 81%, clinic 80%.

result.other_findings: Children attended school visits best (86%) whereas parents attended best virtually (83%). Home and school visits, afternoon slots and strategies for younger children were suggested.

result.topic: Early inflammatory arthritis time to assessment and DMARD
result.setting: Rheumatology Department, Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust, Preston (National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit data)
result.standard: NICE quality standard QS33 (QS2 and QS3), measured as being seen within 3 weeks of referral and starting DMARD within 6 weeks of referral

cycle1.result: 41% of all patients seen within 3 weeks of referral and 58% of RA patients started DMARD within 6 weeks, compared with 54% and 56% in year 2 (268 patients).

result.other_findings: Comparison of the COVID-19 period with the previous year rather than a change in practice. In year 3 symptoms before referral were longer and DAS28 was higher at baseline (47% high) and at 3 months.

result.topic: Sexual health screening in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Four general adult female psychiatric inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines and Trust Clinical Policy SD29 for physical health care (target 100%)

cycle1.result: Valid annual physical health check 94% (none fully complete); cancer screening covered in 55% of eligible, sexual health history 55%, menstrual history 22%, obstetric and gynaecology history 12%; pregnancy test on admission 48%; STI screening considered in 13%; sexual health counselling offered to 11%; 90% lacked contraceptive discussion beyond oral contraception.

result.other_findings: 25% non-completion of pregnancy tests in over-45s, likely due to undocumented menopausal status. Staff teaching, policy updates and wider policy distribution were suggested.

result.setting: District general hospital outpatient gastroenterology, Tunbridge Wells Hospital

cycle1.result: 11 (65%) had a clinical response; 7/17 (41%) responded and tolerated tacrolimus; 7 of the 10 non-responders or intolerant patients had colectomy.

result.other_findings: Four responders stopped because of intolerance (renal impairment 2, tremor 1, paraesthesia 1). Close monitoring of renal function and trough levels is advised.

result.setting: Inpatient psychiatry wards
result.standard: Trust guidelines: routine FBCs for all patients on clozapine and clozapine levels only on consultant guidance; target inappropriate tests reduced from 53% to zero by April 2024

cycle1.result: 53% of clozapine-related tests inappropriate, with missed FBCs.

result.intervention: 20-minute training sessions for nurses on clozapine blood monitoring on three days, plus an aide-memoire at key ward locations.

cycle2.result: FBCs sent routinely for all patients on clozapine; no inappropriate clozapine level requests.

result.other_findings: Staff confidence in clozapine monitoring increased on pre- and post-training questionnaires. Periodic refresher training was recommended.

result.setting: Eight general adult psychiatric inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust alcohol detoxification policy and NICE guidance

cycle1.result: CIWA score documented within 24 hours in 1% of patients with alcohol misuse.

cycle2.result: Alcohol history documented on admission in 55%; weekly intake recorded in 28% of those with prior misuse; CIWA within 24 hours 17%; chlordiazepoxide started in 14%, thiamine 25%, Vitamin B Compound Strong 3%; gamma GT 31%, Mg2+ 25%; 0% offered referral to community alcohol services.

result.other_findings: A 2022 re-audit showed CIWA within 24 hours in 4%. Referral to community alcohol services worsened compared with earlier audits; clerking proformas and targeted education were recommended.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Male and female long-term psychiatric rehabilitation wards (Cygnet Health Care)
result.standard: NICE guidelines, RCPsych report on physical health in mental health and Cygnet Health Care physical health policy

cycle1.result: Physical assessment within 24 hours 98%; monthly physical health reviews 62%; annual Health Improvement Profile 30%; high-dose antipsychotic monitoring 10%; ECG/bloods for antipsychotic monitoring 64%.

result.intervention: QI approach with 4 PDSA cycles: MDT strategies to improve engagement with monthly physical health clinics, care plan points, diary reminders for bloods and ECGs, MDT and patient health education, and a designated support staff member for observations and physical health files.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 92%; high-dose antipsychotic monitoring 100%; monthly physical health clinics 88%; annual HIP 75%; annual antipsychotic monitoring/bloods/ECG 95%.

result.other_findings: At baseline 10 female and 12 male patients regularly refused observations, weights and physical health monitoring.

result.setting: NHS Tayside colonoscopy surveillance programme, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee
result.standard: BSG guidelines for colorectal cancer screening and surveillance

cycle1.result: 319 requests adhered to guidelines (73.5%); 328 (75.6%) scoped; 44 colonoscopies fell outside guidelines, 38 of them brought back too early or late.

result.other_findings: 58% of surveillance colonoscopies were normal and 1% showed cancer, with the highest normal rate in genetic family history patients. Nurse specialist review saved many appointments.

result.setting: Macclesfield Memory Services, Jocelyn Solly Resource Centre (nationally accredited memory service)
result.standard: NICE NG97 and Memory Services National Accreditation Programme standards

cycle1.result: 23/140 (16.4%) referred to the Involvement, Recovery and Wellness Centre, 12 booked onto workshops; 16 (11.4%) clinic letters documented referral, none gave a rationale; 100% compliance for trained staff and carer support standards; 99.3% offered pharmacological intervention.

result.other_findings: No access to individual/maintenance CST, creative therapies, psychology or OT due to vacancies, and no under-65s signposted to work or education. Recommended amending clinic letter proformas and educating staff.

result.setting: Danby Ward, adult psychiatric inpatient ward, Cross Lane Hospital (Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Trust PRN guidance PHARM-0041-v4.2 (standard 100%): indication, dose/formulation/frequency, minimum interval, maximum 24-hour dose, review date, first-/second-line guidance, review if unused for four weeks

cycle1.result: 15 prescriptions with 32 PRN medicines: indication and dosing parameters 32/32 (100%); documented review date 0/32; first-/second-line guidance 0/18 where applicable; review or discontinuation after four weeks unused 0/8.

result.intervention: Trust-wide post-audit actions: automatic 14-day review date on PRN oral and IM regimens, updated PRN guidance on first-/second-line options with EPMA content and training materials, EPMA upgrade, and EPMA e-learning plus a quick reference handbook.
result.other_findings: Customisation of regimen dose screens is still in progress. A re-audit is planned after full implementation.

result.setting: Community mental health service (Monash Health)
result.standard: Monash Health clozapine patient management guidelines and RANZCP clinical practice guidelines

cycle1.result: Monthly weight, physical examination, medical officer review and full blood examination 97%; BMI monitoring 66.7%; six-monthly consultant review 42.4%; lipid profile 90.1%; echocardiogram 75.8%; most metabolic bloods 70–90%; all doses within recommended range.

result.other_findings: Clozapine level was subtherapeutic in 54.5% and 54.5% were on an adjunct psychotropic. Hypersalivation (57.6%) and weight gain (39.4%) were the commonest side effects.

result.setting: George Mackenzie House low-secure unit (CPFT) and HMP Whitemoor Fens Unit prison personality disorder unit (NHFT)
result.standard: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust and Northamptonshire NHS Foundation Trust physical health monitoring guidelines for antipsychotics

cycle1.result: 17/18 GMH and 23/50 Fens Unit patients eligible; laboratory markers monitored in 88–100%; waist circumference omitted in 100% at both sites; ECG omitted in 60% in prison and 14% at GMH.

result.other_findings: Suggested staff and service user teaching on metabolic syndrome and electronic reminders for due measurements.

result.setting: Working-age and old-age psychiatric inpatient wards, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE and Maudsley guidelines for baseline and follow-up prolactin monitoring with medium- to high-risk antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Prolactin monitoring compliance 47% for patients established on antipsychotics before admission and 43% for inpatient initiation.

cycle2.result: Prolactin monitoring compliance 100% both before admission and at inpatient initiation; of 25 started on medium- to high-risk antipsychotics, 9 had hyperprolactinaemia, 4 had appropriate management and 3 had repeat testing.

result.other_findings: Trust-wide recommendations from the 2021 audit were implemented but not described. Management of raised prolactin remains poor; a standardised pathway with electronic prompts and education is proposed.

result.setting: Community intellectual disability service; residential homes and carers
result.standard: PRN protocol standards (source not named): written protocol accessible to care staff, when to use, de-escalation methods, expected effect, minimum dose interval, maximum 24-hour dose and recording of use

cycle1.result: Medical file standards 100% achieved; PRN protocol standards achieved in only 53% of cases.

result.other_findings: Protocol gaps included when to use PRN, non-pharmacological de-escalation, expected effect, minimum interval and maximum 24-hour dose.

result.topic: Physical health screening in Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia
result.setting: Five Mental Health Services for Older Persons inpatient wards, Leicestershire

cycle1.result: Antipsychotics considered in 11/11 (100%) with psychosis; bloods in 20/24 (83%); ECG before antipsychotic or cholinesterase inhibitor in 21/24 (88%); cholinesterase inhibitors considered in 13/17 (76%); dopaminergic therapy optimised in 8/18 (44%); PD specialist advice sought in 5/24 (21%).

result.other_findings: Screening for autonomic dysfunction was poor and the pathway to PD specialist input unclear. Planned: raising awareness on parkinsonian medication review and autonomic screening, and discussions with PD specialists before re-audit.

result.setting: Rheumatology, University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay NHS Foundation Trust, Royal Lancaster Infirmary
result.standard: BSR draft guidance on patient-initiated follow-up

cycle1.result: 9/100 triggered a review; 8 received a nurse call-back within 48 hours; 1 needed urgent consultant review and was seen within 7 days; all 9 reverted to regular follow-up.

result.other_findings: 420 patients were on PIFU; commonest trigger was inflammatory arthritis flare (7). Authors concluded the pathway was safe with no worse outcomes.

result.setting: UK multi-regional audit, 85 hospitals (NHS trusts with BSG representation)
result.standard: Guidelines on use of red blood cells, fresh frozen plasma, platelets and cryoprecipitate

cycle1.result: 391/1313 (30%) transfused; Hb >8 g/dL before RBC transfusion for bleeding in 69/220 (31%); prophylactic transfusion without a planned procedure in 94/153 (61%); FFP at INR ≤1.5 for high-risk procedures 3/16 (19%) and INR ≤2 for low-risk 6/18 (33%); platelets at count >50 before a procedure 9/25 (36%).

result.other_findings: Case fatality 10% (128/1313) and in-hospital VTE 2%. Prophylactic transfusion needs greater scrutiny.

result.setting: Acute medical unit and urgent care, Countess of Chester Hospital
result.standard: NICE NG225 self-harm guidance and NHS England Mental Health Access Standards (referral and assessment within 1 hour)

cycle1.result: Mean time to referral 20.03 hours (0% within 1 hour); mean time from referral to assessment 21.53 hours (9.09% within 1 hour); mean presentation to assessment 41.88 hours (0% within 1 hour); full psychosocial assessment 63.6%; risk assessment 0%; risk formulation 63.6%; safe prescribing in follow-up plan 33%.

result.other_findings: The commonest cause of delay was waiting for medical optimisation. Formal staff training and re-audit were recommended.

result.setting: Two regional dermatology departments, Royal Cornwall Hospital, Truro and Derriford Hospital, Plymouth

cycle1.result: Median EASI improved from 18 to 2.2 and DLQI from 20 to 7 at 16 weeks; EASI 50, 75 and 90 in 73%, 67% and 33% at 16 weeks.

result.other_findings: 39 patients were treated and 10 excluded for missing data. Ocular surface problems occurred in 8 (27%), newly in 3 (10%); six stopped treatment.

result.setting: Three dermatology departments: University Hospitals Southampton, University Hospitals Dorset and Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust
result.standard: UK guidelines for the management of soft-tissue sarcomas (2016 and 2024) follow-up schedule

cycle1.result: Wide variation in management and follow-up; at one centre (22 patients) 4/22 had 5-year follow-up, 4/22 had staging investigations and 3/22 had tumour grade stated.

result.other_findings: Results from the other two centres were still being analysed. Authors call for a UK-wide PDS guideline with standard histopathology reporting, staging and follow-up.

result.topic: Resuscitation trolley drug contents and checks
result.setting: 47 hospital clinical areas with resuscitation trolleys and/or emergency drug boxes
result.standard: Resuscitation Council (UK) acute care equipment and drug lists (2013) and local Trust trolley content list; daily trolley checks

cycle1.result: Drug content compliance 50%; oxygen cylinders on trolley 5/29; daily trolley checks 29/32; guidelines present on 31/32 trolleys but needed revision.

result.intervention: Trolley content list changed from 250 mL to 500 mL sodium chloride 0.9% bags kept as routine stock, and resuscitation guidelines revised for clearer paediatric dosing.
result.other_findings: 84.4% of areas did not stock 250 mL sodium chloride bags and 20 trolleys held unlisted drugs. The resuscitation committee agreed to re-audit at least every 6 months.

result.setting: Trainee induction, Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Aim to improve trainee confidence in remote psychiatric assessment by at least 40%; consent documentation audited against NHS England remote consultation guidance

cycle1.result: Pre-induction confidence: extremely uncomfortable 16%, not confident 31%, neutral 47%, confident 6%, very confident 0%.

result.intervention: Article of remote consultation tips, trust-wide video presentation, and an induction session with a video-simulated remote consultation, over three PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Post-induction confidence: extremely uncomfortable 0%, not confident 22%, neutral 52%, confident 26%, very confident 0%.

result.other_findings: Only 2/34 respondents had previous remote consultation training; early PDSA cycles had low response rates. The local consent documentation audit cycle is not yet complete.

result.topic: Bone health management in primary hyperparathyroidism
result.setting: Osteoporosis service, Basildon University Hospital, Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE NG132 (2019): parathyroidectomy as definitive treatment, cinacalcet if surgery inappropriate

cycle1.result: Parathyroidectomy in 21 (32.8%); cinacalcet 10 (15.6%); alendronic acid 37 (68.5%), denosumab 24 (37.5%), zoledronic acid 10 (18.5%), risedronate 2 (3.7%); fragility fractures in 41 (64%).

result.other_findings: Denosumab and zoledronic acid gave consistent spine and hip BMD gains, while parathyroidectomy improved spine BMD but hip BMD declined. Local pathways are to be standardised.

result.setting: Old age liaison psychiatry covering 3 hospitals in Glasgow City
result.standard: Existing referral pathway using a Microsoft Word referral template

cycle1.result: 114 referrals (82%) adhered to the referral template; 72 (52%) contained adequate information.

result.other_findings: Delirium was the referral reason in 23% but the diagnosis in 34%, suggesting under-recognition. An electronic referral pathway with mandatory fields is pending.

result.topic: Menopause screening in women with intellectual disability
result.setting: Greenwich Learning Disability Team, Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Perimenopause screening of women over 40 at psychiatric assessment; target 90% of clinicians confident in identifying menopause symptoms

cycle1.result: None of the 7 eligible patients were screened for perimenopause, menopause or menstruation status.

result.intervention: Gynaecologist-led teaching for clinicians, an easy-read perimenopause screening tool adapted from the Greene Climacteric Scale, a prompt on the psychiatry assessment template, and menopause groups for patients and carers, developed through PDSA cycles.
result.other_findings: After teaching (31 clinicians), knowledge rose from 9% to 70%, confidence discussing symptoms from 57% to 80% and service awareness from 17% to 90%. All group patients improved by >1 point on a 3-point Likert scale.

result.setting: Long-stay dementia (old age) psychiatry inpatient unit, Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local QIP objectives: MDT notes to separate current and resolved issues, track progress, and assign actions to named individuals with review dates

cycle1.result: Key clinical elements recorded in only 0–15% of MDT entries; responsible team documented in 1.67%; review dates in 0%.

result.intervention: Co-designed structured MDT template (current issues, better/same/worse progress, named actions with review dates), closed-loop communication and weekly MDT summary sheets for nursing handover, through PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 100% completion across all measured domains by the second cycle; responsible team 100% and review dates 100%.

result.other_findings: Core fields reached 84–100% after the first cycle. Nursing staff used the summaries unprompted during handovers.

result.topic: Sexual health screening in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Female acute psychiatric inpatient ward, later extended to a neighbouring ward
result.standard: Current national guidance on sexual and reproductive health (not named)

cycle1.result: 12.5% of inpatients offered at least one of contraceptive counselling, cervical and breast screening or STI screening.

result.intervention: Women's health assessments with provision of emergency contraception and STI swabs, sexual health clinic referral protocol, dedicated clinic time, poster and leaflet, and an outcome proforma, over six PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 87.7% offered a leaflet and 63.1% offered counselling; 48.8% of these accepted at least one intervention.
