result.setting: Chase Farm Place of Safety (Section 136 suite)
result.standard: GP discharge summary completed and sent for patients discharged home from Section 136; aim to increase by 50% over 12 months

cycle1.result: 2/89 patients (0.02% as reported) had a completed GP summary emailed to the GP practice.

result.intervention: New protocol: nursing staff copy the discharging doctor's electronic progress note entry into the S136 discharge template and email it to the GP; all doctors emailed the protocol and told what the entry should contain.

cycle2.result: 33/60 patients (55%) had a completed GP summary emailed to the GP practice.

result.other_findings: Authors report a 54.8% improvement and plan to explore remaining barriers.

result.setting: Plastic Surgery, Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (large teaching hospital)
result.standard: BSSH closed hand fracture guidelines: surgery within 7 days of injury when fixation is first choice, or within 72 hours when conservative management fails

cycle1.result: Compliance 59% when operative management was first choice; average 7.47 days to surgery.

result.intervention: Department-wide education on BSSH guidelines and a sporadic dedicated closed hand fracture WALANT list staffed by hand fellows.

cycle2.result: Compliance 75% when operative management was first choice; average 5.44 days to surgery.

result.other_findings: 23/156 (15%) cases were operated on the additional list, where compliance was 78%; authors recommend a weekly closed hand fracture list and patient leaflets.

result.setting: 16 Scottish hospitals, nationwide multicentre study (SNAP FEMUR)

cycle1.result: 268/332 (80.7%) treated surgically; median time to theatre 120 hours for arthroplasty vs 46 hours for fixation, and 94 vs 48 hours with vs without inter-hospital transfer.

result.other_findings: 251/332 (75.6%) were associated with a proximal femoral implant and 81/332 (24.4%) with a distal femoral implant; barriers include varied classification, coding and registry limitations.

result.topic: Continence wear use in older inpatients
result.setting: St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin, model 4 teaching hospital medical wards
result.standard: HSE Guideline for the assessment, promotion and management of continence in adults by registered nurses (2020)

cycle1.result: 12/76 (15.8%) incontinent before admission but 41 (54%) wearing continence wear at audit; of 64 not incontinent at admission, 22 (34.4%) felt they needed continence products.

result.other_findings: Over 50% of patients were unaware of more appropriate continence products; staff education and review of continence assessment documentation recommended.

result.setting: Surgical department (University of Glasgow affiliation)

cycle1.result: Average epidural duration 3 days with 1.77 top-ups per patient; 36 required top-ups, mainly levobupivacaine (53.98%) and diamorphine (46.02%).

result.other_findings: Authors propose patient-controlled epidural analgesia, estimated to reduce clinician input by 54%, and a diamorphine dosing protocol.

result.setting: Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, general surgery elective and emergency cases
result.standard: RCSEng Good Surgical Practice (2025) operation note documentation standards

cycle1.result: Surgeon details, procedure, date and findings >98%; time of operation 2%, elective/emergency status 10%, complications 22%, prosthesis 18%, EBL 2%, antibiotic prophylaxis 50%, DVT prophylaxis 48%.

result.intervention: Findings presented at departmental audit meeting and posters displayed in the theatre office.

cycle2.result: Time of operation 28%, elective/emergency status 28%, complications 40%, prosthesis 55%, EBL 20%, antibiotic prophylaxis 66%, DVT prophylaxis 56%.

result.other_findings: Core elements remained well recorded but several fields stayed below the expected standard; repeat audit in 6–12 months recommended.

result.topic: Deprescribing diabetes medication in frail older people
result.setting: Hereford County Hospital (patients presenting to the emergency department)
result.standard: NICE (June 2022) individualised HbA1c targets and review of anti-hyperglycaemic therapy in frail patients

cycle1.result: 20% had HbA1c reviewed; only one had evidence of deprescribing consideration.

result.intervention: Poster highlighting the importance of considering deprescribing in frail patients.

cycle2.result: 22% had HbA1c reviewed with subsequent consideration of deprescribing.

result.other_findings: Total sample of 28 across both cycles; the poster generated positive informal feedback and conversations about deprescribing.

result.topic: Cardiovascular risk factor optimisation in peripheral arterial disease
result.setting: St George's Vascular Institute, tertiary referral vascular surgery centre, inpatients
result.standard: NICE secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease (smoking cessation, lipid modification, antiplatelet therapy, blood pressure control, diabetes risk assessment); target 100%

cycle1.result: Smoking cessation 40.5%, lipid modification 18.8%, blood pressure control 29.5%, diabetes risk assessment 21.1%, antiplatelet therapy 38.9%.

result.other_findings: Admissions over 10 days had higher adherence (35.5% vs 19.8%, p=0.017); shorter elective admissions had worse optimisation.

result.topic: Frailty assessment and geriatric review in emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Large district general hospital (Yorkshire), patients aged 75+ undergoing emergency laparotomy
result.standard: NELA 2023: clinical frailty score recorded in over-65s and Care of the Elderly input if frail or aged 80+

cycle1.result: 0 patients had CFS recorded; 16% had COE review.

result.intervention: Presentation at clinical governance, discussion with the COE consultant, and a poster for the surgical assessment unit.

cycle2.result: 92% had CFS recorded; 46% had COE review.

result.other_findings: 94 patients in total across cycles; suggested a COE referral pathway and a general surgery geriatrician role.

result.setting: Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital, emergency department and paediatric surgery (children 0–16 years)
result.standard: 17 GIRFT best-practice standards for acute appendicitis and national benchmarks

cycle1.result: Full compliance with 15/17 standards; readmission 0% at 6 months (0/53) and 2.9% at 3 years (8/275) vs national 9.7%; negative appendicectomy 1.9% (1/53) vs 6.1% nationally.

result.other_findings: Shortfalls were peritoneal swab sampling and surgery within 24 hours of admission; re-audit planned after departmental education.

result.setting: Basharat Hospital, Rawalpindi
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England (2014) operation note guidelines

cycle1.result: Documentation rate 37.5%; timing of surgery, findings, complications, additional procedures, blood loss, closure technique and DVT prophylaxis lacking.

result.intervention: Improved version of the operation note introduced in line with RCS guidelines.

cycle2.result: Documentation rate 83.3%, with all parameters exceeding 83% (overall improvement 45.8%).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Intraoperative lymph node staging in lung cancer surgery
result.setting: Tertiary thoracic surgery centre (Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: ESTS and BTS intraoperative lymph node staging guidelines for NSCLC resection

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 16.3% (thoracotomy 8.7%, VATS 6.5%); RATS highest-performing.

result.intervention: Presentation of results and dissemination of guideline summaries.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 17.1% (thoracotomy 12.5%, VATS 8.0%); RATS remained highest.

result.other_findings: Median 5 LN stations dissected (range 1–9; IQR 4–6); station 7 consistently dissected but clearance below ESTS standards, partly as hilar nodes were included in the specimen.

result.topic: Carotid imaging timeliness after stroke or TIA
result.setting: Sligo University Hospital, inpatient and outpatient carotid Doppler service
result.standard: 2023 National Clinical Guideline for Stroke for the UK and Ireland: carotid imaging within one week of ischaemic stroke or TIA diagnosis

cycle1.result: 94 (97%) had appropriate indication; 95% of inpatient studies done within 7 days of order (median 2 days) vs 14% of outpatient studies (median 16 days).

result.other_findings: Of untimely outpatient scans for stroke or TIA, 2/33 (6%) showed significant carotid stenosis.

result.setting: Royal Liverpool University Hospital, Upper GI surgical team
result.standard: VTE prevention guidelines (risk assessment, prescription accuracy and timing)

cycle1.result: 99% risk assessed; enoxaparin prescribed in 84%; 11% received prophylaxis when not indicated and 6% missed it when indicated; appropriate dosing 82%; timing met guidance in 79%.

result.other_findings: Prophylaxis suspended peri-operatively in 40% (typically two missed doses); stockings prescribed in 87% (93% appropriate); in-hospital VTE 6%.

result.topic: Sensory impairment documentation for delirium prevention
result.setting: Three elderly care wards, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham
result.standard: NICE delirium prevention guideline: assessment of sensory impairment

cycle1.result: 30% had documentation of sensory needs (hearing and/or vision).

result.intervention: Bedside signs showing whether patients use hearing aids or glasses, plus ward teaching on sensory impairment and delirium.

cycle2.result: Doctors' documentation of sensory impairment increased by 81%.

result.other_findings: 49% of the first cohort were documented as having delirium and/or dementia.

result.topic: Dual antiplatelet therapy duration after stroke
result.setting: Acute Stroke Unit, Beaumont Hospital, tertiary referral centre
result.standard: Documented DAPT duration on discharge and DAPT not continued beyond six weeks

cycle1.result: 57 discharged on DAPT, 18 (31.6%) without documented duration; of 33 with clinic medication review, 9 (27.3%) still inappropriately on DAPT.

result.intervention: Education session for stroke staff and redesigned stroke discharge summary template highlighting DAPT duration; emphasis on GP communication and patient counselling.
result.other_findings: Average OPD review was 4 months after discharge; 5/9 inappropriately continued had no duration instruction on discharge.

result.topic: Lying and standing blood pressure measurement
result.setting: Geriatric medicine department, Good Hope Hospital, UHB NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians guidance on measuring lying and standing blood pressure (Falls and Fragility Fracture Audit Programme)

cycle1.result: Lying and standing BP measured in 27 patients, 4 as per RCP guidance (14.8%).

result.intervention: Local presentations of audit results and RCP guidance flyers displayed on department bulletin boards.

cycle2.result: Lying and standing BP measured in 32 patients, 20 per RCP guidance (62.5%).

result.other_findings: None of 34 surveyed staff were aware of the RCP guidance at baseline.

result.topic: Clinical Frailty Scale and social history documentation
result.setting: Intensive care unit, Morriston Hospital, Swansea Bay University Health Board
result.standard: Complete CFS and social history documentation in ICU clerking proformas; aim above 80% CFS completion

cycle1.result: CFS completion 52%; social history completion 54%.

result.intervention: Educational posters, daily reminders at morning handover, and results shared at the monthly audit meeting.
result.other_findings: Mental health history (11%) and recreational drug use (42%) remained poorly documented; 87% of consultants felt CFS and social histories were often incomplete.

result.setting: Broomfield Hospital, open hernia repair (elective and emergency)

cycle1.result: Post-operative blood transfusion rate 1.46% in open hernia repairs.

result.intervention: Selective group and save policy (for emergency repair, ASA 3 or above, or abdominal wall reconstruction) replacing routine pre-operative group and save.

cycle2.result: Post-operative transfusion rate 0%; pre-operative group and saves reduced to 117, saving £6,840.19.

result.other_findings: Case numbers fell in cycle 2 because of COVID-19.

result.setting: Surgical wards, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (district general hospital)
result.standard: NICE guideline on patient experience in adult NHS services (clear information on diagnosis, oral and written communication, communication with family)

cycle1.result: Understanding of diagnosis varied before the intervention.

result.intervention: Clear written information on imaging results and plans, and a patient information sheet to use throughout admission and share with family.

cycle2.result: Majority (n=9) felt information was appropriately pitched; 13 received accessible information and found the sheet helpful.

result.other_findings: Clarity and helpfulness ratings for healthcare professionals improved after the intervention.

result.setting: General surgery department, district general hospital (Barnsley Hospital NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: NCEPOD 2010 recommendation of routine geriatrician input; target 95% of eligible emergency laparotomy patients (aged 80+ or 65+ and frail) receiving geriatric review

cycle1.result: 23% geriatric review; 30-day mortality 15.4%.

result.intervention: Liaison geriatric consultant employed after cycle 1; eReferral system introduced after cycle 2, but the liaison role became vacant.

cycle2.result: 4.2% geriatric review; 30-day mortality 3.8%; average LOS 23.2 days.

result.other_findings: Middle cycle 2020/21 (14 patients) had 64.3% geriatric review, 15.8% mortality and 17.7-day LOS; the liaison role was re-established after the final cycle.

result.topic: Skin assessment in comprehensive geriatric assessment
result.setting: Two geriatric wards, Southend University Hospital
result.standard: Skin assessment as part of comprehensive geriatric assessment documented by doctors

cycle1.result: 15.8% of skin assessments documented by doctors (80.7% by nurses).

result.intervention: Three PDSA cycles over 6 weeks: informal teaching at morning meeting, formal teaching by tissue viability nurse, and a reminder poster with escalation contacts.

cycle2.result: After PDSA 3, 8.8% of skin assessments completed.

result.other_findings: PDSA 1 raised completion to 31.6% but PDSA 2 fell to 11.9%; authors suggest regular teaching every rotation.

result.setting: Surgical department, Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons twelve-point handover guideline

cycle1.result: Highlighting need for additional review 33.3%; handover of outstanding tasks 31.5%; resuscitation status 7.0%.

cycle2.result: Highlighting need for additional review 91.0%; outstanding tasks 84.3%; resuscitation status 9.2%.

result.other_findings: 28 handovers covering 337 patients in total; team introductions and opportunity to raise concerns improved, but resuscitation status stayed low.

result.topic: Gambling screening in substance misuse services
result.setting: Local drug and alcohol service (opiates, non-opiates and alcohol teams)
result.standard: Enquiry about and recording of problem gambling at initial assessment

cycle1.result: 0% had any gambling activity recorded at initial screening; 3.5% (n=99) had ever discussed gambling with a worker.

result.other_findings: Most (n=52) who discussed gambling had only one positive search result; recommended adding the lie/bet screening tool to the assessment proforma.

result.topic: Weight loss before joint replacement for osteoarthritis
result.setting: Darwen Health Link Surgery, primary care
result.standard: NICE NG226: >5% (ideally >10%) weight loss in osteoarthritis; 50% of patients to lose >5% before joint replacement

cycle1.result: All 15 given weight-loss advice; only 20% (n=3) lost >5% of baseline weight against the 50% standard.

result.intervention: Targeted poster, detailed weight-loss advice packs for patients, and clinician education on local weight-loss programmes.
result.other_findings: Re-audit planned 3 months after the interventions.

result.setting: Solihull community mental health teams, Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health Foundation Trust
result.standard: BSMHFT clozapine guideline (January 2023): levels >600mcg/L assessed for toxicity and dose reduction considered; >1000mcg/L reviewed urgently

cycle1.result: 24 had levels >600mcg/L, of whom 16 (67%) were screened for toxicity; 11 had levels >1000mcg/L, of whom 9 (82%) were screened.

result.intervention: Flow chart summarising the updated clozapine guidelines to prompt toxicity review.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Later life psychiatry inpatient ward, Greater Manchester (GMMH trust)
result.standard: Medication changes based on the anticholinergic effect on cognition (AEC) score

cycle1.result: Roughly 50% scored 0 at 4 weeks; 5 patients had a lower anticholinergic burden.

result.intervention: Recommendations from the first audit (not described in detail); authors report they were not adequately implemented.

cycle2.result: Only 13% scored 0 at 4 weeks; 3 patients had a decrease and eight more patients had an increase in AEC score than in the audit.

result.other_findings: No improvement between audits; recommended posters, pharmacist teaching, routine AEC scoring in ward round proforma and an AEC calculator in electronic prescribing.

result.setting: Major trauma centre (Addenbrooke's Hospital), tibial osteomyelitis treated with fine wire frames
result.standard: British Orthopaedic Association guidelines for microbiology sampling; poor compliance defined as <70%

cycle1.result: Antibiotic-free period before sampling 46/51 (90.2%); five separate samples 26/51 (51.0%); sterile non-touch separate instrument technique documented 5/51 (9.8%).

result.other_findings: Recommended admission and operative templates and better surgeon–microbiologist communication.

result.setting: George Eliot Hospital, district general hospital endoscopy service
result.standard: World Endoscopy Organization PCCRC framework; JAG threshold of 5%

cycle1.result: One PCCRC (0.6%), WEO Category C, after poor bowel preparation and delayed definitive management.

result.intervention: Strengthened bowel preparation and rebooking, surveillance tracking and pathway awareness.

cycle2.result: One PCCRC (0.7%), diagnosed 28 months after index colonoscopy.

result.other_findings: Learning points included missed surveillance, investigation choice and referral delays; rates stayed below the 5% threshold.

result.setting: Acute medical inpatients aged over 65, Royal Berkshire Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: Admission delirium screen and documentation of delirium within the first 48 hours

cycle1.result: Delirium screening completion 3%; explicit delirium diagnosis 10%; potentially missed delirium 18%.

result.intervention: Electronic notes, pop-up notifications, obligatory screen completion and change from CAM to 4AT.

cycle2.result: Delirium screening completion 87%; explicit delirium diagnosis 32%; potentially missed delirium 10%.

result.other_findings: 873 notes reviewed over four cycles; 2017 and 2019 screening rates were 13% and 69%, and delirium in the first 48 hours stayed between 30% and 42%.

result.setting: Physiotherapy department, St James's Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Every patient referred to physiotherapy aged over 65 or at risk of falls receives a personalised falls assessment and intervention

cycle1.result: Falls assessment 57%; fear of falling assessment 30%; falls outcome measures 26%; falls intervention 49%.

result.intervention: Physiotherapy falls committee, 'Ask, Assess, Intervene' falls algorithm, in-service and induction training, falls champions, weekly falls newsletter, updated electronic physiotherapy assessment forms, and a falls prevention booklet and online education talk.

cycle2.result: Falls assessment 99%; fear of falling assessment 88%; falls outcome measures 74%; falls intervention 100%.

result.other_findings: Gait and balance deficits were assessed in 94% at the final audit; audits ran weekly then monthly.

result.setting: UK NHS anaesthetic departments (NAP7 organisational baseline survey)

cycle1.result: 199/277 departments responded (72%); resuscitation lead in 113 (58%); defibrillator in every theatre suite in 193 (99%); advanced airway equipment not in all remote locations in 103 (57%).

result.other_findings: Annual chest compression and defibrillation updates were available in 76% and 67% of departments; peer support after cardiac arrest in only 29%.

result.setting: North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust (Hinchingbrooke Hospital), district general hospital
result.standard: RCPath Thy category malignancy risks and BAETS guideline for investigation of thyroid nodules

cycle1.result: 21% malignant; Thy1a/c malignancy 5% vs 4% nationally; 100% of Thy3–5 had diagnostic hemithyroidectomy; 84% compliance with repeat FNAC and 97% with MDT discussion; 15 lacked U classification.

result.other_findings: 15% malignancy was found in U1/U2 nodules, which BAETS says need no follow-up.

result.setting: Acute general surgical ward, Hull University Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: SHOT recommendations (pre-transfusion TACO risk assessment with mitigation, reporting and incident review) and NICE NG24 weight-adjusted red cell dosing

cycle1.result: TACO checklist completed for 15% of transfusions (35% nationally); mitigation considered for 4%.

result.intervention: Teaching sessions, information leaflets and posters, induction pack presentation, and liaison with transfusion practitioners to modify the transfusion pathway.
result.other_findings: Discordance among junior doctors on TACO management; authors state interventions reduced inconsistencies but give no figures.

result.setting: One GP practice, London (primary care)
result.standard: Local commissioning group (2019) primary care guidance on interval ultrasound for gallbladder polyps

cycle1.result: 30/72 (41.6%) lost to follow-up; 31/72 (43.1%) complied with guidance; 11/72 (15.3%) due appointments within guidelines.

result.intervention: Invitation for repeat imaging or consultation with a doctor.
result.other_findings: Median 36 months overdue (IQR 45.5); Indian ethnicity was associated with 46.6% greater average polyp size.

result.setting: University Hospital Limerick, tertiary referral hospital

cycle1.result: No emergency cholecystectomies; 25.6% (11/43) biliary cases had ERCP and 41.9% referred for outpatient cholecystectomy; 37.2% of alcoholic pancreatitis admissions had cessation advice; 18.6% not fully investigated.

result.other_findings: No documentation of HbA1c, DEXA or faecal elastase monitoring; a standard operating procedure and re-audit are planned.

result.setting: Colorectal department, Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals, elective ERAS patients
result.standard: Local standards based on international ERAS guidelines (medication and analgesia prescribing, nutrition, mobilisation, catheter and PCA duration)

cycle1.result: Of 51 on regular medications, 37% had them prescribed on the day of surgery; reason for extended catheter and PCA use missing in 45% and 74%.

result.intervention: MDT-developed admissions protocol with flowchart at workstations, ERAS patients highlighted on handover documents, and ward-round templates.

cycle2.result: Prescribing of regular medications on day of surgery improved to 62%.

result.other_findings: Documentation improvement noted in early results; full re-audit analysis ongoing.

result.setting: Bronglais General Hospital, rural district general hospital
result.standard: Recommended quality standards and national and international published data (not specified)

cycle1.result: Conversion rate 1.5% (5); re-operation for bile leak 1.5%; no major bile duct injury; readmission 2.4% within one week and 0.9% within 30 days; mean LOS 6.8 days; mortality 0.579% (3/518).

result.other_findings: Described as a re-audit; time to surgery reduced compared with the previous cycle, with shorter LOS, but earlier figures are not given.

result.setting: Medical assessment unit, Mallow General Hospital (model 2 hospital), older adults
result.standard: Completion of all 5 subsections of the medication reconciliation page in the MAU admission booklet

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Education session on medication reconciliation for NCHDs.

cycle2.result: 1 page fully completed, 26 partially completed and 2 not completed; medication list section fully completed in 7, partially in 20 and not in 2.

result.other_findings: Results were similar to the previous audit, showing no significant improvement; further education and re-audit planned.

result.setting: Northampton General Hospital, patients over 65 with COVID-19
result.standard: CFS documented on admission for patients over 65 to support treatment escalation plans

cycle1.result: 42% had a CFS documented.

result.intervention: Trust-wide email plus reminder emails and WhatsApp messages; then an e-poster as screensaver on trust computers for 2 weeks.

cycle2.result: CFS compliance 65% after the first intervention and 68% after the second.

result.other_findings: All patients with CFS 5 or above had DNACPR decisions; escalation plans varied when CFS was 4.

result.setting: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, single centre, adult native joint aspirations

cycle1.result: Septic arthritis diagnosed in 13.0% (n=21): 16 (9.9%) culture positive and 5 (3.1%) culture negative.

result.other_findings: Gram stain organisms, high synovial WCC, fever, IVDU and previous septic arthritis were associated with diagnosis; CRP did not discriminate (AUC 0.63).

result.setting: Royal Surrey County Hospital, adult admissions
result.standard: National guidance and WATERFALL trial moderate fluid resuscitation (10ml/kg bolus then 1.5ml/kg/hr), two regular and one PRN analgesic, imaging sequence and Glasgow-Imrie scoring

cycle1.result: 33% received recommended minimum fluids in 24 hours; 37% had one or no regular analgesic; urine output monitored in 25%; ultrasound first in 25% (CT in 87%); Glasgow-Imrie documented in 12%.

result.other_findings: A pancreatitis care bundle and re-audit are planned.

result.setting: General medical ward and specialist geriatric ward, Letterkenny University Hospital
result.standard: HSE Guideline – Delirium on General Hospital Wards: identifying patients at risk, delirium screening and next steps

cycle1.result: 4AT documented in 9/10 (90%) on the geriatric ward vs 0/17 (0%) on the general medical ward; of 7 with delirium, 4/4 documented on the geriatric ward vs 1/3 (33.33%) on the general medical ward.

result.other_findings: All 7 patients with delirium had non-pharmacological measures; pharmacological management was given in 2 (28.57%).

result.setting: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust, elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy
result.standard: Local and national guidance: no prophylactic antibiotics for low-risk elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, reserved for high-risk patients

cycle1.result: 24.4% (10/41) received correct antibiotic prophylaxis; 58.5% prescribed unnecessary post-operative antibiotics.

result.intervention: Pre-printed stickers of local antibiotic prophylaxis guidance attached to pre-operative notes.

cycle2.result: 55% (11/20) received correct antibiotic prophylaxis; 25% prescribed unnecessary post-operative antibiotics.

result.other_findings: Further re-audit planned to check the improvement is sustained.

result.setting: Theatre-based surgical staff, University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust (tertiary care)

cycle1.result: Awareness of the Green Theatre Checklist 37.5%; knowledge of reducing anaesthetic environmental impact 57.5%; intra-operative measures 40%; post-operative measures 22.5%.

result.intervention: Results presented at clinical governance with a brief educational session, posters and QR codes in theatres and notice boards, and dissemination via mobile messaging.

cycle2.result: Awareness of the Green Theatre Checklist 64.5%; anaesthetic impact knowledge 77.4%; intra-operative measures 93.5%; post-operative measures 87.9%.

result.other_findings: Awareness of sustainable surgical practices rose from 67.5% to 93.5%; measured by staff questionnaire rather than practice.

result.setting: Emergency general surgery department, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (district general hospital)
result.standard: Local trust guideline on weight- and renal function-adjusted VTE prophylaxis

cycle1.result: 49 (86.0%) prescribed per guideline; of 8 non-adherent, 5 (62.5%) had no prophylaxis and 3 (37.5%) incorrect doses.

cycle2.result: 39 (90.7%) adhered; no dosing errors, but 4 (9.3%) had no prophylaxis prescribed.

result.other_findings: No bleeding or thromboembolic complications in either cycle; omissions did not improve.

result.setting: Dumfries and Galloway Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Tokyo Guidelines indications for percutaneous cholecystostomy (CCI 6 or above and/or ASA 3 or above, or septic shock with organ dysfunction)

cycle1.result: Adherence to Tokyo Guideline indications 76%.

result.other_findings: Interval cholecystectomy in 32% of patients meeting criteria vs 43% of those not meeting them.

result.topic: Blood pressure lowering in intracerebral haemorrhage
result.setting: Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, Dublin, tertiary referral stroke centre
result.standard: Systolic BP below 150mmHg within 1 hour of presentation in acute spontaneous ICH (AHA guidelines and local protocol)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Introduction of a BP-lowering protocol for acute spontaneous ICH.

cycle2.result: Mean BP 186/93mmHg at presentation and 161/93mmHg at 1 hour; median time to target 129 minutes (mean 120); at least 1 protocol violation in 66.6%.

result.other_findings: Commonest violation was failure to escalate to intravenous infusion when bolus therapy failed; the protocol did not improve performance.

result.topic: Deceased donor kidney time to theatre
result.setting: 14 UK kidney transplant centres, national multicentre prospective audit (NTACT)

cycle1.result: Median CIT 10:51 (DBD) and 11:09 (DCD); CIT recommendations exceeded by 40% of DCD and 14% of DBD organs; median arrival to knife-to-skin 04:16.

result.other_findings: 476 transplants recorded (59 excluded); crossmatch arrived after the organ in 17%; delays in 34%, mostly surgical, anaesthetic, porter and theatre availability.

result.setting: One UK general practice
result.standard: NICE CG189/NG246 and BOMSS 2020: specialist follow-up for at least a year then lifelong annual monitoring in primary care

cycle1.result: Bariatric service involvement 100% NHS, 87.5% private, 0% abroad; at least 1 annual review 45.5%, 62.5% and 40%; annual biochemistry 54.5%, 62.5% and 50%.

result.other_findings: Patients operated abroad had poorest discharge communication (30%), supplementation (20% vs 81.8% NHS) and weight review (10%); recall alerts and a review template proposed with re-audit in 12 months.

result.setting: Royal Liverpool University Hospital

cycle1.result: Overall complications 71.9% (n=59); anastomotic leak 13.4% (n=11); chyle leak 6.1%; respiratory complications 40.2%; R0 resection 85.4% (n=70); mean LOS 23 days.

result.other_findings: Delayed conduit emptying needing endoscopy in 28%; parenteral nutrition in 25.6% and feeding jejunostomy eventually in 7.3%.

result.topic: Post-operative weight recording for drug dosing
result.setting: Aintree University Hospital, tertiary vascular centre, major lower-limb amputation
result.standard: Accurate post-operative weight to guide weight-dependent medication dosing after major amputation

cycle1.result: 74.2% reweighed post-operatively but only 36.4% within one week; 27% never reweighed; 54.5% had both weights documented; 6 of 11 needing dose adjustment received incorrect doses.

result.intervention: Intraoperative weighing of amputated limbs to calculate post-operative weight.

cycle2.result: All had accurate post-operative weights; 60% reweighed within one week; all required dose changes correctly made.

result.other_findings: Theoretically at least 23 patients (35%) needed dose changes; 12 post-operative weights were inaccurate.

result.setting: Three geriatric wards (92 beds), Beaumont Hospital tertiary centre and St Joseph's rehabilitation centre, Dublin
result.standard: European Society of Cardiology guidelines: no routine aspirin for primary prevention

cycle1.result: 9 patients (47.5%) on aspirin for primary prevention.

cycle2.result: 3 patients on aspirin for primary prevention.

result.other_findings: 2 patients on primary prevention aspirin had dementia and higher risk of side effects.

result.topic: Emergency laparotomy risk prediction in over-80s
result.setting: Two UK centres (James Paget University Hospital and Ipswich Hospital)

cycle1.result: Actual 30-day mortality 17.73%; NELA predicted 13.07% and ACS-NSQIP 9.4%; no association between actual and predicted mortality (R²=0.01).

result.other_findings: NELA and ACS-NSQIP predictions correlated with each other (R²=0.79).

result.setting: Frimley Park and Wexham Park Hospitals, Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: GIRFT (September 2022) recommendations adapted into local guidelines: 90% day-case rate with standardised technique

cycle1.result: Day case rate 45% at Frimley Park.

result.intervention: Updated GIRFT recommendations adapted into local trust guidelines.

cycle2.result: Day case rate 70% at Frimley Park (n=121) and 77.8% at Wexham Park (n=72).

result.other_findings: Common causes of delay were pain (30%) and drain monitoring (28%); 14-day readmission 9% at both sites.

result.setting: Wirral University Teaching Hospital

cycle1.result: Triple assessment by surgery, anaesthesia and critical care in 10 (62%); antibiotics initiated within 5 hours of diagnosis with inconsistent regimens; 10 (62%) had surgery, mostly within 12 hours; mortality 20% among those who had surgery.

result.other_findings: No standardised local protocol existed; ten patients needed intensive care and 100% of cultures were polymicrobial. Authors propose guidelines and a multicentre audit.

result.setting: Medical Assessment Unit, Mallow General Hospital (Model-2 hospital), Cork
result.standard: Local frailty screening pathway: all MAU patients aged 75 or over screened with the Clinical Frailty Scale using a bespoke sticker; CFS 6 or more triggers referral to the CNS for the Older Adult

cycle1.result: Of 94 eligible patients (of 247 attendees), 81% (n=77) had a bespoke sticker and 71% of these were completed (n=55). Of 40 admitted, 57.5% (n=23) referred and seen by CNS, 35% (n=14) appropriately not referred, 2.5% (n=1) not referred but should have been, 5% (n=2) referred but not seen.

result.other_findings: Median CFS of admitted screened patients was 6; 5% of admissions would have benefited from CNS input but did not get it.

result.setting: Southampton University Hospital
result.standard: Mental Capacity Act 2005 and DoLS Code of Practice: 100% timely submission of urgent DoLS renewal requests

cycle1.result: 79% compliance (34/43 timely renewals).

result.intervention: Tracking system using a whiteboard to monitor DoLS renewal deadlines.
result.other_findings: Delays persisted owing to manual tracking limitations and workload; an electronic tracking system with automated alerts is recommended.

result.topic: Time to revascularisation for chronic limb-threatening ischaemia
result.setting: Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, major vascular centre, London
result.standard: VSGBI PAD-QIF 2019 and CQUIN 2022/23: revascularisation within 5 days of referral for inpatients and 14 days for outpatients

cycle1.result: 59 inpatients and 33 outpatients; 54% of inpatient and 83% of outpatient revascularisation candidates breached targets. Most inpatient breaches revascularised within 6-10 days; most outpatient breaches within 46-75 days.

result.other_findings: 7 outpatients were still awaiting revascularisation, all more than 5 months since CLTI onset. Delays related to pre-surgery optimisation, bed/theatre pressures, pre-assessment, MDT discussion and investigations.

result.topic: Timing of cholecystectomy in gallstone pancreatitis
result.setting: Dorset County Hospital, Dorchester
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology: index or early (within 2 weeks) cholecystectomy for mild gallstone pancreatitis; delayed surgery for moderate/severe

cycle1.result: 71% adherence to BSG guidance.

result.intervention: Listing gallstone pancreatitis patients as P2 when booking, cancelling other elective activity when required, and encouraging inpatient cholecystectomy.
result.other_findings: Median length of stay for index cholecystectomy rose from 3 to 6 days (p<0.05), attributed to CEPOD theatre access; non-compliance linked to poor documentation and slow outpatient processing.

result.setting: Surgical ward, Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth
result.standard: NICE antimicrobial prescribing guidance: stop/review date recorded for antibiotics

cycle1.result: 56% had a recorded stop/review date.

result.intervention: Informal discussions and an email to junior doctors on findings and NICE guidance, plus posters in doctors' stations.
result.other_findings: Causes included lack of awareness, patient transfers between teams and decisions documented on paper rather than electronic prescribing; a mandatory stop/review field in e-prescribing is proposed.

result.setting: Leighton Hospital, Mid Cheshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: World Society of Emergency Surgery 2020 guidelines for acute appendicitis

cycle1.result: Pre-operative imaging in 92.5%; CT PPV 96.9%; CT used in 96% of patients over 40; 89.1% had appendicectomy within 24 hours; negative appendicectomy rate 4.2%; postoperative complications 10.1%.

result.other_findings: 45.2% discrepancy between CT and intra-operative grading of complicated versus uncomplicated appendicitis; drain use 34.4%; mean LOS 8.5 days for complicated cases.

result.setting: Cavan General Hospital
result.standard: NICE CG141, QS38 and BSG guidelines: GBS risk stratification, endoscopy within 24 hours (variceal within 12 hours), terlipressin and antibiotics for variceal bleeds

cycle1.result: 100% vital signs and IV access, 97% fluid resuscitation; GBS not documented in most cases; PPI ~98%; endoscopy in 85% but only 63% within 24 hours (mean delay 42.8 h); only 1/5 variceal cases within 12 hours; variceal bleeds: 50% terlipressin, 83% antibiotics.

result.other_findings: Transfusion practice appropriately restrictive (mean pre-transfusion Hb 7.5 g/dL). A UGIB proforma and checklists are being introduced with re-audit planned within 12 months.

result.topic: Best medical therapy in peripheral arterial disease
result.setting: Vascular department, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary, NHS Grampian
result.standard: NICE: best medical therapy with high-dose statin (atorvastatin 80mg) and antiplatelet for PAD; standard 100%

cycle1.result: 28% (n=7) on BMT on admission, 40% (n=10) on discharge; 100% (n=25) on antiplatelet and 28% (n=7) on high-dose statin.

result.intervention: New admission document prompting antiplatelet and statin review, plus departmental teaching on BMT.

cycle2.result: 25% (n=5) on BMT on admission, 80% (n=16) on discharge; 100% (n=20) on antiplatelet and 80% (n=16) on high-dose statin.

result.other_findings: Low BMT rates on admission suggest poor implementation in primary care.

result.topic: Frailty screening in emergency surgical admissions
result.setting: Emergency general surgery, Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: GIRFT and BGS 'Six Steps to Better Care': frailty screening on admission for all patients aged 65 or over (CFS, baseline mobility, 4AT, MUST)

cycle1.result: CFS documented 8%; baseline mobility 44%; 4AT 100%; MUST 82%.

result.intervention: Raising awareness, education of clerking teams and promotion of a frailty screening bundle (CFS, baseline mobility, 4AT, MUST).
result.other_findings: Compliance remained below recommended levels and nutritional screening declined.

result.topic: Management of functional somatic symptoms in children
result.setting: Alder Hey Children's Hospital, paediatric tertiary centre (General Paediatrics and Child Health Psychology)

cycle1.result: No standardised approach to assessment, investigation or management; excessive investigations without coordinated MDT involvement; very few received a formal diagnosis by discharge.

result.other_findings: Communication and psycho-education with young people and families was lacking; national and local guidelines are recommended.

result.setting: Medical ward, Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital, Drogheda

cycle1.result: Inhaler technique errors in 24%; asthma control within target in 75%, COPD in 31%; 80% of inhalers prescribed for licensed indication; 35% had potential complications (25% pneumonia, 10% oral candidiasis).

result.other_findings: Higher 4AT score correlated with inhaler errors (R = 0.63); all pneumonias were associated with fluticasone.

result.setting: Department of Oncology, Ministry of the National Guard - Health Affairs, Riyadh
result.standard: Lung cancer guidelines: pathological diagnosis, staging before treatment, tumour board within 30 days, EGFR testing, end-of-life care

cycle1.result: Histological subtype identified in 94%; tumour board presentation 35%; EGFR testing for non-squamous 77%.

result.intervention: Education and discussion with team members about deviations, with annual audit and feedback.

cycle2.result: Histological subtype 100%; tumour board presentation 82%; EGFR testing 100%; staging documented in 100%.

result.other_findings: Annual audits were run from 2012 to 2015.

result.setting: York and North Yorkshire CAMHS
result.standard: Mental Health Services Data Set: 100% of patients should have ethnicity documented

cycle1.result: 823 (20%) documented as 'unknown' and 49 (1.2%) missing.

result.other_findings: Recommendations include emailing care coordinators, a clinician and family questionnaire, process review and staff training, with re-audit planned.

result.topic: On-call email request quality and response time
result.setting: Teesside on-call email system (psychiatry)
result.standard: Local trust criteria: completed request form, adequate clinical information, patient identification and location, and doctor response within 45 minutes; standard 100%

cycle1.result: Three of four standards were above 70% (exact figures not reported).

cycle2.result: Compliance below 70% across all four standards.

result.other_findings: Requests for inappropriate non-urgent tasks increased; SBAR in request forms and staff induction are recommended.

result.topic: Hair tourniquet removal with depilatory cream
result.setting: Children's emergency department

cycle1.result: 95% had the hair removed within 1 hour of arrival; depilatory cream effective first time in 83% of 18 children and 94% overall.

result.other_findings: Mild skin breakdown in 3 patients (16.6%) after cream; one child needed removal by plastics under general anaesthetic.

result.setting: Department of Upper GI Surgery, University Hospital Hairmyres, NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: RCS England / GIRFT 32 essential components of operation notes

cycle1.result: Median GIRFT score 27 (IQR 26-29); 0 notes with all 32 points; pressure settings 0; laparoscope under direct vision 2 (1.5%); reverse Trendelenburg 4 (3.0%); intraoperative pictures 94 (71.2%).

result.intervention: Implementation of GIRFT operation note recommendations.

cycle2.result: Median GIRFT score 30 (IQR 29-32); all 32 points in 37 (32.7%); pressure settings 95 (84.1%); direct vision 77 (68.1%); reverse Trendelenburg 79 (69.9%); intraoperative pictures 88 (77.9%).

result.other_findings: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy notes from two biliary surgeons over two years; all notes included 19 of 32 points in both cycles.

result.setting: Virtual fracture clinic, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, NHS GGC, Glasgow

cycle1.result: 80 inappropriate referrals: 52.5% injuries not requiring follow-up, 30% no identifiable fracture; 3 patients needed urgent inpatient orthopaedic assessment.

result.intervention: Updated referral guidelines developed jointly with A&E to resolve discrepancy between A&E and orthopaedic protocols.

cycle2.result: 24 inappropriate referrals: 70.8% injuries normally discharged from A&E, 8.3% no fracture, none required inpatient assessment.

result.other_findings: Remaining inappropriate referrals may reflect a need for reassurance or delayed uptake of the new guidelines.

result.setting: Older person's rehabilitation unit, Cork University Hospital

cycle1.result: Average contribution: current status 59%, goal setting 18%, SMART goals 4%, predicted date of discharge 27%; overall discipline contribution 27%.

result.intervention: Collaborative Rehabilitation Plan (CRP) structured booklet for MDT meetings.

cycle2.result: Current status 59%, goal setting 40%, SMART goals 28%, predicted date of discharge 52%; overall discipline contribution 42%.

result.other_findings: Wide variation between disciplines persisted.

result.setting: Stroke unit, Cork University Hospital, large teaching hospital
result.standard: 100% compliance with visible name badge wearing (#hellomynameis)

cycle1.result: 7 staff (29.16%) wore name badges, 5 with photos; standard not met.

result.other_findings: Speech and language therapists, occupational therapists and nurses had higher compliance; most staff relied on swipe-card lanyards. Education and badge distribution planned before re-audit.

result.setting: DGH general surgery service (Prince Charles Hospital, Merthyr Tydfil; Arrowe Park Hospital, Wirral)

cycle1.result: Endoscopic detorsion in 77.77% (repeated in same admission in 33.3%); 17 (27%) had sigmoid resection with primary anastomosis in 64.7% and one leak; readmission rate 30.1%.

result.other_findings: 50.8% had more than one previous presentation; authors suggest a lower threshold for surgery in recurrent volvulus.

result.topic: Pre-operative weight loss before joint replacement
result.setting: Darwen Health Link Surgery (primary care)
result.standard: NICE NG226: weight-loss advice and more than 5% weight loss in osteoarthritis patients with BMI over 30; standard 50% achieving more than 5% loss

cycle1.result: 100% (n=15) given weight-loss advice; 20% (n=3) lost more than 5% of baseline weight against a 50% standard.

result.intervention: Targeted poster, detailed weight-loss advice packs for patients and clinician education on local weight-loss programmes (re-audit planned at 3 months).
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Medical students across Scotland (tertiary, district general and rural general hospitals)
result.standard: RCS Undergraduate Curriculum in Surgery (2023) learning outcomes

cycle1.result: 56% felt they met learning outcomes; 42% felt prepared for a surgical FY1 role; 94% had theatre exposure but only 42% had assessed or presented patients in clinic.

result.other_findings: Questionnaire study; DGHs most valued (40%) for hands-on opportunities and tertiary hospitals reported more bullying.

result.topic: Readmission after elective colorectal cancer surgery
result.setting: East Surrey Hospital, Redhill

cycle1.result: 13.8% (17/123) readmitted; 70.6% (12/17) within 30 days of discharge and 29.4% (5/17) beyond 90 days.

result.other_findings: Commonest reasons were small bowel obstruction and abdominal/pelvic collection (23.5% each); LAR was the commonest index operation (52.9%).

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis in elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy
result.setting: Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother Hospital, Margate (district general hospital)
result.standard: SIS, NICE and local trust guidelines: no prophylactic antibiotics for low-risk elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy

cycle1.result: Guideline adherence 5.3%; 94.7% received prophylactic antibiotics contrary to recommendations.

result.other_findings: Postoperative complication rate 3.9%; the one SSI occurred in a patient who did not receive antibiotics.

result.topic: Oesophageal biopsies for suspected eosinophilic oesophagitis
result.setting: Two-week-wait OGD pathway, Dorset NHS Foundation Trust, Poole
result.standard: BSG and UEG: at least six biopsies from two or more oesophageal levels

cycle1.result: Of 174 dysphagia patients, 121 (69.5%) received six biopsies; 11 (6.3%) had fewer than four; 66 (37.9%) multilevel with unspecified locations and only 40 (23.0%) clearly documented segmental biopsies.

result.other_findings: Food bolus group (n=7): 71.4% had multilevel biopsies. Clinician education, documentation templates and checklists are being introduced before re-audit.

result.setting: Elective T&O surgery at 3 centres in North London (Royal Free London NHS Trust)
result.standard: BOAST 2021 tourniquet safety: full documentation and pressure based on intra-operative blood pressure

cycle1.result: 14.0% of surgeon notes did not mention tourniquet and 86% incomplete; 97.6% of nursing notes incomplete; upper limb pressure above recommendation in 70% and lower limb above maximal calculated pressure in 47.5%.

result.other_findings: Mean pressures 237 mmHg (upper limb) and 261.7 mmHg (lower limb); education on guidelines recommended.

result.setting: Two older adult psychiatric inpatient wards, Thurrock Community Hospital
result.standard: National standards for discussion and documentation of DNACPR decisions

cycle1.result: 13/38 (34.21%) had a DNACPR form, 10/13 (76.92%) complete; no CPR discussion in 29/38 (76.32%); mental capacity assessments and best interest meetings documented in 0% of the 4 patients without LPA.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: District General Hospital, East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust
result.standard: GIRFT 26-point Best Practice operation note recommendations (RCS, ASGBI)

cycle1.result: Compliance: pre-operative 40%, incision 65%, findings 60%, procedure 48%, closure 75%, post-operative plan 59%.

result.other_findings: Sections built into the electronic template had 96% compliance versus 44% for free text; 71% of notes written by registrars.

result.setting: Emergency general surgery, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (major tertiary acute hospital)
result.standard: GIRFT Best Practice operation note guidelines

cycle1.result: Significant omissions: appendiceal base visible 0%, artery dissection 46%; cholecystectomy findings 73%; hernia testis in scrotum 0%; laparotomy staple-line check 5%.

result.intervention: Electronic Patient Record operation note template based on GIRFT guidelines.

cycle2.result: Appendiceal base visible 68%, artery dissection 96%; cholecystectomy findings 100%; testis in scrotum 100%; staple-line check 66%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Specialist swallow assessment after acute stroke
result.setting: Our Lady's Hospital, Navan (acute hospital)
result.standard: National Clinical Guidelines for Stroke: specialist swallow assessment within 24 hours and no more than 72 hours after admission

cycle1.result: 14% assessed by SALT within 72 hours.

result.intervention: Introduction of a full-time speech and language specialist.

cycle2.result: 8/20 (40%) seen by SALT within 72 hours; 7 within 24 hours.

result.other_findings: Now in line with National Stroke Audit rate of 37%, but overall assessment rates still need to rise.

result.setting: Head and neck surgical inpatients, University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: CQUIN smoking and alcohol questions in discharge summaries; local standard 95% completion

cycle1.result: Smoking status documented 27.3% (27/99); alcohol use 36.3% (36/99).

result.intervention: Education of ENT juniors (foundation and core trainees) and ward-based prompts.
result.other_findings: At re-audit many were recorded as 'unable' to answer (smoking 41.7%, alcohol 42.6%), mostly day cases.

result.topic: Early outcomes after deceased donor kidney transplant
result.setting: 14 UK transplant centres (NTACT national prospective audit)

cycle1.result: 30-day mortality 0.47% (2/417); primary graft function 81%; 30-day readmission 18%; 30-day reoperation 12%, mostly for bleeding (49%).

result.other_findings: Reoperation 16% for DCD vs 9% for DBD organs (not significant).

result.topic: Pre-operative group and save for cholecystectomy
result.setting: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (single tertiary centre)

cycle1.result: Routine G&S in over 92%; one patient (0.12%) required postoperative transfusion; no intraoperative transfusions.

result.other_findings: Consistent with a 2020 audit (n=448) with no transfusions; a selective risk-based approach is proposed.

result.topic: Red cell transfusion threshold in critical care
result.setting: Nine intensive care units in the Wessex regional network
result.standard: UK best practice: restrictive transfusion threshold of haemoglobin below 70 g/l in stable non-bleeding patients

cycle1.result: Median pre-transfusion Hb 73 (68-77 [53-106]) g/l; only 34% of episodes used a threshold below 70 g/l.

result.other_findings: 444 transfusions, 148 excluded; in patients without cardiac disease only 36% used the below 70 g/l threshold.

result.setting: Endoscopy unit, Cork University Hospital (tertiary referral centre)
result.standard: BSG/AUGIS 2017: photographic documentation of anatomical landmarks as an OGD key performance indicator

cycle1.result: GOJ 68% (69/102), fundus on retroflexion 71% (72/102), gastric body 32% (33/102), antrum 61% (62/102), duodenal bulb 35% (36/102).

result.other_findings: Surgeons documented upper oesophagus more (31% vs 12%) and gastroenterologists distal duodenum more (90% vs 47%); an educational session and re-audit are planned.

result.topic: Antibiotic guideline compliance in acute cholecystitis
result.setting: Watford General Hospital
result.standard: Local microbiology antibiotic guidelines for acute cholecystitis

cycle1.result: Compliance 12.8%.

result.intervention: Dissemination of results, educational material and appointment of antibiotic champions.
result.other_findings: Demographics, fever, inflammatory markers and liver function did not predict non-compliant prescribing.

result.setting: King's College Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Appropriate immediate management response 71.4% (n=5) of medical staff and 50% (n=5) of healthcare professionals; mean confidence 3.6/10 and 7.4/10 respectively.

result.other_findings: Knowledge did not correlate with self-reported confidence; MDT teaching on the NTSP algorithm is planned.

result.setting: Surgical unit, Colombo South Teaching Hospital (tertiary care)

cycle1.result: Low fibre diet 22.72% (n=20); enhanced instructions 14.7% (n=13); split-dose 42.04% (n=37); specific instructions 28.4% (n=25); routine enema used.

result.intervention: Protocol based on ESGE guidelines, education of nursing and junior staff, adjusted split-dose timing, stopping enemas, clear patient instructions and a checklist.

cycle2.result: Low fibre diet 90.62% (n=87); enhanced instructions 70.8% (n=69); split-dose 81.25% (n=78); specific instructions 97.9% (n=94); routine enema eliminated.

result.other_findings: Last dose timing within 5 hours also improved.

result.topic: Lymph node FNA diagnostic timelines in skin cancer
result.setting: Mersey West Lancashire NHS Trust
result.standard: Faster Diagnosis Standard: diagnosis within 28 days; Cheshire and Merseyside guidelines and GIRFT standards

cycle1.result: 22 (38%) underwent FNA; median time from detection to FNA result exceeded the 28-day target by 8 days; inconclusive FNAs averaged 62.5 days to final diagnosis.

result.other_findings: Main delay was between node detection and USS/FNA owing to radiology capacity and no two-week-wait prioritisation; surgeon-performed USS/FNA is proposed.

result.setting: Kettering General Hospital NHS Trust (district general hospital)
result.standard: EAU (2025) and BAUS: pre-operative AFP, beta-hCG and LDH, and repeat 5-7 days post-orchidectomy; target 90% or more

cycle1.result: Pre-operative markers complete in 100%; repeat markers within 5-7 days in only 3/23 (13%) against a 90% target; post-operative marker plan documented in 26%.

result.other_findings: 48% eventually had markers checked, often weeks to months later and mostly prompted by MDT; automatic post-operative blood test scheduling and pathway education are proposed.

result.setting: General surgical department, East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 112 units in 42 patients; 45 units (40.2%) prescribed per NICE guidelines; 23 units (20.5%) transfused back-to-back inappropriately.

result.intervention: Departmental teaching sessions and posters of NICE transfusion thresholds on surgical wards.

cycle2.result: 133 units in 43 patients; 67 units (50.4%) prescribed per NICE guidelines; 6 units (4.51%) back-to-back inappropriately.

result.other_findings: Transfusion reactions fell from 2 (1.79%) to none; estimated saving £1830 over four months (£5493 per year).

result.setting: One major public hospital and one private hospital in Dublin, all surgical specialties
result.standard: Local surgical antibiotic prophylaxis guidance on indication, duration and agent

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 23.7% (72 patients); 22% public vs 26% private; 100% of indicated patients received SAP; 19 (21.1%) received SAP without indication; duration over 48 h in 58 (25%); correct agent 43.5%.

result.other_findings: 40 patients (17.5%) received prophylaxis for more than 6 days.

result.setting: Oral and maxillofacial surgery, district general hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 100% given prophylactic antibiotics; compliance 100% for uncomplex dentoalveolar/salivary surgery, 20% for fractured mandible and 0% for all other categories.

result.other_findings: Raising awareness of the MicroGuide app and presenting findings to the department are proposed.

result.setting: Medical colleges and teaching hospitals in Nepal

cycle1.result: 72.3% familiar with audit principles; 54.5% had participated in audits, mainly data collection (63%).

result.other_findings: Barriers were lack of training (51%), time (47%) and resources (43%); 96% wanted audit workshops.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis in ventral hernia repair
result.setting: University Hospitals of North Midlands
result.standard: Local guideline (in line with European and British Hernia Societies): prophylaxis only for high-risk mesh repair using the standard regimen

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 27.1%; unnecessary antibiotics in 35.6%; only 1 of 23 high-risk mesh patients received recommended prophylaxis.

result.intervention: Departmental presentation of findings and educational posters.

cycle2.result: Overall adherence 80%; 90.9% compliance among high-risk mesh patients; 2 of 4 low-risk patients received unnecessary prophylaxis.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Three inpatient mental health units
result.standard: NICE QS3: all patients receive VTE and bleeding risk assessment on admission

cycle1.result: 8% of patients in one unit (n=48) had a documented risk assessment; none in the other two units (n=39, 44).

result.other_findings: Where assessments were documented, subsections were 100% complete; a risk assessment checklist in the clerking proforma is recommended.

result.topic: Endoscopic mucosal resection of large colonic polyps
result.setting: Gastroenterology, University Hospitals of Leicester

cycle1.result: 47/59 (80%) had no recurrence at repeat endoscopy; 12/59 (20%) recurred, 8 retreated successfully; 93% complete eradication overall.

result.other_findings: Procedural bleeding in 13 (19%), one perforation clipped; no deaths or surgery for complications.

result.setting: District general hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BMJ Best Practice (preoperative prophylaxis for all; postoperative antibiotics only for complicated cases) and local trust MicroGuide guidelines

cycle1.result: 100% received prophylaxis but only 25% of penicillin-allergic and 2.2% of non-allergic patients received trust-adherent agents; 100% of complicated cases had postoperative antibiotics while 80% of uncomplicated cases had them unnecessarily.

result.other_findings: Complicated cases made up 30%; presentation at audit meeting, MicroGuide awareness and re-audit are planned.

result.setting: Single vascular surgery department, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, London
result.standard: UKHSA SSI definitions; national pooled vascular SSI figures and GIRFT

cycle1.result: 7 SSIs (4.8%) in 145 procedures (125 patients); skin preparation absent in 36% of operative records and dressing type unspecified in 28.9%.

result.other_findings: Prospective surveillance via a departmental spreadsheet, weekly MDT review and an induction poster are being introduced.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis in third molar surgery
result.setting: Single centre (Nottingham University Hospitals / Bedfordshire Hospitals)
result.standard: Locally developed criteria justifying antibiotic prophylaxis; BNF and SDCEP prescribing guidance

cycle1.result: 52% received prophylactic antibiotics; only 9% had clear appropriate justification; 27% not prescribed per BNF or SDCEP guidance.

result.intervention: Dissemination of results and implementation of suggested improvements (second cycle commenced).
result.other_findings: No postoperative infections in the cohort.

result.topic: Complications after facial soft tissue injury repair
result.setting: Maxillofacial on-call team, Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Postoperative complication rate 8% (infection, dehiscence, haematoma).

result.other_findings: 58% of complications followed repairs between 5pm and 5am by a sole DCT/SHO, and 83% followed repairs in the Emergency Department.

result.topic: Heart failure medication after cardiac surgery
result.setting: Cardiac surgery department, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh
result.standard: 2016 ESC guidelines: ACEi/ARNI, beta-blocker and MRA prescribed, titrated or contraindication documented in HFrEF (LVEF 40% or less)

cycle1.result: Compliance ACEi/ARNI 67% (10/15), beta-blocker 80% (12/15), MRA 67% (10/15).

result.other_findings: 217 patients screened; barriers were LVEF not available on ward rounds, lack of awareness and unclear responsibility. Interventions to communicate LVEF and heart failure clinic referral have been introduced before a next cycle.

result.setting: HPB and transplant theatres, Cambridge University Hospital

cycle1.result: 56 patients in 30 sessions; transfer out of theatre 16.6±12.8 min.

cycle2.result: 48 patients (85.7% of capacity) in 30 sessions; transfer out 17.6±10.5 min.

result.other_findings: COVID period-1 (April 2020) treated 16 patients (28.6% of capacity) with transfer out 39.4±10.9 min (p<0.00001); no change in transfer to theatre or induction times.

result.topic: Neurovascular documentation in long bone fractures
result.setting: Orthopaedic admissions, Nottingham University Hospitals (major trauma centre)
result.standard: BOAST guidelines on neurovascular assessment documentation

cycle1.result: Complete neurovascular documentation 29%; pulses documented 36%; 20% had no neurovascular documentation.

result.intervention: Tick-box neurovascular sticker, plus local presentation of results and colleague education.

cycle2.result: Complete neurovascular documentation 86%; pulses documented 89%; no patients without documentation.

result.other_findings: The tick-box proforma is to be built into the clerking booklet.

result.setting: Northumbria Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: WSES acute appendicitis 2020 and local guidelines

cycle1.result: Preoperative antibiotics 85%; omission of postoperative antibiotics in simple appendicitis 79%; 3-5 days postoperative antibiotics in complicated appendicitis 12.1%.

result.intervention: Local presentation, informative posters in clinical areas, local guidelines and an appendicectomy operation note proforma.

cycle2.result: Preoperative antibiotics 95%; omission in simple appendicitis 97%; 3-5 days in complicated appendicitis 61%.

result.other_findings: Three cycles; the 2023 cycle showed 87%, 100% and 20% respectively. Postoperative antibiotics in complicated appendicitis remain inconsistent.

result.topic: Periprosthetic femoral fracture epidemiology and outcomes
result.setting: 16 centres across Scotland (SNAP Femur national study)

cycle1.result: Management: fixation 53%, revision arthroplasty 30%, conservative 15%; median stay 15 days; one-year mortality 21%.

result.other_findings: Mortality predictors: interprosthetic fracture, male sex, older age and CFS 5-9; 70% did not undergo revision so registries underestimate burden.

result.topic: NELA risk prediction accuracy in emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Two UK district general hospitals (Ipswich Hospital, James Paget University Hospital)

cycle1.result: Actual 30-day mortality 9.74% vs NELA-predicted 9.8%; over-70s 13.96% vs 14.01%.

result.other_findings: No association of mortality with day of week, surgeon subspecialty, surgeon grade or procedure.

result.topic: Microbiology sampling in diabetic foot infection
result.setting: Tertiary vascular centre in the North East of England (Sunderland Royal Hospital / Freeman Hospital)
result.standard: NICE NG19 and International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot guidance on microbiological sampling

cycle1.result: 56.8% (21/37) had microbiology sent; 47.6% (10/21) before antibiotics; tissue samples 35.1% (13/37).

result.intervention: Introduction of a podiatrist-led 'Hot Foot Clinic'.

cycle2.result: 74.2% (23/31) had microbiology sent; 23.5% (4/17) of tissue samples taken before antibiotics.

result.other_findings: All 3 patients admitted via the Hot Foot Clinic had samples before antibiotics vs 6.3% (1/16) via the Emergency Admissions Suite.

result.setting: Department of Surgery, St John of God Subiaco Hospital, WA

cycle1.result: Mean MCQ score 46.4% (median 35.7%, range 28.6-85.7%); standard not met.

result.intervention: Practical multidisciplinary teaching session with scrub nurse educators demonstrating a general surgical set and draping.

cycle2.result: Mean MCQ score 80.4% (median 71.4%, range 71.4-100%); standard met (p<0.001).

result.other_findings: 81% felt the topic was overlooked; the session is now delivered biannually.

result.setting: Acute and community hospitals in England and Wales (175 trusts in England and 8 Welsh organisations); national comparative audit

cycle1.result: Possibility of dying documented in 88% of cases; 71% of Category 1 deaths had an individualised end of life care plan; median time from recognition of dying to death 41 hours; 80% of Quality Survey respondents rated care of the patient and 75% care of families as outstanding/excellent/good.

result.other_findings: One-fifth of responses said families' needs were not asked about and 20% reported lack of peace and privacy; only 36% of hospitals had face-to-face specialist palliative care 8 hours a day, 7 days a week. First round median recognition-to-death time was 36 hours.

result.setting: Six ENT departments in the North West of England

cycle1.result: 162 patients with 180 case discussions (170 morbidities, 10 mortalities); 133 had postoperative complications, most often post-tonsillectomy (62/133, 47%) and post-thyroid surgery (19/133, 14%); 66% low grade, 18% needed management under general anaesthetic.

result.intervention: Standardised ENT Quality Improvement Program data collection tool adopted into daily practice at all sites
result.other_findings: Action plans led to four policy reviews and three new policies; all sites found the tool user-friendly and continued using it.

result.topic: IV iron prescribing for iron deficiency anaemia
result.setting: Elderly care wards, Nottingham University Hospitals

cycle1.result: 8 of 81 female patients given IV iron despite not being anaemic; ferritin, TSAT, iron and transferrin not checked in 7.5%; ferritin not checked in 16%; 82% had no documented rationale for not proceeding to invasive investigation.

result.intervention: Proforma being written to guide IV iron prescribing, investigation and follow up (planned)
result.other_findings: 30% of patients were on anticoagulation and 27% on an antiplatelet, highlighting the need for medication review.

result.topic: Flexible cystoscopy appropriateness for recurrent UTI and LUTS
result.setting: Outpatient cystoscopy clinic, Northampton General Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: European Urological Association guidelines on indications for flexible cystoscopy

cycle1.result: Of 240 flexible cystoscopies, 58 (24.1%) were for rUTI (32) or LUTS (26); only 37.9% had one or more risk factors warranting cystoscopy under the guidelines.

result.intervention: Local consensus criteria for flexible cystoscopy and a new referral pathway; departmental education suggested
result.other_findings: Over 13% of patients were under 40 years old; a substantial monthly cost saving was predicted.

result.setting: District general hospital, Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, London
result.standard: World Journal of Emergency Surgery and BMJ guidance: no postoperative antibiotics for uncomplicated appendicitis and no more than 3 to 5 days for complicated appendicitis

cycle1.result: 90.2% of uncomplicated cases received postoperative antibiotics; mean course 7.8 days in complicated and 2.9 days in uncomplicated appendicitis.

result.intervention: Findings presented at the local surgical forum and clinical governance meeting, and a poster displayed in emergency theatres

cycle2.result: 84.4% of uncomplicated cases received postoperative antibiotics; mean course 6.3 days in complicated and 2.7 days in uncomplicated appendicitis.

result.other_findings: Adherence remained poor after the intervention, especially routine antibiotics in uncomplicated cases.

result.topic: Acute frailty identification and comprehensive geriatric assessment
result.setting: 58 wards in 10 hospitals across the Wessex region

cycle1.result: Three themes: lack of frailty awareness and training outside older people's medicine, and significant variability in frailty identification and comprehensive geriatric assessment (no figures given).

result.other_findings: PDSA cycles were used to design the audit tool; sample size is number of wards.

result.setting: Major Scottish transplant centre (University of Edinburgh)

cycle1.result: Total annual transport expenditure £177,260; air transport 65.5% (£116,056); single charter flights up to £18,905; short hospital-to-airport transfers by private ambulance up to £1,951 per leg.

result.other_findings: Modelling suggested a long-range drone would break even after 10 to 12 missions and avoid lost charter deposits of about £10,000.

result.setting: Surgical Emergency Unit, Oxford University Hospitals (tertiary centre)

cycle1.result: Glasgow-Imrie severity scoring completed in 9 of 81 patients; 14 of 21 gallstone pancreatitis patients had cholecystectomy during index admission (time to surgery 6.5 days).

result.other_findings: 70 patients admitted with mean stay 5.73 days; three needed ITU and one died.

result.setting: Vascular Department, University Hospitals North Midlands
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England operation note guidelines

cycle1.result: Operation time recorded in 3%; urgency 32%; intraoperative complications 12%; extra procedures 9%; blood loss 0%; surgeon's signature 0%.

result.intervention: Results presented in a teaching session for clinicians

cycle2.result: Time 6.67%; complications 13.3%; extra procedures 23.3%; blood loss 6.67%; signature 13.3%; urgency fell to 10%.

result.other_findings: All items stayed well below standard; revision of the operation note proforma was recommended.

result.setting: Emergency diagnostic laparoscopy and appendicectomy, University Hospital of Wales and Swansea Bay University Health Board
result.standard: Legal consent standards and the Montgomery ruling

cycle1.result: Risk documentation: blood transfusion 0%, drain insertion 16.7%, adhesions 38.9%; EIDO leaflet use 11.1%; COVID risk 66.7%.

result.intervention: EIDO leaflets provided on the surgical unit and consent teaching at induction (two PDSA cycles)

cycle2.result: Blood transfusion 71.4%, drain insertion 85.7%, adhesions 76.2%; EIDO leaflet use 66.7%; COVID risk 28.6%.

result.other_findings: Intermediate cycle (n=15) had EIDO leaflet use of 80.0%; consent was by SHOs in 38% to 47%, and bleeding, infection and damage to structures stayed above 90% throughout.

result.setting: Shendi Teaching Hospital and El-Mek Nimer University Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons operation note guidelines

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: At Shendi Teaching Hospital documentation improved by 1% to 37% for most items; name of procedure, extra procedures, anticipated blood loss and antibiotic prophylaxis decreased.

result.other_findings: Compliance increased at both hospitals but remained suboptimal for most criteria.

result.setting: Raigmore Hospital, Inverness
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons operation note guidelines (18 points)

cycle1.result: Completion 47% to 77% by sub-specialty (overall 72%); 29% illegible; time of operation 0%; electronic notes 9%.

result.intervention: Electronic typed operation notes with templates, extra computers and software in elective and emergency theatres

cycle2.result: Electronic notes 34%; legibility 96%; time of operation 22%; overall completion 82%; 100% for surgeon names, mode of surgery, date, procedure, findings and closure.

result.other_findings: Time of operation, blood loss and antibiotic prophylaxis were the items most often missed.

result.setting: Orthopaedic service, Lewisham and Greenwich NHS Trust (urban district general hospital)
result.standard: BOAST guidelines for management of musculoskeletal soft tissue infections

cycle1.result: 3 of 20 referrals (15%) confirmed; all 3 received sepsis six within one hour; all had emergency surgery with mean decision-to-incision time 2 hours (range 1 to 3); intra-operative sampling in all, histology in 2/3.

result.intervention: Planned focused teaching and workshops, structured pathway reinforcement and re-audit
result.other_findings: One patient died within 72 hours; the others needed 3 and 7 returns to theatre, with mean stay 50 days.

result.topic: Bone sampling in diabetic foot surgery
result.setting: Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, London
result.standard: NICE guidelines on tissue sampling in diabetic foot surgery

cycle1.result: Clinically clean bone samples 68% (n=40); microbiology changed targeted antibiotics in 58% (n=33).

result.intervention: Departmental teaching programme, then an online operation note proforma

cycle2.result: Clinically clean bone samples 89% (n=24) (p=0.140); antibiotics changed in 95% (n=19).

result.other_findings: After teaching alone (PDSA 2, n=27) clean samples were 75% (n=12). Targeted therapy had re-infection 5% vs 12.5% and re-intervention 63% vs 47%.

result.setting: 38 UK centres, multicentre prospective national audit (ARROW)
result.standard: BSG, ICARUS and AUGIS guidelines: manometry, pH monitoring and endoscopy 100%; minimally invasive surgery 95%; readmission under 10%

cycle1.result: Manometry 332 (54%); 24-hour pH monitoring 319 (53%); endoscopy 520 (83%); laparoscopic or robotic surgery 99%; readmission 45 (7%).

result.other_findings: Only 3% were day cases; three units had readmission above 10%; under 1% had unplanned reoperation.

result.setting: Tertiary oncoplastic breast reconstruction unit (Sheffield Teaching Hospitals / Nottingham University Hospitals); breast free flap reconstruction

cycle1.result: Proforma in notes 0%; anti-emetics 32%; anti-inflammatory plus PPI 32%; day 1 trial without catheter 0%; day 2 drain documentation 26%; mean stay 5.5 days.

result.intervention: ERAS proforma covering pre-operation to day three

cycle2.result: Proforma in notes 92%; anti-emetics 100%; anti-inflammatory plus PPI 100%; day 1 trial without catheter 50%; day 2 drain documentation 100%; mean stay 3.75 days.

result.other_findings: 31 patients in total across both cycles; analgesia, laxatives and enoxaparin were prescribed in 100% before and after.

result.setting: Acute stroke unit, Galway University Hospital
result.standard: 2023 National Clinical Guidelines for Stroke (UK and Ireland): at least 3 hours of rehabilitation a day on at least 5 of 7 days

cycle1.result: None of 9 patients met the guideline; therapy 44 to 132 minutes a day; average 49.1% of recommended therapy; therapy assistants provided 59.3% of therapy.

result.intervention: Two new stroke therapy assistant posts funded before the audit
result.other_findings: Stroke assistants increased therapy time but the guideline was still not achieved.

result.topic: CT cervical spine with CT head in head injury
result.setting: Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth
result.standard: BOAST: if CT brain is needed for head injury it should include CT cervical spine

cycle1.result: Compliance 23% (2021) and 37% (2022).

result.intervention: Single request tab for CT brain and CT C-spine in the ICE imaging requesting software (May 2023)
result.other_findings: Subdural haematoma was the commonest diagnosis (55%); education for ED staff was recommended.

result.topic: Emergency care at home for older adults
result.setting: EDITH (Emergency Department in the Home) service, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 2,909 remained at home and 228 were transferred to hospital (conveyance 7.2%); 336 referred to primary care or day hospital.

result.other_findings: Mean age 82; the service was estimated to save 2,909 bed days.

result.setting: Tertiary vascular centre, London

cycle1.result: Results available 9.1 days after sampling (7.3 days after lab receipt); average transit 44 hours (71 hours for Friday surgery); one sample missing.

result.intervention: Use of the existing urgent sample pathway and raising staff awareness

cycle2.result: Average transit 33 hours (36 hours on Friday); results available 7.7 days after sampling.

result.other_findings: Further analysis needed to confirm sustained improvement.

result.setting: Emergency surgical admissions, Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Smoking status documented 83% (n=166); proforma completed 55% (n=112); among 49 smokers NRT prescribed 29%, CURE involvement 31%; 10% accepted ongoing support.

result.intervention: Structured teaching session on smoking cessation for incoming doctors (August 2022)

cycle2.result: Smoking status documented 96% (n=157); proforma completed 91% (n=148); among 47 smokers NRT 40%, CURE involvement 64%; 21% accepted ongoing support.

result.other_findings: NRT prescribing remained low despite improvement.

result.topic: Lying and standing blood pressure after falls
result.setting: Three geriatric wards, Basildon University Hospital
result.standard: National Audit of Inpatient Falls: lying and standing BP for patients over 65, using RCP technique

cycle1.result: LSBP measured in 28%; correct technique 12%; medication review 0%; lifestyle advice 0%.
