result.intervention: Formal and informal teaching, RCP guidance displayed on noticeboards and BP devices, and a postural hypotension sticker

cycle2.result: LSBP measured in 96% (p<0.00001); correct technique 37.5%; medication review 87.5%; lifestyle advice 37.5%.

result.other_findings: Correct technique and lifestyle advice remained low; patient information leaflets were produced.

result.setting: Breast clinic, West Middlesex University Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Clinical history 58% (n=69); examination findings 43% (n=52); contributing factors 36% (n=43); imaging or bloods 28% (n=34); overall adherence 45% (n=54).

result.intervention: GP education on referral guidelines, a structured referral template and educational materials
result.other_findings: Authors report substantial improvement in the second cycle but give no figures.

result.setting: Acute older person medicine ward (age over 85), Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth
result.standard: National Inpatient Falls Audit: call bell within reach; target 95% or more

cycle1.result: Call bell in reach 56%.

result.intervention: Four PDSA changes: stickers in notes, teaching for nurses, a video in a closed ward social group, and a safety huddle and handover reminder

cycle2.result: Call bell in reach 93.88% after the 4th PDSA cycle, sustained.

result.other_findings: Data were from 10 beds; reminders at huddle and handover were the most effective change, and no correlation with falls was shown.

result.setting: St James's Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: B12 supplementation guidelines after total and subtotal gastrectomy

cycle1.result: Compliance 92% (79/86) after total gastrectomy and 53.8% (21/39) after subtotal gastrectomy (p<0.001).

result.other_findings: 62.6% knew supplementation was important, 37.8% could explain why and 14.8% knew the complications of deficiency.

result.setting: Two tertiary centres, University Hospitals of Derby and Burton
result.standard: RCPath: 100% inclusion of Thy categories; Thy5 PPV 97 to 99%; 100% MDT discussion for Thy4 and Thy5

cycle1.result: Thy categories included in 100%; Thy5 malignancy rate 92.3%; MDT discussion 100% for Thy4 and Thy5, 76.4% for Thy3f and 63.6% for Thy3a.

result.other_findings: Thy5 PPV fell short of the benchmark; re-audit is planned.

result.topic: Phantom limb pain management after amputation
result.setting: Major trauma centre, Royal Preston Hospital; major limb amputations
result.standard: NICE guidance on early neuropathic pain treatment

cycle1.result: PLP assessment within 48 hours 44%; pain team referral 52%; neuropathic medication within 48 hours 42%; discharge plan documented 21%.

result.intervention: Education sessions and posters for junior ward doctors

cycle2.result: PLP assessment 33%; pain team referral 67%; neuropathic medication 37%; discharge plan 22%.

result.other_findings: Education alone did not improve assessment or prescribing; an electronic amputation order set and discharge template are planned.

result.setting: Vascular surgery department, Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital
result.standard: Norfolk and Waveney CCG referral to treatment criteria: only disease above C4 treated

cycle1.result: 71 referrals rejected and 158 should have been; of 70 seen in clinic 35 did not meet criteria; 62.9% (22) of ineligible attenders had investigations; discharge rate SpRs 13.3% vs consultants 45% (p=0.046).

result.intervention: Education of SpRs on referral criteria recommended
result.other_findings: Duplex scans ordered by SpRs were more often outside criteria than by consultants (75% vs 30.3%, p=0.003).

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis in inguinal hernia repair
result.setting: University Hospitals of North Midlands
result.standard: HerniaSurge, European and British Hernia Society and trust guidelines: no routine prophylaxis for low-risk elective open mesh or laparoscopic repair

cycle1.result: 6 of 22 high-risk patients received compliant prophylaxis; antibiotics unnecessary in 32.5%; overall compliance 27.1%.

result.intervention: Departmental presentation of findings and educational posters

cycle2.result: 90.9% of 11 high-risk patients compliant; 1 of 2 low-risk patients given unnecessary antibiotics; overall adherence 84.6%.

result.other_findings: Baseline showed both overuse and inappropriate antibiotic selection.

result.setting: Two Irish hospitals (Beaumont Hospital, Dublin)
result.standard: Local surgical antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines (indication, agent, timing and duration)

cycle1.result: Compliance with all four aspects 72/303 (23.7%); correct agent 43.5% (71/165); given post-incision 18.9% (21/111); mean duration 70.4 hours.

result.intervention: Education of surgical prescribers and anaesthetists, edited sign in/time out sheet and an antibiotic duration sticker on the drug chart

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 39.8%; correct agent 65.3% (94/144); given post-incision 10.8% (14/129); mean duration 28.2 hours.

result.other_findings: 620 records audited over one year; full compliance remained low.

result.setting: Robotic general surgery programme, James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Mean docking time 34 minutes; inguinal hernia about 28 minutes; major resections 58 minutes.

result.intervention: Phase-based docking workflow with five timed steps

cycle2.result: Mean docking time 32 minutes; inguinal hernia 20 minutes; major resections 42 minutes.

result.other_findings: Cholecystectomy docking time rose slightly, attributed to small numbers and a new surgeon.

result.setting: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit database

cycle1.result: Intra-operative mortality 1 in 400 (450/180,985).

result.other_findings: Acute mesenteric ischaemia (OR 2.97), hypotension (OR 1.56) and lactate 4 to 6 (OR 3.89) predicted on-table death.

result.setting: University Hospital Limerick (university teaching hospital)
result.standard: Irish National Audit of Stroke 2019, 6th SSNAP Annual Report and AHA 2013 indicators

cycle1.result: Thrombolysis 10%; median door to needle 60 minutes; stroke unit admission 78.5%; swallow assessment 81.1%; inpatient mortality 10.5%; thrombectomy 1.9%; median door to imaging 104 minutes; mood screening 11.5%; median stay 12 days.

result.intervention: Ongoing PDSA quality improvement with annual audit (planned)
result.other_findings: Thrombectomy, length of stay, time to imaging and mood screening were the areas for improvement.

result.topic: Ultrasound for suspected appendicitis in children
result.setting: District general hospital, Mid Cheshire Hospitals, Crewe; patients up to age 16 admitted to general surgery
result.standard: Ultrasound as the recommended first-line imaging for suspected appendicitis in children

cycle1.result: Ultrasound used in 30% of patients diagnosed with appendicitis; MRI was the index modality in 42%.

result.intervention: More ultrasound slots, access to sonographer training and a standardised ultrasound reporting format

cycle2.result: Ultrasound was the index imaging in 77%; specificity 93% (n=80), sensitivity 27% (n=11).

result.other_findings: Only 5% of reports commented on all markers of inflammation; 25% needed re-imaging.

result.setting: General surgery department, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons handover guidance

cycle1.result: Weekend handover present 82%; diagnosis 21%; imaging review 29%; IV fluid plan 21%; bloods 24%; nutrition 24%; antibiotics 30%; drug monitoring 1%; discharge planning 44%; escalation plan 0%.

result.intervention: Weekend handover sticker with education of the surgical team on its use

cycle2.result: Handover present 96% (p=0.0004); diagnosis 96%; imaging review 94%; IV fluids 84%; bloods 94%; nutrition 90%; antibiotics 90%; drug monitoring 90%; discharge planning 94%; escalation plan 87% (all p<0.00001).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Inpatient angioplasty, The Princess Alexandra Hospital, Harlow (district general hospital)
result.standard: National guidance that limb perfusion and complications are assessed; domains: pulses, wound, haemodynamic stability, perfusion, ABPI, anticoagulation decision, same day review

cycle1.result: Peripheral pulses 33%; wound site 47%; limb perfusion 40%; same day review 73%; anticoagulation decision 60%.

result.intervention: Teaching session on examination, Doppler and ABPI; internal guidelines displayed on surgical wards

cycle2.result: Peripheral pulses 100%; wound site 93%; limb perfusion 93%; same day review 86%; anticoagulation decision 71%.

result.other_findings: Haemodynamic stability and ABPI documentation were unchanged.

result.setting: Surgical assessment unit, East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: UK national average readmission rate of 5%

cycle1.result: Readmission rate 8.1%; about two-thirds on day one after discharge, half due to pain; almost 90% needed no intervention.

result.intervention: Proposed: more clinic time for consent, junior doctor and nurse education, and patient leaflets and websites
result.other_findings: This is a QI proposal aiming to cut readmissions from 8.1% to 5% within a year.

result.setting: Rehabilitation services (inpatient and community), CNTW NHS Trust
result.standard: Trust guideline on safe prescribing of clozapine: levels at baseline, annually and when clinically relevant, with reason, result and action plan documented

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Under 50% compliance for baseline and annual monitoring, reason for request and action plan; over 50% for scanned results and levels when clinically relevant.

result.other_findings: No significant improvement from the previous audit except documentation of levels; clozapine key cards to be disseminated.

result.setting: Plastic surgery outpatients, Royal Sussex County Hospital, Brighton (major trauma centre)

cycle1.result: 95% of consultant clinics over capacity; 54 forced bookings.

result.intervention: Virtual specialist nurse-led clinic replacing suitable face-to-face follow-ups

cycle2.result: 71.8% of consultant clinics over capacity (p=0.002); 10 forced bookings (p=0.006); new patients seen per month up 15.3% (p=0.019).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Medical wards, University Hospital Kerry (acute hospital)
result.standard: Polypharmacy (five or more medications) recorded as an admission diagnosis in patients aged 70 or over

cycle1.result: 0 of 32 patients had polypharmacy in the admission diagnoses.

result.intervention: Suggested use of a prescribing screening tool in the emergency department
result.other_findings: Commonest admission diagnoses were hyponatraemia, acute kidney injury and confusion.

result.setting: Jean Bishop Integrated Care Centre, Hull (community)
result.standard: Published ReSPECT data (NHS Forth Valley report: 39% completion, 79% uploaded)

cycle1.result: Of 71 without a form, 57 had discussions (80%) and 29 forms were completed (41%); 24/29 (82%) uploaded.

result.intervention: Posters of results in clinic rooms and feedback to key team members

cycle2.result: 13 (94%) had ReSPECT discussions and 6 forms completed; 81% had a form or discussion.

result.other_findings: Regular training and spot checks recommended for sustainability.

result.topic: Nutritional screening and weight loss in older inpatients
result.setting: Department of Medicine for Older People and Stroke ward, Liverpool University Hospitals

cycle1.result: 70% lost weight during admission; 48% had weekly MUST assessments.

result.intervention: MUST Mondays (weekly weighing and MUST) and A3 laminated food preference menus at the bedside

cycle2.result: 55% lost weight during admission; 80% had weekly MUST assessments.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Regular medication prescribing while nil by mouth
result.setting: District general hospital, London; adult general surgical inpatients
result.standard: National guidance to continue most regular medications while nil by mouth

cycle1.result: Regular medications prescribed while NBM on day of surgery 13.7%; emergency patients 15.0% (n=20); omission 4 or more days 19.6%.

result.intervention: Graphical reminders in clinical workspaces and a departmental presentation

cycle2.result: Prescribed 28.6% (p=0.12); emergency patients 43.5% (n=23, p=0.054); omission 4 or more days 11.9% (p=0.40).

result.other_findings: Failure to prescribe was the commonest reason for omission in both cycles; electronic prescribing prompts are planned.

result.setting: Tertiary breast unit, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: NHSBSP guidance: previously five-year annual mammography for B3 lesions with atypia after excision; new guidance returns to routine screening

cycle1.result: 64% (36/56) referred for five-year annual mammograms; concordance with previous guidance 86% (48/56); 57% (32/56) would not need surveillance under new guidance.

result.other_findings: Estimated mammographic cost saving of £288 per patient under the new guidance.

result.setting: UK national trauma and orthopaedic trainee-led collaborative projects

cycle1.result: 10 trainee-led collaborative projects since the pandemic vs 0 in 2019; 6 published; 5 audits and 5 cohort studies.

result.other_findings: Projects included 927 to 140,231 patients from 2249 centres in total.

result.setting: Whittington Hospital NHS Trust (district general hospital)
result.standard: GIRFT operation documentation guidance for common general surgical procedures

cycle1.result: Overall compliance: open inguinal hernia 36%, laparoscopic cholecystectomy 44%, laparoscopic inguinal hernia 45%, bowel resection 54%, laparoscopic appendicectomy 56%; critical view of safety documented in 28%.

result.intervention: Planned standardised pre-populated electronic operation notes with re-audit
result.other_findings: Ilioinguinal nerve handling documented in 35% and vas/testicular vessels in 50% of open hernia repairs.

result.topic: Abscess packing after incision and drainage
result.setting: General surgery department, Barnet Hospital, Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Consensus guidelines: intra-operative packing for haemostasis; insufficient evidence for regular post-operative packing

cycle1.result: Intra-operative packing 100%; regular packing after discharge recommended in 89%.

result.intervention: Results discussed with the department, recommending post-discharge packing only when necessary

cycle2.result: Intra-operative packing reduced by 10% and post-operative packing by 43%.

result.other_findings: Estimated carbon emissions 16% lower without regular post-operative packing (57 vs 68 kgCO2e).

result.topic: Frailty assessment in emergency surgical admissions
result.setting: Surgical Assessment Unit, Bedford Hospital
result.standard: NELA recommendation for early frailty screening

cycle1.result: No patients aged 65 or over had a frailty score documented and none received geriatric input.

result.intervention: Frailty liaison service with twice-weekly geriatric ward rounds

cycle2.result: CFS documented in 88% (103/117); 43% (44/103) frail; only 18% (8/44) of frail patients received geriatric input.

result.other_findings: Delayed referral limited geriatric input; a mandatory electronic referral system is recommended.

result.setting: Southport and Formby District General Hospital

cycle1.result: Imaging within timeframe 60%; surgical review within timeframe 38.2%; antibiotics within 1 hour for septic patients 80%; NELA score documented 5.5%.

cycle2.result: Imaging 78% (p=0.03); surgical review 91% (p<0.01); antibiotics within 1 hour 50% (p=0.33); NELA score 1% (p=0.15).

result.other_findings: Antibiotic timing and NELA score documentation worsened.

result.topic: Consultant review time in emergency surgery
result.setting: Emergency general surgical take, single centre (Imperial College / North West London NHS Trust)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England timeframes for consultant review

cycle1.result: 70% reviewed within recommended time; 10% missing documentation; 20% seen 1 to 2 hours outside the window.

result.intervention: Educational sessions and email reminders on documentation

cycle2.result: 80% reviewed within recommended time; 5% missing documentation.

result.other_findings: No worse outcomes were seen in patients reviewed outside the timeframe.

result.setting: Stroke unit, Beaumont Hospital, Dublin (tertiary referral hospital)

cycle1.result: DAPT duration documented in discharge letters of 28/34 (82%); 5 of these were still inappropriately on DAPT at follow up; 19 of 22 co-prescribed PPI had no documented PPI plan.

result.intervention: Results presented at stroke unit teaching; NCHD education and EMR changes recommended
result.other_findings: 12 of 19 patients without a PPI plan were still on PPI at follow up; 100 records were screened.

result.topic: Best medical therapy in carotid stenosis
result.setting: Outpatient stroke clinic, Beaumont Hospital tertiary stroke centre, Dublin
result.standard: European Stroke Organisation guidelines for best medical therapy; LDL-C target below 1.8

cycle1.result: 89% on best medical therapy; 56% achieved LDL-C below 1.8; smoking status documented in 66% (n=18).

result.other_findings: 81% of symptomatic patients had stable stenosis; 50% of asymptomatic patients progressed.

result.setting: Meridian Ward, old age psychiatric inpatient ward, Hammersmith and Fulham Mental Health Unit

cycle1.result: 50% fully vaccinated, 20% one dose, 30% unvaccinated; 20% of unvaccinated received a first dose during admission.

result.other_findings: Recommends recording vaccination status on admission and in the summary care record.

result.setting: Surgical wards, Oxford University Hospitals
result.standard: Trust and departmental ward round documentation criteria and VTE guidelines

cycle1.result: No ward round entry on 8% of inpatient days; essential criteria documented 32%; VTE compliance 70%; two prescribing near misses.

result.intervention: Concise ward-round template, promoted by poster to junior doctors and presented at clinical governance

cycle2.result: Ward round entry on all inpatient days, 96% using template; essential criteria 93% (p<0.05); VTE compliance 98% (p<0.05); no prescribing errors.

result.other_findings: Template use remained high several months after implementation.

result.setting: Major trauma centre, Royal Stoke University Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England Good Surgical Practice (18 parameters)

cycle1.result: 100% for date, surgeon, assistant, procedure, diagnosis and signature; prosthesis 0%; blood loss 1%; extra procedures 1%; elective/emergency 1%; time 4%; complications 19.8%.

result.intervention: Template proforma for post-operative instructions recommended
result.other_findings: Over 1 in 3 notes lacked detailed post-op instructions; 19.7% omitted DVT prophylaxis and 20% clip or suture removal.

result.topic: Substance use screening in liaison psychiatry
result.setting: Ealing Liaison Psychiatry Service
result.standard: NICE: all patients asked about substance use

cycle1.result: 69% asked about substance use; over 80s 0%; females 55% vs males 81% asked about illicit substances; ward referrals 33.3% vs ED 74.2%.

result.intervention: Training session on the audit results and NICE recommendations

cycle2.result: 93% asked about substance use; over 80s 60%; females 96%; ward referrals 85%.

result.other_findings: Of those asked, 50% to 65.2% were using a substance, most often alcohol.

result.setting: Royal Oldham Hospital; samples from patients across Manchester
result.standard: Pro-Implant and BOA guidelines on PJI diagnosis and antibiotics

cycle1.result: 100% compliance with microbiology discussion, sample labelling and CRP; poor compliance with guideline diagnosis, sending more than 5 samples and discharge antibiotic plans; no sonication, PCR or histology used.

result.intervention: Recommended intraoperative PJI proforma, dedicated MDT, joint microbiology clinic and funding for PCR, sonication and histology
result.other_findings: 68 PJI samples from 17 patients; intervals between two-stage exchange stages often not met.

result.topic: Perioperative iron deficiency anaemia in hip fracture
result.setting: Geriatric hip and femur fracture inpatients, University Hospitals Bristol and Weston (tertiary hospital)
result.standard: Centre for Perioperative Care perioperative anaemia guideline

cycle1.result: Full iron studies in 25.8% of anaemic patients; IV iron given to 62.5% of patients with iron deficiency anaemia.

result.intervention: Cluster 1: local guideline and ward stock of parenteral iron; cluster 2: Silver Trauma team, wider guideline communication and two teaching sessions
result.other_findings: After cluster 1 alone, full iron studies were 57.9% and IV iron 73.3%.

result.setting: Sunderland Royal Hospital, South Tyneside and Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Vascular Society of Great Britain and Ireland and NCEPOD standards

cycle1.result: 100% consultant review within 24 h, antibiotic and VTE prophylaxis and physiotherapy input; 67% amputated within 48 h of decision; 45% of diabetic patients had diabetes team input; below-knee to above-knee ratio 2:1.

result.intervention: Recommended blanket diabetes referral or weekly MDT ward rounds and more physiotherapy input
result.other_findings: Stump complications 20%, 30-day mortality 2.2%, mean stay 34 days with nearly half staying over 30 days.

result.setting: Wellington Regional Hospital; inpatients with pneumonia, heart failure, asthma or COPD
result.standard: Documented target SpO2 range and SpO2 kept within it

cycle1.result: Target SpO2 range documented in 62 of 100; mean (SD) proportion of SpO2 measurements within range 56.2 (30.6)%.

result.other_findings: A hypercapnic target range was associated with SpO2 above range (OR 5.34).

result.setting: Ealing Hospital, surgical admissions
result.standard: British Consensus Guidelines on Intravenous Fluid Therapy for Adult Surgical Patients (GIFTASUP)

cycle1.result: Resuscitation (n=59): 43% received optimal fluid resuscitation, 36% received no fluids, 34% prescribed non-optimal fluid types. Maintenance (n=53): 74% prescribed fluids, 66% met daily sodium requirements, 47% met free fluid requirements.

result.intervention: Targeted educational interventions for junior doctors.

cycle2.result: Resuscitation (n=53): optimal fluid resuscitation 83%, non-optimal prescriptions 17%, fluid prescription rate 64% to 94%. Maintenance (n=24): prescription rate 91.7%, sodium requirements 91.7%, free fluid targets 75%.

result.other_findings: Use of appropriate fluid types improved only from 36% to 45.5%.

result.setting: Single centre, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, London

cycle1.result: CT correctly identified 4 of 13 complicated and 16 of 18 uncomplicated appendicitis cases; for complicated appendicitis sensitivity 31%, specificity 100%, PPV 100%, NPV 69%, false-negative rate 69%.

result.other_findings: Two patients labelled uncomplicated appendicitis on CT had no appendicitis at surgery, and two with a normal appendix on CT had uncomplicated appendicitis intraoperatively.

result.setting: General medical ward, Sligo University Hospital (level 3 hospital)
result.standard: Clinical guidelines recommending routine delirium screening of patients aged 65 and over

cycle1.result: 1 (2.7%) patient had a 4AT documented; of 5 patients with 4AT ≥4, 2 (40%) flagged by the CNM and 1 (20%) by the medical team.

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary education and awareness programme on delirium, standardised delirium screening with recognised tools, and a new delirium management tool placed in medical notes.

cycle2.result: 64% (25) had a 4AT or SQUID documented; of 3 patients with 4AT ≥4, 2 (67%) flagged by the CNM and 3 (100%) by the medical team; 66.67% documented as delirious in medical notes.

result.other_findings: Weekly prospective chart reviews over one month in patients aged 65 and over; mean age 81.

result.setting: Tertiary metabolic bone service, Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust, London
result.standard: British Society for Rheumatology guidance (September 2021) on appropriate referrals to adult rheumatology

cycle1.result: 45/50 (90%) referrals were within the new BSR guidance.

result.other_findings: Referrals outside guidance were for bone density deterioration without fracture and family history of osteoporosis; 48% of patients were advised to start parenteral bone protection. A re-audit for 6 months after the guidance is planned.

result.setting: London university teaching hospital (Croydon University Hospital), emergency surgical admissions
result.standard: ACPGBI guidelines: incision and drainage within 24 hours; antibiotics not indicated in routine uncomplicated perianal abscess

cycle1.result: 15/36 received empirical post-operative antibiotics, with no clear indication in 60% of those; 86% had surgical drainage within 24 hours.

result.other_findings: Most common agent was co-amoxiclav (53%), then co-amoxiclav with metronidazole (33%); one patient readmitted for second drainage at 3 months.

result.setting: Acute tertiary hospital, Sir Salimullah Medical College and Hospital
result.standard: BSG risk stratification guidance for lower gastrointestinal bleeding (Shock Index and Oakland score)

cycle1.result: Shock Index calculated in 27% (18/66), Oakland score in 36% (24/66); admission rate 53% (35/66); 44% (15/35) of admitted patients had Oakland scores consistent with safe discharge.

cycle2.result: Shock Index 82% (47/57), Oakland score 79% (45/57); admission rate 38% (22/57); 18% (4/22) of admitted patients had Oakland scores consistent with safe discharge.

result.other_findings: Reduced avoidable admissions with reported cost savings.

result.setting: Stroke service, level III acute hospital (Tipperary University Hospital)
result.standard: Published evidence of AF burden around 30% in acute ischaemic stroke

cycle1.result: 41% (N=65) had AF deemed the cause of stroke: 18% (N=29) newly diagnosed and 23% (N=36) known AF. Of known AF, 13.8% (N=5) not anticoagulated, 58.3% (N=21) on adjusted dose, 27.7% (N=10) not fully compliant.

result.other_findings: All patients screened with 72-hour R-testing; all new and existing AF patients not anticoagulated were started on anticoagulation.

result.setting: General surgical patients, busy teaching hospital (Doncaster and Bassetlaw Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: NICE NG148 and local guidance: urine dipstick in all, renal ultrasound within 24 hours unless clear cause, documented medication and fluid balance review, follow-up plan after discharge

cycle1.result: Documented AKI review 59.1%, medication review 18%, blood gas 4.5%, urine dip interpretation 18.5%, AKI mentioned on discharge 8.7%, fluid balance 40.9%.

cycle2.result: Documented AKI review 42.3%, medication review 40.7%, blood gas 15.3%, urine dip interpretation 15.3%, AKI mentioned on discharge 26.9%, fluid balance 38.4%.

result.other_findings: Compliance remained suboptimal; an updated AKI pathway is being implemented.

result.setting: Gwent Specialist Substance Misuse Service, inpatient alcohol detoxes, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board
result.standard: Local aim: increase discharge summary completion from 57.7% to 80% by June 2019

cycle1.result: Discharge summary completion rate 57.7%.

result.intervention: PDSA cycle with process mapping, root cause analysis by brainstorming, education, communication and a checklist.

cycle2.result: Compliance rose to 100% before tapering off to 85% by the end of the project.

result.other_findings: Continuous monitoring, team engagement and regular feedback were noted as important for sustaining improvement.

result.topic: Bone health assessment in older inpatients
result.setting: Medical wards, Department of General Internal Medicine, Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth
result.standard: NICE guidelines on bone health assessment in women aged 65 and over and men aged 75 and over; NOGG 2021 for treatment

cycle1.result: 29 out of 45 patients had bone health assessment done.

result.intervention: Teaching session after each audit to raise awareness of bone health assessment; at-risk patients assessed with FRAX and treated per NOGG 2021.

cycle2.result: 41 patients had assessment done, an improvement of 26%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Elective colorectal cancer surgery, Royal Derby Hospital
result.standard: NICE recommendation to screen for and treat anaemia; local guideline advocating pre-operative IV iron via day-case unit

cycle1.result: 27.5% (11/40) anaemic; 18% (2/11) received pre-operative iron infusion; 45% (5/11) of anaemic patients had post-operative transfusion.

result.intervention: Departmental education on anaemia management and further publicity of the day-case iron infusion pathway.

cycle2.result: 45.4% (20/44) anaemic; 60% (12/20) received iron infusion; 20% (4/20) of anaemic patients required post-operative transfusion.

result.other_findings: None of the cycle 1 transfused patients had pre-operative IV iron, and 3 of 4 transfused in cycle 2 had not received it.

result.setting: Large general practice (Thorndike Medical Centre, Rochester)
result.standard: National immunisation and antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines for post-splenectomy patients

cycle1.result: Three patients had outstanding pneumococcal vaccine in the past five years; 100% compliance with annual influenza vaccine; two patients on incorrect antibiotic prophylaxis and four without antibiotic prophylaxis.

result.other_findings: All patients had at least two COVID vaccinations; the audit led to recall for outstanding pneumococcal vaccination and review of antibiotic prophylaxis.

result.setting: Major trauma centre, Addenbrooke's, Cambridge University Hospitals
result.standard: NICE guidelines on neurovascular assessment and documentation; poor compliance defined as <75%

cycle1.result: Basic mention of neurovascular status 911/959 (95%); gross sensation 492/959 (51%); named nerve assessment 143/959 (15%); MRC motor assessment 71/959 (7%); pulse assessment with pulses documented 367/959 (38%).

result.other_findings: 885 patients with tibial or femoral fractures (959 fractures); a pre-written neurovascular documentation template is recommended.

result.setting: Plastic surgery theatres, Mid Yorkshire Teaching NHS Trust (Pinderfields Hospital)
result.standard: BOAST tourniquet standards and trust six-use-day tourniquet infection control policy

cycle1.result: Operation notes documented duration in 90.3%, type in 67.7%, pressure in 39.5%; skin integrity, isolation and exsanguination not recorded in any notes; fixed 250 mmHg used in 95.3%, exceeding BOAST standards in 53.5%; all within 120-minute limit.

result.intervention: Teaching session and poster reminders introduced; re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: Electronic peri-operative pathway had 100% compliance, paper pathways 88.7–97.7%; tourniquets were not marked per trust policy but were disposed of after each list.

result.setting: District general hospital (Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust)
result.standard: Guideline-recommended cholecystectomy within 10 days for acute cholecystitis and gallstone pancreatitis

cycle1.result: Of 73 patients fit for surgery, only 11% underwent cholecystectomy within 10 days.

result.other_findings: 13 of 28 (46%) awaiting elective surgery beyond 10 days were readmitted; emergency surgery had about 75% drain usage and mean length of stay 3 days.

result.setting: Geriatric service, St Vincent's University Hospital (Caritas), Dublin
result.standard: NICE 2013 falls guideline (formal vision assessment for all) and BGS/RCP bedside vision assessment tool

cycle1.result: 11 (69%) not asked about vision; of 5 asked, only 2 had documented visual field assessment; none had all RCP-recommended checks.

result.intervention: Planned: basic visual assessment tools (e.g. Snellen chart), updated falls proforma and staff education before re-audit.
result.other_findings: 7 (44.7%) had visual problems or conditions affecting vision.

result.setting: Older emergency laparotomy patients on NELA database, Leeds Teaching Hospitals Trust
result.standard: NICE 2017: MUST on admission, with high-risk score triggering a response

cycle1.result: 99.3% had MUST recorded on admission; of 114 high MUST patients, 35% had no dietetic review and 24% received neither oral nor parenteral supplementation.

result.other_findings: 30-day mortality 13.9%; a supplementation protocol before dietetic review and prescriber education are recommended.

result.topic: LUTS care after negative prostate cancer referral
result.setting: District general hospital urology outpatient service (Barts Health NHS Trust)
result.standard: NICE CG97 and EAU 2024: LUTS assessment at 2WW appointment and lifestyle counselling, follow-up or LUTS pathway activation

cycle1.result: LUTS assessment documented in 203/268 (76%); of 143 with LUTS, 54 (38%) had LUTS pathway activated, 4 (3%) lifestyle advice; 84 (59% of those with LUTS) had no documented advice, pathway or follow-up.

result.other_findings: Routine LUTS evaluation and automatic pathway referral are recommended.

result.setting: Acute surgical wards, Hull University Teaching Hospitals
result.standard: National guidance on early frailty assessment, recognition of high-risk patients and specialist geriatric involvement

cycle1.result: 29 (34.9%) frail (CFS ≥5); frailty documented in all cases; none referred to or reviewed by the frailty team; DNACPR undocumented in 24.1% of frail patients.

result.other_findings: Frail patients had mean length of stay 24.7 days, 30-day readmission 24.1% and mortality 17.2%; a structured frailty pathway is planned.

result.setting: Tertiary stroke unit, Beaumont Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: 2021 Irish National Audit of Stroke key performance metrics

cycle1.result: Thrombolysis rate 18% with 75% receiving tPA within 1 hour of arrival (INAS 10% and 56%); median door-to-image 24 mins and door-to-needle 42 mins (INAS 63 and 43 mins).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Department of General Surgery, St Richard's Hospital, University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE: imaging within 24 hours of admission for suspected complicated acute diverticulitis

cycle1.result: Previous audit cycle imaging rate 94.3%.

cycle2.result: 76/83 (91.6%) had contrast CT within 24 hours of admission.

result.other_findings: Of 7 not imaged within 24 hours, 3 had recent imaging, 2 were treated with antibiotics, 1 refused and 1 was delayed by dialysis; educational sessions planned.

result.topic: NELA data entry and risk documentation
result.setting: Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother Hospital, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Emergency Laparotomy Best Practice Tariff 2023–2025: ≥85% formal mortality risk assessment documented on NELA

cycle1.result: Only 11.7% (n=7) documented on NELA.

result.intervention: Presentations at surgical and anaesthetic clinical governance meetings, surveys, NELA log-in details at trainee induction, and a QR code on the CEPOD booking form.

cycle2.result: 86.2% (n=50) using the NELA tool, achieving the ≥85% target.

result.other_findings: Two PDSA cycles over one year; future plans involve the POPS team and IT department.

result.setting: Single centre, lower-limb operation notes (trauma and elective), Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: BOAST guidance on weight-bearing terminology and documentation; target 80% compliance

cycle1.result: 6% compliance (non-weightbearing cases only); no rationale given for limited or non-weightbearing status; functional and duration limitations given in 60% and 86% respectively.

result.intervention: After consultation with physiotherapists: theatre posters, template training and reminder messages via WhatsApp groups for surgeons.
result.other_findings: Significant variability in terminology; rapid-cycle re-audits are under way.

result.topic: Perioperative care of older emergency surgical patients
result.setting: District general hospital trauma and emergency theatres, Kingston Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Anaesthetists standards for perioperative care of older patients

cycle1.result: Trauma: pre-operative delirium screen 93%, post-operative 77%, geriatrician input 93%. Emergency theatres: 15%, 0% and 15% respectively. Time with systolic BP <100 mmHg 25% (emergency) vs 12% (trauma).

result.intervention: Proposed care bundle for emergency theatres: geriatrician access, anaesthetic chart prompts for BP targets and pEEG, modified WHO checklist.
result.other_findings: MAC >1 for 21% of operative time in emergency theatres (10% with pEEG) and 41% in trauma theatres (62% with pEEG).

result.setting: Department of General Surgery, Warwick Hospital, laparoscopic appendicectomy
result.standard: RCS England Good Surgical Practice 2014 (18 parameters)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Compliance increased significantly in 9 of 18 parameters, 6 unchanged at almost 100%; post-op antibiotic instructions 83%, DVT prophylaxis 53%.

result.other_findings: Gynaecological findings in females recorded in only 13%; legibility improved.

result.setting: Chesterfield Royal Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BMJ Best Practice guidance on post-operative antibiotics after appendicectomy (total duration 5 days)

cycle1.result: 52/67 (77.6%) uncomplicated cases received post-operative antibiotics; where op note said no further antibiotics this was followed in 14/29 (48%); compliance with specified duration or route 27.78%; 47 complicated cases received ~3 days IV then 5 days oral.

result.intervention: Recommendations implemented and targeted teaching sessions for junior doctors; second cycle planned.
result.other_findings: 25 uncomplicated patients were discharged with more than 5 days of oral antibiotics.

result.setting: Tertiary care teaching hospital, University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust, Brighton
result.standard: NICE: cholecystectomy during index admission or within two weeks of discharge for non-severe gallstone pancreatitis

cycle1.result: Of 30 mild or moderate cases, 2 (6.6%) had cholecystectomy during index admission; of 14 (45%) with elective surgery within five months, 2 (14%) were within two weeks.

result.intervention: Planned dedicated hot cholecystectomy pathway with protected theatre capacity and re-audit.
result.other_findings: Delays due to uncertain fitness (4), awaiting MRCP (6) and awaiting ERCP (3); 3 (10.7%) readmitted with recurrent biliary pathology.

result.topic: Bone health assessment in care homes
result.setting: Enhanced Health in Care Homes team, five residential homes, Whittington Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Before CGA, 37% of residents with high or very high FRAX score were on appropriate bone protection.

result.intervention: Comprehensive geriatric assessment with FRAX and management plan by the new EHCH team.

cycle2.result: After EHCH CGA, 85% on appropriate bone protection; 100% (183) had bone health assessment including FRAX.

result.other_findings: Largest improvement in one home was from 0% to 83%.

result.setting: NHS Forth Valley substance misuse service

cycle1.result: 61% of keyworkers were notified of the NFO; only 21% had a timely review by a doctor (within 1 month).

result.other_findings: 86% were prescribed methadone (mean 57 mg, 54% >60 mg/day); 14% of NFOs occurred in the titration phase.

result.setting: Single tertiary centre, Addenbrooke's, Cambridge University Hospitals

cycle1.result: Mortality 64.7%; 41.1% had an advance care plan or DNACPR on admission; 88.2% received palliative care or geriatric input after decision for conservative management.

result.other_findings: Median age 87, median CFS 8, mean NELA-predicted mortality 51.8%.

result.setting: Emergency general surgery, Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Trust
result.standard: Guidance recommending selective pus swabbing for recurrent, persistent or treatment-resistant abscesses

cycle1.result: Pus swabs taken in 76/122 (62.3%), with results acted on in only 5/76 (6.6%).

result.other_findings: 30-day recurrence 3.9% swabbed vs 4.3% non-swabbed; discharge on antibiotics associated with recurrence (aOR 13.76, P = 0.004).

result.setting: Southport Hospital (MWL Teaching Hospitals), Year 5 medical student teaching

cycle1.result: Previous cycle: confidence responding to NEWS rose 62.2%, taking histories 7.09%, examining a patient 25.3%.

result.intervention: Compound questionnaire added to assess confidence and formatively test knowledge before and after each session.

cycle2.result: Confidence responding to NEWS rose 87%, using ABCDE 51%, escalating concerns 38%, emergency treatments 86%; formative scores rose from 61% to 72%.

result.other_findings: Students underperformed mainly on septic screening questions.

result.setting: Stroke service, Mayo University Hospital, Castlebar
result.standard: RCP Stroke Guidelines 2016 and National Guideline for Swallow Screening in Stroke (2017): swallow screen within 4 hours of admission

cycle1.result: 38 (48.1%) had a documented swallow screen during admission, 27 (34.2%) did not, 14 (17.7%) unclear; 5 of 38 (13.2%) within 4 hours.

result.intervention: Planned education and training programme for stroke unit nurses and doctors, with re-audit in 6–12 months.
result.other_findings: Over 90% of stroke patients were admitted to the stroke unit.

result.setting: Ealing Hospital, elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy

cycle1.result: 64 (90.1%) booked as day cases, with day-case success rate 74.4%.

result.other_findings: Success lower with age 60–79 (55.6%) and over 80 (33.3%) and with operations over 120 minutes; only 37% of failures were anticipated preoperatively.

result.setting: District general hospital, Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust, laparoscopic cholecystectomy
result.standard: NHS England GIRFT recommendations for operation notes

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Surgeon education and modified laparoscopic cholecystectomy-specific operation note proforma.

cycle2.result: Documentation of Calot's triangle dissection, bile or gallstone spill management and extraction port increased by 13%, 42% and 48% respectively.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Two teaching hospitals: Guy's and St Thomas' (London) and National Hospital of Sri Lanka (Colombo), inpatients and podiatry outpatients

cycle1.result: GVG-compliant foot examination in inpatients: GSTT 10 (26%), NHSL 0 (0%); outpatients: GSTT 21/21, NHSL 0/28; limb severity scoring in all GSTT outpatients vs 5/28 (18%) at NHSL.

result.other_findings: 49 outpatients also included (GSTT 21, NHSL 28).

result.topic: PICC line timing for IV antibiotics
result.setting: Orthopaedic department, NHS Lothian, Edinburgh; patients with bone, joint or soft tissue infection

cycle1.result: 30 PICCs requested, 26 inserted; mean diagnosis to request 8.7 days (1–33), request to insertion 6.7 days (1–15), diagnosis to insertion 15.9 days (4–39); 10 of 30 (33.3%) missed antibiotics due to lack of IV access.

result.intervention: Department policy and induction programme updated, with education.

cycle2.result: 36 PICCs requested, 18 inserted; mean diagnosis to request 4.4 days (1–15), request to insertion 4.2 days (1–8), diagnosis to insertion 8.6 days (1–21); missed IV antibiotics reduced from 33.3% to 15.4%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Emergency general surgery, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Time to surgery 3 to 116 hours (mean/median 18 hours); 50.6% operated within 18 hours of ED arrival and 75% within 18 hours of diagnostic decision.

result.other_findings: Perforation 16% on imaging and 28% intra-operatively; 15% had no imaging; longer delays were linked to higher perforation and postoperative intervention.

result.setting: One-stop breast clinic, Whipps Cross Hospital (Barts Health NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: Non-lump presentations 19.4% (n=19); symptom documentation 100%; palpation score recorded in 73.7% (n=14) of non-lump cases; clinical examination sensitivity 64.3% in this subgroup.

result.other_findings: 2,611 patients attended; 17.3% of cancers were screen-detected and 61.2% presented with a lump.

result.setting: ENT service, Oxford University Hospitals
result.standard: ENT UK standard: manipulation within 21 days

cycle1.result: Telemedicine-first pathway: mean time to face-to-face review 16.5 days; mean time to MUA 15.2 days; MUA within 14 days 38.9%; 1.23 consultations per patient.

result.intervention: Change from a telemedicine-first to a face-to-face-first pathway.

cycle2.result: Mean time to face-to-face review 13.3 days (p=0.0068); mean time to MUA 13.9 days (p=0.19) with 100% within 21 days; MUA within 14 days 57.1%; 1.04 consultations per patient.

result.other_findings: Discharge from ENT earlier (15.2 to 12.2 days, p=0.0019); MUA patients were younger (mean 31.3 vs 41.7 years).

result.setting: Regional tertiary cardiac surgery centre, Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast
result.standard: EACTS 2017 guidelines: beta-blockers (bisoprolol, metoprolol, carvedilol or nebivolol) on discharge after CABG in low LVEF

cycle1.result: 90 (89%) discharged with beta-blockers; 83 (81%) with a recommended beta-blocker; 11 (11%) not discharged on beta-blockers.

result.intervention: Departmental presentation and raising awareness; discharge checklist inclusion recommended.
result.other_findings: Second cycle data were being analysed at time of abstract.

result.topic: Sentinel lymph node biopsy service for melanoma
result.setting: Northern Ireland Regional Plastic Surgery Unit, Ulster Hospital
result.standard: Predetermined performance indicators (not specified); interim COVID-19 criteria of SLNB for pT3a or greater

cycle1.result: 94.4% complete datasets; 141 eligible patients had SLNB (18.4% positive, 75.9% negative, 5.7% failed); 7.9% unsuitable and 4.5% declined.

result.other_findings: 168 patients did not meet interim criteria and had wide local excision alone.

result.setting: Five UK transplant centres (NTACT audit)

cycle1.result: Preoperative antibiotics universal; consultant surgeons led all operations but 62.5% directed by consultant anaesthetists; 42% advanced haemodynamic monitoring; 75% to ICU.

result.other_findings: 30-day mortality 0%; primary graft function 83% kidney and 92% pancreas; readmission 29% and re-operation 33%.

result.setting: North West Regional Urology Audit Group, regional audit across North West England
result.standard: 42 agreed regional guidelines for prostate, testis, bladder and kidney cancer care

cycle1.result: Overall adherence to guidelines 63.4% in the original audits.

result.intervention: Regional audit process with annual repeat audits.

cycle2.result: Overall adherence 73.4% (p < 0.05); preoperative investigation +13% and planning, counselling, follow-up and documentation +12% (p < 0.05).

result.other_findings: Intraoperative care guidelines rose by only 0.1% (p = 0.95); 3659 case notes gave 20,470 observations across four complete cycles.

result.setting: Neurosurgical ward, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee

cycle1.result: 88% of electronic discharge documents inadequate in quality; 22% adequate.

result.intervention: Copy-paste template, educational poster and presentation, developed with the MDT.

cycle2.result: Adequate EDDs doubled from 22% to 43%; inadequate reduced by 33%.

result.other_findings: Neurological status on admission and discharge was the most often missed item; follow-up and new medications were also often omitted.

result.setting: TARN national registry, England, Wales and Ireland

cycle1.result: Operative management 84%; CT imaging 77%; 30-day mortality 9.1% and 24-hour mortality 5.3%.

result.other_findings: 30-day mortality fell from 11.4% in 2013 to 7.3% in 2021 while annual case volume rose from 249 to 510.

result.setting: General surgery department, Broomfield Hospital, Essex, laparoscopic appendicectomy
result.standard: GIRFT/RCS/ASGBI Best practice for Laparoscopic Appendicectomy Documentation (September 2022), 44 recommendations

cycle1.result: Average adherence to the guideline 35%.

result.intervention: Electronic operation note template designed in Microsoft Word with stakeholder feedback, rolled out November 2022.

cycle2.result: Average adherence 55% overall, and 89% in notes using the template.

result.other_findings: Surgeons reported the template was easy to use and quicker than typing on a blank document.

result.setting: Emergency surgery, Musgrove Park Hospital
result.standard: National guidance: routine peri-operative paracetamol and post-operative NSAIDs

cycle1.result: 89% received paracetamol peri-operatively (83% regular); less than half at maximum frequency; 34 avoidable IV paracetamol administrations; only 28% without contraindications prescribed post-operative NSAIDs (15% regular).

result.other_findings: 83% of paracetamol prescriptions were IV/oral without oral preference.

result.topic: Emergency laparotomy risk assessment and documentation
result.setting: Ealing Hospital, emergency laparotomy patients
result.standard: NELA standards for preoperative risk assessment, risk communication and multidisciplinary input

cycle1.result: NELA score calculated preoperatively in 94.7%; mortality risk discussion documented on 17.86% of consent forms; elderly care involvement in 12.5% of patients aged ≥60; critical care input in 66.07%.

result.other_findings: NELA score sensitivity 33.33% and specificity 84.31% for mortality at a 10% threshold; overall mortality 5.26%.

result.setting: Large UK district general hospital, West Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: International Association of Pancreatology guidance on initial severity assessment (Modified Atlanta Classification)

cycle1.result: None had a formal severity assessment recorded.

result.intervention: Pancreatitis Severity Scoring proforma with Modified Atlanta criteria in e-care, plus education at M&M meetings, junior doctor inductions and multidisciplinary awareness campaigns.

cycle2.result: 66.6% (18/27) had a proforma completed, of which 38.8% (7/18) were fully completed.

result.other_findings: Only a minority of proformas were fully completed; further education and re-audit are planned.

result.topic: WHO safety checklist compliance in ECT
result.setting: ECT clinic, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust, Bolton Directorate
result.standard: WHO surgical safety checklist modified for ECT including NPSA advice, per ECT accreditation service standards; target 100% completion

cycle1.result: 19/20 (95%) completed by the duty psychiatrist; 5/20 (25%) not signed; 75% complete and valid.

result.other_findings: Checklists were present in all case notes; a repeat audit is planned.

result.setting: District general hospital, University Hospital Lewisham, London
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines: mortality <10% (<30% severe), diagnosis within 48h, gallbladder ultrasound within 24h, severity stratification within 48h, cause established in >80%, ICU for severe cases, definitive gallstone treatment within 14 days

cycle1.result: Mortality 2.9% (33.3% in severe); diagnosis within 48h in all; severity stratification 91.2%; aetiology established 82.4%; ultrasound within 24h 41.2%; all severe cases discussed with intensivists; 7.1% of gallstone pancreatitis had definitive treatment within 2 weeks.

result.intervention: Planned meetings with surgical leads to implement a pathway, with re-audit in 4 months.
result.other_findings: No weekend ultrasound was available; 50% of those without ultrasound at 24h had CT.

result.setting: Major trauma centre (Cardiff)
result.standard: BOAST-15 blunt chest wall trauma guidance: surgical stabilisation within 48 hours (72-hour benchmark used)

cycle1.result: Median time to SSRF 3 days (range 1–12); 74 (62.2%) within 72 hours and 45 (37.8%) delayed.

result.other_findings: Longer ITU stay correlated with delay (Spearman 0.479, p<0.001); ventilated patients had longer mean time to SSRF (4.3 vs 3.0 days, p=0.028).

result.setting: General adult psychiatry inpatient wards
result.standard: Discharge summaries to include hypnotic medication review and specific discontinuation plan for the GP; target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: 0% compliance on two wards: no discharge summaries had a hypnotic medication review or discontinuation plan.

result.intervention: Implementation of previous audit recommendations (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Across six wards, 56.25% included a medication review for hypnotics and 18.75% a specific discontinuation plan.

result.other_findings: A 2024 re-audit on the original two wards showed 66.6% with medication review and 33.3% with a specific discontinuation plan.

result.topic: Parenteral nutrition use in paediatric surgery
result.setting: Paediatric Surgery Unit, Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge
result.standard: ESPGHAN 2005 paediatric parenteral nutrition guidelines: optimal benefit with ≥5 days PN

cycle1.result: 28 PN episodes; sub-optimal PN in 15 (54%), with median 3 days of full-dose feed.

result.other_findings: Nine (32%) central line complications, including loss of access (4) and infection (2); prior dietician review made no significant difference.

result.setting: General surgical FY1 doctors, Oxford University Hospitals and Milton Keynes University Hospital

cycle1.result: Pre-intervention mean confidence lowest for hand-tying (1.5/4) and drain management (2.1/4), highest for scrubbing (3.3/4).

cycle2.result: Confidence rose by 1.05 Likert points (+52% overall), e.g. hand-tying mean 3.1/4 and jejunostomy tube securing 2.5/4; 95% rated sessions excellent or very good.

result.other_findings: A third PDSA cycle is planned to assess sustained confidence after placement.

result.setting: Surgical ward round bedside teaching for Year 3 BSMS students, University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 48% strongly agreed teaching fellows were engaging and approachable; 35% agreed sessions were well organised and relevant.

result.intervention: Surgical teaching fellows, smaller teaching groups, improved communication with surgical teams and improved teaching material.

cycle2.result: 60% strongly agreed teaching fellows were engaging and approachable; 55% agreed sessions were well organised and relevant.

result.other_findings: Students requested more fellows on ward rounds, debriefs, clearer learning objectives and more time on history and examination.

result.setting: All adult surgical wards, district general hospital (King's Mill Hospital)

cycle1.result: Bowel chart present in 79% of nursing folders; bowel movements documented in 25% of nursing and 30% of medical notes.

result.intervention: Bowel chart paper colour changed from white to yellow with identical content.

cycle2.result: Bowel chart present in 90%; documentation in nursing and medical notes 74% and 69%.

result.other_findings: The change was rolled out trust-wide.

result.setting: Kingston Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, laparoscopic cholecystectomy
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice (18 items)

cycle1.result: 100% compliance for surgeon's name, operation name, incision, port placement and closure; lowest items were postoperative instructions 46%, elective/emergency 38%, complications 36%, additional procedures 23%, operative diagnosis 16%, estimated blood loss 8%.

result.intervention: Planned standardised proforma via an online app integrated with the electronic record.
result.other_findings: Indication and operative findings were recorded in 98%.

result.topic: Prehospital ECG in acute coronary syndrome
result.setting: MINAP national myocardial infarction registry

cycle1.result: PHECG use rose from 51% to 64% (STEMI 64% to 79%); with PHECG more call-to-balloon <90 min (27.9% vs 21.4%) and door-to-needle <30 min (90.6% vs 83.7%).

result.other_findings: 30-day mortality lower with PHECG (7.4% vs 8.2%, aOR 0.94).

result.setting: Northwick Park Hospital, General Surgery
result.standard: British Society of Haematology guidance: no indiscriminate coagulation screening; detailed bleeding history instead

cycle1.result: 19% appropriate requests; 81% of tests done were inappropriate.

cycle2.result: Appropriate requests increased to 56%; inappropriate tests fell to 44%.

result.other_findings: 148 patients in total across both cycles; each coagulation screen cost an average of £29.42, with an estimated £2971.42 spent on inappropriate requests.

result.setting: Secondary care orthopaedic department, Liverpool University Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE Blood Transfusion Guidance (2015): threshold Hb <70 g/L, target 70–90 g/L; altered threshold only for acute coronary syndrome

cycle1.result: 21.4% transfused in line with NICE threshold and targets; average Hb threshold 75.5 (range 60–110); 54.2% prescribed 1 unit at a time.

result.other_findings: Most common reason for altered threshold was an inconsistently defined 'coronary history', yet 0% had an ACS; iron deficiency anaemia identified in 11.4% and treated pre-operatively in 7%.

result.setting: District general hospital, General Surgery department (Altnagelvin Area Hospital)
result.standard: ATLS protocols: documentation of primary and secondary surveys

cycle1.result: Primary survey done in 9%; secondary survey in 7%; missed injury rate 4.5%.

result.intervention: Resident doctor education on ATLS principles, promotion of ATLS certification, and a structured ATLS trauma clerk-in template.

cycle2.result: Primary survey 78%; secondary survey 69.5%; no missed injuries.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Ealing Hospital general surgical department, district general hospital, London
result.standard: Criteria for appropriate admission derived from NICE national guidelines

cycle1.result: 14 of 18 (77.8%) admitted; 11 of the 14 admitted could have been safely ambulated under national guidelines (15 of 18 overall).

result.other_findings: Inappropriate admissions stayed a mean 3.27 days (range 1–8), 49 avoidable patient-days, estimated cost £78,400 p.a.; none received surgery.

result.topic: Cardiorespiratory assessment in upper abdominal pain
result.setting: Surgical units, University Hospitals Birmingham
result.standard: Trust protocol: all patients with upper abdominal pain require chest assessment; those older than 40 require ECG

cycle1.result: Chest assessment in 48%; ECG in 28% of patients older than 40.

result.intervention: Staff education on chest assessment and ECG interpretation, protocol flyers and posters in A&E and SAU, and electronic system changed so ECGs can be uploaded.

cycle2.result: Chest assessment rose to 85%; ECG in patients older than 40 rose to 61%.

result.other_findings: No life-threatening cardiac or respiratory conditions were missed in the re-audit.

result.setting: Adult general surgery, North Middlesex University Hospital Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local trust guidelines on antibiotic stewardship in intra-abdominal infection after source control

cycle1.result: Average post-operative antibiotic duration 11.2 days (± 7.7).

result.intervention: Results presented locally to the surgical team, highlighting trust guidance on intra-abdominal infection prescribing, with microbiology input.
result.other_findings: Duration remained well beyond local recommendations; possible barriers include surgical apprehension about stepdown and electronic prescribing systems.

result.topic: Timing of acute major nerve repair
result.setting: Single centre, Birmingham (University Hospitals Birmingham / Royal Orthopaedic Hospital hands, plastics and peripheral nerve team)

cycle1.result: 76% repaired <72 h; ≥M3 recovery 65.5% (<72 h) versus 64.7% (≥72 h); time to surgery weakly associated with motor recovery (ρ = –0.26, p = 0.19) and moderately with sensory recovery (ρ = –0.38, p = 0.043).

result.other_findings: Retrospective outcome cohort; overall 65.3% achieved ≥M3 and 45.8% ≥M4; median time to repair 38.7 h.

result.setting: Peterborough City Hospital
result.standard: Local trust guidelines for multiple rib fractures (analgesia, imaging, chest injury scoring, pain team and regional anaesthesia referral, ABG, CCU referral)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Targeted interventions following first-cycle recommendations (not detailed).

cycle2.result: Improvement in appropriate analgesia prescription and chest injury scoring documentation; over 75% of eligible patients not referred to Critical Care; ABG compliance in hypoxic patients deteriorated.

result.other_findings: Regional analgesia associated with shorter LOS (9.8 vs 12.6 days); pneumonia increased mean stay from 10.4 to 18.3 days; ≥16 fractures had higher complication rates (27% vs 9%).

result.setting: Tertiary colorectal surgery department, London
result.standard: Professional Records Standards Body and Royal College of Physicians national discharge summary guidelines (7-point score)

cycle1.result: Median and modal score 5.00/7.00, mean 4.15/7.00; safety netting advice lowest (14%); events/procedures highest (89%); 4 had no discharge summary.

result.intervention: Results presented locally and a discharge summary proforma based on national standards disseminated.

cycle2.result: Median and modal score 6.00/7.00, mean 6.06/7.00; safety netting lowest (32%); reason for admission, events/procedures and post-op plan 100%.

result.other_findings: All individual criteria improved significantly, but safety netting advice stayed poor.

result.setting: District general hospital ENT department, University Hospitals Sussex

cycle1.result: Baseline clinician ratings (/5): efficiency 2.0, accuracy 2.6, transparency 2.0 and 1.8, patient safety 3.4.

result.intervention: Live patient lists on NHS SharePoint replacing clinician-to-clinician email handovers.

cycle2.result: Efficiency 4.8 (p=0.0016), accuracy 4.8 (p=0.0029), transparency 4.8 (p=0.0060) and 4.8 (p=0.001); patient safety 4.3 (not significant).

result.other_findings: Questionnaire-based QI of perceived handover quality, not measured against a standard.

result.topic: Testicular torsion pathway and time to theatre
result.setting: Wexham Park Hospital, district general hospital (ED and urology)
result.standard: Timely surgery for suspected testicular torsion with TWIST score risk stratification

cycle1.result: Mean time to theatre 276 minutes from ED presentation and 200 minutes from decision-to-operate; TWIST score calculated in 3.6% of cases.

result.intervention: New torsion pathway in 2023: expedited referral from triage, electronic TWIST-based risk stratification tool, and targeted ED and urology education.

cycle2.result: Mean time to theatre 162 minutes from presentation and 100 minutes from decision-to-operate; TWIST documented in 75%.

result.other_findings: Prompted by five missed torsions in 2021-2022; no missed torsions from implementation to re-audit, and TWIST ≥5 predicted torsion in all cases.

result.setting: Collaborative national audit of 22 hospitals in England, Wales and Scotland
result.standard: BOAST guideline for paediatric ACL injuries

cycle1.result: 65% of centres used acute knee pathways; 68% locally collaborative imaging pathways; 59% radiological growth monitoring; 30% reported functional outcomes; fewer than 50% reported re-rupture rates; 74% followed rehabilitation protocols.

result.other_findings: Data were collected by online questionnaire of surgeons and trainees about service provision.

result.topic: Epistaxis first aid knowledge in the emergency department
result.setting: Single-centre emergency department, Barts Health NHS Trust, London
result.standard: ENT UK epistaxis management guidelines (Hippocratic first aid)

cycle1.result: Knowledge of appropriate epistaxis first aid 53%; mean confidence in prevention advice 2.7/5.

result.intervention: 30-minute interactive tutorial on epistaxis during local ED teaching.
result.other_findings: Questionnaire-based assessment of clinician knowledge and confidence.

result.topic: Perioperative ACE inhibitor and ARB withholding
result.setting: Cardiac surgery unit, James Cook University Hospital, Middlesbrough
result.standard: 100% of patients to have ACEi/A2RBs stopped at least 24 hours preoperatively, with clinical exceptions documented

cycle1.result: 96% stopped; reasoning not documented for continuations (n=1).

result.intervention: Team meetings to remind staff of the protocol (particularly ward and in-house unit staff), alongside the trust's new online prescribing platform.

cycle2.result: 92% stopped; reasoning not documented for continuations (n=2).

result.other_findings: Three cycles: cycle 2 (December 2021, 51 patients) fell to 76% stopped, with reasoning not documented for 50% of continuations (n=12).

result.topic: Oral health care in care homes
result.setting: Lime Tree Gardens, care home/community rehabilitation centre for adults with severe mental illness
result.standard: NICE oral health quality standards: mouth care needs assessed on admission, recorded in care plan, and support for twice-daily tooth cleaning and denture care

cycle1.result: More than 90% of patients had unmet oral health needs.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Renal transplant graft and patient survival
result.setting: Department of Transplant Surgery, Belfast City Hospital
result.standard: National benchmarks for five-year survival (figures not given)

cycle1.result: Overall five-year survival was below national benchmarks.

result.other_findings: Older donor age, prolonged cold ischaemic time, pre-transplant dialysis and biopsy-proven rejection predicted poorer survival; lower discharge creatinine correlated with better function.

result.setting: Tertiary urology centre, emergency presentations, NHS Lothian, Edinburgh
result.standard: EAUN key documentation domains for catheterisation, including care plan use

cycle1.result: Variable compliance; highest for catheter size and indication; urinalysis most frequently missed (14.9%).

result.intervention: Poster developed and deployed, with discussion with staff.

cycle2.result: Similar pattern of compliance; urinalysis 9.5%; only balloon volume documentation improved significantly (p=0.0019).

result.other_findings: Care plan use remained generally poor; an electronic notes text prompt is in development.

result.setting: Specialist hand unit, Royal Derby Hospital
result.standard: BOAST (October 2021): tourniquet inflated 50-100mmHg above systolic blood pressure in upper limb surgery

cycle1.result: 36% (18/50) compliant.

result.intervention: Specific educational interventions about the newly published standard.
result.other_findings: All non-compliance was overinflation (average 20.6mmHg); non-compliance higher among senior hand consultants (63.4%); no tourniquet complications.

result.setting: High-volume tertiary urology centre, Western General Hospital, Edinburgh
result.standard: NICE guidelines on fluid assessment parameters

cycle1.result: Fluid balance recorded 38%, heart rate 35%, blood pressure 38%; 27% of FY1s confident in fluid reviews.

result.intervention: Electronic proforma in TrakCare with NICE review parameters as headers, plus urology-specific fluid teaching for FYs.

cycle2.result: Fluid balance 78%, heart rate 96%, blood pressure 96% (all p<0.01); FY1 confidence 90%.

result.other_findings: Only 27% of FY1s reported sufficient fluid teaching before starting.

result.setting: St Columcille's Hospital, Dublin, teaching hospital inpatients
result.standard: National Consent Policy: resuscitation decisions made with patient or family, by the most senior decision maker, and carefully documented

cycle1.result: 25.5% had a DNACPR order; 100% had a form but none fully completed; 48% not endorsed by the consultant; 74% not discussed with patient or no reason documented; 41% no discussion documented.

result.other_findings: 92% had DNACPR status documented in nursing notes; results to be used in an education session.

result.setting: Three surgical wards, Hereford County Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission and reassessment within 48 hours (aim 100%)

cycle1.result: First assessments within 24 hours above 65%; second assessments within 48 hours 36.1%; breast 95.3%, colorectal 90%, general surgery 86.6%.

result.intervention: Results presented at departmental meetings and educational posters displayed.

cycle2.result: Second assessments within 48 hours 47.6%; breast 100%, colorectal 93.3%, general surgery 88.0%; first assessments within 24 hours remained above 65%.

result.other_findings: Variation between wards persisted; next step is making the late-shift FY1 responsible for outstanding assessments.

result.setting: General surgery emergency admissions, University Hospital Galway

cycle1.result: Of 36 eligible, 29 adequately treated with chemoprophylaxis and 7 under- or overtreated for weight and renal clearance; 35 of 40 charted for TED stockings.

result.intervention: Educational presentation and two checkboxes added with pharmacy to the prophylactic anticoagulant page of the drug chart, prompting weight and renal function.

cycle2.result: 37 of 38 eligible received weight and renal function-adjusted doses; all 40 received TED stockings.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Royal Devon & Exeter Hospital

cycle1.result: Pharyngocutaneous fistula in 20% of cases; longer stay with fistula (24.5 v/s 11.1 days).

result.other_findings: Fistula more common with pec major than ALT flaps and in salvage cases; clear margins less often in supraglottic than glottic disease (45% v/s 93%).

result.topic: Core surgical training rota training time
result.setting: Core surgical training rotas across 17 hospitals in one training region
result.standard: JCST Quality Indicator 10: minimum 5 consultant-supervised training sessions per week

cycle1.result: 6 (25%) rotas met the standard; mean deficit 18.5 (+/-29.5) sessions per 6-month rotation.

result.other_findings: Counting 0.5 hours of supervised training per on-call session gave 9 (38%) compliant, and 1 hour gave 13 (54%); compliant rotas averaged 1 in 11 versus 1 in 9.

result.topic: Head and neck two-week-wait cancer pathway timelines
result.setting: Two week wait head and neck ENT clinic (William Harvey Hospital / Frimley Park Hospital)
result.standard: Cancer diagnosis within 28 days and treatment within 62 days

cycle1.result: Mean times to initial consultation, diagnosis and first treatment reported for 12 cancer patients (no figures given).

result.intervention: Telephone triage by a head and neck clinical nurse specialist as an adjunct to clinic.

cycle2.result: No significant difference in time to initial consultation (p=0.1875), diagnosis (p=0.0620) or first treatment (p=0.7747); telephone-triaged patients (n=7) had shorter time to initial consultation (p=0.0198).

result.other_findings: 273 referrals were analysed in total.

result.setting: Salford Royal Hospital, oesophagogastric cancer surgery
result.standard: Local staging laparoscopy and peritoneal washings guidelines

cycle1.result: 225 had washings; 2 appropriately not done due to extent of disease; 12 had washings not in line with policy, all with a clinical reason.

result.other_findings: 12 patients had positive cytology, all with T3/T4 disease.

result.setting: Elective ENT surgery, Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: RCS England Good Surgical Practice and GMC consent guidance

cycle1.result: Diagnosis documented 52%, surgical risks 50%, alternative or no treatment 30%, registrar discussion with consultant 31%; letters copied to patients 10% (registrars) vs 47% (consultants); 10% received a leaflet.

result.other_findings: 90% of patients were satisfied or very satisfied; refresher sessions, template letters and leaflets planned.

result.topic: Next of kin communication after laparotomy
result.setting: Laparotomy patients identified from NELA database, Lewisham and Greenwich NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE CG138 on involving family members and carers

cycle1.result: NOK details documented 86%; 75% of telephone numbers reachable; 33% documented contact within 48 hours post-operation.

result.intervention: Data presented at educational meetings with informal reminders for a week.

cycle2.result: NOK details documented 97%; 97% of numbers reachable; 41% documented contact within 48 hours.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Nasal trauma assessment in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department referrals to a major ENT centre emergency clinic, Imperial College Healthcare Trust
result.standard: Assessment and documentation of septal haematoma, infraorbital nerve status and airflow symptoms

cycle1.result: Septal haematoma documented 79%; airflow symptoms 32%.

result.intervention: Presentation at ED teaching and board rounds, then a new trust guideline uploaded to the ED guidance app.

cycle2.result: Septal haematoma 85%; airflow symptoms 33%; infraorbital nerve reviewed in 5% more patients.

result.other_findings: Three cycles with 137 patients in total; referrals were 26% higher before the first intervention.

result.setting: UK national trauma and orthopaedic trainee collaboratives

cycle1.result: 10 trainee-led national T&O collaborative projects since the pandemic versus 0 in 2019; 3 published.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Interventional radiology, South Tees NHS Trust, Middlesbrough
result.standard: RCR standards: written consent 100%, procedural documentation 100%, pseudoaneurysm/AV fistula ≤1%, access-site haematoma needing intervention ≤3%, dissection ≤1%, reversible neurological deficit ≤2%, permanent deficit ≤1%, major contrast reactions ≤5%

cycle1.result: Complications broadly within RCR thresholds but pseudoaneurysm frequency exceeded the ≤1% target (groin haematoma with pseudoaneurysm n=2, pseudoaneurysm with groin haematoma n=6); procedure-related bleeding n=4 and stroke n=4; consent and documentation consistent.

result.other_findings: Thirteen deaths occurred, mainly from underlying pathology; recommendations on ultrasound-guided access and monitoring implemented with re-audit planned.

result.setting: Tertiary acute hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Pre-QIP survey of the previous rotation's induction experiences (results not given).

result.intervention: Joint surgical, medical and ED induction programme piloted in August 2024.

cycle2.result: 85% agreed the joint induction promoted better understanding and teamwork; more attendees rated it more effective than a departmental induction.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Medical admissions, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Fall description 91.7%; syncope asked 50%; previous falls 33.3%; cardiac exam 96.7%; neuro exam 71.1%; mobility baseline 41.7%; medication review 60%; mobility assessed under 72 hours 41.6%; differential for the fall 76.7%.

result.other_findings: An education session for medical SHOs was held on 14 May 2024 with cycle 2 planned for June 2024.

result.setting: Single health board in Wales, large teaching hospital (Cardiff and Vale University Health Board)

cycle1.result: 67 (49%) OGD and 24 (57%) FS inpatients waited over one day; 71 (40%) OGD and 19 (11%) FS referrals were priority 1.

result.other_findings: Of 297 referrals, 46 (34%) OGD and 14 (33%) FS patients were discharged within two days of the procedure, suggesting earlier discharge if scoped sooner.

result.setting: General surgery wards, busy teaching hospital (Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle)

cycle1.result: Height and weight documented 11/14; MUST score 9/14; PN commenced 9/14; median HLOS 30 days (6-44).

cycle2.result: Height and weight 15/18; MUST 17/18; PN commenced 15/18; all reviewed by PN nurse within 1 day; median HLOS 17 days (7-38).

result.other_findings: All cases in both cycles had a documented reason for gut failure and baseline bloods; rejected referrals fell by 53% and median PN duration rose from 4 to 6 days.

result.topic: Oakland score in lower GI bleeding
result.setting: Emergency Department referrals to surgery, Ulster Hospital Dundonald
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology 2019 guidelines: Oakland score to risk-stratify lower GI bleeding

cycle1.result: Oakland score documented in 1 patient (4.8%).

result.intervention: Posters in ED and seminar rooms and a departmental teaching session.
result.other_findings: 61.8% of 34 surveyed clinicians were unaware of the Oakland score at baseline.

result.setting: Rowan Ward PICU, Farnham Road Hospital, Guildford

cycle1.result: 12 of 36 (33%) unsuitable for PICU admission; 22% had documented MDT discussions.

result.intervention: Standardised referral form, enhanced consultant-to-consultant communication, and a PICU outreach team.

cycle2.result: 9 of 38 (24%) unsuitable; 3% had documented MDT discussions.

result.other_findings: MDT discussion documentation stayed poor; prior PICU admission among unsuitable admissions fell from 67% to 22%.

result.setting: Memory, general geriatric and hypertension/stroke clinics, Connolly Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 67% of patients reported an up-to-date medication list; 62% of doctors/cANPs felt the patient had one.

result.other_findings: Only 17% of patients felt they themselves held the most up-to-date list; 34% had medications changed at the visit.

result.setting: Older person's rehabilitation setting, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Awareness of physical activity guidelines 10%; patient satisfaction 85.7%; physiotherapy contact time 324.5 hours.

result.intervention: Physical activity information leaflet, open gym sessions and walking groups.

cycle2.result: Awareness 63%; satisfaction 97.5%; physiotherapy contact 411.25 hours; time to physical readiness for discharge fell by 5 days (orthopaedic) and 9 days (non-orthopaedic).

result.other_findings: 5STS, TUG and CAS improved beyond clinically important thresholds; estimated savings €5,290 and €9,522.

result.setting: Model 4 Trauma Centre, Cork University Hospital
result.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standard 1: dedicated orthopaedic bed within 4 hours of ED arrival

cycle1.result: Fewer than 41% reached an orthopaedic bed within 4 hours (national average 36%); mean 3 hours from arrival to specialist assessment.

result.other_findings: Delays mainly before X-ray and orthopaedic review, with duplicated digital and paper documentation; a co-designed digital admission proforma is being developed.

result.setting: Surgical inpatients, Mersey and West Lancashire NHS Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Pathology, NHS England and NICE guidance on FBC and U&E retesting intervals

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Raised awareness among surgical teams and guideline-based recommendations.

cycle2.result: 49% improvement in appropriately requested necessary tests; 5% reduction in unnecessary tests; 22.8% overall increase in compliance.

result.other_findings: 731 FBC and U&E requests reviewed across both cycles from 70 patients.

result.setting: Department of Pancreatic Surgery, Leeds Teaching Hospital NHS Trust
