cycle1.result: Optimal metabolic therapy in 4/46 (8.7%) high-risk, 6/38 (15.8%) moderate-risk and 29/30 (96.7%) low-risk patients; MACE+ACM at 1 year 15.2%, 7.9% and 6.7%.

result.other_findings: QRISK3 independently predicted survival (HR 1.033, p=0.037), including in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (HR 1.056, p=0.047).

result.topic: Physical health checks on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Ward 4, Dr Gray's Hospital, Elgin, psychiatric inpatient ward
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists standards: physical examination, ECG and bloods within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Bloods 52.9%; physical examination 76.4%; ECG 58.8%.

result.intervention: Admission checklist of required examinations and investigations.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Pilot sites in five hospitals across four countries (international co-creation initiative)

cycle1.result: Global clinician survey (n=308, 46 countries), two bi-national audits (n=965, 63 hospitals) and interviews (n=15) confirmed a widespread evidence-practice gap.

result.intervention: Co-created SIMPLER nutrition pathway and toolkit, pilot-tested with action-reflection cycles.
result.other_findings: 46 healthcare services in 23 countries have committed to implementing SIMPLER; a global evaluation is underway.

result.setting: Elective thoracic theatres, Royal Stoke University Hospital

cycle1.result: Mean turnover time 94±14 minutes; handover to recovery 23±8 minutes and sign-in/transfer to anaesthetic room 36±6 minutes.

result.other_findings: Patients ready for discharge spent an extra 48±13 minutes in recovery awaiting ward transfer, blocking handover.

result.topic: Tissue sealant and leaks after oesophagectomy
result.setting: Tertiary upper GI centre

cycle1.result: No significant difference in anastomotic leak (4.0% vs 7.4%, p = 0.24) or chyle leak (6.6% vs 4.3%, p = 0.44) with Tisseel.

result.other_findings: Re-thoracotomy after anastomotic leak was lower with Tisseel (16.7% vs 85.7%, p = 0.021).

result.topic: Septic arthritis of the wrist management
result.setting: Orthopaedic department, Conquest Hospital, Hastings, district general hospital
result.standard: BSR & BHPR, BOA, RCGP and BSAC hot swollen joint guidelines: serial aspiration to dryness

cycle1.result: No patients underwent serial aspiration; 6/11 had wrist aspiration; 2/11 had surgical washout.

result.other_findings: Only 2/15 orthopaedic doctors were aware of national guidelines and 2/15 considered repeated aspiration to dryness as definitive management.

result.setting: Adult tertiary centre, Aintree University Hospital, Liverpool
result.standard: Tokyo Guidelines 2013 and 2018 indications for percutaneous cholecystostomy

cycle1.result: 28 (36.8%) met all Tokyo criteria for emergency PC; 29 (38.2%) had severe (grade 3) cholecystitis; all had pre-procedural imaging and cultures; 63 (82.9%) received immediate antibiotics.

result.other_findings: PC appears overperformed relative to the guidelines.

result.setting: Tertiary bariatric surgery centre (St James University Hospital, Leeds)
result.standard: BOMSS guidelines: 6 weeks of liquid/crushed medications on discharge

cycle1.result: Paracetamol liquid 49%; codeine tablet 11%; senna liquid 11%; ondansetron liquid 20%; lansoprazole dispersible 97%; enoxaparin 100%.

result.intervention: Digital prescription tab/checklist created with the MDT, plus education of junior doctors, ACPs and trainee pharmacists.

cycle2.result: Paracetamol liquid 58%; codeine 42%; senna liquid 58%; ondansetron liquid 58%; lansoprazole 100%; enoxaparin 100%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Lynch syndrome MMR testing in colorectal cancer
result.setting: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE guidance: MMR IHC or MSI testing for all colorectal cancers

cycle1.result: 97% had MMR testing; 90% reported within 10 days; biopsy to histology 8.6 days; MMR to MLH1 result 251 days.

cycle2.result: 100% had MMR testing; 97% reported within 10 days (average 4.3 days); biopsy to histology 8 days; MMR to MLH1 result 91 days.

result.other_findings: Four patients were MMR deficient, three of whom had BRAF and MLH1 methylation testing.

result.setting: Acute Care at Home service, Southern Health and Social Care Trust, Craigavon

cycle1.result: Dementia 93%, delirium 85%, depression 6%, falls 99%, fractures/osteoporosis 27%, medication 100%, pain 91%, nutrition 98%, skin 93%, incontinence 94%, advance care planning 39%, visual acuity 7%, social support 99%.

result.other_findings: Electronic assessment lacked a Geriatric Depression Score; electronic assessments have been adjusted and a re-audit is planned in 6 months.

result.setting: General surgery virtual outpatient clinics, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Satisfaction with telephone consultations significantly higher than pre-COVID face-to-face survey results; 51% confident and 27% confident to some extent about listing without examination.

result.other_findings: More than a third were not happy to be discharged after a telephone consultation; 10% not confident about the risks of surgery.

result.setting: Breast unit, Ashford and St Peter's Hospital
result.standard: RCPath dataset for pathology reporting of breast disease in surgical excision specimens: 90% of reports to include items

cycle1.result: Specimen type, histological grade and invasive disease well reported; date of surgery 0%, core biopsy site 1.5%, microinvasion 4.3%.

result.other_findings: Prompted by a serious incident; a streamlined reporting proforma with RCPath core items is proposed.

result.setting: Endocrine ward, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: 16-point ward round documentation checklist based on guidelines and standards

cycle1.result: Average completeness 71.38%; bleep number 37%; VTE prophylaxis 26.5%; antibiotics 30.1%; analgesia 19.28%.

result.intervention: Structured ward round template in the electronic patient record.

cycle2.result: Average completeness 82.1% (range 43.75% to 100%); bleep number 57%; VTE prophylaxis 69.5%; antibiotics 58.5%; analgesia 58.5%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Royal Hospital for Children and Young People, Edinburgh, paediatric trauma admissions
result.standard: South-East Scotland Major Trauma Guidelines: tertiary survey within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Tertiary survey completed in 34% (15 of 44); within 24 hours 20% (3 of 15); median time 44.5 hours.

result.intervention: Educational package and major trauma coordinators empowered to enforce tertiary surveys as a discharge prerequisite, with weekly check-ins.

cycle2.result: Completed in 72% (124 of 172); within 24 hours 56% (70 of 124); median time 15.9 hours.

result.other_findings: Evolving injuries identified in 13% in both cycles.

result.setting: Whole hospital adult inpatients, Barnet Hospital

cycle1.result: 30% (n = 65) had possible delirium (4AT ≥ 4).

result.other_findings: Delirium was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (10.7% vs 3.9%), 20-week mortality (26.2% vs 14.2%) and discharge to institutional care.

result.setting: Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Acute pancreatitis management metrics: Glasgow score within 48 hours, imaging within 24 hours, cholecystectomy within 2 weeks, escalation and referral

cycle1.result: Escalation of severe cases 0%; cholecystectomy within 2 weeks 75%; transfer of non-gallstone cases to gastroenterology 33%.

result.intervention: Weekly benign UGI MDT with gastroenterology and radiology, streamlined ERCP pathway, hot cholecystectomy pathway, and targeted surgical education.

cycle2.result: Glasgow score within 48 hours 50%; escalation 60%; imaging within 24 hours 100%; median admission to ERCP 5 days; cholecystectomy within 2 weeks 100%; transfer to gastroenterology 50%.

result.other_findings: 131 patients were included across both cycles.

result.setting: South London hospital (St George's Hospital)

cycle1.result: Clinically significant cancer in 59.3% (97/163); any cancer 72.2% (118/163); complications 2.47%, no infections.

result.other_findings: PI-RADS 5 lesions had clinically significant disease in 90% versus 53% for PI-RADS 4.

result.setting: District general hospital (James Paget University Hospital)
result.standard: England average negative appendicectomy rate (GIRFT data)

cycle1.result: Negative appendicectomy rate in children 16% (England average 12%).

result.intervention: Quality improvement programme using Kotter's 8-step model (specific changes not detailed).
result.other_findings: Balancing measures: perforated/gangrenous appendicitis fell from 23% to 16%, LOS from 4 to 3 days, and 7-day readmissions were 1 (3%) vs 2 (6%), none due to delay.

result.topic: Neurovascular documentation around distal radius fracture MUA
result.setting: Emergency department and fracture clinic, Queen's Medical Centre, Nottingham
result.standard: BOAST distal radius fracture standard: circulation and sensation documented before and after MUA

cycle1.result: Neurovascular assessment in ED 98%; before Bier's block 34%; vascular assessment after Bier's block 22%; fracture clinic neurovascular assessment 76%.

result.intervention: An intervention after the first cycle (not described).

cycle2.result: Neurovascular assessment in ED 88%; before Bier's block 60.3%; vascular assessment after Bier's block 39.7%; fracture clinic neurovascular assessment 64%.

result.other_findings: Suggested next steps include teaching upper limb neurological assessment and a sticker or stamp aide-memoire.

result.setting: Borders General Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Local hospital antibiotic guidelines for appendicectomy

cycle1.result: 68.8% (11/16) compliance with local antibiotic guidelines; non-compliant cases had correct antibiotics but different gentamicin doses.

result.intervention: Antibiotic prescribing teaching for surgical and anaesthetic doctors, including use of the gentamicin dosing calculator.
result.other_findings: Gaps in prescriber awareness of antibiotic guidelines were identified at baseline.

result.setting: Vascular surgery, Royal Sussex County Hospital, Brighton
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians Ward Round Audit Standard 2015

cycle1.result: Overall documentation 67% across all domains; patient identification 68%.

result.intervention: Ward round proforma displayed in each set of patient notes and communal ward areas; memory aids.

cycle2.result: Overall documentation 81%; patient identification 93%; operation name and date improved by 28% and 24%; abnormal observations documentation improved by 48%.

result.other_findings: Antibiotics and thromboprophylaxis documentation improved by 25% and 30% but remained under 50% in cycle 2. The abstract lists 230 entries (109 and 121) with both labelled cycle 2.

result.setting: Flexor tendon laceration repair pathway; UCL, Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust, University of Bristol

cycle1.result: Estimated carbon footprint approximately 113.2 kgCO2eq per patient; rehabilitation 59.85 kgCO2eq (52.9%); patient travel 79.42% of emissions (89.88 kgCO2eq).

result.other_findings: Equipment production and transport contributed 8.52 kgCO2eq (7.53%); virtual hand therapy, reusable gowns and drapes, procedure packs and WALANT were recommended.

result.setting: General surgery department, Peterborough City Hospital
result.standard: NICE antimicrobial stewardship guideline NG15 1.1.2.4 and trust guidelines

cycle1.result: 57% of antibiotic prescriptions were in line with the correct treatment guidelines (238 prescriptions from 109 patients).

result.intervention: Trust guidelines put on the Microguide mobile app and laptops; educational posters and a presentation to the surgical department.

cycle2.result: Accuracy of antibiotic prescriptions significantly improved; no figures given.

result.other_findings: Some improvement in documentation of indication and duration of antibiotic prescriptions.

result.setting: Royal Lancaster Infirmary, single centre
result.standard: ACPGBI guidance on colonoscopy after diverticulitis

cycle1.result: 90 uncomplicated diverticulitis without surgery: 71 (59% of total) had colonoscopy, 19 (16%) did not; 78.9% of uncomplicated cases had colonoscopy, which may have been unnecessary. Complicated: 15 surgery, 15 no surgery, 11 (9.2%) colonoscopy, 4 (3.3%) no colonoscopy.

result.other_findings: Of 82 patients who had colonoscopy, no colorectal cancer was detected (0%); 3.3% of complicated cases had no colonoscopy due to patient choice, comorbidities or frailty. FIT suggested as an adjunct.

result.setting: Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust, trust-wide
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice standards for operation notes

cycle1.result: Handwritten notes 68% compliance with GSP vs typed notes 79% (p <0.05); 15/29 (52%) handwritten notes legible.

result.intervention: Trust-wide electronic operation note proforma on Forms4Health being implemented (PDSA); re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: Typed notes were better at recording time of surgery, elective or emergency status, complications and thromboprophylaxis instructions.

result.setting: Tertiary hospital, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons handover guidelines (minimum dataset)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance with RCS minimum dataset 45%; patient identification 75%, date of admission 30%, location 80%, responsible consultant 40%, diagnosis 60%, pending investigations 50%.

result.intervention: Standardised handover sheet (PDSA 1), then posters reinforcing the guidelines (PDSA 2).

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 75%; patient identification 95%, date of admission 50%, location 88%, responsible consultant 60%, diagnosis 75%, pending investigations 67%.

result.other_findings: Re-audit was done after each of two interventions; final results reported.

result.setting: Dartford and Gravesham NHS Trust
result.standard: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit NoLap reporting criteria

cycle1.result: No NoLap cases recorded before intervention.

result.intervention: PDSA 1: education at M&M, monthly reminders, retrospective case review; PDSA 2: junior doctor data collection, shared NELA folder, review of M&M cases and on-call lists, engagement with anaesthetists.

cycle2.result: Three cases identified retrospectively after cycle 1; ten further NoLap patients identified after cycle 2.

result.other_findings: Project ran March 2024 to October 2025; awareness of NoLap criteria improved across teams.

result.setting: Survey of Dutch Surgical Society members

cycle1.result: Survey: 67% agreed inguinal hernia care should be improved; 66% said registration of outcomes could achieve improvement.

result.other_findings: 91% agreed chronic pain and recurrence should be quality indicators; opponents cited administrative burden.

result.setting: Surgical department, NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists guidance that requests include comprehensive relevant information

cycle1.result: 73% (52/71) of radiology requests accepted; rejections due to inappropriate imaging (4/19), duplicate requests (4/19) and insufficient clinical details (4/19), each 21%.

result.intervention: Structured request format developed and staff educated on its use.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Birmingham

cycle1.result: Whole cohort 437 PD patients (2020-24): CR-POPF 17.4%, 90-day mortality 4.6%; 44 high-risk POPF patients (historical 13, prospective 31). CR-POPF historical controls scanned at median 8 days and intervention at 12.5 days.

result.intervention: Protocol CT scans in asymptomatic high-risk POPF patients (CR score >5) from September 2022.

cycle2.result: Prospective CR-POPF patients scanned earlier (median 5 v 8 days; p<0.001) and had earlier intervention (10 v 12.5 days; p=0.03); protocol CT positive in 17/24 (70.8%), 13 (76.5%) had intervention.

result.other_findings: No difference in length of stay (21 v 17 days; p=0.57) or 90-day mortality (19.5% v 14.3%; p=0.76).

result.setting: Campbelltown Hospital, NSW, inpatients

cycle1.result: No patients received all therapeutic options recommended by the guideline; most received basic blood tests and imaging; compliance lower for echocardiography, iron replacement and angiotensin blockers.

result.other_findings: Median age 77, 71% frail; older patients trended towards fewer advanced investigations and appropriate medications.

result.setting: Patients with alcohol use disorder, Southern Taiwan

cycle1.result: 17 (9.6%) suicidal thoughts, 4 (2.3%) suicide plan, 22 (12.5%) self-injured; self-harm associated with lower AUDIT scores (-7.24).

result.other_findings: Physical stress, interpersonal difficulties and loneliness associated with higher AUDIT scores.

result.topic: Oakland score in lower GI bleeding
result.setting: University Hospital Lewisham, district general hospital
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidance on Oakland score risk stratification (safe discharge threshold ≤8)

cycle1.result: 6/63 (10%) had a documented Oakland score; three patients with OS <8 were inappropriately admitted.

result.intervention: Tailored teaching with a summary sheet and link to an e-calculator, after a departmental survey.

cycle2.result: 16/38 (42%) had a documented Oakland score; all 8/8 with OS ≤8 appropriately discharged.

result.other_findings: Survey of 11 surgical team members: 27% (3/11) aware of the Oakland score and 9% (1/11) used it.

result.setting: Royal Stoke Hospital, single centre
result.standard: AUGIS advice: emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 72 hours of diagnosing acute cholecystitis

cycle1.result: Median admission to theatre 106.5 hours; median length of stay 7.5 days.

cycle2.result: Median admission to theatre 70.7 hours (IQR 48.4-107.7); median admission to imaging 11 hours; median length of stay 5.6 days.

result.other_findings: 2021 cycle: admission to theatre 76.7 hours, stay 5.3 days. 2022: 9.2% subtotal cholecystectomies, 14.8% post-op complications including 2.2% bile leaks.

result.setting: Croydon University Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Model Hospital target day-case rate of 75% for laparoscopic cholecystectomy

cycle1.result: 34% (29/85) were not day cases; causes included post-operative nausea or pain (11), monitoring (9), MRCP (3), social issues (3), bleeding (2), IV antibiotics (1).

result.other_findings: Of the 29 non-day cases, 58% had afternoon operations, 48% Nassar grade >1 and 38% BMI >30; morning slots for high-risk patients suggested.

result.setting: Hillingdon Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, district general hospital
result.standard: Major Trauma Network Northwest London guidelines

cycle1.result: 58.4% adherence to guidelines; primary and secondary survey documentation 92.1% and 81.2%; imaging times 3 h 10 min (general) and 6 h 29 min (silver trauma).

result.intervention: Educational sessions, presentation of findings to stakeholders, an ED trauma lead assigned each shift and a silver trauma toolkit.

cycle2.result: Adherence 71.8% for general trauma and 100% for silver trauma; primary and secondary survey documentation 96.9% and 90.6%; imaging times 2 h 29 min (general) and 3 h 21 min (silver).

result.other_findings: High staff turnover and temporary staffing made education difficult.

result.topic: Index admission cholecystectomy for gallstone disease
result.setting: East Surrey Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Chole-QuIC target: 80% of eligible patients to have cholecystectomy within 8 days

cycle1.result: 31/53 (58.5%) eligible acute gallstone disease patients had cholecystectomy within 8 days; 25/40 fit acute cholecystitis patients had inpatient cholecystectomy.

result.other_findings: 5/15 discharged acute cholecystitis patients were readmitted within 30 days; inpatient surgery had shorter wait (3 v 31 days) but longer fasting and stay.

result.setting: Irish Hip Fracture Database, national clinical audit
result.standard: 7 IHFD clinical standards and 2 data quality standards linked to Best Practice Tariff

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: National audit feedback, Best Practice Tariff and Golden Hip Award; led to national hip fracture bypass pathway, orthogeriatric services and hip fracture governance committees.

cycle2.result: 29% admitted through ED within 4 hours, 75% surgery within 48 hours, 4% pressure injury, 83% seen by geriatrician or ANP, 87% bone health assessment, 83% falls assessment, 87% mobilised day after surgery.

result.other_findings: Statistically significant improvements in all standards 2013–2023; only 49% had day 1 delirium screen and 71% nutritional screen; median stay 12 days.

result.setting: Vascular surgery department, James Cook University Hospital
result.standard: RCSEng Good Surgical Practice operative note criteria

cycle1.result: Good compliance for date (97.5%), operator (97.5%), anaesthetist (100%), procedure (100%), closure (95%); poor for time (0%), blood loss (2.5%), elective/emergency (10%).

result.intervention: Results presented at departmental meeting; aide-memoire of poorly met criteria placed in all vascular theatres.
result.other_findings: Time, elective/emergency status and legibility showed minimal improvement.

result.setting: In-patient wards and SDEC referrals to vascular surgery, Princess Alexandra Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Professional Record Standards Body (PRSB) referral guidelines

cycle1.result: Median 2.5 of 10 PRSB criteria fulfilled; demographics 60%, referrer details 51%, reason 93%, family history 40%, patient ICE 40%.

result.intervention: Vascular surgery referral proforma emailed to a dedicated vascular surgery inbox.

cycle2.result: Median 9 of 10 criteria fulfilled (p <0.0001); demographics 100%, referrer details 100%, reason 100%, family history 84%, patient ICE 81%.

result.other_findings: Social history improved from 47% to 93% and investigation findings from 63% to 91%.

result.setting: Scunthorpe General Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Pathologists parameters for colorectal cancer resection request forms

cycle1.result: Approach mentioned 78%; diagrams 44%; preoperative therapy 4.5%.

cycle2.result: Approach 30%; diagrams 36%; preoperative therapy 20%; no significant overall improvement.

result.other_findings: Consultants who emphasised form completion achieved 97% type of surgery and 91% diagrams; marginal improvement in screening, familial cancer and IBD information.

result.setting: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, tertiary spinal surgery centre, London
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons documentation guidelines; GMC/NICE guidance

cycle1.result: Insufficient documentation of preoperative and postoperative clinical findings in spinal surgical patients; no figures given.

result.intervention: Standardised clerking proforma for surgical spinal patients.

cycle2.result: Early results suggest the proforma significantly improved admission clerking documentation; no figures given.

result.other_findings: Work remains to achieve widespread use of the proforma.

result.topic: Group and save before laparoscopic surgery
result.setting: Darent Valley Hospital, district general hospital

cycle1.result: 2 patients (0.11%) received transfusion within 72 hours of laparoscopic procedures.

result.intervention: Local trust policy changed to reduce or eliminate group and save for most elective and emergency laparoscopic procedures.
result.other_findings: Each group and save costs about £20 and 116g CO2; colorectal and gynaecological procedures excluded.

result.setting: Emergency Department; University of Edinburgh and Edinburgh Orthopaedics

cycle1.result: NV documentation pre-manipulation: ankle fractures 73%, wrist 93%; post-manipulation: ankle 31%, wrist 14%.

result.intervention: Video on NV assessment for new starters, teaching session for current staff and an electronic record shortcut for NV assessment, after staff interviews.

cycle2.result: NV documentation pre-manipulation: ankle 96%, wrist 96%; post-manipulation: ankle 46%, wrist 36%; named nerve documentation up 16.4% (p<0.05).

result.other_findings: Barriers included forgetfulness and poor induction; improvements sustained over 6 months and a third cycle is in progress.

result.setting: Cardiac surgery, St Bartholomew's Hospital, London (OR and ICU notes)
result.standard: Operation note as the standard for operation name in later documents

cycle1.result: 30% of OR notes and 9% of ICU notes accurately named the operation; urgency incorrect or missing in 2% of OR and 87% of ICU notes.

result.intervention: Standardised operation names and staff education.

cycle2.result: 84% of OR notes and 23% of ICU notes accurately named the operation; urgency incorrect or missing in 0% of OR and 29% of ICU notes.

result.other_findings: Discrepancies persisted in ICU notes, attributed to frequent staff turnover.

result.setting: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Time of recognition documented in 53%; infusion stopped and limb elevated in 67%; injury photographed in 56%; plastic surgery advice sought in 81%.

result.intervention: Hospital-specific extravasation guideline proposed; staff education and re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: Complications in 22% and surgery in 11%; incidence lower than other trusts, suggesting gaps in recognition and coding.

result.setting: Older persons' acute hospital ward, St James's Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Irish National Audit of Dementia (INAD-2) environmental checklist and national standards

cycle1.result: Reduced compliance with national standards; no figures given.

result.intervention: Orientation clocks, orientation whiteboards and increased signage and labels on the ward.

cycle2.result: Increased compliance with national standards; no figures given.

result.other_findings: Staff observed better wayfinding and orientation; infection control measures were a barrier.

result.setting: Ealing Hospital, London
result.standard: NICE, British Hernia Society and European Hernia Society guidance on prophylactic antibiotics in elective hernia repair

cycle1.result: 35/44 (79.5%) mesh repairs received prophylactic antibiotics; all laparoscopic repairs received them; 3 of 5 low-risk non-mesh open repairs received antibiotics.

result.other_findings: Clear local guidelines and documenting reasons for giving antibiotics were recommended.

result.setting: Somerset NHS Foundation Trust, Taunton
result.standard: Local guidelines for post-operative calcium management after total or completion thyroidectomy

cycle1.result: 100% had calcium checked the following morning; 58% had Calcichew-D3 recommended before surgery; 3 readmitted with hypocalcaemia.

result.intervention: Updated local guidelines, staff education session and a pre-operative pack (consent form, hypocalcaemia symptoms, Calcichew-D3 prescription if eligible).

cycle2.result: Local guidelines followed correctly in 100%; no readmissions for hypocalcaemia.

result.other_findings: Correct guideline use could save costs by avoiding unnecessary blood tests.

result.setting: Emergency general surgery, Wirral University Teaching Hospitals, district general hospital
result.standard: National Audit on Small Bowel Obstruction (NASBO)

cycle1.result: Combined 86 patients: non-operative management successful in 60%, 40% surgery; 78% of adhesional SBO with water-soluble contrast managed non-operatively.

cycle2.result: Results reported only for both cycles combined.

result.other_findings: Nutritional support documented in 76%; 37% had recurrent SBO, 80% of whom needed emergency surgery.

result.setting: Inpatient ERCP referral between two district general hospitals, NHS Lanarkshire

cycle1.result: Questionnaire (50% response): 90% dissatisfied; 45% of ERCPs delayed due to poor communication.

result.intervention: Shared online Excel Live referral database for both hospitals, with training sessions.

cycle2.result: 90% response with 100% satisfaction; only 2 patients had delayed ERCP.

result.other_findings: 95% reduction in logistical disruptions; fewer missed coagulation screens, cross-site calls and lost referrals.

result.setting: Tertiary plastic surgery centre, Queen Victoria Hospital

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Trello project management board with timelines and standardised progress checklists, overseen by a research lead.

cycle2.result: Increase in completion of closed-loop audits and research projects; no figures given.

result.other_findings: Reduced duplication and partial completion of projects.

result.setting: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust
result.standard: Target graft failure rate below 33% (for re-audit)

cycle1.result: Overall graft failure 26.1%; on anticoagulants 37.5% vs 19.6% (p=0.114); FTSG 35.7% vs SSG 17.4% (p=0.087).

result.other_findings: SCC grafts failed more than BCC (30.8% vs 16.2%, p=0.048); chloramphenicol ointment reduced failure (7.7% vs 33.9%, p=0.022).

result.setting: Lewisham and Greenwich NHS Trust, district general hospital
result.standard: BOAST guidelines for management of musculoskeletal soft tissue infections

cycle1.result: 7/86 (8.1%) confirmed septic arthritis; 2 had pre-antibiotic joint fluid cultures and 2 pre-antibiotic blood cultures; all had microscopy; 6 had arthroscopic washout; cultures in 5, histology in 1.

result.intervention: Teaching series and workshop, pathway optimisation and re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: Thirty-day mortality zero; median stay 16 days; knee 57% of cases.

result.setting: Surgical wards, Frimley Park Hospital
result.standard: Local ERAS post-operative mobility goals (4 x 60m walks)

cycle1.result: 10% of patients aware of ERAS; 77% completed the recommended 4 x 60m walks.

result.intervention: Ward-based educational posters at each bedspace and bathroom door.

cycle2.result: 46% aware of ERAS; 87% completed 4 x 60m walks; 24% increase in sitting out of bed for meals.

result.other_findings: Barriers were unfamiliarity with ERAS and inadequate analgesia; analgesia requests increased by 29%.

result.topic: Otitis externa management in emergency clinic
result.setting: Junior-led ENT emergency clinic, University Hospitals Birmingham, tertiary hospital

cycle1.result: 24/40 appointments with suspected complications or atypical features escalated appropriately, 16 had no documented escalation; antimicrobial prescribing appropriate in 78%.

result.intervention: Protocolisation and structured induction teaching proposed before second cycle.
result.other_findings: Five cases had ototoxic topical drops without documented intact tympanic membrane and one despite a documented perforation; 243 true OE cases identified.

result.topic: DNACPR and treatment escalation plan documentation
result.setting: Hospital-wide medical and surgical wards (ICU excluded), Beaumont Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Hospital DNAR and Treatment Escalation Plan policy

cycle1.result: Old DNACPR forms: 56% had a TEP.

result.intervention: New green DNACPR form (2020) with yes/no resuscitation choice and TEP moved to the front page.

cycle2.result: 15.7% (100/634) had a form, 92% stating DNAR; 99% of patients not for CPR had a TEP; doctor's name and grade documented on all forms.

result.other_findings: 2020 audit after redesign: 19% had forms (68% DNACPR, 29% for CPR) and 76% had a TEP. 83.3% of patients had no documented resuscitation status.

result.setting: Royal Devon and Exeter NHS Foundation Trust and referring peripheral units
result.standard: BSSH standards for managing open hand fractures

cycle1.result: All but 1 (who declined) received antibiotic prophylaxis; 19 (76%) washout and closure within 24 hours; antibiotics stopped at definitive closure in 3 (12%); 22 (88%) attended hand therapy.

result.other_findings: 21 patients continued antibiotics beyond 72 hours; 3 (12%) wound infections, 2 needing theatre debridement. Education and the BSSH triage app were proposed.

result.setting: Bristol Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Post-operative complications in 45.2%, including 2 anastomotic leaks; mean interval to reversal 10 months; median length of stay 6 days.

result.other_findings: Complications in 1 of 5 reversed within 6 months vs 50% when reversal interval was 7 months or more; wound infection most common (4 patients).

result.setting: General surgery; Norwich & Norfolk University Hospital and Darent Valley Hospital
result.standard: RCS Good Surgical Practice 18 key operation note criteria

cycle1.result: Baseline documentation of the 18 key criteria; no figures given.

result.intervention: Five actions to increase electronic notes, including an electronic operation note proforma and presentation at the surgical M&M meeting.

cycle2.result: Overall increase in documentation; use of electronic notes increased by 59%.

result.other_findings: Handwritten vs electronic (80 vs 78 notes): relative risk of not completing key criteria 0.461 (95% CI 0.417-0.509), p<0.0001.

result.topic: Lipase in diagnosis of acute pancreatitis
result.setting: Derriford Hospital, Plymouth, single centre

cycle1.result: Pancreatitis caused 37% of raised lipase (>78 U/L); with lipase >234 U/L (n=46), 70% pancreatitis; AUC 0.89; sensitivity 86.5%, specificity 77.4% at 3xULN.

result.other_findings: Up to 30% of patients above the 3xULN cut-off may have alternative diagnoses.

result.topic: NELA section completion on CEPOD forms
result.setting: General surgery, Portsmouth University Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit requirement to assess all emergency surgical patients for inclusion

cycle1.result: 42.7% of CEPOD forms included the completed NELA section.

result.intervention: Formal emails to surgical junior doctors, informal discussions with doctors and nurses, and posters near where CEPOD forms are collected.
result.other_findings: Newly rotated doctors lacked understanding of NELA's importance.

result.setting: Tertiary hospital theatres, University College Hospital, Ibadan

cycle1.result: Checklist used in 52.1% of surgeries (80% major, 5.4% minor); activities stopped at Time Out in 23%; Sign Out least completed.

result.other_findings: 65.4% of 81 surveyed staff had no formal SSC training; 28% who witnessed adverse events thought the SSC could have prevented them.

result.topic: Acute diverticulitis management and endoscopic follow-up
result.setting: University Hospital of North Durham
result.standard: ACPGBI emergency colorectal surgery guidelines on acute diverticulitis and follow-up endoscopy

cycle1.result: 41/106 (39%) with an indication had no follow-up endoscopy; 42/55 without an indication had endoscopy; antibiotics given to all but 2 uncomplicated patients and 85% admitted.

result.other_findings: Unindicated endoscopies cost an excess £35,202; four malignancy/high-grade dysplasia lesions found only in the indicated group.

result.setting: Elective HPB surgery, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, tertiary centre
result.standard: RCS Good Surgical Practice 2025 operative note standards plus HPB-specific fields

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 67%; operative diagnosis 18.3%, estimated blood loss 23.9%, intraoperative complications 1.4%, IOUS 40.9%.

result.intervention: EPIC SmartPhrase operation note template (hpbopnote), departmental presentations, theatre visual reminders and targeted education.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 94%; operative diagnosis 93.9%, blood loss 95.5%, complications 69.7%, IOUS 100%, Pringle's time 100%.

result.other_findings: Frozen section (21.4% to 69.2%) and ICG (28.6% to 58.3%) documentation stayed lower.

result.topic: Pus swabs and antibiotics in perianal abscess
result.setting: Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust, district general hospital
result.standard: ACPGBI consensus guidance: no routine pus swabs or antibiotics in uncomplicated perianal abscess

cycle1.result: Pus swabs taken in 70% (35/50); antibiotics given in 54% (27/50); only 6% (2/35) of cultures reviewed.

result.intervention: Targeted education to the surgical team, theatre staff engagement and guideline distribution.
result.other_findings: Antibiotic use without a clear indication remained unchanged.

result.setting: Medical wards, Cork University Hospital

cycle1.result: Mean 2.6 days from admission to physiotherapy review (7 seen same day, 3 awaiting); postural blood pressure requested in one third, mainly under geriatric services.

result.other_findings: Bone health assessment showed a similar pattern; half were on an osteoporosis agent. Weekend frailty team cover and a falls pathway were suggested.

result.setting: Elective colorectal cancer surgery, Royal Derby Hospital
result.standard: NICE and local guidelines: screen for and treat preoperative anaemia with day-case IV iron

cycle1.result: 11/40 (27.5%) anaemic; 2/11 (18%) received pre-operative iron infusion; 5/11 (45%) anaemic patients transfused post-operatively.

result.intervention: Departmental education on anaemia management and publicity of the day-case iron infusion pathway.

cycle2.result: 20/44 (45.4%) anaemic; 12/20 (60%) received iron infusion; 4/20 (20%) transfused post-operatively.

result.other_findings: 3 of the 4 transfused patients in cycle 2 had not received IV iron.

result.setting: Emergency General Surgery Unit, Northwick Park Hospital, London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE NG125 surgical site infection guideline (target 100%)

cycle1.result: Pre-op nose swab 61%, perioperative showering 44%, theatre wear 100%, jewellery removal advice 97%, informed about pre-op antibiotics 66.67%, intra-op antibiotics 14.29%, closure method 77.14%, wound dressing education 49.29%; SSI rate 6.76%.

result.other_findings: Shortfalls were attributed to communication; a checklist and patient leaflets before discharge were recommended.

result.setting: Emergency department, West Hertfordshire Teaching Hospitals, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Wound photography 52%, X-ray 73%, tetanus status considered 58%, washout 65%, dressing 73%, antibiotics 60% (all high-risk lacerations); all suspected tendon injuries (13) referred.

result.intervention: BSSH hand triage guideline implementation and second cycle planned.
result.other_findings: Poor documentation of neurovascular and tendon examination limited the audit.

result.topic: Acute kidney injury after colorectal surgery
result.setting: Prospective multicentre audits (OAKS and IMAGINE) of elective colorectal resections

cycle1.result: OAKS 7-day AKI rate 11.8% (n=346).

result.intervention: Results presented at participating centres to stimulate local quality improvement.

cycle2.result: IMAGINE 7-day AKI rate 11.5% (n=205), p=0.737; risk-adjusted AKI rate lower by 1.8% (95% CI -2.3% to -1.3%, p<0.001).

result.other_findings: Centres with a recorded local presentation showed no significant difference in later AKI rate (-0.7%, p=0.278).

result.topic: Variation in colorectal cancer surgery outcomes
result.setting: National Bowel Cancer Audit data from 145-146 hospitals

cycle1.result: Laparoscopy rate, APER, pre-operative radiotherapy and distant metastases significantly (p<0.05) affected length of stay and 18-month stoma rate.

result.other_findings: 18-month stoma rate was significantly associated with 2-year mortality.

result.setting: Major trauma centre, Cambridge University Hospitals

cycle1.result: Compliance figures not given; ORIF (7) vs tibiocalcaneal fusion (5) showed no significant difference in EQ-5D-5L (P=0.13), FAAM-ADL (P=0.20), infection (P=0.55) or time to weight bearing (P=0.39).

result.other_findings: Fifteen open talus fractures in 14 patients; fusion group had more polytrauma and Hawkins III and IV fractures.

result.setting: Surgical department, NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists guidance that requests include comprehensive relevant information

cycle1.result: 73% (52/71) of radiology requests accepted; rejections due to inappropriate imaging (4/19), duplicate requests (4/19) and insufficient clinical details (4/19), each 21%.

result.intervention: Structured request format developed and staff educated on its use.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Two theatres, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Pre-trial survey: 97.7% (74/77) of staff favourable to trying reusable gowns.

result.intervention: Disposable gowns replaced with reusable gowns in two theatres; standard gowns substituted for reinforced where appropriate; staff notified and posters on removal.

cycle2.result: 91.3% (42/46) positive feedback and 97.8% (45/46) happy to continue; 3051 gowns substituted, saving 3.292 tonnes CO2e and £366.

result.other_findings: Trust-wide scale-up estimated to save 234.7 tonnes CO2e per year.

result.setting: CAMHS, St Ann's Hospital (Haringey)
result.standard: Established standards for monitoring weight, height, blood pressure and heart rate on ADHD medication

cycle1.result: 46/50 had blood pressure, pulse, height and weight measured at every appointment; 1 had no height checks; 1 had no blood pressure or pulse at follow-up; 2 referred for shared care.

result.other_findings: A re-audit is planned.

result.setting: Luton and Dunstable University Hospital, single centre
result.standard: NICE guidance against prophylactic antibiotics in acute pancreatitis; local antimicrobial guidelines

cycle1.result: Previous audit: 74% of patients received antibiotics without clear indication.

result.intervention: Recommendations from the previous audit and improved awareness.

cycle2.result: 31 (40%) received IV antibiotics, of whom 14 (45%) had no clearly documented indication.

result.other_findings: Metronidazole was most used (58%), then amoxicillin (38.7%) and co-amoxiclav (35.4%).

result.setting: Two hospitals in South Wales
result.standard: National performance target: 10% or less undiagnostic intra-oral radiographs

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Ten two-hour radiographer training workshops (didactic and hands-on) with 52 attendees.

cycle2.result: Undiagnostic radiographs reduced by 33.2% to 6.3%, meeting the standard.

result.other_findings: 50% of radiographers rated the workshops 10/10; future cycles will use the 2020 PHE standard of no more than 5% not acceptable.

result.setting: Aneurin Bevan University Health Board, single health board

cycle1.result: 23 of 92 patients had disease recurrence at 5 years.

result.other_findings: Younger age, tumour perforation, positive nodes, CRM involvement, EMVI and post-operative complications (26%, p=0.009) were associated with recurrence.

result.setting: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust (RD&E), Exeter
result.standard: MAGIC (Management of Acute surGIcal absCesses) national audit; recommended practice from literature review (no benefit of postoperative packing; antibiotics only in specified circumstances)

cycle1.result: 22/31 had surgical intervention (17 general, 5 local anaesthetic); 18 had antibiotics before admission and 19 on admission; of the surgical cohort 19 underwent packing and 6 were discharged with antibiotics.

result.other_findings: Most common abscess type was pilonidal sinus (n=10); postoperative care varied widely, with prolonged packing and frequent postoperative antibiotics.

result.setting: East Suffolk and North Essex Foundation Trust (ESNEFT), on-call general surgery
result.standard: Trust standard: surgical referrals reviewed within 30 minutes (to support the four-hour ED standard)

cycle1.result: 33% of referrals reviewed within 30 minutes (27% in General Surgery); mean referral-to-review 1h 52m, median 1h 8m; administrative tasks 33.2% of time.

result.intervention: Advanced Nurse Practitioner introduced to General Surgery.

cycle2.result: 34% reviewed within 30 minutes; mean referral-to-review 1h 2m, median 40m; administrative tasks 24.4% of time (p = 0.045).

result.other_findings: Medical scan waiting times fell (p = 0.026); SHOs saw fewer patients within the trust guideline in cycle 2 (100% to 25%); cycle 1 also included Vascular and Urology.

result.setting: Barking, Havering and Redbridge NHS Trust, ENT operations across three sites
result.standard: RCS England Good Surgical Practice: typed operative notes on e-records compliant with RCSEng guidance

cycle1.result: 36/134 (27%) had an e-operative note.

result.intervention: Two RCSEng-compliant electronic operative note templates (generic and tonsillectomy-specific) with a user guide.
result.other_findings: E-operative notes were more likely with a registrar present (72%) than a consultant operating alone (6%); uptake of the tonsillectomy e-proforma was low (33%).

result.setting: 7th National Audit Project of the Royal College of Anaesthetists (NAP7), UK-wide

cycle1.result: 104 paediatric peri-operative cardiac arrests (12% of reports), incidence 3 in 10,000 anaesthetics (95%CI 2.2–3.3 per 10,000); quality of care judged good in 64 (62%).

result.other_findings: Incidence highest in neonates (27, 26%), infants (36, 35%) and children with congenital heart disease (44, 42%); common precipitants were severe hypoxaemia, bradycardia and major haemorrhage.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis timing for skin lesion excision
result.setting: Plastic Surgery Treatment Centre, Morriston Hospital, Swansea
result.standard: Swansea Bay guidelines: pre-operative oral antibiotic (doxycycline) prophylaxis within the recommended time frame for excision of ulcerated skin lesions

cycle1.result: Doxycycline given on average 52 minutes before the procedure; 2 patients received it after their procedure; 4 had side effects (3 vomited, 1 nausea).

result.other_findings: Trust guidelines are under review to consider alternative antibiotics.

result.setting: Tertiary care centre, Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital, oesophagogastric resection
result.standard: NICE: patients with anaemia should be offered iron therapy before and after surgery

cycle1.result: Preliminary: 71% had haemoglobin <130 g/l (men) or <120 g/l (women), but only 6.7% received any preoperative iron therapy.

result.intervention: Planned intervention to raise pre-operative haemoglobin, followed by repeat audit (not yet done).
result.other_findings: 42.8% of patients had a post-operative complication.

result.setting: Udston Hospital, community hospital with two older adult acute mental health wards, transfers from acute site
result.standard: All patients transferred should have a transfer letter

cycle1.result: 38% transferred with medical notes, 50% with no written documentation, none with a transfer letter.

result.intervention: Results discussed at the local clinical governance meeting; need for a transfer letter highlighted at a local management meeting.

cycle2.result: 88% had a transfer or discharge letter; 12% had no written documentation.

result.other_findings: Sample populations differed between cycles and samples were small.

result.setting: University Hospital Limerick, four consultant surgical teams
result.standard: Health Information and Quality Authority (HIQA) national standard for discharge summaries

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 49%; future management 20%; medications 25%; admission and discharge details 36%; clinical narrative 37%.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 69%; future management 45%; medications 59%; admission and discharge details 59%; clinical narrative 64%.

result.other_findings: Auto-populated patient details (97%) and primary care details (100%) performed best; consultants had not signed off any letters.

result.topic: Intra-operative imaging documentation in operation notes
result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics, Torbay and South Devon NHS Trust
result.standard: IR(ME)R 2017: documented clinical evaluation for each exposure to ionising radiation

cycle1.result: 87% showed clear use of ionising radiation and 60% a clear description or diagnostic implications of images.

result.intervention: Operation note template with mandatory image reporting section.

cycle2.result: 73% used the template; of these 100% showed clear use of ionising radiation and 100% a description/diagnostic implications; without the template 62.5% and 50%.

result.other_findings: 90 operation notes assessed in total; the template can be bypassed.

result.setting: General surgery inpatients (upper GI, sarcoma, colorectal), Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham
result.standard: University Hospitals Birmingham guideline: patients on regular or as-required opioids for >1 day co-prescribed stimulant and softener laxatives

cycle1.result: 35/40 (87%) prescribed opioids; 12 (34%) co-prescribed laxatives; only 6 (17%) had both stimulant and softener.

result.intervention: Planned: share results, education, encourage nursing bowel charting, then re-audit.
result.other_findings: Bowel motions charted for 26 (74%) of patients on opioids.

result.setting: GCA fast track clinic, NHS Tayside (Ninewells Hospital, Dundee)
result.standard: British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) GCA standards

cycle1.result: 70.8% seen by rheumatology within 24 hours; 50% with visual symptoms seen by ophthalmology within 24 hours; 89% given steroids within 24 hours; 80.8% had ultrasound or biopsy; written information, recurrence advice, CRP and bone protection documentation 100%.

result.other_findings: 35% diagnosed with GCA; one patient lost vision while on steroids; immediate follow-up time was 6 weeks.

result.setting: Major Trauma Centre, St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, London

cycle1.result: 46% of attendees unaware of NELA before the meeting.

result.intervention: Collaborative case-based NELA training meeting (surgery, anaesthetics, radiology).

cycle2.result: 95% confident in understanding NELA after the meeting; knowledge of NELA outcome measures rose by 25% to 95%.

result.other_findings: 100% attendee satisfaction; 96% interested in a further meeting.

result.topic: Group and save before laparoscopic cholecystectomy
result.setting: Northumbria Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, elective and emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy
result.standard: Valid group and save sample within 72 hours pre-operatively

cycle1.result: 383/571 elective and 245/265 emergency patients had a valid G&S; no elective patient required transfusion and no patient needed intra-operative transfusion.

result.other_findings: Two emergency patients needed non-urgent post-operative transfusion; authors suggest stopping routine G&S.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis compliance and SSI in hip and knee surgery
result.setting: UK trauma centre, primary hip or knee surgery (Birmingham)
result.standard: Updated perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis bundle (agent, dose, timing); SSI by CDC criteria

cycle1.result: Full antibiotic bundle compliance 74.1%; SSI rate 5.4% (n=32).

result.other_findings: SSI associated with smoking (p=0.018), HbA1c ≥58 mmol/mol (p=0.029), operative duration >120 minutes (p=0.041) and incorrect antibiotic dosing (p=0.022); alcohol-based chlorhexidine had lower SSI than povidone-iodine (p=0.037).

result.setting: Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow

cycle1.result: 8 (8%) had complications (5 hardware removal, 2 non-union or malposition, 1 infection); 6% complication rate for upper limb surgeons vs 17% for non-specialists.

result.other_findings: 83% of procedures were done by upper limb surgeons; 87.5% of complications were in smokers.

result.setting: Haematuria Clinic, single UK teaching hospital (Brighton and Sussex University Hospitals NHS Trust), two-week wait referrals
result.standard: NICE 2015 suspected cancer referral criteria (superseding BAUS 2008 haematuria guidelines)

cycle1.result: 123 (39%) referrals used BAUS 2008 criteria and 193 (61%) NICE 2015; for visible haematuria, urinary tract cancer found in 20% of NICE vs 4.4% of BAUS referrals.

result.other_findings: For non-visible haematuria, cancer was found in 2.5% of BAUS referrals and none of the NICE referrals.

result.setting: Large teaching hospital, University Hospitals Bristol and Weston Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE NG89: all patients risk-assessed for VTE on admission and re-assessed at consultant review; NHS Standard Contract

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment completion 16.67%; median time to re-assessment 97 hours.

result.intervention: Use of technology for VTE risk assessments, mandatory teaching sessions and prompts in clerking proformas.

cycle2.result: VTE risk assessment completion 100%; median time to re-assessment 21 hours.

result.other_findings: Positive feedback on the interventions was received.

result.setting: District general hospital, Wrexham Maelor Hospital
result.standard: NICE: hip fracture surgery on the day of or the day after admission

cycle1.result: 3/5 patients on warfarin for atrial fibrillation met the NICE time-to-surgery target; mean ED arrival to surgery 43.2 hours; median fracture confirmation to IV vitamin K 8 hours.

result.other_findings: Mean admission INR 2.8 and preoperative INR 1.3; all received IV vitamin K; one patient died within 30 days. Standardised warfarin protocols and staff education are recommended.

result.topic: Management of short-term insomnia in inpatients
result.setting: Adult Acute Admissions Ward, West of Scotland
result.standard: Local and national guidance: sleep hygiene advice before drugs; non-benzodiazepine hypnotic prescribed; one-off trial dose before regular prescription; target 100%

cycle1.result: Of 8 reviewed for insomnia: 12.5% (n=1) offered sleep hygiene advice; 25% (n=2) trial dose of non-benzodiazepine hypnotic; 25% (n=3) regular hypnotic with no trial dose; 50% (n=4) alternative sedative.

result.intervention: Planned: sleep hygiene leaflet, presentation of data to medical and nursing staff, guidelines made available on the ward; re-audit in six months.
result.other_findings: The cohort reviewed was 21 patients, of whom 8 were reviewed for insomnia.

result.topic: ED four-hour breaches for orthopaedic admissions
result.setting: District general hospital, Trauma and Orthopaedics (Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: 86% of T&O patients breached the four-hour target.

result.intervention: Cycle 2: updated protocols and new joint ED–T&O guidelines; cycle 3: posters asking for TTO prescriptions to be completed before 15:00.

cycle2.result: Cycle 3: 67% breached (no significant change from cycle 2, p > 0.05).

result.other_findings: Cycle 2 (n=51) breaches fell to 65% (p < 0.05); breaches due to bed shortage rose from 45% in cycle 2 to 75% in cycle 3 (p < 0.05).

result.setting: General Surgery, University Hospitals of Leicester, digital consent (Concentric)
result.standard: RCS Good Surgical Practice consent guidance

cycle1.result: Benefits and risks 100%, clinicians involved 100%, indication 87%, alternative treatment 62%, patient information leaflet with follow-up information 37%.

result.other_findings: Only 32% of elective patients (186 episodes) were consented before the day of surgery; only 52% had consent reconfirmed when >24 hours elapsed. Mandatory form fields are suggested.

result.setting: Major trauma patients, Barts Health NHS Trust (specialist major trauma ward and outlier wards)
result.standard: RCP discharge summary toolkit; target 100% completion

cycle1.result: Average completion 44.1%.

result.intervention: Standardised discharge proforma for multiply injured patients, local training and education, then further reinforcement.

cycle2.result: Third cycle: 78.92% (trauma ward 81.08% vs outlier wards 76.76%; t(50)=2.12, p=0.037).

result.other_findings: Second cycle 66.57%, with major trauma ward 73.14% vs outliers 60.00% (t(50)=5.42, p=0.000); outlier ward patients at higher risk of discharge issues.

result.setting: Chelsea and Westminster Hospital, London, elective and emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons England guidance on operative documentation

cycle1.result: Poor compliance: indications 33%, positioning 27%, skin preparation 10%, number of clips 53%, post-operative antibiotics 57%, post-operative bloods 20%, VTE prophylaxis 40%, follow-up 57%.

result.intervention: Electronic EPR template with drop-down menus, advertised by poster to registrars.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Musamedics clinic, Leicester, Plastibell circumcision
result.standard: WHO guidelines for early infant male circumcision

cycle1.result: Post-operative checks 0%; missing gestation 4%, missing Plastibell size 10%; 55% discharged within 15–30 minutes; intraoperative complications 2.5%; mean local anaesthetic 2.36 ml.

result.intervention: Cycle 1 findings presented to staff; recommendations discussed and implemented.

cycle2.result: Post-operative checks 98.3%; missing gestation 0.8%, missing Plastibell size 5.8%; 91.6% discharged within 15–30 minutes; intraoperative complications 0.8%; mean local anaesthetic 2.18 ml.

result.other_findings: Anaesthetic onset time fell from mean 4.63 to 4.36 minutes; dose variability fell (SD 0.72 to 0.48).

result.setting: Hand surgery, Lister Hospital, Stevenage (K-wire fixation)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons 2014 guidance on operative documentation, including K-wire removal timing

cycle1.result: 27% lacked K-wire removal date and 22% lacked K-wire size; other variables 98-100%.

result.intervention: Laminated posters and education; second cycle planned.
result.other_findings: Documentation of removal date and wire size were associated (p = 0.00002075, Cramér's V = 0.464).

result.topic: Mental Capacity Act and DoLS documentation
result.setting: Four Complex Medical Units (geriatric wards), John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford
result.standard: Mental Capacity Act 2005 and Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards: MCA assessment for patients with AMTS <8 or AMTS not done, DoLS if indicated

cycle1.result: 6/38 eligible patients (16%) had an MCA and 2 (5%) had a DoLS.

result.intervention: Presentation of audit findings and discussion between consultants and registrars.

cycle2.result: 15/35 eligible patients (43%) had an MCA and 5 (14%) had an appropriate DoLS.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Treatment escalation plan and DNACPR documentation
result.setting: James Cook University Hospital, unplanned general surgical admissions
result.standard: Local trust standard (with Resuscitation Council UK guidance): TEP and DNACPR documented within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Ceiling-of-care decisions documented in 18% (n=54); only 6% (n=18) had TEP or DNACPR documented within 24 hours; DNACPR present in 12% (n=36), 40% of which lacked clear clerking documentation.

result.intervention: Planned: structured training for junior doctors and strengthened admission proformas, then re-audit.
result.other_findings: 68% had CCI ≥4; among hospital DNACPR orders only half were timely.

result.setting: Male secure rehabilitation ward
result.standard: Electronic admission documentation of substance use history

cycle1.result: 7/12 patients asked about substance misuse at admission review; 5 not asked.

result.other_findings: 11/12 met ICD-10 harmful use of illegal substances and 9 harmful use of alcohol; reasons and attitudes for use were rarely explored.

result.setting: HPB surgery, Manchester Royal Infirmary (Manchester Foundation Trust), liver resection
result.standard: NICE guidance on risks and additional procedures for liver resection; GMC Good Medical Practice

cycle1.result: Paper consent forms (baseline); numbers per item not reported.

result.intervention: Electronic patient record (HIVE) consent, then 'smart texts' automated consent forms.

cycle2.result: After smart texts, 14 of the risks and additional procedures improved further; 15 of 20 had already improved after moving to HIVE (n=29).

result.other_findings: Particularly marked increase in documenting drains, lines and catheter insertion.

result.setting: Chest drain clinic, Department of Thoracic Surgery, City Hospital, Nottingham

cycle1.result: 64% needed only one clinic visit before drain removal; 1,038 bed days saved; 7.2% re-admitted with complications.

result.other_findings: Estimated cost saving about £361,200.

result.setting: District general hospital, West Suffolk Hospital, surgical staff
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons core criteria for safe handover (13 criteria)

cycle1.result: Mean total compliance score 44.6%; shortcomings in operational issues and resuscitation status.

result.intervention: Structured RCS-aligned handover proforma (later incorporated into the electronic system).

cycle2.result: Mean total compliance score 70.2% (p<0.001), improved across all criteria.

result.other_findings: Biggest gains were in admission date, existing management plans and outstanding tasks; data came from staff questionnaires.

result.setting: Trauma meeting, Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester
result.standard: Eight documentation standards: consultant on-call, consultants present, imaging discussed, MDT concerns, diagnosis, laterality, clear plan, weight-bearing status

cycle1.result: Only 64% of cases discussed had documentation.

result.intervention: Structured electronic smart-phrase proforma, adjusted after MDT feedback.

cycle2.result: 88% of cases discussed were documented; all eight standards improved.

result.other_findings: PDSA 2 (n=98) documented 94%; lack of consultant time to complete documentation was highlighted.

result.setting: Consultant-led general medical and specialist geriatric clinic, Wexford General Hospital
result.standard: National protocol for outpatient waiting list management; Clinically Recommended Timeframe (CRT)

cycle1.result: 94% seen within the CRT; both urgent referrals (2) not seen within the CRT; median waitlist 15.5 weeks.

result.other_findings: 11 (16.4%) did not attend, only 3 cancelling beforehand; 8 (11.9%) had duplicate referrals to a second point of contact.

result.setting: General surgery inpatients, Northwick Park Hospital (London district general hospital)
result.standard: NICE: complete medicines reconciliation within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.dates: First three weeks of October to December 2020
cycle1.result: 38.0% had incomplete reconciliation.

result.intervention: Sequential: baseline data presented at a team meeting with posters; pharmacists flagging missing medicines on the daily jobs list; medicines reconciliation ward round.

cycle2.result: 2.8% incomplete after the medicines reconciliation ward round (p=0.001).

result.other_findings: Presentation and posters reduced incompletion to 23.4% (n=64, p=0.037); pharmacist flagging did not help further (23.0%, n=74, p>0.999); one significant harm in week 1.

result.setting: Acute Medical Unit, Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Regular hydration assessment 10%; appropriate resuscitation fluid 32%; maintenance fluid when indicated 52%; correct maintenance composition 0%.

result.intervention: Findings presented at a local meeting, posters and regular teaching on safe IV fluid prescribing.

cycle2.result: Regular hydration assessment 28%; appropriate resuscitation 66%; maintenance fluid when indicated 84%; correct composition 15%.

result.other_findings: Compliance remained low despite improvement.

result.setting: General Surgery, University Hospital of North Durham, nil-by-mouth patients
result.standard: NICE recommendations for maintenance IV fluids in nil-by-mouth patients

cycle1.result: Significant lack of potassium and glucose prescribing.

result.intervention: Teaching sessions for FY1/2 doctors and posters on surgical wards.

cycle2.result: 82% met daily water, 94% sodium and 96% chloride requirements; only 24% met glucose and 16% potassium requirements.

result.other_findings: Increases of 40%, 10% and 11% in water, sodium and chloride adherence; 55% and 54% rises in glucose- and potassium-containing bags.

result.setting: District general hospital (Blackpool)

cycle1.result: 236 (45.6%) had surgery; negative appendicectomy rate 10.6% (n = 25).

result.other_findings: Of 25 normal appendices, 17 had prior imaging (7 suggested appendicitis); readmission after negative appendicectomy was 20%, all female.

result.setting: Emergency general surgery, Kingston Hospital NHS Foundation Trust (district general hospital)
result.standard: European Society of Coloproctology 2020 guidelines (including no routine antibiotics)

cycle1.result: 97% had CT and 100% received IV antibiotics; only 57% referred for outpatient lower GI endoscopy.

result.other_findings: Mean length of stay 3.7 days for uncomplicated vs 9.3 days for complicated disease, suggesting a role for ambulatory care.

result.setting: District general hospital, Antrim Area Hospital
result.standard: National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction (NASBO) recommendations: early CT, water-soluble contrast, early nutritional assessment and specialist input

cycle1.result: CT 88%; water-soluble contrast 12%; average days to CT 0.18; no oral intake >5 days 44%; parenteral nutrition 6%.

result.intervention: Findings presented at an audit and governance meeting, reiterating NASBO recommendations.

cycle2.result: CT 94%; water-soluble contrast 44%; average days to CT 0.43; no oral intake >5 days 17%; parenteral nutrition 17%.

result.other_findings: AXR plus CT rose from 75% to 88%; nutritional assessment did not improve (malnourished identified 6% then 5%).

result.setting: Frimley Park Hospital, elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy
result.standard: GIRFT: anticipated day case rate 90%, plus recommended technique (e.g. low pressure insufflation 10mmHg, no drains)

cycle1.result: Day case rate 45% (58 of 107 stayed overnight); no surgeon documented pneumoperitoneum pressure.

result.other_findings: 34% of overnight stays had no clinical indication, mostly patient preference or delayed recovery.

result.setting: Leighton Hospital, Crewe, ureteric stent database
result.standard: Trust stent database documenting insertion and removal dates

cycle1.result: 173 (42.5%) had no documented stent outcome; 16 overdue stents, 12 already listed; two patients missed completely.

result.other_findings: Missing outcomes mostly followed removal in flexible cystoscopy lists or clinics without database update; a designated person for database maintenance is suggested.

result.setting: Stroke ward, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham
result.standard: All new stroke admissions to have IPC applied by the post-take consultant ward round unless contraindicated

cycle1.result: 21.6% did not have IPC applied on time.

result.intervention: Posters in doctors' offices and nursing bases reminding staff to prescribe and apply IPC.

cycle2.result: 18.1% did not have IPC applied on time (3.5% improvement).

result.other_findings: Timely prescribing by doctors improved by 5.9% but nursing application worsened by 2.2%.

result.setting: ENT department, Pinderfields Hospital, Wakefield
result.standard: Good Surgical Practice; Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (ten key items) and VTE risk assessment

cycle1.result: Referral source 28%, consultant in charge 35%, name/grade/bleep 25%, VTE risk assessment 14%.

cycle2.result: Referral source 97%, consultant in charge 90%, name/grade/bleep 94%, VTE risk assessment 78%.

result.other_findings: All parameters improved; trainee response was positive.

result.setting: London major trauma centre (Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust), non-local ambulatory orthopaedic trauma patients
result.standard: BOAST Fracture Clinic Services and trust recommendations

cycle1.result: Named local trust 65%; phone referral 94%; name of doctor taking referral 24%; local on-call consultant's name 6%; repatriation letter sent 0%.

result.intervention: First: departmental guidelines (referral pathway, electronic repatriation letter template, patient e-leaflet); second: educational posters and a doctor tutorial.

cycle2.result: Named local trust 89%; phone referral 100%; name of doctor 94%; on-call consultant's name 83%; letter sent 94%; letter uploaded 89%.

result.other_findings: Second cycle (n=25): named trust 96%, doctor's name 88%, consultant 48%, letter sent 92%, letter uploaded 40%.

result.topic: Time to ERCP in acute gallstone cholangitis
result.setting: UK district general hospital (Princess Alexandra Hospital, Harlow)
result.standard: NICE: ERCP within 72 hours for acute gallstone cholangitis

cycle1.result: Median time to ERCP 10 days (5–24); moderate-to-severe 8 days (5–19); mild 28 days (9–46).

result.intervention: Results presented to the surgical MDT; referral pathways to 3 nearby tertiary centres for ERCP.

cycle2.result: Median time to ERCP 6 days (4–9); moderate-to-severe 6 days (6–8); mild 4 days (4–25).

result.other_findings: 41 patients in total; median length of stay fell from 8 (6–13) to 7 days (4–10).

result.topic: CT versus operative findings in emergency laparotomy
result.setting: George Eliot NHS Trust Hospital, Nuneaton (General & GI Surgery and Radiology)

cycle1.result: Discrepancy rate 27.2%, 11.4% major; only 23% of reports completed within 24 hours.

result.intervention: Recommendations to improve pre-operative communication and radiologist expertise.

cycle2.result: Discrepancy rate 5.8%, of which 21.1% major and 73.7% minor.

result.other_findings: Age, gender and reporting type were not associated with discrepancy (p > 0.05); discrepancies were linked to complex conditions.

result.setting: UK district general hospital, Maidstone & Tunbridge Wells NHS Trust, patients under 18
result.standard: Locally defined standard: blocks under the shorter limb where there is clear leg length discrepancy, equal pelvic height and patella facing forwards

cycle1.result: 116/243 (48%) performed with patella facing forwards; of 110 patients needing blocks, none had them used.

result.other_findings: 133/243 radiographs were for reasons other than leg length discrepancy.

result.setting: Fracture Liaison Service, Sligo General Hospital (level 3 university hospital)
result.standard: Royal Osteoporosis Society FLS clinical standards: patients over 50 with a new fragility fracture offered axial DXA within 12 weeks of diagnosis

cycle1.result: 598 (70.6%) recommended to the GP to order DXA; 8 (0.94%) booked by FLS; 133 (15.70%) already had DXA; 26 (3.07%) DXA not necessary; 1 (0.12%) booked by the clinical team.

result.other_findings: Authors believe reliance on GPs to order DXA causes delay.

result.setting: Orthopaedic department, Lister Hospital, Stevenage
result.standard: BOAST 11 standards for paediatric supracondylar humerus fractures (Gartland 2 or 3)

cycle1.result: Baseline compliance with BOAST 11 domains; figures not reported.

result.intervention: Information booklet distributed to all doctors in the department.

cycle2.result: Compliance improved in five domains: neurovascular assessment documented in clerking improved by 28%; 2mm K-wire use documented improved by 23%.

result.other_findings: Compliance with surgery within 24 hours regressed, thought to reflect COVID-19 measures.

result.setting: Multi-centre district general hospital, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust (A&E and urology)
result.standard: BAUS 2018 guidance on acute ureteric colic, including clinic follow-up within 4 weeks

cycle1.result: Baseline figures not reported separately.

result.intervention: Teaching sessions for doctors and nurses in A&E and urology.

cycle2.result: Serum calcium 60.4%, CT KUB within 24 hours 97.7%, NSAIDs 67.2% (increases of 20.4%, 0.4% and 5.2%); only 26.4% seen in clinic within 4 weeks, mean wait 41 days.

result.other_findings: Only 31.3% had acute surgical intervention; a daily emergency theatre slot and computerised clinic booking are recommended.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis for transperineal prostate biopsy
result.setting: Taunton and Somerset NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 1 patient presented with sepsis within 28 days (infection rate 0.5%); no GP presentations or community antibiotics within 28 days.

result.other_findings: Audit followed a Trust decision to stop routine antibiotic prophylaxis.

result.setting: Vascular surgery, Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, patients aged 65 and over
result.standard: Centre for Perioperative Care: daily delirium screening with a validated tool such as the 4-AT in patients 65 and over

cycle1.result: 4-AT screening in only 39.2% (n=20), on average 90 hours post-operatively; never documented in consultant-led post-operative review (100%, n=51).

result.intervention: Recommended: stakeholder discussion, the mantra 'Post-op bloods and 4AT', and education on the 4-AT proforma.
result.other_findings: Delirium concerns documented 7 times, with 4-AT documented in 5 of these.

result.setting: Regional trainee-led orthopaedic network, Birmingham

cycle1.result: 17 of 19 students responded; mean improvement in understanding of audit 1.18±1.07 (p<0.001) and ability to conduct an audit 1.77±1.15 (p<0.001).

result.other_findings: 80% of responding supervisors had inactive projects; all were happy with student work.

result.setting: General surgical ward, Sri Jayewardenepura General Hospital
result.standard: Guideline recommendations for documenting urinary catheterisation

cycle1.result: Only 2% had complete documentation.

result.intervention: Printed catheterisation documentation form filed in patients' notes.
result.other_findings: 50 patients were included in total.

result.topic: Risk scoring and imaging in suspected appendicitis
result.setting: District general hospital, Wexham Park Hospital, Frimley NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: WSES (adults) and GIRFT (children) guidance: risk score all suspected appendicitis to guide imaging

cycle1.result: No adult had a risk score documented; 2 (9%) children had one; 9/46 (20%) imaged adults were low risk; 34/46 (74%) had CT first line.

result.other_findings: 6/13 children who had ultrasound were high-risk males recommended for diagnostic laparoscopy without imaging.

result.topic: Emergency cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
result.setting: Urban acute trust, Barking, Havering & Redbridge NHS Trust
result.standard: National guidelines on early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease

cycle1.result: 49 patients had LC, only 20% performed acutely; 70% of acute operations were during re-admissions.

result.intervention: Hot cholecystectomy list opened to other surgeons and acute LC encouraged on the emergency theatre list.

cycle2.result: 21% underwent LC, of which 52% were acute operations; 50% of emergency operations were in re-admissions.

result.other_findings: Average wait from admission to LC in the initial cohort was 118.5 days; provision still does not comply with national guidelines.

result.topic: GLP-1 receptor agonist use in surgical patients
result.setting: Surgical Observation Unit, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh (NHS Lothian)

cycle1.result: Biliary colic most common diagnosis (23/91, 25.3%); 82/91 (90.1%) on tirzepatide; 35/57 (61.4%) stopped their GLP-1RA.

result.other_findings: Only 28/57 (49.1%) had complete symptom resolution and 19/57 (33.3%) received support or safety netting from their drug provider.

result.topic: Major lower limb amputation perioperative care
result.setting: Sunderland Royal Hospital

cycle1.result: 100% consultant review <24h and antibiotic/VTE prophylaxis; below:above-knee ratio 2:1; only 67% operated <48h of decision; 45% of diabetic patients seen by diabetes team; 29% physio reviewed pre-operatively; 0% received formal information.

result.intervention: Patient information leaflet and enhanced MDT pathways implemented; re-audit underway.
result.other_findings: Stump complications 20%; length of stay >30 days in 44%; 6-month mortality 22%.

result.setting: District general hospital, ED and surgery, children aged 6-18 (Frimley Park Hospital)
result.standard: Local 2017 policy: children aged 6-18 with acute abdominal pain reviewed by ED registrar/consultant with a documented Alvarado score

cycle1.result: Negative appendicectomy rate 28%.

result.intervention: Cycle 1 recommendations (better ultrasound quality, more CT) discussed at the M&M meeting.

cycle2.result: Only 36% had a documented Alvarado score and 55% a senior ED review; negative appendicectomy rate 11%.

result.other_findings: Only 2 patients had CT; Alvarado specificity was 14.29%; an ambulatory pathway for children has since been introduced.

result.setting: Breast surgery, Dartford & Gravesham NHS Trust
result.standard: Association of Breast Surgery Summary Statement (2015) on operative notes (17 parameters)

cycle1.result: 7/17 parameters failed to meet the standard; 61% (19/31) of notes electronic.

result.intervention: Electronic operative note proforma based on recommendations and MDT feedback.

cycle2.result: 1/17 parameters failed to meet the standard; 97% (32/33) electronic; 52% (17/33) used the proforma.

result.other_findings: 63% (5/8) of nurses surveyed found handwritten notes often illegible.

result.setting: University Hospital Limerick, tertiary referral centre
result.standard: World Society of Emergency Surgery (WSES) Jerusalem guidelines 2020 for investigation, diagnosis and management of acute appendicitis

cycle1.result: Clinical scores documented in 2.6% (n=1); CT 33.3% (n=13), ultrasound 33.3% (n=13), no imaging 33.3% (n=13); 100% managed surgically; average time to theatre 16.9 hours; 100% had histopathology; negative appendicectomy 15.4% (n=6).

result.other_findings: Compliant for timely surgery and routine histopathology; 74.4% laparoscopic, 23.1% open; average length of stay 3.6 days. An educational intervention on clinical scoring systems was proposed.

result.topic: Renal replacement therapy after cardiac surgery
result.setting: Northern General Hospital, Sheffield, adult cardiac surgery
result.standard: GIRFT 2018 benchmark RRT rate (1.56%) and NICOR data (isolated CABG 0.98–1.45%)

cycle1.result: 90 of 3,261 patients required RRT (1.14%), below the GIRFT benchmark of 1.56%; isolated CABG RRT rate 2.76%, higher than NICOR reports (0.98–1.45%).

result.other_findings: Mortality was higher in the RRT group (33.3% vs 2.2%, p < 0.0001), with longer stays (38.41 vs 15.91 days) and more reoperations (6.7% vs 1.6%). Lower preoperative eGFR, CVA, higher EuroSCORE and complex surgery predicted RRT.

result.setting: University Hospitals Bristol and Weston NHS Foundation Trust, single centre

cycle1.result: Oesophageal perforation 0/21 after robotic HC vs 3/21 (14.3%) after laparoscopic HC; no conversions; no mortality.

result.other_findings: All perforations needed ITU admission and return to theatre, with mean stay 46 days. Other morbidity in 2/21 (9.5%) laparoscopic cases.

result.setting: Two adult inpatient psychiatric wards (Clark Ward and Beamshaw Ward), South West Yorkshire Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust standard: inpatient discharge summary completed within 24 hours of discharge; compliance threshold >91%

cycle1.result: 76% (n=38) completed within 24 hours; 24% (n=12) delayed, below the >91% threshold.

result.other_findings: Most common cause of delay was an unclear EPMA discharge process, with summaries signed off but not finalised (n=5). Recommended reinforcing EPMA processes, MDT-linked updates, proactive review of anticipated discharges and visible guidance.

result.setting: Salford Royal Hospital
