cycle1.result: Median time to neurosurgical advice 229 minutes (IQR 60-690); mortality 24%; median length of stay 4 days (IQR 3-13.5).

result.intervention: Head injury proforma and care of the elderly input.

cycle2.result: Median time to neurosurgical advice 80 minutes (IQR 40-120, P < 0.05); mortality 14%; median length of stay 3 days (IQR 2-4).

result.other_findings: Main cause of delay was inadequate information transfer; estimated saving of £14,043 per quarter in bed occupancy.

result.setting: Emergency and elective general surgery, Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: GIRFT and PHE recommendations on SSI surveillance; CDC SSI definition

cycle1.result: 153/699 (21.8%) flagged as probable infection; 20/153 (13%) true infection; wound assessment clearly documented in 86/153 (56%).

result.intervention: Electronic SSI bundle to standardise documentation.
result.other_findings: Median length of stay with true infection 15 days; 12/20 infections after emergency surgery.

result.topic: Body scheme signs predicting healthcare use after fracture
result.setting: Plaster room, Cambridge University Hospitals

cycle1.result: 3/44 (7%) had both finger perception and body scan abnormalities and used more analgesia and healthcare resources; cost difference about £530 per patient.

result.other_findings: Estimated annual cost of £175,000 for the trust.

result.setting: Tertiary referral centre, Karolinska University Hospital, Stockholm

cycle1.result: 23 robotic vs open: bleeding 550 ml vs 2085 ml (P < 0.001); Clavien-Dindo > II 17% vs 34%; R0 in all robotic colorectal cases.

result.other_findings: One robotic case (4%) was converted to open.

result.setting: ENT inpatients, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Completion of standardised treatment escalation planning form for inpatients

cycle1.result: TEP forms completed 0%; in-hospital DNACPR 23%; community DNACPR 0%.

result.intervention: Staff education and physical reminders on handover documentation.
result.other_findings: One patient had a community DNACPR not converted to an inpatient DNACPR.

result.setting: ENT ward, Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast
result.standard: Documentation of nasogastric tube position after X-ray confirmation using the NGT documentation sticker (Never Event prevention)

cycle1.result: Sticker used 42.1%; patient identity verified 39.5%; most recent X-ray confirmed 44.7%; time and date verified 34.2%; NGT position documented 63.1%; feeding instructions 65.8%; confirming staff recorded 60.5%.

result.intervention: Teaching doctors to use the sticker supplied with each NGT pack, ward posters, and reminding nurses to check documentation before feeding.

cycle2.result: Sticker used 85%; identity verified 100%; most recent X-ray 100%; time and date 85%; position documented 75%; feeding instructions 75%; confirming staff 75%.

result.other_findings: 58 chest X-rays were reviewed in total across both cycles.

result.topic: Time to mitomycin C after nephroureterectomy
result.setting: Single tertiary centre, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow
result.standard: EAU guidelines: MMC instillation 2–10 days after radical nephroureterectomy

cycle1.result: Laparoscopic RNU: average time to MMC 14 days (SD 6.7); average length of stay 5 days; bladder recurrence 41% (n = 14).

result.intervention: Expansion of the robotic-assisted RNU service.

cycle2.result: Robotic RNU: average time to MMC 2 days (SD 0.57); average length of stay 4 days; bladder recurrence 30% (n = 8).

result.other_findings: Follow-up was longer in the laparoscopic cohort (30.6 vs 13 months).

result.setting: Breast unit, East Lancashire Hospitals Trust, Blackburn
result.standard: Association of Breast Surgery margin guidance; national re-excision rates of 13% (invasive) and 22% (DCIS)

cycle1.result: Re-excision rate 15.1% (31/205) for invasive disease and 33.3% (9/27) for DCIS.

result.other_findings: 7.5% needed more than one re-excision; some chose completion mastectomy.

result.setting: Virtual fracture clinic, Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Glasgow virtual fracture clinic pathway: simple stable fractures discharged directly from ED with advice and telephone support

cycle1.result: 21% of VFC referrals were simple stable fractures suitable for direct ED discharge; 22.1% of VFC first attendances discharged without change in management versus 19.4% of 529 physical fracture clinic first attendances.

result.other_findings: Suggested closer collaboration between orthopaedics and ED to improve referral quality.

result.setting: Multi-specialty surgery, district general hospital, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: National targets: SSI rate < 1% after clean and < 10% after clean-contaminated surgery

cycle1.result: Overall SSI rate 14.5% (n = 138); general surgery 18.1% (45/249), elective 12.84% and emergency 22.14%; paediatric surgery 4.3% (2/47).

result.intervention: Oxford 8-point SSI reduction bundle implemented; re-audit scheduled for 2023.
result.other_findings: 38 SSIs were found only by follow-up telephone calls; in orthopaedics procedure type correlated with SSI (Rs 0.961, P < 0.001).

result.setting: Abdominal wall reconstruction pathway, Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust; single centre

cycle1.result: Estimated carbon footprint about 669.56 kgCO2eq per patient; inpatient stay 558.0 kgCO2eq (83.3%).

result.other_findings: Suggested ERAS, better waste segregation and continued TIVA to reduce emissions.

result.topic: Gallstone pancreatitis time to definitive treatment
result.setting: Ulster Hospital Dundonald, Belfast
result.standard: BSG guidelines: definitive management of gallstone pancreatitis during index admission or within 2 weeks

cycle1.result: Non-COVID 2019 cohort: 30% (n = 7 of 23) had definitive management within index admission or 2 weeks; first-wave COVID-19 2020 cohort: 64.7% (n = 11 of 17).

result.other_findings: Patients not treated within 2 weeks during COVID-19 waited longer and had more readmissions.

result.setting: General surgery and gynaecology theatre lists at nine hospital sites across Northern Ireland; prospective multicentre audit
result.standard: National benchmarking target of 15 minutes theatre turnaround

cycle1.result: Mean overall turnaround 37.7 mins (SD 15.4), above the 15-minute target; cleaning 8.11 mins, extubation 5.11 mins, scrub 4.7 mins.

result.other_findings: Turnaround was longer in general surgery than gynaecology; no difference between trusts in delayed list starts (p=0.2703).

result.setting: General surgery inpatients, Prince Digna Referral Hospital, Port Sudan
result.standard: NICE recommendation to document diabetic foot ulcers with a standardised system such as SINBAD

cycle1.result: Site 65%, ischaemia 41%, neuropathy 0%, bacterial infection 35%, area 58%, depth 35%; no notes used a standardised system.

result.intervention: Staff training and a SINBAD-based documentation template.
result.other_findings: Neuropathy assessment was limited by lack of monofilament testing.

result.setting: Emergency general surgery unit, Wirral University Teaching Hospital

cycle1.result: 107 (93%) managed on a rib fracture pathway; 37 (32%) pulmonary complications; 8 (7%) died.

result.other_findings: Median length of stay 3 days under 65 versus 6.5 days over 65 (p = 0.00144).

result.setting: Thoracic surgery inpatients, Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Birmingham
result.standard: Departmental guideline: remove chest drain stitches 5–7 days after drain removal

cycle1.result: Compliance 20.8% (24 drains/stitches); stitches in place 6–44 days (median 10.5 days).

result.intervention: Date of drain removal documented on the electronic medical record with a recommended stitch removal range.

cycle2.result: Compliance 54.5% (22 drains/stitches); stitches in place 4–18 days (median 7 days).

result.other_findings: Bleeding, difficulty or abandoned stitch removal occurred in two cases in cycle 1 and fewer in cycle 2.

result.topic: Infection risk management before flexible cystoscopy
result.setting: Diagnostic and therapeutic flexible cystoscopy across one NHS trust (St George's, London)

cycle1.result: Urinalysis performed and recorded in 227 appointments; 18 asymptomatic patients nitrite positive, 9 of whom were cancelled; no symptomatic patient had cystoscopy; 72 appointments had no infection safety netting documented.

result.other_findings: Infection was the most common reason a cystoscopy did not go ahead.

result.setting: General surgery department, Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines on information for patients with acute pancreatitis and their families

cycle1.result: 60% not satisfied with information; none given written information; over 90% not shown a diagram; not informed about investigations 40%, treatment 60%, alcohol as a cause 27%.

result.intervention: Results shared with surgical team; patient information leaflet designed and given to every patient with acute pancreatitis.

cycle2.result: Improvement in almost all areas; satisfaction improved from 60% to 92%.

result.other_findings: No patient leaflets were available before the intervention.

result.setting: Large district general hospital, Whiston Hospital, Prescot
result.standard: Use of the acute abdomen pathway proforma for patients meeting its criteria

cycle1.result: Only 4 of 112 eligible patients were started on the pathway; with the proforma, CT request to report 5 hours (from 14), triage to diagnosis 5 hours (from 12), triage to management 5 hours (from 13).

result.intervention: Planned: raise awareness of the pathway and re-audit.
result.other_findings: 65 (58%) of the 112 had an acute abdomen diagnosis; 390 patients were screened.

result.setting: General surgery department, district general hospital, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidance on confirming NG tube position by aspirate pH testing or X-ray if indeterminate

result.other_findings: No NG tube complications occurred.

result.topic: Mental Health Act capacity assessment documentation
result.setting: Vales Ward, Discovery House (LPFT); psychiatric inpatient unit
result.standard: Mental Health Act 1983: capacity to consent assessed on admission and at three months for Section 3 patients

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment at admission documented in 46.2% (6/13); three-month reassessment in 7.7% (1/13).

result.intervention: Planned: automated RiO reminders, targeted staff education and patient information leaflets; re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Breast unit, East Lancashire Hospitals Trust (Burnley Hospital)
result.standard: not reported (compared with average reported sensitivity and specificity)

cycle1.result: Sensitivity 69.69%; specificity 86.54%; diagnostic accuracy 69.75%; false-negative rate 18.18%; inadequate reports 12.3%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Plastic surgery procedure room (elective skin lesion excision), Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals
result.standard: Local consensus of the consultant body on consenter details, form completion and documented risks (no standard guidelines)

cycle1.result: All consenters documented job title, signed and dated; 100% used correct form, documented procedure, site and risks and labelled every page; intended benefits 83%; procedure name in full 58%; risks documented: bleeding and infection 100%, pain 54%, re-excision 75%, recurrence and wound breakdown 71%, scarring 96%, injury to surrounding structures 46%, anaesthetic risk 0%.

result.other_findings: All FTSG patients had graft loss documented as a risk.

result.topic: Genetic testing for hereditary diffuse gastric cancer
result.setting: Upper GI cancer MDT, Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: CDH1 testing criteria for patients with diffuse type gastric cancer

cycle1.result: 12/17 (70%) referred to clinical genetics; 10 (58%) had CDH1 testing; 3 pathogenic mutations.

result.intervention: Standard operating procedure for mainstream CDH1 testing within the UGI cancer service, with oncology and clinical genetics.

cycle2.result: 13/15 (87%) seen at the institution had mainstream CDH1 testing; 3 pathogenic mutations; only 2/10 (20%) seen at peripheral centres were referred.

result.other_findings: 7 patients before the SOP had no histological subtype recorded.

result.setting: Elective inguinal hernia repair, large tertiary centre, The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidance on routine preoperative tests by ASA grade

cycle1.result: Poor overall compliance with NICE guidelines (figures not given).

result.intervention: Results presented locally; updated trust guidance and a digital decision-aid tool.

cycle2.result: ASA 1 unnecessary tests fell by 20.5% (FBC), 21.4% (haemostasis), 22.6% (U&E), 33.0% (ECG); ASA 2 fell by 75.0%, 16.7%, 11.9% and 9.4%.

result.other_findings: No lung function tests or ABG in either cycle; cycle 2 was limited to one of the trust's two hospitals.

result.setting: Orthopaedic department, Royal Surrey County Hospital, Guildford (elective hip and knee arthroplasty)
result.standard: Hospital perioperative arthroplasty protocol: regular opioids plus regular non-opioid analgesics plus PRN analgesia (score 3)

cycle1.result: 34% achieved protocol-standard analgesia (score 3).

result.intervention: Elective arthroplasty protocol powerplan implemented in the Surrey Safe Care electronic patient record.

cycle2.result: 61% achieved score 3; 87% of those adherent used the powerplan.

result.other_findings: A subset of patients still did not receive recommended analgesia; 20 knee and 31 hip arthroplasties in cycle 2.

result.setting: International multicentre cohort (Oesophagogastric Anastomosis Audit)

cycle1.result: 90-day mortality 5% after CROSS vs 1% after FLOT (p=0.005); pCR 18% vs 10% (p=0.004); margin-negative resection 93% vs 76% (p<0.001).

result.other_findings: Higher CROSS mortality was linked to pulmonary (74% vs 60%) and cardiac (42% vs 20%) complications.

result.setting: Large urology centre, North Manchester General Hospital
result.standard: 2016 Laboratory Guidelines for Post-vasectomy Semen Analysis (British Andrology Society) for clearance

cycle1.result: 132 (51.6%) had PVSA at median 16.4 weeks; 71 (54.5%) cleared, 45 (63.4%) after a single PVSA; 7 (9.9%) special clearance; 2 (1.5%) not cleared despite meeting special clearance criteria.

result.other_findings: 33 patients (25%) had at least one sample rejected, mainly for timing or incomplete request forms; clearance letters issued at median 2.7 weeks.

result.topic: Frailty assessment in older breast clinic patients
result.setting: New patient breast clinic, Bolton Breast Unit, Royal Bolton Hospital
result.standard: NABCOP fitness assessment form to be completed for all patients aged 70 or over at first breast clinic attendance

cycle1.result: 0% compliance.

result.intervention: Results presented and staff teaching; forms re-printed on yellow paper; nurses highlight patients aged 70 or over on clinic lists.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Single site acute hospital, Royal Alexandra Hospital, Paisley
result.standard: UK negative appendicectomy rate estimated at 20%; comparison with previous local study

cycle1.result: Preoperative imaging 69%; NAR 10.3%.

result.intervention: not reported (increased preoperative cross-sectional imaging since 2019)

cycle2.result: Preoperative imaging 88% (mostly CT); NAR 3% (histology available in 84).

result.other_findings: 22% had normal WCC and 22% normal CRP on admission; imaging and operative findings agreed on nature of appendicitis in 76%.

result.topic: Frailty and outcomes in older inpatients
result.setting: Endocrinology service, tertiary hospital, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Frail patients (n=23) had longer mean LOS (49.5 vs 19.0 days, p = 0.035) and more change in care needs (56.5% vs 14.3%, p = 0.008).

result.other_findings: Discharge to long-term care 21.7% vs 14.3% (p = 0.19).

result.setting: Elective colorectal resections, North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local Enhanced Recovery after Surgery (ERAS) protocol

cycle1.result: not reported (baseline compliance figures not given).

result.intervention: Staff education and a postoperative ERAS booklet completed during the inpatient stay.

cycle2.result: Oral nutritional supplements, deep breathing, oral fluids and stoma care plans all above 90% compliance; average length of stay fell from 9 to 6 days between cycles 2 and 3.

result.other_findings: Three cycles over two years (30 patients); discharge planning documented in under 50% and mobilisation quantified in under 50%.

result.setting: Emergency and trauma theatres, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Local policy: preoperative hair removal in the anaesthetic room

cycle1.result: 6/15 (40%) shaved in the anaesthetic room; general surgery 2/9 (22%), trauma and orthopaedics 2/4 (50%).

result.intervention: Results presented to surgical leadership and SSI steering groups, information disseminated to teams, and posters on hair removal location.

cycle2.result: 9/12 (75%) shaved in the anaesthetic room; general surgery 7/9 (78%), trauma and orthopaedics 1/1 (100%).

result.other_findings: SSI rates were not measured.

result.topic: Public understanding of surgeon outcome data
result.setting: In-person survey at a state fair (Department of Urology, University of Minnesota)

cycle1.result: 142 (40.6%) correctly estimated the complication rate; 7.6% recognised it was above the 99th percentile.

result.other_findings: Misinterpreters were more likely to make an inappropriate hypothetical decision (OR 2.75).

result.setting: Great Western Hospital, Swindon; district general hospital
result.standard: GIRFT 2019 hip and knee arthroplasty best practice documentation data items

cycle1.result: 26 THR and 23 knee arthroplasties; average compliance knee 71%, THR 68%.

result.intervention: Clinician education and discussion of the guidelines among local surgeons.

cycle2.result: 34 THR and 28 knee arthroplasties; average compliance knee 74%, THR 64%.

result.other_findings: 100% compliance in 5/23 THR and 9/27 knee criteria; range of movement and vascular status at end of surgery improved least.

result.topic: Early mobilisation of stable distal radius fractures
result.setting: Orthopaedic team receiving virtual fracture clinic referrals (Chelsea & Westminster Hospital, London; Worthing Hospital)
result.standard: BOAST guideline for distal radius fractures: patients with a stable fracture should be considered for early mobilisation with a removable support once pain allows

cycle1.result: 49.7% of 163 referred distal radius fractures were stable; of these only 37% were mobilised early, the rest fully immobilised for 6 weeks without an active mobilisation protocol

result.intervention: Proposed only: a protocol to screen all distal radius fractures in virtual fracture clinic as stable or unstable, with stable fractures seen for early physiotherapy face to face or virtually
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Outcomes of trainee-performed emergency inguinal hernia repair
result.setting: Single clinical unit, Department of General Surgery, tertiary care hospital (All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar)

cycle1.result: SSI 4 (9.3%); mesh explantation 1 (2.32%); re-exploration 1 (2.32%); 1 mortality; mean LOH 4.33 days; long-term pain 20.93%; no recurrence; mean operating time 116.92 min; mean blood loss 93.7 ml

result.other_findings: Compared with published literature, trainee cases had more blood loss, more long-term pain (20.93% vs 1.2%) and slightly more wound complications (9.3% vs 6.74%), with comparable operating time, LOH, recurrence and mortality.

result.setting: Tertiary hospital (Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) national figures used as comparison

cycle1.result: Mean length of stay 33.59 vs 15.1 days nationally (median 15 days); geriatrician review 87% vs 24% nationally; 30-day mortality 5.5% vs 9.7% nationally

result.intervention: Proposed only: special discussion of long-staying patients in weekly ward round meetings
result.other_findings: Patients with stomas had higher mean LOS (42 vs 26 days); more patients had high pre-operative mortality risk (51.5% vs 43.5%), ischaemia (20.8% vs 8.9%) and haemorrhage (5.6% vs 2.6%) than nationally.

result.setting: not reported
result.standard: Department of Health and Social Care and other national/local guidelines: post-diagnostic support offered to all patients diagnosed with dementia

cycle1.result: All patients were offered post-diagnostic support; diagnosis discussed in about 93%, medication in 82%, driving in only 64% and LPA in only 63%

result.other_findings: Slightly more women chose the post-diagnostic support group over a dementia adviser; 21% more patients opted for the group when they had a carer.

result.topic: Preoperative group and save before mastectomy
result.setting: Department of Breast Surgery, University Hospital Limerick

cycle1.result: All patients had a routine preoperative G&H; 2/100 received post-operative blood transfusion (transfusion probability 2%); only 15% had a post-operative haemoglobin checked

result.other_findings: Mean haemoglobin drop was 2.3 g/dL; selective G&H requesting was projected to give significant cost savings but would need a validated risk stratification system.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis prescribing
result.setting: Adult ENT ward, emergency and pre-operative admissions (NHS GGC, Glasgow)

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment clearly done for 39%; 22/63 (35%) meeting LMWH criteria received it; 5/96 (5%) meeting TEDS criteria received it; 45% had both prescribed according to the guideline

result.intervention: Planned only: departmental policy and staff education
result.other_findings: Pro-forma clerking (n = 148) improved risk assessment compared with freehand clerking (n = 25) (43% vs 12%) but not correct prescription (45% vs 40%); no VTE or unexpected bleeding occurred.

result.setting: Single bariatric centre (Phoenix Health, Chester)

cycle1.result: 17 patients underwent SADIS, average BMI 55; weight loss greater than bypass patients at 6 months, 1 year and 2 years, with better sustained weight loss at 6-10 years; no increase in nutritional deficiencies

result.other_findings: The ratio of psychological to physiological co-morbidities was higher than average.

result.topic: Routine postoperative blood tests after arthroplasty
result.setting: One hospital, elective hip and knee arthroplasty (Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: Four (3.8%) patients had no post-operative blood tests; mean haemoglobin drop 22.5 g/L; no transfusions or iron given; seven patients given IV fluids (one AKI, six hyponatraemia)

result.other_findings: Mean creatinine and eGFR were essentially unchanged after surgery; authors suggest targeting postoperative bloods to higher-risk patients.

result.setting: Buckinghamshire Breast Unit (Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust)
result.standard: ABS 2023 Phyllodes guidelines for excision margins

cycle1.result: Unit not yet fully compliant; 59% (n=20) had one operation, 29% (n=10) two and 12% (n=4) three to obtain clear margins; 41% (n=14) required >1 operation; one mastectomy for malignant phyllodes might have been avoided under new guidelines

result.intervention: Planned: disseminate new guidance within departmental and regional networks, then re-audit
result.other_findings: 29 women (85%) had breast conservation and 5 (15%) mastectomy; no excess mastectomies for wide clear margins were identified.

result.setting: Regional plastic surgery department (Department of Burns and Plastic Surgery, Whiston Hospital, Liverpool)

cycle1.result: X-ray findings documented 55%; antibiotic plan 35%; post-op plan 100%; post-op antibiotics 90%; follow-up plan 95%

result.intervention: Updated hand trauma proforma including a free text box

cycle2.result: Overall completion increased; responsible consultant 100%; X-ray findings 85%; antibiotic plan 80%; but post-op plan fell to 85%, post-op antibiotics 75% and follow-up plan 60%

result.other_findings: Operation note documentation of anaesthetic type and tourniquet use/time improved; clinicians asked for a larger free-text box and hand diagram.

result.setting: Tertiary hospital surgical unit (Glasgow Royal Infirmary)
result.standard: Local gentamicin dosing and serum level monitoring guidelines

cycle1.result: 70% of initial doses matched weight-based dosing; 55% had serum levels measured within the appropriate timeframe

cycle2.result: 92% of initial doses accurately prescribed; 78% had timely serum level measurements

result.other_findings: Re-audit was done at both one and two months after the interventions.

result.topic: Pre-operative mortality risk documentation in emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Great Western Hospital NHS Trust
result.standard: NELA key performance indicator: pre-operative mortality risk calculated and documented on consent form and in medical record; target ≥ 85%

cycle1.result: 80% (n = 39) had a calculated risk; of 27 (55%) who went to theatre, none had correct documentation as per NELA standards

result.intervention: Proposed only: NELA pathway document, poster and pre-operative mortality risk sticker
result.other_findings: Of 7 trainee and consultant questionnaire respondents, 4 rarely or never documented pre-operative mortality risk as per NELA guidance.

result.setting: Emergency departments, St Helier and Epsom hospitals (Epsom & St Helier Hospitals, London)
result.standard: NICE quality standards for assessment and management of renal colic (CTKUB timing, NSAID analgesia, time to urological intervention, bone profile/calcium, stone diet advice)

cycle1.result: CTKUB reported within 24 hours 97.9%; NSAIDs 54.5%; surgical intervention within 48 hours 70%; calcium requested 77.9%; dietary/fluid advice 8.7%

result.intervention: Patient leaflet on stone diet and a renal order-set, plus raising clinician awareness

cycle2.result: CTKUB reported within 24 hours 100%; NSAIDs 71.9%; surgical intervention within 48 hours 100%; calcium requested 94.7%; dietary/fluid advice 39.4%

result.other_findings: Dietary and lifestyle advice improved but remained low at 39.4%.

result.setting: North Devon District Hospital (Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, Barnstaple)
result.standard: NICE bladder cancer guidance 1.2.6 and 1.2.7 (documentation of tumour size and number, and mitomycin instillation)

cycle1.result: 78.20% of operation notes did not include mitomycin instillation or justification for not giving it; tumour number documented in 98.71% and tumour size in 88.46%

cycle2.result: Quality of operation note documentation improved doubly (no further figures given)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Emergency department, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standard 1: admission to an orthopaedic ward bed within 4 hours of attending ED

cycle1.result: Average time to ward 8 hrs 29 mins; 26% (8/31) reached ward <4 hours

result.intervention: 90 minute multidisciplinary simulation training programme on the hip fracture pathway for ED and related staff (32 people), in person and via Zoom, February 2021

cycle2.result: Average time to ward 5 hrs 58 mins (32% reduction); 72% (18/25) reached ward <4 hours

result.other_findings: Training included Emergency Medicine, Orthopaedics, nursing, Radiology, Radiography and porters.

result.setting: Single multicentre tertiary health network (Monash Health), Melbourne

cycle1.result: 23 438 ENA tests in 19 603 patients; 2636 (13.4%) had repeat testing, of whom 2523 (95.7%) had stable results and 53 (2.2%) changed from negative to positive; five new AARDs among 34 eligible patients

result.other_findings: 20 918 (89.2%) tests were negative; the commonest specificity was anti-Ro52 (1185, 51.4% of positives). No guidelines exist for repeat ENA ordering.

result.topic: Identification of faecal incontinence in inpatients
result.setting: Hospital inpatient wards, spot-check audit (Scunthorpe General Hospital)

cycle1.result: Nursing bowel documentation 90%, medical 48%; 10.8% had FI; 31% would have been identified by medical documentation; all (100%) referred appropriately

cycle2.result: Nursing bowel documentation 94%, medical 47%; 5.3% had FI; only 28% would have been identified by medical documentation; some action taken in 71.42% but no referral arranged in any

result.other_findings: 28.57% of patients with FI were on general surgical wards; medical documentation and onward referral need improvement.

result.setting: 8 UK district general hospitals, multicentre

cycle1.result: Negative appendicectomy rate 21%; no association between PAS scores and histology (Spearman 0.004, p=0.951) or between ultrasound and histology (p= 0.336)

result.other_findings: Age differed significantly between operative and conservative groups (p = 0.0023); antibiotics on admission did not prevent readmission of conservatively treated patients (p=0.039).

result.setting: Breast surgery under one consultant (Ysbyty Gwynedd, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, Bangor)
result.standard: Association of Breast Surgery (ABS UK) recommendations on chemoprophylaxis in high-risk groups; national VTE risk <0.4%

cycle1.result: No VTE in any patient (compliant with national risk <0.4%); only two patients received chemoprophylaxis despite 11 with anaesthetic >3 hours and 22 with predisposing conditions

result.intervention: Planned only: a breast-specific standardised local VTE protocol
result.other_findings: 119 (73.5%) operations were for malignancy; one patient was imaged for suspected pulmonary embolism and was negative.

result.setting: Acute surgical unit, University Hospital Limerick
result.standard: University Hospital Limerick guidelines on urine testing

cycle1.result: 68% had urinalysis and 48% urine culture; only 23 of 47 (49%) cultures were indicated

result.intervention: Information sheet placed in the ASU and an education session for nursing staff

cycle2.result: 39% had urinalysis; 28% had urine culture, of which 79% were indicated

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Admission for epistaxis with nasal packing
result.setting: ENT department (Ulster Hospital, Dundonald)

cycle1.result: 100% (n = 15) of patients with rapid rhino admitted; average 3.9 bed-days; 5 (33%) needed arterial ligation

result.intervention: Patients sent home with nasal pack in situ and outpatient follow-up

cycle2.result: 7% (n = 1) admitted; average 2 bed-days; one (7%) needed ligation; no difference in 30-day morbidity and mortality

result.other_findings: Total bed-days 57 v 4, costing £12654 v £888 at £222 per bed-day; 60% attended out of hours.

result.topic: Botulinum toxin injection for plantar fasciitis
result.setting: Musculoskeletal clinic

cycle1.result: All patients improved on VAS at 4 weeks, 38 (90.48%) pain free; 38 (90.48%) had no heel pain on palpation; 40 (95.24%) had improved HTI scores

result.other_findings: 15 patients (35.71%) had severe pain before injection and none after; longer-term effect not assessed.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis in inguinal hernia repair
result.setting: District general hospital, elective inguinal hernia repair (University Hospital North Durham)
result.standard: National guidance: no antibiotic prophylaxis for low-risk patients; single dose for high-risk patients

cycle1.result: 53.33% of patients received antibiotics in line with national guidelines; 50.00% had prophylactic antibiotics overall

result.other_findings: Wound infection rate 1.04% (0% with antibiotics vs 2.08% without, P = 0.175); 94.79% of repairs were open.

result.setting: Paediatric tonsillectomy discharge summaries (Musgrove Park Hospital, Taunton)
result.standard: ENT UK guidelines for paediatric tonsillectomy discharge information

cycle1.result: Go to ED if significant bleed 21% (6); see GP if persistent fever 7% (2); regular analgesia 78% (22); regular diet 46% (13)

result.intervention: One-click pre-defined discharge summary inserts ("snippets"), designed after a departmental survey

cycle2.result: Go to ED if significant bleed 93% (14); see GP if persistent fever 73% (11); regular analgesia 100% (15); regular diet 73% (11)

result.other_findings: Further cycles planned on parent understanding and satisfaction.

result.setting: Community mental health team, Parkview Mental Health Resource Centre, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde

cycle1.result: Two simultaneous online MDTs run by the same staff, with staff dipping in and out and no formal structure (no baseline figures given)

result.intervention: Two designated nursing teams feeding into the two MDTs on alternate weeks, plus a new structured MDT presentation template (PDSA cycle; pilot March 2022)

cycle2.result: 100% of staff felt the new MDT structure was useful; 84% satisfied with the new way of running MDT; 84% satisfied with designated MDT teams

result.other_findings: Outcome was measured by staff feedback survey only.

result.setting: Laparoscopic appendicectomy consent forms (The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust)
result.standard: GMC and RCS England consent standards; 17 key risks from national guidelines and consultant consensus

cycle1.result: Only four risks documented in >75%: bleeding 98.5%, infection 95.6%, injury to nearby structures 83.8%, conversion to open 88.2%; bowel injury 61.8%, bladder injury 36.8%, ureter injury 22.1%, death 13.2%, reintervention 23.5%, hernia 63.2%

result.intervention: Procedure-specific consent template introduced; re-audit planned
result.other_findings: Among 46 female patients, gynaecological risks were documented in just 30.4%.

result.setting: General surgery and urology receiving wards (Glasgow Royal Infirmary)
result.standard: Clinical governance: every patient should have a named consultant, with bedside whiteboard matching the electronic system (TrakCare)

cycle1.result: 7 (18.4%) bed-boards had incorrect or no entries (2 no consultant name, 5 incorrect)

result.intervention: Verbal and written communication with nursing staff and junior doctors

cycle2.result: Third cycle: only 1 (2.6%) missing consultant's name

result.other_findings: Second cycle, 2 weeks after the intervention, found only 1 (2.6%) bed-board with incorrect or no names.

result.setting: Major trauma centre (University Hospital Coventry)
result.standard: Departmental guideline on upper limb bite injuries, updated in line with the British Society for Surgery of the Hand

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Departmental guideline updated in accordance with BSSH guidance, with an action plan

cycle2.result: 86% of all patients, including 100% with infection, who required an operation had it within 24 hours; first contact practitioners gave thorough ED washout in 25%; 30% needed formal theatre washout, of whom 25% needed a second operation

result.other_findings: 23% of those managed in Hand Trauma Clinic needed more than one follow-up; further recommendations include ED washout training for first contact practitioners, better documentation and a dedicated minor ops room.

result.setting: Surgical ambulatory unit, general surgery (Southern Health & Social Care Trust, Craigavon)
result.standard: NICE QS174 and RCS England safe handover guidance: referral to include diagnosis, background and plan

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Team education and reminder prompts across the department

cycle2.result: Improvement in all domains: diagnosis (p<0.0001), background (p<0.0001) and plan (p=0.0007); referrals with no information significantly reduced (p=0.0063)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Tertiary referral neurosurgery centre (Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: 77.2% of surgeries were same day or within 24 hours; mean admission to theatre 1.25 days; in a random sample of 225, 30 cases were delayed (20% for imaging, 6% awaiting consultant review, 10% awaiting other results such as COVID swab)

result.other_findings: Average length of stay 17 days; average theatre time 2h11m; designated acute theatres used about 75% of the time. Re-audit planned.

result.setting: District hospital internal paper referral slips (University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay Trust)

cycle1.result: 60 sheets equated to 43g of CO2e; estimated annual usage 520 sheets, 2.6 kg CO2e per year

result.intervention: Planned: replace paper referral sheets with an electronic form in the Lorenzo IT system
result.other_findings: True usage was approximated because some sheets were retained by consultants.

result.setting: Laparoscopic appendicectomy patients (Aneurin Bevan Health Board; Cardiff & Vale Health Board)

cycle1.result: 100% included infection and bleeding; 88% conversion to open; 82% bowel resection and damage to local structures; 76% blood clots; 76% legible; 65% contained acronyms; 82% documented alternative therapies discussed

result.other_findings: 18 different complications were used with high variability; on questionnaire only 64% of patients recalled basic complications and 43% remembered being offered alternative treatments.

result.setting: University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay NHS Foundation Trust, regional audit
result.standard: BOAST guidelines for management of ACL injury

cycle1.dates: 1st of July 2018 and the 1st of July 2019 (pre-covid); 1st of July 2021 and 1st of July 2022 (post-covid)
cycle1.result: 82% had timely clinic assessment; 37% had MRI within 14 days; 38% referred for prehabilitation; 84% had post-operative physiotherapy

result.other_findings: Average time to surgery rose from 230.5 days pre-covid (n=37) to 353.9 days post-covid (n=23).

result.topic: Violence and aggression on inpatient mental health wards
result.setting: Pine Ward, Park Royal mental health unit
result.standard: Project aim: improve patient and staff safety by 20% by end of December 2025

cycle1.result: Verbal aggression 4 per day shift; aggression towards objects 2; PRN psychotropic use 4 per day shift

result.intervention: Weekly community meeting, observation of patient positive strengths, messages in nursing station on using soft words, and Section 17 leave flow chart for patients

cycle2.result: Patient safety improved by 25% and staff safety by 30%; verbal aggression fell from 4 to 2 per day shift; aggression towards objects 2 to 1; PRN use 4 to 2

result.other_findings: Verbal aggression against staff remains a key concern; Datix incident records to be reviewed in a future audit.

result.setting: Emergency surgical unit (Belfast Health & Social Care Trust)
result.standard: GAIN Guidelines 2011; Trust discharge proforma of 33 parameters, summary acceptable if >90% of information recorded accurately

cycle1.result: Discharge failure rate 60%

result.intervention: Dedicated teaching and training on E-Discharge compilation at induction
result.other_findings: Recording of follow-up care and ongoing primary care involvement remained inadequate.

result.setting: ENT Rapid Access Clinic, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary
result.standard: ENT UK guidelines for management of sudden onset sensorineural hearing loss

cycle1.result: Average referral to intervention 1.47 days, to first ENT review 3.82 days, to first audiogram 4.43 days; presentation to oral steroids 0.33 days; symptom onset to oral steroids 7.5 days

result.intervention: Management pathway reinforced as per ENT UK guidelines and urgent audiogram organisation improved
result.other_findings: Late patient presentation noted; importance of tuning fork testing when an audiogram is not immediately available emphasised.

result.topic: Below knee amputation pathway in orthoplastic trauma
result.setting: Major trauma centre, orthoplastic patients (Royal London Hospital)
result.standard: NICE guidelines for complex fractures and the Vascular Society guidance for major amputations

cycle1.result: 100% compliance with pre-operative MDT discussion, recording decision to amputate, and formal referral to amputee rehabilitation; average time to surgery after decision 1.75 days

result.intervention: Planned: a written pathway for lower limb amputations in the trust
result.other_findings: Lower compliance with written counselling for families, naming a discharge co-ordinator pre-operatively and pain team review within 24 hours post-operatively.

result.topic: qFIT use in two week wait colorectal referrals
result.setting: Two week wait referrals, Somerset Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE recommendation of qFIT as replacement for faecal occult blood testing

cycle1.result: 74 patients eligible for qFIT, only 7 had it; 93 qFIT performed by GPs with 11 positive; 11 (3.8%) colorectal cancers identified

result.intervention: New 2WW referral form and qFIT made available to general practitioners

cycle2.result: 18 patients eligible for qFIT, all had it; 155 qFIT performed with 18 positive; 12 (5.4%) colorectal cancers identified

result.other_findings: qFIT use rose as 2WW referrals and qFIT-eligible patients fell.

result.setting: Monday-Friday emergency general surgery theatre lists (The Prince Charles Hospital, Brisbane, Queensland)
result.standard: Operating Theatre Efficiency Guideline: late start is time into operating room after the scheduled session start time

cycle1.result: 81% of morning lists delayed; afternoon lists 50% delayed; Mondays 77% and Thursdays 69% delayed

result.intervention: Educational intervention for surgical and anaesthetic teams and an updated registrar role

cycle2.result: 66% of morning lists delayed; afternoon lists 55% delayed; Mondays 56% and Thursdays 43% delayed

result.other_findings: No reasons were documented for morning delays; afternoon delays were mostly due to overrunning elective lists but poorly documented.

result.setting: On-call urology team (Cambridge University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Trust guidelines: 10 documentation items for urethral catheterisation

cycle1.result: Only 28% (14/50) had all 10 items documented; indication best at 94% (47/50); chaperone and groin examination lowest at 44% (22/50)

result.intervention: Electronic record 'smart phrase' (.icat, i-CATHETAR mnemonic) prompting all 10 items; second cycle under way
result.other_findings: 72% (36/50) of catheters were inserted by the urology team.

result.setting: National trainee survey of UK renal transplant units

cycle1.result: 91% of trainees had performed <01 LDN as primary surgeon

cycle2.result: 92% of trainees had performed <01 LDN as primary surgeon (OR 0.87, 0.32-2.37, p=0.50); only 33% had been on an LDN course; likelihood of performing >01 LDN <1 in 30 vs <1 in 25 in 2013

result.other_findings: No improvement in LDN training since the 2014 report; 03% of units offer robotic-assisted LDN.

result.topic: Surgical teaching programme for junior doctors
result.setting: Surgical department, major trauma centre (Royal Sussex County Hospital, Brighton)

cycle1.result: 8.7% of doctors felt they had enough teaching

result.intervention: Teaching programme with journal clubs, case presentations, practical sessions and high-fidelity simulation, delivered in hybrid format

cycle2.result: 55.5% of doctors felt they had enough teaching

result.other_findings: 44.4% could not attend half the sessions because of clinical commitments; morning sessions before handover recommended.

result.setting: Regional hospital (Wexford General Hospital)
result.standard: NICE blood transfusion guidelines, with five local criteria for appropriate out-of-hours transfusion

cycle1.result: 70.6% of 51 out-of-hours RCC units were appropriate; 29.4% not indicated

result.intervention: Planned: verbal proforma before re-audit and guidelines on appropriate requests
result.other_findings: Active haemorrhage in 31.4% and symptomatic anaemia in 51%; no transfusion complications recorded.

result.setting: Surgical Same Day Emergency Centre and Surgical Assessment Unit (Royal Stoke University Hospital)
result.standard: GIRFT epididymo-orchitis pathway and local antimicrobial guidelines

cycle1.result: Antibiotic compliance 50%

result.intervention: Posters with QR code links to GIRFT pathways and antimicrobial guidelines in SSDEC and SAU

cycle2.result: Antibiotic compliance 70%; sexual health history and assessment uptake increased by 34%

result.other_findings: Main barrier was IM ceftriaxone non-compliance due to unfamiliarity with reconstituting with 1% lidocaine, prompting a switch to IV administration; further re-audit planned.

result.setting: Single-centre cardiac surgery (Royal Papworth Hospital, Cambridge)
result.standard: Local e-discharge summary template standards; target 100%

cycle1.result: 5 of 16 domains complete in 100%; reason for admission misplaced 43%; GP request reasoning in allocated box 55%; N/A for no GP requests 23%; no ECHO specified 20%; acronyms avoided 17%

result.intervention: Results shared at a team meeting and on a poster in the MDT office

cycle2.result: 7 of 16 domains complete in 100%; reason for admission misplaced 40%; GP request reasoning 57%; N/A for no GP requests 48%; no ECHO specified 27%; acronyms avoided 15%

result.other_findings: 110 patients across both cycles; the 100% standard was not met for most criteria and template revision is planned.

result.topic: Night-time noise and light in critical care
result.setting: Intensive Therapy Unit and High Dependency Unit (Newcastle Upon Tyne Hospitals)
result.standard: Trust guideline: lights out and radios off by 10 pm

cycle1.result: ITU lights 20%, radio 70%; HDU lights 56%, radio 56%; night-time noise 46 dB; RCSQ ITU 53.5, HDU 34.8

result.intervention: Staff awareness, eye masks and ear plugs for patients, and clustering of overnight nursing care

cycle2.result: ITU lights 30%, radio 70%; HDU lights 70%, radio 80%; night-time noise 40 dB; RCSQ ITU 56.4, HDU 60.2

result.other_findings: Sleep duration rose in ITU (5.1 to 5.3 hours) and HDU (4.0 to 5.5 hours); fewer patients disturbed by noise and alarms (ITU 33% to 25%; HDU 80% to 30%).

result.setting: General surgery inpatients, district general hospital (Ysbyty Glan Clwyd, Rhyl)

cycle1.result: Documented management plan 100% (other baseline figures not reported)

cycle2.result: Improvement in 11 of 15 items: 3-point patient ID 100% (+43.7%), NEWS/observations +22.5%, medication review +26.7%, thromboprophylaxis +53.4%, examination +45.3%, escalation/DNACPR +37.7%; management plan remained 100%

result.other_findings: Proforma used in 85 of 106 entries (80.2%); ward round lead name (-8.5%), date (-2.4%) and time (-10.6%) declined, attributed to proforma design, now revised for re-audit.

result.topic: Timely cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
result.setting: Surgical department, Great Western Hospital, Swindon
result.standard: Current guidelines on cholecystectomy within target time frame after diagnosis; national average 15% (RCSEng)

cycle1.result: Very low number of patients had cholecystectomy within the target time frame; biliary readmissions 58%

cycle2.result: 10.7% increase in timely cholecystectomies, overall compliance 14%; biliary readmissions 37%

result.other_findings: 47.3% of patients were still awaiting surgery, but the waiting list fell by 5.2% in 1 year despite COVID-19.

result.setting: Colorectal target (two week wait) investigation pathway (North Middlesex University Hospital)
result.standard: Faster diagnosis standard: cancer ruled in or out within 28 days of referral; treatment within 62 days

cycle1.result: Mean time to diagnosis 45.8 days; only 47/159 (29.6%) diagnosed within 28 days; STT 36.3 days (95% CI 28.1-44.6) vs traditional 50.5 days (95% CI 45.4-55.7) (P = 0.005); 4/7 cancers treated within 62 days (median day 59)

result.other_findings: Of 212 referrals, 53 declined, did not attend or were unfit; 7 cancers were diagnosed (4 colorectal, 1 gastric, 2 lung).

result.setting: Emergency department of a major trauma centre, hand radiographs (University Hospitals of Leicester; University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire)
result.standard: National guidelines: all jewellery removed as the initial step in hand trauma, before imaging

cycle1.result: 115 of 3542 patients had jewellery in situ on radiograph

cycle2.result: 107 of 4021 patients had jewellery in situ, an improvement of 18.1%

result.other_findings: Patients with jewellery in situ were mostly female (64%), usually with a metal ring on the left ring finger (84%); 1 in 4 needed a further surgical procedure.

result.topic: Laparoscopic to open conversion in colorectal resection
result.setting: Elective colorectal resections (Letterkenny University Hospital)
result.standard: Standard conversion rate of 14.3% (Journal of the Society of Laparoscopic and Robotic Surgeons, 2014)

cycle1.result: Laparoscopy attempted in 83 (96.5%); 5 of 83 (6.1%) converted to open; colon cancer conversion 10.3% (3 of 29) in 2021 and 9.5% (2 of 21) in 2022; rectal cancer 0% both years

result.other_findings: Primary open surgery in 03 (3.4%) patients.

result.topic: Lynch syndrome testing in colorectal cancer
result.setting: District general hospital (Airedale General Hospital, West Yorkshire)
result.standard: NICE guidelines on Lynch syndrome testing and genetic referral for MMR-deficient colorectal cancer

cycle1.result: 17 (8.8%) had deficient MMR; genetic testing referrals made for 5 dMMR cases, with 1 missed referral

result.other_findings: 14 dMMR cases had MLH1 mutations and 3 non-MLH1; the missed referral was promptly followed up.

result.setting: Patients with suspected ureteric colic, NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: BAUS recommendation for urgent CT KUB; EAU guidelines on metabolic tests (calcium, uric acid) in confirmed urolithiasis

cycle1.result: CT KUB positive in 60/136 (44.1%); calcium checked in 38.3% (23/60); urate in 20.0% (12/60)

result.intervention: Email reminder to urology middle grades and consultants
result.other_findings: Abnormal calcium found in 4.3% (1/23) and 6.25% (2/32); 48.3% had previous urolithiasis.

result.topic: Periprosthetic femoral fracture time to surgery
result.setting: St. Richard's and Worthing Hospitals (University Hospitals Sussex NHS Trust)
result.standard: NICE hip fracture guidance of surgery on the day of or the day after admission used as comparison; no guideline exists for periprosthetic fractures

cycle1.result: Average admission to surgery 3.7 days for periprosthetic fractures vs 1.3 days for neck of femur fractures (random cohort of 30)

result.intervention: Planned: reduce time to CT and to hip surgeon specialist opinion, and educate team members; re-audit under way
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Best medical therapy in peripheral arterial disease
result.setting: Vascular unit, ward admissions and vascular clinics (University Hospital Ayr)
result.standard: Best medical therapy for PAD: diabetes and hypertension control, statin, antiplatelet, exercise and smoking cessation advice

cycle1.result: 4 of 11 smokers given cessation advice; all clinic patients given exercise advice; only 5 of 12 who should have had an antiplatelet received one; statins started in 7 of 14 not on one; 32 had lipid profile checked

result.other_findings: 3 patients never had HbA1c checked; 7 of 14 poorly controlled diabetics had medication changed; neither newly diagnosed hypertensive patient was prescribed treatment.

result.setting: 27 UK Major Trauma Centres, multicentre prospective audit (VISTA)

cycle1.result: 153 extremity vascular injuries with 92 primary interventions (86 open, 6 endovascular); median time to intervention 169 (IQR 112 - 371) minutes; consultant vascular surgeon present in 84%; 16 amputations (7% primary, 11% secondary)

result.other_findings: 51% of operated injuries were from blunt trauma, with concomitant orthopaedic injury in 33%.

result.setting: Neurosurgical unit (St. George's Hospital)
result.standard: Essential components of a neurosurgical discharge summary defined by senior neurosurgeons

cycle1.result: Half of the neurosurgical team rated summaries as below expectations

result.intervention: Visual aid placed above computer stations in junior doctors' offices, followed by formal departmental teaching

cycle2.result: Ward round documentation and discharge summary quality improved dramatically (no figures given)

result.other_findings: Challenges included poor ward round documentation and unclear expectations of structure.

result.setting: Surgical Triage Unit, tertiary centre (Nottingham University Hospital)

cycle1.result: 85% of low AAS patients imaged; 12 of 17 appendicectomies within 24 hours; antibiotics stopped after surgery in 53% of uncomplicated cases; 34 out of 50 (68%) had open access and safety netting

result.intervention: Interventions and local guidelines developed (details not reported)

cycle2.result: 93% of low AAS patients imaged; 8 out of 9 had surgery within 24 hours; antibiotics stopped in 42% of uncomplicated cases; 92% gained open access to STU

result.other_findings: Antibiotic stopping after surgery for uncomplicated appendicitis worsened and still needs improvement.

result.setting: Large rural GP practice under shared-care agreement with local mental health trust
result.standard: Shared care lithium monitoring agreement (individualised by age and comorbidity)

cycle1.result: 26% of those needing annual ECG had one in the past year; 78% had lithium level in previous 3 months; 81% had renal function within requirements; 52% had lipids in previous year

result.other_findings: Standards linked to a QOF incentive were more often met; lithium QOF indicators were retired in April 2019.

result.setting: Inpatient psychiatric wards, East Suffolk

cycle1.result: Polypharmacy in 52% of inpatient episodes; 74% combination and 26% augmentation therapy

result.other_findings: More than a quarter were on sedative augmentation with no deprescribing plan after discharge; more frequent medication reviews recommended.

result.setting: Teaching hospital; clinicians in anaesthetics, surgery, intensive care and geriatrics
result.standard: Rockwood Clinical Frailty Scale (no compliance target stated)

cycle1.result: Geriatricians judged 1/4 cases (25%) frail, anaesthetists 50%, surgeons 75%, intensivists 100%; mean CFS with a reference guide was similar across specialties (e.g. case C: 5.80; 6.14; 5.67; 6.50).

result.other_findings: Non-geriatricians were more likely to label a patient as frail, but assigned CFS scores were more homogeneous between specialties.

result.setting: Tallaght University Hospital (TUH) emergency department, Dublin
result.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standard 1: admission to an orthopaedic ward bed within 4 hours of ED attendance

cycle1.result: Average time to ward 8 hrs 29 mins; 26% (8/31) reached ward <4 hours.

result.intervention: 90-minute multidisciplinary simulation training programme on the hip fracture pathway for ED and key stakeholders (32 people), in person and via Zoom, February 2021.

cycle2.result: Average time to ward 5 hrs 58 mins (32% reduction); 72% (18/25) reached ward <4 hours.

result.other_findings: Data were collected retrospectively from the Symphony electronic record.

result.setting: Department of General Surgery, University Hospital Galway (tertiary care centre)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland 'Code of Practice for Surgeons' consent standard

cycle1.result: Patient name, DOB and PID correctly labelled in 100%; 38 (76%) documented without abbreviations or acronyms.

result.intervention: Virtual teaching sessions for non-consultant hospital doctors obtaining consent.

cycle2.result: Labelling 100%; 65 (87%) documented without abbreviations or acronyms.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: General surgical team, North Middlesex University Hospital, London
result.standard: Local guideline: IV co-amoxiclav plus gentamicin first line; gentamicin, teicoplanin and metronidazole if penicillin allergic; stop 24 hours post-surgery or continue 5-7 days if no source control

cycle1.result: Compliance with IV co-amoxiclav and gentamicin 4.0% (2/50); penicillin-allergic regimen adherence 4.0% (2/50); mean duration 4.59 days; 54.0% (27/50) received under 5 days.

result.intervention: Two teaching sessions and guideline dissemination via posters.

cycle2.result: Compliance 33.3% (16/48); penicillin-allergic regimen 6.25% (3/48); duration 5.71 days; 39.6% (19/48) received under 5 days.

result.other_findings: Gentamicin was the most under-prescribed antibiotic; overuse (>7 days) occurred in 12.0% (6/48) after the intervention.

result.topic: MSU sampling before antibiotics in suspected UTI
result.setting: New urology admissions via the Emergency Department, Royal Bolton Hospital
result.standard: National and local guidance on MSU sampling for suspected UTI; SMART aim 100% adherence by July 2025

cycle1.result: MSU compliance 60%; 16.7% had MSU sent before antibiotics; median MSU-to-first-antibiotic time 22.25 hours.

result.intervention: PDSA cycles raising awareness first among doctors, then nursing and HCA staff.

cycle2.result: MSU sampling 67%; 50% received antibiotics after MSU collection; median MSU-to-antibiotic time 5 hours.

result.other_findings: Full adherence not achieved; yellow wristbands in ED proposed for further PDSA cycles.

result.setting: 59 surgical units, online questionnaire via RCS COVID group and ALSGBI members

cycle1.result: Units performing minimal access procedures fell from 94.9% to 39.0% (P<0.001); open approach 54.2% vs 39.0% (P<0.001); post-operative COVID-19 complications 15.3%.

result.other_findings: Combined screening methods with a designated 'clean' theatre were commonly used; COVID-19 mortality was low.

result.setting: Orthopaedic trauma ward, district general hospital (Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust)
result.standard: NICE NG89 and local VTE guidelines

cycle1.result: Inadequate VTE prophylaxis in 8 cases (18%); minor prescribing concerns in 15 cases (34%); 48% appropriate with no prescribing or documentation errors.

result.intervention: Staff teaching, a nominated VTE guardian, VTE plans in operation notes, a dedicated spinal guideline and a spinal section in the trust VTE guideline.

cycle2.result: Inadequate prophylaxis in 1 (4%); minor concerns in 3 (14%); 82% appropriate with no errors.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Breast surgical department, Dublin hospital
result.standard: RCSG criteria for documentation of operative notes

cycle1.result: At least 90% compliance in 10/20 criteria; signature 82%, assistant 80%, anaesthetist 71%, diagnosis 61%; start and finish times 51%; complications 4%, extra procedures 4%, prosthesis 2%, elective/emergency 0%, blood loss 0%.

result.intervention: Poster and educational programme for surgical registrars (second cycle planned).
result.other_findings: Legibility 88% and diagram use 65%; second cycle with more emergency procedures planned.

result.topic: Carbon footprint of outpatient clinic travel
result.setting: In-person bariatric clinics, high-volume bariatric centre, South Tyneside & Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 87.5% travelled by car, 4.2% by bus or taxi; total 2727 km (58.5 hours); CO2 277.4 kg; travel costs £534.98.

result.other_findings: Interim findings; data collection ongoing to reach at least 100 patients.

result.setting: Regional hepatobiliary unit (Belfast Health and Social Care Trust)

cycle1.result: Pathway adherence day 2 22%, day 3 11%; median 8 days to soft diet; median day 9 to stop parenteral nutrition; median length of stay 15 days.

result.intervention: Pathway updated so all patients followed the same oral pathway (then second cycle); education session for surgical trainees by a dietitian (before third cycle).

cycle2.result: Adherence day 2 57%, day 3 43%; median days to soft diet 5; median day stopping parenteral nutrition 6; median length of stay 10 days.

result.other_findings: Second cycle (May-June 2023, n=8) had day 2 adherence 75% and day 3 63%; day 1 and CREON/supplement prescribing were consistently good.

result.topic: Axillary staging in early breast cancer
result.setting: Single centre, The Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Association of Breast Surgery guidelines for axillary management; axillary recurrence below 5% at 5 years

cycle1.result: All patients with U3 or higher ultrasound underwent biopsy; 25/26 B4 biopsies had ANC; axillary recurrence 3 (1.27%) at 5 years.

result.other_findings: SLNB in 203, ANC in 26 and axillary sampling in 2 patients.

result.setting: Emergency general surgery, Stockport NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) data and high-risk criteria

cycle1.result: 30-day mortality 11.1% (NELA Year 3); time to CT 2d19hrs.

result.intervention: 'Abdominal Pain Pathway' leading to CT in ED for high-risk features (ASA >2, previous surgery, sepsis, raised lactate, >45 yrs).

cycle2.result: Mortality 2.4% (NELA Year 6); time to CT <4 hours; all patients requiring laparotomy identified on CT.

result.other_findings: Two cycles over two fortnights of ED presentations were audited before pathway implementation.

result.setting: Dedicated botox clinic, single centre (NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde)

cycle1.result: Fissure confirmed in 63%; 89% received clinic Botox with no major complications; 85% healed at three months.

result.other_findings: Five patients needed EUA with Botox; estimated saving £1,308.50 per case.

result.setting: AMD clinic, University Hospital Southampton

cycle1.result: Opticians made 62.88% (566/900) of referrals; diagnostic accuracy rose from 22.94% to 37.64% in the second half of 2018 (p<0.0003).

result.other_findings: False positive referrals increased; an electronic referral system is planned.

result.setting: General surgery admissions, district general hospital (Wye Valley NHS Trust)
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for diagnosis, aetiology assessment and risk stratification of acute pancreatitis

cycle1.result: Correct diagnosis within 48 hours 97%; risk stratification within 48 hours 38%; aetiology assessment 62%.

result.intervention: Results presented at audit meeting, MDT posters and teaching sessions.
result.other_findings: 5% of cases were deemed idiopathic; risk stratification still below standard.

result.setting: Endoscopy department, Walsall Manor Hospital
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines (cost analysis)

cycle1.result: Total cost £55,973; 13/147 (9%) received medical treatment, 29 (20%) symptomatic treatment, 98 (66%) no intervention, 7 (5%) surgery; 85.3% of spend (£47733) did not lead to surgical or medical management.

result.other_findings: 126 colonoscopies and 21 flexible sigmoidoscopies.

result.topic: Surgical site infection in head and neck surgery
result.setting: Tertiary centre, Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 7 SSIs; 7/14 diabetic patients received prophylactic antibiotics; 2 diabetic patients had early post-operative infection.

result.intervention: Flow-chart antibiotic prophylaxis protocol and presentation at a local meeting.

cycle2.result: 6 SSIs; 16/19 diabetic patients received prophylactic antibiotics; 0 diabetic infections.

result.other_findings: SSI was more likely with surgical drains (8/94, p=0.008498) and prophylaxis in this group was inconsistent in both cycles.

result.setting: NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: WSES and ESCP guidelines: colonoscopy 6-8 weeks after complicated diverticulitis

cycle1.result: 1 of 21 colonoscopies within 6-8 weeks; timely colonoscopy in 5% of complicated cases; 1 malignancy.

cycle2.result: 6 of 18 complicated cases had timely colonoscopy; overall 46% of complicated cases timely; no malignancies.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest routine colonoscopy for uncomplicated cases should be reconsidered.

result.setting: NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: WSES and ESCP guidelines: colonoscopy 6-8 weeks after complicated diverticulitis

cycle1.result: 1 of 21 colonoscopies within 6-8 weeks; timely colonoscopy in 5% of complicated cases; 1 malignancy.

cycle2.result: 6 of 18 complicated cases had timely colonoscopy; overall 46% of complicated cases timely; no malignancies.

result.other_findings: Same abstract as DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.393; routine colonoscopy for uncomplicated cases should be reconsidered.

result.setting: Stroke unit, Cork University Hospital
result.standard: National Clinical Guideline for Stroke (UK and Ireland): IPCs for immobile patients days 3 to 30

cycle1.result: VTE risk section completed in 21 (68%); of 9 eligible immobile patients none had IPCs prescribed and 1 (11%) had them in situ; 56% had no VTE prophylaxis.

result.other_findings: The VTE risk section was blank in 32% of charts; a root cause analysis and quality improvement initiative are planned.

result.topic: Same-day theatre cancellations and pre-operative fasting
result.setting: Single surgeon's elective paediatric plastic surgery list, Great Ormond Street Hospital, London
result.standard: European Society of Anaesthesiology perioperative fasting guideline and local trust pre-operative fasting guideline

cycle1.result: 3 patients (10%) cancelled on the day; 2 (66%) due to non-adherence to fasting rules and 1 (33%) due to parental deferral.

result.other_findings: A pre-operative fasting information sheet for patients and parents was developed and a re-audit is planned.

result.setting: Vascular surgery, UK tertiary centre (Countess of Chester Hospital)
result.standard: Good Surgical Practice and Royal College of Surgeons advice that formal records of M&M discussions are kept

cycle1.result: No record included the hospital number; 20.6% had all five sections complete; 'when' completed in 29.4% and 'attending consultants' in 41.2%; 29.4% had no record of discussion; 35.2% no action plan; 47.0% no responsible person.

result.other_findings: Results presented at the local governance meeting with plans to create a better way of recording discussion.

result.topic: Day hospital access and waiting times
result.setting: Day Hospital, St Columcille's Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Hospital targets for reducing length of stay and early supported discharge (no numeric target stated)

cycle1.result: Average wait for a day hospital appointment 270 days.

result.intervention: Week-long Rapid Improvement Event using Lean methods: process mapping, visual management and clinic flow boards, five new clinic pathways, early supported discharge slots, monthly staff meetings and streamlined administration.

cycle2.result: Average wait 70 days (75% reduction); new patient referrals up 184%; 98% of patient survey feedback positive.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Semi-elective trauma pathway and clerking documentation
result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic department, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, London
result.standard: RCSEng Standards for the Clinical Structure and Content of Patient Records

cycle1.result: 36% had complete clerking documentation; two near misses; no comprehensive referral pathway.

result.intervention: Semi-Elective Trauma Pathway and a Medical Clerking Proforma introduced after presentation at Clinical Governance meeting.

cycle2.result: 88% had complete clerking documentation; no near misses; 95% went through the new pathway.

result.other_findings: The 181 patients are the total across both cycles.

result.setting: Royal Albert Edward Infirmary (Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: AUGIS quality standards for laparoscopic cholecystectomy

cycle1.result: Compliant with only 1/6 criteria; 67% (38/56) day case; no emergency cholecystectomy within 7 days of presentation; 7/56 readmitted; no bile duct injuries.

result.other_findings: 53 laparoscopic and 3 open cholecystectomies.

result.setting: Surgical floor, tertiary major trauma centre (University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Documented ceiling of care in a completed treatment escalation plan (TEP) form

cycle1.result: 58% (45/78) had a completed TEP form.

result.intervention: Results discussed at clinical governance meeting with the frailty consultant; recommendations implemented with regular frailty consultant reviews of patients.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: General surgery department, district general hospital (Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: GIRFT national pathway for testicular torsion (seven standards); NCEPOD Twist and Shout

cycle1.result: 70% seen in one or fewer settings; 40% seen by surgical decision maker within 60 minutes; 0% TWIST score documented; 18% had ultrasound if >48 hours of pain; 0% in theatre within one hour; 67% of orchidectomy patients followed up.

result.intervention: Results presented, teaching on the TWIST score and guideline posters in general surgery and the paediatric ED.

cycle2.result: 70% seen in one or fewer settings; 50% seen by decision maker within 60 minutes; 0% TWIST score; 50% ultrasound if >48 hours; 0% in theatre within one hour; 75% of orchidectomy patients followed up.

result.other_findings: TWIST score use and time to review and theatre remained poor.

result.setting: Surgical ward rounds, James Paget University Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians 'Ward Rounds in Medicine'

cycle1.result: First checklist used in a mean of 13% (SD 22%); documentation with checklist 67% vs 26% without (t(64)=8.85, p<.00001).

result.intervention: Novel peri-operative ward round checklist, revised after feedback for the second audit.

cycle2.result: Second checklist used in a mean of 56% (SD 28%), t(75)=7.59, p<.00001.

result.other_findings: Documentation improved especially for fluid balance, analgesia and physiotherapy needs; a third audit is planned.

result.setting: Emergency department, Dorset County Hospital
result.standard: NICE 2016: consider MRI as first-line imaging for suspected scaphoid fracture

cycle1.result: 16% of patients with normal X-ray but clinical signs were not referred for MRI; average time to MRI 37.6 days.

cycle2.result: 1% not referred for MRI in re-audit; average time to MRI 11.4 days.

result.other_findings: Intermediate re-audit December 2017 to February 2018 had time to MRI 19.9 days; 35% of ED scaphoid injuries were not referred for orthopaedic assessment.

result.setting: Major trauma centres in England, Trauma Audit and Research Network database

cycle1.result: 4375 (43%) intubated pre-hospital and 5889 (57%) in ED; 3264 (75%) of ED intubations within 30 min of arrival.

result.other_findings: Of 1593 with non-intubation pre-hospital airway interventions, 881 (55%) were intubated in ED, 805 (91%) within 30 min.

result.setting: Emergency department, tertiary trauma centre (St George Hospital, London)
result.standard: Existing ED guidelines: photo documentation, antibiotic administration, tetanus prophylaxis, neurovascular assessment pre and post splint

cycle1.result: 97.5% received antibiotics (13.3% within 1hr, 60% within 3hr, 100% within 6hr); 48.8% tetanus prophylaxis; 4.87% documented tetanus assessment; 100% neurovascular examination.

result.other_findings: Titled a closed loop audit but only one data set reported; 72% needed surgery with average 16.7 hours to theatre.

result.setting: Cardiothoracic theatres, Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Birmingham
result.standard: Zero preventable delays and 100% required hair removal (trust guidelines)

cycle1.result: Delay in arrival in the anaesthetic room 81%; delay from theatre arrival to operation start 52%; hair removal before theatre 41%.

result.intervention: Education of clinicians and posters promoting the 'Ready4Theatre' initiative (showered, hair removed, changed).

cycle2.result: Anaesthetic room arrival delay 51%; theatre arrival to start delay 36%; hair removal before theatre 90%.

result.other_findings: 86% still had some delay and hair removal was inadequate in 50%.

result.setting: Emergency department, Leighton Hospital, Crewe
result.standard: BOAST guidelines for management of ankle fractures

cycle1.result: 100% compliance for documentation of mechanism and clinical findings, comorbidities, and urgent radiographs before manipulation of deformed ankles; 75% for radiographs before transfer; neurovascular reassessment after manipulation documented clearly by only one of five reviewers.

result.other_findings: Posters were circulated and the LocSSIP for ankle fracture reduction was edited to include post-manipulation neurovascular reassessment.

result.setting: Two surgical inpatient wards, district general hospital (Princess Alexandra Hospital, Harlow)
result.standard: NICE CG174: maintenance 25-30ml/kg/day water and 1mmol/kg/day sodium, potassium and chloride

cycle1.result: Maintenance fluids prescribed for 76%; mean 2.3L/day; net sodium +221mmol, potassium -62mmol, chloride +162mmol (295% excess sodium, 216% excess chloride, 82% less potassium than required).

result.other_findings: A maintenance fluid prescribing protocol and teaching sessions are planned.

result.topic: Port positioning in paediatric laparoscopic appendicectomy
result.setting: Paediatric laparoscopic appendicectomy (East Surrey Hospital; Royal Surrey Hospital)
result.standard: Local policy mandating left iliac fossa port placement; voiding status in paediatric WHO checklist

cycle1.result: Left iliac fossa port placement 72%; pre-operative voiding documented 12%; intra-operative catheterisation 20%.

result.intervention: Education programme for operating department practitioners, paediatric nurses and surgeons, with seminars and regular dissemination of the local protocol.

cycle2.result: Left iliac fossa port placement 100% (p<0.0001); voiding documented 40% (p=0.0026); catheterisation 8% (p=0.1478).

result.other_findings: Pre-operative voiding status has since been added to the local paediatric WHO checklist 'SIGN IN'.

result.setting: Urgent laparoscopic cholecystectomy theatre list (ESAC), University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff
result.standard: National standards for complications listed on consent

cycle1.result: High variability in listed complications: 'bile leak' 75%, 'post-cholecystectomy syndrome' 55%; 50% used abbreviations; most were legible.

result.other_findings: Just over half of patients could give a moderately detailed list of complications; a procedure-specific consent form is recommended.

result.setting: Paediatric service assessing suspected appendicitis (Doncaster and Bassetlaw Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: Documented CAS 9% (1/11); surgical referral 100% (11/11); theatre 55% (6/11).

result.intervention: Educational sessions to promote the use of CAS.
result.other_findings: CAS use remained poor; all operated patients had histologically confirmed appendicitis.

result.setting: Surgical wards, large city hospital (Birmingham Heartlands Hospital)
result.standard: National (BTS) and local standards that oxygen is prescribed; SMART aim to increase prescribing by 20% each month

cycle1.result: 78% of patients not prescribed oxygen (22% prescribed).

result.intervention: PDSA cycle 1: departmental poster (seminar with induction material and system checklist notification planned for later cycles).

cycle2.result: Mean percentage prescribed increased from 22% to 60%.

result.other_findings: Later results (>75% and >95%) are projections, not measurements.

result.setting: Borders General Hospital
result.standard: 2012 National Appendicectomy Audit: negative appendicectomy rate <20%

cycle1.result: Negative appendicectomy rate 14.3% (74/518); imaged 12.8% (CT 6.3%, ultrasound 32.1%) vs no scan 17.1% (p=0.188).

result.other_findings: NAR higher in females (18.1%) than males (11.1%, p<0.05); 34.9% had no imaging before surgery.

result.setting: Department of Digestive Disease and General Surgery, Royal Sussex County Hospital

cycle1.result: Consent for virtual consultation 70%; explaining what will happen and duration 30%; confirming remote contact agreement 70%.

result.intervention: Teaching session and RCS guidelines handed to surgical consultants.
result.other_findings: Twelve consecutive clinics per cycle; introduction, history, plan and follow-up letters were satisfactory in both cycles.

result.topic: Environmental cost of printed MDT documents
result.setting: Colorectal MDT meetings, Northampton General Hospital

cycle1.result: 8078 pages (4036 sheets) printed across five MDTs; 29.1 kg CO2e total (mean 5.8 kg per MDT); cost £41.31; annualised 279 kg CO2e and £396.

result.other_findings: National estimate approximately 488 tonnes CO2e/year; switching to digital-only documentation is recommended.

result.setting: Local ENT department acute clinic (Bedfordshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Luton)
result.standard: Locally created referral guideline based on protocols from major UK trusts

cycle1.result: 29% of referrals inappropriate (50% too complex, 45% not acute, 5% double-bookings); nasal fracture reviews within 10 days one third of the time; 37% no contact number; 13.8% incorrect or unclear clinical information.

result.other_findings: An electronic referral system and guideline dissemination were introduced ahead of a planned re-audit in September 2021.

result.setting: 18 Scottish centres, elective and emergency general surgery admissions
result.standard: Documentation of pregnancy status in women of reproductive age

cycle1.result: Pregnancy status documented in 274 (51.7%): elective 52 (30.8%), emergency 222 (61.5%); possibility of pregnancy established in 237 (44.7%).

result.other_findings: Of 318 emergency admissions with abdominal pain, 211 (65.1%) had documented pregnancy status; authors advocate including it in pre-theatre safety brief and checklist.

result.setting: Adult Intellectual Disability Service, Rivington Unit, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE and GMMH guidelines for physical health monitoring with atypical antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Routine blood monitoring compliance 71.79% to 76.92%; prolactin 28.21%; ECG 17.95%.

result.other_findings: Improved documentation and communication with primary care are recommended.

result.setting: Single general surgery unit, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar

cycle1.result: 50 (17.7%) developed fascial dehiscence; lower albumin (2.45 vs 2.97 g/dl), diabetes, smoking, SSI and class 4 wounds (70% vs 44%) were associated.

result.other_findings: Suture type (loop PDS No. 1 vs PDS 2-0) did not significantly influence dehiscence.

result.setting: Elective surgical ward, NHS Tayside, Dundee
result.standard: Correct prescribing and management of regular medications before elective surgery

cycle1.result: 19/50 (38%) received medications correctly.

result.intervention: Posters in elective surgical wards (first cycle) and local departmental teaching (second cycle).
result.other_findings: After posters 56% (25/45); second cycle baseline 55% (33/60); electronic drug chart introduction under way.

result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics ward, district general hospital (Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust)
result.standard: Local Trust blood transfusion guideline (haemoglobin thresholds)
