cycle1.result: 34 units across 16 patients; 73.5% of transfusions inappropriate (patient did not meet the guideline Hb threshold); 26.4% for active haemorrhage; TACO assessment completed in 58.8%.

result.intervention: Teaching session for all rotational doctors on the Trust guideline; induction booklet highlighting the guideline.

cycle2.result: 11 units transfused; inappropriate transfusions 45.5%; 18.2% for active haemorrhage; TACO assessment 90.9%.

result.other_findings: No transfusions were for major haemorrhage.

result.setting: Acute Surgical Unit, University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust (regional centre)
result.standard: RCSEng guidelines on safe handover ('minimum' standard)

cycle1.result: 31% (26/84) of patients met the RCSEng minimum handover standard.

result.intervention: Educational guide for foundation doctors on handing over surgical patients, based on RCSEng guidelines.

cycle2.result: 67% (56/84) met the minimum standard (p=0.003) across 13 handovers.

result.other_findings: 48% (12/25) of questionnaire respondents wanted more handover teaching; the guide was added to the foundation doctor induction pack.

result.setting: Surgical emergency unit, Basildon University Hospital
result.standard: NICE diverticular disease guideline: antibiotics only if systemically unwell, immunosuppressed or complicated diverticulitis

cycle1.result: All patients (100%) with uncomplicated (Hinchey Ia) diverticulitis were prescribed antibiotics.

result.other_findings: 85% had a NEWS score of 0-1 and only 15% had pyrexia.

result.setting: University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Thy3a managed per guidance 29% in 2014 and 34% from 2015; Thy3f 83% in 2014 and 92% from 2015.

result.other_findings: Malignancy rates were 17.2% for Thy3f and 14.8% for Thy3a; most nodules were managed by diagnostic hemithyroidectomy.

result.topic: Rib fracture risk stratification and analgesia
result.setting: General surgical take (Wexham Park Hospital; Milton Keynes University Hospital)
result.standard: Battle score for rib fracture complication risk

cycle1.result: 20% (n=9) scored ≥31; 64% initially had oral analgesia only; 2.2% (n=1) regional analgesia; only four proactive critical care referrals despite 35.6% (n=16) scoring ≥21; pneumonia 20%.

result.other_findings: Two deaths, both in the ≥31 group; a local pathway based on the Battle score has been created.

result.setting: Ipswich Hospital NHS Trust
result.standard: National audit of small bowel obstruction 2017 and Bologna guidelines

cycle1.result: IV fluids 100%; analgesia 38 (88.4%); anti-emetics 36 (83.7%); NG tube 21 (72.1%); 37% of conservatively managed patients received water-soluble contrast; average time to theatre 4 days (96 hours).

result.other_findings: Contrast led to resolution in 20 patients (83.3%); an ASBO flow chart is proposed.

result.setting: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: NCEPOD and GIRFT recommendations for suspected testicular torsion

cycle1.result: 53.1% (n=17) reviewed by surgical team within 1 hour; 37.5% (n=12) explored within 1 hour of review; torsion in 21.8% (n=7), 3 (42.8%) needed orchidectomy.

result.other_findings: 7 patients (21.8%) re-presented after surgery; a new clinical pathway has been created and a re-audit is planned.

result.topic: Axillary staging in early breast cancer
result.setting: Single centre, Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Association of Breast Surgery guidelines for axillary management; axillary recurrence below 5% at 5 years

cycle1.result: All patients with U3 or higher ultrasound underwent biopsy; 25/26 B4 biopsies had ANC; axillary recurrence 3 (1.27%) at 5 years.

result.other_findings: Same abstract as DOI:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.324; SLNB in 203, ANC in 26 and sampling in 2.

result.setting: Urology patients, University Hospital Monklands, Airdrie
result.standard: Completion of the Treatment Escalation/Limitation Plan (TELP) form

cycle1.result: TELP completion 48%; correct completion 11.1%.

result.intervention: Cycle 1 findings presented at the Departmental Education Meeting.
result.other_findings: 'Discussion with patient or family' and 'patient capacity' were commonly missing; staff reported barriers such as time and document size. The 100 patients are the total across both cycles.

result.setting: 59 surgical units, online questionnaire via RCS COVID group and ALSGBI members

cycle1.result: Units performing minimal access procedures fell from 94.9% to 39.0% (P<0.001); open approach 54.2% vs 39.0% (P<0.001); post-operative COVID-19 complications 15.3%.

result.other_findings: Same abstract as DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab258.063; COVID-19 mortality was low.

result.topic: Gastrografin in adhesive small bowel obstruction
result.setting: Two NHS Trusts (Queen Elizabeth Hospital, King's Lynn)

cycle1.result: 82 patients (75.9%) opened bowels after the first dose; contrast reached the large bowel in 76 (70.3%) after the first dose.

result.other_findings: Of 10 given a second dose, 4 (40%) opened bowels and 6 (60%) required surgery.

result.setting: Adult laparoscopic appendicectomy, East Midlands hospital (University Hospitals of Leicester)

cycle1.result: 4.4% met the 2-day LOS target; mean LOS 4.3 days; imaging-to-operation 29.15 hours; digital consent 78%.

result.intervention: Increased theatre and imaging capacity, including weekend capacity.

cycle2.result: 14.3% met the 2-day target; mean LOS 3.7 days; imaging-to-operation 26.82 hours (p=0.003); digital consent 98%.

result.other_findings: Weekend admissions had shorter imaging-to-operation times (36.23 vs 21.91 hours, p<0.01); LLR remains in the highest GIRFT quartile.

result.setting: Ninewells, Dundee; NDDH, Barnstaple
result.standard: NCEPOD and GIRFT recommendations for suspected testicular torsion

cycle1.result: 53.1% (n=17) reviewed by surgical team within 1 hour; 37.5% (n=12) explored within 1 hour of review; torsion in 21.8% (n=7), 3 (42.8%) needed orchidectomy.

result.intervention: Data presented at local governance meeting and a new clinical pathway created.
result.other_findings: Post-pathway data are said to have been collected and analysed but are not reported; 7 patients (21.8%) re-presented after surgery.

result.setting: Belvedere and Rougemont wards, Franklyn Community Hospital
result.standard: Clinician assessment within 12 hours of inpatient fall, NICE head injury guideline, medication review and treatment escalation plan

cycle1.result: Medication reviewed after falls 58% (Rougemont) and 52% (Belvedere); treatment escalation plan documented 0% (Rougemont) and 43% (Belvedere).

result.other_findings: Assessment within 12 hours was generally good; a standardised falls proforma and re-audit are proposed.

result.topic: Oakland score use in lower GI bleeding
result.setting: Worcestershire Royal Hospital, emergency department
result.standard: Validated Oakland Score for safe discharge of patients presenting with PR bleeding (discharge thresholds of 8 and 10 tested)

cycle1.result: 0/72 patients had an Oakland Score on initial clerking. On retrospective application, 41/75 (55%) (threshold 8) and 42/75 (56%) (threshold 10) were admitted or discharged correctly.

result.other_findings: A threshold of 8 would have increased admissions by 20/37 (54%) and a threshold of 10 by 3/37 (8.1%); 88 notes were reviewed and 75 included.

result.setting: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust, single centre
result.standard: Guidelines advise against routine ureteric stenting after uncomplicated ureteroscopy for stones

cycle1.result: 91/143 (63.6%) were stented and 52 (36.4%) were not stented.

result.other_findings: Emergency re-presentations occurred in 7 stented patients (7.7%) and 2 non-stented patients (3.8%); day-case rates were 61.5% stented vs 75% non-stented.

result.topic: ED to ward time in delirium
result.setting: Mater Misericordiae University Hospital emergency department, Dublin
result.standard: Local Dementia/Delirium Combined Pathway and Care Bundle: door to ward admission under 6 hours for patients over 65 with suspected delirium

cycle1.result: Median ED wait for patients with 4AT ≥4 was 25.26 hours (range 6.75-83.73) vs 21.65 hours (range 5.98-50.53) with 4AT=0; the 6-hour target was not met.

result.other_findings: Only 19% (n=18) of patients with 4AT ≥4 were admitted to a specialist geriatric ward; mean length of stay was 28.457 vs 14.132 days (p=0.002).

result.setting: East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust, orthopaedic on-call

cycle1.result: Clinician obtained further contact information for 18 patients (25.3%), the electronic system had more information for 16 (22.5%), and there was no discrepancy for 37 (52.1%).

result.other_findings: About 25% of patient contact information was incomplete, which can affect theatre flow for urgent outpatient surgery.

result.topic: Scrotal exploration for suspected testicular torsion
result.setting: Grange University Hospital, Newport, general surgical unit

cycle1.result: 4/41 (9.8%) had confirmed testicular torsion. 33 of those without torsion (89.2%) underwent orchidopexy; most orchidopexies were 3-point fixation with PDS (66.7%).

result.intervention: Local intervention aiming for consensus (details not stated); second cycle planned
result.other_findings: Transverse (43.9%) and longitudinal para-median (41.5%) incisions were the most common; practice varied among general surgeons.

result.topic: New cancer diagnosis in orthopaedic inpatients
result.setting: Orthopaedic department, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow
result.standard: Scottish Cancer National Standards on wait times

cycle1.result: 68% of patients met current cancer diagnosis standards.

result.other_findings: 36% had a cancer of unknown primary and 55% were deceased at one year, higher than the Scottish average.

result.setting: Acute Surgical Ambulatory Care Unit, Altnagelvin Area Hospital, Western Health and Social Care Trust

cycle1.result: Only 40% (18/45) of calls were formally documented; 24 (53%) resulted in ASACU referral and 9 were redirected to ED.

result.other_findings: GPs initiated 78% of calls; recommendations include mandatory documentation and clear referral criteria, with a re-audit planned.

result.setting: Furness General Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Local Laparotomy Pathway (NELA): CT performed within one hour of request and reported within one hour of being performed

cycle1.result: 59% of pre-laparotomy CTs complied with the standard.

result.intervention: Dedicated 'CT Emergency Laparotomy' protocol giving the scan top priority for radiographers and radiologists
result.other_findings: 14/16 (87.5%) patients fitting urgent laparotomy criteria were operated on within 6 hours; non-compliance reasons included instability, awaiting renal profile and COVID deep cleaning.

result.setting: Northampton General Hospital, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Mean compliance score 4.91 out of 7 (70%); opioid avoidance only 2 (8%); no nasogastric tube in 22 (96%).

result.other_findings: Higher compliance was associated with shorter length of stay (p=0.01) but not 30-day morbidity; 91% mobilised by day 3.

result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedics, Prince Charles Hospital
result.standard: RCP Generic Record Keeping Standards 2, 4, 6, 10 and PRSB Section 2 Admission Record (17 admission and 8 documentation criteria)

cycle1.result: 41% of pages had appropriate patient identification; 7/17 admission criteria scored above 90%; vital signs 38%, AMTS 18%, VTE assessment 32%; 48% of entries in chronological order.

result.intervention: Updated admission proforma and education on documentation

cycle2.result: 46% of pages had correct patient identification; 5/17 admission criteria scored 90% or above; 7/8 ward entry sections improved, 62% in chronological order, 4/8 documentation criteria above 90%.

result.other_findings: The admission proforma needs further improvement to meet record-keeping standards.

result.setting: St Michael's Hospital, Dun Laoghaire, acute hospital wards
result.standard: HIQA nutrition and hydration standards (used to develop audit tool); Dementia Friendly Hospital Guidelines 2018

cycle1.result: Almost all patients had a drink and water jug available; 38% required prompting or reminding to drink.

result.other_findings: Not all patients were able to access drinks or hydrate independently.

result.setting: Adult ENT ward, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
result.standard: Modified Royal College of Surgeons of England documentation guidelines (25 parameters)

cycle1.result: Pro-forma completed for 77% of admissions.

cycle2.result: Pro-forma completed for 91%; documentation improved in 19/25 parameters, 9 significantly (including initial vital signs and differential diagnosis).

result.other_findings: Pro-forma use (n=126) significantly improved 11 parameters compared with freehand clerking (n=24).

result.topic: Extended VTE prophylaxis after cancer surgery
result.setting: Oesophagogastric unit, University Hospital Southampton
result.standard: NICE NG89: 28 days extended VTE pharmacological prophylaxis after major abdominal cancer surgery

cycle1.result: 14% compliance; median prophylaxis duration 7 days; correct weight-based dose in 89%.

result.intervention: Unit protocol change to 14 days and then 28 days postoperative prophylaxis, with clinician education

cycle2.result: 91% compliance; median duration 28 days; correct dose in 100%.

result.other_findings: Three cycles: cycle 2 (2019-21) had 26% compliance and median 23 days; 2 bleeding and 1 VTE event in cycles 1 and 2, none in cycle 3.

result.topic: Time to surgical review from ED
result.setting: The Grange University Hospital, Cwmbran, emergency department
result.standard: RCS England: surgical assessment within 30 minutes for life- or limb-threatening emergencies and 60 minutes for routine emergency referrals

cycle1.result: Mean time from referral to surgical review 103 minutes (range 5 to 476 minutes), longer than the standard.

result.other_findings: 56 (69.1%) had a surgical diagnosis, 63 (77.8%) were admitted and 16 (19.8%) had surgical intervention.

result.setting: Specialist neuropsychiatry service
result.standard: NICE guidelines for epilepsy care in patients with intellectual disability

cycle1.result: Carer involvement 100%; non-medication treatment offered 67%; special considerations for intellectual disability 24%; best interest considerations 24%; capacity assessment 19%.

result.other_findings: Waiting period ranged from 4 to 46 weeks; seizure improvement documented in 66%.

result.setting: General surgery, Whittington Hospital, London
result.standard: Trust guideline: all patients should have a treatment escalation plan form completed

cycle1.result: 21% of TEP forms were completed.

result.intervention: Results disseminated and admission clerking proforma modified

cycle2.result: 36% of admitted patients had the TEP form completed.

result.other_findings: A total of 24 patients were included across the audit.

result.topic: Length of stay for mandibular fractures
result.setting: Oral and maxillofacial surgery, Leeds General Infirmary
result.standard: GIRFT OMFS 2016: 2-day length of stay for isolated mandible fractures (1 day pre-operative, 1 day post-operative)

cycle1.result: 78% had surgery within 24 hours of admission and 92% were discharged within 24 hours post-operatively; average length of stay met the 2-day standard.

result.other_findings: Saturday admissions had the longest stays (mean pre-operative 1.60 days, total 2.55 days); reasons for delay were often not recorded or due to lack of theatre space.

result.setting: Surgical team admissions, Croydon University Hospital
result.standard: NICE head injury guideline (2014): printed advice about driving on discharge

cycle1.result: Only 2 patients had driving status documented; no patients received advice specific to DVLA guidelines.

result.other_findings: Documentation adequacy was the main limitation.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis timing in emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Morriston Hospital, Swansea Bay UHB, regional tertiary hospital
result.standard: WHO: pre-operative antibiotic prophylaxis within 120 minutes before incision; SIGN: 30-60 minutes

cycle1.result: 83% had documented POAP; 68% of these had a recorded time before incision (mean 99 minutes, range 19 to 386); 77% of those received POAP within 120 minutes.

result.other_findings: Documentation location varied (53% anaesthetic record, 31% operation note, 16% before surgery); proforma amendment planned.

result.setting: UGI, HPB and colorectal surgery inpatients, tertiary referral centre (University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire)
result.standard: Francis Report: 100% of patients aware of their responsible consultant

cycle1.result: 56.5% of patients were aware of their responsible consultant; 43.5% of headboards showed the named consultant.

result.intervention: Results presented to FY1 doctors and surgical departments; juniors given whiteboard pens for headboards
result.other_findings: Awareness improved significantly for UGI patients (p<0.001); electronic noting was introduced between cycles. 107 patients were included across both cycles.

result.setting: Single breast unit, Wrightington Wigan and Leigh NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE: SLNB for mastectomy for DCIS; considered in high-risk breast-conserving surgery

cycle1.result: 85 had WLE and 17 mastectomy; 4 high-risk BCS patients had upfront SLNB (one microinvasion); 3 of 81 BCS patients without upfront SLNB developed invasive disease and needed SLNB as a second procedure.

result.other_findings: Odds ratio for invasive disease in high-risk patients was 8.66 (95% CI 0.68–109.9, p=0.0956).

result.setting: Woodend General Hospital, NHS Grampian: theatre vs ward (DOSA)

cycle1.result: Full compliance with BSSH safety standards on ward-based lists (n=40); infection 2% (3/150) theatre vs 1.6% (2/129) DOSA (p=0.95).

result.other_findings: DOSA had shorter stays (2.2 vs 4.4 hours), fewer staff (3 vs 9) and less waste (2.1kg vs 3kg) with similar operative time.

result.topic: E. coli bacteraemia of hepatobiliary origin
result.setting: Tertiary centre, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee

cycle1.result: 68% community-acquired and 15% healthcare or hospital-associated; 89% not on clinic and 92% not on surgery waiting lists.

result.other_findings: No association was found between bacteraemia rates and waiting lists; mortality was 17%.

result.setting: Acute surgical unit, district general hospital, East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: Documentation of antibiotic indication and course length on drug charts at prescription (recommended in numerous publications)

cycle1.result: Indication documented in 54.0% and course length in 42.0%.

result.intervention: Results presented to junior doctors and reminder cards attached to drug charts

cycle2.result: Indication documented in 74.0% and course length in 68.0%.

result.other_findings: Co-amoxiclav and Tazocin were the most common agents in both cycles.

result.topic: Testicular torsion assessment and time to theatre
result.setting: General surgery department, district general hospital, Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: GIRFT national paediatric testicular torsion pathway (seven standards), following NCEPOD Twist and Shout

cycle1.result: 40% seen by surgical decision maker within 60 minutes; 0% TWIST score documented; 18% had ultrasound if >48 hours of pain; 0% in theatre within one hour; 67% of orchidectomy patients followed up.

result.intervention: Results presented, teaching on TWIST score and guideline posters in general surgery and paediatric ED

cycle2.result: 50% seen by decision maker within 60 minutes; 0% TWIST score; 50% ultrasound if >48 hours of pain; 0% in theatre within one hour; 75% followed up.

result.other_findings: 70% were seen in one or fewer healthcare settings in both cycles; TWIST score use and timing to review and theatre remain poor.

result.topic: Junior doctor knowledge of DKA management
result.setting: Department of paediatrics, Alshuhada hospital, Khartoum

cycle1.result: Correct initial fluid choice 55.5%; initial management of cerebral oedema 33.3%; investigations for suspected DKA 66%.

result.intervention: Teaching sessions (cycle 1), then posters and teaching sessions (cycle 2)

cycle2.result: Correct initial fluid choice 100%; cerebral oedema management 100%; investigations 100%.

result.other_findings: After the first cycle, figures were 88.8% for fluids, 66.7% for cerebral oedema and 77% for investigations.

result.topic: Outcomes of best supportive care in colorectal cancer
result.setting: Royal Derby Hospital, colorectal MDT

cycle1.result: Overall median survival 16 months [IQR 7-25.5]; 29 referred to palliative oncology, 14 (48%) had palliative radiotherapy and none had chemotherapy.

result.other_findings: Median survival 14 months for colonic vs 21 months for rectal primaries (p=0.35).

result.setting: Urgent MRCP pathway, district general hospital, Croydon University Hospital

cycle1.result: Median request to scan 3 days (IQR 2-6), mean 7.99 days; inpatients (n=85) median 2 days (IQR 1–4); outpatients (n=34) median 13 days (IQR 3–31).

result.other_findings: Scheduling delays (54%) and weekend delays (28%) were key contributors; 4 readmissions and 252 inpatient bed-days (£86,940) while awaiting MRCP. Protected slots and escalation triggers are planned with re-audit.

result.setting: Urological cancer MDTs across South West England Trusts
result.standard: NICE Improving Outcomes in Urological Cancer (2002) and NICE guidelines in force at the time

cycle1.result: MDTs were not consistent in decision making, and some decisions contradicted NICE guidelines.

result.other_findings: Ten anonymised patient cases were sent to the MDTs in two tranches and compared with a regional panel's optimal decisions.

result.setting: Surgical wards, Musgrove Park Hospital, Taunton
result.standard: DVLA guidance on resuming driving after surgery; driving advice documented on discharge summaries

cycle1.result: 62% had driving advice documented on discharge summaries.

result.intervention: Posters encouraging inclusion of driving advice and showing how to add it to discharge summaries
result.other_findings: Cycle 2 (October 2020, n=30) reached 80%; the fall at cycle 3 followed registrar changeover, and teaching and a fourth cycle are planned.

result.setting: District general hospital, Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: British Thyroid Association guidelines for thyroid nodule ultrasound reporting

cycle1.result: U classification used in 32.5% of reports with nodules; measurements 86.4%, characteristics 92.9%, location 96.8%; lymph node comment 89.4%.

cycle2.result: U classification 85.3%; measurements 96.0%, characteristics 100.0%, location 100.0%; lymph node comment 95.9%.

result.other_findings: FNA or referral for U3–5 nodules rose only from 71.4% to 75.0%, and 4.5% of U1/2 nodules were recommended for FNA in both cycles.

result.setting: Hand trauma clinic and ward admissions, tertiary centre (Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals)
result.standard: BSSH guidelines; RCS England Safe Handover minimum data

cycle1.result: X-ray obtained in 80%; hospital of X-ray documented in 40%; X-ray findings documented in 60%.

result.intervention: Access to a generic doctors' account for external PACS as a temporary measure; re-audit planned in 6 months
result.other_findings: Results fell from a previous audit that reported 95.5% X-ray reporting and 100% completion; lack of external PACS access was the main barrier.

result.setting: District general hospital, Barts Health NHS Trust
result.standard: European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) guidance on post-ERCP complication rates

cycle1.result: 11 patients had surgical complications: perforation 3 (1.9%), acute cholecystitis 4 (2.6%), acute pancreatitis 2 (1.3%); marginally higher than the ESGE standard.

result.other_findings: One perforation required surgery and two were managed conservatively.

result.setting: District general hospital in London (St George's, Epsom and St Helier, Kingston)
result.standard: BMJ Best Practice algorithm and National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction (NASBO) recommendations

cycle1.result: All but one had CT, 90% within 12 hours of assessment; 64% of conservatively managed patients received a water-soluble study.

result.other_findings: Seven had immediate surgery within 12 hours; of 5 who failed conservative management only one was operated on after 72 hours.

result.setting: District general hospital, surgical wards and surgical assessment unit (West Hertfordshire / Barking, Havering and Redbridge)
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology 2019 lower GI bleeding guidelines (admission advised for Oakland score >8)

cycle1.result: 37/47 (78.7%) had major LGIB, of whom 6 (16%) were discharged the same day; inpatient endoscopy 14.9%; 0% of unstable patients had CT angiogram on admission.

result.intervention: Departmental teaching session and posters of BSG guidelines on surgical wards and surgical assessment unit

cycle2.result: 29/30 (96.7%) had major LGIB and none were discharged the same day; inpatient endoscopy 66.7%; 50% of unstable patients had CT angiogram on admission.

result.other_findings: Of 10/47 minor LGIB in cycle 1, 6 (60%) were discharged the same day; impact on clinical outcomes not yet assessed.

result.topic: Dermal matrix for open foot wounds
result.setting: Tertiary vascular unit, Mid and South Essex Vascular Unit, Basildon

cycle1.result: One surgical site infection with no matrix loss and no osteomyelitis; wound healing in 5 patients after median 51 days (IQR 12 days).

result.other_findings: Two patients died before healing and one was lost to follow-up; one healed after an extra skin graft and one did not heal.

result.setting: Southport and Formby Hospital, Southport and Formby NHS Trust
result.standard: BOA 2015 Traumatic anterior shoulder instability guidelines

cycle1.result: 88% had AP and lateral X-rays; 11.9% had no pre-reduction X-ray and 1.5% no post-reduction imaging; 79% seen in clinic within 6 weeks, but only 40.3% by a shoulder specialist and 43.3% had appropriate imaging.

result.other_findings: 16.4% were not given fracture clinic follow-up; suggestions include naming fracture clinics by subspecialty and a guideline review session.

result.topic: COVID-19 risk mitigation for elective surgery
result.setting: Royal Derby Hospital, elective colorectal cancer surgery 'green' pathway
result.standard: Green pathway standards: appropriately timed pre-operative CT chest, COVID-19 swabs and shielding adherence

cycle1.dates: 6 weeks after the first wave of COVID-19
cycle1.result: All had a 2-week pre-operative swab and shielded until surgery; 48/49 had a swab 2 days pre-op; CT chest performed in all.

result.other_findings: 49 of 56 planned operations went ahead; 4 (8%) had Clavien-Dindo ≥2 complications, none COVID-related, and 1 patient tested positive post-operatively but stayed asymptomatic.

result.setting: Conquest Hospital, East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust / Medway Maritime Hospital
result.standard: National Audit of Small Bowel Obstruction (NASBO) recommendations

cycle1.result: CT on admission 98.3% (NASBO 80%), average time to CT 9 hours; surgery 27% with average time to surgery 2.4 days (NASBO 1 day); nutritional screening 100% (NASBO 90%).

result.other_findings: 30-day mortality 14% (NASBO 8%) and 30-day readmission 18% (NASBO 13%) despite shorter length of stay (7 vs 10.7 days).

result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedics, Portsmouth University Hospital
result.standard: RCS England Good Surgical Practice guidelines for operative notes

cycle1.result: Poorly documented items: emergency/elective 25%, weight bearing status 25%, VTE instructions 75%, follow-up instructions 35%, investigations after procedure 25%, wound care instructions 50%.

result.intervention: Mnemonic for post-operative instructions and presentation at departmental M&M meeting; second cycle planned
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Single breast unit, Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE: SLNB for mastectomy for DCIS; considered in high-risk breast-conserving surgery

cycle1.result: 85 had WLE and 17 mastectomy; 4 high-risk BCS patients had upfront SLNB (one microinvasion); 3 of 81 BCS patients without upfront SLNB developed invasive disease and needed SLNB as a second procedure.

result.other_findings: Odds ratio for invasive disease in high-risk patients was 8.66 (95% CI 0.68–109.9, p=0.0956).

result.setting: Acute surgical admissions at two district general hospitals, Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: TEPs documented for 39 patients (19.5%); 21 (53.8%) completed within 24 hours, 6 (15.4%) within 72 hours and 12 (30.8%) after 72 hours; CPR status recorded for all.

result.other_findings: Capacity assessments were noted in 34 cases (17%) and patient preferences in 14%; findings were similar at both sites.

result.setting: Maidstone & Tunbridge Wells NHS Trust
result.standard: Glasgow-Imrie Criteria scoring on admission for acute pancreatitis; scores ≥3 reviewed by senior and/or HDU/ITU

cycle1.result: 44% (22/50) of patients were scored using the Glasgow-Imrie Criteria.

result.intervention: Presentation, posters and email, then a scoring tick box in the electronic clerking notes

cycle2.result: 84% (49/58) scored; escalation of scores ≥3 rose from 17% to 100%.

result.other_findings: After the first intervention 66% (21/32) were scored; mean length of stay fell from 14.5 to 11 days and documentation completeness rose from 78% to 96%.

result.topic: Audit and QI in surgical training selection
result.setting: NHS England surgical specialty national selection shortlisting matrices

cycle1.result: Mean 12% of shortlisting points (range 6-35) were for audit/QI; 1/12 specialties required audit specifically and 2/12 required specialty-specific activity.

result.other_findings: Maximum points need on average 1.9 complete projects (range 1-4); applicants would generate 11,631 projects.

result.setting: District general hospital, Isle of Wight NHS Trust
result.standard: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) data entry for all emergency laparotomies

cycle1.result: 66% (n=73) of laparotomies entered into the NELA database.

result.intervention: Surgical registrars added to the NELA team, redesigned theatre booking form and continuity of team roles during doctors' inductions
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Vascular tertiary referral centre, Imperial College Hospitals Trust, London

cycle1.result: Presenting complaint 57%, diagnosis 89%, clinical history 35%, significant results 13%, outstanding tasks 6.2%.

result.intervention: New handover list on the shared drive with more comprehensive fields; junior doctors briefed

cycle2.result: Presenting complaint 92%, diagnosis 98%, clinical history 91%, significant results 86%, outstanding tasks 80% (p=0.001).

result.other_findings: 85% found the new list easier to navigate and 76% felt it reduced risk to patient safety; antibiotics and VTE fields were added after feedback.

result.topic: CT as first-line imaging in bowel obstruction
result.setting: Tertiary general surgical unit, St James's University Hospital, Leeds
result.standard: NCEPOD 'Delay in transit' 2020: CT as first definitive imaging for acute bowel obstruction

cycle1.result: Median time to decision to treat when X-ray preceded CT was 7 hours 3 minutes (IQR 4 hours 32 minutes to 16 hours 42 minutes); 82% needed CT after X-ray for decision making.

result.other_findings: The unit was not yet compliant with the NCEPOD recommendation.

result.setting: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE Guidelines (2022) on sentinel lymph node biopsy for malignant melanoma

cycle1.result: 91.4% compliance with NICE indications; no clear indication 8.6%; Breslow thickness not documented 2.9%; LVI not documented 14.3%; mitotic index not documented 14.3%.

result.intervention: Results of cycle A presented to the department

cycle2.result: 92.6% compliance; no clear indication 3/42 (7.1%); T stage and Breslow thickness documented in all; LVI and mitotic index not documented in 4/42 (9.5%) each.

result.other_findings: Pre-operative staging, Breslow thickness and intraoperative narrative were documented in 100% in both cycles; ulceration, mitotic index, LVI and node appearance need better documentation.

result.setting: General, colorectal and vascular surgery inpatients, district general hospital (Princess Alexandra Hospital)
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians: every entry dated, timed and signed with name and designation, standardised structure and chronological order

cycle1.result: 89.8% dated; 42.0% timed; 93.2% standardised structure; 6.8% had author designation and 3.4% signature.

result.other_findings: Admission entries had the most consistent structure; suggested causes include inadequate junior doctor training, ward round pace and reliance on electronic notes.

result.topic: Hip fracture mobilisation by day after surgery
result.setting: Bradford Royal Infirmary, elderly care
result.standard: NICE Hip Fracture Quality Statement 6 and NHFD KPI 4: mobilised by the day after surgery

cycle1.result: 15/23 (65%) mobilised within a day of surgery.

result.intervention: Early and regular analgesia suggested for pain; system misses discussed with the local physiotherapy team

cycle2.result: 17/23 (74%) mobilised within a day of surgery.

result.other_findings: Mobilised patients had shorter length of stay in both cycles (15.1 vs 18.1 and 21.2 vs 29.7 days); similar reasons for delay remained.

result.topic: Fertility preservation counselling in young breast cancer
result.setting: Belfast Health and Social Care Trust, regional breast unit
result.standard: European Society of Medical Oncology: young patients counselled on fertility preservation options before cancer treatment

cycle1.result: Over 50% of patients had at least one child before referral and less than 5% had considered pregnancy during or after treatment; counselling rate not reported.

result.other_findings: 23 received neoadjuvant chemotherapy first and 68 had surgery first.

result.setting: Trust inpatients (Salisbury NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: NHS Standard Contract: 95% of inpatients VTE risk assessed; NICE NG89

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment completed in 72.1%, accurate in 15.4%; prescription rate 84.6%, prescribing accuracy 41.2%.

result.intervention: Mandatory VTE prescribing training for all junior doctors joining the trust

cycle2.result: Risk assessment completion 94.2%, accuracy 34.5%; prescription rate 90.6%, prescribing accuracy 79.5%.

result.other_findings: Paediatric, obstetric and ITU patients were excluded.

result.setting: Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital, inpatients
result.standard: ENT UK advice (swabs and imaging in outpatient recognition)

cycle1.result: At admission 66% had a swab and 7% had imaging; IV antibiotics started within 24 hours in all; microbiology consulted within 6 days in 93%.

result.other_findings: Mean 2.3 presentations before admission, systemic antibiotics before admission in 20%; mean IV antibiotic duration 13 days and mean stay 19 days.

result.setting: Stockport Hospital, elective and emergency procedures
result.standard: BOAST guidelines on the safe use of intraoperative tourniquets

cycle1.result: Pressure recorded in 230 (87.8%) limb procedures; tourniquet type documented in 8.2% and exsanguination method in 34.7%; no record of skin isolation or skin condition.

result.other_findings: Mean tourniquet time 61.5 minutes, exceeding 120 minutes in 13 cases; re-audit planned in 3-4 months after education and visual aids.

result.setting: ENT department, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, London
result.standard: RCS Guidance on Safe Handover (2007) using the RAAAIDSSS handover method

cycle1.result: Good compliance; least compliant component was 'structure' at 62%.

result.intervention: Results presented at local teaching; format implemented in the handover sheet

cycle2.result: Almost all components 100% compliant except 'intake' at 90%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Operating theatres, NHS hospital
result.standard: WHO surgical safety checklist (mandated for all NHS surgery) and 5 qualitative criteria

cycle1.result: Brief 7/8, Sign In 32/34, Time Out 30/34, Sign Out 18/34, Debrief 2/8; 3/34 operations achieved grade 3.

result.other_findings: Component steps were completed more fully in major than minor operations (17.3/28 vs 8.4/28); a minor-operation checklist is suggested.

result.setting: Ashford and St Peter's Hospital NHS Trust, colonoscopy

cycle1.result: Only 10.02% of random biopsies had positive findings; 10 showed microscopic colitis.

result.other_findings: Change in bowel habit was the main indication (328), with 2.44% microscopic colitis; 10% in patients over 50 with significant diarrhoea.

result.setting: Surgical assessment unit, Southmead Hospital
result.standard: VTE risk assessment and prophylaxis at admission

cycle1.result: VTE risk documented in 92%; enoxaparin prescribed for 96%; TED stockings 96%.

result.intervention: Induction VTE teaching, HCA VTE champions, digital reminders and monthly email reminders after successive cycles

cycle2.result: VTE risk documented in 53%; enoxaparin 73%; TED stockings 73%.

result.other_findings: Five annual cycles: risk documentation 92%, 65%, 57%, 76% and 53% (2017-2021), with a drop during the first pandemic wave; electronic prescribing with mandatory VTE checklists has begun.

result.topic: Bone health in primary endocrine treatment for breast cancer
result.setting: Single consultant database, district general hospital in South Wales (Aneurin Bevan University Health Board)

cycle1.result: 5 patients (10%) had a DEXA scan and 16 (33%) were on bone protection; 3 had fractures on PET.

result.other_findings: 27 deaths (54%), mean 14 months from diagnosis to death; co-morbidity was the commonest reason for PET (65%).

result.setting: Barnet Hospital emergency department, Royal Free London NHS Trust
result.standard: BAUS/NICE guidelines for suspected ureteric colic

cycle1.result: 98% had CT-KUB within 14 hours (mean 4 hours 50 minutes); 52% received analgesia in ED (mean 3 hours 26 minutes from triage); calcium measured in 51% and urate in 4%.

result.intervention: Education and pathway review; second cycle in progress
result.other_findings: 22% had an obstructing stone; 75% of these were referred to the stone MDT and 45% had repeat CT-KUB requested.

result.setting: General surgical admissions, North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Academy of Medical Royal Colleges Guide to Record Keeping Standards

cycle1.result: Consultant review documented within 14 hours of admission 47%; social history taking 58%.

result.intervention: Introduction of a doctor's assistant role as part of the extended surgical team.

cycle2.result: Consultant review documented within 14 hours of admission 97%; social history taking 75%; standardised proforma, MUST score and VTE prescriptions remained >85%.

result.other_findings: Dementia screening tool completion and oxygen prescriptions improved somewhat but still needed improvement.

result.setting: District general hospital, Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust; patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy

cycle1.result: 88% received the EIDO patient information leaflet; 19% did not know what a gallbladder was or described the wrong organ; 76% had day-of-surgery consent; 50% of consultants said they were not allocated enough time to initiate consent to this standard.

result.intervention: Departmental teaching session; SHOs allocated to clinics with consultants; training video for SHOs and operative video for patients in production.
result.other_findings: Survey tool piloted on 8 patients first; SHOs were unsure of procedural complications but still took day-of-surgery consent.

result.setting: Adult surgical inpatients on maintenance IV fluids, district general hospital, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, Wrexham

cycle1.result: About 50% of patients prescribed appropriate IV fluid volumes; FY1 survey mean score 54%.

result.intervention: Tutorial on fluid management for FY1s and a fluid management algorithm made available in SAU.

cycle2.result: Some improvement in appropriate volumes and choice of maintenance fluids; FY1 survey score 64%.

result.other_findings: Previous fluid prescriptions were often copied.

result.setting: Watford General Hospital, emergency laparotomy cases (NELA data)
result.standard: ASGBI and NCEPOD recommendations on small bowel obstruction management

cycle1.result: 198 emergency laparotomies with 24 mortalities (12%); 87 SBO cases with 12 mortalities (SBO operative mortality 14%); SBO accounted for 50% of emergency laparotomy deaths.

result.intervention: SBO management flowchart and allocation of a theatre slot within 72 hours for patients suitable for operation.

cycle2.result: 152 emergency laparotomies with 13 mortalities (9%); 57 SBO cases with 3 mortalities (SBO operative mortality 5%); SBO-related deaths 23% of emergency laparotomy deaths.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Leeds Neurosurgery department, referrals for suspected cauda equina syndrome
result.standard: BASS/SBNS national guidelines: MRI before referral for suspected CES

cycle1.result: 15% of referrals had an MRI before referral (15.5% in hours, 14.5% out of hours); 65 had radiologically confirmed CES; 31% increase in referrals compared with before the ENTICE study.

result.other_findings: 8% of referrals from centres with out-of-hours scanning had no MRI before referral; only 7% of referrals had confirmed CES.

result.setting: Frimley Park Hospital Foundation Trust, emergency laparotomy theatre cases
result.standard: NELA and Royal College standards: NELA score documented by ST3+, frailty assessment in patients 65+

cycle1.result: NELA score documented 39.6%; documented by ST3+ 24.8%; P-POSSUM documented 61.4%; both NELA and P-POSSUM 32.7%; frailty assessed in 38.6% of patients 65+.

result.other_findings: Authors propose education and procedural change with re-audit.

result.setting: District general hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Trust; SPC inserted in theatre
result.standard: BAUS guidelines: open or ultrasound-guided SPC insertion in patients with previous lower abdominal surgery

cycle1.result: 21 (13.6%) had previous lower abdominal surgery: 2 (10%) ultrasound-guided, 3 (14%) open, 11 (52%) cystoscopy-guided alone, 5 (24%) unknown; 4 (2.6%) bowel injuries overall.

result.other_findings: None of the bowel injuries occurred in patients with previous lower abdominal surgery; authors recommend image-guided insertion in all patients where possible.

result.setting: South West London Elective Orthopaedic Centre, high-volume elective orthopaedic theatres
result.standard: Local theatre protocol: team meeting to start at 08:00

cycle1.result: Average team brief start time 08:05; 17/18 (94%) late starts due to surgeon/anaesthetist lateness.

result.intervention: Findings presented at clinical governance; changes to local protocols.

cycle2.result: Average team brief start time 08:08; 10/22 (45%) late starts due to surgeon/anaesthetist lateness.

result.other_findings: Late starts led to further delays in sending for patients; extraneous factors contributed to later average start times in the second cycle.

result.setting: Freeman Hospital, Newcastle

cycle1.result: 98% same-day discharge; 17/88 complications (UTI 8%, haematuria 3%, urethral stricture 3%, salvage HoLEP 1%); 97% successful initial TWOC; 80% of 71 followed up reported complete symptomatic benefit; mean wait 154 days.

result.other_findings: Mean prostate size 57cc for GLPVP versus 41cc for TURP; 25/88 anticoagulated.

result.topic: Single-dose intravesical mitomycin C after TURBT
result.setting: Tertiary urology service, Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust, Chelmsford
result.standard: NICE NG2 1.2.7: single dose of intravesical mitomycin C at first TURBT for new bladder cancer

cycle1.result: 5-10% compliance.

result.intervention: Initial audit presented at departmental meeting in 2023.

cycle2.result: MMC given in 28 (36% compliance); 86% of these given post-operatively (n=24); not given in 49 (63.6%), with no documented reason in 76% (n=37) and bleeding-related risk in 7 (14%).

result.other_findings: Third cycle planned to measure the effect of a new electronic prescribing system and new TURBT proforma.

result.setting: District general hospital vascular service (King's College Hospital / West Hertfordshire NHS Trust)
result.standard: Society for Vascular Surgery: clinical examination, ABPI and duplex at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months then annually

cycle1.result: 8 patients (40%) had a duplex within 1 month; 10% had no scan; time to first duplex 1-11 months (mean 4 months); all discharged on antiplatelet, 70% on statins.

result.intervention: Suggested booking duplex in theatre after the procedure, junior doctor education and re-audit in 1 year (not yet done).
result.other_findings: Six patients needed intervention for blocked grafts and failed; only one had timely duplex and was salvaged by angioplasty. Weekend discharges by general surgery made duplex booking unlikely.

result.topic: Consent documentation in patients lacking capacity
result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedics, University Hospital Southampton; patients with dementia undergoing emergency orthopaedic operations
result.standard: GMC guidance: discuss with close family members when patients lack capacity

cycle1.result: 36% compliance; 9 of 30 cases had documented discussion with an appropriate family member.

result.intervention: Results presented at local meeting; teaching session, posters and email from the clinical lead.
result.other_findings: Further audit loops planned to sustain improvement.

result.topic: Laparoscopic peritoneal dialysis catheter insertion outcomes
result.setting: Laparoscopic PD catheter insertion service, NHS Lanarkshire (University Hospital Monklands)
result.standard: International Society for Peritoneal Dialysis (ISPD) guidelines

cycle1.result: 0% 30-day peritonitis and SSI; 6-month PD peritonitis 22% (4/18); urinary retention 11% (2/18); overnight stay 83% (15/18).

result.intervention: Maturation of the reintroduced service over time (no specific change described).

cycle2.result: 0% 30-day peritonitis and SSI; 6-month PD peritonitis 5.8% (2/34); urinary retention 2.9% (1/34); overnight stay 44.1% (15/34).

result.other_findings: Only one case of PD peritonitis had a positive fluid culture (Stenotrophomonas maltophilia).

result.topic: Community-acquired pneumonia care by route of admission
result.setting: British Thoracic Society national community-acquired pneumonia audit dataset
result.standard: National CAP guidelines: chest X-ray within 4 h, first antibiotic within 4 h, antibiotic choice and route (secondary outcomes)

cycle1.result: 75.6% admitted via ED; adjusted 30-day mortality similar for ED vs non-ED (OR 1.10, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.25); ED admission associated with chest X-ray within 4 h (adjusted OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.79 to 4.12) and first antibiotic within 4 h (adjusted OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.42 to 1.84).

result.other_findings: ED admissions had more comorbidity and severity and greater use of IV antibiotics regardless of severity (adjusted OR 1.58, 95% CI 1.43 to 1.74).

result.topic: Rota gaps, locum cover and trainee theatre time
result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, Huddersfield Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Safe daily staffing levels as per rota

cycle1.result: Safe staffing daily; locums covered 36.6% of ward duties and 42.9% of on-call shifts, costing £25,190.

result.intervention: Advanced Clinical Practitioners rostered to cover trauma wards.

cycle2.result: Safe staffing daily; locum cover of ward duties 23.7% and on-calls 33.3%; locum cost £17,050 (saving £8,140 over three weeks).

result.other_findings: Protected theatre allocation for core surgical trainees remained less than 1 day/week.

result.topic: Rescheduling of cancelled elective operations within 28 days
result.setting: Tertiary vascular surgery department, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, London
result.standard: NHS Constitution: procedures cancelled for non-clinical reasons rescheduled within 28 days

cycle1.result: 165 of 402 scheduled procedures cancelled; 28-day rescheduling 14.75% (17.5% open, 12.0% endovascular).

result.intervention: Results communicated to consultants, admissions and waiting list manager and cardiovascular service manager; targeted departmental collaboration and awareness of guidelines.

cycle2.result: 28-day rescheduling 65.2% (15/23) for open and 87.7% (57/65) for endovascular procedures.

result.other_findings: Bed unavailability remained the main reason for cancellation.

result.topic: Inpatient falls prevention and post-fall management
result.setting: National Audit of Inpatient Falls, all hospitals in England and Wales (inpatient femoral fractures from National Hip Fracture Database)
result.standard: NICE guidelines/quality standards for multifactorial falls risk assessment and safe post-fall management

cycle1.result: Checked for injury before moving from floor 69%; flat lifting equipment 22%; medical assessment within 30 mins of fall 52%.

result.intervention: Continuous national audit with improvement resources and activities.

cycle2.result: Checked for injury before moving 77%; flat lifting equipment 29%; medical assessment within 30 mins 60%.

result.other_findings: Around 2000 inpatient femoral fractures a year; these patients have double the 30-day mortality of those who fracture elsewhere. Most aspects of MFRA improved.

result.setting: On-call surgical team, East Surrey Hospital, Redhill; patients assessed but not admitted
result.standard: NHS Standard Contract: discharge summary within 24 hours of assessment and discharge

cycle1.result: 18 of 47 (38.3%) had a clinical note or discharge summary on the electronic system; 6 (12.8%) had a discharge summary.

result.intervention: Planned: highlight importance to juniors at surgical meeting before re-audit.
result.other_findings: Of 9 patients discharged directly from A&E, 3 had a note or summary completed.

result.setting: District general hospital, Mid Yorkshire NHS Teaching Trust, Wakefield
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology LGIB guidelines

cycle1.result: 11 (25%) had no imaging, treatment or procedure; 6 (14%) unnecessary admissions per BSG criteria; 7 (16%) transfused, 3 (7%) not meeting BSG criteria; 2 (5%) CT angiogram with Shock Index <1; 4 (9%) with Shock Index >1 had no CT angiogram.

result.other_findings: 3 (7%) had inpatient flexible sigmoidoscopy despite haemodynamic stability; virtual wards suggested to prevent unnecessary admissions.

result.setting: Royal Devon and Exeter NHS Foundation Trust after move to electronic record system
result.standard: Required follow-up (wound assessment clinic, hand therapy, outpatient clinic) per operation note booked or requested

cycle1.dates: First week of new electronic system (October 2020)
cycle1.result: WAC 100% (24/24) and hand therapy 100% (13/13) completed; 14% (4/27) of required OPC appointments not requested.

result.intervention: Departmental education on the new electronic system.

cycle2.result: Similar results; 12% (4/31) OPC follow-up not requested, all where the operation note did not specify whether follow-up was required.

result.other_findings: Stating the follow-up plan in the operation note, including when none is needed, is recommended.

result.topic: Index admission cholecystectomy for gallstone pancreatitis
result.setting: Royal Berkshire Hospital, Reading
result.standard: BSG guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy during index admission or within 2 weeks of discharge

cycle1.result: 14 (67%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy, 9 (64%) of these within 2 weeks; 7 (33%) had no surgery; median wait 3 days, average 64 days; 6 readmissions while waiting.

result.intervention: Weekly semi-emergency theatre list introduced; re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: Of those not operated, 4 were not eligible, 1 went private and 2 were awaiting surgery; pain was the commonest readmission reason.

result.setting: Acute Surgical Unit, University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust (regional centre), evening handover

cycle1.result: 15 handovers; 31% (26/84) of patients met the RCSEng minimum standard.

result.intervention: Educational handover guide for foundation doctors based on RCSEng guidelines, later added to the induction pack.
result.other_findings: Of 25 questionnaire responses (92% foundation doctors), 48% (12/25) wanted more teaching on handover.

result.setting: The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust, emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy consent forms
result.standard: Documentation of 15 commonly accepted risks of laparoscopic cholecystectomy

cycle1.result: Bleeding, infection and conversion to open documented in 100%; keloid 17.4%, death 2.2%, chest infection 6.5%.

result.intervention: Pre-printed consent form template listing all standard risks.

cycle2.result: All 15 risks documented in 100% of cases.

result.other_findings: Limited by smaller post-intervention sample and short re-audit period.

result.topic: Orbital fracture imaging and eye assessment
result.setting: Oral and maxillofacial surgery, teaching hospital, University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: GIRFT orbital fracture pathway: appropriate imaging and ophthalmic/orthoptic referral

cycle1.result: All 27 had CT; 12 met criteria for plain radiographs but only 3 (25%) had them first; 15 had ophthalmic and 13 orthoptic assessment; 12 had neither.

result.other_findings: The 12 without ophthalmic or orthoptic assessment had no positive findings beyond mild bruising or swelling; a local protocol with a checklist of physical signs is proposed.

result.setting: George Eliot Hospital, elective colorectal resections
result.standard: ERAS protocol elements (pre-, intra- and post-operative)

cycle1.result: Counselling documentation 6.25%; pre-operative documentation 93.75%; fasting 87.5%; carbohydrate drink 75%; regional anaesthesia and normothermia 100%; NG tubes 25%; drains 14/16; opioids 100%; POD1 mobilisation 75%.

cycle2.result: All pre-operative measures 100%; mobilisation within 24 hours 85%; liquids by POD1 95%; solids by POD3 85%; median LOS 5 days; drains 85%, NG tubes 80%, opioids 100%.

result.other_findings: Drain and NG tube use and universal opioid use remained high and are targets for the next cycle.

result.topic: Extended VTE prophylaxis after abdominal surgery
result.setting: Stockport NHS Foundation Trust, patients over 16 undergoing surgery for appendicitis
result.standard: NICE NG89: pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for a minimum of 7 days after abdominal surgery and mechanical prophylaxis from admission

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment completed in 12 (52.2%); TEDS 15/23 (65.2%); enoxaparin 18 (78.2%); 4 (17.4%) had no prophylaxis; none prescribed seven days of pharmacological prophylaxis.

result.other_findings: Mean hospital stay 2.8 days; prophylaxis often missed in short stays.

result.setting: Bronglais General Hospital, Aberystwyth, rural general hospital managed by on-call general surgeons
result.standard: Available national and international guidelines on testicular torsion

cycle1.result: 13 had torsion; 4 of these had a non-viable testis, 3 of whom presented late (1-3 days after onset).

result.intervention: Local protocol being developed with direct referral to on-call surgical registrar and TWIST score.
result.other_findings: Management judged timely; raising awareness among children and carers is emphasised.

result.setting: Southport and Formby Hospital
result.standard: BOA 2015 traumatic anterior shoulder instability guidelines

cycle1.result: 88% had AP and lateral x-rays; 8.9% pre-reduction AP only; 11.9% no pre-reduction x-ray; 1.5% no post-reduction imaging; 79% seen in clinic within 6 weeks; 40.3% seen by a shoulder specialist; 43.3% had appropriate imaging; 16.4% not given fracture clinic follow-up.

result.intervention: Suggested: rename fracture clinics by subspecialty and a session reviewing the guideline with senior surgeons.
result.other_findings: Acute management mostly compliant; follow-up and later investigation were weaker.

result.setting: General surgery department, South Tyneside and Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust (2 hospitals), elective operations
result.standard: Trust policy of two-stage consent process

cycle1.result: 58% of electronic consent forms generated on the date of surgery rather than at first clinic consultation.

result.other_findings: Main error was consent confirmation signed but not dated, mostly in forms generated on the day of surgery.

result.setting: Medway Maritime Hospital, Kent
result.standard: IAP/APA and BSG guidance: diagnosis within 48 hours, ultrasound within 24 hours of diagnosis, CT at 72-96 hours after onset or after 48 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Correct diagnosis within 48 hours 90%; CT after 48 hours of admission 6.15%; CT within 72-96 hours of onset 29.23%; ultrasound within 24 hours 17%; CT initial imaging in 75%.

result.other_findings: Staff education and increased ultrasound availability suggested.

result.topic: Sentinel lymph node biopsy eligibility in melanoma
result.setting: Royal Free Hospital, London
result.standard: NICE 2022 melanoma guideline: SLNB for Breslow >1mm, consider for 0.8-1mm with ulceration, lymphovascular invasion or mitotic rate ≥2/mm2

cycle1.result: Compliance 97.4%.

result.intervention: Ongoing departmental audit (no specific intervention described).

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 53/61 (87%); of 15 with Breslow 0.8-1mm, 7/15 (46.7%) appropriately offered SLNB, 7/15 (46.7%) did not meet criteria, 1/15 (6.7%) lacked documentation.

result.other_findings: All 15 patients with Breslow 0.8-1mm had negative nodes; compliance fell compared with the previous cycle.

result.setting: Tertiary care centre, University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust; inpatients and ambulatory care unit
result.standard: WSES recommendations: flexible sigmoidoscopy not required after CT-proven uncomplicated acute diverticulitis without red flags

cycle1.result: 80 of 115 admissions (69.5%) had CT-proven UAD; 39 (48.8%) booked for flexible sigmoidoscopy; 10 (25.64%) had sub-centimetre polyps.

cycle2.result: 34 of 49 patients had UAD; 10 (29.4%) underwent flexible sigmoidoscopy; polyps in 3 (8.8%).

result.other_findings: Low rate of positive findings suggests outpatient sigmoidoscopy requests in uncomplicated cases were unjustified.

result.setting: Ninewells Hospital, NHS Tayside; geriatrician-led Surgical Acute Frailty Team, ELLSA patients aged ≥65
result.standard: NELA frailty and care of the elderly review recommendations (compared with 31.8% in 8th NELA report)

cycle1.result: 98.6% had documented Clinical Frailty Scale score (mean 3.6); 87.7% reviewed by SAFT; 63.3% had pre-operative frailty review.

result.intervention: Frailty screening on admission, weekly ELLSA MDT and designated ELLSA MDT board introduced, aiming for 100% geriatrician review.
result.other_findings: 70% discharged home independently; 7% needed a care package.

result.setting: Single-centre district general hospital, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board; emergency general surgical take

cycle1.result: 188 bleeps (average 37 per day: SHO 11, registrar 26); mean 34 patients clerked and 17 admissions per day.

result.intervention: eReferral pathway: all general surgical referrals from ED placed on an online platform, with bleeps reserved for patients of clinical concern; guidance and training provided.

cycle2.result: 189 bleeps (average 38 per day: SHO 13, registrar 25); mean 39 patients clerked and 22 admissions per day.

result.other_findings: eReferral did not reduce bleeps and possibly increased referrals.

result.setting: Elective upper GI surgery ward, tertiary hospital, Hull University Teaching Hospitals
result.standard: Trust policy and NICE guidance: 95% VTE risk assessment completion within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: 75% of VTE assessments completed.

result.intervention: Issue raised at departmental governance; ward junior doctors given responsibility for daily checking and completion; fortnightly snap audits.

cycle2.result: Compliance increased to 89% and then to 98.5%.

result.other_findings: Sustainability with rotating juniors expected to be the main issue; induction teaching and a 'VTE champion' recommended.

result.setting: ASD diagnostic pathway, Greater Preston area; children under 18
result.standard: NICE: first appointment within 13 weeks of referral; follow-up within 6 weeks of diagnosis

cycle1.result: Seen within 13 weeks: 18.9% of school-age and 16.7% of preschool children; follow-up within 6 weeks: 18.9% of school-age and 20.8% of preschool children.

result.other_findings: 37 school-age and 48 preschool children included.

result.setting: General surgery department, district general hospital, Kettering General Hospital
result.standard: RCS guidance on operation note documentation (18 elements)

cycle1.result: Time of operation recorded in 9%; signed by surgeon in 46%; satisfactory adherence to most other elements.

result.intervention: Results communicated to surgeons and electronic operation note templates updated.

cycle2.result: Time of operation recorded in 76%; signed by surgeon in 67%.

result.other_findings: Continuous audit cycle recommended to maintain standards.

result.setting: Acute adult mental health wards/PICU and specialist NHS addictions units in 45 NHS mental health trusts (POMH national audit)
result.standard: POMH audit standards for medically assisted alcohol withdrawal

cycle1.result: 908 patients on acute wards/PICU and 347 in specialist addictions units; MAAW overseen by an addiction specialist in 33 (4%) of acute ward patients.

result.other_findings: Alcohol history, breath alcohol, Wernicke's screening, parenteral thiamine, relapse-prevention prescribing and referral for continuing care were more often documented with specialist addictions involvement.

result.setting: Ophthalmology department, Galway University Hospital

cycle1.result: Macular hole closure rate 96.55%; logMAR change at 6 weeks -0.29 (SD 0.29, P=.22).

result.other_findings: No significant difference between ILM peel (N=21) and ILM peel with graft or flap (N=11).

result.setting: Surgical assessment unit, district hospital (Pinderfields Hospital)
result.standard: NICE NG147: aetiology identified in at least 80%, no more than 20% idiopathic

cycle1.result: Biliary 88 (30%), alcohol 40 (16%), other 20 (7%), idiopathic 134 (46%).

result.intervention: Action plan for detailed history and step-wise investigation formulated.
result.other_findings: Other blood tests often not done in index admission, drug history not elicited, and repeat ultrasound not done.

result.topic: Pre-operative feed fasting in burns patients
result.setting: Northern Regional Burn Centre, Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle; major burns patients on NG feeding

cycle1.result: Calories lost 2226-23,929kcal (7% to 39% of prescribed, mean 17.6%); protein lost 143g-1,240g (7% to 40%, mean 19.4%).

result.other_findings: Authors recommend adding nasojejunal feeding to the burns nutrition policy.

result.topic: Straight-to-test CT pathway for emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Stepping Hill Hospital, emergency department and emergency general surgery
result.standard: National guidelines: senior surgical assessment of emergency laparotomy patients; NELA data

cycle1.dates: 1 week (EGS admissions) and 2 weeks (ED GI-coded patients)
cycle1.result: EGS audit: 23 CTs, 50% needed GS admission, 25% another specialty, 25% no admission. ED audit: 147 GI-coded patients, 34 potential EL, 20 had CT, only 15 referred to GS.

result.intervention: Straight-to-test CT pathway drawn up using local characteristics and NELA data.

cycle2.result: 139 CTs, no discrepancies; 7 EL patients (5%); 134 (96%) changed management; 66 (54%) admissions avoided; 11% new cancers; 10-12 STT CTs per day needed (1/30,000 population/day).

result.other_findings: 66 EGS admissions (132 bed days) avoided.

result.topic: Single-dose intravesical mitomycin C after TURBT
result.setting: Glasgow Royal Infirmary
result.standard: NICE guidelines: intravesical chemotherapy after TURBT for new and recurrent tumours

cycle1.result: Mean time from end of TURBT to mitomycin C instillation 7.66 hours.

result.intervention: Improved communication between theatre staff, nursing staff and pharmacy to deliver IVCT to theatre.

cycle2.result: Third cycle: mean interval 4.24 hours; 24-hour administration rate >90%.

result.other_findings: Second cycle (24 patients) showed mean interval of 4.67 hours.

result.topic: VP shunt valve documentation in operation notes
result.setting: Queen's Medical Centre, Nottingham University Hospital
result.standard: Documentation of shunt valve type and settings in the operation note

cycle1.result: Valve type and settings documented in 209/247 procedures; 3 of 55 programmable valve procedures lacked documentation.

result.intervention: Action plan agreed after first audit (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Documented in 96/107 procedures; all 33 programmable valve procedures properly documented.

result.other_findings: 11/107 procedures still lacked valve type and settings documentation.

result.setting: Craigavon Area Hospital, single surgeon's potentially curative rectal resections
result.standard: Published standards for tumour perforation and CRM positivity

cycle1.result: R0 resection 94.1%; R1 (nodes or deposit <1mm from margin) 3.92% and 1.96%; tumour perforation 3.92% (all pre-operative); local recurrence 5.88%; 90-day mortality 1.96%; median LOS 7 days.

result.other_findings: This is a re-audit; the previous audit also showed rates below published standards but its figures are not given.

result.setting: Emergency Surgical Unit, Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
result.standard: National peer review monthly readmission figure (1.71%-7.53%)

cycle1.result: 39 recorded readmissions (11.8%); true 30-day readmission rate 17 (5.1%); 7/17 had a post-operative complication.

result.other_findings: Trust coding overstated readmissions; most readmissions could have been managed in a surgical ambulatory service. No mortalities.

result.setting: Plastic surgery inpatients staying longer than 24 h, Sheffield Teaching Hospital
result.standard: Trust VTE risk assessment guideline and form; target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: Chemoprophylaxis prescribing 69.5%; VTE risk assessment form used 0%; inappropriate chemoprophylaxis 18.8%.

result.intervention: Results presented at departmental meeting; VTE checkbox added to handover list; posters in doctors' office with VTE forms attached.

cycle2.result: Chemoprophylaxis prescribing 95%; VTE form used 70%; inappropriate chemoprophylaxis 8%; mechanical prophylaxis increased by 15.8%.

result.other_findings: 100% target not met; electronic VTE assessment recommended because of junior doctor turnover.

result.setting: ENT emergency outpatient clinics, St George's Hospital, London
result.standard: ENT UK guidelines: oral steroids first line, intratympanic steroids if no improvement

cycle1.result: 36 referred, 18 (50%) confirmed on PTA; 15 (83.3%) received oral prednisolone, 3 (20%) improved; of 13 with no or partial response, 5 (38%) received IT steroids; 4 of 6 (67%) given IT injections improved.

result.other_findings: 8 (62%) non-responders did not get IT injections, mainly due to delay from symptom onset (6), plus 1 declined and 1 moved away.

result.setting: Hand Therapy Trauma Clinic, Mid Yorkshire Teaching NHS Trust, Wakefield
result.standard: BSSH closed hand fracture guidelines: clear documentation of the decision for non-operative management

cycle1.result: Electronic documentation of referral 8%.

result.intervention: Intervention made after initial audit (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Electronic documentation of referral 17% (p=0.45); specific diagnosis 34 (94%); senior input documented 32 (89%); detailed mechanism of injury 64%.

result.other_findings: 21 adults (58%) and 15 children (42%).

result.topic: Bone health assessment after fragility fracture
result.setting: 48-bed rehabilitation unit, Tymon North Rehabilitation Unit, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Database key performance indicator for bone health assessment

cycle1.result: All charted for vitamin D; 13 already given bone protection; 6 had a documented plan not yet given; 1 had no clear plan.

result.intervention: Bone health round designed to ensure documented assessment.
result.other_findings: 15 were hip fractures; delays due to vitamin D deficiency, dental issues and pharmacy access; 2 patients had denosumab charted only as a one-time dose.

result.topic: Urine culture before antibiotics for UTI
result.setting: Urology on-call team, Freeman Hospital, Newcastle upon Tyne
result.standard: NICE guidelines: urine culture sent for suspected UTI, ideally before starting antibiotics

cycle1.result: 41 (91%) had urine culture sent, 4 (9%) none; of those sent, 34 (83%) before antibiotics and 7 (17%) after the first dose.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: NHS Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh Foundation Trust, laparoscopic cholecystectomies
result.standard: Correct HRG coding based on comorbidity and complication index

cycle1.result: 69.23% of procedures coded incorrectly; £72,232 lost potential tariff (£372.33 per cholecystectomy); commonest correct code GA10J (CCI 3 in 29%), commonest wrong code GA10K (presumed CCI 0).

result.intervention: Education and awareness under way before re-audit.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: NELA case ascertainment and data entry
result.setting: District general hospital, North Manchester General Hospital; emergency laparotomies
result.standard: NELA requirement: all emergency laparotomies registered and submitted by the deadline

cycle1.result: 31 (50%) entered; 4 (13%) met submission deadline; 18 (67%) registered more than 6 months after discharge; average delay 206 days.

cycle2.result: 84% registered in Year 9 and 95% in Year 10; average time to entry 100 days; all submitted before the deadline.

result.other_findings: Year 9 had 75 and Year 10 had 38 patients.

result.setting: Tertiary vascular centre, Royal Free Hospital, London
result.standard: Good Surgical Practice framework for operation notes

cycle1.result: Antibiotic prophylaxis recorded in 4/31 (13%); post-operative anticoagulation in 21/31 (68%).

result.intervention: Electronic patient record introduced, then departmental education (posters, regular teaching sessions, presentations).

cycle2.result: After education: antibiotic prophylaxis 18/30 (60%); post-operative anticoagulation 22/30 (73%).

result.other_findings: After EPR alone (October 2021, 28 operations): antibiotic prophylaxis 16/28 (57%), anticoagulation 17/28 (61%). Vascular proformas planned.

result.setting: UK national registry, 7th National Audit Project of the Royal College of Anaesthetists

cycle1.result: Incidence 3 in 10,000 anaesthetics (95%CI 3.0-3.5 per 10,000); commonest causes major haemorrhage (17%), bradyarrhythmia (9%), cardiac ischaemia (7%).

result.other_findings: Cardiac arrest most prevalent in orthopaedic trauma (12%) and lower GI surgery (10%); patient factors a key cause in 82%, anaesthesia 40%, surgery 35%.

result.setting: University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay Trust, Lancaster

cycle1.result: Thy3a managed per guidance 29% in 2014 and 34% from 2015; Thy3f 83% in 2014 and 92% from 2015.

result.other_findings: Malignancy rates 17.2% for Thy3f and 14.8% for Thy3a; both were mostly managed by diagnostic hemithyroidectomy.

result.setting: Emergency department, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board, Newport
result.standard: BAUS and NICE renal colic recommendations: CT within 14 hours, NSAIDs, referral criteria

cycle1.result: NSAIDs prescribed 87%; CT within 14 hours 93%; 100% meeting referral criteria referred; 67% not meeting referral criteria referred.

result.intervention: Updated NSAID dosing and updated health board renal colic pathway.

cycle2.result: NSAIDs prescribed 50%; CT within 14 hours 100%; 50% not meeting referral criteria referred.

result.other_findings: Low numbers; all patients having CT KUB suggested as a better identifier for future audits.

result.setting: Surgical inpatients, Lincoln County Hospital NHS Trust
result.standard: WHO analgesic ladder and NICE 147 guideline

cycle1.result: Pain managed adequately in 30%; anti-emetics offered to 92%.

cycle2.result: Pain managed adequately in 46%; prophylactic laxatives prescribed in 100% of eligible patients; anti-emetics 82%.

result.other_findings: Inadequate prescribing habits reported as 30% vs 16% between cycles; staff changeover affected prescribing.

result.setting: Orthopaedic department, Bristol Royal Infirmary
result.standard: BOAST standards for documentation of mobilisation and weightbearing after orthopaedic surgery

cycle1.result: 11 operation notes compliant; lower limb (excluding NOF) 14% (7/50), upper limb 7% (4/59), neck of femur 0% (0/50).

result.intervention: Suggested reformatting of the operation note and education (not yet done).
result.other_findings: All but one NOF note ticked 'full weightbearing' rather than the new term 'unrestricted weightbearing'.

result.setting: Geriatric wards, Healthcare of Older People Department, Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Documentation of discharge summary and functional status in electronic discharge letters

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Compulsory discharge summary template introduced on all geriatric wards.

cycle2.result: Documentation of summaries in discharge letters improved (figures given in a table not supplied).

result.other_findings: 162 discharged in second cycle; 18 deceased and 4 without letters excluded.

result.setting: West Middlesex University Hospital, surgical inpatients
result.standard: Public Health England antimicrobial standards: documentation of allergy status, prescriber contact, indication and review/stop dates; appropriate antimicrobial choice and IV/total duration

cycle1.result: Prescriber contact details 69%, review/stop dates 17%, indications 78%, appropriate selection 76%, appropriate IV duration 63%, total duration 87%.

result.intervention: Educational session, once-weekly microbiology round of surgical inpatients and introduction of electronic prescribing (Cerner).

cycle2.result: Prescriber contact details 100%, review/stop dates 100%, indications 96%, selection 90%, IV duration 93%, total duration 100%; p < 0.05 throughout.

result.other_findings: E-prescribing prompts clinicians to enter contact details, review dates and indications before prescribing, which partly explained the improvement.

result.setting: General surgical ward, Gloucestershire Royal Hospital (general hospital)
result.standard: ReSPECT forms (Resuscitation Council UK) completed for surgical inpatients

cycle1.result: Completion rate of accurate ReSPECT forms 31%.

result.intervention: Cycle 1 intervention: a ReSPECT column added to the surgical take list. Cycle 2 intervention: team education with a novel prioritisation poster and a teaching session.

cycle2.result: After the poster and teaching, ReSPECT column use rose to 39% and overall completion was 33%.

result.other_findings: After the take-list column alone, the column was completed for 15% of inpatients and overall completion was 35%.

result.topic: Acute pancreatitis with GLP-1 receptor agonist use
result.setting: 105 UK hospitals (national snapshot audit, White Rose and North West research collaboratives)
result.standard: Compliance with MHRA Yellow Card reporting

cycle1.result: 8% of patients with proven acute pancreatitis were taking a GLP-1RA; fewer than 5% of these cases were reported to the MHRA. Critical care admission 4.8% (GLP-1RA) vs 4.2% (non-GLP-1RA).

result.other_findings: Interim analysis; GLP-1RA use was mostly for weight loss (90%) and often sourced from private pharmacies (42%). Gallstones were the commonest aetiology (54%).

result.setting: St John's Wood PCN, North Westminster community mental health team
result.standard: Rate of did-not-attends for outpatient appointments (no target stated)

cycle1.result: Mean DNA rate 7.5%.

result.intervention: SMS reminders sent one working day before each scheduled appointment.

cycle2.result: Mean DNA rate 5.0% (33.3% improvement); range from 8.3% (highest) to 4.1% (lowest).

result.other_findings: A re-audit at 12 months is recommended to assess sustained effect.

result.topic: Emergency laparotomy risk scoring and documentation
result.setting: North Manchester General Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: NELA guidance on preoperative risk stratification and NELA fifth report recommendations

cycle1.result: NELA risk score documented in 26%; NELA score discussion with patient/family documented in 14%.

result.other_findings: Even when the NELA score was calculated preoperatively, discussion with the patient was usually not documented.

result.setting: General surgical department, emergency surgery (Royal Oldham Hospital and collaborating centres)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons guidelines on operation note documentation

cycle1.result: Initial audit found areas for improvement (figures not reported).

cycle2.result: 100% compliance for operative findings, incision, closure, procedural details, extra procedures and postoperative instructions; indication/diagnosis missing in 17.6%, DVT prophylaxis missing in 15.3%, antibiotics missing in 25.57%, blood loss missing in 71.6%.

result.other_findings: Significant improvement in most domains from the initial audit; blood loss documentation remained poor.

result.setting: Aesthetic clinics in Greater London (online cross-sectional review)
result.standard: Advertising Standards Authority enforcement notice on advertising prescription-only medicines

cycle1.result: 206/233 clinics (88%) directly infringed the enforcement notice by advertising a prescription medicine.

result.other_findings: Average cost per ml was £330.89 for dermal filler (significant borough variance, p<0.05) and £284.45 for botulinum toxin (p=0.058).

result.setting: Kasturba Medical College Hospital Attavar, tertiary care hospital; ASA 1-2 elective non-obstetric surgery
result.standard: Indian Society of Anaesthesiologists national preoperative fasting guidelines

cycle1.result: Median fasting 10 hours from clear fluids and 12.5 hours from solids; 99% gave an incorrect reason or did not know the reason for fasting.

result.intervention: Patient information leaflets in English and the local language distributed to every ward for patients the day before surgery; surgical and anaesthetic trainees and nurses made aware of the findings.

cycle2.result: Median fasting 3 hours from clear fluids and 11 hours from solids; 35% knew the correct reason, 50% gave an incorrect reason, 15% did not know.
