result.other_findings: Solid fasting remained prolonged despite the fall in clear fluid fasting.

result.setting: University Hospital Crosshouse, district general hospital surgical unit
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons guidelines on adult surgical ward round documentation

cycle1.result: 21 daily and 21 post-take ward round entries: date 90%, consultant name 95%, time documented 29% and 35%, examination findings 33% (DWR) and 40% (PTWR), presenting complaint 45% of PTWR.

result.other_findings: Survey of 26 doctors: all rated date, time and examination findings important; planned improved admission proforma and electronic handover.

result.setting: Dr Gray's Hospital, Elgin, secondary care hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England operative note documentation guidelines

cycle1.result: Compliance with RCS standards 69%; postoperative template use 18.2%; electronic documentation 60%.

result.intervention: Facilitated online access to the theatre system, consultant induction, user guides and mass communication to surgical teams.

cycle2.result: Compliance 96.6%; template use 44.1%; electronic documentation remained at 60%.

result.other_findings: Lack of timely online access at staff induction was a major barrier to electronic notes.

result.topic: Perioperative cardiac arrest in obstetric patients
result.setting: UK hospitals, 7th National Audit Project of the Royal College of Anaesthetists

cycle1.result: 28 obstetric cardiac arrests (3% of NAP7 arrests); incidence 7.9 per 100,000 (95%CI 5.4-11.4).

result.other_findings: Haemorrhage was the leading single cause; no arrests from failed airway management or remifentanil PCA.

result.topic: Enhanced recovery discharge after colorectal surgery
result.setting: St Richard's Hospital, Chichester, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Previous audit found delayed discharge in over 50% of elective colorectal patients; 46% discharged on day checklist completed; median LOS 5 days; catheter removed day 1 in 63%.

result.intervention: Introduction of an ERP discharge checklist.

cycle2.result: Median LOS 4 days; 61% discharged on the day the checklist was completed; 80% catheter removed on day 1.

result.other_findings: Commonest reasons for delay were weekends (6) and comorbidities (6); weekend discharge strategy planned.

result.topic: Length of stay after open aortic surgery
result.setting: Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, single centre
result.standard: National benchmark length of stay of 7 days or less

cycle1.result: Only 26% achieved LOS of 7 days or less; 54% had ICU step-down delays despite clinical readiness.

result.other_findings: Prolonged LOS was linked to complexity, higher ASA and ICU step-down delays; ICU de-escalation protocol and vascular ERAS planned.

result.topic: Early intervention in psychosis referral-to-treatment times
result.setting: Sandwell early intervention service
result.standard: Referral-to-assessment 5-10 days and referral-to-treatment 14 days (national targets from April 2016)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: New national waiting time targets introduced April 2016.

cycle2.result: Preliminary evidence of marked improvement in referral-to-assessment and referral-to-treatment pathways (figures not reported).

result.other_findings: Most referrals were not appropriate for the service; all accepted patients were offered a NICE treatment package.

result.topic: Timing of cholecystectomy after gallstone pancreatitis
result.setting: Queen Elizabeth Hospital, London
result.standard: BSG guidelines: definitive management of mild gallstone pancreatitis on the same admission or within 2 weeks

cycle1.result: All suitable patients had timely cholecystectomy.

cycle2.result: None of the 4 patients had cholecystectomy within 2 weeks.

result.other_findings: The fall was attributed to the COVID-19 elective backlog; all patients eventually had surgery.

result.setting: Single bariatric centre

cycle1.result: Average weight loss 32% at 6 months, 69.6% at 1 year, 86.2% at 2 years and 76% at 6-10 years; no protein energy malnutrition; 4 zinc and 3 calcium deficiencies.

result.other_findings: Outcome series rather than audit against a standard; one patient lost to follow-up.

result.topic: Antipsychotic side-effect monitoring (GASS) for depot injections
result.setting: Guildford community mental health recovery service, Surrey and Borders Partnership
result.standard: Trust guideline: GASS completed at 12 weeks and 6 months after initiation, annually thereafter and at each dose titration

cycle1.result: GASS conducted in 8 cases (26.6%); 7 (23.3%) within the last year.

result.intervention: Findings shared at the service with a recommendation for staff to use GASS at outpatient appointments and document scores on depot charts and SystmOne.

cycle2.dates: Six months after the initial audit
cycle2.result: GASS completed in 16 cases (55.17%), all within the last year.

result.other_findings: Further suggestions included refresher courses, pharmacy team adherence and motivating medical and nursing staff.

result.topic: ICU admission after high-risk emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Huddersfield Royal Infirmary, Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: ICU admission aligned with preoperative mortality risk (NELA or P-POSSUM above 10%)

cycle1.result: 241 had NELA and 86 had P-POSSUM scores documented; 31.94% (NELA) and 28.12% (P-POSSUM) of high-risk patients were not admitted to ICU despite bed availability on most days.

result.other_findings: Risk category was significantly associated with ICU admission (p < 0.00001); mean NELA 9.74% and P-POSSUM 14.19%.

result.setting: East Surrey Hospital, on-call surgical team (patients assessed but not admitted)
result.standard: NHS Standard Contract: discharge summaries completed within 24 hours of assessment and discharge

cycle1.result: 18/47 (38.3%) had a clinical note or discharge summary on the electronic system; 6 (12.8%) had a discharge summary.

result.other_findings: Of 9 patients discharged directly from A&E, only 3 had a clinical note or summary; awareness teaching for juniors planned.

result.topic: Preoperative group and save before appendicectomy
result.setting: Department of General Surgery, Royal Sussex County Hospital Brighton

cycle1.result: No patients required transfusion; 75% had two G&S samples and 21% had one.

cycle2.result: No transfusions required; similar G&S sampling pattern.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend selective G&S based on comorbidity, anticoagulant use and anaemia.

result.setting: Acute surgical unit, Royal Alexandra Hospital Paisley
result.standard: Oral metronidazole prescribed when the oral route is viable

cycle1.result: 12.5% of patients were prescribed oral instead of IV metronidazole.

result.intervention: Education and awareness campaigns to encourage oral metronidazole.
result.other_findings: Oral prescribing would save about £64.77 per dose, or £971.55 per 5-day course.

result.setting: General surgery department, central London hospital; emergency admissions
result.standard: Trust standard: treatment escalation plans completed within 36 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Average time to TEP completion 39.6 hours; 15% discharged before TEP completion.

result.intervention: Posters distributed to junior doctors encouraging prompt TEP completion.

cycle2.result: Average time 34.6 hours (p > 0.05); 5% discharged before TEP completion.

result.other_findings: The average met the trust standard after the intervention though the change was not statistically significant.

result.setting: Otolaryngology theatres, Castle Hill Hospital, Hull
result.standard: National guidance that medical documentation is clear, accurate and legible

cycle1.result: 35% (n=7) of operation notes legible; 25% (n=5) electronic; electronic notes 100% legible, handwritten 13%.

result.intervention: Results presented to the department to raise awareness.

cycle2.result: Legibility 65% (n=13); electronic notes 50% (n=10), 100% legible; handwritten legibility 30% (n=3).

result.other_findings: Electronic notes were always legible and are encouraged.

result.setting: Surgical same-day emergency care unit, West Suffolk Hospital
result.standard: NICE guidance: Murphy's sign examined in suspected cholecystitis (100% standard)

cycle1.result: Murphy's sign examined in 54% overall; ED 54% and general surgery 56%.

result.other_findings: Results differed between teams in 24% of cases; sensitivity 67% for both, specificity 42% (surgery) and 15% (ED). An examination proforma was developed with re-audit planned.

result.topic: Timing of cholecystectomy after gallstone pancreatitis
result.setting: Emergency general surgery, Guy's and St Thomas', London
result.standard: Biliary key performance indicators: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 2 weeks of pancreatitis, time to Lap-C, inpatient Lap-C rate

cycle1.result: 2-week Lap-C after pancreatitis 27%; average time to Lap-C 68 days; inpatient Lap-C rate 2%.

result.intervention: Consultant-led biliary service, live biliary patient tracking system, increased inpatient Lap-C, ambulatory pathways and integrated care approach.

cycle2.result: 2-week Lap-C 79% (43% as inpatients); average time to Lap-C 13 days; inpatient Lap-C 19%.

result.other_findings: Three earlier audit cycles showed delays; 191 outpatient appointments saved (£22920).

result.setting: Al-Mouwasat University Hospital, Damascus University, tertiary centre
result.standard: SAGES guideline on drain use after laparoscopic cholecystectomy

cycle1.result: Drain used in all patients (100%), though indicated in only 16.6%.

result.intervention: Education of the surgical team on the SAGES guideline.

cycle2.result: Drain used in 53.3% while 23.3% required it; inappropriate drain use fell from 100% to 39.13%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Emergency theatre booking and time to theatre
result.setting: Acute surgical unit, University Hospital of Southampton
result.standard: Time to theatre within allotted CEPOD classification timeframe

cycle1.result: 632 (85%) achieved the time frame; 116 (15%) delayed, of which 94 (81%) were appropriately booked.

result.other_findings: In a third of delays no reason was recorded; no difference in postoperative length of stay or unexpected findings.

result.topic: Preoperative group and screen in breast surgery
result.setting: St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Local guideline: group and screen for mastectomy and reconstruction

cycle1.result: Group and screen done in 90% of mastectomy/reconstruction and 21% of WLE/SLNB cases; no transfusions.

result.other_findings: At least 24 unnecessary type and screen orders were identified.

result.setting: Aintree University Hospital, major trauma centre, Liverpool
result.standard: 80% CT/FAST; 100% correct AAST grading; 100% management per WSES guidelines

cycle1.result: All had CT; 73% AAST graded (93% correctly); 37% managed according to WSES guidelines; management undetermined in 27%.

result.other_findings: Adherence was lower for WSES III and IV (40% and 43%); 5% failed conservative management.

result.topic: Severity scoring and monitoring in acute pancreatitis
result.setting: The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE and BSG guidelines on severity stratification, observations and escalation in acute pancreatitis

cycle1.result: Severity scores documented in 10%; monitoring inconsistent.

result.intervention: BISAP score introduced through educational sessions and a printed format added to clerking proformas.
result.other_findings: Fluid balance, observations and investigation documentation also improved.

result.topic: Staging laparoscopy and peritoneal cytology in gastric cancer
result.setting: Royal Liverpool University Hospital, oesophagogastric resection centre
result.standard: AUGIS recommendation for staging laparoscopy; local selective cytology threshold (T3 and above or N+)

cycle1.result: No tumours below T3 with negative nodes had positive cytology.

result.intervention: Selective peritoneal cytology for T3 and above or node-positive disease.

cycle2.result: 4 (6%) changed from curative to palliative pathway, 2 (3%) with positive cytology; no positive cytology at T2 or below with negative nodes.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Royal Albert Edward Infirmary, Wigan

cycle1.result: Same-day discharge 48%.

result.other_findings: Cycle 2 (2019) same-day discharge was 64%; late operation note times were linked with overnight admission; one serious postoperative event 2018-2021.

result.setting: Aintree University Hospital, major trauma centre, Liverpool
result.standard: 80% CT/FAST; 100% correct AAST grading; 100% management per WSES guidelines

cycle1.result: All had CT; 73% AAST graded (93% correctly); 37% managed according to WSES guidelines; management undetermined in 27%.

result.other_findings: Adherence was lower for WSES III and IV (40% and 43%); 5% failed conservative management.

result.setting: Derriford Hospital, Plymouth
result.standard: British Association of Day Surgery: 60% of TURBTs could be performed as day case

cycle1.result: 36% of TURBTs performed as day case; readmission 12%; bladder perforation 3.8%.

result.intervention: All TURBTs listed as day case from 1 December 2019 (protocol change).

cycle2.result: 64% performed as day case; readmission 3% with no urology input needed; bladder perforation 1.6%.

result.other_findings: 133 resections in total across both periods; haematuria was the main reason for admission (74% and 82%).

result.setting: Medical school area teams (first audits in Cardiff and London)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes a student-led research and audit collaborative to improve psychiatry recruitment; student feedback showed high satisfaction.

result.topic: Timing of cholecystectomy for acute gallbladder disease
result.setting: Tertiary hepatobiliary unit, Oxford
result.standard: AUGIS 2016 and NICE 2021: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 7 days of admission for hot gallbladder

cycle1.result: 75.3% had LC within 7 days; 24.7% within 3 days.

result.intervention: Departmental teaching session and guideline posters.

cycle2.result: 68% had LC within 7 days; 36% within 3 days; average admission to LC 6.4 days.

result.other_findings: Commonest causes of delay were waiting for ERCP/MRCP and theatre availability.

result.setting: Queens Hospital Burton on Trent, district general hospital
result.standard: NICE guidelines on management of rectal cancer

cycle1.result: Compliance with NICE guidelines not satisfactory (figures not reported); local recurrence 24%, distant metastasis 32%, disease free 52%, mortality 12% at median 34 months.

result.other_findings: Outcomes were below those of national cancer centres of excellence.

result.setting: Chesterfield Royal Hospital

cycle1.result: 19/52 (36.5%) with uncomplicated pancreatitis given antibiotics; 22/36 (61.1%) with infection received antibiotics; 36/41 (87.8%) given broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.

result.other_findings: Trust approved procalcitonin testing in acute pancreatitis after the audit; re-audit planned.

result.setting: Older adult community mental health team

cycle1.result: Inaccuracies and inconsistencies in ACE-III scoring identified (figures not reported).

result.intervention: ACE-III training delivered by a neuropsychologist to the multidisciplinary team.

cycle2.result: ACE-III scores more accurate (figures not reported).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Surgical admissions unit, East Lancashire Hospitals NHS Trust, acute district general hospital
result.standard: Completion of the 26-item trust General Admission Document

cycle1.result: Mean GAD completion 50.88% (95%CI 46.65-55.11); 48.47% on days with junior absences and 54.98% without (p = 0.074).

result.other_findings: Juniors often deferred to the senior review section; induction teaching proposed.

result.setting: NHS hospital in North West England (Salford Royal Hospital)
result.standard: Local policy on CT use in acute pancreatitis

cycle1.result: 42 (79.2%) had CT; 12 (28.5%) of scans considered unnecessary.

result.other_findings: 42.9% of scans were in patients without diagnostic amylase.

result.topic: Acute kidney injury management after orthopaedic surgery
result.setting: Orthopaedic postoperative patients, Lincoln County Hospital, United Lincolnshire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 20% adherence to the AKI care bundle.

result.intervention: Targeted teaching sessions, visual reminders on wards and a structured AKI assessment proforma.

cycle2.result: 100% compliance with the AKI care bundle.

result.other_findings: Project integrated into junior doctors' induction programme.

result.setting: William Harvey Hospital, district general hospital, adult general surgery
result.standard: Royal College and other published guidelines on ward round documentation (good compliance 75% or more)

cycle1.result: Good compliance for date (100%), time (83%), ward round lead (99%), legibility (88%), management (100%); poor for fluid balance (16%), urinalysis (4%), VTE assessment (0%), ceiling of care (1%), antibiotic review (15%).

result.other_findings: A ward round proforma is proposed.

result.setting: 55 centres, acute general surgical services (national prospective audit)

cycle1.result: 84.4% treated with incision and drainage, half (51.9%) also with antibiotics; recurrence 5.7% vs 6.7% and readmission 14.0% vs 10.3%.

result.other_findings: 26.6% of hospitals had dedicated abscess pathways; wide variation in management.

result.setting: General surgery junior doctors, Southend University Hospital
result.standard: Association of Stoma Care Nurses national guidelines on high output stoma

cycle1.result: 51% of survey answers correct.

cycle2.result: 72% of answers correct; 83% used the checklist; IV fluids 50% to 100%, fibre restriction 37% to 70%, loperamide dosing 5% to 30%.

result.other_findings: Knowledge survey of junior doctors rather than a patient notes audit.

result.setting: Surgical handover meeting (University of Edinburgh, Wishaw General Hospital, Royal Infirmary Lancaster)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England handover guidelines (2007) and NICE

cycle1.result: 80% of junior surgical doctors responded; no standard handover format, incomplete information and lack of privacy.

result.intervention: Staff training and a standardised handover sheet.

cycle2.result: Noticeable improvement in staff satisfaction (figures not reported).

result.other_findings: Use of a quiet room and nurse attendance remained poor.

result.topic: Surgical site infection in colorectal surgery
result.setting: Local colorectal unit, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust; elective colorectal surgery
result.standard: Change of gloves and instruments before abdominal closure (ChEETAh trial); 30-day SSI rate

cycle1.result: Baseline SSI rate 29%.

result.intervention: Change of gloves and instruments by the whole scrub team before abdominal closure, then reinforcement with team education.

cycle2.result: SSI rate 15%, sustained across 6 months after intervention.

result.other_findings: Three cycles over 11 months; SSI fell to 23% after COGI implementation before the reinforcement cycle.

result.topic: Critical care admission after high-risk emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Royal Bolton Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Updated 2023 NELA standards: high-risk patients (NELA risk 5% or more) admitted directly to critical care

cycle1.result: 38 of 43 high-risk patients directly admitted to critical care; median LOS 14 days, 7 died within 30 days (O/E mortality 1.12).

result.other_findings: 112 laparotomies overall; none of the 5 high-risk patients sent to the ward died (median LOS 8 days).

result.setting: Infectious diseases and medicine for the older person services, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Health Information and Quality Authority National Standard for Discharge Summaries

cycle1.result: MFTOP produced 7 ideal summaries and ID none (p=0.0083); average completion time 0.75 days (MFTOP) vs 14.4 days (ID); complete prescription 9 MFTOP vs 1 ID.

result.other_findings: Barriers included inadequate staffing, short-notice discharges, high staff turnover and unclear documentation.

result.setting: Chelsea and Westminster Trust, emergency abdominal X-rays
result.standard: RCR iRefer guidelines for abdominal X-ray indications

cycle1.result: 36 (6%) had no indication documented; 364 of 539 (68%) met RCR iRefer guidance; 496 (86%) reported normal.

result.other_findings: 35% of guideline-compliant AXRs needed further imaging; abdominal pain and toxic megacolon were the commonest non-compliant indications.

result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedics department, Kingston Hospital NHS Trust
result.standard: Criteria in the NHS National Audit and Governance report

cycle1.result: Half of 25 audits were presented and only 20% completed the audit cycle; only two were against national standards and 28% used no standard.

result.other_findings: Action plans were implemented in a third of junior doctor-led audits vs 75% of consultant-led and 67% of nurse-led audits.

result.setting: Chesterfield Royal Hospital, emergency department renal colic presentations
result.standard: NICE and BAUS guidelines on ureteric stones (CT within 24 hours)

cycle1.result: Average time to CT 16 hours 31 minutes; 6% (3) had definitive inpatient surgery; 62% conservative, 26% stent, 4% nephrostomy.

result.other_findings: Patients with stents or nephrostomy waited about 7 weeks for definitive treatment.

result.topic: Enhanced care after colorectal cancer surgery
result.setting: Hywel Dda University Health Board, district general hospital

cycle1.result: 72% used an ITU bed (252 bed days); median LOS 8 days; return to theatre 2.9%; readmission 1.5%; 90-day mortality 1.5%.

result.intervention: Introduction of a ward-based level 1 enhanced care unit.

cycle2.result: 29% used an ITU bed (87 bed days); median LOS 6 days; return to theatre 1%; readmission 1%; 90-day mortality 1.1%.

result.other_findings: 55% used the enhanced care unit (186 bed days, median 4 days). Outcome comparison rather than audit against a named standard.

result.topic: Surgical site infection after lower limb amputation
result.setting: Single vascular centre, Black Country vascular network, Dudley

cycle1.result: SSI rate 40% (10/25); staples significantly associated with infection (p = 0.0027).

result.intervention: Data presented at local audit meeting.

cycle2.result: SSI rate 10.2% (4/39); sutures significantly associated with lower infection (p = 0.0154).

result.other_findings: No other risk factors differed significantly; small sample limits conclusions.

result.setting: Cardiology clinic, American Hospital Tirana

cycle1.result: Failure rate 13.5%; average turnaround 56 minutes.

result.intervention: Laminated information sheet, scripted messages for healthcare assistants, take-home patient leaflet, staff teaching and a Holter equipment box (3 PDSA cycles).
result.other_findings: After PDSA 1 failure was 13.04% with 65.2% patient compliance; after PDSA 2 failure was 5.7% but turnaround 1:07.

result.setting: Surgical department, Royal Stoke University Hospital, tertiary university hospital
result.standard: Joint Committee on Surgical Training quality indicators for core surgical trainees

cycle1.result: 75% had the chance to reflect on the case with the senior surgeon; 50% had a preoperative briefing; preoperative discussion of learning points had the lowest compliance.

result.other_findings: A checklist and loop-closing audit are planned.

result.setting: Virtual fracture clinic, Barts Health NHS Trust
result.standard: BOAST 7 Fracture Clinic Services: seen in fracture clinic within 72 hours of injury

cycle1.result: Mean injury to VFC review 2.33 days; 51% discharged after VFC review; mean VFC to face-to-face review 15.17 days; mean time to advanced imaging 30 days.

result.other_findings: 9% of injuries did not match injury diagnosis codes; funding, staffing, A&E education and protocol updates planned with re-audit.

result.setting: Aneurin Bevan University Health Board, high volume centre

cycle1.result: Transport time inaccurately documented in 66 cases; median transport 20 minutes (15 over 45 minutes); median anaesthetic time 50 minutes; median recovery time 137 minutes.

result.other_findings: 15 patients needed more than 12 hours in recovery.

result.setting: Princess Alexandra Hospital, Harlow, inpatients
result.standard: Trust gentamicin prescribing protocol (dose adjustment for age, renal function and weight; level monitoring)

cycle1.result: 2224 doses; dosing not adjusted for obesity or creatinine clearance (p<0.05); 86% needing a level had one, 15% taken too early; 100% with level >1 had next dose held.

result.other_findings: Electronic prescribing tools recommended.

result.setting: Elective colorectal surgery, University Hospitals of North Midlands
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice (17 operation note data points)

cycle1.result: 12 data points met 100%; estimated blood loss documented in 18.1% (n=42); DVT prophylaxis in 6% (n=14); tissue removed missing in 3%; antibiotic prophylaxis missing in 1.7%.

result.other_findings: Drop-down sections on the electronic operation note planned with re-audit.

result.setting: Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust and Homerton Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, London; neck of femur fracture patients
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England standards for operation notes (100% ideal)

cycle1.result: Overall 69.4% of measurable standards met; 3 standards met 100% of the time.

result.intervention: Findings presented at clinical governance meeting and autotext templates for operations introduced.

cycle2.result: Overall 76.4% of measurable standards met; 4 standards met 100% of the time; largest improvement in one standard from 33.3% to 93.8%.

result.other_findings: The five least adherent standards all improved; notes using templates generally met more standards than those without.

result.setting: University Hospital Coventry & Warwickshire; hepatobiliary (HPB) patients
result.standard: Trust and national guidance on record keeping and consent

cycle1.result: All entries legible and signed but GMC number and designation often omitted (81%); allergy status and drug history omitted in 62% and 63%; consent forms all present and described name/benefits/risks; information leaflet not documented in 77%; carbon copy given in 23%; abbreviations used in 54%.

result.other_findings: Where the carbon copy stayed in the file, the consenter never circled 'no' to show the patient declined it.

result.topic: Anaesthesia and packing in abscess incision and drainage
result.setting: St James's University Hospital, Leeds; incision and drainage of subcutaneous abscesses
result.standard: New RCS guidance introduced during COVID-19 pandemic (no widely used UK guideline previously)

cycle1.result: Local anaesthesia used in 4 (5.6%); wound packing in 62 (87.3%).

result.intervention: Introduction of new RCS guidance during COVID-19 pandemic.

cycle2.result: Local anaesthesia used in 52 (82.5%), p < 0.0001; wound packing in 43 (68.3%), p = 0.00452.

result.other_findings: Most abscesses were still packed in both cohorts; patient satisfaction and recurrence not assessed.

result.topic: Pus swabs in pilonidal abscess drainage
result.setting: Barts Health NHS Trust; incision and drainage of pilonidal abscess

cycle1.result: Swabs sent in 77% of cases; average reporting time 4.3 days; 92% discharged on antibiotics; swab results did not alter management.

result.intervention: Treatment protocol changed to stop routine swabs; multiple teaching sessions for trainees and education of theatre staff.
result.other_findings: 250 patients in total across the study; the change was reported to give large cost savings.

result.setting: Southern Health and Social Care Trust, Northern Ireland
result.standard: BSG key quality indicator of PCCRC rate (published rates 2-8%)

cycle1.result: 33 of 524 CRCs (6.3%) were PCCRCs; of these 21 (63.6%) had complete colonoscopy, 22 (66.6%) fair/satisfactory bowel preparation, 24 (72.7%) a lesion detected, 3 (9%) prior IBD.

result.other_findings: Of 24 with a lesion detected, 13 (54%) had complete resection and 10 (41.6%) biopsy only or incomplete resection.

result.topic: Chest trauma and rib fracture management
result.setting: District general hospital, Royal Devon University Hospitals NHS Trust; patients with traumatic rib fractures
result.standard: Regional major trauma centre chest trauma guidelines (CISS, pain team review, MTC referral)

cycle1.result: CISS calculated on admission in 2 patients; 89.2% scored over 11 retrospectively; 28 (75.7%) met MTC referral criteria but only 8 referred; 27 (73.0%) seen by pain team; 16 received a nerve block.

result.intervention: Trust chest trauma pathway updated and electronic patient record tools developed for CISS calculation and referrals.
result.other_findings: 5 (13.5%) readmitted within 30 days with pain or dyspnoea; 2 deaths (5.4%) within 30 days.

result.setting: John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; patients after coronary artery bypass grafting
result.standard: Updated guidelines on secondary prevention medications at discharge after CABG

cycle1.result: 99% discharged on antiplatelets (12% on dual antiplatelets without indication); 97% on beta-blocker; 96% on lipid-lowering agents; 74% on ACEi/ARBs.

result.other_findings: This is a re-audit of a 2014 audit that showed reduced compliance; of the 26% without a RAAS inhibitor, 9% had no clear indication and 7% had a contraindication.

result.setting: University Hospital Limerick; 14 inpatient wards
result.standard: HSE Standards and Recommended Practices for Healthcare Records Management; Practice Standards and Guidelines for Nurses for Prescriptive Authority

cycle1.result: 48% of drug kardexes legible; 68% on medical vs 19% on surgical wards (p<0.05); upper case used in 13%.

result.other_findings: Planned targeted prescribing education, kardex layout changes and electronic prescribing.

result.setting: Dumfries and Galloway Royal Infirmary; adult surgical inpatients
result.standard: NICE IV fluid guidelines, GIFTASUP and local hospital policies

cycle1.result: Only 10% had U&Es pre-checked; 63% of prescriptions for maintenance; 0.18% NaCl/4% dextrose used in 35% and Hartmann's in 30%; commonest rate 150 ml/hr (35%); 25% had complications.

result.other_findings: Most fluids prescribed by FY1s (40%) and ANPs (20%); hyponatraemia 15% and hypokalaemia 5%.

result.setting: District general hospital general surgery theatres (Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: Average total waste 5.9kg per case, mostly clinical; recyclable waste 17%; much non-infectious recyclable waste wrongly placed in clinical bins.

result.intervention: Surveys and posters to raise awareness of waste segregation guidelines.

cycle2.result: Recyclable waste proportion increased to 28%; average total waste per operation higher.

result.other_findings: Higher total waste in cycle 2 may reflect longer operations in the second sample.

result.setting: Medway Hospital ENT on-call service, Kent
result.standard: Local ENT emergency referral proforma (ten documentation items)

cycle1.result: One proforma scored 100%; average completion 80%; patient details 100%; ED informed of plan 8%.

result.other_findings: 5% of referrals needed potential resuscitation in ED and none met all criteria for safe handover.

result.setting: Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast; adults with distal radius fractures via ED and virtual fracture clinic
result.standard: BOAST: consultant review (virtual or face-to-face) within 72 hours of ED presentation

cycle1.result: 46/50 (92%) reviewed within 72 hours; VFC pathway 46/49 (93.8%).

result.other_findings: Four breaches (8%) due to delayed referral or weekend presentation; the one face-to-face review was outside 72 hours.

result.setting: District general hospital, Altnagelvin Area Hospital; acute pancreatitis admissions
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology: severity scoring within 48 hours of admission

cycle1.result: 2 of 12 (16.7%) had a Glasgow Imrie score recorded.

result.intervention: Targeted teaching for resident doctors and a process for the on-call team to ensure scoring of all new admissions.
result.other_findings: In cycle 1 one patient with score ≥3 was not escalated until day five and needed ICU for ARDS; no ICU admissions in cycle 2.

result.topic: Thyroidectomy for Graves' disease perioperative management
result.setting: Large UK tertiary centre, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 98% euthyroid or hypothyroid pre-operatively; 49% received potassium iodide, 53% beta-blockers, 48% vitamin D; calcium and PTH checked on day 0 in 99% and 97%, day 1 in 100% and 98%.

result.intervention: Protocol developed to improve consistency of pre-operative optimisation.
result.other_findings: Post-operative hypocalcaemia 26% (temporary in 92%); vocal cord palsy 11%, all temporary.

result.setting: Torbay Hospital, district general hospital; adult general surgical admissions

cycle1.result: 76% diagnosed by CT; significant pathology in 41% (7/17) of incidental and 52% (28/54) of symptomatic cases.

result.other_findings: 71% of patients with significant pathology were managed surgically; 68% of symptomatic significant pathology was bowel cancer.

result.topic: Sentinel lymph node biopsy eligibility in melanoma
result.setting: Royal Free Hospital; patients undergoing SLNB for malignant melanoma
result.standard: UK consensus statement: SLNB for primary cutaneous melanoma ≥pT2a, or pT1b with lymphovascular invasion or mitotic rate ≥2/mm2

cycle1.result: 6.5% (n = 9) did not meet criteria; a further 4.3% (n = 6) lacked documented lymphovascular invasion or mitotic index.

result.intervention: Standard referral letters disseminated to referring sites, with instruction to include full histology reports.

cycle2.result: 3% (n = 3) did not meet criteria; a further 11% (n = 11) lacked documented lymphovascular invasion or mitotic index in the referral.

result.other_findings: Authors state the interventions did not lead to sustained change.

result.setting: Nine tertiary neuromuscular centres across the UK and Ireland; multicentre retrospective national audit
result.standard: Benchmark criteria from a prior single-centre UK audit of 20 patients with no DMD family history

cycle1.result: Mean age at definitive diagnosis 53.9±29.7 months, at first HCP engagement 49.9±28.9 months, at first symptoms 36.4±26.8 months; presentational delay 21.1 (±21.1) months; time to diagnosis 4.6 (±7.9) months; symptoms to diagnosis 24.2±20.9 months.

result.other_findings: Motor symptoms recorded in 88% (106/121) and non-motor in 47% (57/121); time to diagnosis shorter than benchmark but presentational delay observed.

result.topic: MRI pathway for suspected scaphoid fracture
result.setting: Southmead Hospital; patients with suspected scaphoid fracture and normal initial x-rays

cycle1.result: Full wrist MRIs: 12% positive for scaphoid fracture; 63% of MRIs performed within 14 days.

result.intervention: New pathway from October 2020 replacing repeat x-rays at 2 weeks with urgent limited sequence scaphoid MRI.

cycle2.result: Limited sequence MRIs: 2 (9.1%) positive for scaphoid fracture; 73% performed within 14 days.

result.other_findings: 19 scans (86%) showed alternative pathology and 1 (4.5%) was normal; fewer outpatient follow-ups with no increase in cost.

result.topic: Foundation doctor knowledge of free flap monitoring
result.setting: Single centre; general surgery foundation doctors managing plastic surgery patients

cycle1.result: Baseline ability to spot a healthy flap and venous congestion was good; confidence and recognition of arterial occlusion were poorer.

result.intervention: Simple reference poster on free flaps and complications designed and distributed.

cycle2.result: Mean confidence significantly improved (p <0.0001); identification of arterial occlusion (p <0.0001) and healthy muscle flap with split-thickness skin graft (p = 0.0091) significantly improved.

result.other_findings: PDSA methodology using a questionnaire with images and clinical scenarios.

result.setting: Appendicectomy cases; cohort of females aged 15–45 years
result.standard: Accepted overall negative appendicectomy rate up to 20–25%

cycle1.result: Overall NAR 29%; NAR in females of child-bearing age 43.5% (156 cases, 37%).

cycle2.result: Overall NAR 25%; NAR in females of child-bearing age 37% (82 cases).

result.other_findings: 632 cases in total, 238 females of child-bearing age; authors suggest appendicitis scores, serial examination and imaging to reduce NAR.

result.setting: District general hospital; patients undergoing emergency appendicectomy
result.standard: GIRFT and Royal College of Surgeons benchmarks for operative approach, length of stay, complications and readmission

cycle1.result: Laparoscopic in 95.0%, conversion 0.8%; median LOS 1 day (IQR 1–2), mean 2.0 days; 30-day readmission 6.7%; SSI 4.2%.

result.other_findings: Complicated appendicitis and post-operative complications were associated with longer LOS.

result.topic: Unstable ankle fracture management in ED
result.setting: Scunthorpe General Hospital; admitted patients with unstable ankle fractures
result.standard: BOAST guidelines for ankle fracture management

cycle1.result: Several aspects of A&E management inadequate (figures not reported).

result.intervention: Poster with ankle fracture management algorithm in A&E; orthopaedic doctor attends A&E to reduce fracture after first failed attempt.

cycle2.result: Documentation of neurovascular assessment and skin integrity improved by 57%; whole-leg radiographs for suspected Maisonneuve injury in 60% more patients; adequacy of reduction improved by 25%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Major trauma time to CT and theatre
result.setting: Regional major trauma centre; Code Red major trauma needing immediate surgery

cycle1.result: Time to CT 32 minutes; time to theatre 144.5 minutes.

cycle2.result: 89% had preoperative CT; average time to CT 15 minutes (range 5 to 57); median time to theatre 88 minutes (range 39 to 325).

result.other_findings: Overall mortality 22%; seven cases from road traffic collisions.

result.setting: General surgical inpatients over 64 years
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians national falls guidance and local protocol

cycle1.result: All assessed for falls risk within 24 hours of admission; all falls reviewed but local protocol fully followed in 10 (71%); 57% (8/14) further investigated.

result.other_findings: Standard falls proforma not routinely used; one moderate harm and one death in a patient admitted with a fall who fell again.

result.setting: Orthopaedic theatres, local adult tertiary centre
result.standard: British Orthopaedic Association recommendations on lead aprons with adequate coverage, especially axillary coverage for women

cycle1.result: 115 items: 43 standard vests, 9 tabard gowns with and 4 without side coverage, 48 skirts, 11 thyroid covers; no boleros, high axilla vests or vests with axillary protection.

result.other_findings: Limited size range (XS 4, S 21, M 15, L 46, XL 12, unidentifiable 6).

result.setting: ENT Department, Imperial College NHS
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons (England) Good Surgical Practice 1.3 'Record your work clearly, accurately and legibly'

cycle1.result: not reported separately

result.intervention: First-cycle results presented at a regional meeting.

cycle2.result: Almost all domains 100% compliant except DVT prophylaxis (10%), blood loss (5%), antibiotic prophylaxis (85%) and anaesthetist's name (50%).

result.other_findings: n=27 across both cycles; results not clearly split by cycle.

result.topic: Severe acute pancreatitis management in critical care
result.setting: Adult critical care unit, King's Mill Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 10 of 11 received antibiotics, 7 started before critical care admission; 3 completed courses without positive culture or source; 7 fed via nasogastric and 1 via nasojejunal tube; 4 not reviewed by dietitian.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend a separate critical care pancreatitis guideline, microbiology rounds and daily dietitian review.

result.setting: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit database, adult patients
result.other_findings: Unplanned return to theatre 11.3% vs NELA average 4.8%; LOS 26 to 35 days vs NELA median 15.

result.setting: University Hospital North Durham theatres
result.standard: Local trust Golden Patient criteria (ASA grade/anaesthetic type, case duration, team availability, sent for before 08:30)

cycle1.result: Baseline operation start times of first patients on list (figures not reported).

result.intervention: Golden Patient policy: first patient on next day's list identified and reviewed the day before.

cycle2.result: Start times improved by 30 minutes on average; 62.9% of Golden Patients met all criteria; 68.6% sent for before 08:30; 97.1% met ASA/anaesthetic and 94.3% case duration criteria.

result.other_findings: Main shortfall was getting patients to theatre quickly rather than choosing them.

result.setting: ENT department, West Middlesex Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: not reported separately

result.intervention: Data presented to the local department with updated SSNHL guidance and treatment pathway.

cycle2.result: 80% received proton pump inhibitors with oral steroids in the second cycle.

result.other_findings: Across 35 patients: 92% same-day audiogram, 76% MRI, all oral steroids, 52% intratympanic steroids within six weeks, 66% complete or partial resolution.

result.setting: Lister Hospital, Stevenage; patients under 18 undergoing scrotal exploration for suspected torsion
result.standard: NCEPOD and GIRFT 2024: senior review and surgery within one hour

cycle1.result: Orchidectomy rate 8.5%.

result.intervention: Earlier pathway and education interventions (sustained local QI measures).

cycle2.result: Median time to senior review 101 minutes (IQR 65–147), 19% within one hour; median decision to theatre 77 minutes (55–96), 13% within one hour; orchidectomy 1.3% (p=0.045).

result.other_findings: Torsion confirmed in 14 (17.5%); ultrasound use and torsion detection rates were similar to the historical cohort.

result.setting: Inpatient wards in mid Essex (electronic system Paris); cross-sectional study
result.standard: Trust policy: VTE risk assessment for every admitted patient (100%)

cycle1.result: 82% completion; 45% completed on day of admission or next day; 34% no documentation of prior prophylactic anticoagulants; 3% no documented outcome.

result.intervention: Recommendations made to improve completion rate; audit tool updated to reflect changes to the electronic form.

cycle2.result: 95% completion; 74% completed on day of admission or next day; 26% no documentation of prior prophylactic anticoagulants; 7% no documented outcome.

result.other_findings: The 100% target was still not met.

result.topic: Pre-operative blood tests before minor surgery
result.setting: Surgical Emergency Unit, Walsall Manor Hospital; incision and drainage of abscess
result.standard: NICE NG45: no routine bloods for ASA 1 or 2 patients having minor surgery

cycle1.result: 93 patients had pre-operative blood tests; 7 were ASA 3 or higher; cost of unnecessary tests £4,092 (£24,552 per year).

result.other_findings: Blood tests did not change management; 16 had CRP >50 and 9 had WCC >15.

result.topic: Abdominal wall closure and incisional hernia
result.setting: University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff; colorectal cancer resections
result.standard: European Hernia Society guidelines: small bites closure and off-midline incisions

cycle1.result: Incisional hernia rate 31.4% at mean 24.9 months; small bites used in 38 (23.6% hernia) vs large bites in 80 (35.0%); midline 40.7% vs off-midline 6.3%.

result.other_findings: Hernia rates 44.1% laparotomy, 37.2% midline extraction, 8% Pfannenstiel, 0% transverse; uptake of small bites and off-midline incisions low.

result.topic: Carotid endarterectomy symptom to surgery time
result.setting: Vascular unit, Cumberland Infirmary; patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy
result.standard: National standards (National Vascular Registry): surgery within 14 days and referral within 7 days of symptoms

cycle1.result: 60% had surgery within 14 days (national 49%); median symptom to surgery 13 days (national 14); 60% referred within 7 days (national 72%).

result.other_findings: No post-operative deaths; adjusted stroke and death rate 2.5% vs national 1.9%; average stay two days.

result.topic: Treatment escalation plan and CPR documentation
result.setting: West Middlesex University Hospital, district general hospital; emergency surgical admissions
result.standard: Target of TEP completion on first consultant ward round

cycle1.result: 19 (15%) had TEP forms; 5 (26%) by parent surgical team; median time to completion 2 days; 39 of 47 operated patients (83%) had no TEP.

result.intervention: Results presented at departmental meeting and target set for TEP completion on first consultant ward round.

cycle2.result: 26 (17%) had TEP forms; 11 (42%) by parent surgical team; median time 1 day; 56 of 69 operated patients (81%) had no TEP.

result.other_findings: Completion rates remained low across both cycles.

result.setting: York Teaching Hospital; endoscopy service
result.standard: PC-CRC rate as endoscopy performance benchmark

cycle1.result: 32 PC-CRCs; most plausible cause missed lesion despite adequate bowel preparation (76%); commonest subtype non-interval C (38%); 3 of 18 endoscopists poor performers (≥4 PC-CRC).

result.other_findings: Withdrawal time, CIR and ADR did not differ between good and poor performers; overall rate described as acceptable.

result.topic: Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis
result.setting: District general hospital; patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis
result.standard: NICE CG188: LC within 1 week of diagnosis; BBUGSS morbidity <10%

cycle1.result: None (0/61) had LC within 1 week; 26 (43%) had grade II and IIIa complications.

result.other_findings: All LCs were elective, many as day cases.

result.topic: Treatment escalation plan and CPR documentation
result.setting: NHS Fife; General Surgery admissions and referrals

cycle1.result: 42% completion after intervention in the 2019 audit (12% before).

cycle2.result: 46.6% (34/73) had CPR and escalation status completed; all not-for-resuscitation patients had DNACPR forms, discussion and documentation.

result.other_findings: Earlier audits in 2017 and 2018 showed 0% and 2% completion.

result.setting: Great Western Hospital; patients admitted from A&E or SAU with acute bowel obstruction
result.standard: NCEPOD 2020 report on acute bowel obstruction (avoid imaging delays and AXR before CT)

cycle1.result: 70.1% had CT, 42% of these after AXR; average time to definitive radiological diagnosis 27.8hr.

result.intervention: Evidence-based acute bowel obstruction care pathway implemented and publicised.

cycle2.result: 18% had both AXR and CT; average time to diagnosis 10.7hr.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Royal Preston Hospital; junior clinicians and patients prescribed maintenance fluid
result.standard: Trust/NICE guidelines: 0.18% saline in glucose 4% as recommended maintenance fluid

cycle1.result: 16% prescribed the recommended maintenance fluid; Plasma-Lyte most prescribed (42%).

result.intervention: Posters and email reminders of trust IV fluid prescribing guidelines.
result.other_findings: Junior knowledge (n=21) improved: recommended fluid 52% to 80%, ml/kg/day 66% to 70%, monitoring 52% to 100%.

result.setting: Warwick Hospital; ED referrals with biliary disease

cycle1.result: 5 biliary colic, 4 cholangitis, 13 cholecystitis; 16/17 with cholecystitis/cholangitis had raised bloods and 16/17 had US; 1 cholecystitis patient had LC, 7 on waiting list.

result.other_findings: Biliary colic patients had near-normal bloods, suggesting a group for discharge with outpatient US; access to timely LC needs improvement.

result.setting: Bristol Royal Hospital for Children; children undergoing tonsillectomy
result.standard: National standards; new ibuprofen guidance 7.5mg/kg QDS

cycle1.result: 95% prescribed inadequate ibuprofen (mean 5.5mg/kg); 6% presented with bleeding, none returned to theatre.

result.intervention: New ibuprofen prescribing guideline (7.5mg/kg QDS instead of 5mg/kg TDS) with reduced opioid prescribing.

cycle2.result: 55% prescribed correct 7.5mg/kg QDS; no readmissions for pain; low number of bleeds.

result.other_findings: All readmissions for pain or haemorrhage in cycle 1 were on TDS ibuprofen; about 110 tonsillectomies per cycle (approximate).

result.setting: On-call orthopaedic service, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow

cycle1.result: 42% of referrals remote; back pain 22% of referrals with 76-77% needing no orthopaedic intervention; 45% of all referrals needed no orthopaedic intervention.

result.other_findings: 381 referrals recorded, 313 analysed; suggests streamlined back pain referral pathways.

result.topic: Preoperative risk optimisation in hernia repair
result.setting: Three hospitals (FPH, WPH and HWH); elective umbilical and epigastric hernia repair
result.standard: European and American Hernia Society guidelines on preoperative smoking cessation and weight optimisation

cycle1.result: 19 (32.2%) BMI ≥35: 1 postponed and referred, 17 (89.5%) proceeded without documented intervention; 10 (16.9%) smokers: 2 received documented cessation advice, 8 none.

result.other_findings: Six patients were both smokers and BMI ≥35.

result.setting: Wirral University Teaching Hospitals; patients with gallstone pancreatitis

cycle1.result: Average time to surgery 47.4 days; 25 had surgery; 15 had index admission surgery; average LOS 11.8 days.

result.intervention: not reported (comparison with COVID-19 first wave period)
result.other_findings: COVID group (March–June 2020, n=26): average time to surgery 56.7 days, 9 had surgery, 3 at index admission, LOS 8.8 days.

result.setting: District general hospital ENT on-call SHO bag (Royal Free London NHS Trust)
result.standard: ENT UK guidelines on on-call bag contents (checklist)

cycle1.result: Bag missing numerous items (tongue depressors to nasal catheters) and contained bulky unnecessary items such as Lahey forceps.

result.intervention: Bag replenished, unnecessary items removed, PPE added and a nightly SHO checklist introduced.

cycle2.result: Bag remained well stocked with only minor items missing (Merocel packs, Sofradex drops), with alternatives present.

result.other_findings: Checklist later moved to weekly completion to reduce SHO workload, with re-audit planned.

result.setting: Frimley Park Hospital single urology centre; primary TURBT specimens
result.standard: European Association of Urology guidelines (detrusor muscle in TURBT specimens)

cycle1.result: Detrusor muscle present (quality resection) in 39%.

result.intervention: Awareness of current practice; EAU guidance with separate tumour-base specimen pot; dedicated bladder cancer urologists using en-bloc resection where appropriate.

cycle2.result: Quality of resections improved to 66% (50–84% for intermediate and high grade).

result.other_findings: Three consecutive audit loops, 301 cases in total under seven consultant urologists.

result.setting: Tertiary centre (University Hospitals of Leicester); robotic theatre use across specialties

cycle1.result: Robot used on average 14.6 days per month, 20.25 operations per month, mean operating time 214.43 minutes; urology 10 days, gynaecology 3.38, general surgery 1.5 days per month.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest using the robot for training on non-operating days.

result.topic: Preoperative risk optimisation in hernia repair
result.setting: District general hospital (Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust); elective umbilical hernia repairs
result.standard: European Hernia guidelines: smoking cessation and BMI <35 before elective umbilical/epigastric repair

cycle1.result: 12% (N=7) known smokers; 13% (N=8) BMI over 35; smoking status clearly documented in only 15 cases; 10% (N=6) poor diabetic control (HbA1c > 48) not addressed.

result.other_findings: Of 15 with documented status, 6 remained smokers despite cessation advice.

result.topic: Chest trauma and rib fracture management
result.setting: Single NHS trust (East Surrey Hospital); admissions with rib fractures

cycle1.result: Battle score documented 5%; correct analgesia 10%; lidocaine patches 12.5%; rib block within 24 hours when indicated 25%.

result.intervention: Presentation of first-cycle results and circulation of the trust Rib Fracture Pathway.

cycle2.result: Battle score documented 15%; correct analgesia 35%; lidocaine patches 56%; rib block within 24 hours 38%.

result.other_findings: No improvement in Major Trauma Centre consultations when criteria were met; prescribing careplan and pathway update in progress.

result.setting: The Queen Elizabeth Hospital King's Lynn; general surgery operation notes (electronic and handwritten)
result.standard: RCS Good Surgical Practice operation note standards (100%)
result.intervention: Awareness raising on operation note requirements and reminders (re-audit planned).
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Ashford and St Peter's Hospital, district general hospital; ankle fracture ORIF

cycle1.result: Good compliance with documentation and review within 6 weeks; only 45% of patients under 60 had surgery within 24 hours.

result.other_findings: Surgery delayed up to 19 days in under-60s; COST scores did not differ between surgery within and after 24 hours.

result.setting: Vascular surgery inpatients, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Trust; PAD and AAA

cycle1.result: 15 of 52 (29%) optimised to atorvastatin 80mg on discharge.

result.other_findings: 124 and 190 patients collected before exclusions; 2.2-fold increase.

result.setting: Upper gastrointestinal surgery admissions, University Hospitals of North Midlands NHS Trust
result.standard: Take Ten principles and the Shine Toolkit

cycle1.result: HPC 100%, NEWS 46%, examination 96%, diagnosis 94%, advice to patients 0%, medication 42%, clinician name 60%.

result.intervention: Induction lecture on surgical assessment unit, admission and post-take ward round, documentation and job roles.

cycle2.result: HPC 100%, NEWS 54%, examination 94%, diagnosis 94%, advice to patients 16%, medication 54%, clinician name 72%.

result.other_findings: Recommended SAFE ward round tool, electronic notes and more computers on wheels.

result.setting: General surgery rotation, female FY1 doctors (Royal United Hospital Bath)

cycle1.result: 84% reported misidentification by patients.

result.intervention: 'Hello my name is' badges with 'Dr lastname' for all new FY1s; seniors encouraged to introduce FY1s as doctors on ward rounds.

cycle2.result: All had badges; 86% reported misidentification; 72% said seniors introduced them regularly.

result.other_findings: 100% response in both cycles; all felt badges reduced misidentification subjectively.

result.setting: Digestive disease department, tertiary centre (Royal Sussex County Hospital); surgical and endoscopy consent forms

cycle1.result: Abbreviations in 99% of surgical and 76% of endoscopy consent forms.

result.intervention: Posters, teaching sessions and clinical governance discussion.

cycle2.result: Abbreviations in 56% of surgical and 4% of endoscopy consent forms.

result.other_findings: Risk and title sections had most abbreviations in both cycles.

result.setting: Letterkenny University Hospital; emergency general surgery admission proforma

cycle1.result: Observations 25%, antibiotics 63%, IV fluids 25%, VTE risk 45%, nutrition 48%, estimated LOS 10%, ceiling of care 12%.

result.intervention: Education of the surgical on-call team and use of the Take 10 checklist on the post-take ward round.

cycle2.result: Observations 95%, antibiotics 90%, IV fluids 95%, VTE risk 100%, nutrition 100%, estimated LOS 85%, ceiling of care 78%.

result.other_findings: Examination and impression were 100% in both cycles.

result.setting: Countess of Chester Hospital; operative hand trauma
result.standard: BSSH: surgery within 24 hours for open fractures and bites, 7 days for closed fractures, 4 days for other injuries

cycle1.result: 24 (52%) did not meet criteria; 73% of open fractures and bites not operated within 24 hours; 1 of 3 closed fractures and 13 of 28 other injuries delayed.

result.other_findings: Infection in 6 (13%); delay not significantly associated with infection (p=0.90).

result.topic: Open hand fracture time to surgery
result.setting: Single centre; patients with open hand fractures
result.standard: BSSH: wound washout and closure within 24 hours of injury if definitive treatment not possible

cycle1.result: 60% (n=3) definitive surgery within 24 hours; 40% (n=2) neither surgery nor WWC.

result.intervention: Flyers to departmental staff and weekly announcements in departmental meetings.

cycle2.result: 53.8% (n=7) definitive surgery within 24 hours; 46.2% (n=6) WWC; 16.7% (n=1) neither within 24 hours.

result.other_findings: Authors report a 30% improvement in BSSH compliance.

result.setting: Teaching hospital (Victoria Hospital Kirkcaldy); emergency department, ENT and surgical clinicians

cycle1.result: Survey of 31 clinicians: 48.4% only 'somewhat' to 'not at all confident' prescribing correct antibiotics for ENT patients; 58.1% 'somewhat' to 'not at all confident' finding ENT antibiotic guidelines; 96.4% felt an ENT section on MicroGuide would be useful.

result.intervention: Planned creation of online ENT antibiotic guidelines on MicroGuide with microbiology (not yet evaluated).
result.other_findings: Survey of clinician confidence rather than measurement of prescribing against a standard.

result.setting: Emergency department, Birmingham Heartlands Hospital (large acute general hospital)
result.standard: BESS guidelines for first-time shoulder dislocation

cycle1.result: 85% seen in fracture clinic but only 25% seen by a consultant; 40% had appropriate imaging requested; 50% correctly referred to a shoulder surgeon or shoulder clinic.

result.intervention: Pathway designed so all first-time dislocations are followed up in fracture clinic with timely investigations (not yet re-audited).
result.other_findings: A large number of concomitant injuries were found; most patients were seen by a physiotherapist.

result.topic: Emergency theatre timing against NCEPOD category
result.setting: General and colorectal surgery department, Leicester Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Local CEPOD guidelines for time from booking to surgery

cycle1.result: Overall 28% breached CEPOD time to surgery: abscesses 27% (of 30), appendicectomies 30% (of 33), colorectal operations 33% (of 21). By category: 18% of category 2, 31% of category 3, 26% of category 4, 37% of category 5 breached.

result.other_findings: Of colorectal operations, 67% required bowel resection and 43% needed a stoma.

result.setting: General surgical unit, South Eastern Health and Social Care Trust, after introduction of an electronic health care system (EPIC)
result.standard: RCS Edinburgh SHINE Ward Round Tool and unit consultant consensus on the ideal ward round note

cycle1.result: Essential information missing in several domains.

result.intervention: Feedback/educational session with resident doctors responsible for ward round documentation.

cycle2.dates: One week after the feedback session
cycle2.result: Improved recording of names of team members present, examination findings, patient understanding and management plan (p <0.05).

result.other_findings: No improvement in recording of diagnosis, new issues, observations, VTE and antimicrobials (p>0.05).

result.topic: Bariatric surgery weight loss and comorbidity outcomes
result.setting: Bariatric surgery centre (Phoenix Health, Chester)

cycle1.result: Sleeve and bypass similar for weight loss and comorbidity resolution in first 6 months; subsequently weight loss better and better sustained with bypass.

result.other_findings: Resolution of comorbidities was greatest within the first 6 months after surgery.

result.topic: Ear swabs in acute ear presentations
result.setting: ENT treatment room, University Hospital Monklands

cycle1.result: Swabs taken in 77% of acute ear presentations; no follow-up in 20% of swabbed patients; swab results changed management in 9%.

result.intervention: Poster in the ENT treatment room with indications for ear swabbing.

cycle2.result: Swabs taken in 47% of cases; 12% of swabbed patients had no follow-up; swab results changed management in 11%.

result.other_findings: Swab results changed management in very few cases, so routine swabbing is not recommended.

result.topic: Physical health screening in mental illness
result.setting: South Barnet primary care mental health pilot (multidisciplinary team)
result.standard: Discussion and recording of physical health, smoking, drugs and alcohol screening; team target 100%

cycle1.result: 82% of records confirmed discussion and screening of physical health, smoking, drugs and alcohol.

result.intervention: Results discussed in team meetings; team agreed to improve the monitoring process.

cycle2.result: 98% of patients assessed had annual health checks and appropriate screening discussed and recorded.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Transanal excision of rectal neoplasms outcomes
result.setting: Airedale General Hospital

cycle1.result: TART 24 (63.1%), TAMIS 14 (36.8%); 81.5% of lesions in lower rectum; histology tubulovillous adenoma with low-grade dysplasia in 60.5%, malignancy in 2.6%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Orthopaedic trauma ward, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons standards for documentation

cycle1.result: Initially only two criteria had above 95% compliance; 'note signed' 60%, 'date stamp' 66%, 'contact number' 0%.

result.intervention: Educational posters; change from handwritten to online admission forms; optimisation of the online proforma with further education.

cycle2.dates: Fourth cycle, one year after the third
cycle2.result: All criteria documented in over 95% after further education and proforma modification.

result.other_findings: Four cycles: posters improved 'note signed' (60% to 96%); moving online improved 'date stamp' (66% to 100%) and 'contact number' (0% to 34%) but reduced 'time recorded' (18% to 0%) and 'name and grade' (74% to 26%).

result.setting: Emergency department, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh
result.standard: ATLS guidelines: completion and documentation of secondary survey in polytrauma

cycle1.result: Secondary survey documented in 10/20 (50%); mean time to secondary survey 8 hours (range 3-49).

result.intervention: Emergency department trauma booklet and policy of secondary survey on admission to Intensive Care.

cycle2.result: Secondary survey documented in 24/28 (87.5%); mean time 4 hours 30 minutes (range 1-21 hrs); Fisher's exact P = 0.017.

result.other_findings: Documentation was still not universal.

result.setting: Hospital-wide inpatients, small district general hospital (STDH)
result.standard: Trust infection prevention and control policy: cannulae correctly dressed and labelled, documented in the electronic record and assessed twice daily

cycle1.result: 38% of inpatients (n=86) had a cannula; just over 30% documented in notes; only 10 had a date label; 26 had spoiled dressings; 18 had thrombophlebitis. Time since insertion 24 to 240 hours.

result.intervention: Results presented at grand round and a poster of recommendations created (second cycle planned).
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Paediatric orthopaedic department, Bristol Royal Children's Hospital (tertiary referral centre)

cycle1.result: Acute fracture clinic and fracture clinic follow-up bookings fell by 40% and 48%; patient-initiated follow-up rose from 16% to 75% (AFC) and 12% to 35% (FFO); radiographs needed in only 17% (AFC) and 39% (FFO).

result.other_findings: Virtual fracture clinic introduced; on-call referrals and trauma cases fell by 50%; all elective operating cancelled.

result.setting: Paediatric department, tertiary care hospital, Kashmir

cycle1.result: Positive BAL report in 131 (46%); 55 (42%) positive culture/microscopy; MTB isolated in 25 (19%); pulmonary hydatidosis in 23 (17.5%).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Distal radius fracture reduction in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department (Oxford University Hospitals / University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire)
result.standard: BOAST guidelines for distal radius fracture management

cycle1.result: Requirement for operative reduction in theatre 45% (2018) and 24.1% (2020).

result.intervention: Three training sessions for ED staff on BOAST standards, including finger-trap manipulation and three-point moulded plaster.

cycle2.result: Satisfactory reduction in ED in 42.8%; operative reduction rate fell to 17.3%.

result.other_findings: No patients received a three-point moulded plaster in the ED; operative rate still above literature rate (10%).

result.topic: Lower GI bleed risk scoring (Oakland score)
result.setting: Surgical assessment unit, Bradford Royal Infirmary (large teaching hospital)
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology: Shock Index (≤1) and Oakland Score (≤8) for safe discharge in acute PR bleeding

cycle1.result: SI documented in 0/37 and OS calculated in 1/37 at clerking; 12/34 (35%) managed appropriately; by OS, 20/34 (58.9%) incorrectly discharged.

result.other_findings: Two patients had an unnecessary CTA.

result.topic: Abdominal X-ray use in acute abdomen
result.setting: Surgical admissions unit, district general hospital (NHS Fife)
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists guidelines on AXR in the acute setting

cycle1.result: 97% of AXR requests compliant with RCR guidelines; 30/62 also had CT after AXR.

result.other_findings: Of those with both, 9 had normal AXR but abnormal CT and 8 had abnormal AXR confirmed on CT.

result.setting: Three orthopaedic wards, Queen's Medical Centre, Nottingham
result.standard: RCS and NICE guidance on consent form completion

cycle1.result: Patient details and operation name complete in all forms; responsible health professional named in 75.6%; blood transfusion likelihood in 78.6%; name in print and contact number in 53%.

result.intervention: Awareness raised of poorly completed sections (no re-audit reported).
result.other_findings: More than 90% documented intended benefits and risks appropriately.

result.topic: Blood result flagging on ward rounds
result.setting: Urology ward, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Institutional protocol: daily blood sheet with outstanding bloods flagged

cycle1.result: Outstanding blood results flagged in 70%; baseline eGFR documented in 32%; 73% of results filed in the correct patient folder.

result.intervention: Discussions with nursing and medical staff and posters on the ward and in staff rooms.

cycle2.result: Flagging 74%; baseline eGFR documented 44%; results correctly filed 100%.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend sustained intervention through audits and induction.

result.topic: Ceiling of care and escalation plan documentation
result.setting: General surgery, James Cook University Hospital, Middlesbrough
result.standard: South Tees Trust resuscitation guidelines: escalation plan completed within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Adherence 6.18%.

result.intervention: Email to all junior doctors and consultants highlighting first-cycle findings and importance of ceiling of care documentation.
result.other_findings: 10 patients with a community DNAR had no documentation of it in clerking; teaching sessions planned.

result.setting: Barnet Hospital, London
result.standard: NICE and AUGIS guidelines (laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 7 days)

cycle1.result: Only 18.4% underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy, median time to surgery 95 days (IQR 43.5–324.5) versus recommended 7 days; median delay 5 days for MRCP and 8 days for ERCP; median LOS 8 days; 49.6% readmitted.

result.intervention: Proposed Hot Gallbladder Pathway with expedited imaging, dedicated theatre lists and MDT collaboration (not yet evaluated).
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy theatre lists (University NHS Foundation Trust Manchester)

cycle1.result: Of 63 instruments on the tray, a maximum of 19 and minimum of 7 were used; around 5000 litres of water and 220 kg carbon emissions unjustified waste over 100 operations.

result.intervention: New smaller 'Lap general tray' with 60% fewer instruments.
result.other_findings: Surgeon survey confirmed acceptance of new tray contents.

result.setting: University Hospitals Plymouth NHS Trust
result.standard: NCEPOD classification: urgent 2b, surgery within 6-18 hours

cycle1.result: 61% had surgery within 18 hours of documented decision; mean wait 17.5 hrs; longest wait 41 hours (excluding outlier).

result.other_findings: Documentation of decision to operate was poor (undocumented in 5 cases); operative and histological diagnoses of appendicitis varied.

result.setting: Endoscopic ultrasound service, Hull University Teaching Hospitals
result.standard: BSG and NICE: COVID-19 test within 3 days of EUS; target >90% swabbed within 3 days/72 hours

cycle1.result: 95.7% swabbed within 3 days but only 40.9% within 72 hours.

result.intervention: Results discussed at mortality and morbidity meeting with recommendations.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Tertiary colorectal surgery unit (University of Edinburgh), admissions via SAU or transfer
result.standard: Complete pregnancy status documentation (β-hCG and gynaecological history) in females aged 16-55

cycle1.result: 4/13 (30.8%) had complete documentation of pregnancy status, 3 of whom were transfers from other departments.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: General surgery (Epsom and St Helier / Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons guidance on operation notes

cycle1.result: Overall compliance below 80%; 7 parameters with low compliance ranging 5% to 77%.

result.intervention: Electronic operation note proforma introduced with IT department.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Extended VTE prophylaxis after cancer surgery
result.setting: Elective colorectal cancer surgery, Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE: 28-day post-operative pharmacological VTE prophylaxis after abdominopelvic surgery

cycle1.result: Compliance 32%.

result.setting: Three acute functional and organic psychiatric inpatient wards
result.standard: Local pathway: VTE and physical health assessment within 6 hours of admission; NICE assessment on admission, standard 100%

cycle1.result: 60% had VTE assessment and 54% had physical health assessment within 6 hours of admission.

result.intervention: Importance of assessments communicated in staff induction programmes (no re-audit reported).
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Spinal surgery department, UHNM, Stoke-on-Trent
result.standard: GIRFT and West Midlands Regional Spinal Network standards for suspected cauda equina syndrome

cycle1.result: Presentation to spinal referral 176 minutes; arrival to MRI 438 minutes; MRI reporting 254 minutes.

result.other_findings: Referral source changed: cycle 1 16 self-presented and 9 GP referrals; cycle 2 22 GP referrals, 2 self-presented, 1 transfer.

result.topic: Open hand injury time to surgery
result.setting: Plastic Trauma Clinic, Bradford Royal Infirmary
result.standard: BSSH guidelines on timing of surgery for open soft tissue hand trauma (target 100%)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 74% (62.5% for dominant hand); flexor tendon 83.3%, extensor tendon and digital nerve 76.4%.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 72%; flexor tendon and digital nerve 62.5%, extensor tendon 81.5%.

result.other_findings: Non-compliance mainly due to bed capacity and lack of list space; 69 days of delay causing 17 overnight stays.

result.topic: ERAS adherence in elective colorectal surgery
result.setting: Letterkenny University Hospital
result.standard: ERAS guidelines for elective colorectal surgery

cycle1.result: Overall adherence 63.9% (pre-admission 59.2%, pre-operative 73.9%, intra-operative 70.1%, post-operative 52.7%); no ERAS anaesthetic component; mean LOS 9.8 days.

result.setting: Southport District General Hospital
result.standard: Enhanced recovery protocols (NG tube and catheter removal)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.topic: Ultrasound timeliness in acute abdominal pain
result.setting: Accident and Emergency, Bedford Hospital

cycle1.result: Mean admission to request 1.77 (±5.48) days, 90.1% requested within 2 days; mean request to scan 1.37 (±4.04) days, 93.1% within 2 days.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: District general hospital (Lewisham University Hospital)

cycle1.result: Cause identified in 70%; 100% of alcoholic pancreatitis referred to alcohol services; nutritional assessment in only 10%; uncontrolled comorbidities not referred onwards.

result.intervention: MDT teaching sessions and an admission proforma (second loop planned).

result.setting: Ain Shams University Hospital, Cairo (teaching hospital)
result.standard: Established guidelines on complication rates after emergency midline closure

cycle1.result: Wound infection 123/621 (19.8%); acute fascial rupture 66/621 (10.6%); incisional hernia 87/621 (14%).

result.setting: A&E and surgical assessment unit, Great Western Hospital, Swindon
result.standard: NICE NG118: urgent low-dose non-contrast CT for suspected renal colic and serum calcium measurement

cycle1.result: CT within 24 hours in 100%; serum calcium measured in 21%.

result.topic: Head and neck cancer referral waiting times
result.setting: Head and neck cancer clinic, district general hospital (Wirral University Teaching Hospital)

cycle1.result: 96.9% seen within 14 days; 98.7% initially reviewed by telephone; for cancer patients, telephone vs face-to-face: 80% v 57% diagnosed by 28 days and 100% v 17% started treatment by 62 days.

result.setting: Emergency Surgery Clinic, Milton Keynes University Hospital

cycle1.result: 218 (27%) given antibiotics; only 77 (35%) of these prescribed appropriately.

result.other_findings: All UTI patients (n = 15) treated correctly; 71% of renal stone patients (n = 68) incorrectly given antibiotics.

result.setting: Orthopaedic wards, NHS Tayside, Dundee
result.standard: British Orthopaedic Association guidance on consent

cycle1.result: 8% of consent forms mentioned all possible complications; 12% emphasised the incidence of main risks.

result.topic: Consent and chaperone documentation for intimate examination
result.setting: Emergency department and surgical assessment unit (Glasgow Royal Infirmary)
result.standard: GMC, Royal College of Emergency Medicine and Royal College of Surgeons standards on consent and chaperones

cycle1.result: Consent documented in 7 (11%); chaperone offered in 17 (27%), with name and role of chaperone documented on 11 occasions.

result.other_findings: Male examiners offered a chaperone 50% of the time versus 6% for female examiners.

result.topic: Ultrasound use in right iliac fossa pain
result.setting: Ambulatory ultrasound, district general hospital (Royal Oldham Hospital)
result.standard: National guidelines on ultrasound in selected patients with RIF pain

cycle1.result: 41% had working diagnosis matching USS request; 13% had working diagnosis matched with USS results.

cycle1.result: More than 90% of HES-recorded cases accrued; most surgery at 10 centres doing >20 procedures/year; over 50% high-volume low-risk, 32.3% intermediate, 12.5% lower-volume or higher-risk.

result.standard: BOAST guidelines for management of ankle fractures

cycle1.result: Deficiencies in documentation and management (figures not reported).

cycle1.result: 100% satisfied with the patient-triggered pathway; leaflet clarity rated excellent 27%, very good 32%, good 32%, fair 7%.

result.topic: Vein harvesting technique outcomes in CABG
result.setting: Cardiac surgery (University of Manchester)

cycle1.result: Endoscopic (15) vs open (10): LOS 8 vs 9 days; day 3 AMEXO 7.7 vs 6.8 and pain 7.2 vs 8; satisfactory wound healing 100% vs 60%.
