cycle2.result: Proforma completed for only 28% of patients, but its use was associated with higher documentation of all parameters

result.other_findings: Referral pathways worked efficiently and red-flag patients were managed more appropriately; targeted slit lamp teaching and a further re-audit were planned.

result.setting: Conquest Hospital, East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: Legal requirements for controlled drug prescriptions

cycle1.result: 89% error rate in end-of-life discharge prescriptions

result.intervention: Single standardised pre-written dispensing chart for Just in Case and syringe driver medications with flow-chart guidance

cycle2.result: Error rate 11%; improved dispensing turnaround time

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Red eye assessment in primary care
result.setting: Birchwood Medical Practice, general practice (Lincolnshire)
result.standard: Documentation of four red flag findings in acute eye consultations

cycle1.result: All four red flag findings documented in 2.8%; pain 26%; visual acuity 35%; photophobia 6%; laterality 88%

result.intervention: Education with memory aids and an eye examination kit in each consultation room

cycle2.result: All four findings documented in 50% (p < 0.01); pain 63%; visual acuity 69%; photophobia 63%; laterality 94%

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Urology department, Leighton Hospital, Mid Cheshire Foundation Trust; out-of-hours acute admissions
result.standard: NICE: all urgently admitted patients to have a completed VTE assessment within 24 hours and appropriate prophylaxis

cycle1.result: Completed VTE form 56%; LMWH appropriately prescribed 65%; TEDS 35%; 3 VTE-related complications

result.intervention: Urological admissions proforma and teaching sessions for junior doctors

cycle2.result: Completed VTE form 92%; LMWH prescribed 84%; TEDS 76%; 1 VTE-related complication

result.other_findings: First re-audit (n=42): VTE form 93%, LMWH 83%, TEDS 64%, 0 complications.

result.setting: Acute urology take, Arrowe Park Hospital

cycle1.result: Rates of handover and registrar involvement audited (numbers not stated)

result.intervention: Foundation doctor induction training in acute urology, explanation of importance of handover, and review of team approachability

cycle2.result: Significant improvements in early registrar involvement and successful handover (numbers not stated)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Emergency Department, Cheltenham General Hospital
result.standard: Gold standard referral documentation parameters from national guidelines and literature review

cycle1.result: Referral documentation adequacy assessed (numbers not stated)

result.intervention: Educational meeting with results and case studies, and a 'record of telephone referral to neurosurgery' (RTRN) form

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in documentation with use of the RTRN form (numbers not stated)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Elderly care ward, Watford General Hospital, West Hertfordshire Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) documented, correctly calculated and acted on

cycle1.result: MUST scores calculated in 73%; dietitian referral 62%

result.intervention: Liaison with hospital teams, encouraging regular nurse training, and weekly dietitian ward rounds to screen for malnutrition

cycle2.result: MUST scores calculated in 97%; dietitian referral 86% (second cycle)

result.other_findings: Three cycles (May, July, November 2013; n=64, 62, 63); MUST scores were often miscalculated owing to BMI errors and unknown previous weights.

result.topic: Vision and hearing aids in ICU delirium prevention
result.setting: Intensive care unit, University Hospital Bristol NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: UK Clinical Pharmacy Association guidance on minimising delirium risk factors

cycle1.result: High prevalence of vision/hearing aid need and low availability (numbers not stated)

result.intervention: Changes to the ICU Innovian assessment system to prompt nurses' daily delirium reduction checks

cycle2.result: Rate of assessment 100% and vision aid use near 100% after further amendments

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Acute medical assessment unit
result.standard: Local hospital antibiotic guidelines for UTI (CQUIN)

cycle1.result: 20% with culture-confirmed UTI not given antibiotics; 25% of prescriptions non-compliant; stop dates missing on 77%; duration 1 to 11 days

result.intervention: Group teaching sessions, proactive pharmacist checks and widely distributed posters

cycle2.result: Compliance with local policy 100%; stop/review date on 100%; duration 1 to 7 days; 35% not prescribed antibiotics

result.other_findings: The proportion of patients with no antibiotic prescription worsened (20% to 35%).

result.setting: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Trust; electronic inpatient discharge documentation
result.standard: Locally developed 'golden rules' for discharge communication

cycle1.result: One third missing discharging doctor details; medication changes unclear in 68%; follow-up not completed in 40%

result.intervention: Interactive teaching for foundation doctors, an e-learning module and suggested software changes to the electronic discharge proforma
result.other_findings: A re-audit at twelve months was planned.

result.setting: Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BTS COPD admission care bundle and local CQUIN target

cycle1.result: 63% received all bundle elements (up from 10% before bundle paperwork was introduced in June 2014)

result.intervention: Focus group of junior medical staff to raise awareness, following introduction of bundle paperwork with training

cycle2.result: 73% received all elements of the bundle; steroids and antibiotics within four hours 96%; appropriate oxygen prescription 87% (from 97%)

result.other_findings: Blood gas analysis, nebuliser use and respiratory review improved; oxygen prescription declined.

result.topic: Physical health investigation documentation in mental health inpatients
result.setting: 12-bed adolescent mental health inpatient unit, Swindon (Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Documentation of five investigations (blood tests, ECG, MRI head, DEXA, ovarian ultrasound) in ward round entries

cycle1.result: Blood tests documented in 2/22 (9.1%); ECG, MRI head, DEXA and ovarian ultrasound 0/22 (0%)

result.intervention: Electronic ward round template modified with headings, free-text and drop-down boxes for each investigation

cycle2.result: Blood tests 21/22 (95.5%); ECG, MRI head, DEXA and pelvic ultrasound 22/22 (100%)

result.other_findings: A further audit a month later showed results were largely sustained.

result.setting: Inpatient wards, Royal Devon and Exeter NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: National Patient Safety Agency (NPSA) guidance on post-fall medical assessment

cycle1.result: Pilot audit: 50% of expected data points not recorded; thorough musculoskeletal examination documented in 54%

result.intervention: Teaching session for new junior doctors, then a falls proforma

cycle2.result: Fall history documented in 100% (improved by nearly 30%); musculoskeletal examination 77% (100% where proforma used)

result.other_findings: Three data collection cycles of 15 to 17 notes each; proforma was incorporated into hospital policy.

result.setting: Medical inpatients, Wrexham Maelor Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Trust guidelines for treatment of hypokalaemia (serum potassium <3.5 mmol/L)

cycle1.result: 7/32 (22%) received adequate treatment

result.intervention: Set of interventions including a hypokalaemia treatment algorithm

cycle2.result: 19/30 (63%) correctly prescribed appropriate doses consistent with the algorithm

result.other_findings: Analysis at 3 months showed a trend towards sustained improvement.

result.setting: Emergency department, tertiary hospital in London (St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust); abdominal pain patients
result.standard: RCEM analgesia guidelines, including analgesia within 20 minutes for severe pain

cycle1.result: Guideline-compliant analgesia 29%; pain score at triage 38%; rechecked 19%; severe pain treated within 20 minutes 22%

result.intervention: Locally adapted RCEM guidelines, monthly doctor and nurse teaching, and a nurse prescriber champion

cycle2.result: Pain score at triage 87%; guideline-concordant analgesia 52%; severe pain acted on in time 40%

result.other_findings: Cycle 3 (n=33) showed improvement returned to baseline without monthly education.

result.setting: Child and adolescent mental health inpatient unit (St George's Hospital, London)
result.standard: Local trust guidelines, NICE schizophrenia guidance and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines: baseline and 12-week physical health checks

cycle1.result: Overall monitoring of physical health parameters poor (numbers not stated)

result.intervention: Prompting tool filed in physical health files and education of staff

cycle2.result: Significant improvement for the majority of parameters (numbers not stated)

result.other_findings: 39 case notes in total, 24 post intervention.

result.setting: Acute surgical receiving, Victoria Infirmary, Glasgow
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England record keeping guidelines

cycle1.result: Name/ID 96%; subjective 84%; objective 48%; impression/diagnosis 30%; plan 98%; diet status 16%; discharge decision 16%; discharge planning 20%; signature 96%; grade 62%

result.intervention: Problem-based SOAP post-take ward round proforma

cycle2.result: Name/ID, subjective, objective, plan, signature and grade 100%; impression/diagnosis 98%; diet status 83%; discharge decision 66%; discharge planning 40%

result.other_findings: Discharge planning remained low at 40%.

result.topic: Community mental health referral to assessment time
result.setting: Older adults community mental health team, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Previously set waiting time standards for routine and urgent assessment

cycle1.result: Mean time to assessment 15.89 days routine, 9.81 days urgent (2011: 12 and 3.6 days)

result.intervention: Duty worker role for triage and allocation of referrals

cycle2.result: Mean time to assessment 10.68 days routine, 6.8 days urgent

result.other_findings: Most urgent referrals were still not reviewed in time.

result.setting: Respiratory ward, NHS Lothian, Edinburgh
result.standard: Local antimicrobial guidelines: indication and intended duration documented on drug chart

cycle1.result: Indication documented 24%; duration 39%

result.intervention: Antibiotic guardian pocket cards with a three-point checklist, mini-posters, MDT feedback and certificates, then an MDT awareness session
result.other_findings: Second cycle: indication 97%, duration 69%.

result.setting: Department of Urology, St Mary's Hospital, Imperial College NHS Trust, London
result.standard: European Association of Urology guidelines on single post-operative dose of intravesical chemotherapy

cycle1.result: 15 (28% of NMIBC) given PSDIVC; 23 (36%) given PSDIVC or had documented contraindication

result.intervention: Intervention bundle: pre-operative delivery of mitomycin C to theatre, proforma in operative notes and designated roles

cycle2.result: 12 (50% of NMIBC) given PSDIVC; 28 (90%) given PSDIVC or documented contraindication

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: A&E department, Northumbria Healthcare Trust (old and new sites)
result.standard: National guideline CT head within 12 hours; trust guideline CT head within four hours and a specified stroke blood panel

cycle1.result: Old site: CT head within four hours 97%; full stroke bloods 53%

result.intervention: Updated one-click 'Stroke/TIA' blood panel on the trust computer system, promoted throughout the trust

cycle2.result: Correct blood tests 75%; CT head within four hours 100%

result.other_findings: At the new site before intervention, CT within four hours was 94% and full stroke bloods 22%.

result.setting: Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery, Royal Brompton Hospital, London; tertiary centre
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England and BMA guidance on Safe Handover

cycle1.result: No handover in 52%; 64% of handovers by phone; age, consultant and recent procedures not handed over a third of the time; perceived safety 5/10

result.intervention: Handover proforma implemented; face-to-face handover recommended
result.other_findings: Name, ward and current diagnosis were handed over 100% of the time; a re-audit was planned.

result.setting: Surgical department, district general hospital (Ysbyty Gwynedd, Bangor)

cycle1.result: Correct prescribing for at-risk patients 76–93%; risk assessment documented in fewer than 50%; explanation to patients fewer than 66%

result.intervention: Proforma introduction and feedback (cycle 1), then VTE prophylaxis teaching (cycle 2)

cycle2.result: Prescribing and risk assessment improved after proforma and feedback (p = 0.009 and p = 0.001); teaching not associated with improvement; overall NICE compliance no more than 25%

result.other_findings: 394 admissions across four data collections; verbal feedback was the only intervention with modest improvement.

result.setting: St Francis Hospital Nsambya, Kampala
result.standard: Criteria-based standards of care for PPH (4 standards) and severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia (10 standards)

cycle1.result: Adherence rates to standards assessed (numbers not stated in abstract)

result.intervention: Feedback, continuing medical education, drills and display of guidelines

cycle2.result: 7 of 10 pre-eclampsia/eclampsia standards and 3 of 4 PPH standards significantly higher

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: All general adult psychiatric inpatient wards in the North Central London Training Scheme
result.standard: Documentation of capacity and consent to treatment on admission and in the preceding 7 days

cycle1.result: Capacity and consent on admission 49.8%; capacity assessment in previous 7 days 61.9%; consent in previous 7 days 60.5%

result.intervention: Teaching sessions on mental capacity, then an admission clerking proforma with a capacity prompt

cycle2.result: Sustained improvement of 26% from baseline across all measures

result.other_findings: Cycle 1 at 6 months (n=213): 77% on admission, 87.3% capacity and 85.5% consent in previous 7 days.

result.setting: National sentinel audit across hospitals, general practice and nursing homes (NHS local coalition teams)
result.standard: Evidence-based prescribing criteria for specific conditions in patients over 65, assessed by computerised algorithms

cycle1.result: Methodology paper; baseline results not given in the abstract.

result.intervention: Feedback to participants plus nationally guided and locally driven intervention

cycle2.result: Re-audit described as showing encouraging results; no figures given in the abstract.

result.other_findings: Software tool was shown to be feasible and its data reliable; questions of cost and methodology remain.

result.setting: Regional rehabilitation unit, inpatients aged 16-65 with brain injury (Northwick Park, Harrow)
result.standard: Locally set standards for documentation, assessment, management and review of depression

cycle1.result: Baseline mood and start of medication documented in 54-61%; review 29%; subsequent treatment 27%.

result.intervention: Evidence-based multidisciplinary integrated care pathway (ICP) for depression

cycle2.result: All documentation standards improved to 94-100%, except assessment with a validated measure (84%) and follow-up assessment (76%).

result.other_findings: ICP raised staff awareness of depression.

result.topic: Blood pressure measurement technique and equipment
result.setting: 28 community family planning clinics, North Mersey Community NHS Trust, Liverpool

cycle1.result: 82% response on equipment showed it in relatively good condition but with maintenance and health and safety problems; 67% response on technique showed considerable variation in measurement technique.

result.intervention: All mercury devices replaced with aneroid devices; staff guidelines and updating on measurement technique
result.other_findings: Described as a professional survey; a re-audit was planned.

result.setting: Central London teaching hospital (Guy's and St Thomas')

cycle1.result: Total CS rate 20.9%; emergency CS 14.8%; failure to progress delivered within 1 hour 76%; fetal distress within 30 minutes 39%; cord pH documented 60%; ranitidine prescribed 53%; heparin 88%.

cycle2.result: Total CS rate 19.2%; emergency CS 13.6%; failure to progress within 1 hour 64%; fetal distress within 30 minutes 39%; cord pH documented 96%; ranitidine 81%; heparin 87%.

result.other_findings: No effect on decision-to-delivery times or fetal blood sampling (41% vs 34% of fetal distress cases).

result.setting: Stepping Hill Hospital, Stockport
result.standard: RCOG 1995 working party: risk assessment for all caesarean sections and heparin prophylaxis if high risk

cycle1.result: Heparin given to 0% of high-risk emergency and 25% of high-risk elective caesarean sections.

result.intervention: Structured thromboembolism risk assessment form for every caesarean section

cycle2.result: Adequate heparin prophylaxis in 72.7% of high-risk emergency and 85.7% of high-risk elective caesarean sections.

result.other_findings: Risk assessment form formally incorporated into all maternity case records.

result.setting: Multicentre HIV clinics, Yorkshire region

cycle1.result: Not reported in detail.

cycle2.result: Improvement with more patients on three or more drugs; 53% of patients on ART had viral load <50 copies/mL; 42% of ART-naive starters suppressed at 24 weeks.

result.other_findings: Third regional audit; future audits to focus on adherence.

result.setting: Glasgow Royal Maternity Hospital
result.standard: Local intrapartum prophylaxis protocol: adequate if antibiotics given more than 4 hours before delivery in women with risk factors

cycle1.result: Of 359 deliveries, 37 (10.3%) had risk factors; adequate prophylaxis in 32%.

result.intervention: Changes to the indications for prophylaxis in the protocol and circulation of results to medical and midwifery staff

cycle2.result: Of 378 deliveries, 49 (13%) had risk factors; adequate prophylaxis in 42%.

result.other_findings: Intrapartum pyrexia made timely prophylaxis difficult; better education and documentation of risk factors needed.

result.setting: Colorectal surgery unit, Derriford Hospital, Plymouth
result.standard: RCS England and ACPGBI 1996 guidelines for colorectal cancer management

cycle1.result: Marked variation; colorectal specialists more likely to meet guidelines, performed fewer APRs and more extensive lymphadenectomy.

cycle2.result: Compliance with guidelines markedly improved and fewer rectal procedures done by non-colorectal surgeons.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Maternity unit, district general hospital (Inverclyde Royal, Greenock)

cycle1.result: General anaesthesia in 58.0% of emergency and 45.5% of elective sections (53.0% overall); 25.3% had anaesthetic complications or side-effects; 90.3% satisfied.

result.intervention: Findings presented to the multidisciplinary team and changes to anaesthetic practice introduced

cycle2.result: General anaesthesia fell to 23.8% (P < 0.05); complications or side-effects 17.2%; satisfaction maintained.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Labour room, Glasgow Royal Maternity Hospital
result.standard: Local magnesium sulphate protocol compliance and achievement of therapeutic magnesium levels

cycle1.result: Protocol violations caused delayed therapeutic levels or high magnesium concentrations in 5 of 8 cases.

result.intervention: Circulation of results and staff education

cycle2.result: Near complete protocol compliance and more consistent time to therapeutic magnesium concentration.

result.other_findings: No eclampsia or magnesium toxicity during the audit.

result.setting: Kingston Hospital, Greater London university hospital

cycle1.result: Under 80% documented several key items; only 41% had complete signature with printed name and 35% correct time and date.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in almost all items assessed.

result.other_findings: Urgency terminology confused and cord gas results poorly documented at baseline.

result.setting: Intensive care units at a teaching hospital and a district hospital (Oxford)
result.standard: Protective ventilation strategy; proportion of data points with unnecessary hyperventilation

cycle1.result: Clear differences in practice between teaching and district hospitals.

result.intervention: Intensive education programme with nurse-run simple ventilation protocols

cycle2.result: District hospital practice closely mirrored the teaching centre.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Emergency department, district general hospital (East Surrey Hospital, Redhill)
result.standard: New local guidelines based on literature (diclofenac analgesia, prompt IVU)

result.intervention: New interdepartmental guidelines, junior doctor training, ED staff performing 3-film IVUs

cycle2.result: 5 of 19 admitted, 1 waiting for IVU; mean IVU wait 4.1 (SD 0.96) hours; rectal diclofenac the drug of choice.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: National Sudden Infant Death Register, Ireland
result.standard: Modified Rushton scoring; minimum accepted standard of necropsy per recent guidelines

cycle1.result: Of 245 reports overall, 55.5% below the minimum accepted standard.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in necropsy quality after guidelines.

result.other_findings: Necropsies in regional paediatric pathology centres were of significantly higher quality.

result.setting: Great Western Hospital, Swindon
result.standard: Radio-opaque side marker on the right side of the face for all paranasal sinus CT

cycle1.result: Marker identified in 85% of scans; 30% of clinical staff aware of it.

result.intervention: Changes indicated by the first cycle (details not stated)

cycle2.result: Marker identified in 100% of scans; staff awareness 90%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Colposcopy unit and GUM department, Singleton Hospital, Swansea
result.standard: Adequate treatment and partner notification for all chlamydia-positive patients

cycle1.result: Not reported; need for a formal protocol became apparent.

result.intervention: Interdepartmental fast-track referral protocol to the GUM health adviser for immediate treatment and partner notification

cycle2.result: All infected patients received adequate treatment and partner notification.

result.other_findings: Minimal use of doctor time or disruption of routine GUM services.

result.setting: Chemotherapy services, University Hospitals of Leicester

cycle1.result: Previous audit found differences between standard-treatment and clinical-trial patients in information and involvement.

result.intervention: Routine nurse appointment at least one day before consent with standardised written chemotherapy information

cycle2.result: Of 160 questionnaires, 131 replies; significantly more standard-chemotherapy patients remembered written nurse information and signing a consent form.

result.other_findings: Difference in feeling involved between standard and trial patients was no longer detectable.

result.setting: Tertiary obstetric unit, Liverpool Women's Hospital (5000 deliveries per year)
result.standard: New local guideline for repair of obstetric anal sphincter tears

cycle1.result: Repairs in theatre 70%; Prolene used 64%; adequate anaesthesia 70%; complete follow-up 66%.

cycle2.result: Repairs in theatre 82% then 97%; Prolene 76% then 93%; adequate anaesthesia 82% then 97% (P<0.05); complete follow-up 86% then 80%.

result.other_findings: 124 third-degree tears over 3 years (0.81%); only transient improvement in defecatory symptoms and more Prolene suture migration (7% vs 34% vs 16%).

result.setting: Rotunda Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: RCOG 1995 guidelines on thromboprophylaxis for caesarean section

cycle1.result: 21 of 75 (28%) moderate-risk women received appropriate prophylaxis; all low-risk women appropriate.

result.intervention: Pre-operative risk assessment checklist completed by obstetricians with risk-based prophylaxis

cycle2.result: 45 of 66 (68%) moderate-risk women received appropriate prophylaxis; all low-risk women appropriate.

result.other_findings: Further improvement still needed.

result.setting: Two tertiary referral children's hospitals, PICU (Manchester)
result.standard: UK Royal Colleges' guidelines on brainstem death testing (two tests by two doctors)

cycle1.result: Proforma completed 61%; two tests by two doctors 54%; cause of coma not stated 85%; exclusion of other causes stated 54%.

result.intervention: Dissemination of results; dedicated consultant intensivists appointed and emphasis on a single validated brainstem death proforma

cycle2.result: Proforma completed 100%; cause of coma stated 91%; exclusion of other causes 94%; two tests by two doctors 94%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: District general hospital endoscopy unit (Wycombe Hospital)

cycle1.result: Unit completion rate 89.1% (95% CI 87-92%); individuals ranged 75% to 97%.

result.intervention: Working practices altered for endoscopists not meeting the target

cycle2.result: Trend towards improvement in those individuals.

result.other_findings: Trainees needed at least 40 procedures to reach 85% completion; colorectal cancer detected in 3.9%.

result.setting: General paediatric outpatient department, large district general hospital (Luton and Dunstable)

cycle1.result: Mean quality score 23.3 (95% CI 22.1-24.4); 15 letters from each of 7 doctors.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: CT staging accuracy in laryngeal cancer
result.setting: Otolaryngology department, Hull Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Pathological T staging of total laryngectomy specimens

result.topic: HIV testing uptake in STI patients
result.setting: GU clinic, St Thomas' Hospital, London
result.standard: National Sexual Health strategy HIV testing targets

cycle1.result: HIV test uptake 18% overall, 14% in STI group, 33% in negative-screen group.

cycle2.result: Uptake 53% overall (n = 573), 41% in STI group (n = 285), 65% in controls (P < 0.01).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Community CAMHS clinic, Ashurst Hospital, Southampton
result.standard: Local protocol for assessment and treatment of children on psychostimulants

cycle1.result: Protocol used appropriately in the majority of children.

result.other_findings: Children often had co-morbid psychopathology and family and psychosocial difficulties.

result.topic: Extended role of health care assistants
result.setting: Critical care unit, Royal Sussex County Hospital, Brighton

cycle1.result: Staff questionnaire, 64% response; support for an extended HCA role but varied views on skills and training.

result.intervention: Initiatives from the initial survey to extend the HCA role

cycle2.result: 58% response; most staff aware of and positive about the changes but wanted more information and involvement.

result.other_findings: Survey of staff opinion rather than measurement against a standard.

result.setting: All UK radiotherapy centres, national audit
result.standard: Joint Collegiate Council for Oncology (JCCO) waiting time guidelines

cycle1.result: Not reported in detail.

cycle2.result: Waiting times lengthened in most centres; fewer patients in all categories treated within JCCO guidelines; no further rise in median palliative wait.

result.other_findings: Single-fraction palliation now common; no simple link between staff or machine numbers and waits.

result.setting: District general hospital, Scotland (about 3800 deliveries per year)

cycle2.result: 81% received prophylaxis (difference 67%, 95% CI 60-74%); infective morbidity 16%; wound infection 9%.

result.other_findings: 90% target not met; postnatal stay significantly shorter (P < 0.0001).

result.setting: St George's Hospital, London teaching hospital
result.standard: Local targets: low rupture rates, high sonographic diagnosis, acceptable tubal conservation and laparoscopic surgery rates

cycle1.result: Not reported in detail.

cycle2.result: Substantial improvement, mainly in ultrasound diagnosis, with fewer ruptured ectopics; laparoscopic rate stable.

result.other_findings: More junior doctors performed laparoscopic surgery; laparoscopy shortened hospital stay.

result.setting: Children's hospital (Alder Hey, Liverpool)

cycle1.result: 27.8% met criteria for a full audit; 22.2% were re-audited.

result.other_findings: Recommends audit methodology training and annual audit of audits.

result.setting: Dental polyclinic, St Thomas' Hospital, London (undergraduate dental students)

cycle1.result: Department where patient was seen most often missing, followed by illegible demonstrator and student signatures.

result.intervention: Tutorial presentation of results and teaching session on good record keeping to 20 students

cycle2.result: Almost all elements improved, most reaching 100%, except updated medical history and most recent complaint.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Multicentre GU clinics, North Thames region
result.standard: National guidelines for antibiotic treatment of chlamydia and test of cure

cycle1.result: Previous audit; figures not reported.

cycle2.result: Significant increase in centres following national antibiotic prescribing guidelines and offering test of cure when indicated.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Gynaecology department, Stobhill Hospital, Glasgow
result.standard: Auditable standards from published guidelines on counselling for female sterilisation

cycle1.result: Long-term alternatives 33%; irreversibility 94%; failure rate 96%; ectopic risk 48%; intended method 39%; operative risks 67%; continuing contraception 37%.

cycle2.result: Proforma used in 62% (100% compliant when used); long-term alternatives 68%; irreversibility 78%; failure rate 78%; ectopic risk 66%; intended method 66%; operative risks 66%; continuing contraception 64%.

result.setting: Hull and East Yorkshire Multidisciplinary Thyroid Clinic, tertiary referral

cycle1.result: Permanent vocal cord palsy 8%; haematoma 5%; permanent hypoparathyroidism 8%.

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary thyroid clinic established and best practice principles implemented

cycle2.result: Permanent vocal cord palsy 0%; haematoma 2%; permanent hypoparathyroidism 2%.

result.other_findings: Caseload rose, preoperative investigations fell and surgery types were standardised; outcome comparison rather than audit against a standard.

result.setting: General practices in Lothian; CABG patients from the regional centre (Royal Infirmary, Edinburgh)

cycle1.result: Mean systolic BP 142.5 (19.2) mm Hg.

result.intervention: Lists of CABG patients and first survey results sent to practices; Lothian Health recall project for cardiac patients (65 of 128 practices)

cycle2.result: 918 questionnaires (92%) on 875 patients: 17% smoked, 86% took aspirin; mean systolic BP 139.4 (19.1) mm Hg.

result.other_findings: 43% reduction in admissions and 45% reduction in hospital deaths, with a 12% increase in visits; proportion admitted by care home staff doubled.

result.setting: General medical clinics, Sarawak General Hospital, Kuching
result.standard: Diabetes-related process and intermediate outcome measures

cycle1.result: Annual HbA1c testing 68.4%.

result.intervention: Results fed back to doctors and measures implemented to improve care.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 85 general practices contributing to an accredited clinical audit
result.standard: Preset best-practice standards for acne management

cycle1.result: Some treatment inconsistent with best practice, especially undertreatment or suboptimal antibiotic therapy in moderate and moderate to severe acne.

result.intervention: Educational material sent to GPs between cycles.
result.other_findings: 1638 patients from 85 GPs across two cycles; authors suggest the treatment gap is likely overestimated.

result.setting: ENT department, Wexham Park Hospital, Slough
result.standard: ENT UK guidelines for disinfection of nasendoscopes

cycle1.result: Expiry date checked 5/10 sessions; discard date recorded 0/10; dirty bag transport 0/31; scope washed 0/31; adequate disinfection time 16/31; rinse and alcohol dry 0/31; clean bag storage 0/31.

result.intervention: Instructional poster and staff training session.

cycle2.result: Expiry date checked 10/12; discard date 10/12; dirty bag 19/36; washed 36/36; adequate disinfection time 33/36; rinse and dry 35/36; clean bag 35/36 (all P ≤ 0.048 or better).

result.other_findings: 10 sessions audited in cycle 1 and 12 in cycle 2.

result.setting: 72 general dental practices in the East of England
result.standard: CDC guideline/EPA drinking water standard (no more than 5% coliform contaminated, at most 500 cfu/ml); EU potable standard (under 100 cfu/ml, no faecal coliforms) encouraged

cycle1.result: 25% met EU potable standard; 3% met only CDC/EPA; 72% failed minimum standard; coliforms in 5 (7%).

result.intervention: All practices used a suitable disinfectant (mainly Alpron or Sterilox) for at least a month.

cycle2.result: Nearly 81% met EU standard (54% zero planktonic bacteria); nearly 6% more met CDC/EPA; 13% failed; coliforms in 1 (1.5%).

result.other_findings: No E. coli in any sample in either round.

result.setting: Mental Health Assessment Unit, South Essex University Partnership NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 100 referrals, 48 admitted; average stay 2 nights; 37 discharged home, 11 transferred to inpatient units.

result.other_findings: Most referrals came through the emergency department despite 25 having care coordinators; 5 patients admitted more than once.

result.setting: British Journal and International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery

cycle1.result: RCTs 2% in BJOMS (28) and 3% in IJOMS (40); one closed-loop audit in BJOMS.

result.other_findings: Most studies were observational or descriptive; 40% were non-clinical.

result.setting: Regional Maxillofacial Unit, University Hospital Aintree, Liverpool
result.standard: Free tissue transfer success rates above 95%

cycle1.result: 16% early return to theatre; flap salvage rate 73%.

cycle2.result: Return to theatre fell to 4%; 2005-2009 free flap survival 98%.

result.other_findings: Salvage most successful within 24 hours and for venous compromise; composite flaps survived less (93%) than fasciocutaneous or perforator flaps (96%).

result.setting: General surgery (upper GI, colorectal, vascular), Huddersfield Royal Infirmary
result.standard: RCS England Good Surgical Practice 2008 (18 operation note items)

cycle1.result: Poor documentation of emergency/elective (36%), time (36%), date (87%), assistant (87%) and postoperative management (88%).

result.intervention: Findings presented at clinical governance, surgeon education and theatre aide-memoires.

cycle2.result: Clear improvement in four of five deficient areas, with compliance reaching almost 100%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Plastic surgery unit, University Hospital North Staffordshire

cycle1.result: Observational audit showed shortcomings in flap monitoring.

result.intervention: Nursing teaching session, a universal flap monitoring chart and protocol, and a cartoon poster on the ward.
result.other_findings: Nursing confidence and doctor-nurse working relationships improved.

result.setting: Acute medicine, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, London
result.standard: Trust guideline on VTE in adult medical inpatients (2007)

cycle1.result: Guideline adherence 56%; lack of VTE risk assessment documentation.

result.intervention: Guideline launched with education and feedback, IT intervention, verbal and written reminders, regular audit and process redesign.

cycle2.result: Most patients received appropriate thromboprophylaxis but risk assessment documentation was poor.

result.other_findings: 2008 audit showed adherence of 96%; some low-risk patients received unnecessary treatment.

result.setting: Otolaryngology departments in England

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: No abstract available.

result.setting: North Tyneside General Hospital
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for acute pancreatitis

cycle1.result: Imaging within 24 h 35.2%; severity stratification within 48 h 28.7%; critical care for severe cases 39.3%; definitive treatment in index admission 22.2%; survival 95%.

result.intervention: Simple written care pathway for acute pancreatitis.

cycle2.result: Imaging within 24 h 47.7%; stratification within 48 h 75%; critical care for severe 63.6%; definitive treatment 38.5%; survival 100%.

result.other_findings: Care still did not reach BSG standards.

result.setting: Ophthalmology department, Royal Hallamshire Hospital, Sheffield

cycle1.result: Request form completion reviewed (figures not given in abstract).

result.intervention: Redesigned ophthalmic histopathology request form circulated.

cycle2.result: Improved completion of important sections of the form.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Department of Clinical Radiology, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists 2003 sedation guidelines

cycle1.result: Low awareness of guidelines and variable practice on fasting and drug order.

cycle2.result: Some improvements; persisting deviation on fasting and giving opiate before benzodiazepine; trend towards shorter acting benzodiazepines.

result.other_findings: Monitoring of vital signs was generally well done.

result.setting: Royal Aberdeen Children's Hospital
result.standard: Correct identification of bile vomit (dark green) and its significance (intestinal obstruction)

cycle1.result: 41% of nurses selected yellow as the colour of bile; 33% identified intestinal obstruction as the cause of bile vomiting.

cycle2.dates: six months after the primary audit
cycle2.result: 18% of nurses selected yellow, approximately 70% selected dark green; 64% identified intestinal obstruction as the cause.

result.other_findings: The second audit also compared knowledge across different medical professionals.

result.setting: District General Hospital, Croydon University Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines on operation note documentation

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Standardised operation note proforma based on RCS England guidelines.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in documentation with the proforma (no figures given in abstract).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: CBT for dental phobia and IV sedation use
result.setting: Community dental services and specialist psychotherapy services, Sheffield Health and Social Care Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Of 19 patients previously successful with CBT, 100% had not received IV sedation in the ten years since the original study.

result.other_findings: In the original pilot, 20 of 21 patients (95.2%) who attended CBT could have dental treatment without IV sedation.

result.setting: 7 clinical teams in Essex and Bedfordshire & Luton, South Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust (POMH-UK programme)
result.standard: POMH-UK 9b: indication documented (Deb 2006); continuing need reviewed at least annually (Deb 2006); annual side-effect review including EPS and 4 aspects of metabolic syndrome (NICE CG82, 2009)

cycle1.result: Standard 1 100%; Standard 2 over 90%; Standard 3 lower than at re-audit (figures not given).

cycle2.result: Standard 1 maintained 100%; Standard 2 over 90%; Standard 3 improved from baseline.

result.other_findings: Analysis and benchmarking done centrally by POMH-UK with an individual Trust report.

result.setting: Two Older Adult inpatient wards, Maudsley Hospital, London
result.standard: 90% of patients to have a full physical examination within 72 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Previous audit: results slightly worse than re-audit (figures not given).

cycle2.result: 58% had a brief physical examination and 43% a full physical examination on admission; 65% had a full examination by 72 hours.

result.other_findings: Recommendations: education of doctors, a proforma for physical examination and a further re-audit.

result.setting: John Connolly Wing ECT clinic, Ealing, West London Mental Health Trust
result.standard: NICE ECT TA59 (2003) and depression guidance CG90 (2009)

cycle1.result: Good compliance on indications for ECT and prior adequate treatment trial; poor documentation of risk-benefit discussion and poor post-ECT and ongoing cognitive assessment. No reason for stopping ECT documented in 3 patients.

result.intervention: ECT Care Pathway document produced and introduced; re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: 9 patients consented; 5 lacked capacity. Roles of the RMO team and ECT team needed clarifying.

result.setting: Bedford East Mental Health Team

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Increase in identification of PTSD patients; many drug treatments used were outside NICE guidelines; less availability of psychological therapy than expected.

result.other_findings: Patients had high levels of comorbidity and risk factors.

result.setting: Large rural general practice (17,435 patients), Haverhill
result.standard: MHRA guidelines and licence for co-cyprindiol use

cycle1.result: 26 individuals prescribed co-cyprindiol; 30.7% of prescriptions met MHRA guidelines. Acne was the most common indication (69%).

result.intervention: Prescribers contacted and sent the MHRA guideline; all patients invited for review.

cycle2.result: 12 individuals prescribed co-cyprindiol; 75% of prescriptions met guidelines.

result.other_findings: Co-cyprindiol was 3.4% of combined oral contraceptive prescriptions; non-compliant prescriptions had run longer (32 vs 19.5 months).

result.setting: Surgical high-dependency unit, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: 27 (37%) assessed within 4 hours; 15 (21%) individual reviews; 23 (32%) reviewed due to nursing concerns. Documentation of PMH 2 (3%), medications 1 (1%), allergies 0, complications 8 (11%), post-operative instructions 26 (36%).

result.intervention: Staff education, designated HDU bleeps and a post-operative assessment proforma.

cycle2.result: 46 (74%) assessed within 4 hours; 38 (61%) individual reviews; 1 (2%) due to nursing concerns. Documentation of PMH 18 (29%), medications 28 (45%), allergies 20 (32%), complications 18 (29%), instructions 55 (89%).

result.other_findings: Differences were highly significant but further improvement is needed to reach best practice.

result.setting: Liaison psychiatry service, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Locally introduced guidelines for time from referral to consultation

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Introduction of guidelines for time to consultation.

cycle2.result: Significant reduction in time to consultation (chi-squared = 43.84).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Physical health screening in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Two psychiatric inpatient wards, Exeter

cycle1.result: Screening performed inconsistently and infrequently.

result.intervention: One ward modified the admission proforma; the other set up a discharge screening clinic.

cycle2.result: Modified admission proforma raised screening rates by 4.7% on average versus 30.7% for the discharge screening clinic.

result.other_findings: The discharge clinic gave statistically significant improvement and delivered health promotion advice.

result.setting: All NHS hospital wards and ENT departments performing tonsillectomy in Scotland
result.standard: Recommended reading level set by patient education experts

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Original audit results mailed to all ENT wards, presented at a national meeting and published.

cycle2.result: 61% of information sheets had changed; 6 of 31 (19%) written at or below the recommended reading level; average reading grade still above recommendation.

result.other_findings: Interventions had limited success; ENT-UK tonsillectomy information sheets (2006) are recommended.

result.setting: Oral and maxillofacial department, large tertiary teaching hospital (King's College London Dental Institute at Guy's)
result.standard: Pre-operative instructions for conscious sedation with midazolam

cycle1.result: Over 55% of patients non-compliant; no competent escort 17%, alcohol within 24 hours 17%.

result.intervention: Patient information leaflet revised; given at listing and with appointment letter, plus verbal reminder before attending.

cycle2.result: 22% increase in compliance across all instructions; all patients brought competent escorts.

result.other_findings: Reduced non-compliance reduced appointment delays and waiting lists.

result.setting: Oral and maxillofacial department, large tertiary teaching hospital
result.standard: Pre-operative instructions for conscious sedation with midazolam

cycle1.result: Over 55% of patients non-compliant; no competent escort 17%, alcohol within 24 hours 17%.

result.intervention: Patient information leaflet revised; given at listing and with appointment letter, plus verbal reminder before attending.

cycle2.result: 22% increase in compliance across all instructions; all patients brought competent escorts.

result.other_findings: Reduced non-compliance reduced appointment delays and waiting lists.

result.topic: Informing psychiatric inpatients of their rights
result.setting: Wards at South West London and St George's Mental Health Trust
result.standard: Agreed trust standards on informing inpatients about legal status and rights (Mental Health Act 1983, revised 2007)

cycle1.result: 54.2% of informal inpatients aware of their legal status; 37.5% knew they could refuse treatment.

cycle2.result: Wards A-C: 81.3% aware of legal status (P = 0.101), 68.8% knew they could refuse treatment (P = 0.105). All 10 wards: 90.2% knew status (P = 0.0002), 65.6% knew they could refuse treatment (P = 0.0184).

result.other_findings: 105 people (61 informal, 44 detained) on 10 wards were interviewed; patient experience still sometimes crossed legal boundaries.

result.setting: Acute Medical Unit, Heartlands Hospital, Birmingham
result.standard: NHS Litigation Authority criteria for safe transfer

cycle1.result: Extremely poor uptake of the transfer checklist.

result.intervention: Education of nursing staff and raising awareness at regular staff meetings, following introduction of a redesigned checklist.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in completion rate; subsequent monitoring showed compliance up to 95%.

result.other_findings: Transfer-related incident reports decreased significantly.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring in severe mental illness
result.setting: Early intervention in psychosis service, Northumberland
result.standard: Annual physical health monitoring for people with severe mental illness

cycle1.result: 20% had at least one annual physical health check.

result.intervention: Raised awareness in the multidisciplinary team and liaison with primary care.

cycle2.result: 58% had at least one annual physical health check; a record was in the notes for 75% of those checked.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Role 4 care (Royal Centre for Defence Medicine, Birmingham) for casualties evacuated from Afghanistan

cycle1.result: Prescription rate of 50%; poor pre-injury compliance.

cycle2.result: 5 of 305 (1.64%) inpatients prescribed appropriate post-deployment chemoprophylaxis.

result.other_findings: Suggested recording compliance in field records and modifying PICS software.

result.setting: Otolaryngology clinic, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, London
result.standard: Structured format for outpatient clinic letters (readability score 0-4)

cycle1.result: SpR letters 71.91% structured, mean readability 2.87/4; consultant letters 46.58% structured, mean 1.25/4.

result.intervention: First audit results presented to participating doctors.

cycle2.result: SpR letters 84.72% structured, mean readability 3.41/4; consultant letters 52.56% structured, mean 2.04/4.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
result.setting: District general hospital, Dorset County Hospital

cycle1.result: 10.42% of emergency gallstone admissions had early laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

result.intervention: Departmental education on early cholecystectomy and altered management guidelines to consider it for all suitable patients.

cycle2.result: 21 of 36 suitable patients (58%) had early laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

result.other_findings: Of 15 with planned delayed surgery, 6 (40%) were readmitted while waiting; conversion rates were similar between groups.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring in severe mental illness
result.setting: 15-bedded male medium secure forensic psychiatric rehabilitation unit

cycle1.result: 80% smokers, 80% raised BMI, 87% raised 10-year cardiovascular risk.

result.intervention: Physical health monitoring sheet introduced in all patient records.

cycle2.result: Monitoring sheets up to date in 100% of records; serum lipids and 10-year cardiovascular risk reduced.

result.other_findings: No significant change in BMI, central obesity, blood pressure or smoking. Country taken from the corresponding author's affiliation.

result.setting: Anaesthetic room, district general hospital theatre (Northwick Park Hospital, London)

cycle1.result: Three inpatient airway deaths in 2 years before the course.

result.other_findings: 78 candidates gave 100% feedback; average scores 4.8 to 5.6 out of 6.

result.setting: Trust-wide, rural NHS foundation trust (Northern Lincolnshire and Goole Hospitals)
result.standard: Local infection prevention and control standard on uniform use, laundry and storage

cycle1.result: Staff generally adhered: uniforms changed daily and immediately on soiling, aprons worn where indicated, machine-washed and ironed hot; few placed laundered uniforms in protective covers.

result.other_findings: 399 of 597 sampled staff responded (67%); re-audit recommended.

result.setting: Otolaryngology theatres, Wexham Park Hospital, Slough
result.standard: Local version of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (National Patient Safety Agency guidance)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 63.7% (SEM 8.9%). 44% undocumented at Sign in; Time out interrupted in 39%; procedure started before completion in 33%; Sign out not read out in 94% and not fully documented in 42%.

result.other_findings: 72 cases were assessed in total across both audits.

result.setting: District general oral and maxillofacial surgery department, Royal Derby Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines on operative notes

cycle1.result: Mean data point inclusion 76.1%.

result.intervention: Paper-based operative note proforma designed and piloted.

cycle2.result: Mean data point inclusion 98.3%; all criteria improved.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Dentist experience of clinical audit schemes
result.setting: General dental practices in Essex

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews: evidence of change after audit, but audits often done by the dentist alone, little dissemination or feedback, and very limited re-auditing.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: North Bristol NHS Trust
result.standard: National Patient Safety Agency guidance on nasogastric tube placement (never event)

cycle1.result: Seven junior doctor check-image interpretation errors in the mis-sited tube cohort.

result.intervention: Recommendations on documentation, intubation, interpretation training (e-learning package) and radiology; new protocols for radiologists and radiographers.

cycle2.result: Interpretation errors reduced from seven to one; documentation improved by 22%.

result.other_findings: Service still not perfect; radiology should lead on reducing misinterpretation risk.

result.setting: Oral and maxillofacial departments, Homerton University Hospital, London
result.standard: Set standard for oral surgery referral content

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Redesigned referral proforma, guidance and feedback questionnaires distributed to referrers.

cycle2.result: Increases of 52% in stating anaesthesia type, 48% medical history, 38% referral date, 35% symptom duration, 31% treatment provided, 18% reason for referral, 14% diagnosis, 10% radiograph inclusion.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 27-bedded teaching hospital intensive care unit (Royal Sussex County Hospital, Brighton)
result.standard: National guidelines for clinical audit; UK Clinical Governance Support Team Audit Project Assessment Tool

cycle1.result: 22 of 25 projects were true audits; all retrospective; 4 were re-audits (3 showed improvement, 1 deterioration); 11 of 22 rated good quality.

result.intervention: Series of improvements to the audit programme after the review.
result.other_findings: Few projects were truly multidisciplinary.

result.setting: 87 UK radiology departments (national audit, Royal College of Radiologists)
result.standard: Audit standards for pain, hypotension, haemorrhage, haemobilia, puncture of another organ and haemorrhage-related death

cycle1.result: Standards met for pain, hypotension, haemorrhage, haemobilia and organ puncture; haemorrhage-related death target narrowly missed (0.11%, 4 of 3486). INR absent in 3% (97/2951), platelets absent in 1% (32/2986), INR over 1 week old in 8% (229/2888), platelets over 1 week old in 10% (291/2955).

result.other_findings: 15 further patients had at least one major complication; repeat audit of clotting assessment recommended.

result.topic: Image-guided liver biopsy adequacy and accuracy
result.setting: 87 UK radiology departments (national audit, Royal College of Radiologists)

cycle1.result: Sample adequacy 97.96% (3401/3472), narrowly missing the standard; diagnostic accuracy 98.55% (3187/3234), meeting the standard.

result.other_findings: Ultrasound guidance used in 96.38% (2808/3490); poor compliance with post-biopsy documentation.

result.topic: CT sinus imaging for facial pain
result.setting: ENT department, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary
result.standard: EPOS 2007 guideline and International Headache Society criteria for investigating rhinosinusitis

cycle1.result: 16% had positive nasal endoscopic findings; 30 patients had Lund-Mackay score 0 and only 9 had significant changes (LMS 8 or more).

result.intervention: Implementation of IHS and EPOS criteria.

cycle2.result: Only 10 patients had CT per EPOS guideline, 4 with significant changes; 80% diagnosed and treated for non-sinogenic causes.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Australian general practices (Type2Care audit)
result.standard: Annual cycle of care and diabetes targets (e.g. microalbumin)

cycle1.result: Mean HbA1c 6.9%.

result.intervention: Feedback to GPs and a decision support tool.

cycle2.result: Use of annual cycle of care plans increased by 12%; performance improved on all measures; mean HbA1c 6.9%.

result.other_findings: Greatest gains were in care plan use and microalbumin measurement and targets.

result.topic: Head and neck cancer referral waiting times
result.setting: Head and neck clinic, Barts Health, London
result.standard: NICE 2004 Improving outcomes in head and neck cancer; 2-week wait referrals

cycle1.result: Mean time from referral to being seen 11 days for 2-week wait referrals and 34 days for other referrals.

result.intervention: One-stop Rapid Diagnostic Clinic with on-site ultrasound and cytology.

cycle2.result: Mean waiting time 9 days for 2-week wait and 23 days for other referrals; most reached a definitive outcome at first consultation.

result.other_findings: Over one-third used ultrasound with or without FNAC during the RDC period.

result.topic: CTPA scan length and radiation dose
result.setting: Department of Radiology, Bristol Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Optimal scan length from lung apex to lung base

cycle1.result: Mean excess scan length 39.1 mm (SD 20.4) with frontal topogram only.

result.intervention: Additional lateral topogram in the CTPA protocol and radiographer education.

cycle2.result: Mean excess scan length 19.5 mm (SD 17.4), significantly lower.

result.other_findings: Dose to liver and stomach significantly reduced; thyroid dose potentially lowered.

result.setting: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Joint otolaryngology and haematology treatment algorithm for anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy

cycle1.result: 58% of patients were taking anticoagulant or antiplatelet medication on admission (across the study).

cycle2.result: Significant decrease in withholding of aspirin, clopidogrel and warfarin.

result.other_findings: 100 patients across both cycles; no significant rise in re-bleeding or re-admission.

result.topic: Prehospital airway management in cardiac arrest
result.setting: North East Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: i-gel insertion success 94% versus endotracheal tube 90%; airway management method poorly documented in 11% of records.

result.intervention: Individual feedback from Quality Improvement Officers on documentation.

cycle2.result: i-gel insertion success 92% versus endotracheal tube 86%; upward trend in i-gel use.

result.other_findings: Staff avoiding i-gel cited confidence with new equipment; airway soiling and aspiration prompted ET intubation.

result.topic: Preventable death in low-risk cardiac surgery
result.setting: Cardiothoracic Surgical Unit, Papworth Hospital, Cambridge

cycle1.result: Previous FIASCO study (2009): mortality 0.37%; modifiable causes were inadequate myocardial protection and unclear chain of responsibility.

cycle2.result: 7 deaths (0.27%) in low-risk patients, 3 preventable and 4 non-preventable; none from inadequate myocardial protection or communication failure.

result.other_findings: Specialty not in the given list, so stated as cardiothoracic surgery.

result.topic: Lung cancer resection and lymph node sampling standards
result.setting: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Nottingham University Hospitals (single surgeon)
result.standard: Intraoperative gold standards: anatomical resection and mediastinal lymphadenectomy

cycle1.result: Non-anatomical resections 12%; excision of at least 1, 2 and 3 N2 stations 86%, 63% and 40%.

cycle2.result: Non-anatomical resections 6% (not significant); at least 1, 2 and 3 N2 stations 91%, 77% and 63% (p = 0.003).

result.other_findings: Non-anatomical resection linked to VATS, previous malignancy and high predicted risk; less complete node excision with VATS and in octogenarians.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment in surgical patients
result.setting: ENT elective operating lists, Ipswich Hospital NHS Trust

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment 3/23; encouraged to mobilise 0/23; VTE leaflet at discharge 1/23.

cycle1.result: not reported

result.setting: Otolaryngology admissions and day cases, Queen's Hospital, Romford

cycle1.result: Baseline rate of HRG change 16%.

result.setting: 42-43 UK mental health trusts (POMH-UK programme)

result.topic: Cervical lymph node biopsy waiting times

result.standard: National cancer services guidelines for waiting times
