cycle1.result: 34%-39% of coagulation screens were inappropriate across AMU areas; one-third of requests lacked a clear clinical indication

result.intervention: Three PDSA cycles: revised triage order sets, condition-specific electronic order sets, and a digital decision prompt requiring clinicians to confirm test indication

cycle2.result: Inappropriate testing reduced to 20% in mSDEC, 10% in AMU 1B and 15% in AMU 1C

result.other_findings: Projected annual reduction of 44 000 tests, saving £130 000, 367 staff hours and 3.6 tonnes CO2e; the 90% reduction aim was not stated as met.

result.setting: Tertiary university hospital (Fondazione Policlinico Tor Vergata), monocentric prospective cohort
result.standard: Four RESECT surgical quality indicators: detrusor muscle sampling, completeness of resection, accuracy of operative documentation, and single immediate intravesical chemotherapy

cycle1.result: Detrusor muscle presence 61.9% in the pre-audit phase; 70.7% during the prospective audit phase (128 patients across all phases, March 2023 to June 2025)

result.intervention: Participation in the RESECT audit and feedback programme

cycle2.result: Detrusor muscle presence 85.9% in the post-audit phase

result.other_findings: Improvements in quality indicators were sustained after programme completion but did not yield a detectable reduction in recurrence.

result.setting: District General Hospital pathology unit, single centre
result.standard: Sample adequacy of fine-needle aspiration cytology in non-thyroid head and neck masses

cycle1.result: 134 of 207 (64.7%) samples adequate (dry slides only)

result.intervention: From 2017, samples prepared as both dry slides and liquid cytology
result.other_findings: All four clinicians achieved higher adequacy rates in the re-audit cycle.

result.setting: Tertiary Neonatal Intensive Care and Special Care Nursery, Centenary Hospital for Women and Children, Canberra
result.standard: Recommended ISOAP (Introduction, Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan) format for nursing handover reports

cycle1.result: 2% adherence to ISOAP format

result.intervention: Two PDSA cycles (paper-based then digital health records): neonatal-specific ISOAP templates, education sessions, peer mentorship, visual reminders and ongoing staff support

cycle2.result: Adherence 78% by January 2022 and 100% by March 2022; after DHR transition adherence improved from 65% in May 2023 to 92% by July 2023

result.other_findings: Staff reported improved clarity, communication, reduced time for clinical reviews and greater satisfaction.

result.setting: Paediatric Department, Birmingham Dental Hospital, Birmingham Community Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Recording of vaccination status of new patients in clinical notes

cycle1.result: 0% adherence to recording vaccination status

result.intervention: Dissemination of results, prompts added to clinical templates and increased staff awareness
result.other_findings: Of records with vaccination information, 13% of children were not up to date with vaccinations.

result.topic: SABA overuse and MART in asthma
result.setting: Wickham Surgery, general practice, Fareham
result.standard: Guidelines recommending MART for patients aged 12 or over; target >50% of 12-18-year-olds issued 3 or more salbutamol inhalers in a year transitioned to MART by May 2025

cycle1.result: 22 patients identified; eight already on MART

result.intervention: Structured face-to-face consultations, adolescent-friendly education tool, personalised asthma action plans and MART initiation where appropriate

cycle2.result: 23 patients identified, 10 (43%) on MART; >50% target not reached

result.other_findings: 10 patients attended consultations, leading to five further MART initiations; some apparent overuse reflected duplicate inhalers for school or sports.

result.topic: SABA overuse and MART in asthma
result.setting: The Willows Medical Practice, general practice, Chigwell, Essex
result.standard: NICE and BTS/SIGN asthma guidelines recommending AIR and MART for patients over-relying on SABA

cycle1.result: 94 patients issued 2 or more SABA inhalers in 12 months; 72 (76.6%) contacted; 37 (51.4%) overused SABA 3 or more times per week

result.intervention: Asthma reviews, inhaler technique assessment and initiation of AIR/MART therapy where appropriate

cycle2.result: 35 patients identified (-62.8%); 23 (65.7%) contacted; 18 (78.3%) reported SABA overuse (overuse count down from 37 to 18, -51.4%)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Vascular surgery department, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust, single centre
result.standard: Documentation standards derived from Royal College of Surgeons guidance

cycle1.result: Documentation incomplete across all four safety-critical fields; indication for surgery documented in 43.2%

result.intervention: Standardised procedure-specific operative note templates developed collaboratively and introduced at a departmental governance meeting

cycle2.result: Indication for surgery improved to 79.5% (OR 5.07, 95% CI 2.38-10.80); significant improvement in two of four domains

result.other_findings: Estimated blood loss and postoperative plan recording did not improve significantly.

result.topic: Admission glucose and ketone testing in diabetes
result.setting: Department of Acute and General Medicine, St James's Hospital, Dublin; admissions via emergency department
result.standard: JBDS-IP and ADA recommendations for glucose and ketone testing in all hospitalised diabetic patients

cycle1.result: Glucose measured on admission in 83% and ketones in 58%

result.other_findings: Four patients (4%) with neither test developed metabolic acidosis; education, workflow changes and re-audit are planned.

result.setting: District general hospital (Kettering General Hospital NHS Foundation Trust), radiology and emergency departments
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists 2024 major trauma guidance: six minimum data elements for WBCT requests and RCR WBCT criteria

cycle1.result: Mechanism of injury 74%, primary survey 94%, haemodynamic status 7%, preceding investigations 5%, past medical history 13%, trauma team leader contact 0%; 57% of requests met RCR WBCT criteria

result.intervention: Educational feedback to radiology and emergency medicine staff, RCR-derived electronic request proforma embedded in CareFlow EPR, and real-time radiologist feedback

cycle2.result: Mechanism of injury 100%; past medical history 18% (p = 0.329); preceding investigations 4% (p = 1.000); requests meeting RCR WBCT criteria 96%

result.other_findings: Preceding investigations and past medical history documentation remained low after intervention.

result.topic: Lipid management after acute coronary syndrome
result.setting: District general hospital (Wiltshire Cardiac Centre, Great Western Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Swindon)
result.standard: Guideline-based post-ACS lipid management: inpatient lipid profile, inpatient lipid-lowering therapy management and outpatient repeat lipid profile

cycle1.result: Baseline full lipid profile testing 10%; appropriate LLT management 65%; post-discharge repeat testing 37%

result.intervention: Structured intervention including updated blood testing panels, education and reference resources

cycle2.result: Full lipid profile testing 75%; appropriate LLT management 78%; post-discharge repeat testing 63%

result.other_findings: At one year post-ACS, 35% of patients remained subtherapeutic but medication changes were rare.

result.topic: Late GI toxicity after prostate radiotherapy
result.setting: Department of Clinical Oncology, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, academic centre
result.standard: National Prostate Cancer Audit severe late GI toxicity rate after EBRT; national average 10%

cycle1.result: Severe late GI toxicity confirmed in 16% (follow-up available for 281/290, 96.8%)

result.intervention: Protocol changes in 2020-2021: tighter rectal dose constraints, enema use, updated verification pathway and reduced CTV-PTV margins

cycle2.result: NPCA reported severe late GI toxicity reduced to 7.5%

result.other_findings: Higher rectal mean dose was associated with severe late GI toxicity (p=0.043); 36% of toxic cases had rectal diameters of 4.5 cm or more.

result.setting: Specialist cancer hospital (Royal Marsden Hospital, London)
result.standard: Palliative care unit recommendations for morphine prescribing

cycle1.result: Weaknesses included lack of breakthrough doses, prn oral morphine without regular oral morphine, and no guideline reference to co-prescription of aperients, antiemetics and night sedation

result.intervention: Education programme targeting the identified deficiencies

cycle2.result: Some improvement in prescribing practice (no figures reported)

result.other_findings: Persistent problems showed the need for an ongoing hospital-wide education programme.

result.topic: Barium enema detection of colorectal cancer
result.setting: Wessex regional radiology audit (multi-hospital)
result.standard: 100% demonstration and 100% diagnosis of colorectal carcinoma on barium enema performed in the 12 months before histological diagnosis

cycle1.result: Carcinoma demonstration rate 97%; reporting rate 85% (471 of 557 enema reports)

result.other_findings: Non-reporting due to failure to demonstrate (18 cases, 3%), failure to perceive (23, 4%) and failure to analyse a perceived lesion (45, 8%).

result.setting: All 147 Leicestershire general practices, audit led by a medical audit advisory group
result.standard: Agreed criteria for appropriate use of vitamin B12 injections

cycle1.result: Appropriate use 62%; 521 patients inappropriately receiving B12; correct frequency 58%; full pernicious anaemia diagnostic criteria established in 27%

result.intervention: Central analysis and feedback of anonymous aggregated data by the medical audit advisory group

cycle2.result: Appropriate use 72%; 352 inappropriately receiving B12 (32% reduction); correct frequency 72%; diagnostic criteria established in 28%

result.other_findings: 264 GPs (55%) completed both phases; only 10 of 37 singlehanded practices completed the audit.

result.setting: Institute of Biochemistry, Glasgow Royal Infirmary; GP and satellite hospital services
result.standard: Recommendations from an earlier laboratory turnaround time study

cycle1.result: GP reports reaching destination within one and two days: 13% and 68%; satellite hospital 25% and 60%; median total turnaround 50 hours (GP) and 69 hours (satellite)

result.intervention: Posting results directly from the laboratory, then a twice-daily courier service

cycle2.result: Within one and two days: GP 29% and 82%, satellite 78% and 82%; courier cut median turnaround to nine hours (GP) and 18 hours (satellite)

result.other_findings: Analytically old samples arriving the day after collection fell from 25% to 3%.

result.setting: not reported
result.standard: Written infection control guidelines such as Hospital Infection Society model guidelines

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Discussion paper on the audit cycle in infection control; recommends risk-adjusted nosocomial infection rates via repeated prevalence surveys.

result.setting: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Discussion paper on choosing audit topics and standards for antibiotic use.

result.setting: Inpatients (Research Unit, Royal College of Physicians, London)
result.standard: Local guidelines in accordance with British Society for Haematology recommendations

cycle1.result: Confirmatory investigations in 93% (DVT) and 79% (PE); baseline coagulation screen 52%, platelets 95%, LFT 70%, renal 87%; 33% of APTT and 58% of INR subtherapeutic; 72% of 62 discharged with therapeutic INR; 74% had anticoagulant clinic appointments

result.other_findings: 37% stopped heparin without an INR that day or with INR under 2; only 6 of 25 (24%) with delayed clinic appointments had interim INR checks.

result.setting: Two dermatology units (Glasgow Royal Infirmary)
result.standard: Criteria set of 18 questions devised by 66 dermatologists

cycle1.result: Centre B 60% satisfactory completion of the criteria set

result.intervention: Policy decisions and protocols established at centre B only; no changes at centre A

cycle2.result: Centre B 74% satisfactory completion (P < 0.0001); no improvement at centre A

result.other_findings: Doctors in training grades performed best and responded most to policy changes.

result.topic: Electronic study guide for problem-based learning
result.setting: Medical Education Unit, University of Liverpool

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes an electronic study guide for oncology using an educational audit loop; not a clinical audit.

result.topic: Cleft lip and palate service standards
result.setting: Surgical practices in England and Wales (Royal College of Surgeons Surgical Audit and Epidemiology Unit)
result.standard: Recommended minimum standards of care for cleft lip and palate produced by a multidisciplinary steering group

cycle1.result: Widespread involvement of low-volume operators, incomplete networks of associated professionals and non-standardised record keeping

result.other_findings: Further investigation planned to validate standards and provide a baseline for future audit cycles.

result.topic: Asthma guideline implementation and patient education
result.setting: Tertiary hospital (John Hunter Hospital, Newcastle, NSW)

cycle1.result: Satisfactory emergency assessment and treatment but poor compliance with patient education aspects of the asthma management plan

result.intervention: Asthma education and management service developed

cycle2.result: Improvements in asthma control and management skills for attenders and reduced re-admission rates for referred patients (no figures reported)

result.other_findings: Non-attenders to the service remain a target; an area Asthma Health Outcomes Council was formed.

result.setting: Scotland: 132 consultant gynaecologists surveyed and casenote review in 12 representative hospitals
result.standard: 15 evidence-based criteria for good quality care in female laparoscopic sterilisation

cycle1.result: 6% of women under 25; over 85% documented counselling on failure and permanency; 88% by consultant or senior registrar; only 22% mentioned vasectomy discussion; 30% of gynaecologists provided local leaflets; day-case use 19% to 99%

result.other_findings: Questionnaire response rate 94%; four methods of tubal occlusion in use; re-audit planned after dissemination.

result.setting: Victoria Infirmary NHS Trust, Glasgow
result.standard: Agreed written protocols for prophylactic antimicrobials and parenteral co-amoxiclav and metronidazole

cycle1.result: 65% of courses appropriate; 16% of courses too long; co-amoxiclav appropriateness 30%

result.intervention: Agreed protocols distributed and explained to each resident; automatic stopping system

cycle2.result: 72% of 226 courses appropriate; 9% too long; co-amoxiclav appropriateness 68% and use 33% lower

result.other_findings: 82% of doses appropriate when written in the once-only Kardex section versus 51% in the general part; inappropriate choice rose to 19% owing to one-cephalosporin rule.

result.setting: Hospitals in South Thames (East) Region
result.standard: Standards set by the Regional Radiology Audit Committee at the end of the first cycle

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Standards set after the first cycle

cycle2.result: No significant difference in accuracy or false negative and false positive rates between screening and non-screening units; non-screening units more likely to issue equivocal reports (P = 0.000001)

result.other_findings: Recommends issuing an audit grade with reports and double reporting of equivocal images.

result.setting: Department of Radiology, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff
result.standard: Removal of antiscatter grid during filling phase of barium enemas

cycle1.result: Grid removed in 6 of 100 examinations

result.intervention: Data presented at local audit meeting; departmental policy changed to recommend routine grid removal

cycle2.result: Grid removed in 96 of 100 enemas; 46.5% dose reduction for filling phase (95% CI 38-61%)

result.other_findings: None of 22 trainee radiologists routinely removed the grid at baseline; further re-audit showed sustained practice.

result.setting: Department of General Practice, University of Glasgow; final year GP attachment

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Only two students completed the audit cycle in 4 weeks; 90.6% understood audit better and 78% of tutors found teaching audit valuable.

result.setting: Urology department, district general hospital (Torbay Hospital)

cycle1.result: Blood loss equivalent to Hb fall of 10-15 g/L (8-11%); overall transfusion rate 10.8%

cycle2.result: Overall transfusion rate 8.2%; 4.4% to 1% in smaller resections

result.other_findings: Resected weight was the main determinant of blood loss; regional anaesthesia associated with less blood loss.

result.setting: Nine maxillofacial units, prospective multicentre audit

cycle1.result: 73 attended at 6 and 12 weeks; 41 had symptoms at 12 weeks; 50-85% correlation between clinician and external auditor radiographic findings

result.other_findings: Displaced fractures and dislocations had suboptimal outcome in nearly 30%; no gold standard exists to close the loop.

result.setting: Nuclear medicine departments in South Thames Regional Health Authority
result.standard: Guidelines set for ventilation-perfusion, bone, liver, thyroid and renal DMSA imaging

cycle1.result: Organisational audits in 10 departments found lack of facilities and space; high patient satisfaction in nine departments

result.other_findings: A programme of re-audit has commenced.

result.topic: Care of newly diagnosed childhood diabetes
result.setting: Eight districts of East Anglia, paediatric diabetes services

cycle1.result: Good education on injection, blood testing and diet; variable home visits; poor school contact and support group introduction; only three units had adolescent joint clinics; 75% questionnaire return

result.intervention: Peer review and implementation of an action plan

cycle2.result: Modest improvements in problem areas (no figures reported)

result.other_findings: Confidence was best with a dedicated paediatric specialist nurse and adequate cover.

result.setting: District General Hospital (Glan Clwyd), all anaesthetic machines
result.standard: Extended checklist based on Association of Anaesthetists of Great Britain and Ireland checklist

cycle1.result: 236 faults found by 24 tests (range 1.1-64%); 65 (27.5%) day to day, 171 (72.5%) non-recurring

cycle2.result: Faults on 59 occasions by 20 tests (range 1.0-11.6%); 16 (27%) day to day, 43 (73%) non-recurring

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Haematology, consultant haematologists (Guy's Hospital, London)
result.standard: Guidelines on management of platelet refractoriness produced by a working group

cycle1.result: Clinicians differed on the definition of platelet refractoriness; non-immune causes considered less important

result.intervention: Guidelines on recommended practice produced and implemented

cycle2.result: More patients receiving HLA-compatible platelets tested for HLA antibodies; mean 50.9% reduction in HLA-compatible platelet use

result.other_findings: No apparent increase in haemorrhagic complications.

result.setting: Neonatal unit, City Hospital, Nottingham

cycle1.result: Three serious deteriorations in transit

result.intervention: Nine-person nursing transport team formed, improved training and upgraded monitoring

cycle2.result: Improved temperature and pH transport scores on completion; no serious deteriorations in transit

result.other_findings: Stabilisation before transfer took longer in 1994-95.

result.setting: District general hospital (Inverclyde Royal NHS Trust), main clinical specialties
result.standard: SIGN guideline on prevention of deep vein thrombosis; target 90% of at-risk patients prescribed prophylaxis

cycle1.result: 72.8% (n = 163) prescribed prophylaxis; 54% (n = 122) prescribed correct prophylaxis

result.intervention: Local prevention protocols developed or upgraded in line with SIGN guideline; seconded clinician coordinated implementation
result.other_findings: Low-cost initiative of approximately 3,800 pounds.

result.setting: Ninewells Hospital, Dundee
result.standard: Local protocol for magnesium sulphate in eclampsia and severe pre-eclampsia

cycle1.result: Problems with time to therapeutic levels and clinical monitoring of magnesium levels

result.intervention: Protocol changes and introduction of an administration and monitoring chart

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in monitoring and adequacy of prophylaxis (no figures reported)

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: OPAT documentation and bed days saved
result.setting: Acute Care at Home OPAT service, Cornwall Foundation Trust (referrals from primary care and RCHT)
result.standard: 100% of patients receiving IV antibiotics with an indication under OPAT; 100% with dose, frequency and administration method documented; 100% with an OPAT acceptance date

cycle1.result: 343 bed days saved and 302 OPAT treatment days; course lengths within range of NORS 2015-2020 data (compliance with documentation standards not reported)

result.other_findings: Ceftriaxone was the most prescribed antibiotic (27 patients); re-audit with a longer data collection period recommended.

result.setting: Tertiary burns and plastic surgery department
result.standard: Updated local plastic surgery infection guidelines

cycle1.result: Prescriber compliance with the guideline 50%

result.intervention: Guideline updated using local resistance data, departmental teaching, appropriate antibiotics made available in burns and plastics theatres, and all guidelines combined into one document

cycle2.result: Prescriber compliance 71% after three intervention cycles

result.other_findings: Co-amoxiclav and clindamycin were the most common non-compliant prescriptions, reflecting historical usage.

result.topic: Gentamicin level timing and dose administration
result.setting: Acute Medical Unit, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, NHS Lothian
result.standard: Gentamicin guidelines on level sampling window and dosing interval

cycle1.result: 23/31 (74%) levels taken within the recommended window; 23/31 (74%) second doses on time

result.intervention: Gentamicin labels placed in each AMU bay to raise staff awareness

cycle2.result: 31/40 (78%) levels within the window; 30/40 (75%) subsequent doses at the right interval

result.other_findings: Most delayed second doses were in patients whose first dose was given in the emergency department before AMU admission.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis review in recurrent UTI
result.setting: Three GP practices, Bridgend Locality, Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board; later Bridgend locality-wide
result.standard: NICE NG15 and NG112: clinical review within 6 months for patients on antibiotic prophylaxis for recurrent UTI

cycle1.result: Of 160 on prophylaxis for >6 months, 24% had a review within 6 months; 39% on prophylaxis >3 years; 82.5% continued on a potentially ineffective antibiotic after resistant MSU

result.intervention: Audit feedback to practices, co-designed action plan to review patients, pharmacist support; rolled out through Welsh GMS contract QI basket

cycle2.dates: Re-audit 6 months after review (Welsh GMS 2019/20, live until September 2022)
cycle2.result: 334 (77.5%) of 431 reviewed; 171 (51%) of those reviewed stopped; 40% locality reduction in rUTI prophylaxis

result.other_findings: 54.7% had at least one acute UTI while on prophylaxis; estimated 2223 fewer antibiotic prescriptions per year.

result.setting: Medical specialties, RCHT (Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust)
result.standard: NICE guidance to stop antibiotics at day 5 for CAP/HAP if clinically stable

cycle1.result: 10 (45%) received 5 or 6 days; 12 (55%) received 7 to 10 days despite meeting stop criteria; mean 6.5 and median 6.3 days

result.other_findings: Education and an EPMA day-5 alert are proposed; re-audit with a larger sample recommended.

result.topic: Early intervention in psychosis waiting times
result.setting: Early Intervention in Psychosis team, Liverpool
result.standard: NICE access and waiting time standard: 60% of people with first episode psychosis treated with an approved care package within two weeks of referral

cycle1.result: Average referral pathway time 9.8 days

result.intervention: Recommendations from the initial audit implemented (details not reported)

cycle2.result: Average pathway time 22.5 days, exceeding the NICE standard

result.other_findings: Main delays were referral assessment, care coordinator allocation and prescriber review, related to COVID-19 and a 50% rise in FEP patients.

result.setting: Behavioural Sciences Institute, Al Ain Hospital, inpatient and outpatient services
result.standard: Local Al Ain Hospital guidelines and Royal College of Psychiatrists ECT standards

cycle1.result: 16 (53%) had no capacity documentation on consent papers; 4 of 8 lacking capacity had reasons documented; 20 (67%) had no documented risk-benefit discussion

result.other_findings: Staff training and a risk-benefit section on the ECT consent form are proposed, with re-audit after one year.

result.setting: Community Mental Health Team, St Davnet's Hospital, Monaghan
result.standard: British Association for Psychopharmacology guidelines for metabolic syndrome monitoring

cycle1.result: 39.6% had MetS monitoring charts; 29.2% completed; BP, lipids and glucose documented in 31.3%; BMI/girth 29.2%

result.intervention: Psychoeducation for nursing staff on monitoring and documentation guidelines

cycle2.result: MetS charts 100% completed; glucose 95.7%; blood pressure 91.3%; BMI/girth and lipids 87%

result.other_findings: Colour-coded stickers and a MetS clinic proposed to sustain improvement.

result.setting: Inpatient adult intellectual disability assessment and treatment unit, New Craig's Psychiatric Hospital, Inverness

cycle1.result: Missing records included anxiolytic use before seclusion, respiration rate and appearance at 15-minute checks, plans to end seclusion at 2 hours, consultant informed at 4 hours, and Datix submission

result.other_findings: Results shared via working group, teaching and governance forum; re-audit planned.

result.topic: Prolactin monitoring on antipsychotics in children
result.setting: Child psychiatry outpatient clinic, Al Ain Hospital
result.standard: NICE CG155: prolactin at baseline, 12 weeks and every six months in children on antipsychotics

cycle1.result: No baseline prolactin measured; 10 (7%) checked at 12 weeks; none checked six-monthly

result.other_findings: Local guidance, staff training and electronic monitoring alerts recommended, with re-audit after one year.

result.topic: Physical health checks on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Samphire ward, acute inpatient psychiatric facility (Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: NSFT Physical Healthcare Policy (C84): 100% baseline bloods, physical examination and ECG within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Physical examination 34.5%; ECG 53%; bloods 68% (correct bloods 4.5%); all three components 0%

result.intervention: A3 visual aid placed on the ward

cycle2.result: Physical examination 47%; ECG 61%; bloods 71% (correct bloods 33%); all three components 33%

result.other_findings: Ward doctors adhered to the standard significantly more than duty doctors.

result.topic: Depression screening in chronic physical illness
result.setting: Acute medical services, North Middlesex University Hospital

cycle1.result: 85% with past depression reported current symptoms; 48% with chronic physical condition reported low mood or anhedonia

result.intervention: Screening questions added to the medical clerking proforma, new referral pathway with liaison psychiatry, and departmental teaching on CG91

cycle2.result: Clinician completion of screening questions 65%; 44% with chronic physical problems reported depressive symptoms; 84% of identified patients had a planned referral

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Emergency department and radiology, East Lancashire Hospitals Trust
result.standard: NICE CG176: 100% scanned within 1 hour of risk factors identified; 100% provisional reports within 1 hour of scan; all ED requests document head injury risk factors

cycle1.result: 36% met criteria for 1-hour scan; 19 (52%) of those met all 3 standards; 4 of 8 positive scans scanned and reported on time

cycle2.result: 45% met criteria for 1-hour scan; 37 (83%) met all 3 standards; 11 of 13 positive scans on time

result.setting: Surgical Assessment Unit, Royal Gwent Hospital, Newport
result.standard: Timely completion of discharge summaries (target not reported)

cycle1.result: 36.2% delayed discharge summaries; average 7 days to complete

cycle2.result: 45.3% delayed discharge summaries; average 12 days to complete

result.topic: Timely cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
result.setting: Surgical Department, Great Western Hospital
result.standard: Current guidelines on timing of cholecystectomy after diagnosis; RCSEng national average 15%

cycle1.result: Very low number of patients had cholecystectomy within the target timeframe; biliary re-admissions 58%

cycle2.result: Timely cholecystectomy compliance 14% (10.7% increase); biliary re-admissions 37%

result.setting: Emergency general surgery, East Surrey Hospital, Redhill
result.standard: Published guidelines on consenting for COVID-19 risks

cycle1.result: COVID pneumonia consented 70%; ITU admission 25%; risk of death 21%

cycle2.result: COVID pneumonia 89%; ITU admission 56%; risk of death 63%

result.other_findings: 57 consent forms were assessed across both cycles.

result.setting: District general hospital, emergency and elective general surgery (Victoria Hospital, Kirkcaldy)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England COVID-19 guidance: COVID-19 infection to be discussed as a possible complication during consent

cycle1.result: 77.1% (27/35) of consent forms mentioned COVID-19 infection; 5/6 by clinical fellows or CT trainees, 10/13 by registrars, 12/16 by consultants.

result.other_findings: No significant correlation between grade of consent taker and COVID-19 being mentioned. Results to be presented and a re-audit planned in a few weeks.

result.topic: Escalation of care and DNAR documentation
result.setting: Older adult mental health inpatient unit, Angelton Clinic, Bridgend
result.standard: GMC recommendations on discussion of cardiopulmonary resuscitation and escalation of care

cycle1.result: 18% of notes had escalation of care plans; 84% had DNAR forms.

result.intervention: New escalation of care proforma designed with MDT input, implemented through education and communication with the medical team.

cycle2.result: 78% of notes had completed escalation of care forms; 83% had completed DNAR forms.

result.other_findings: Unit nurse practitioner to champion completion; proformas made available on all inpatient wards.

result.setting: NAViGO Health and Social Care, community mental health teams and inpatient teams, North East Lincolnshire
result.standard: NICE guidance adapted as local Shared Care Guidelines: baseline and follow-up physical health monitoring for 12 months after starting antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Overall baseline compliance across 16 parameters 50% (CMHT 60%, inpatient 38%); 1-, 3- and 6-month compliance 33%, 29% and 29%. GASS completed 7% at baseline, 0% at 1 and 3 months, 7% at 6 months.

result.other_findings: This was a re-audit of a 2018 local audit; baseline compliance highest (80%) for renal function, liver function and blood pressure/pulse. GASS performance was unchanged from the previous audit.

result.setting: Community intellectual disability service, Lincolnshire Partnership Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE CG11 and physical health CQUIN targets (Lester adaptation tool): cardiometabolic monitoring for people with intellectual disability on antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Baseline cardiometabolic assessment in 50–65%; less than 15% at 3–6 months. Weight and blood pressure recorded in 15% and 2.5% at 3–6 months. GP collaboration for annual health check 78–100%.

result.other_findings: Compliance was significantly better when the nursing team was involved. Re-audit planned in one year.

result.setting: Mildred Creek Unit, inpatient CAMHS ward, Great Ormond Street Hospital
result.standard: Ward risk assessment policy: risk assessment within one working day of admission

cycle1.result: Average delay between admission and risk assessment was 2 weeks.

result.intervention: Posters prompting on-call liaison doctors, written and verbal information for new junior doctors, and a risk prompt added to the weekly ward round proforma.

cycle2.result: No patients had risk assessment delayed beyond the next working day.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Physical health monitoring of psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Male and female psychiatric rehabilitation wards, Delfryn Lodge, Cygnet Health Care
result.standard: NICE guidelines, RCPsych report on physical health in mental health and Cygnet physical health policy

cycle1.result: 98% physical assessment within 24 hours of admission; monthly physical health reviews 62%, annual HIP 30%, high-dose antipsychotic monitoring 10%, ECG/bloods for antipsychotic monitoring 64%.

result.intervention: QI approaches (4 PDSA cycles, driver diagrams): MDT strategies to improve engagement, care plan points, diary reminders for bloods and ECGs, patient and staff health education, and a designated support worker for physical observations and files.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 92%; high-dose antipsychotic monitoring 100%, monthly physical health clinics 88%, annual HIP 75%, annual antipsychotic monitoring/bloods/ECG 95%.

result.other_findings: 10 female and 12 male patients regularly refused observations, weights and physical health monitoring at baseline.

result.setting: Liaison psychiatry department, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford (tertiary centre)
result.standard: NCEPOD Treat as One (2017) recommendations on content of liaison psychiatry documentation

cycle1.result: Primary diagnosis 77.9%, reason for referral 66.3%, mental capacity 19.8%, need for DOLS 2.3%, risks 27.9%, risk management 7%; clear plan 61.6%, medication changes 51.4%, useful plan 73%, answered referral question 69.8%, action points assigned 47.7%, non-medical MDT advice 18.6%.

result.intervention: Electronic documentation template developed from the report recommendations and implemented for all initial reviews.
result.other_findings: Re-audit planned for March 2020.

result.setting: Heddfan adult mental health inpatient unit, BCUHB, north Wales
result.standard: Standard based on RCPsych core training intended learning outcomes and textbooks; target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: GMC number documented 30%, route of admission 4%, consultant name 8%, nursing observation level 20%; no personal history or formulation documented; risk assessment, mental state and physical examination often incomplete.

result.other_findings: Clerking and physical health proforma planned, with re-audit after introduction.

result.setting: General adult psychiatry inpatients, University Hospital Hairmyres and University Hospital Wishaw, NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: SIGN 131 and NHS Lanarkshire recommendation: GASS offered on admission and after antipsychotic initiation or titration

cycle1.result: GASS on admission 4.2%, after initiation/titration 9.5%, discussed at MDT 3.7%.

result.intervention: Presentations at clinical governance and departmental teaching, email to consultants, meetings with senior charge nurses, and GASS added to routine admission paperwork.

cycle2.result: GASS on admission 11.1%, after initiation/titration 40.0%, discussed at MDT 21.7%.

result.other_findings: Improvement was modest; greater gains in prescriber-led measures.

result.setting: High security forensic psychiatric hospital (Broadmoor Hospital)
result.standard: Public Health England national guidance on investigation and management of suspected and confirmed COVID-19

cycle1.result: SARS-CoV-2 detected in 1 patient; practice consistent with national guidance.

cycle2.result: SARS-CoV-2 detected in 12 patients; identification and management consistent with national guidance.

result.other_findings: Three cycles (10, 12 and 21 patients), one per wave. All patients recovered; three needed oral antibiotics and dexamethasone and one was admitted to a general hospital for oxygen.

result.setting: Heddfan Psychiatric Unit, Wrexham Maelor Hospital
result.standard: Public Health England PPE donning and doffing guidance

cycle1.result: Donning per guidance 64% (about one third by another measure); only half removed apron and mask correctly; 7/50 used hand gel during doffing; 10–14% did not wear PPE.

result.intervention: PPE donning and doffing training for almost 150 staff.

cycle2.result: 100% followed donning technique and hand washing before donning; only 2/50 did not follow doffing guidance; almost 90% used hand gel correctly.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Enfield South Locality Team, Barnet, Enfield and Haringey Mental Health Trust
result.standard: Locally agreed audit standards (95%) on frequency of prolactin monitoring, time to review and referral

cycle1.result: Only 7/30 (23.33%) tested within the last year; no audit standards met. 2 (6.667%) had new hyperprolactinaemia, both reviewed and treated within one month.

result.intervention: New risk-stratified hyperprolactinaemia guidance developed (awaiting ratification).
result.other_findings: Reasons for failure included loss to follow-up, tests not requested and missed appointments. Re-audit planned for 2020.

result.setting: Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust inpatient services
result.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice, NICE and Trust seclusion policy

cycle1.result: Above 90% for time of review, record keeping, management plan, risk, mental state and physical health; prescribed medications 60%, medication side effects 40%, physical observations 40%.

result.intervention: Seclusion medical review template incorporated into the existing documentation template, with teaching for doctors.

cycle2.result: Quality of seclusion medical review between 95% and 100%; no major concerns.

result.other_findings: Project prompted nurses to audit nursing seclusion reviews.

result.setting: Dova Unit, Dane Garth, psychiatric inpatient unit
result.standard: Completion of VTE prophylaxis admission assessment

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 35%; VTE risk assessment 50%, active VTE on admission 30%, active VTE at 72 hours 20%, risk assessment form 40%.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 50%; VTE risk assessment 60%, active VTE on admission 40%, active VTE at 72 hours 40%, risk assessment form 60%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Older persons community mental health team, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: NICE guideline on antipsychotics for behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia; local CAIR form

cycle1.result: CAIR form present in 73% (new shorter version 37%); 63% of forms fully completed. 100% had assessment of causes, non-drug measures first, target symptoms and risk-benefit discussion; all reviewed within three months.

result.intervention: Teaching session at team meeting, health board leaflet for patients and carers, and reversion to the original CAIR form.
result.other_findings: Risk-benefit discussions were documented vaguely. Re-audit planned in 6 months.

result.setting: Clozapine clinics, Worcester, Kidderminster and Redditch, Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE CG178 psychosis and schizophrenia in adults; target 100%

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: HbA1c and FBC monitoring remained good; improved monitoring of alcohol, substance misuse and side effects; respiratory rate still poorly recorded; decline in recording temperature, BMI and concomitant therapies.

result.other_findings: Recommendations: junior doctor induction teaching, staff training, ECG machines for each site, GP data sharing, re-audit in 1 year.

result.setting: Psychiatric intensive care unit, Parklands Hospital

cycle1.result: 3 of 10 PICU patients were on high-dose antipsychotics; 2 reported constipation, one needing daily review and laxatives.

result.other_findings: Recommended Bristol stool chart in care plans, teaching, early prophylactic laxatives and more fruit and vegetables; re-audit handed over.

result.setting: Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust inpatient services
result.standard: Trust seclusion policy based on Mental Health Act Code of Practice (review within first hour then every 4 hours until MDT, then twice daily)

cycle1.result: Above 80% for time of review, record keeping, plan for continuing seclusion, risk and mental state; less than 60% for prescribed medications, medication side effects and physical observations.

result.intervention: Seclusion medical review template developed, with teaching and example documentation for doctors.
result.other_findings: Re-audit planned in 1 year.

result.setting: Specialist addictions service (opioid substitution therapy), three hubs, Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Attendance at an addictions prescriber review in the last 3 months
result.intervention: New appointment letter, text confirmation and reminder, keyworker verbal reminder, prescriber calls to persistent non-attenders, and medication safety review for non-attenders (enhanced QIP).

cycle2.result: 86% (78/91) attended; all 13 non-attenders had a medication review.

result.other_findings: Hub 1 fell to 51% (48/92) in October 2018 before the enhanced plan; December 2018 all hubs 76% (258/339), with medication reviews for 94% (74/81) of non-attenders.

result.setting: Shannon Clinic, secure psychiatric unit
result.standard: Correct prescribing of nicotine replacement therapy

cycle1.result: 22% of drug charts had NRT prescribed incorrectly.

result.intervention: Poster on correct NRT prescribing placed on each ward.

cycle2.result: 0% of drug charts had NRT prescribed incorrectly.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Inner-city psychiatric ward, Phoenix Care Centre
result.standard: Mental Health Commission Judgment Support Framework version 5; target 100% physical examination on admission

cycle1.result: 3/13 had physical examination on admission (23%); 6 had examination in ED.

result.intervention: Colour-coded physical examination proforma developed and implemented, with MDT and NCHD briefing.
result.other_findings: Proforma to be audited every 6 months.

result.topic: SSRI monitoring in children and adolescents
result.setting: Child and adolescent mental health service, Black Country Healthcare
result.standard: NICE and Maudsley guidelines: follow-up one week after starting SSRI and review every 4–6 weeks

cycle1.result: 17/18 followed up; median follow-up 42 days; none within a week. Improvement monitored in 88%, adverse effects in 36%; 53% had no documented adverse-effect monitoring.

result.other_findings: Dose increased in 22% without documented adverse-effect monitoring. One-week follow-up judged impractical; re-audit recommended.

result.setting: Male medium secure service, The Spinney Hospital, Atherton

cycle1.result: 9 of 51 without current diagnosis screened positive on B-BAARS (17.65%); 1 had current ADHD diagnosis.

result.other_findings: B-BAARS to be added to the admission care plan for new admissions, with future re-audit.

result.topic: Capacity and consent to treatment documentation
result.setting: Inpatient wards, Atherleigh Park Hospital, Northwest Boroughs Healthcare NHS FT
result.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice: six standards on capacity assessment, consent to treatment and medication education

cycle1.result: Capacity and consent forms recorded in 77%; 57% re-assessed when capacity changed; standards 2–4 fully compliant; concordance documented 76%, adverse effects 39%; 47% given leaflet, 28% educated on side effects.

result.other_findings: Actions: link capacity form to electronic ward round notes, post-prescription monitoring and leaflets; re-audit planned.

result.topic: Physical health form completion on psychiatric wards
result.setting: General adult inpatient psychiatric ward, Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Five Year Forward View for Mental Health; target ≥95% physical health form completion (HbA1c and cholesterol or declined) within 4 months

cycle1.result: 61.54% of physical health forms completed (HbA1c 61.54%, cholesterol 76.92%).

result.intervention: PDSA cycles of completion trackers: paper list, Word table, Excel spreadsheet, then colour-coded conditionally formatted Excel spreadsheet.

cycle2.result: 97.7% completion (after 100% in November, n = 34, and December, n = 39).

result.other_findings: Paper list 84.85% (n = 33), Word table 96.43% (n = 28), Excel 96.67% (n = 30), colour-coded Excel 100% (n = 28) within 8 weeks.

result.topic: Physical health checks in substance misuse services
result.setting: Gwent Specialist Substance Misuse Service (North Team)
result.standard: Completion of physical examination, 12-lead ECG and blood-borne virus screening

cycle1.result: Physical examination 60/121 (50%); ECG 37/121 (31%); BBV test in last 6 months 62/121.

result.other_findings: Abnormality found in 77% of examinations, most often hypertension (n = 9) and abdominal tenderness (n = 9). Physical examination rates had risen from 0% previously; a front-of-notes checklist was recommended.

result.topic: Life support training of psychiatric ward staff
result.setting: Acute inpatient psychiatric wards, Stepping Hill Hospital, Stockport
result.standard: NICE CG25 (2005) and NPSA Rapid Response Report 2008/RRR010 on medical emergency training

cycle1.result: Nursing staff training met standards except new staff or staff returning from prolonged leave; gaps in other staff and in the remaining standards.

result.other_findings: This was a re-audit of a 2016 audit; gaps attributed to new or bank staff covering wards without training or orientation.

result.setting: Emergency department and acute medical unit, Royal Berkshire Hospital
result.standard: Trust guidelines on penicillin allergy classification (causative antibiotic, symptoms, timing and management of reaction)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Findings fed back to the ED team at departmental teaching.

cycle2.result: Small improvement in documentation; 56% of notes still lacked enough information to classify severity.

result.other_findings: Under 5% of documented histories were an absolute contraindication to penicillin. Trust classification guideline being updated and a multidisciplinary QI project started.

result.setting: General adult psychiatry wards, University Hospital Wishaw
result.standard: Local trust guidelines: ASSIGN score calculation, statin prescribing, lifestyle advice or GP communication for abnormal lipids

cycle1.result: 85/116 had a lipid profile on admission; 29 had abnormal levels without a statin; 6 had abnormal results in the discharge letter without ASSIGN score or lifestyle advice.

result.intervention: Email with flyer of trust guidelines to doctors and presentation at internal teaching.

cycle2.result: 35/120 had a lipid profile on admission; 12 abnormal without a statin; 1 ASSIGN score calculated; 7 had results communicated to the GP.

result.other_findings: No significant improvement after re-audit; QRISK3 suggested as an alternative to ASSIGN.

result.setting: General adult psychiatric inpatient unit, Heddfan Psychiatric Unit, Wrexham, BCUHB
result.standard: Psychiatry core competencies, NICE guidelines, BCUHB physical health policy and Department of Health VTE guidance; target 100% within 18 months

cycle1.result: Baseline showed incomplete vital data at clerking (figures not reported).

result.intervention: Admission clerking proforma developed using fishbone and driver diagrams and PDSA cycles, with junior doctor education.

cycle2.result: Improved completion of medication details, allergy status, legal and forensic status, mental state, risk assessment, VTE assessment and investigations (figures not reported).

result.other_findings: Weaknesses included no ECG machine and missing documentation of completed investigations.

result.setting: Department of Psychiatry and Behavioural Sciences, Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, Karachi

cycle1.result: 70% of trainees rated very good and 30% excellent.

result.intervention: Individual feedback to trainees immediately after sessions using the audit tool.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Acute medical wards, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: Health board antipsychotic policy for delirium based on NICE guidelines

cycle1.result: Antipsychotics prescribed in 57%; 100% compliance for appropriate drug, maximum dose and investigations (except chest x-ray and CT); 54% stopped before discharge; monitoring by GP stated in 23% and by treating team in 23%.

result.other_findings: Cause of delirium documented in 55% (UTI 31%, multifactorial 27%). Training planned and re-audit in 6 months.

result.setting: Mental Health Service for the Elderly, Cavan and Monaghan Mental Health Service, County Monaghan
result.standard: NICE guidelines on lithium prescribing and monitoring

cycle1.result: All 3-monthly lithium levels completed; 100% had information booklet, record book and BMI; 60% of 6-monthly levels completed; 20% of 6-monthly bloods done but not documented.

cycle2.result: 100% completed 3- and 6-monthly lithium levels, with 100% documentation.

result.other_findings: Lithium clinic recommended, with blood pathways, reminder letters, recording tables and alert cards.

result.topic: Substance misuse assessment in liaison psychiatry
result.setting: Liaison psychiatry service, Derriford Hospital (Livewell Southwest)
result.standard: Assessment of alcohol and drug use and offer of advice, intervention or referral

cycle1.result: Nearly half of patients assessed were not asked about alcohol or drug use.

cycle2.result: Alcohol use asked in 78%, drug use in 77%; 73% of those with an identified problem (n = 15) offered advice or intervention.

result.other_findings: Documentation of advice or intervention rose by 21% since August 2020. Misuse identified in 10% of those asked about alcohol and 13% of those asked about drugs.

result.setting: Langley Green Hospital, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Post-ligature assessment including ABCDE documentation, NEWS monitoring and follow-up plan

cycle1.result: Medic informed in 4; 0 ABCDE documentation; 0 NEWS monitoring; 3 follow-up plans.

result.intervention: Locality teaching on audit findings, post-ligature assessment tool, and trial in simulation induction for new trainees.

cycle2.result: Medic informed in 4; 0 ABCDE documentation; NEWS monitored in 6; 4 follow-up plans.

result.other_findings: Documentation remained highly variable; teaching was not trust-wide and some incidents involved locum doctors.

result.setting: Inpatient general adult mental health units, Wrexham, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: NICE guideline: Smoking – acute, maternity and mental health services

cycle1.result: 71.88% asked about smoking history; less than 10% assessed in detail.

result.intervention: PowerPoint presentation on smoking assessment tools shared with doctors (after a first re-audit without intervention).

cycle2.result: 57.14% assessed for smoking; less than 40% assessed in detail.

result.other_findings: First re-audit without intervention (n = 19) fell to 36.84%, with less than 16% assessed in detail. Change in doctors' postings may explain minimal improvement.

result.setting: Elective endoscopic ultrasound service, Hull University Teaching Hospitals
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology and NICE guidance: COVID-19 test within 3 days (72 hours) before EUS; target >90%

cycle1.result: 95.7% swabbed within 3 days but only 40.9% within 72 hours.

result.intervention: Results discussed at a morbidity and mortality meeting with recommendations made.

cycle2.result: 98.4% swabbed within 3 days and 95.2% within 72 hours.

result.other_findings: Target of >90% met by mid-2021.

result.setting: 12 general practices in a primary care network (North Solihull)
result.standard: NICE NG114, NG168 and local formulary: 100% no prophylactic antibiotics for COVID-19; 100% no antibiotics for COVID-19 symptoms; 90% of regimens adherent to guidelines

cycle1.result: Standard 1 100% adherence; standard 2 99.4% (2 patients given antibiotics for suspected COVID-19); standard 3 only 28.7% adherent, mainly due to 7-day rather than 5-day courses.

result.other_findings: Antibiotic prescribing did not change significantly between 2019 and 2020 (1029 vs 1134 prescriptions; p>0.05). Re-audit suggested after NG191.

result.setting: Tertiary pancreatic (HPB) surgery centre
result.standard: NICE NG85: avoid preoperative biliary drainage to allow early curative surgery

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Additional theatre sessions obtained and a fast-track referral pathway established after the prior audit.

cycle2.result: 42/71 received preoperative biliary drainage; 29 did not. Median imaging to surgery 21 days (3–42) without drainage vs 62 days (22–305) with drainage (p=0.00028).

result.other_findings: No significant difference in HDU/ITU stay, Clavien-Dindo >2 complications (30% vs 27.8%), R0 rates or hospital stay. COVID-19 constraints likely increased drainage rates.

result.setting: Emergency theatres, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Baseline sending, anaesthetic, operating and recovery times (values not reported).

result.intervention: Established COVID-19 testing protocols and recommendations from first audit, including a second emergency theatre.

cycle2.result: Sending time decreased by 27% (p=1.25*10–7); anaesthetic time decreased by 31% (p=0.0001); recovery time in theatre decreased by 26% (p = 0.06); total recovery time increased by 19% (p=0.097).

result.other_findings: Sending time also 17% better than pre-pandemic figures.

result.topic: Group and save before TURBT and cystoscopy
result.setting: Urology pre-operative assessment for TURBT or rigid cystoscopy and bladder biopsy

cycle1.result: 32.8% (21/64) had a preoperative group and save; 98.4% (63/64) had Hb measured; no transfusions required.

result.intervention: Telephone pre-operative assessment during COVID-19 where group and save was deemed unnecessary.

cycle2.result: 6.25% (3/48) had a group and save; 70.8% (34/48) had Hb measured; no transfusions required.

result.other_findings: Routine group and save judged not clinically indicated, saving £964 over 6 months (64 cases); each sample costs £7.54.

result.setting: Mount Carmel Hospital (mental hospital), Malta
result.standard: NICE guidelines (2014): lithium levels every 3 months for patients at increased risk of toxicity; target level 0.4–0.8 mmol/L

cycle1.result: Only 1 of 28 high-risk patients had 3-monthly lithium levels; 35.7% of last levels within 0.4–0.8 mmol/L.

result.intervention: Lithium monitoring sheet created in line with NICE guidance.

cycle2.result: 12 patients (42%) met 3-monthly testing; 50% of last levels within 0.4–0.8 mmol/L.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Tertiary paediatric rheumatology day-care and outpatient clinics
result.standard: National guidance: immunocompromised 12–18-year-olds offered three primary Pfizer BioNTech doses 8 weeks apart plus a booster within 3 months

cycle1.result: 6/31 (19%) knew the correct regime (3 + 1); 18/31 (58%) had received the vaccine.

result.other_findings: 9 (29%) unvaccinated were unsure if they needed it and 4 (13%) declined for personal beliefs; 4 refused further doses after side effects. Action plan includes documenting status at every contact, nurse education, default clinic letter text and re-audit in six months.

result.setting: National postgraduate psychiatry training programme, Malta

cycle1.result: Difficulty accessing clinical supervision (66%), lack of research presentation opportunities (75%) and difficulties with the psychotherapy module (66.7%).

result.other_findings: Report presented to training committees; suggested changes include rotation-specific teaching and an annual research day, with re-survey in one year.

result.topic: Vaccination in patients on biologic therapy
result.setting: Dermatology clinic, patients over 65 on biologic therapy
result.standard: British Association of Dermatologists guidelines (August 2021): COVID-19, influenza and pneumococcal vaccination for patients on biologics

cycle1.result: 100% (n=18) had three COVID-19 vaccines; 94% (n=17) influenza vaccine; 66% (n=12) pneumococcal vaccine.

result.other_findings: Unvaccinated patients advised to have pneumococcal vaccine; educational intervention and re-audit planned next year.

result.setting: Paediatric inpatient ward, district general hospital
result.standard: Trust guidelines: 5–7 days of amoxicillin for simple community-acquired pneumonia

cycle1.result: Median antibiotic duration 7 days (range 1–9); 7 children (23.3%) received more than 7 days. 40% amoxicillin only, 26.7% co-amoxiclav only, 33.3% combinations.

result.intervention: Trust guideline changed via Paediatric Microguide to allow a 3-day amoxicillin course.
result.other_findings: 9 of 28 children with chest x-ray (32.1%) had no focal changes but all received antibiotics. Re-audit planned for winter 2022–23.

result.setting: Emergency department, St. Boniface General Hospital (tertiary care centre), Manitoba
result.standard: Guidelines: first medical contact to thrombolysis within 30 minutes and to primary PCI within 90 minutes

cycle1.result: 41 (70.7%) received reperfusion; for thrombolysis median first contact to reperfusion 54 [37-72] minutes, with 12.0% (remainder of result truncated in abstract).

result.intervention: Results conveyed to emergency room staff and a dedicated EKG machine placed in the ER.
result.other_findings: Treatment times were longer than guideline recommendations.

result.setting: Department of Radiotherapy, PGIMER, Chandigarh

cycle1.result: Median overall survival 36 months and disease-free survival 26 months; local recurrence 19% radical radiation, 22% surgery, 6% chemoradiation; bladder preserved in 61% after chemoradiation.

result.other_findings: Nodal involvement was the only factor affecting DFS and OS on multivariate analysis.

result.topic: Oral morphine prescribing for cancer pain
result.setting: Department of Pain and Palliative Care, St. John's Medical College Hospital, Bangalore (tertiary care)
result.standard: Locally set standards for adequacy of pain relief with oral morphine

cycle1.result: Only 50% achieved adequate pain relief; rescue dose given to only 20%.

result.intervention: Education for doctors and nurses on starting, titrating and giving rescue doses of morphine, followed by circulation of local guidelines.

cycle2.result: 80% achieved adequate pain relief and 100% received rescue doses.

result.other_findings: Twenty case files were analysed across the pre- and post-education audits. Failure to give regular and rescue doses caused inadequate pain relief.

result.setting: Primary care (general practitioners), Castelnovo né Monti healthcare district with Puianello district as control, Reggio Emilia
result.standard: Jointly developed pathology-specific laboratory profiles and inclusion of provisional diagnosis on request forms

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Seven pathology-specific laboratory profiles developed by a multidisciplinary team, with 8 training sessions for the 23 trial GPs.

cycle2.result: Number of tests requested in the trial district fell by about 5% (remainder truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Significant decrease in tests ordered only in the trial district, not in the 21-GP control district; most GPs improved prescriptive compliance.

result.setting: Elective paediatric surgery, Christian Medical College, Vellore (tertiary care)
result.standard: International guidelines: 2 h clear fluids, 4 h breast milk, 6 h solids and formula milk

cycle1.result: Mean fasting 11.25 h for solids and 9.25 h for water; causes were incorrect orders by ward nurses (74%) and surgical schedule changes (32%).

result.intervention: Ward nurse education on fasting guidelines and anaesthetist coordination with surgeons and nurses to give water by telephone instruction when delays exceeded 2 h.

cycle2.result: Mean fasting 9 h for solids and 4 h for water.

result.other_findings: Change in surgical schedule (30%) remained the main cause of prolonged fasting on re-audit.

result.setting: Moshupa clinic and catchment area, Moshupa District
result.standard: Target standards for structure, process and outcome of hypertension care

cycle1.result: None of the target standards met.

result.intervention: Simple interventions designed and implemented to improve care (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Six of nine structural, five of 11 process and one of two outcome target standards achieved.

result.other_findings: Significant improvement in blood pressure control was also seen.

result.setting: Non-communicable disease clinic, rural health and training centre, Puducherry
result.standard: Standard guidelines for monitoring blood pressure, blood glucose, lipid profile and renal function

cycle1.result: BP 78 (50%), blood glucose 70 (44.9%), lipid profile 49 (31.4%), renal function 19 (12.2%).

result.intervention: Clinical audit cycle applied (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Monitoring improved significantly: blood glucose by 35%, BP by 20.7%, lipid profile by 36.4% and renal function by 56.1%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Medical inpatients, Charing Cross Hospital, London teaching hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians handover guidance

cycle1.result: Handover proformas: ceiling of care 4%, past medical history 23%; problem list on 62% of Friday ward round entries (n=84).

result.intervention: New handover proformas and Friday ward round sheets, explained via medical meetings and emails.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in all parameters, e.g. past medical history 52% on proformas; only 10% of Friday entries used the sheet, but problem list 100% when used.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Transoesophageal echocardiography service

cycle1.result: Midazolam doses exceeding Trust guidelines were given, especially risky in under 18 and over 60 year-olds.

result.intervention: Paediatric sedation dosing section added to Trust guidelines and pre-procedure checklist updated with age and maximum midazolam dose.
result.other_findings: Changes accepted at clinical governance meeting; re-audit needed.

result.setting: ENT emergency clinic
result.standard: National guidelines on safe clinic numbers

cycle1.result: 45% attended without primary care assessment; mean wait 75 minutes; clinic numbers above safe levels; 60% of attendances inappropriate.

result.intervention: Open access clinic changed to appointment-based Rapid Access Clinic with trained triage nurse, improved record keeping and formal post-consultation communication.

cycle2.result: 43% fewer patients; clinic numbers at safe levels; mean waiting time fell 70% to 22 minutes; inappropriate referrals halved.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Macular treatment centre, Manchester Royal Eye Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Ophthalmologists' recommendations on appointment intervals for ranibizumab treatment

cycle1.result: Appointment system did not meet standards and visual outcomes were poorer than trial standards.

result.intervention: Changes to the appointment system, expansion of the treatment facility and employment of additional staff.

cycle2.result: Appointment standards reached Royal College recommendations; visual outcomes approached landmark study standards.

result.other_findings: Regular re-audits were used between cycles.

result.setting: Emergency department, Scotland (with Scottish National Blood Transfusion Service)

cycle1.result: 3209 units ordered; 39.5% transfused; 9.5% (289 units) unaccounted for.

result.intervention: Staff education, monthly traceability reports, ED transfusion guideline, blood fridge moved to resuscitation room, named transfusion consultant and link nurse, and hospital transfusion group representation.

cycle2.result: 1034 units ordered (64% reduction); 687 transfused (39% reduction); 68% increase in proportion transfused; 9 units unaccounted for (96% reduction).

result.other_findings: SNBTS spent £306,437 less in 2011 than 2007 on ED transfusion requests.

result.setting: Adult wards, hospital
result.standard: Immediate availability of 1:1000 adrenaline for anaphylaxis

cycle1.result: Adrenaline unavailable on 50% of audited wards; staff lacked knowledge of anaphylaxis management and drug location.

result.intervention: Anaphylaxis packs (adrenaline, chlorphenamine, hydrocortisone, algorithm) added to crash trolleys and checklist, piloted on four wards via PDSA then trust-wide.

cycle2.result: 100% ward stock of anaphylaxis packs, more consistent drug location and improved staff knowledge.

result.other_findings: 17 coded anaphylaxis incidents in 2011.

result.setting: Elderly care ward
result.standard: Target 20% reduction in inpatient falls rate

cycle1.result: 14.70 falls per 1000 bed days.

result.intervention: Falls risk care plan, 'walking-stick' incentive poster for nurses and post-fall guidelines, with staff feedback sessions.

cycle2.result: 12.44 falls per 1000 bed days, a 15.4% reduction.

result.other_findings: Care plan compliance 89%; up to 81% of patients high-risk. 20% target not yet met.

result.topic: Ureteric stone admission and discharge from the emergency department
result.setting: Accident and Emergency department, Croydon University Hospital
result.standard: Appropriate admission or discharge of patients with radiologically proven ureteric stones (no specific criteria existed at baseline)

cycle1.result: No easily accessible, specific criteria were used to guide which patients were admitted and which discharged.

result.intervention: Admission criteria and a discharge proforma were developed and implemented in A&E.

cycle2.result: Fewer unnecessary admissions and fewer inappropriate discharges (no figures given in abstract).

result.other_findings: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: New physical health clinic with telephone invitations, height, weight, BP and pulse checks, blood forms, GP letters requesting ECG, and school visits for patients unable to attend

cycle2.result: Overall improvement in adherence to monitoring guidelines, particularly for patients on antipsychotics (figures not given)

result.other_findings: Challenging behaviour prevented some BP, blood tests and ECGs, and it was unclear how to obtain an ECG in CAMHS; parent feedback was positive.

result.setting: Assertive Outreach Team, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust guidance: patients on high dose antipsychotic treatment (HDAT) should have a HDAT monitoring form plus physical health assessment

cycle1.result: Four patients on HDAT (117-150% of maximum BNF dose); only one had a HDAT form and it was out of date; 39/52 (75%) had a physical health assessment in the past 12 months

result.other_findings: Two of the 13 without a physical health assessment were on HDAT; barriers were poor team awareness of HDAT, no reliable reminder system and insufficient equipment.

result.topic: CAMHS to adult mental health transition planning
result.setting: Hounslow Adolescent Team, Central North West London NHS Trust
result.standard: Transition CQUIN: young people should have a transition plan 6 months before they turn 18

cycle1.result: Transition discussed in 11/25 (44%) aged 17.5-18; referrals completed in 7 (28%); 35 open cases were over 18, at least 16 needing closure

result.intervention: Transition discussions made a regular team meeting agenda item and care co-ordinators reminded to explore transition plans

cycle2.result: 100% of cases over 18 closed; transition discussed in the remaining 56%

result.other_findings: 14 of the over-18 cases had an unclear plan at baseline.

result.topic: Physical health checks on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Park House inpatient unit, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local expectation that initial physical examination, admission bloods and ECG are completed and recorded on the PHIT electronic tool

cycle1.result: IPE 73%, admission bloods 84%, ECG 74%; recorded on PHIT in 33-42%; valid refusal reason documented in 63-91%

result.intervention: Interventions to increase completion and documentation, with regular monitoring of PHIT completion (details not reported)
result.other_findings: Re-audit under way at time of writing.

result.setting: Inpatients over 65, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust IMRT policy: verbal de-escalation and oral medication before IM rapid tranquillisation, prescription location and post-IMRT physical monitoring

cycle1.result: 83 RT events in 20 patients; de-escalation attempted 34%; oral medication offered first 59%; physical monitoring fully completed 23%

result.intervention: IMRT treatment algorithm for over-65s, staff teaching package, IMRT prescription area on medicine cards and post-IMRT physical monitoring forms

cycle2.result: 34 RT events in 17 patients; de-escalation 62%; oral medication offered first 71%; physical monitoring fully completed 50%

result.other_findings: IMRT events fell by 49%; 119 inpatient records were reviewed in 2019.

result.setting: Acute mixed inpatient psychiatry unit, south Manchester, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local GMMH medication chart policy standards, plus capacity assessment and consent to treatment forms

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment form 22 (71%); consent to treatment form 16 (52%); route recorded in 40% of depot prescriptions; regular medications date of administration 84%, signature 29%; allergy reaction recorded in 6/21 (29%)

result.other_findings: PRN administration details were 100% complete; patient identifiers were not maintained beyond page 1. Re-audit planned in 3-6 months.

result.setting: Ardenleigh blended women's secure unit, Birmingham
result.standard: Locally set standard: pregnancy testing within one month of admission (target 100%)

cycle1.result: Only 54% of women with unknown pregnancy status screened within one month of admission; 43% in under-25s and 0% in those aged 36-45

result.intervention: Planned: add pregnancy testing to the admission checklist
result.other_findings: Unscreened women were mostly admitted from other hospitals or medium secure units, and 2 admitted from prison were not tested; 92% of tests were urine hCG and none were positive. Re-audit recommended 6 months after checklist introduction.

result.topic: Depression pathway compliance in children and young people
result.setting: 26 community children and young people's teams, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust depression pathway derived from NICE QS48, CG28 and NG134 (comprehensive assessment, parent/carer mental health assessment, psychological therapy first line in mild depression)

cycle1.result: ICD-10 diagnosis recorded in 19%; RCADS symptom tracking under 40%; identification or referral to other pathways for mild depression in 16-18 age group 0%; 29% of teams did not respond

result.intervention: Action plan following the initial audit (details not reported)

cycle2.result: Over 90% compliance for comorbidity, social and educational context; 100% offered psychological interventions; ICD-10 diagnosis 30%; RCADS tracking over 50%; identification and referral for mild depression in 16-18s 82% and 100%; only 1/26 teams (4%) did not respond

result.other_findings: Weekly monitoring of medication side effects in the first 4 weeks (43%) and referral of parents/carers to mental health services (40%) remained poor.

result.topic: Pregnancy and contraception assessment on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Mixed-sex acute adult inpatient psychiatry ward, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists and local guidelines: all female inpatients asked about sexual health within seven days of admission

cycle1.result: 57% asked about contraception; possibility of pregnancy explored in less than half

result.intervention: Planned: discussion at clinical governance meeting for recommendations
result.other_findings: Minimal variation by age group (18-26, 27-35, 36-45). Re-audit planned.

result.setting: Addictions service, Plummer Court, Newcastle upon Tyne
result.standard: NICE: all patients completing alcohol detoxification should be considered for acamprosate or oral naltrexone

cycle1.result: Anti-craving medication considered in 47%; acamprosate offered in all but one case; accepted in all but one case where offered

result.intervention: Monthly follow-up with addictions services for six months, template letter to GPs requesting acamprosate prescription, audit presented to medical team and treatment pathway amended to specify medical role at initial appointment
result.other_findings: Follow-up of prescriptions was unclear and several GPs declined to prescribe acamprosate citing an outdated local policy. Re-audit planned in six months.

result.topic: Physical health checks on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Mill Lodge Tier 4 CAMHS inpatient unit, York
result.standard: Tier 4 CAMHS service specification standard 2.6.3: initial assessment including physical examination within 24 hours of admission (target 100%)

cycle1.result: Among patients who did not refuse, within 24 hours: physical examination 85%, bloods 82%, ECG 84%; during admission bloods and ECG 100%, physical examination 90%

result.other_findings: No reason documented for missing procedures in several patients (3 examinations, 2 bloods, 3 ECGs); one blood test delayed by lack of tubes. Re-audit planned in twelve months.

result.setting: Child and Family Clinic, tier 3 outpatient CAMHS, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
result.standard: Belfast Trust CAMHS Antipsychotic Medication Monitoring Schedule (2015), based on CAMESA, NICE CG185, CG155 and Maudsley guidelines

cycle1.result: Baseline bloods (or declined) 92%; baseline ECG (or declined) 75%; complete monitoring bloods 33%; physical health parameters complete 42%; monitoring schedule present and current 42% (0% on PARIS)

result.intervention: Standardised recording of monitoring using PARIS clinic letters and the schedule at the front of clinical notes; baseline ECG made mandatory

cycle2.result: Baseline bloods (or declined) 89%; baseline ECG (or declined) 67%; complete monitoring bloods 44%; parameters complete 56%; schedule present and current 38%, present but not current 50% (0% on PARIS)

result.other_findings: Small re-audit numbers limit interpretation; further recommendations are an initiation checklist, central bloods diary and a co-produced care-pathway booklet.

result.setting: ECT clinic, Bolton Directorate, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: WHO surgical safety checklist modified for ECT including NPSA advice, per ECT accreditation service standards (target 100% completion)

cycle1.result: 19/20 (95%) completed; 5/20 (25%) not signed; 75% complete and valid; checklists present in all case notes

result.other_findings: A repeat audit was recommended.

result.topic: Appropriateness of referrals to community mental health team
result.setting: Oxford City and NE Oxon Adult Mental Health Team

cycle1.result: 21% of referrals inappropriate

result.intervention: Team remodelled in January 2020 into separate assessment and treatment functions

cycle2.result: 19.5% (546/2803) of referrals inappropriate; 14.7% (97/658) pre-COVID-19 vs 20.9% (449/2145) during the pandemic; 32.9% returned to GP after a single assessment

result.other_findings: Students made up 26% of referrals, with more ADHD (17.7% vs 3%) and neurodevelopmental referrals than non-students. Automated logging of referral outcomes is planned.

result.setting: Community forensic supported accommodation, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust medicines reconciliation guidance: 100% concordance between mental health and general practice records for medication and allergies

cycle1.result: Allergy status discrepancy in 2 patients (25%); medication discrepancy in 2 patients (25%), both vitamin D omitted from mental health records

result.other_findings: Allergies were documented in ward discharge summaries but not in GP records; primary care asked to update. Re-audits every four months planned.

result.topic: Eating disorder referrals from primary care
result.setting: Manchester Foundation Trust Community Eating Disorders Service, Greater Manchester
result.standard: NICE: children and young people with suspected eating disorders referred immediately and directly to specialist services at first presentation

cycle1.result: 35% of referrals made correctly; 43.5% not initially made to MFT-CEDS; 58% made immediately; North and South Manchester 10% and 8% correct

result.intervention: Recommended: information document and video, GP referral template and interviews with GPs
result.other_findings: Most of the 10 GP survey respondents did not know the referral guidelines or feel confident identifying eating disorders. Re-audit planned after 6 months.

result.topic: Psychosocial assessment after self-harm in children
result.setting: Service for Adolescents and Families in Enfield, for paediatric inpatients at North Middlesex and Barnet hospitals, London
result.standard: NICE self-harm quality standard QS34: comprehensive psychosocial assessment, assessment within 24 hours if high risk, collaborative risk management plan and follow-up

cycle1.result: 100% had comprehensive psychosocial assessment; 93% seen within 24 hours of referral; 97% documented risk assessment; 92% had 7-day follow-up review

result.intervention: Assessment protocol and safety plan, daily liaison with hospitals, paediatric nurses trained in the Time to Talk programme and a full-time crisis liaison nurse employed
result.other_findings: Hospital referrals rose 141% from 2014/15 to 2018/19; 74% of presentations were girls and 87% involved self-harm, suicidal ideation or attempt. Re-audit planned.

result.setting: Mental Health Liaison Team, general hospital, Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Project target: handover time under 30 minutes within one month, with improved handover quality

cycle1.result: Average handover 44 minutes; 7 interruptions; key information available 69%; staff member allocated 80%; review date allocated 83%
