cycle1.result: Checklist process compliance 85.0%; checklist quality pass rate 40.0%; item completion 91.9%; site marking accuracy 73.1%; preparation-area verification 89.6%; theatre entry verification 91.2%.

result.intervention: Standardised site marking with mandatory original-imaging review, revised challenge-response laterality checklist items, three-stage closed-loop digital verification workflow and HIS/EMR/PACS integration with forced constraints.

cycle2.result: Checklist process compliance 100.0%; quality pass rate 90.0%; item completion 99.0%; site marking accuracy 97.7%; preparation-area verification 95.0%; theatre entry verification 98.0%.

result.other_findings: Triggered by a near-miss wrong-side event; over six months the digital system logged 9,847 verifications with 99.3% imaging review completion and no wrong-laterality near misses.

result.setting: Nine clinical departments, tertiary cardiac care centre, Karachi
result.standard: IPBAI tool of ten domains aligned with WHO IPC core components

cycle1.result: General indicator score 72.5%; standard and transmission-based precautions 20%; environmental cleaning 0%; spill response 20%; antimicrobial stewardship 20%.

result.intervention: Structured multimodal IPC training module delivered in two cycles to 607 healthcare workers.

cycle2.result: General indicator score 94%; all ten domains 100%.

result.other_findings: Training reached 391 staff in the first cycle and 216 in the second.

result.setting: Three primary care paediatric practices

cycle1.result: Overweight/obesity 26.3%.

result.intervention: Revised weaning and feeding protocol up to 36 months, mainly reducing excess protein and sugar.
result.other_findings: Outcome (overweight frequency) rather than compliance with a named standard was measured.

result.setting: Children's inpatient unit, University Hospital Limerick, regional paediatric centre
result.standard: Full compliance with comprehensive biopsychosocial history documentation for all medical admissions

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Teaching interventions and educational sessions, with a survey of non-consultant hospital doctors.

cycle2.result: Compliance 82.5% at second re-audit, down from 95% at first re-audit.

result.other_findings: First re-audit showed a net 53% increase in some social history documentation; improvement over baseline was sustained.

result.setting: Residential care home (electronic nursing records)
result.standard: N-Catch II audit instrument; standard is complete documentation (score 3 of 3)

cycle1.result: No records met the standard; mean scores from 0.4 (aims for nursing care) to 1.1 (nursing diagnoses).

result.intervention: Tailored multifaceted implementation strategy addressing local barriers.
result.other_findings: Further audit cycles were considered needed before standards are met.

result.setting: Emergency laparotomy patients, Royal Oldham Hospital
result.standard: NICE guidelines on nutritional assessment; accurate MUST scoring

cycle1.result: MUST accurate in 27 (54%); 23 (46%) inaccurate.

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary approach and a standard online MUST calculator.
result.other_findings: Accuracy was judged by senior medical rescoring of nursing MUST scores.

result.setting: UK registered internet pharmacies
result.standard: British Association of Sexual Health and HIV (BASHH) guidelines

cycle1.result: Gonorrhoea: 3 of 5 (60%) sold BASHH-approved antibiotics; chlamydia first-line options 22 of 25 (88%); herpes simplex 13 of 22 (59%); trichomonas 4 in line with BASHH.

result.intervention: Results fed back to each provider.

cycle2.result: Improvement in standards (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Advice before, during and after treatment remained variable; no website assessed for proctitis.

result.setting: Specialist mental health rehabilitation service inpatient units, North-West of England
result.standard: Current guidelines for employment of assistant psychologists

cycle1.result: All standards unmet.

result.other_findings: Only some assistant psychologists received the stipulated support and worked within their pay band; re-audit suggested after new guidance.

result.setting: Psychiatric hospital ECT service

cycle1.result: ECT prescription completed by consultant in 100%; administering doctor's signature missing in 40%.

cycle2.result: ECT prescription completed in 100%; administering doctor's signature missing in 21%.

result.other_findings: Practice generally adhered to ECTAS standards; bilateral ECT used in all cases.

result.setting: ENT and multidisciplinary 'Dizzy Clinic'

cycle1.result: 40% of patients referred with dizziness did not require a face-to-face appointment.

result.intervention: Telephone triage to a rapid access BPPV clinic or a multidisciplinary complex balance clinic with audiologists, physiotherapists and ENT surgeons.

cycle2.result: Only 35.8% streamed to face-to-face appointment; 90% of face-to-face appointments by non-ENT surgeons; 60% discharged after first assessment (61% previously).

result.other_findings: Examinations were more thorough in the new clinic.

result.setting: Otolaryngology outpatient department
result.standard: Hospital OPD guidelines enacted by the Pakistan Otolaryngology Association

cycle1.result: 52.5% of patients with ear discharge required referral to ENT theatre/emergency for suctioning.

result.intervention: Changes in practice and simple protocols to allow ear suction in the outpatient clinic.

cycle2.result: Referrals to ENT theatre fell to 9.5%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Tertiary dermatology outpatient department
result.standard: British Association of Dermatologists guidelines for biologic therapy

cycle1.result: Baseline disease severity scores documented in 68%; full viral screen 87%; vaccination status 80%.

result.intervention: Screening and monitoring checklists created and being implemented.
result.other_findings: Family planning discussions were a weakness; re-audit planned in six months.

result.setting: Pulmonary Rehabilitation Unit, Local Health Authority of Reggio Emilia

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Title only (no abstract): states that an audit-intervention-reaudit cycle can improve diagnostic standards for COPD.

result.topic: Prescription quality and WHO prescribing indicators
result.setting: Outpatient departments of Jhalawar Medical College and Hospital and Chintpurni Medical College and Hospital
result.standard: WHO Guide to Good Prescribing, WHO drug core indicators and the updated WHO Essential Medicines list

cycle1.result: Baseline prescription audit on the last date of the first month of each cycle (n=250 prescriptions per month); figures not reported in the abstract.

result.intervention: Monthly continuous evaluation with active feedback on conformity to WHO prescribing guidance.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in completeness and rationality of prescription formats at the end of the 2nd and 3rd months of each cycle; WHO drug core indicators improved with every re-audit in each cycle (p value truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Four 3-month cycles over two years, each followed by three months without audit; stopping the audits began to reverse the improvement in prescribing behaviour.

result.topic: HIV testing in patients with tuberculosis
result.setting: The James Cook University Hospital, clinic and community TB service
result.standard: BHIVA/BASHH/BIS 2008 and HPA 2009 guidance: HIV testing should be offered to all patients with active TB

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Introduction of nurse-led HIV testing following the initial audit.

cycle2.result: Patients with confirmed active TB were offered HIV testing in 90.3% of cases.

result.other_findings: Nurse-led testing improved uptake in both clinic and community settings; baseline figures not given in the abstract.

result.setting: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Correspondence (no abstract) about a two-cycle audit of SIGN 117 in 169 adult and paediatric tonsillectomy patients.

result.topic: Neighbourhood systematic social observation tool reliability
result.setting: 1,306 street segments in 149 neighbourhoods of Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Re-audit of 149 segments for inter-rater reliability: mean Fleiss kappa 0.57 (SD 0.24); 53% substantial or almost perfect agreement, 20.4% moderate agreement.

result.other_findings: Instrument reliability study for public health research, not a clinical audit; instrument best for characteristics that are not time-dependent.

result.setting: Adult medical and surgical inpatients, Whangarei Hospital, Northland District Health Board
result.standard: Local inpatient hypoglycaemia protocol (oral treatment 9-15 g glucose; repeat capillary glucose at 10-15 minutes)

cycle1.result: 117 hypoglycaemic episodes in 32 patients; initial glucose treatment in 46 (40.4%); repeat capillary glucose at 10-15 minutes in 35 (30.7%); only 36.7% of episodes corrected within 30 minutes.

result.other_findings: 40% of episodes lasted more than one hour and 72% of patients had more than one episode; recommended protocol review, nurse education and regular re-audit.

result.setting: Australasian Gastrointestinal Trials Group ARCTIC study; St John of God and Royal Perth Hospital

cycle1.result: No patients had further cardiac toxicity after switching to raltitrexed.

result.other_findings: Retrospective outcome study; four patients who continued the same fluoropyrimidine with nitrates and calcium antagonists had further cardiac events.

result.setting: Neonatal unit, The Royal Children's Hospital, Melbourne (tertiary paediatric hospital)

cycle1.result: Audit identified suboptimal immunisation status of preterm infants; figures not reported in the abstract.

result.intervention: Preterm infant immunisation reminder sticker and feedback of the original audit findings to hospital staff.

cycle2.result: Follow-up audit using the Australian Childhood Immunisation Register (n = 57, median age 2.5 years); immunisation results truncated in the abstract, which concludes vaccine delivery improved.

result.other_findings: 44% (25/57) had a history of chronic lung disease.

result.setting: Inpatients at a London teaching hospital
result.standard: Waterlow pressure ulcer risk assessment scale

cycle1.result: Nursing Waterlow score recorded for 81% of patients; nursing scores were lower than study scores.

result.intervention: Staff questionnaires, educational sessions, presentations and posters on risk stratification.

cycle2.result: Nursing Waterlow score recorded for 100% of patients (p value truncated in abstract); differences between nursing and study scores reduced.

result.other_findings: Cycle 1 under-scoring was mainly from failing to assess certain Waterlow categories; greater multidisciplinary input was still needed.

result.topic: Discharge summary communication to primary care
result.setting: Deployed military Role 3 hospital to Role 1 facilities, Op HERRICK 18

cycle1.result: 1/40 (2.5%) discharge summaries arrived from Role 3 to Role 1.

result.intervention: Implementation of a system to transfer discharge information from Role 3 to Role 1.

cycle2.dates: 1 month after the system was implemented

result.other_findings: Recommended a single electronic patient record across Defence Medical Services and regular audits in future operations.

result.setting: Radiotherapy centres in Belgium, organised by the Federal College of Radiotherapy
result.standard: IAEA manual for comprehensive clinical radiotherapy audits; Euratom 97/43 directive article 11

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes how the national audit programme was organised (peer-review visits by a radiation oncologist, physicist and therapist); no results in the abstract.

result.setting: Inpatients, Canterbury District Health Board, Christchurch

cycle1.result: Oxygen prescribed in 24.5%.

cycle2.result: Oxygen prescription rate 13.9% four years on, a significant deterioration from 58.8% at the second audit (P = 0.01).

result.other_findings: Second audit (102 inpatients, September 2009 to February 2010) showed improvement from 24.5% to 58.8% (P = 0.01), which was not sustained.

result.topic: Perineal wound infection after vaginal birth
result.setting: Maternity services of an NHS trust

cycle1.result: Higher than average perineal wound infection rate among women with an instrumental birth.

result.intervention: Delivery packs separated into a birth pack and a suturing pack, plus a back-to-basics update session for maternity staff.

cycle2.result: Overall perineal wound infection rate in the trust reduced.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: DNA contamination prevention in forensic medical examinations
result.setting: Forensic and Medical Sexual Assault Care, Canberra Hospital and Health Services
result.standard: 24 JBI audit criteria based on inquiry recommendations to minimise DNA contamination

cycle1.result: 20 of 24 criteria had 100% compliance; the remaining 4 had compliance between 65% and 90%.

result.intervention: Education and awareness training targeted at clinicians.

cycle2.result: Compliance improved in 2 of the 4 non-compliant criteria; the other 2 were unchanged.

result.other_findings: External factors outside clinicians' control influenced compliance.

result.topic: Patient information on ethanol content of anaesthetic sprays
result.setting: Gastroscopy services

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Title only (no abstract): a re-audit of patient information about ethanol in anaesthetic throat sprays used for gastroscopy.

result.topic: Metabolic screening in pregnancy in primary care
result.setting: 76 community-controlled or government-operated primary health care centres serving mainly Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities in five states and territories
result.standard: Recommended pregnancy care: screening and follow-up for BMI, blood pressure and diabetes in pregnancy

cycle1.result: Diabetes screening at baseline (before the first CQI cycle) 56.1%.

result.intervention: Up to four continuous quality improvement cycles supported by the Audit and Best Practice for Chronic Disease Research Partnership.
result.other_findings: Diabetes screening was 63.7% after cycle 1, 61.6% after cycle 2 and 63.7% after cycle 3; screening was associated with higher self-ratings of organisational systems (P = 0.03), self-management support (P = 0.04) and organisational integration (P = 0.01). 2592 audited records in total.

result.topic: Paediatric physiotherapy service quality for Indigenous children
result.setting: Community-based paediatric allied health (physiotherapy) service in Northern Australia
result.standard: Audit and Best Practice for Chronic Disease CQI audit tool

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: CQI workshop in which clinicians assessed their systems and set goals and strategies for improvement.

cycle2.result: Second audit and workshop reported improvements in clinical and organisational aspects of the service; figures not reported.

result.other_findings: Case study comparing CQI results with 12 client and carer interviews: CQI reported better communication and client input than interviews did; lack of resources and child-friendly environment were weaknesses.

result.setting: Elective ENT surgery at an NHS trust
result.standard: NICE 2003 guidelines on preoperative testing for elective surgery

cycle1.result: 69.2% of blood tests unnecessary (FBC 44.9%, U&Es 63.5%, clotting 99.2%), costing £1955.77 (annual estimate £7,823.08); no results changed management.

result.intervention: Staff training programme and targeted written information for clinics.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Four regional central hospitals in the Tampere University Hospital tertiary care area
result.standard: Modified European Union of Medical Specialists 1997 protocol

cycle1.result: Key areas performing poorly were identified for follow-up; figures not reported.

result.intervention: Follow-up of poorly performing key areas; increase in paediatric specialist resources.

cycle2.result: Most key follow-up issues had improved, but educational objectives needed clarifying and following up, and trainees needed more outpatient time.

result.other_findings: An intermediate audit in 2008 also showed improvement in most key follow-up issues.

result.topic: Blood culture collection practice and contamination
result.setting: A district hospital in Cape Town
result.standard: 2010 South African guideline for blood cultures (22 standards); contamination benchmark 3%

cycle1.result: Contamination 4.5%; 33% of bottles had the recommended 8-10 mL fill; 96.9% of patients had a single culture in 24 hours; 7.8% had a combined volume of at least 20 mL; median needle-to-incubator time 11 hours 25 minutes.

result.other_findings: 12.5% of cultures grew organisms; pathogen yield after antibiotic exposure 4.9% vs 7.5% without (p=0.3). A re-audit was recommended.

result.topic: Early psychosis intervention best practice documentation
result.setting: 12 Early Psychosis Intervention programme sites in rural Northeastern Ontario
result.standard: 12 EPI best practices specified in the Carepath

cycle1.result: Pre-Carepath chart audit of 110 client files; figures not reported.

result.intervention: Implementation of an early psychosis intervention Carepath outlining best practice care pathways.

cycle2.result: Significantly higher frequencies for 2 of 12 best practices (assessing impact on family and assessing substance use); standardisation of documentation did not improve significantly.

result.other_findings: Barriers included staff resistance, resources and agency documentation parameters.

result.topic: ADHD management in children and adolescents
result.setting: Central and peripheral clinics, Division of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, Red Cross War Memorial Children's Hospital, Cape Town
result.standard: 17 audit standards from NICE ADHD guidelines; good compliance ≥80%, fair 50-79%

cycle1.result: Compliance low, with only four of 17 standards rated good; physical monitoring especially poor.

result.other_findings: The central clinic group received more treatment options and safer monitoring; an audit checklist was produced for future cycles.

result.topic: Postoperative instructions after root canal treatment
result.setting: Dublin Dental University Hospital
result.standard: Proposed benchmarks for delivery of postoperative advice (six categories)

cycle1.result: 56% of charts documented that postoperative advice was given; patient questionnaire showed key messages were not consistently given.

result.intervention: Introduction of a written postoperative advice sheet.

cycle2.result: Benchmarks met in four of six categories.

result.other_findings: Combined oral and written advice was the most effective way to deliver information.

result.setting: Geriatric unit, St Vincent's Hospital, Sydney

cycle1.result: Vitamin D measured in 57.4%.

result.intervention: Education and a bone health mnemonic introduced into discharge summaries.

cycle2.result: Vitamin D measured in 86.6% (P value truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Outcomes also included bone protection medication and communication to GPs; the abstract reports significant improvement but figures are truncated.

result.setting: General surgery ward, Zhongshan Hospital, Shanghai
result.standard: Nine JBI evidence-based audit criteria for implantable port maintenance

cycle1.result: Criteria 2 and 3 0%, criterion 1 80%, criterion 4 92%, criterion 5 68%, criterion 6 100%, criterion 7 12%, criterion 8 0%, criterion 9 88% (25 nurses and 25 patients).

result.intervention: Education, demonstration, clinical practice and assessment (16 May to 15 July 2015).
result.other_findings: Four barriers were identified during implementation and addressed.

result.setting: Coronary care unit, Zhongshan Hospital, Shanghai (tertiary hospital)
result.standard: Five JBI best practice criteria for heart failure discharge planning

cycle1.result: Discharge checklist 0%, comprehensive discharge education 7%, telephone follow-up 0%, structured education 93%, outpatient visit scheduled 93%.

result.intervention: Local discharge planning checklist, nurse training and development of resources.

cycle2.result: Discharge checklist 100%, comprehensive discharge education 100%, telephone follow-up 76%, structured education 100%, outpatient visit scheduled 100%.

result.other_findings: Further audit cycles planned to assess patient outcomes.

result.setting: A medical center (Far Eastern Memorial Hospital affiliation), New Taipei

cycle1.result: Overall caesarean section rate 34.5%; rate for dystocia 9.6%.

result.intervention: Clinical audit of all caesarean section cases from August 2009.

cycle2.result: Overall caesarean section rate 31.1% (adjusted OR 0.83, p = 0.008); rate for dystocia 6.2%.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend strict monitoring of dystocia indications for caesarean section.

result.topic: Antenatal corticosteroids before elective caesarean section under 39 weeks
result.setting: A hospital in Hywel Dda University Health Board
result.standard: Antenatal corticosteroids for elective caesarean section before 39+0 weeks; target 100%

cycle1.result: 66.6% of patients were given antenatal corticosteroids.

result.intervention: Findings discussed at consultant meetings and labour forum and emailed to all department staff.
result.other_findings: Re-audit planned in one year.

result.setting: Oral and maxillofacial surgery, Department of Dentistry, JIPMER, Pondicherry (public sector hospital)
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines on operation notes, plus OMFS-specific criteria

cycle1.result: Mean data point inclusion 84.6%; 94-100% documentation for 9 essential criteria; assistant name and date of surgery poorly documented; OMFS-specific criteria scored poorly.

result.intervention: OMFS-specific consent forms, diagram sheets and a computerised operation note proforma with a prefilled operative findings template.

cycle2.result: Mean data point inclusion 98.4% (P 0.001); excellent documentation in almost all essential and additional criteria.

result.other_findings: Cycle 1 consent forms often contained abbreviations and missing details.

result.topic: Electronic perioperative workflow and synoptic operation notes
result.setting: Christchurch Hospital, Canterbury District Health Board (tertiary centre), hospital-wide

cycle1.result: 5785 of 7179 (80%) general surgical operations had an operation note created in the new system; theatre-booking compliance approached 90% (44,953 bookings); synoptic reporting uptake for laparoscopic cholecystectomy 81%.

result.intervention: Hospital-wide integrated electronic workflow system introduced in 2013 managing the perioperative journey and facilitating audit.
result.other_findings: Synoptic notes documented antibiotic use and safe cholecystectomy steps better (P value truncated).

result.setting: Restorative dentistry department, Morriston Hospital, Swansea, and an endodontic MSc course

cycle1.result: 50 departmental and 10 student record sets; most often missing were consent, anaesthetic details, rubber dam method, working length reference point, irrigation details and obturation technique.

result.intervention: Presentation of results with an educational session; departmental guidelines, consent leaflets and endodontic record keeping forms.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in 24 of 29 areas in the departmental audit and 14 of 29 in the MSc audit (P = 0.05); some areas reached 100% when forms were used.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Second-trimester fetal anomaly scan image quality
result.setting: Sonographers in the southwest region prenatal screening programme
result.standard: Standardised image-scoring method: 25 fetal anatomical structures and six biometric measures per logbook

cycle1.result: 73 of 85 sonographers (86%) met the criteria in the primary audit (425 logbooks).

result.intervention: Individual hands-on training for the 12 sonographers who did not meet criteria.

cycle2.result: 11 sonographers passed the re-audit; one ceased her contract.

result.other_findings: 2.1% of required images were not digitally stored and could not be reviewed.

result.topic: Decision-to-delivery interval for emergency caesarean section
result.setting: Nizwa Hospital, Nizwa
result.standard: Decision-to-delivery interval ≤30 minutes for emergency caesarean section

cycle1.dates: three months, between April 2011 and June 2013 (initial retrospective cycle)
cycle1.result: DDI ≤30 minutes in 23.8% of 84 cases.

result.intervention: Improvement strategies addressing factors causing DDI delays.

cycle2.dates: three months, between April 2011 and June 2013 (third cycle)
cycle2.result: DDI ≤30 minutes in 60.8% of 79 women (P value truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Second cycle achieved 44.6% of 83 cases; DDI over 60 minutes was associated with more SCBU admissions and low Apgar scores.

result.setting: Outpatient chemotherapy, Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai (tertiary cancer centre)

cycle1.result: Guideline-adherent prescriptions were associated with less vomiting (6.6% v 21.9%); baseline adherence rate truncated in abstract.

result.intervention: Clinician education, revised mandatory antiemetic prescription policies and a double-check system.

cycle2.result: Re-audit showed improved guideline adherence; figures truncated in abstract.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Fluid resuscitation in shocked ICU patients
result.setting: ICU, Rotorua Hospital
result.standard: International best practice recommendations on fluid resuscitation and de-escalation from literature review

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: A more measured local approach to fluid resuscitation.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in adherence to best practice guidelines; figures not reported.

result.other_findings: Improvement was associated with better patient outcomes.

result.topic: Breast MRI indications and wait times
result.setting: Academic centre, Université de Montréal, Montreal
result.standard: Evidence-based list of breast MRI indications set at a multidisciplinary meeting (May 2014)

cycle1.result: Surveillance after prior breast cancer 21% (24/113), preoperative staging 18% (20/113), high-risk screening 12% (13/113); 457 pending requests exceeded the recommended delay and 230 were within it.

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary meeting establishing evidence-based indications and prioritisation of requests.

cycle2.result: Prior breast cancer 7% (10/143), preoperative staging 11% (16/143), high-risk screening 46% (66/143); wait times improved for all indications.

result.other_findings: September 2014 re-audit: prior breast cancer 23% (33/141), preoperative staging 9% (13/141), high-risk screening 36% (51/141).

result.topic: COPD diagnosis and management in lung cancer patients
result.setting: Lung Diagnostic Assessment Program, Queen's University Hospitals, Kingston, Ontario

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: DMAIC cycles: cycle 1 engaged stakeholders and prioritised COPD management by respirologists; cycle 2 restructured physicians and introduced a standard work protocol.

cycle2.result: No change in PFT completion over time; abstract reports significantly improved COPD management, figures truncated.

result.other_findings: Respirology-managed patients were more likely to have PFTs (56.7% v 96.1%); 166 patients in cycle 1; a 2014 audit had shown underdiagnosis and undertreatment.

result.topic: ECG monitoring for patients on antipsychotics
result.setting: Psychiatric inpatients, Kowloon Hospital
result.standard: Guidelines for ECG monitoring in inpatients prescribed antipsychotics (ECG before antipsychotic)

cycle1.result: Overall ECG compliance 40.2%.

result.intervention: Quality improvement interventions delivered after baseline audit (not detailed in abstract).

cycle2.result: Overall ECG compliance 69.9% (p value truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Junior doctors (residents) adhered better than more senior doctors.

result.setting: Urban and rural road segments around PIN3 study participants' residences

cycle1.result: Same-day reliability: 81% of items had kappa ≥0.4; two-week reliability 77%.

cycle2.result: One-year stability: 68% of items had moderate to outstanding agreement.

result.other_findings: Instrument reliability study, not a clinical audit; only 8% of items differed significantly by urbanicity.

result.setting: PICU and cardiovascular ICU, quaternary care children's hospital (Baylor College of Medicine, Houston)
result.standard: Protein goals met in the first 5 days of continuous renal replacement therapy

cycle1.result: Group 1: protein goals met 22% of time by day 5 and 35% throughout (cohort n = 55 across groups).

result.intervention: PDSA cycles: interdisciplinary QI group with thrice weekly bedside rounds and protein prescriptions in nephrology notes; education of intensivists; monthly QI meetings reviewing nutrition goals.

cycle2.result: Group 3: protein goals met 71% of time by day 5 and 75% throughout; significant improvement after PDSA 3 (p value truncated).

result.other_findings: Group 2 met goals 33% by day 5 and 39% throughout; 31% of the cohort were malnourished at baseline.

result.setting: General practices in Northland District Health Board region
result.standard: National guidelines for management of GAS pharyngitis

cycle1.result: Audit suggested adherence to national guidelines needed improvement.

cycle2.result: Throat swabs more than doubled and amoxicillin more commonly prescribed, but the proportion not receiving recommended antibiotics, or given inadequate length or no prescription, had not reduced.

result.other_findings: Significant differences in management between Māori and non-Māori patients; management remains substandard.

result.topic: Extrapyramidal side effect monitoring on antipsychotics
result.setting: Outpatient clinic, Community Mental Health Centre, South Tipperary Mental Health Services, Clonmel
result.standard: Clinical guidelines recommending regular monitoring of extrapyramidal side effects

cycle1.result: EPSE documented in 14% of records.

result.other_findings: Assessment improved most among non-consultant hospital doctors.

result.setting: Two postoperative abdominal surgery wards, ZhongShan Hospital of Fudan University, Shanghai
result.standard: JBI evidence-based audit criteria for VTE prevention

cycle1.result: Four audit criteria had compliance under 30% (21 nurses and 30 patients).

result.intervention: VTE education including a VTE video, clinical practice and prophylaxis measures.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Criteria-based audit of obstructed labour and fetal distress
result.setting: Muhimbili National Hospital, Dar es Salaam (tertiary referral hospital)
result.standard: Criteria-based audit checklist for obstructed labour and fetal distress

cycle1.result: Perinatal morbidity and mortality with obstructed labour 42/260 (16.2%); fetal distress baseline n=248.

cycle2.result: Perinatal morbidity and mortality with obstructed labour 22/250 (8.8%) (P=0.012); fetal distress re-audit n=251.

result.other_findings: Using Robson classification in 27,960 parturients, caesarean rate for preterm pregnancies increased (referred OR 1.28; non-referred OR 2.78) and neonatal distress decreased in several groups.

result.setting: Two NICUs at two hospitals in the Gaza Strip
result.standard: Local infection control guidelines for NICU entry and minor and major procedure bundles

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Authorisation and dissemination of infection control guidelines, feedback, and on-site education and training sessions.

cycle2.result: Statistically significant improvement in adherence, including minor and major procedure protocols; figures not reported.

result.other_findings: No significant change in general neonatal handling adherence.

result.topic: Salvage chemotherapy for relapsed aggressive NHL
result.setting: 9 Polish Lymphoma Research Group centres

cycle1.result: Overall response rate 68% (40% CR, 28% PR); grade ≥3 adverse events in 68%.

result.other_findings: Retrospective outcome analysis of the P[R]EBEN regimen; projected 12-month PFS 68% and OS 78%.

result.setting: Acute adult psychiatry unit, Nepean Hospital, Sydney
result.standard: Physical examination within 24 h of admission; quality scored out of 15

cycle1.result: Physical examination in 36/71 (50.7%); mean quality score 7.5/15.

result.intervention: Four brief peer-led feedback sessions and email correspondence to clinicians.

cycle2.result: Physical examination in 41/64 (64.1%); mean quality score 9.3/15.

result.other_findings: Greatest gains in documentation of additional cardiac sounds (33.9% increase), additional breath sounds (17.7%), breath sounds (17.1%), cardiac sounds (14.2%) and bowel sounds (12.5%).

result.topic: Caesarean section rate by Robson classification
result.setting: Obstetrics and Gynaecology Department, Pak Emirates Military Hospital, Rawalpindi (tertiary care hospital)

cycle1.result: CS rate 54% (n=3878); Group 5 contributed 27.42% (n=1976), Group 12 12.07% (n=870), Group 2 7.34% (n=531).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Endoscopy tertiary centre, Zhongshan Hospital of Fudan University, Shanghai
result.standard: Eight JBI best practice criteria for discharge of sedated patients after endoscopy

cycle1.result: Discharge policy, minimum discharge criteria established and met each 0%; written and verbal instructions 12%; discharge care plan documented 0%.

result.intervention: Multiple stakeholder-chosen strategies including a formal organisational discharge policy.

cycle2.result: Discharge policy, criteria established and met each 100%; written and verbal instructions 100%; discharge care plan documented 88%.

result.other_findings: Authorisation by appropriate staff, staff training and accompaniment by a responsible adult changed least as baseline compliance was already high.

result.setting: All 25 Belgian radiotherapy departments

cycle1.result: 381 recommendations: 34% process optimisation, 27% infrastructure, 19% organisation, 20% staff issues.

result.other_findings: 54% of departments rated recommendations very useful; 42.7% of recommendations very relevant and 23.5% had important impact. A second cycle has started with B-QUATRO.

result.setting: Elective general surgery, Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences, Islamabad
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons (England) guidelines 2014 (20-parameter checklist)

cycle1.result: Only 2 of 20 parameters (surgeon's name and procedure) always completed; the other 18 ranged from 0% to 98.3%.

result.setting: Old age liaison psychiatry covering 3 hospitals in Glasgow City

result.other_findings: Delirium was the commonest referral reason (23%) and diagnosis (34%), suggesting under-recognition; an electronic referral with mandatory fields was pending.

result.standard: Aim to increase GP discharge summaries by 50% over 12 months

cycle2.result: Documentation of these discussions improved (figures not reported); no impact on antipsychotic prescribing rates.

result.topic: COVID-19 physical healthcare in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Inpatient psychiatric wards, Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust, London
result.standard: Documented COVID-19 management plan including risk of serious illness, observation frequency, escalation criteria and VTE assessment

cycle1.result: 58% had a documented COVID-19 management plan; 56% mentioned observation frequency, 19% escalation criteria, 9% risk of serious disease; no repeat VTE assessments.

result.intervention: New protocol 'COVID-19: Early Identification of Risk and Management' with adjusted 4C mortality score, observation schedules, VTE prompt and escalation criteria, piloted at one unit.

cycle2.result: 100% (n = 4) had a robust COVID-19 plan and 100% received a VTE assessment.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring for patients on antipsychotics
result.setting: Community mental health team, rural Welsh setting (Powys Teaching Health Board)
result.standard: 10 standards derived from NICE guidelines (NICE QS80, Quality Standard 6)

cycle1.result: Average compliance across the three previous cycles used as comparator (figures not reported).

cycle2.result: Compliance increased in 2/10 standards and decreased in 8/10 compared with the average of the previous three cycles.

result.setting: CAMHS outpatients, Massereene House, Northern Health and Social Care Trust

cycle1.result: Most rated telephone reviews 'somewhat' better; 80% rated overall help 'a great deal' better; 80% would recommend telephone contact 'a great deal'.

result.other_findings: Patient questionnaire; some still preferred face-to-face reviews and the same doctor did the reviews and the audit.

result.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust recommendations for high-dose antipsychotic therapy (HDAT) monitoring and clozapine consideration

cycle1.result: 21/121 on combination therapy, 11 on HDAT (9%); clozapine considered in 9 of 11 HDAT patients; ECG before HDAT 100% but after dose increase only 36%; baseline prolactin 46%, HbA1c 91%.

result.topic: ADHD medication monitoring in intellectual disability

cycle1.result: Previous cycle results not reported.

result.setting: Consultation-Liaison psychiatric service of a metropolitan hospital, Perth
result.standard: Clinical indicators: referrals seen within 24 hours and 36 hours

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing in upper respiratory tract infection
result.setting: Tubas Governmental Hospital, West Bank
result.standard: International guidelines on antibiotic prescribing for sore throat, tonsillitis and acute otitis media

result.topic: Valproate prescribing in women of childbearing age

result.standard: Local and international guidelines on valproate prescribing in women of childbearing age

cycle2.result: 26 (10%) women prescribed valproate on discharge; significant improvements in pregnancy testing, documentation of contraception status and discussion of teratogenic risk.

result.topic: Age at diagnosis of Turner syndrome
result.setting: 14 care centres across Tunisia (neonatal, paediatric, adult endocrinology and genetics departments)

cycle1.result: Median age at diagnosis 12 years (mean 13 ± 9.2); more than half diagnosed after age 12; 35 (23.5%) after 18 years.

result.topic: Blood gas ordering in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency Department, The Royal Melbourne Hospital
result.standard: Choosing Wisely: avoid unnecessary blood gases

cycle1.result: Approximately 45 blood gases per 100 ED presentations.

result.other_findings: Many blood gases were ordered for patients who were not critically unwell and whose disposition was not affected by the result.

result.topic: Anticipatory prescribing at end of life
result.setting: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Title only; described as a completed audit loop.

result.topic: Management of acute pharyngotonsillitis in children

result.standard: Sudan guidelines for prevention, diagnosis and management of rheumatic heart disease (clinical prediction rule and recommended antibiotics)

cycle1.result: 17 (89.4%) diagnosed clinically with bacterial pharyngotonsillitis, 8 of 17 (47%) fitting criteria; 0% given recommended antibiotics.

result.other_findings: Lack of doctors' knowledge of local guidelines was identified.

result.setting: Dermatology Department, Medical Teaching Institution-Lady Reading Hospital, Peshawar; inpatients with pemphigus vulgaris
result.standard: Standard pre-infusion guidelines for rituximab (16 parameters)

result.other_findings: Pneumococcal and influenza vaccination was the only element not universally applied.

result.setting: All 20 paediatric and adult Swiss cystic fibrosis centres (Swiss CF registry, ECFSPR project)

cycle1.result: Data correctness ≥95% for most variables; low proportion of missing data.

cycle2.result: Availability of genetic source data and informed consents improved.

result.other_findings: Inconsistencies in specific variables arose from incorrect application of variable definitions.

result.setting: Medical unit, tertiary care hospital (Holy Family Hospital), Rawalpindi
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians e-discharge summary self-assessment checklist

cycle1.result: Allergies recorded 3%; past medical history 52%; secondary diagnoses 54%; investigations 60%; post-discharge plan 90%; follow-up plan 65%.

cycle2.result: Allergies 51%; past medical history 88%; secondary diagnoses 71%; investigations 88%; post-discharge plan 98%; follow-up plan 93% (all p<0.05).

result.other_findings: Medications, operations and procedures were missing in most first-cycle summaries, and patient concerns or expectations were never mentioned.

result.topic: CT KUB use in renal colic
result.setting: Emergency Department, The Royal Melbourne Hospital
result.standard: Choosing Wisely: avoid unnecessary CT KUB in renal colic

cycle1.result: 75% of patients with suspected renal colic had a CT KUB.

result.intervention: Education, updated ED Renal Colic Policy, electronic medical record ordering and a short stay pathway.

cycle2.result: Absolute reduction of 15% in CT KUBs ordered.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Basic life support training for nurses
result.setting: Intensive care unit, general hospital, Tabriz
result.standard: 13 evidence-based JBI audit criteria for BLS training (American Heart Association guidelines)

result.intervention: Human simulator manikin, nurse education programme, cardiopulmonary-cerebral resuscitation department, skills laboratory and continuous BLS education.
result.other_findings: Barriers included insufficient education tools, supervision and skills laboratories.

result.setting: Thoracic surgery unit, tertiary hospital (Hospital Universitario Miguel Servet, Zaragoza)
result.standard: Nine JBI audit criteria for post-operative pain assessment and management

cycle1.result: Poor compliance with best practice (figures not given).

result.other_findings: Three follow-up audits with 34, 40 and 46 patients.

result.setting: Paediatric unit, Marqués de Valdecilla University Hospital, Santander
result.standard: JBI evidence-based audit criteria for promoting sleep and rest in hospitalised children

cycle1.result: Staff trained in paediatric sleep 4%; multi-faceted sleep promotion 21%; relaxation techniques 0%.

cycle2.result: Staff trained 80%; multi-faceted sleep promotion 87%; relaxation techniques 80%.

result.other_findings: 27 multidisciplinary staff involved; yearly follow-up audits recommended.

result.setting: Taibah University Dental Hospital, Madinah; paediatric patients
result.standard: Guidelines on appropriate antibiotic prescribing in dental practice

cycle1.result: 119 antibiotic prescriptions; inappropriate prescribing prevalent.

result.intervention: Action plan with guidelines and educational sessions.
result.other_findings: Amoxicillin then Augmentin were most prescribed; pulpal diseases and periradicular complications accounted for most prescriptions in both cycles.

result.setting: Rural health clinic, southern United States (University of Mississippi Medical Center)
result.standard: JBI best practice for heart failure management (enrolment in disease management programme)

cycle1.result: 0% compliance with best practice.

result.intervention: Policy/protocol for a disease management programme and a virtual multidisciplinary team.
result.other_findings: Recommends using the electronic health record to identify heart failure patients and 6-monthly chart audits.

result.topic: Prevention and management of contrast media reactions

result.standard: Four JBI best practice audit criteria for prevention and management of allergic-like reactions to iodine contrast media

cycle1.result: Emergency equipment management 37.50%; overall reaction rate 0.56%.

cycle2.result: More than 60% compliance with the four criteria; emergency equipment management 100%; reaction rate 0.19%.

result.other_findings: Smallest improvement was in pre-procedure prophylactic treatment of high-risk patients (27.66%).

result.setting: Neurology ward of a tertiary psychiatric hospital, Tabriz
result.standard: JBI best practice audit criteria for fall prevention and management

result.other_findings: 20 health care professionals also audited at baseline; other criteria were unchanged.

result.setting: Río Hortega University Hospital, Valladolid; labour ward, midwives
result.standard: 13 JBI best practice audit criteria for intrapartum care of occiput-posterior fetal position

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Improvement strategies addressing barriers, including midwife training.

cycle2.result: Improvement in all structure criteria (1-3), five process criteria (4-6, 8, 10) and all results criteria (11-13); criterion 8 at maximum compliance in all audits.

result.other_findings: Recording of upright positions (criterion 7) and CTG interpretation (criterion 9) remained inadequate. Two follow-up audits at 4-month intervals.

result.setting: Primary care nurses, Gran Canaria
result.standard: JBI best practice criteria on discharge planning and telephone follow-up for COPD patients

cycle1.result: 30-day readmission 2.78%; 30-day ED presentation 25% (compliance figures not given).

cycle2.result: 100% for criteria 1 and 2 (discharge plan, plan includes telephone follow-up); 4.88% improvement for criteria 3 and 4 (prompt call, validated questionnaire).

result.other_findings: 30-day readmission rose to 4.88% while 30-day ED presentation fell to 9.76%.

result.setting: Long-term care unit, Hospital José Luciano de Castro, Anadia
result.standard: Three JBI audit criteria: communication training, teamwork/conflict training and use of a structured tool (ISBAR) at handover

result.other_findings: Baseline included 250 observed handovers and a questionnaire of 14 nurses.

result.standard: Four JBI audit criteria for oral hygiene in stroke patients

cycle1.result: Low compliance with all four criteria; criterion 1 (nurse training) 0%.

result.intervention: Recommended interventions after identifying gaps (details not given).

result.standard: Compliance with standardised discharge documentation format

result.topic: Ovarian cancer quality of care indicators

result.other_findings: Treatment in high-volume centres and MDT discussion increased; a 10% increase in adherence was associated with improved 5-year survival (HR 0.91). Earlier regional audit in 2009.

result.other_findings: Cost saving of $4454.84 without patient morbidity.

result.standard: Adaptation of the Riverside model (Doppler ABPI assessment and four-layer high compression)

result.other_findings: Areas for improving efficiency were identified.

result.standard: NICE recommends a stable biomarker such as NTproBNP to detect heart failure

result.standard: 100% of critical medications prescribed within 24 hours of admission (NICE medicines reconciliation)

result.setting: Adult general psychiatry inpatient unit (Sheffield/Rotherham)

result.intervention: One-page flowchart for the multidisciplinary team with an education session.

result.topic: Carer communication in inpatient mental health
result.setting: Junction 17 CAMHS inpatient unit

result.setting: Acute adult and PICU wards and inpatient drug/alcohol units across four boroughs, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: POMH-UK Quality Improvement Programme 14c standards (five standards, 12 criteria, three targets)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Four of 12 criteria (liver function and glucose tests, acute withdrawal prescription, parenteral thiamine) and all three targets under 60% compliance and below the national sample.

result.other_findings: Second re-audit in the cycle; practice across the trust was variable. Recommends a standard junior doctor admission checklist and breath testing at admission.

result.setting: Children and young people's Community Eating Disorders Service (CEDS), East London NHS Foundation Trust (Tower Hamlets, Newham, City & Hackney)
result.standard: Commissioned target of routine assessment within 2 weeks (urgent within 5 days); national standards 1 week urgent and 4 weeks routine. Aim: reduce routine referral wait from 17 weeks to 2 weeks in 12 months.

cycle1.result: Average wait from routine referral to assessment 17 weeks; 73 patients on psychiatry wait list; 50 families on therapy wait list; 65 inactive cases.

result.intervention: QI with PDSA cycles: weekly referral meeting with referral tracker and 2-week deadline for referrers; single-clinician triage and assessment; revised co-designed referral form; psychiatry wait list review, clinics three mornings a week, joint reviews and medication/prescription clinics; therapy wait list review and capacity planning; monthly caseload audit; shorter 2-page discharge letter; staff recruitment campaign.

cycle2.result: Average routine wait fell to 2 weeks (88% reduction), sustained; psychiatry wait list 73 to 0 by December 2022; therapy wait list 50 to 0 by April 2023; inactive cases 65 to 0.

result.other_findings: Agency staff spend fell from about £130,000 a year to 0 by February 2024; staffing rose from 64% (July 2022) to 77% (April 2023) with no current vacancies.

result.setting: Neurodevelopmental Team, outpatient CAMHS, Brent, Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Project aims: reduce time-to-treatment initiation (TTI) for ADHD medication by 10% and increase proportion initiated on medication by 5% by February 2024; NICE NG87 recommends medication as part of a treatment plan.

cycle1.result: Mean TTI 86 days; 64% (n=76) of young people started on ADHD medication; satisfaction 4.13/5 (n=13).

result.intervention: Online post-diagnostic psychoeducation platform (videos, Q&A, e-form medication decision portal with physical health e-form, useful links), emailed to families; QR code posters; text message prompts (PDSA 2); patient experience video (PDSA 3).

cycle2.result: Mean TTI fell to 43 days (n=82) after PDSA 3 (reported elsewhere as 51 days, 41% reduction); 70% (n=52) started on medication; satisfaction 4.37/5 (n=21).

result.other_findings: TTI fell stepwise from 86 to 60 (PDSA 1), 54 (PDSA 2) and 43 days (PDSA 3); about 8 hours of clinician time saved over 2 months.

result.topic: Clinical Frailty Scale accuracy in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (acute general hospital)
result.standard: NHS England CQUIN 05 (2023/24): identify frailty in ED patients aged 65+ using the Clinical Frailty Scale, CGA if CFS 6 or above. SMART target 70% correct identification of CFS 6+ by November 2024; ED nurse scores compared with frailty intervention team scores.

cycle1.result: Correct identification of moderate frailty (CFS 6+) 45–51%; exact CFS accuracy 17%.

result.intervention: Two PDSA cycles of ED nurse training: CFS lanyard card to standardise scoring, 1:1 brief teaching (135 sessions), group/virtual sessions, posters, newsletter and emails (cycle 1, November 2023); plus quizzes, scenarios and individual feedback (cycle 2, September to October 2024).

cycle2.result: Correct identification of CFS 6+ rose to 74–78% (78% at 9–13 October 2024); exact CFS accuracy up to 42%.

result.other_findings: After cycle 1 correct identification rose to 70% then ranged 58–68%; exact accuracy rose to 30% but fell back to 17%, so sustainability of accuracy is uncertain.

result.topic: Follow-up chest imaging after community-acquired pneumonia
result.setting: Acute Medical Unit, district general hospital, University Hospitals Bristol and Weston (Weston-super-Mare)
result.standard: BTS and NICE guidance: follow-up chest imaging within six weeks of diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia (patients aged 50 and over and higher-risk patients) to exclude malignancy.

cycle1.result: 22/42 had repeat imaging (X-ray or CT) within six weeks; 16 had none and 4 died before six weeks; 2 cancers found.

result.intervention: Emails to medical and nursing staff summarising audit results and guidelines, posters and banners in clinical areas, patient leaflets in discharge folders, and standardised discharge summary templates with a follow-up imaging prompt.

cycle2.result: 37/50 had repeat imaging; 13 did not; 3 cancers found (all in men).

result.other_findings: Across both cycles 57.89% had chest X-ray as per guidelines and nearly 9% of those re-imaged were diagnosed with cancer; no significant association of follow-up with age or sex.

result.topic: Renal colic imaging and management in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department, Lister Hospital, East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust (district general hospital)
result.standard: NICE NG118/QS195 (CT-KUB within 24 h, serum calcium), BAUS (CT-KUB within 14 h, calcium and urate, avoid repeat CT within 3 months), RCR iRefer and RCEM four-hour standard. Local targets: four-hour compliance ≥90%; CT-KUB request and report ≤90 min each; >90% scans within imaging windows; STONE score documentation ≥75%; calcium ≥65%, urate ≥20%; ≥30% reduction in repeat CT.

cycle1.result: Median urine dip turnaround 144 min, CT-KUB request 166 min, CT report 124 min; RCEM four-hour compliance 16.7% (19/114); calcium tested 50.9% (58/114); urate 0% (0/114); STONE score 5.3% (6/114); repeat CT within 3 months 19.3%; median ED stay 7.5 h.

result.intervention: 'Straight to CT' pathway with registrar-requested scans, mandatory STONE score prompts in ICE/iRefer requests, three staff training sessions with prompt cards and intranet guides, dedicated porter slots and fast-track radiology queue with hot reporting, early SAU/CDU transfers.

cycle2.result: Urine dip 68 min, CT request 75 min, CT report 70 min (all p<0.001); four-hour compliance 57.0% (65/114; p<0.001); calcium 65.8% (75/114; p=0.022); urate 25.4% (29/114); STONE score 78.9% (90/114); repeat CT 9.6% (p=0.038); ED stay 3.9 h.

result.other_findings: Diagnostic yield rose non-significantly from 57.9% to 68.4% (p=0.090) and alternative diagnoses fell from 11.4% to 7.0%; four-hour compliance remained below the 90% target.

result.setting: Urology operating theatres, Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (Preston)
result.standard: Trust waste management guidelines (in line with Department of Health guidance), assessed by a pictographic staff question sheet.

cycle1.dates: December 2022 for anaesthetic gas review; question sheet date not stated
cycle1.result: No staff member placed all waste items correctly; commonest score 5/9 (32%); most common error was putting all items in the yellow clinical bin. Of 39 general anaesthetics, sevoflurane used in 30 and desflurane in 7.

result.intervention: 20-minute in-person educational update on waste disposal and the new waste stream during audit days and drop-in sessions, plus wall signage; planned switch from yellow clinical to orange waste stream.

cycle2.result: After education 81% of staff scored 80% or higher (8/10: 24%, 9/10: 36%, 10/10: 21%).

result.other_findings: Trust produced 850 tonnes of clinical waste a year; switching waste stream estimated to save 483,650 kg CO2 and £467,500 a year. Desflurane still used in 18% of general anaesthetics.

result.topic: Nasal bone fracture timeliness of review and manipulation
result.setting: ENT hub (email referrals with telephone triage and rapid access clinic), Ulster Hospital, Dundonald, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
result.standard: ENT UK and BAOMS guidance: patients requiring reduction of nasal bone fractures assessed and managed within 7–14 days of injury.

cycle1.result: 93% (52/56) referred within 7 days of injury; 63% (35/56) contacted within 7 days of referral; 74% (25/34) seen in clinic within two weeks of injury (82% in abstract); 68% (13/19) had manipulation within 14 days.

result.other_findings: Telephone triage avoided clinic attendance for 39% (22/56). All three paediatric patients needing manipulation under general anaesthetic exceeded 14 days due to theatre capacity.

result.topic: CT sinus reporting for endoscopic sinus surgery (CLOSE criteria)
result.setting: Radiology departments, Victoria Hospital, Kirkcaldy and Queen Margaret Hospital, Dunfermline (NHS Fife health board)
result.standard: CLOSE criteria (Cribriform plate, Lamina papyracea, Onodi cell, Sphenoid sinus pneumatisation, anterior Ethmoidal artery) for pre-FESS CT sinus reports; RCR principle that reports be accurate and complete.

cycle1.result: Full documentation of all CLOSE components 8/51 (15.7%); full compliance in reports with surgically relevant high-risk variants 5/51 (9.8%).

result.intervention: Educational CLOSE poster emailed and displayed in radiology reporting areas (after cycle 1); presentation at departmental radiology meeting and wider poster circulation including to a teleradiology company (after cycle 2).

cycle2.result: Full documentation of all CLOSE components 11/21 (52.4%); high-risk variant compliance 9/21 (42.9%) (χ2=10.375, p<0.01).

result.other_findings: Cycle 2 (July to August 2025, n=20) showed intermediate results. Sphenoid sinus pneumatisation remained least often fully documented (23.81% in cycle 3); 45% of surveyed ENT consultants felt CLOSE only partly sufficient.

result.setting: Department of General Surgery, Whiston Hospital, Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (tertiary centre)
result.standard: GIRFT national 30-day readmission benchmarks: 6.1% for elective colonic resections and 8.8% for elective rectal cancer resections.

cycle1.result: 30-day readmission rate 14.2% (4/28), above GIRFT benchmarks; median length of stay 6 days. Causes: blocked catheter/urinary retention, port-site hernia, collection near anastomosis, gastrointestinal symptoms.

result.intervention: Proposed/initiated: ERAS refresher training with quarterly compliance audits, pilot prehabilitation pathway for high-risk patients, virtual telephone follow-up within 7 days of discharge, revised discharge checklists and updated patient leaflets.
result.other_findings: All readmitted patients had length of stay 6 days or less and had robotic anterior resections. Model Health System data showed 12.6% (colonic) and 17.5% (rectal) readmissions in July–September 2024 and 13.1% and 17.6% in October–December 2024; formal re-audit planned.

result.setting: Two Diabetes and Endocrine wards (D1 and D3), Royal Blackburn Teaching Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: Nursing documentation standards for daily bowel movement recording using the Bristol Stool Chart (frequency, consistency, correct chart format, escalation/clinical action).

cycle1.dates: April to October 2025 study period (cycle 1 date not stated)
cycle1.result: Daily bowel documentation 8/30 (27%); Bristol Stool Chart used 17 (57%); stool frequency 9 (30%); correct chart format 14 (47%); consistency 15 (50%); clinical action taken 15 (50%).

result.intervention: 'Bowel Matters' reminder posters at workstations, ward areas and toilets; summary to ward manager to cascade; staff advised to add bowel documentation to shift handover checklist and daily nursing care bundles.

cycle2.result: Daily documentation 18 (73%) (χ2 p=0.0092); Bristol Stool Chart 27 (87%) (p=0.0035); frequency 16 (60%); correct chart format 21 (70%, reported elsewhere as 87%); consistency 23 (87%) (p=0.0321); clinical action taken 15 (50%).

result.other_findings: Nurse questionnaire (n=12) identified time constraints and forgetfulness as main causes. Changes were then spread to older people's, rehabilitation and stroke wards.

result.topic: Critical care follow-up and recovery experiences
result.setting: Adult Critical Care Unit, Royal London Hospital (large adult critical care service), within evaluation of a pilot follow-up service

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews with 16 survivors and 7 clinicians; shared themes of uncertain recovery, fragmented care and psychological impact, with differing perceptions of timing and responsibility.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend earlier discussion of recovery expectations, clinicians acting as care navigators, and better integration of health and social care.

result.topic: Antibiotic use for suspected early onset neonatal infection
result.setting: Neonatal unit and transitional care unit, University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust (tertiary neonatal service)
result.standard: NICE NG195 neonatal infection guideline and Kaiser Permanente Neonatal Infection Calculator (KPNIC); aim to reduce antibiotic initiation and duration in low-risk infants.

cycle1.result: 13% of live births started on antibiotics for suspected EONI in 2018; 12.4% of live births >35 weeks in 2019; 1089 transitional care cefotaxime care days in 2019.

result.intervention: Five PDSA cycles: CRP threshold raised to 20 mg/L to stop antibiotics at 36 hours in well culture-negative infants ('20 is the new 10'); GBS-positive mothers added to KPNIC; use of KPNIC risk after clinical exam rather than risk at birth; background EONI rate changed to 1/1000; KPNIC extended to 34 weeks. Supported by guideline updates, teaching, posters, emails and newsletters.

cycle2.result: 6.8% of live births >34 weeks on antibiotics in 2024 and 6.6% in 2025 (to 30 June); transitional care cefotaxime days fell to 270 in 2024 (75% reduction).

result.other_findings: No infant given a shortened course with CRP 10–20 or not started on antibiotics re-presented with infection within 14 days. Neonatal unit antibiotic care days stayed static at 110–120 a month.

result.topic: Topical lidocaine for paediatric airway procedures
result.setting: Paediatric anaesthesia department, University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust (tertiary paediatric centre); survey of consultant paediatric anaesthetists
result.standard: Advocated standards based on APAGBI guidance and published evidence: maximum topical lidocaine dose 4.0 mg/kg at concentration ≤4%; nil-by-mouth 60 minutes after topicalisation; mucosal atomisation device as standard.

cycle1.result: Median self-reported maximum dose 3.0 mg/kg (range 2.0–9.0); 2/22 (9.1%) used the 4.0 mg/kg standard; median NBM time 120 minutes (range 60–360), 8/22 (36.4%) adherent; Jelco device 18/22 (81.8%), MAD 14/22 (63.6%).

result.intervention: 45-minute structured teaching session within mandatory departmental teaching presenting survey findings, complications and advocated guidelines.

cycle2.result: Median maximum dose 4.0 mg/kg; 8/15 (53.3%) used 4.0 mg/kg (p=0.006); median NBM 60 minutes, 11/15 (73.3%) adherent (p=0.045); Jelco 12/15 (80.0%), MAD 10/15 (66.7%), unchanged.

result.other_findings: Wide dose variation (2.0–9.0 mg/kg) persisted and device choice did not change. No respondent used concentrations above 4%; incidents were rare and not linked to practice variables.

result.setting: Post-Anaesthesia Care Unit (main and burns theatres), Chelsea and Westminster Hospital (large tertiary hospital)
result.standard: NICE delirium guidance: high-risk patients (age over 65, cognitive impairment, hip fracture) screened with a validated tool (4AT or CAM) before PACU discharge. Target at least 50% adherence within 1 month of launch.

cycle1.result: 3/130 (2.3%) at-risk patients screened for delirium in PACU; nurse confidence median 7/10 and guideline clarity median 4/10.

result.intervention: PDSA 1: new trust-wide perioperative delirium guideline. PDSA 2: 4AT made easily accessible on electronic systems, PACU discharge checklist updated to require screening, simplified guidance signposted, daily list review at morning huddles to flag at-risk patients, staff education, and leadership engagement using coding/funding data.

cycle2.result: 48/67 (71.64%) at-risk patients screened (p<0.0001); 81.50% in final week; nurse confidence and guideline clarity both median 10/10 (p<0.0001).

result.other_findings: PDSA cycle 1 (29 March to 12 April 2025) screening 15/49 (30.61%). Of 63 screened, 11 (17.46%) scored 4+ suggesting delirium; medical team pathway for positive screens not yet formalised.

result.setting: Learning disability female low secure forensic unit, Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust
result.standard: Trust and national guidelines on psychotropic prescribing and monitoring (indications on drug chart, HDAT/combined antipsychotic care plans, consent to treatment and capacity forms, annual health check, blood monitoring, annual valproate risk acknowledgement form).

cycle1.result: 100% compliance for indications on drug chart, HDAT/combined antipsychotic care plans, consent to treatment forms, annual health check and psychotropic blood monitoring; MHA capacity assessment form 71%; annual valproate risk acknowledgement form in women of childbearing age 0%.

result.other_findings: Investigation results were hard to locate. Recommendations: care plans for all patients on valproate with review dates for risk acknowledgement forms and consistent filing of results.

result.topic: PTSD treatment in people experiencing homelessness
result.setting: Inner-city homelessness health service (University of Manchester affiliation)
result.standard: National guidance recommending trauma-focused psychological therapies for PTSD.

cycle1.result: 11% of individuals received some form of psychological therapy; medication was the main treatment.

result.other_findings: Commonest reasons for unsuccessful therapy were lack of contact or engagement, discharge because of substance misuse, and missing records or follow-up.

result.topic: Ethnic inequalities in perinatal mental health service access
result.setting: Perinatal Mental Health Services, Southwark (South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists gold standards for equitable access to perinatal mental health care.

cycle1.result: Ethnicity not documented in 6.6% of referrals; no clear inequity at referral, but 3 of 4 admissions (75%) were Black women and all detained; only 2/35 Asian and Mixed ethnicity women referred for psychology; 83% (5/6) of antipsychotics prescribed to Black women; 48% of 31 safeguarding alerts involved Black women.

result.other_findings: Authors concluded the service was not meeting RCPsych gold standards for equitable care.

result.setting: Harrogate Older Adult Community Mental Health Team, Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE NG97 (June 2018) Dementia guideline and local trust guidance on antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring.

cycle1.result: 88% had assessment of sources of distress; 42% had non-pharmacological intervention before antipsychotic (58% after starting); 63% risk discussion documented; 63% baseline bloods; 54% baseline ECG; 33% of those treated over 12 weeks had discontinuation or dose-reduction trial; under 22% had physical health monitoring at one year.

result.other_findings: Random sample of 24 from 55 patients. Recommended a pre-prescribing checklist and a system to flag when monitoring and review are due.

result.setting: Adult inpatient psychiatry ward, Greater Manchester Mental Health trust (Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust affiliation)
result.standard: NICE guidance on monitoring patients on long-term antipsychotics (14 standards: BMI, ECG, blood pressure, lipids, prolactin, urea and electrolytes at baseline, set time points and dose changes).

cycle1.result: 5 of 14 standards attained, 7 not attained, 1 partially analysed and 1 (12-month monitoring) not analysable.

result.other_findings: Recommendations: comprehensive admission proforma, reminder tool for 3, 6 and 12-month rechecks, and regular ECG machine maintenance.

result.topic: Baseline physical health checks before starting antipsychotics
result.setting: Intensive Home Treatment Team, Bradford District Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust Antipsychotic Physical Health Monitoring Shared Care Guidelines.

cycle1.result: 32% had a full physical health check before antipsychotic initiation, 56% incomplete; no individual investigation fully compliant; BMI/weight least completed, HbA1c least completed blood test; 40% had results reviewed by a relevant professional.

result.other_findings: Diet and physical activity were recorded less often than illicit drug use and smoking status. Results shared with the team.

result.setting: Pine Ward, 17-bed male low secure forensic inpatient ward, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust guidance: mandatory ALL-Physical Health Assessment on admission and six-monthly (14 categories).

cycle1.result: 76.4% of patients had ALL done; 67.2% of completions green, 15.5% amber, 17.2% red; QRISK 70%, alcohol 58%, diet 82%, exercise 70%, diabetes 58%, smoking 76%.

cycle2.result: 15/17 (88%) had ALL in last 6 months; 89.9% of completions green, 4.6% amber, 5.5% red; QRISK, alcohol, diet and exercise 100%; diabetes 82%, smoking 88%.

result.other_findings: Some areas still below expected standard; authors recommend raising importance of the assessment with trainees.

result.topic: Safety plans for high intensity users of mental health services
result.setting: Section 136 suite, liaison psychiatry and inpatient wards, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust
result.standard: Aim that high intensity users of acute mental health services have a person-centred safety plan in place.

cycle1.result: More than 80% had a safety plan but plans lacked detail to avert crisis; EUPD commonest diagnosis (77%); 93% on CPA.

result.intervention: QI with process mapping, driver diagram, co-production and focus groups: additional 'HIU response plan' template, best practice example for care coordinators, process to flag HIUs to community teams.

cycle2.result: HIU response plans incorporated into the safety plans of 20/26 HIUs.

result.other_findings: PDSA ongoing; quality and effectiveness of changes still to be reviewed.

result.setting: Stroud Recovery community mental health service, Gloucestershire Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidance: antipsychotics not recommended for EUPD and should be reviewed with aim of reducing and stopping.

cycle1.result: 30/37 (81%) with EUPD ever prescribed antipsychotics; 24 (80%) had no licensed comorbid indication; mean duration 36.79 months; 12 (50%) had more than one antipsychotic; only 10 (42%) had prescriptions reviewed to stop or reduce; none offered routine physical review.

result.other_findings: Subgroup without licensed indication mostly female (75%) and aged 20–29 (46%); quetiapine most used.

result.setting: Community Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service team, Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Licensed use per Summary of Product Characteristics and NICE, BAP and BNFc guidance.

cycle1.result: 177 prescriptions: 25% prescribed within licence; 42% compatible with NICE, 62% with BAP, 67% with BNFc; 12% deviated from all guidance (mirtazapine 1, melatonin 9, quetiapine 6, risperidone 1, olanzapine 4).

result.other_findings: 88% of prescriptions were supported by licence or at least one guideline; unsupported prescriptions were linked with higher comorbidity.

result.setting: Older adult psychiatric inpatient units across Dudley, Walsall, West Bromwich and Wolverhampton, Black Country Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE CG183: drug and reaction documented on all prescriptions and records; standard 100% of drug charts and Rio EPR with allergy status.

result.intervention: Allergy status prompt in electronic clerking document, stickers and posters on wards, pharmacy to update EPR allergy status, and allergy alert added to ward matrons' bed state view.
result.other_findings: Re-audit across older and working age adult wards (about 300 patients) under way at time of writing.

result.topic: Prescribing for challenging behaviour in intellectual disability
result.setting: Intellectual Disability Team, large acute mental health trust (Leicestershire Partnership NHS Trust)
result.standard: NICE and STOMP guidelines for pharmacological management of challenging behaviour in intellectual disability.

cycle1.result: Risk assessment 68%; description of target behaviours 74%; metabolic monitoring 0%; documentation of interventions 48%; mental health evaluation 87%; physical health 61%; consent 19%; side-effect discussion 32%; 6-week efficacy review 52%.

cycle2.result: Risk assessment 100%; target behaviours 100%; metabolic monitoring 95%; interventions documented 86%; mental health evaluation 60%; physical health 60%; consent 46%; side-effect discussion 50%; 6-week review 50%; positive behaviour support plan 75%.

result.other_findings: Middle cycle 2014 (n=17). Polypharmacy declined, with single-drug therapy 19%, 35%, 34%; outpatient-dependent standards worsened, partly due to COVID-19 service pressures.

result.topic: Prescribing in emotionally unstable personality disorder
result.setting: Trust-wide, South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE EUPD guidance: no drug treatment specifically for EUPD; time-limited crisis prescribing only; written information and regular reviews if prescribing.

cycle1.result: 71/87 (81.6%) prescribed medication; of these 39.4% (n=28) consistent with time-limited prescribing, 57.7% (n=41) had timely reviews, 4.2% (n=3) had written information recorded.

result.other_findings: Random 10% sample of 869 patients with EUPD. Results presented to Clinical Reference Group and a working group formed.

result.setting: George Mackenzie House low secure unit (Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust) and Fens Unit, HMP Whitemoor prison personality disorder unit
result.standard: Respective trust (CPFT and NHFT) physical health monitoring guidelines for patients on antipsychotics.

cycle1.result: Laboratory markers monitored in 88–100% at both sites; waist circumference omitted in 100% at both sites; ECG omitted in 60% (prison) and 14% (low secure unit).

result.other_findings: 17/18 low secure and 23/50 prison service users eligible. Suggested staff teaching and electronic reminders.

result.setting: Sandwell CAMHS (Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust), Rio electronic record
result.standard: NICE guidance on documentation of drug allergy status (substance, reaction, severity, date, evidence and certainty).

cycle1.result: 60/516 had allergy status recorded (18 possible allergy, 42 no known allergy); 456 no recording. Of 18 allergies: reaction 12, severity 13, date 3, evidence/certainty 1.

result.other_findings: Recommendations included Rio prompts for annual allergy updates, trust policy, junior doctor handbook/e-learning, and re-audit in 6–12 months.

result.topic: Mental health triage form use in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency Department, Royal Cornwall Hospital (with Cornwall Partnership NHS Foundation Trust psychiatric liaison)
result.standard: RCEM recommendation (in line with NCEPOD 'Treat as One') to use a mental health proforma; local Mental Health Triage Form.

cycle1.result: Mental Health Triage Form used in 44/125 (35%); 15 (12%) had missing ED documentation; 25% average increase in information recorded when the form was used.

result.other_findings: Form use had fallen from 46% in June 2020 to 35% in June 2021; triage code questions improved most with form use.

result.standard: Local algorithm/Trust protocol for doctors (allocated team or on-call) participating in Mental Health Act assessments.

cycle1.result: At least one trust doctor involved in 91% of assessments (92% in Section 136 suite; 89% out of hours).

result.other_findings: 45% detained under section 2 and 35% under section 3; substance misuse part of 26% of assessments. Recommended amending the Section 136 form to record the doctor's role.
