result.setting: Five EBUS centres in the Greater Manchester Cancer Alliance

cycle1.result: 1309 staging and 590 diagnostic EBUS procedures; major complications in six cases; over 85% of procedures performed within 7 days of referral (abstract text truncated).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Antimicrobial stewardship analytics from electronic records
result.setting: Six specialities, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham
result.standard: AMS standards of care and prescribing guidelines

cycle1.result: 22% of low-severity community-acquired pneumonia therapy episodes were guideline-congruent; IV to oral switch delayed by an average 3.6 days; cultures taken before treatment in 22% of antibacterial prescriptions.

result.other_findings: Feasibility study of EHR-based stewardship measures.

result.topic: Eye care provision in special schools
result.setting: Orthoptic service areas across the UK (survey)

cycle1.result: 65 areas provide a special school service; 24 have no specialist provision; 29 (44%) include vision and orthoptic assessment and 31 (48%) also refraction in school.

result.other_findings: 26 (40%) involved optometric input in school; none had optical dispensing in school.

result.setting: UK radiology departments (135 hospitals)
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists guidance on providing seven-day acute care

cycle1.result: 96% have a diagnostic radiologist rota for acute cases; 48% lack a fully staffed 24/7 consultant interventional radiology rota; MRI radiographer availability 18.8% to 63.9%.

result.other_findings: 40% have no 24/7 RIS technical support and 34% no out-of-hours PACS support; 54% lack a working-time-compliant IR rota.

result.topic: Imaging dose in ocular proton beam therapy
result.setting: The National Centre for Eye Proton Therapy, The Clatterbridge Cancer Centre
result.standard: Ionising Radiation (Medical Exposure) Regulations audit context

cycle1.result: Patients with no clips visible needed mean 14.6 vs 9.6 image pairs (p = 2.74 × 10^-6), an additional 1.5 mGy.

result.other_findings: Secondary cancer risk rose from 0.0004 to 0.0007%, judged not clinically significant; 399 patients audited.

result.topic: Acute medicine services for pregnant women
result.setting: 130 UK hospitals, Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit
result.standard: National recommendations for acute medical care in pregnancy

cycle1.result: 5.5% had an acute medicine consultant trained in obstetric medicine; 38% had a named maternal medicine lead; 64 units had local guidelines; 43% had a VTE in pregnancy guideline.

result.other_findings: Centres with a named lead had more guidelines (p = 0.019).

result.topic: Type A aortic dissection surgery outcomes
result.setting: UK National Adult Cardiac Surgical Audit dataset, national registry

cycle1.result: Registry outcome analysis of operative mortality; patient characteristics, intraoperative factors, cardiac centre and high-volume surgeons were determinants of outcome.

result.other_findings: Age was retained in the final model (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.02-1.03); hospital and surgeon variation shown with risk-adjusted funnel plots.

result.topic: Conversations about children at end of life
result.setting: Professionals attending a 2-day virtual palliative care congress

cycle1.result: 73.2% of professionals felt confident starting a conversation with adult patients at end of life about important children; 64.7% signposted families to support services.

result.other_findings: 76.7% wanted training, with demonstration videos the preferred option; labelled an audit but is a survey of professionals.

result.setting: Real-time surveillance systems of suspected suicides covering about 13 million population

cycle1.result: 121.3 suicides per month in April-October 2020 after lockdown versus 125.7 per month in January-March 2020 (-4%; 95% CI -19% to 13%, p = 0.59).

result.other_findings: No rise in lockdown period April-May 2020 (IRR 1.01 [0.81-1.25]) or June-October 2020 (0.94 [0.81-1.09]).

result.setting: All Wales Medical Genomics Service, national genetics service

cycle1.result: Overall germline/somatic pathogenic variant detection rate 11.6%; germline 9.2% (73/791). Parallel testing in 169 patients detected 14.8%, with 6.5% (11/169) somatic variants.

result.other_findings: Two BRCA1 dosage variants (2.0%, 2/98) would have been missed by tumour testing alone.

result.topic: Medical student clinical audit in general practice
result.setting: Graduate entry medical students and 25 GP practices, University College Dublin

cycle1.result: Students reported positive educational impact (55%), better understanding of the audit cycle (72%) and real-world prescribing (77%); significant difference in audit-cycle knowledge versus non-participants (p = 0.001).

result.other_findings: 96% of responding GPs would host future student audits; research skills confidence did not improve.

result.setting: Children's Palliative Care Education and Training Action Group across UK and Ireland

cycle1.result: Framework with four levels (Public Health, Universal, Core, Specialist) and four learning outcomes each; an audit tool template was developed for quality assurance.

result.other_findings: Framework development paper; no audit data reported.

result.setting: BAUS cystectomy registry, 78 UK hospitals
result.standard: High-quality surgery defined by pathological (negative margins, level I node dissection with at least ten nodes), recovery (length of stay 10 days or less) and technical criteria

cycle1.result: 914 patients (19.6%) received high-quality surgery.

result.other_findings: Surgeon volume of at least 20 and hospital volume of at least 68 cystectomies per year were thresholds for better quality; high-quality surgery predicted lower index admission mortality (OR 0.38).

result.setting: Flinders Medical Centre, South Australia
result.standard: Surgical safety checklist compliance on direct observation

cycle1.result: Observed compliance 3.5% despite documented compliance of 100%.

result.intervention: Paper checklist replaced with reusable laminated form, multidisciplinary education and marketing campaign, targeted coaching and changes after staff feedback, over four PDSA cycles.
result.other_findings: Five direct observational audits and two staff surveys were done; staff felt the new process improved safety.

result.setting: Emergency department, Cork University Hospital
result.standard: Evidence-based guidelines recommending against routine radiological and laboratory investigations in bronchiolitis

cycle1.result: Infants under 12 months with bronchiolitis were receiving unnecessary investigations; mean average weekly CXR rate 25%.

result.intervention: Locally agreed flowchart with regular performance feedback using run charts and in-person sessions.

cycle2.result: Mean average weekly CXR rate fell to 11% (57% reduction, p = 0.009974).

result.other_findings: Outcome measure was weekly length of stay; balancing measure was representation rate.

result.setting: Emergency department, large teaching hospital, East Lancashire Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: NAP4 recommendation to use a safety checklist for intubation; aim 90% checklist use within 6 months

cycle1.result: Checklist used in 16.7% of applicable cases.

result.intervention: Interventions to raise awareness and expectation of checklist use, build a favourable view of its benefits and prompt its use at the right moment.
result.other_findings: Run chart showed a shift soon after interventions began; some cases likely missed by the capture method.

result.topic: Colonoscopy audit and feedback adverse effects
result.setting: Six English NHS endoscopy centres

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews: unmet targets prompted anxiety and consideration of gaming, including inaccurate documentation of patient comfort and removal of insignificant polyps.

result.other_findings: Negative feedback without an improvement plan risked reducing confidence.

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
result.setting: Primary care in 18 European countries

cycle1.result: Antibiotic prescribing varied considerably between countries; point-of-care testing ranged from 0% (Croatia, Moldova, Romania) to over 65% (Denmark, Norway).

result.other_findings: Prescribing related to severity, comorbidity, age, fever and country, not to POC testing; GPs were confident in nearly 90% of decisions.

result.topic: Phenylalanine control and mental health in phenylketonuria
result.setting: Mark Holland Adult Inherited Metabolic Disorders Unit, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust, single large centre
result.standard: ESPKU guidelines: lifelong phenylalanine control of 600 micromol/L or less

cycle1.result: 220 of 244 patients had a recorded Phe level; approximately 75% did not meet the ESPKU guideline for Phe control.

result.other_findings: Patients with two-year average Phe above 600 micromol/L were more likely to have low mood, depression, anxiety or mood swings, but only low mood was statistically significant.

result.setting: Acute medicine services at 93 UK hospitals, Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit
result.standard: Survey questions derived from national guidance

cycle1.result: All services had taken measures for increased demand; 81.7% had expanded medical inpatient beds and 80.4% had added extra clinical staff.

result.other_findings: A quarter of units had reduced Same Day Emergency Care beds on the survey day; patients were waiting in ED corridors in 56.3% of units.

result.setting: 60 general practices in 4 Australian states, cluster randomised trial

cycle1.result: Removing audit/feedback: testing fell from 21.0% to 11.6% versus 19.9% to 14.5% where retained (adjusted difference -2.6%, p = 0.0336). Removing incentives: 20.2% to 11.7% versus 20.6% to 14.3% (adjusted difference -0.9%, p = 0.2267).

result.other_findings: Trial of removing financial incentives and audit/feedback; audit/feedback was more effective at sustaining testing than incentives.

result.topic: Linked cancer registration and cardiovascular audit data
result.setting: Virtual Cardio-Oncology Research Initiative linking national English cancer registration and cardiovascular audits

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Data resource profile; no abstract supplied.

result.setting: Neonatal unit, Kamuzu Central Hospital, Lilongwe, low-resource setting using NeoTree app

cycle1.result: 2,413 (88.3%) had an electronic outcome; 492 (20%) died, case fatality rate 204/1,000 admissions. Data were 100% complete for mandatory fields and 96% across all fields.

result.other_findings: Leading causes of death were prematurity with respiratory distress (51%), sepsis (23%) and encephalopathy (16%); 59 (29.2%) of 202 HIV-exposed neonates did not receive nevirapine prophylaxis.

result.setting: Drive-through IOP clinic at City West for Royal Victoria Eye and Ear Hospital and Mater Misericordiae University Hospital

cycle1.result: 301 of 672 attendees had a hospital follow-up; mean drive-through iCare IOP 19.4 mmHg ± 6.0 was significantly higher than Goldmann measurement.

result.other_findings: Authors concluded the drive-through clinic was a safe way to monitor glaucoma patients during COVID-19.

result.topic: Transgender patient care in primary care
result.setting: One primary care population, Falmouth and Penryn Primary Care Network, Cornwall
result.standard: International secondary care evidence-informed guideline (no primary care standard found)

cycle1.result: Up to two-thirds of patients did not receive all recommended monitoring standards.

result.other_findings: Long waits and high medical complexity were found; a fifth of patients stopped hormones, more than half of whom cited regret or detransition.

result.setting: Emergency Laparoscopic and Laparotomy Scottish Audit (ELLSA)

cycle1.result: 10.6% were frail (CFS 5 or more); 30-day mortality rose from 2.1% at CFS 1 to 25.3% at CFS 6 and 7.

result.topic: Old age liaison psychiatry service provision
result.setting: Old age liaison psychiatry, St James Hospital, Dublin, large teaching hospital

cycle1.result: 195 patients assessed with a mean of 2.6 consultations (range 1-15), almost all face to face.

result.intervention: COVID-19 pandemic; service moved to mainly remote work.

cycle2.result: 197 patients assessed with a mean of 3.1 consultations (range 1-19).

result.other_findings: More referrals for behavioural disturbance and confusion, and more diagnoses of BPSD, delirium and adjustment disorder in the pandemic period.

result.setting: 47 hospital emergency departments across 15 European countries, European Audit of Seizure Management in Hospitals

cycle1.result: Of those with known epilepsy, 41.2% had attended ED in the previous 12 months and only 64.7% had seen an epilepsy specialist; only 37.5% of first seizure patients were given driving advice.

result.setting: National Bowel Cancer Audit, 145-146 hospitals

cycle1.result: Laparoscopy rate, abdominoperineal resection, preoperative radiotherapy and distant metastases significantly affected length of stay over five days and 18-month stoma rate (p < 0.05).

result.other_findings: 18-month stoma rate predicted two-year mortality (p < 0.001).

result.topic: Variable rate intravenous insulin infusion use
result.setting: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Joint British Diabetes Societies 2014 VRIII guidelines, including use of balanced substrate fluid

cycle1.result: Hypoglycaemic events per VRIII 0.73 (±1.78); hypokalaemic events per VRIII 0.15 (±0.54); VRIII episodes with hyponatraemia 26%.

cycle2.result: Hypoglycaemic events per VRIII 0.28 (±0.84) (p<0.05); hypokalaemic events 0.05 (±0.25); hyponatraemia 12% (p<0.01).

result.other_findings: Some improvements were not sustained at 1-year follow-up; substantial net cost saving reported.

result.setting: Mixed urban and rural primary care practices, Victoria

cycle1.result: Diabetes screening rate 26% before the intervention.

result.other_findings: Critical factors included involving mothers, collective staff strategies, leadership and acting on feedback.

result.topic: Complications of transoesophageal echocardiography in children

cycle1.result: No reports of major upper gastrointestinal or aerodigestive tract trauma in 1,059 TEE studies.

cycle1.result: Qualitative themes: reliability and validity of feedback, feedback useful but limited, and feedback needs to be easily digestible.

result.setting: 27 Australasian general practitioners on the Skin Cancer Audit Research Database

cycle1.result: Diagnostic and therapeutic management was closely aligned with current guidelines; most melanomas were in situ or thin invasive.

result.topic: Perioperative critical events in neonatal anaesthesia
result.setting: 17 UK centres in the NECTARINE European multicentre observational study

cycle1.result: Critical events triggered interventions in 300/876 (34.3%) cases; cardiovascular instability 16.9% and reduced oxygenation 11.4%.

result.topic: Inflammatory bowel disease care audit via electronic record

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: No abstract supplied.

result.topic: Congenital heart disease audit data linkage

result.topic: Cervical screening in pregnant and postnatal women

result.setting: 11 emergency departments in Ireland, National Emergency Resuscitation Airway Audit pilot

cycle1.result: 131 intubation attempts; first pass success 89%; checklists, video laryngoscopy and bougie used in 55%, 53% and 64% of first attempts.

result.standard: POMH clozapine practice standards (smoking status in care plan, clozapine in Summary Care Record)

cycle1.result: Smoking status change considered in care plans of just under one-third of relevant patients; clozapine in Summary Care Record in 58% of community patients.

cycle2.result: Smoking status change considered in just over a half; clozapine in Summary Care Record in 72%.

result.other_findings: In both audits over a quarter of patients had high-dose and/or combined antipsychotics before clozapine was started.

result.topic: Paediatric blunt liver and spleen injury management
result.setting: All 21 UK paediatric major trauma centres
result.standard: American Pediatric Surgical Association 2019 blunt liver and spleen injury guidance

cycle1.result: ICU care determined by haemodynamic status or concomitant injuries in line with APSA; contrary to APSA, follow-up imaging was done in 44% before and 32% after discharge.

result.topic: Appropriateness of CT in surgical patients
result.setting: Surgical patients at an Irish hospital (ED, inpatient and outpatient)

cycle1.result: 51 (50%) of 102 CT scans were unremarkable.

result.other_findings: Authors suggested better history and examination could reduce unnecessary CT.

result.setting: Emergency department, Cork University Hospital
result.standard: Clinical practice guidelines: all older patients in acute care screened for delirium with standardised measures

result.other_findings: Root cause analysis used to identify reasons for missed screening.

result.topic: Transfer from paediatric to adult congenital heart services
result.setting: LAUNCHES QI linked national dataset, England

cycle1.result: 63.8% transferred by their 22nd birthday; estimated transfer probability 96.5% severe, 86.7% moderate and 41.0% mild CHD.

result.setting: Ambulatory dental clinic, Keta Municipal Hospital, public hospital

cycle1.result: 88.6% (n = 1269) received antibiotics and 87.5% (n = 1254) of antibiotics prescribed were non-compliant with the guidelines.

result.setting: not reported

cycle1.dates: Wave One of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic
cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: No abstract supplied; only the title was available.

result.standard: Local and international recommendations for pre-procedural screening before PFT

cycle1.result: 39% documented as receiving analgesia; 0% regional blocks; 7% of discharged patients had documented advice.

result.setting: Radiotherapy department, Guy's & St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Before and after images of 102 patients showed no loss of clinical usability.

result.intervention: Ten optimised, patient size-specific CBCT protocols introduced.

cycle2.result: Imaging dose reduced for 52% of patients, unchanged for 37% and increased for 12%.

result.setting: 64 UK NHS mental health trusts, POMH audit-based QI programme
result.standard: Licensed indications and monitoring of valproate (baseline health checks, early and annual reviews)

cycle1.result: Licensed indication 38%, off-label 37%, uncertain 25%. Early response and side-effect reviews documented in 70% and 53%; annual reviews in 63% and 49%.

result.setting: 24 international population-based breast screening programmes

cycle1.result: Response 71% (17/24); 12/17 had a programmatic interval cancer audit process.

result.other_findings: No consistent approach to individual interval cancer review or disclosure of results.

result.topic: Pancreatic enzyme replacement in pancreatic cancer

cycle1.result: National PERT prescribing rates rose from 41% in 2015 to 48% in early 2023, still below the 100% standard.

result.topic: Anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation in rheumatoid arthritis

result.topic: Stillbirth and neonatal death audit implementation

cycle1.result: Overall SAP compliance 2.5% (n = 15); appropriate choice 67.0% (n = 400); appropriate duration 8.7% (n = 52).

result.topic: Primary care blood tests before cancer diagnosis

cycle1.result: At least one common blood test used in 41% (n = 16 427/39 752); among tested, FBC 95%, U&E 89%, LFTs 76%.

result.other_findings: Tested patients had longer primary care intervals (10 versus 0 days) and diagnostic intervals (49 versus 32 days).

result.setting: Academic tertiary care otolaryngology-head and neck surgery department, London Health Sciences Centre
result.standard: Institutional target of 50% of discharge summaries distributed within 48 hours of discharge

cycle1.result: Mean ± SD 19% ± 6.4% of discharge summaries distributed within 48 hours

result.intervention: Process mapping, education and engagement, auto-authentication (distribution immediately after transcription without review by the most responsible physician), and audit and feedback

cycle2.result: Mean ± SD 54% ± 20% distributed within 48 hours; target exceeded and sustained

result.other_findings: Balancing measures included workload and revisions to auto-authenticated notes.

result.topic: Time to CT from surgical assessment unit
result.setting: Surgical Assessment Unit, Yeovil District Hospital NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.dates: First two weeks of June 2019, weekday working hours
cycle1.result: 5/25 (20%) had CT within four hours of admission; 4% discharged within six hours and 80% stayed more than 12 hours

result.intervention: A radiology registrar allocated to the SAU to vet and report CT imaging from June 2020

cycle2.dates: First two weeks of June 2020, weekday working hours
cycle2.result: 33/40 (82.5%) had CT within four hours of admission; 57.5% discharged within 12 hours

result.other_findings: 45% of patients in 2020 were discharged within four hours after the CT scan.

result.setting: General Surgery, Royal Cornwall Hospital, Truro (acute hospital)
result.standard: Public Health England antibiotic prescribing audit tool (appropriateness at initiation, pre-72-hour review and duration)

cycle1.result: 1162 days of therapy; 192 (16.5%) excess DOTs in 38 patients (44%): 75/192 (39%) at initiation, 55/192 (29%) after the pre-72-hour review, 62/192 (32%) from protracted courses

result.other_findings: IV antibiotics were 53.4% of DOTs; 72/86 (83.7%) received 620 IV DOTs, of which 79 (12.7%) were unnecessary. The surgeon apportioned fewer excess DOTs (160/1162, 13.8%) than infection specialists.

result.topic: Occupational therapy initial contact after admission
result.setting: Mental health inpatient wards, Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: 90% of patients to receive OT initial contact within two working days of admission by end of June 2020

cycle1.result: Average initial contact within two working days 12.5%

result.intervention: PDSA cycles: standardised initial contact, informal training on the audit tool, more efficient documentation of OT contact, updated inclusion/exclusion criteria, refined documentation for contact and assessment

cycle2.result: Average initial contact within two working days 71.24%; 90% target not achieved

result.other_findings: Tested on two of five wards, then spread to the remaining three; dedicated time for initial contact was linked to high compliance.

result.setting: Online survey of perinatal healthcare workers in high-income countries

cycle1.result: 97.5% considered neonatal near-miss important for identifying cases for morbidity audit, but only 10.0% of institutions used a definition

result.other_findings: Survey of opinion; commonest proposed near-miss criteria were birth asphyxia needing therapeutic hypothermia (68.3%) and unexpected resuscitation at birth (67.5%).

result.topic: Rehabilitation outcomes in COPD and heart failure
result.setting: National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation and National COPD Audit Programme pulmonary rehabilitation audit (211 PR and 237 CR programmes)

cycle1.result: Adults with COPD gained more on incremental shuttle walk test than COPD+CHF after PR (59.3 m vs 37.4 m); CR gains similar (CHF 77.3 m vs CHF+COPD 58.3 m)

result.other_findings: CHF+COPD had lower enrolment and completion of CR than CHF alone; quality of life and mood improvements were comparable regardless of diagnosis.

result.setting: Paediatric outpatient department, private hospital, Abu Dhabi

cycle1.result: Antibiotics in 43.0% of prescriptions; parenteral medicines 16.9%; mean 4.9 drugs per prescription; mean consultation 14 min and dispensing 9.6 min

result.other_findings: Cefaclor was the most prescribed antibiotic (31.1%); antibiotics were used irrationally for acute otitis media and bronchiolitis, but formulary adherence and generic prescribing were appropriate.

result.topic: Retinal screening in Von Hippel-Lindau disease
result.setting: VHL retinal surveillance clinics, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford

cycle1.result: 94 eyes: 12.8% of Optos images positive for angioma vs 11.7% on slit-lamp examination; one discrepancy (1.1%)

result.other_findings: Optos imaging identified all angiomas and was judged non-inferior to slit-lamp fundoscopy.

result.topic: Management of severe hypertension and postpartum haemorrhage
result.setting: Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care facility run by an international humanitarian NGO (about 6500 deliveries per year)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Change ideas from frontline doctors, midwives and nurses, including team simulation training and incident reporting culture work

cycle2.result: Demonstrable improvement reported in treatment of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and in postpartum haemorrhage identification and treatment (no figures in abstract)

result.other_findings: Incident reporting rose only temporarily; team simulation training was hard to sustain.

result.topic: NEWS2 recording and escalation of deteriorating patients
result.setting: Five academic hospitals, Barts Health NHS Trust

cycle1.result: NEWS2 recording 64%

result.intervention: Real-time EHR-integrated dashboard of NEWS2 >5, assessment and escalation

cycle2.result: NEWS2 recording 83%; referrals increased from 170 to 6800 and assessment completion from 23 to 540

result.other_findings: Three nurses interviewed saw the dashboard as a facilitator for auditing NEWS2 recording and escalation.

result.topic: Blood pressure after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
result.setting: ICNARC Case Mix Programme database

cycle1.result: Hospital mortality 56.2%; lowest mortality with lowest MAP 60-63 mmHg and highest MAP 95-104 mmHg

result.other_findings: Both hypotension and hypertension in the first 24 h in ICU were associated with increased mortality.

result.setting: National Lung Cancer Audit Rapid Cancer Registration Datasets

cycle1.result: 26% reduction in incidence during the first national lockdown (adjusted IRR 0.74, 95% CI 0.71-0.78)

result.other_findings: Small cell lung cancer fell 45% (IRR 0.55); incidence later almost recovered without overcompensation (IRR 0.96).

result.setting: Major government secondary care hospital
result.standard: Local/international empirical and therapeutic antibiotic guidelines (ESAC audit tool)

cycle1.result: Compliance with local/international guidelines 78.0%; 54 antibiotics prescribed, 70.4% for treatment and 29.6% for prophylaxis

result.other_findings: 41 of 125 inpatients (32.8%) were on antibiotics; penicillin combinations were most common (31.5%), including amoxicillin-clavulanic acid 22.2%.

result.topic: STEMI care by heart failure status
result.setting: MINAP (UK) and JROAD-DPC (Japan) national databases

cycle1.result: pPCI in Killip 1, 2-3, 4: UK 79.6%, 58.2%, 79.9% vs Japan 86.2%, 81.7%, 78.7%; beta-blocker use Japan 61.4% vs UK 90.2%

result.other_findings: In-hospital mortality for Killip 2-3 was higher in the UK (15.8% vs 6.4%, CSRR 1.80); length of stay longer in Japan (17.0 vs 5.0 days).

result.setting: NHS memory clinics across the UK and Channel Islands (cross-sectional survey)

cycle1.result: 55% of responding clinics offered virtual CST during the pandemic; 45% offered no CST

result.other_findings: Of those offering vCST, 80% planned a hybrid model; barriers included digital poverty, limited digital literacy and staff time.

result.setting: Multiple psychiatric centres (Indian Psychiatric Society multicentre study)

cycle1.result: Alzheimer's disease 59.6%, vascular dementia 20%; 89.4% on dementia medication (donepezil 39.2%, donepezil-memantine 38.4%); 64.8% on antipsychotics (quetiapine 36.3%)

result.other_findings: 19.3% were on antidepressants and 13.7% on sedatives/hypnotics; 55.4% of patients and 65% of caregivers received psychosocial interventions.

result.setting: UK acute medical units (Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit 2021)

cycle1.result: 97/123 (78.9%) AMUs had access to at least one ultrasound machine; 81 (65.9%) had at least one clinician regularly using ultrasound

result.other_findings: Marked geographic variation in ultrasound use and availability of accredited supervisors, with expertise concentrated in a few hospitals per region.

result.topic: Antenatal care for hepatitis B positive women
result.setting: All maternity units in England (national audit)

cycle1.result: Antenatal care started at median 11.3 weeks, late (≥20 weeks) in 10% (251/2491); missed specialist appointments in 18% (426/2339)

result.other_findings: Late booking and missed appointments were commoner in women lacking basic English, recent arrivals, newly diagnosed, aged <25 or with ≥2 previous births.

result.setting: National Oesophago-Gastric Cancer Audit database, England and Wales

cycle1.result: 17 650 had radical surgery; later audit year associated with lower 30-day mortality (OR 0.93) and 90-day mortality (OR 0.94) and shorter stay (IRR 0.98)

result.other_findings: Stage at diagnosis showed little change over time; nodal yields and margin positivity improved.

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
result.setting: General practices in Ireland (point prevalence audit surveys, part of a European study)

cycle1.result: Antibiotics prescribed in 54% of RTI consultations

cycle2.result: Antibiotics prescribed in 21% of RTI consultations (23% in March-May 2020)

result.other_findings: 765 consultations in total; bronchitis and tonsillitis consultations led to antibiotics in 67% and 85%; point-of-care testing used in less than 1%. The fall in prescribing followed the COVID-19 pandemic, not a planned intervention.

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
result.setting: General practices in 13 European countries (point prevalence audit study)
result.standard: ESAC quality indicators, e.g. bronchitis in adults ≤30% antibiotics; acute upper RTI <20%; tonsillitis and sinusitis 0-20%; pneumonia in adults 90-100%

cycle1.result: Antibiotic prescribed in 30% of consultations; tonsillitis 69%; bronchitis indicator met only in Denmark and Spain

cycle2.result: Antibiotic prescribed in 16% of consultations; tonsillitis 75%, exceeding the indicator in all countries

result.other_findings: Upper RTI target met in most countries except Ireland (both surveys), Croatia (PPAS-1) and Greece (PPAS-4); pneumonia prescribing was below 90-100% in most countries.

result.setting: 45 NHS mental health trusts: acute adult wards/PICU and specialist addictions units (POMH audit)

cycle1.result: 908 patients on acute adult wards/PICU and 347 on specialist addictions units; addiction specialist oversight in 33 (4%) of acute ward patients

result.other_findings: Alcohol history, breath alcohol, Wernicke's screening, parenteral thiamine, relapse prevention and onward referral were all documented more often with specialist addictions care.

result.setting: 116 ICUs in a national Brazilian collaborative (Breakthrough Series model)

cycle1.result: Baseline incidence density of CLABSI, VAP and CA-UTI (figures not given in abstract)

result.intervention: Breakthrough Series quality improvement collaborative coaching staff in evidence-based, auditable care bundles and QI tools

cycle2.result: CLABSI fell 43.5%, VAP 52.1% and CA-UTI 65.8%; 5140 infections prevented

result.other_findings: Bundle adherence was inversely correlated with infection incidence (e.g. CLABSI maintenance bundle R = -0.85).

result.topic: Use of national audit feedback for falls improvement
result.setting: 7 of 85 hospitals in the National Audit of Inpatient Falls 2017

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews: staff valued benchmarking, visual data, case studies and recommendations

result.other_findings: Staffing, turnover and poor QI skills were barriers; leadership, ownership and communication were enablers.

result.setting: European radiology departments (ESR position paper, QuADRANT project)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Persisting variability in clinical audit uptake across Europe and lack of awareness of BSSD clinical audit requirements.

result.setting: Multicentre, Barts Health NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Preoperative vitamin D measured 40.3%; day-of-surgery calcium check 76.1%; hypocalcaemia detected in 26.8%

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary perioperative protocol for prevention, detection and management of post-thyroidectomy hypocalcaemia

cycle2.result: Preoperative vitamin D measured 65.2%; day-of-surgery calcium check 87.0%; hypocalcaemia detected in 30.43%; postoperative protocol followed in 78.3%

result.other_findings: Small numbers prevented analysis of the effect on length of stay.

result.setting: In-patient mental health units in England (survey and case series)

cycle1.result: Estimated 622 patients received NGT feeding under restraint; anorexia nervosa in 68.5-75.7%

result.other_findings: Age ranged 11-60 years (mean 19.02); duration varied from once to daily for 312 weeks (mean 29.1 weeks).

result.setting: European radiology, radiotherapy and nuclear medicine (QuADRANT study)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: National clinical audit infrastructure, resources and staff time are lacking in many countries; awareness of BSSD audit requirements varies.

result.setting: 29 institutions in Japan Clinical Oncology Group trials (virtual audit pilot)

cycle1.result: Mean ± SD gamma passing rate 99.4 ± 1.5% for films and 99.2 ± 1.0% for 21 array datasets

result.other_findings: Virtual audits were feasible and may be cheaper and faster than on-site or postal audits.

result.setting: General practices in England (National Cancer Diagnosis Audits)

cycle1.result: Same-day referral 37.7%; median diagnostic interval 40 days; ≥3 pre-referral consultations 26.2%

result.intervention: Publication of NICE 2015 guidance on referral for suspected cancer

cycle2.result: Same-day referral 42.7%; median diagnostic interval 36 days; ≥3 pre-referral consultations 18.8%

result.other_findings: Urgent referrals rose (54.8% vs 51.8%) and emergency referrals fell (13.4% vs 16.5%), but recorded safety netting decreased (40.0% vs 44.4%).

result.topic: Patient selection for pain management programmes
result.setting: INPUT Pain Management Unit, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust (specialty pain service)

cycle1.result: Most patients on the standard pathway were offered a PMP option

result.intervention: Introduction of virtual pain management programmes during the pandemic

cycle2.dates: Start of the pandemic, once virtual PMPs were delivered
cycle2.result: A greater proportion of patients were offered treatment than before the pandemic (figures not given in abstract)

result.other_findings: Psychosocial complexity and unwillingness to engage in a non-pain-reduction approach were the commonest reasons for not being offered a programme.

result.topic: Language development support after very preterm birth
result.setting: 10 Canadian neonatal follow-up programmes (EPIQ quality improvement)
result.standard: Feasibility targets: at least 70% of sites completing four intervention cycles and 75% of cycles meeting their aims

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Parent-integrated evidence-based interventions, online QI education tool, multidisciplinary teams including parents, virtual support for local audit over about 6-month cycles

cycle2.result: 8/10 sites completed at least four cycles; 41/48 (85%) cycles met their aim on audit

result.other_findings: COVID-19 was a barrier; parent involvement, champions and institutional support helped.

result.topic: Urinary tract infection management in primary care
result.setting: 12 general practices in England
result.standard: TARGET UTI audit toolkit and clinical diagnostic guidelines

cycle1.result: Antibiotics prescribed in 98% of cases; adherence to diagnostic guidelines lowest in females aged 65 years and over

result.other_findings: Symptoms were often insufficiently recorded and urinalysis and microbiology guidance poorly followed; men reported less UTI knowledge and longer waits for appointments.

result.topic: Blood test use before cancer diagnosis
result.setting: English National Cancer Diagnosis Audit

cycle1.result: Generic blood test use higher for nonspecific symptoms (fatigue 81%, loss of appetite 79%) and lower for alarm symptoms (breast lump 3%, skin lesion 1%)

result.other_findings: Test use was 64% for symptoms with PPV 2.00-2.99% versus 31% for PPV ≥5%; PSA was used in 88% of men presenting with lower urinary tract symptoms.

result.setting: International expert panel, JPIAMR-PAAN (modified Delphi)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Produced 13 best practice statements for peer comparison audit and feedback on antibiotic prescribing in primary care.

result.topic: Maternal and neonatal quality improvement programme implementation
result.setting: 15 of 21 public health facilities in the Mphatlalatsane programme

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Qualitative evaluation: uptake depended on leaders' motivation, pre-COVID QI training and experienced QI advisors; teams adapted methods during COVID-19.

result.setting: Acute Medicine, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: European Society of Cardiology criteria for iron deficiency in heart failure

cycle1.result: 82/111 (74%) had iron status checked; 52/82 (63%) iron deficient; 34/52 (65%) received iron replacement

result.other_findings: 54% of iron-deficient patients were anaemic; mean stay 13.8 days with iron deficiency versus 11.2 days without.

result.setting: General Surgery, Tameside and Glossop Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Pre-operative haemoglobin >12 g/dL; group and save on admission

cycle1.result: 15/70 (21%) had haemoglobin <12 g/dL; 63 (90%) had group and save on admission

result.intervention: Flowchart poster distribution and addition to the surgical proforma

cycle2.result: 5 (11%) had haemoglobin <12 g/dL; 44 (97%) had group and save on admission

result.other_findings: ASA grade was also collected.

result.topic: Inflammatory bowel disease key performance indicators
result.setting: UK gastroenterology services (Delphi consensus)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Four KPIs agreed: referral to diagnosis time, time to treatment recommendation, appropriate steroid use and advanced therapy prescreening; >85% agreed local adoption was feasible.

result.topic: CT-guided radiofrequency ablation of osteoid osteoma
result.setting: Major orthopaedic centre, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust

cycle1.result: Primary clinical success 37/47 (78.7%); secondary success 83.0%

result.other_findings: Complication rate 4% (one third-degree skin burn); mean treatment delay 6.9 months; no predictors of failure found.

result.setting: Paediatric inpatient and emergency departments, London Health Sciences Centre Children's Hospital
result.standard: Wound swab success rate of 95% by May 2022

cycle1.result: Wound swab success 88.9% (ear and eye 100%, MRSA 98.1%)

result.intervention: Visual aids added to the electronic laboratory test information guide and visual reminders of correct collection equipment in high-traffic areas
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Potentially inappropriate medication prescribing in older adults
result.setting: Four Veterans Affairs emergency departments (EQUIPPED dashboard)

cycle1.result: 40/82 (48.7%) providers viewed the audit and feedback dashboard at least once

result.other_findings: Providers with a higher baseline PIM prescribing rate were more likely to use the dashboard (OR 1.22).

result.setting: Stata software tool (King's College London)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes a Stata command for standardised analysis of matched case-control audits of cervical cancer screening.

result.setting: Magrabi ICO Cameroon Eye Institute (subspecialty eye hospital)

cycle1.result: Mean waiting time 450 (SD 96.6) minutes; satisfied with waiting time 8/25 (32%)

result.intervention: PDSA cycles over 6 weeks with real-time tracking of waiting, service and idling times using Open Data Kit

cycle2.result: Waiting time reduced by 66 minutes (15%, P=.05); satisfaction 8/24 (33%, P=.92)

result.other_findings: No significant association between waiting time and satisfaction; pre-intervention mean service time 112 and idling time 338 minutes.

result.topic: Reasons for blood testing in primary care
result.setting: 57 general practices across England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland (PACT)

cycle1.result: Reasons: symptoms 43.2%, disease monitoring 30.1%, medication monitoring 10.1%; about one-quarter of tests judged partially or fully unnecessary

result.other_findings: 26.6% of patients had completely normal results; 6.2% of tests led to a new or confirmed diagnosis.

result.setting: Acute hospitals in Ireland receiving Irish National Audit of Dementia feedback (co-design and feasibility study)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: The adapted collaborative produced a positive response and was seen as appropriate; adaptation was needed for differences in strategy, ways of working and hospital social structures.

result.setting: Key informant interviews with thought leaders in climate-conscious pharmacy

cycle1.result: A self-assessment audit instrument was identified as a first step for climate-conscious community pharmacy practice

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Large London hospital (Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Care bundle within 24 hours of admission: NT-proBNP test, transthoracic echocardiography and specialist cardiology review

cycle1.result: NT-proBNP testing 162/163 (99.4%); echocardiography 84.7%; specialist input 51.6%

result.intervention: Heart failure admission care bundle implemented using the SHIFT-Evidence quality improvement approach (July 2015 to July 2017)
result.other_findings: Interrupted time series of 15 618 admissions showed reduced 7-90 day readmissions (slope ratio 0.98) and in-hospital mortality (0.96), with no change in length of stay.

result.topic: Inclusion of under-served groups in clinical trials
result.setting: Clinical Trials and Statistics Unit, The Institute of Cancer Research, London
result.standard: NIHR INCLUDE guidance on under-served groups

cycle1.result: Age, ethnicity and health status well collected and no upper age limits; 23/30 (77%) information sheets used gendered terms; median reading age 15-16 years

result.other_findings: Most case report forms did not specify sex or gender and offered only male or female; socio-economic factors were not routinely collected.

result.setting: English National Cancer Diagnosis Audit 2018

cycle1.result: Across 38 cancer sites and 83 symptoms, cancers grouped by dominant single symptom, diverse symptoms or asymptomatic detection

result.other_findings: Symptom case-mix of cancer sites varied by sex.

result.setting: UK hospitals in the Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit 2022
result.standard: National peer review measures for acute oncology services

cycle1.result: 120 hospitals (91.6%) had an AOS, with many failing to meet peer-review measures; 542 (7.6%) admissions were cancer-related

result.other_findings: Cancer-related admissions had higher acuity, longer stays and higher 14-day mortality (adjusted OR 3.54).

result.topic: Mortality risk prediction in emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Retrospective cohort of emergency laparotomies

cycle1.result: AUC for 30-day mortality HAS 0.97 vs NELA 0.86 (p < 0.0001)

result.other_findings: HAS was well calibrated while the NELA score was poorly calibrated (p = 0.001).

result.topic: Audit and feedback to reduce clinical variation
result.setting: State-wide value-based healthcare programme, New South Wales

cycle1.result: Realist interview study identifying eight mechanisms by which audit and feedback worked or failed

result.other_findings: Audit and feedback worked with clinician ownership, understandable data, social influence and accountability; it failed with perceived unfairness, data integrity concerns and threats to autonomy.

result.setting: Emergency department of a tertiary-care hospital
result.standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign hour-1 care bundle

cycle1.result: Hour-1 bundle compliance 0%

result.intervention: Multi-tiered education, adult sepsis screening tool and hour-1 bundle checklist, hospital protocols and empirical antibiotic guidelines, via PDSA cycles
result.other_findings: Guideline-concordant antimicrobial therapy increased (p < 0.05), but length of stay, ICU stay and mortality did not change significantly.

result.topic: National clinical audit of MI, trauma, sepsis and stroke
result.setting: 16 Ministry of Health hospitals
result.standard: 52 clinical care standards for acute myocardial infarction, major trauma, sepsis and stroke developed by clinical expert groups

cycle1.result: 84 measures of compliance with 52 standards (baseline figures not given in abstract)

result.intervention: Workshops on the standards and findings, multiprofessional hospital teams implementing improvement plans after the first round

cycle2.result: Improvement in 58/84 (69.1%) measures; statistically significant in 34 (40.5%)

result.other_findings: All designated hospitals submitted two rounds of data, which were independently reliability tested.

result.topic: Violence and aggression on mental health wards
result.setting: Male acute mental health ward, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Aim to reduce violence and aggression incidents by 20% over 4 months

cycle1.result: Mean 2.5 incidents per week (average 21.3 per month in the preceding 6 months)

result.intervention: Safewards bundle (training package, weekly emails, noticeboard displays) and safety crosses on the ward via PDSA cycles

cycle2.result: Mean 2.0 incidents per week, a 20% reduction, but no special cause variation

result.other_findings: Safety crosses had no effect; safewards interventions recorded and staff safety ratings improved; incidents correlated with restrictive practice rates.

result.setting: NHS Grampian public health
result.standard: 2018 Scottish TB Framework key performance indicator of 85% uptake

cycle1.dates: Infants born 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2021 (reviewed November 2022 to February 2023)
cycle1.result: Uptake 93% in 2019, 89% in 2020 and 93% in 2021, above the 85% target

result.other_findings: Uptake improved compared with earlier rates of 86% in 2012 and 90% in 2013; 2060 of 16 078 live births were eligible.

result.setting: Local health district, Central Coast, New South Wales (hospital and other settings)

cycle1.result: Fewer than 1 in 5 had advance care directives or plans; less than half coded as receiving palliative care at death; more than 2 in 3 had no specialist palliative care

result.other_findings: Almost half of those dying in hospital had an investigation in their final 72 hours; 705 people were identified, with 299 randomly selected for manual audit.

result.topic: Antimicrobial prophylaxis in normothermic liver perfusion
result.setting: Roy Calne Transplant Unit, Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 4 significant microorganisms grown (3 Candida species, 1 Enterococcus faecium) in perfusates with fluconazole and meropenem prophylaxis

result.other_findings: Fluconazole levels stayed stable (median 24.9 to 22.6 mg/L) while meropenem fell (21.8 to 9.4 mg/L) over 10 h; Candida-infected livers were transplanted without adverse consequences.

result.setting: Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust (district general hospital)
result.standard: NICE and British Benign Upper Gastrointestinal Surgery Society recommendations for early emergency surgery

cycle1.result: 32/48 (66.7%) had surgery within seven days of diagnosis; 24 (50%) had no adverse intraoperative event

result.other_findings: No biliary tract injury despite many difficult cases; no correlation between time to surgery and difficulty or readmission.

result.topic: Red eye consultation red flag documentation
result.setting: Primary care practice
result.standard: NICE Clinical Knowledge Summary red flag features for acute red eye consultations

cycle1.result: Headache asked 14% (3/21); pupil changes 5% (1/19); high-velocity injury 10% (2/21); foreign body 14% (3/21); chemical 10% (2/21); photophobia 14% (3/19); lateralisation 90% (19/21); visual changes 71% (15/21); eye pain 67% (14/21).

result.intervention: Red eye consultation template created in EMIS and a teaching session for doctors on red flag features and sight-threatening conditions.

cycle2.result: Headache 74% (14/19); pupil changes 58% (11/19); high-velocity injury 84% (16/19); foreign body 84% (16/19); chemical 84% (16/19); photophobia 79% (15/19) (all p<0.05); lateralisation 100% (19/19); visual changes 84% (16/19); eye pain 79% (15/19).

result.other_findings: Lateralisation, visual changes and eye pain were already often asked and did not change significantly.

result.setting: St. Francis' Hospital, Katete District, general radiography
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists guidelines: all designated variables completed on the radiology request form

cycle1.result: 881 (90.5%) forms incompletely filled; hospital number missing on 597 (61.3%), clinical history missing on 449 (46.2%), urgency missing on 336 (37%), referring department missing on 472 (48.5%).

result.other_findings: Patient name, age, gender and requested examination were almost always completed (under 1% missing).

result.topic: Routine enquiry about trauma in mental health assessment
result.setting: Three Community Mental Health Teams in North-East Glasgow
result.standard: Routine sensitive enquiry of adult interpersonal trauma documented in the Initial Assessment Tool

cycle1.result: 57% of 90 Initial Assessment Tools had evidence of routine sensitive enquiry; of 51 with enquiry, 61% used it to inform risk assessment and 14% documented signposting to support organisations.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest supporting staff in how to ask questions and use disclosures in treatment planning.

result.topic: Ambulatory serratus plane catheter after mastectomy
result.setting: Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust breast surgery service

cycle1.result: Mean pain NRS at rest/movement 1.88/2.56 on POD1; mean satisfaction 9.25/10; day-case rate 66% for mastectomy and 39% with reconstruction.

result.other_findings: Service evaluation; six patients needed opioids on POD1 and none on POD3; minor catheter issues in four patients.

result.topic: Stroke after cardiac surgery risk factors
result.setting: UK National Adult Cardiac Surgical Audit database

cycle1.result: Risk factor analysis: extracardiac arteriopathy OR 1.70, previous stroke OR 1.71, insulin-treated diabetes OR 1.37; thoracic aortic surgery crude OR 3.72.

result.other_findings: Registry outcome and association study, not measured against a standard.

result.topic: Patient experience of prostate cancer care
result.setting: National Prostate Cancer Audit patient-reported experience survey

cycle1.result: Men aged 80+ less likely to feel their views were considered (RR 0.79); black (RR 0.89) and Asian (RR 0.85) men less likely to feel involved in decisions.

result.other_findings: Cross-sectional survey analysis of variation in experience by age, ethnicity and deprivation.

result.setting: UK-wide gynaecology services (national audit)
result.standard: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 67 (2016) on management of endometrial hyperplasia

cycle1.result: Before guidance: 9% with non-atypical hyperplasia had no initial treatment; 31% received intrauterine progestogen; 68% with atypical hyperplasia had first-line hysterectomy; 38% of NEH followed to regression by 2 years.

result.intervention: Publication of national guidance (Green-top Guideline No. 67, 2016).

cycle2.result: After guidance: 3% with NEH had no initial treatment; 48% received intrauterine progestogen; 67% with AEH had first-line hysterectomy; 52% of NEH followed to regression by 2 years (RR 1.38).

result.other_findings: Total 3,307 women across both periods. Follow-up of women with atypical hyperplasia not undergoing hysterectomy needs improvement.

result.setting: Guy's and St Thomas' specialist menopause clinic, teaching hospital
result.standard: NICE guidance: 11 criteria for GP referral to menopause specialists

cycle1.result: 76% of referrals met NICE guidelines.

result.other_findings: One-sixth of referrals could have been prevented or managed through other routes; waiting time for first appointment up to 1 year.

result.setting: Dorset County Hospital NHS Foundation Trust

result.standard: INCLUDE guidance on under-served groups and protected characteristics in the UK Equality Act 2010

cycle1.result: Common exclusions: age (19), severity of illness (17), capacity to consent (14), sex or gender (11), pregnancy (11), multiple conditions (10), language (8); data collected on age (19), ethnicity (16), sex or gender (15), education (11).

result.other_findings: 21 protocols, 29 patient information sheets and 40 data collection tools reviewed; many exclusions (under 18s, non-fluent English speakers, lack of capacity) may not have been essential.

result.topic: Intraoperative pain during caesarean birth under neuraxial anaesthesia
result.setting: Participating hospitals in the UK and Queensland, Australia (SONAR1 protocol)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Study protocol for a 1-week prospective observational cohort; no results reported.

result.topic: HbA1c assessment and deintensification in diabetes and frailty
result.setting: Medical wards, University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Baseline audit showed low rates of inpatient HbA1c assessment and medication deintensification (figures not given in abstract).

result.intervention: Infographic to aid assessment and deintensification, awareness of baseline results via email and WhatsApp groups for resident doctors, then 'Diafrailty Champion' allocated to medical wards.

cycle2.result: Improvements in HbA1c assessment and deintensification after interventions 1 and 2 (n = 102) persisted after the Diafrailty Champion audit (n = 92); figures not given in abstract.

result.other_findings: Three audits in total, 291 patients with diabetes and moderate-severe frailty.

result.setting: All eight radiotherapy centres in Denmark

cycle1.result: 3163 received retreatment, including 1471 reirradiation courses (1035 palliative; 436 curative/ablative).

result.other_findings: Large variation in reirradiation dose and fractionation; numbers increased from 2014 to 2023.

result.topic: Laboratory quality management for antimicrobial resistance testing
result.setting: National AMR reference laboratories in South and Southeast Asia (EQASIA programme)
result.standard: External quality assessment and quality management system practices

cycle1.result: 38% lacked a quality management system, 42% did no internal audits, 50% did no competency assessments, 46% did no root cause analysis for EQA deviations and 42% lacked structured quality control.

result.intervention: Online consultations for root cause analysis and corrective and preventive actions, plus onsite visits and targeted training for persistently underperforming laboratories.

cycle2.result: Improvements observed in quality management system implementation, SOP development, staff training and quality control (no figures given).

result.other_findings: Of four baseline-assessed laboratories, three underperformed twice and one three times across EQA rounds.

result.topic: Low-value diagnostic testing in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency departments across Australia and New Zealand (clinician survey)

cycle1.result: Tests seen as high risk of unwarranted variation or low value: D-dimer (42%), venous blood gas (39%), CRP (35%), abdominal x-ray (35%).

result.other_findings: Doctors rated CRP, urine drug screens and abdominal x-rays higher risk than nurses.

result.setting: 62 mental health trusts (Prescribing Observatory for Mental Health quality improvement programme)

cycle1.result: 951 episodes of acutely disturbed behaviour in patients with personality disorder; 782 (82%) in female patients; personality disorder was the sole diagnosis in 471 (50%).

result.other_findings: Episodes in females were three times more likely to involve self-harm and regularly prompted rapid tranquillisation.

result.topic: Urinary tract infection length of stay
result.setting: Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust, emergency department focus

cycle1.result: Audit linked urine sample errors or samples not sent with prolonged length of stay.

result.intervention: Improved urine sample labelling, easier sample collection, raised awareness of SDEC and a direct triage-to-SDEC pathway.

cycle2.result: White-topped urine sample errors fell by 50%; approximate saving of 10 bed days per month.

result.other_findings: No significant increase in samples sent; urology SDEC use increased marginally; bed day reduction could not be linked to individual changes.

result.topic: Practice data dashboards for antibiotic prescribing
result.setting: Irish general practice (CARA project)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Qualitative design study developing a dashboard with automated audit reports and between-practice comparisons.

result.setting: Tertiary neurosurgical centre (King's College Hospital)

cycle1.result: 210 (66.5%) started on steroids at baseline but only 6% had a documented weaning plan; MDT referral in 252 (79.7%).

result.other_findings: Steroid use over 2 weeks (OR 3.5) and no MDT steroid plan (OR 4.2) predicted complications.

result.setting: Emergency Assessment Unit, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust (tertiary hospital)
result.standard: Guidelines on oxygen prescribing at admission clerking

cycle1.result: 45% (45) prescribed oxygen at initial clerking and 26% (26) later; 29 (29%) never had a documented prescription; 8/19 (42%) COPD patients never prescribed oxygen.

result.other_findings: Errors in 4 (9%) prescriptions; out-of-hours admissions had higher omission rates; 9/11 (82%) junior doctors lacked formal training.

result.setting: Nine adult wards, Bon Secours Hospital, Cork
result.standard: NICE guidelines on VTE risk assessment and prophylaxis

cycle1.result: Alarmingly low compliance with the VTE prophylaxis protocol (no figures given).

result.intervention: Enforced protocol adherence, reporting of incomplete or inaccurate assessments and targeted multidisciplinary staff education.

cycle2.result: Assessment completion with accurate prescription 111/127 (87.39%); assessment within 24 hours 101 (79.52%); 16 (12.64%) unassessed; 22 (17.32%) high-risk patients had no prophylaxis.

result.other_findings: Mechanical prophylaxis used in only 15 (11.81%); electronic prompts suggested.

result.setting: District general hospital (Surrey and Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust)
result.standard: NICE NG118 and GIRFT recommendations for acute ureteric stones

cycle1.result: CT KUB within 24 hours 98%; urgent intervention within 48 hours 35%; non-indicated stent placement 83%; lost stent follow-up 2 patients; hot clinic follow-up loss 16 patients.

result.intervention: Primary ureteroscopy and day-case ESWL pathway, electronic stent recall protocol, Cerner auto-text discharge summaries, posters, presentations and clinician education.

cycle2.result: CT KUB within 24 hours 100%; urgent intervention within 48 hours 53% (p=0.028); non-indicated stents 57% (p=0.001); lost stent follow-up 0 (p=0.042); hot clinic follow-up loss 1 patient.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest adding the MIMIC score to CT reporting.

result.setting: Community paediatric developmental assessment service, South Western Sydney Local Health District
result.standard: 'F-words for Child Development' framework (Function, Family, Fitness, Fun, Friends)

cycle1.result: Child's strengths documented at start of report 74% (n=65); at least 4 of 5 F-words domains documented 8% (n=7).

cycle2.result: Strengths documented at start 95% (n=106); at least 4 of 5 domains 85% (n=95).

result.other_findings: Clinicians (n=21) and families (n=18) rated the framework positively; none rated it unhelpful.

result.setting: Paediatric intensive care unit, tertiary referral hospital in England

cycle1.result: Weekly cleaning audits identified cleaning 'hotspots' (no figures given).

result.intervention: Co-created opportunistic and targeted one-to-one education and training for clinical staff, delivered by infection prevention link nurses and a clinical auditor/educator, with monthly PDSA review.

cycle2.result: Interventions built and maintained excellent cleaning standards (no figures given).

result.other_findings: Training gaps in mandatory study days and cascade to new starters were key themes.

result.setting: District general hospital in the West Midlands (South Warwickshire University NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: 84 (39%) had a pelvic drain; mean stay 5.2 days with drains vs 2.7 days without; readmission 13% with drains vs 52% without; collections 6 (7%) vs 27 (20%).

result.other_findings: Histology showed normal appendix in 8 (3.7%) and adenocarcinoma in 2 (0.9%).

result.setting: General Surgery Department, Managil Teaching Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidance (18 parameters)

cycle1.result: Tissue details 25 (49%); prostheses 20 (39.2%); postoperative instructions 40 (78.4%); complications 15 (29.4%); extra procedures 10 (19.6%); blood loss 10 (19.6%); DVT prophylaxis 15 (29.4%).

cycle2.result: Tissue details 42 (84%); prostheses 38 (76%); postoperative instructions 45 (90%); complications 35 (70%); extra procedures 30 (60%); blood loss 25 (50%); DVT prophylaxis 30 (60%).

result.other_findings: Anticipated blood loss and DVT prophylaxis documentation remained poor.

result.topic: Dermatological presentations in the emergency department
result.setting: Adult emergency department, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham (tertiary centre)
result.standard: NICE and British Association of Dermatologists guidelines

cycle1.result: Dermatology follow-up in only 6.3%; 37.5% had no documented follow-up; 21 (26.3%) admitted; drug history documentation inconsistent.

result.other_findings: Over 85% of parameters improved significantly; complex histories and discharge procedures still need attention.

result.topic: Septal button insertion for septal perforation
result.setting: Tertiary centre, University Hospitals Plymouth NHS Trust

cycle1.result: No further intervention in 39/77 (50.6%); single replacement 20/77 (26.0%); multiple replacements 4/77 (5.2%); removal 12/77 (15.6%).

result.topic: Patient-reported measures for dental quality improvement
result.setting: UK dental practices (deliberative stakeholder consultation)

result.setting: 21 primary care practices (Achieving Clinical Audits with Electronic Records programme, OPCRD Australia)

cycle2.result: Exacerbation rates fell to 32.4 (asthma) and 91.2 (COPD) per 1000 per month; 48.4% (asthma) and 59.3% (COPD) had a maintenance therapy change in the first year.

result.setting: Training course for non-ophthalmologist healthcare providers in Malawi

Reports: osteitis/bone marrow oedema 81.0%, erosions 58.8%, fat metaplasia 6.3%, active inflammation 77.8%, structural changes 51.2%, overall axSpA statement 62.0% (n = 98).
