result.setting: NICU, Aga Khan University, Karachi (high-volume)

cycle1.result: 13 (12.6%) developed sepsis; only two had growth on POD 0 or 1; blood culture sensitivity rose after POD 2; CRP AUROC 0.55.

result.other_findings: Routine immediate post-operative blood cultures and CRP judged of little value.

result.topic: Developmental referral concerns and autism diagnosis
result.setting: Nepean Hospital Child Development Clinic (tertiary paediatric developmental service), New South Wales

cycle1.result: 51% referred for ASD were diagnosed with ASD and 57% referred for developmental concerns were diagnosed with GDD; speech delay was the only referral concern associated with ASD (p = 0.002).

result.other_findings: Speech delay (80%) and social interaction concerns (78%) were the most frequent referral issues.

result.setting: Four wards of a rural hospital (Bowral & District Hospital), New South Wales
result.standard: Delirium assessment and communication practices for eligible patients, benchmark 85%

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: 4Es implementation model with a three-module nurse education programme (face to face, self-directed online, OSCE) rolled out ward by ward every 2 months

cycle2.result: Six key delirium practices reached and remained at the 85% benchmark over the study and for three months after; 378 patient notes audited across 7 audits.

result.other_findings: Nurse knowledge scores unchanged (T0 16.62, T1 17.07, T2 17.67) but self-efficacy improved significantly between T0 and T2.

result.setting: Metropolitan emergency department, Sydney Children's Hospital Network (Fairfield Hospital)
result.standard: Sydney Children's Hospital Network Asthma-Acute Management Practice Guideline

cycle1.result: Severity documentation incomplete (speech 78%, cyanosis 69%); chest X-ray in 34.6%; mean bronchodilator burst longer than recommended (salbutamol 46.7 min, ipratropium 47.7 min); systemic steroids in 92% with appropriate dose in 63%; IV magnesium in 8/27 (29.6%) severe or life-threatening cases.

result.other_findings: 56 (36.6%) admitted; mean ED stay 6.5 h admitted vs 4.3 h discharged.

result.topic: Language assessment in foetal alcohol spectrum disorder
result.setting: UK National FASD Clinic, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Significant correlations between all CELF domains and CCC Semantics, Coherence and GCC; no correlation between CCC Speech and CELF; mixed correlations between VABS and CELF.

result.other_findings: Sample size varied from 77 to 274 by measure.

result.setting: Australian general practice (co-design study)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Intervention development only: seven activities including education, geriatrician drop-in sessions, auditing and benchmarking and a dementia risk alert tool.

result.setting: Ophthalmology-led thyroid eye disease clinic, Queens Hospital, Romford
result.standard: Evidence-based recommendations for glucose and HbA1c monitoring during systemic glucocorticoid therapy

cycle1.result: Baseline fasting glucose before steroids documented in 12/29 (41.4%); follow-up fasting glucose after steroids in 5/29 (17.2%).

result.other_findings: 221 TED patients overall; 29 (13.1%) received systemic steroids, 4 (13.8%) with pre-existing diabetes. A one-stop TED clinic was recommended.

result.topic: Advanced heart failure referral for transplant or LVAD
result.setting: Seven adult heart transplant centres across the UK and Ireland (national audit)

cycle1.result: About 100 referrals per month for transplant or LVAD assessment; age-adjusted referral rates varied significantly by region; women made up only one in three patients assessed.

result.other_findings: Distance to transplant centre and postcode deprivation did not affect referral likelihood; many referred patients had contraindications.

result.setting: Ten radiotherapy physics centres (multicentre audit)
result.standard: Vendor reference water tissue phantom ratio data for 6 MV beams

cycle1.result: Mean dimensional error -0.2 ± 0.3 mm; CT numbers and densities varied by up to 200 HU and 0.20 g/cm3 between centres; water-equivalent thickness varied by up to 3.0 mm and TPR by up to 1.2%.

result.other_findings: Water-equivalent CT density achieved at infill 94.5 ± 3.5% and density 1.10 ± 0.03 g/cm3.

result.setting: Cardiothoracic Critical Care Unit, Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: International guidelines and local policy: hourly documentation of the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale

cycle1.result: 75% (n = 57) of nurse RASS assessments accurate against expert rating; only 33% (n = 25) documented hourly as required.

result.other_findings: Greater experience linked to accuracy; deeper sedation and higher self-reported confidence linked to poorer agreement and documentation respectively.

result.setting: NHS medical retina service, Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Mean BCVA 58.1 letters at baseline, 59.7 at <6 months, 56.9 at 12 months and 54.4 at 24 months (-3.7); CMT reduced by 45.7 µm at 24 months; injection interval extended from 7.88 to 10.67 weeks.

result.other_findings: No intraocular inflammation, retinal vasculitis or endophthalmitis.

result.setting: 1505 phase II cardiac rehabilitation programmes in 90 countries (Global CR Audit survey)

cycle1.result: Median 8 of 10 core components offered per programme (IQR 6-10); upper-middle income countries median 9; high-income vs low-income 8 vs 6.

result.other_findings: Compared with the 2016 Global CR Audit; resource availability differed by country income class.

result.setting: Paediatric intensive care unit, Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: National guidelines (Advanced Paediatric Life Support) for convulsive status epilepticus

cycle1.result: Of 19 transferred by ambulance, 6 (32%) had pre-hospital treatment, only one with correct rectal diazepam dose; mean seizure onset to first drug 81 min (range 30-265) without pre-hospital treatment; APLS guidance strictly followed in ED in 10/26 (38%); 9/36 (25%) benzodiazepine doses too low; guideline drug sequence not followed in 9/26 (35%).

result.other_findings: 7/26 (27%) received more than two benzodiazepine doses and 21 (81%) were intubated and ventilated.

result.topic: Infectious disease screening in unaccompanied asylum-seeking children
result.setting: Single South-East UK local authority spanning two trusts, one with a one-stop clinic (Sussex Community NHS Foundation Trust, Looked After Children service)
result.standard: RCPCH guidance on infectious disease screening for unaccompanied asylum-seeking children

cycle1.result: TB and blood-borne virus testing had high referral and attendance rates; gaps in schistosomiasis and strongyloidiasis testing (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Appointment completion varied across ID services and was low for children placed out of area.

result.topic: Mainstream genetic testing in breast cancer
result.setting: High-volume breast unit, Royal United Hospital, Bath
result.standard: UK National Test Directory criteria R208 and R444.1 for mainstream genetic testing

cycle1.result: 255 of 1812 new diagnoses eligible for testing and 196 consented; 28 (14.3%) had a pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant, 8 eligible only on family history criteria.

result.intervention: Implementation of mainstream genetic testing using R208/R444.1 eligibility
result.other_findings: Positive results changed surgical decisions for 14 women and 3 received a PARP inhibitor; eligibility assessment was time-consuming.

result.topic: Male breast cancer treatment and survival
result.setting: National Audit of Primary Breast Cancer, England and Wales (population-based cohort)

cycle1.result: 2463 men vs 337,701 women; men with ER-positive early breast cancer less often had neoadjuvant chemotherapy (aOR 0.63) and more often post-mastectomy radiotherapy for intermediate and low-risk disease (aOR 1.28 and 2.61); breast cancer-specific death 3.6% vs 4.6%.

result.other_findings: Death from other causes higher in men (12.0% vs 7.7%).

result.topic: Unintended weight loss and early cancer detection
result.setting: Five primary care practices (clinical decision support pilot), Victoria

cycle1.result: 36/60 (60%) flagged patients had true unintended weight loss; 5/36 (14%) actively recalled; 34/36 (94%) had follow-up care by 6 months.

result.intervention: Clinical decision support system flagging unintended weight loss
result.other_findings: Weight-loss intention recorded as free text in 98% but in a structured field in only 20%.

result.setting: 41 radiotherapy centres (national end-to-end dosimetry audit, National Radiotherapy Trials Quality Assurance Group)
result.standard: National guidance for spinal SBRT planning

cycle1.result: Mean PTV dose difference 1.2% [-6.5-8.5%] with alanine and 1.0% [-7.0-8.5%] with film; mean distance to agreement 0.82 mm and centre of dose difference 0.78 mm.

result.other_findings: Dose reporting mode had a statistically significant effect on measured vs calculated dose.

result.setting: Seven sites (10 ICUs) in the Indian Registry for IntenSive care network

cycle1.result: MUSIQ 2.0 readiness scores 118-160 at first assessment and 114-147 at second.

result.other_findings: Themes: cognitive bias, leadership and team dynamics, registry usability and support, and resources and staffing; audit and feedback meetings were the central mechanism.

result.setting: General Surgery and Neurosurgery units, Obafemi Awolowo University Teaching Hospitals Complex, Ife
result.standard: Discharge summary completion of at least 50% within 12 weeks

cycle1.result: Completion 0% (0/56) General Surgery, 33% (7/21) Neurosurgery, overall 9% (7/77).

result.intervention: Discharge summary training at induction, prestructured templates, visual management tools and unit-based champions, tested in PDSA cycles

cycle2.result: Completion 82% (68/83), reaching 100% in some cycles (χ2 = 85.35, p<0.0001); median completion 93.4% General Surgery and 100% Neurosurgery.

result.other_findings: Baseline survey identified poor knowledge and no standard template as barriers.

result.setting: Maternity units at St Thomas' Hospital, London and Royal Berkshire Hospital, Reading
result.standard: National guidance on placental histopathology referral criteria

cycle1.result: St Thomas': 80% of eligible preterm deliveries had placental examination. Royal Berkshire: submission 88% for intrauterine deaths and 71% for very preterm births.

result.intervention: Labour ward fridges for 48-hour placental storage with temperature monitoring, targeted education on indications, and daily cross-checking of neonatal admissions (PDSA cycles)

cycle2.result: Royal Berkshire: 97% for intrauterine deaths and 100% for very preterm births. St Thomas': preterm submissions 96% after education and 98% after storage; intrauterine death 100%.

result.other_findings: Missing histology in national investigation reports at St Thomas' fell from 12% to 0%.

result.topic: Anastomotic leak reporting in national registries
result.setting: International survey of national surgical registries in 38 countries
result.standard: 79 CoReAL (Consensus for Reporting of colorectal Anastomotic Leaks) variables

cycle1.result: 7 countries (18.4%) had national registries capturing post-operative outcomes; median 28 variables registered (range 18-37); median 11/25 preoperative, 6/16 intraoperative, 8/16 early post-operative and 2/22 long-term elements.

result.other_findings: Substantial heterogeneity, especially beyond 30 days.

result.setting: University Hospital, Nottingham
result.standard: Published survival data used as a benchmark

cycle1.result: Immediate survival 43% of cardiorespiratory arrests; 70% of immediate survivors alive at 24 h and 69% at six weeks or beyond; survival 71% from VF, 20% asystole, 9% EMD.

result.other_findings: Need to improve switchboard telephone connections, modify equipment and improve knowledge of hospital geography; training emphasis to change.

result.setting: Coronary care unit, Royal Hallamshire Hospital, Sheffield (teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: 212/335 (63%) received thrombolysis; withheld inappropriately in 8 cases and given inappropriately in 2; inpatient mortality 12% with vs 26% without thrombolysis (p < 0.005).

result.other_findings: Streptokinase stopped in 5 (4%) for allergy or arrhythmia; guideline adjustment suggested.

result.setting: 24 district health authorities and health boards in England, Wales and Scotland (case-control)

cycle1.result: Cases would have been 57% (95% CI 28-86%) greater without screening; 47% of stage 1B+ cases under 70 adequately screened vs 75% of controls.

result.other_findings: 13% of patients under 70 had histories indicating inadequate follow-up of smears needing colposcopy.

result.setting: Single district laboratory, one health district (University of Nottingham)

cycle1.result: Of 109 incident cases without non-GI cause, 19% had upper and lower GI investigation, 21% upper only, 7% lower only; 55 had no investigation or only faecal occult blood tests.

result.other_findings: At 18 months nine colorectal cancers, five gastric cancers and 11 peptic ulcers diagnosed; two deaths from colorectal cancers missed at presentation.

result.setting: Department of Child Health, University of Wales College of Medicine, Cardiff
result.standard: Departmental aims and objectives for the child health attachment

cycle1.result: 45.4% of students completed the questionnaire; 32% received less than 1 hour per week of protected teaching; 54% did not visit casualty.

result.other_findings: Experiences generally satisfactory and covered a wide range of common childhood disorders.

result.setting: 42 hospitals with 400 or more acute beds (national audit)
result.standard: Guidelines and standards suggested by a multidisciplinary working group on communication, referral appropriateness, finding beds, waiting and organisation of clinical care

cycle1.result: Main problems: suboptimal consultant involvement in acute care, frequent mismatch of admitting specialty to condition, and confusion about admission policies for elderly patients.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Myelosuppression with temozolomide chemoradiotherapy in glioblastoma
result.setting: The Christie NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: During adjuvant therapy (n = 76): platelets <=100 31.6% and <=50 3.9%; neutrophils <=1.0 2.6% and <=0.5 0%; lymphocytes <=0.8 65.8% and <=0.5 40.8%; haemoglobin <=100 1.3%.

result.other_findings: Compared with Stupp trial data, thrombocytopenia and neutropenia were higher in the concurrent phase but equivalent or lower in the adjuvant phase; 12 platelet transfusions and one neutropenic sepsis.

result.topic: Stereotactic radiosurgery for brain metastases outcomes
result.setting: Guy's Cancer Centre, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, London

cycle1.result: 122 lesions treated; local failure at 9 months in 26 (21.3%) sites; median overall survival 9.2 months and progression-free survival 5.9 months.

result.other_findings: Local control correlated with randomised trial results.

result.topic: Chlamydia result notification and GUM referral
result.setting: Family planning service and genitourinary medicine service, St Mary's Hospital, Portsmouth
result.standard: All women having termination of pregnancy or IUD fitting offered chlamydia screening, informed of positive results and referred to GUM

cycle1.result: 999 offered a test and 988 tested; 38 positive (3.8%); result documented as given in 27/38 (74%); 24 (63%) seen in GUM.

result.other_findings: Failures largely due to documentation and cross-referencing problems; only 2 of 259 pre-IUD tests positive.

result.setting: Comparative analysis of six published psychiatric nursing audit systems (Newcastle)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Five of the six systems failed to specify some important elements of the audit process.

result.setting: District general hospital in the south of England (hospital-wide postoperative pain audit)

cycle1.result: Telephone interviews with 29 of 360 audited patients identified themes of inadequate information, pain at home, staff attitudes, expectations of pain and ward atmosphere.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Paediatric accident and emergency department, Royal Liverpool Children's Hospital (Alder Hey)
result.standard: Local convulsion protocol: diazepam 0.4 mg/kg up to two doses, then phenytoin 18 mg/kg with rectal paraldehyde 0.4 mL/kg

cycle1.result: Convulsion terminated in ED in 76 (94%); 69 (85%) after a single diazepam dose; 5/10 (50%) stopped with phenytoin plus paraldehyde; 9 (11%) needed ICU.

result.other_findings: Audit to be repeated prospectively.

result.topic: Home versus hospital IV antibiotics in cystic fibrosis
result.setting: University of Ulster, Northern Ireland

cycle1.result: Hospital IV antibiotics gave greater improvements in FEV1, FVC and FEF25-75 than home IV therapy.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Questionnaire survey of British surgeons with an interest in minimal access surgery

cycle1.result: 30.8% used open (Hasson) access; 65.8% used selective intraoperative cholangiography; 12.2% did not perform fascial repair.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Department of Paediatric Surgery, Leeds Teaching Hospitals Trust

cycle1.result: 250 colonoscopies in 215 children; ileoscopy in 164; no colonoscopy complications including 18 polypectomies; one avoidable procedure-related complication.

result.other_findings: Increasing proportion done as day cases.

result.setting: Merton rehabilitation team, Springfield University Hospital, Tooting (psychiatric rehabilitation unit)
result.standard: Criteria for assessing performance in a long-term and rehabilitation setting (developed by the team)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes development of a simple multidisciplinary audit system and the problems met during its development.

result.setting: Five medical record sites in four districts in South Thames regions (Thames cancer registry cases)

cycle1.result: Case note retrieval rate 80% for all districts combined. Incompleteness ranged from 38% to 62% for staging, 8% to 40% for treatment and 70% to 25% for diagnostic tests; treatment information missing in 3% to 20%; survival data omitted in less than 5%.

result.other_findings: In two districts retrieval was associated with patient survival and whether treatment was given. A staging protocol was adopted in one district and a prospective audit is being set up.

result.setting: General ophthalmic clinics, Selly Oak Hospital, Birmingham

cycle1.result: 152 patients (70%) wanted more information about their condition; 49 (23%) did not; 16 (7%) undecided. Patients with common conditions (glaucoma, cataract) understood their condition better than those with rarer conditions or multiple diagnoses.

result.other_findings: Questionnaire survey of 219 patients selected by random systematic sampling; few had a precise understanding of their diagnosis and prognosis.

result.setting: All NHS hospital pharmacies providing clinical pharmacy services

cycle1.result: Pharmacists contributed to medical audit in 50% (204/410) of hospitals, pharmacy audit in 27% (108/404) and clinical audit in 7% (29/404); 59% (235/399) involved in at least one type, 4% (15/399) in all three.

result.other_findings: Participation was higher in trust and teaching hospitals and among highly qualified and specialist pharmacists. Response rate 90% (416/462).

result.topic: Door to needle time for thrombolysis
result.setting: Accident and emergency department and coronary care unit (about 5 km away), district general hospital, Stockport
result.standard: Early thrombolysis after acute myocardial infarction; door to needle and pain to needle times

cycle1.result: Group 1 (thrombolysis in CCU): geometric mean door to needle 128 min, pain to needle 242 min.

result.intervention: Selected patients given thrombolysis in the A and E department before transfer, after oral confirmation of myocardial infarction by the CCU admitting officer on receipt of a faxed ECG.

cycle2.dates: Six months from start of new procedure (prospective)
cycle2.result: Group 2b (thrombolysis in A and E): geometric mean door to needle 38 min and pain to needle 141 min, v 121 min and 237 min in ineligible patients treated in CCU (group 2a, n=30); both p < 0.0001.

result.other_findings: Adverse effects did not differ significantly. Nine deaths (six in group 1, three in group 2b), in-hospital mortality 9.9%.

result.setting: Buckinghamshire Medical Audit Advisory Group (primary care)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Descriptive paper on the facilitator model for promoting medical audit and the National Facilitator Development Project.

result.topic: Undergraduate audit projects in general practice
result.setting: One university department of general practice with 18 general practices, Liverpool

cycle1.result: 150 students did audit projects; 15 of 18 practice questionnaires returned; six practices said the project changed substantially after joint planning; two thirds (10) valued the audits highly and were making changes in care.

result.other_findings: Descriptive evaluation of medical students and GPs doing audit projects together.

result.setting: Brompton and National Heart Hospitals, London (specialist respiratory centre)
result.standard: Appropriateness of bronchial arteriography and embolisation for haemoptysis (retrospective assessment)

cycle1.result: 58 procedures in 35 patients; embolisation technically successful in 33/40 procedures for major haemoptysis, but haemoptysis recurred within 10 days in 17; overall success rate 40% (16/40).

result.other_findings: Five patients died of haemoptysis despite embolisation. Using proposed criteria (not for minor haemoptysis or more than one week after major haemoptysis), 43% fewer procedures would have been done without loss of benefit.

result.topic: Audit of deaths in general practice
result.setting: One inner city academic general practice, Newcastle upon Tyne

cycle1.result: 57 critical incidents identified in eight deaths (mean 7.1 per case, range 2 to 15); failure of communication was the most common factor in incidents causing concern.

result.intervention: Protocols for follow-up of bereaved relatives and carers, a checklist for administrative tasks after death, and monthly review of recent deaths and terminally ill patients.
result.other_findings: Pilot of the critical incident technique; the team found it acceptable.

result.setting: Nottingham and Lincoln (inpatients detained under Section 5(2))

cycle1.result: 80 of 146 Section 5(2) orders converted to Section 2 or 3; Section 5(2) may have been used inappropriately in up to 45% of cases.

result.other_findings: Conversion was lower out of hours, within 12 hours of admission and when junior doctors did not seek senior advice; higher in mental illness than personality disorder, substance misuse or stress reactions.

result.setting: St George's Hospital, London
result.standard: Three indicators: personal visits to pharmacy by ward staff and patients; nurse telephone calls chasing prescriptions; written patient complaints

cycle1.dates: Four months after introduction of revised discharge policy
cycle1.result: All three measures increased substantially compared with the previous four-month period.

result.intervention: Action plan to change behaviour of consultants, junior doctors, ward and nursing staff, patients and pharmacy staff by raising awareness of the consequences of their actions.

cycle2.result: Substantial reductions in all three measures.

result.other_findings: No numbers given in the abstract.

result.setting: British acute hospital

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes adverse event monitoring as a quality improvement technique, with results from ophthalmology; no figures in the abstract.

result.setting: 36 hospitals (12 teaching, 24 district general) in England, Wales and Scotland
result.standard: British Thoracic Society national guidelines for hospital management of acute severe asthma

cycle1.result: Peak flow measured initially in 661/766 (86%); arterial blood gases ever assessed in 534 (70%); 65 (8%) had no steroid in first 24 hours; peak flow variability measured before discharge in 597/759 (78%), of whom 334 (56%) had good control. Only 237 (31%) prescribed oral steroids before admission despite 429 (56%) having treatment increased.

result.other_findings: Respiratory physicians performed significantly better than non-respiratory physicians. Data collected immediately before the guidelines were published.

result.setting: All 189 general practices in Staffordshire

cycle1.result: 44 (26%) practices had done at least one full audit; 40 (24%) had not started audit. Oxford classification scores were higher with a practice manager (2.7 v 1.2).

result.other_findings: Survey of audit activity and quality of the best audit project in each practice.

result.setting: Medical inpatients, Cambridge
result.standard: Recording of quantitative alcohol history, CAGE questionnaire use and alcohol notification in discharge summaries

cycle1.result: Quantitative alcohol history in medical notes 175/792 (22%) and nursing notes 31/792 (4%); excessive drinkers identified 40/792 (5.1%).

result.intervention: Training of junior medical and nursing staff, then feedback of results at a clinical audit meeting.

cycle2.result: After audit feedback: quantitative history in medical notes 241/497 (48%) and nursing notes 237/497 (48%); excessive drinkers identified 45/497 (9.1%); chi 2 for trend p < 0.0001 for notes.

result.other_findings: After training alone (n=690) medical notes 242/690 (35%) and nursing notes 123/690 (18%). Little improvement in CAGE use or discharge summaries.

result.setting: All 104 medical audit advisory groups in England and Wales

cycle1.result: Response rate 86.5%; practices participating in some audit rose from 57% in 1991-2 to 78% in 1992-3 and 86% in 1993-4; 428 multipractice audits identified, diabetes most popular.

result.other_findings: Methods for classifying and collecting audit information varied widely.

result.setting: Airedale NHS Trust, with three general practices, community health and social services

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Recommendations: pre-admission checklist, changes to nursing documentation, faster information transfer and clearer responsibility for contact across the hospital-community interface.
result.other_findings: Audit combined with a research element to inform recommendations; results not given in the abstract.

result.setting: Staffordshire general practitioners

cycle1.result: Most agreed audit is time consuming (86%), training is needed (71%), doctors are compelled to audit (68%); 53% disagreed that government policy on audit will improve health; median four positive responses of 14.

result.other_findings: Women, doctors with smaller list sizes, larger partnerships and longer audit experience were more positive.

result.setting: All family health services authority districts in England and Wales

cycle1.result: Advisory group and authority views on audit were similar; much information collected by advisory groups was not passed on; only a small minority of authorities were dissatisfied.

result.other_findings: Postal survey of perceptions; no figures in the abstract.

result.topic: Total quality management in general practice
result.setting: 18 self selected practices in the former Oxford Region

cycle1.result: 16 of 18 practices implemented quality improvement methods; 48 initiatives considered; 11 intend to continue.

result.other_findings: Programme evaluation; time was the commonest barrier.

result.setting: 53 general practices in Warwickshire

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Links practice culture, team working and decision making to successful audit; proposes six practice types.

result.setting: 18 general practices in Leicestershire
result.standard: Five criteria of care for long-term benzodiazepine users (e.g. told about dependency, withdrawal recommended, consulted in past year)

cycle1.result: 'Told about dependency' 52 (11.1%) in feedback only group and 27 (10.5%) in feedback plus reminders group; 'consulted in past year' 434 (93.1%) and 255 (96.6%).

result.intervention: Audit feedback, with or without reminder cards in medical records (randomised by practice).

cycle2.result: 'Told about dependency' 118 (25.8%) feedback only v 184 (43.0%) feedback plus reminders, OR 1.46; 'consulted in past year' 411 (95.8%) v 400 (99.8%), OR 13.5.

result.other_findings: Randomised trial; reminders improved only two of five criteria and were not recommended for routine use.

result.setting: All primary care teams in County Durham with a patient who died by suicide

cycle1.result: 49 suicides registered with 31 practices; 19 (61%) practices covering 27 (55%) cases took part. Areas for improvement found but no substantive preventive measures within primary care.

result.other_findings: Wider social and economic context was thought more important; the technique encouraged reflection.

result.setting: 28 UK sites using the Royal College of Nursing dynamic standard setting system

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Qualitative study; benefits to clinical practice reported but difficulties with staff motivation, time and training.

result.setting: Moorfields Eye Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Day case surgery under local anaesthesia was the most cost-effective method, with no detriment to visual outcome.

result.other_findings: Outcome and cost review; no figures in the abstract.

result.topic: Thrombolysis use in acute myocardial infarction
result.setting: Four UK district general hospitals
result.standard: Locally set explicit standards for proportion of patients with definite and probable AMI given intravenous thrombolysis (technical standards in two hospitals, population standards in two)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Peer review meetings of baseline results, with standard setting requested by letter and telephone.

cycle2.result: Six of the eight standards set were achieved in at least one of four audits in each hospital.

result.other_findings: Time trends hard to interpret because of small numbers; no clear link between the standard setting process and attainment.

result.topic: Thrombolysis use in acute myocardial infarction
result.setting: Five district general hospitals (one control) in North West Thames Regional Health Authority
result.standard: Proportion of patients with suspected acute myocardial infarction given thrombolysis

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Repeated audits with a series of four audit meetings and subsequent actions.

cycle2.result: Thrombolysis rose by 20% to 37% in three auditing hospitals and fell by 6% in the fourth (baseline over 90%); control rose 15%. Only one hospital differed significantly from control (51 extra treatments per year, 95% CI 0.5 to 61).

result.other_findings: Audit cost 3700 to 5200 pounds per hospital; 101 to 392 pounds per extra patient thrombolysed in the three responsive hospitals, with very wide confidence intervals.

result.setting: Audit groups in hospital, community and primary care and health authorities, North West Region

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Qualitative study; many audit groups remained medically dominated and obstacles to nurse participation included hierarchy, workload and lack of protected time.

result.topic: Inguinal hernia repair in peritoneal dialysis patients
result.setting: All UK renal transplant centres (postal questionnaire)

cycle1.result: Replies from 34/37 centres; wide variation in pre- and post-operative dialysis regimens; only 44% of centres had an established protocol.

result.other_findings: Re-assessment planned after protocol introduction.

result.setting: District general hospital without on-site cardiac surgery, Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital

cycle1.result: Major complications 0.07%; mortality 0.07%; arterial complications needing surgical repair 0.24% brachial and 0.17% femoral.

result.other_findings: Results comparable with surgical centres.

result.setting: Prince of Wales Hospital, Chinese University of Hong Kong

cycle1.result: Conversion 32 (17.7%); mean operation time 203 min; operative mortality 1.7%; four-year survival 100%, 88.3% and 64.5% for Dukes A, B and C; one (0.65%) port-site recurrence.

result.other_findings: Case series of outcomes.

result.setting: Otolaryngology department, Queen's Medical Centre, Nottingham
result.standard: Operation notes should record accurate data, ward, department and name of surgeon, and avoid unacceptable abbreviations

cycle1.result: Clear identification of operating surgeon 74%; avoidance of unacceptable abbreviations 53%.

result.intervention: Aide-memoire attached to the front of the operation sheet.

cycle2.result: Clear identification of operating surgeon 93%; avoidance of unacceptable abbreviations 84%; all criteria improved.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Transjugular liver biopsy safety and adequacy
result.setting: Liver transplantation and hepatobiliary medicine centre, London

cycle1.result: 157 biopsies; major complications 2 (1.3%) capsular perforations; sample adequate in 90%, inadequate in 6%, technically unsuccessful in 4%.

result.other_findings: Clinical impact in 50% of acute, 62% of chronic liver disease and 87% of transplant patients.

result.setting: British Association of Dermatologists consultant members (postal questionnaire)

cycle1.result: 69% had nurse-run clinics; 57% had protocols for nurses to alter treatment; 26% had nurses prescribing with countersignature and 5% without.

result.other_findings: Obstacles included opposition from administration or nursing hierarchies (about 40%) and funding (about 25%).

result.setting: 100 UK hospitals (nuclear medicine departments)

cycle1.result: 88% of results within two percentage points of the study median and 98% within five.

result.other_findings: Significant differences arose from the view used and background subtraction method; standardisation recommended.

result.topic: Diabetes annual review in primary care
result.setting: Multi-practice audits by 17 medical audit advisory groups (495 practices)
result.standard: Annual key process measures for diabetes care

cycle1.result: Annual mean compliance: HbA1c or fructosamine 72.5%, fundi 67.5%, urine 65.8%, blood pressure 87.6%, smoking 71.4%, feet 67.7%, BMI 52.5%, with wide ranges between groups.

result.other_findings: Diabetes prevalence 1.46%; 50.7% managed by general practice only, 19.1% hospital only, 30.2% shared care.

result.setting: General practice, Tonbridge, south east England
result.standard: Evidence-based antithrombotic (warfarin) treatment for patients with atrial fibrillation at risk of thromboembolism

cycle1.result: 132 of 13 239 patients had a history of atrial fibrillation, 100 of them at risk of thromboembolism.

result.intervention: Assessment and educational interview with eligible patients about antithrombotic treatment.

cycle2.result: After the study 52 patients were taking warfarin; of the other 48 (41 on aspirin), eight too ill, 16 unable to consent, four refused interview and 20 declined warfarin.

result.other_findings: Patients' unwillingness to take warfarin was a major limiting factor; those declining sought a higher level of benefit.

result.setting: Academic Surgical Unit, Castle Hill Hospital, Hull (one consultant surgeon)

cycle1.result: 114 plication darn repairs; four recurrences (about 3.5%); actuarial recurrence risk 0.94% at 1 year, 3.02% at 5 years and 9% at 10 years.

result.intervention: The surgeon changed his technique of primary inguinal hernia repair.
result.other_findings: Recurrence judged unacceptable for modern practice.

result.setting: General dental practice

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Illustrates use of the SPSS CHAID statistical package for dental audit and practice management.

result.setting: General dental practice, Glasgow

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Consensus reached on the rationale for antibiotic prescribing.

cycle2.result: Number of antibiotic prescriptions fell by 50%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Axillary management outcomes in breast cancer
result.setting: Glenfield Hospital NHS Trust, Leicester

cycle1.result: Regional recurrence 2% and lymphoedema 5.7% at 5 years.

result.other_findings: No indication for more aggressive axillary treatment.

result.setting: All hospitals in the South West Region

cycle1.result: Mean referral to clinic interval 67 days (54 days if GP PSA > 10 ng/ml, 104 days if < 10 ng/ml); 34% had radical treatment (10% prostatectomy, 24% radiotherapy); 27% hormone treatment; all had histological diagnosis and 84% were staged before treatment.

result.other_findings: Need for better assessment, note keeping and a regional cancer register; intended as a baseline.

result.setting: Hospital-based family planning clinics, King's College Hospital, London

cycle1.result: 28 IUDs inserted by doctors and 22 by nurses; nurses needed no help from doctors; three early removals for bleeding and pain, all after doctor insertion; minor problems in eight, equally split.

result.other_findings: 29 attended six-week follow-up; follow-up ongoing.

result.setting: University Hospital Birmingham

cycle1.result: 24% found biopsy moderately to extremely painful; 19% reported significant complications (voiding difficulty 13%, haematuria 11%); fever or sweats 6%, septicaemia in three; 20% saw their GP within a week.

result.other_findings: Questionnaire completed by 104 of 129 men.

result.setting: West London general practices using EMIS computer system
result.standard: 'Rule of halves' for hypertension; locally agreed guidelines and targets

cycle1.result: Using strict definitions the rule of halves still applied; using looser definitions three-quarters of hypertensives known, two-thirds treated and just under two-thirds controlled.

result.intervention: Feedback of results to practices, agreed management guidelines, standardised computer recording, targets and review dates.
result.other_findings: Wide variation in computer use, follow-up, target BP attainment and prescribing; 15 practices used computers regularly.

result.setting: Specialist liver unit, Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Birmingham

cycle1.result: 658 cannulations (352 subclavian, 306 internal jugular); median INR 2.4 and 2.7; incidence of major vascular complications was low.

result.other_findings: Raised INR alone should not contraindicate central venous cannulation.

result.setting: Christie Hospital, Manchester

cycle1.result: Cancer specific survival 79% and 57% at 5 and 10 years; local control 85% and 73%.

result.other_findings: Six patients developed lung metastases, all adenoid-cystic; one osteoradionecrosis.

result.setting: Haematology clinic, Bishop Auckland General Hospital
result.standard: Patient-set maximum clinic waiting time of 30 min (longer-term target 20 min)

cycle1.result: Patient survey of 50 consecutive patients set the standard; air-tube sample transport with electronic results did not achieve it despite repeated audits.

result.intervention: Point-of-care testing in the clinic, with the backup analyser moved weekly and tests done by trained nurse specialists.

cycle2.result: Clinic waiting times consistently achieved the standard.

result.other_findings: No numbers given in the abstract.

result.setting: Recovery room, Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Norfolk (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Incidence of airway problems 2.8%.

result.other_findings: Incidence judged too low to warrant full-time anaesthetic presence in recovery.

result.topic: History of audit in general practice
result.setting: British general practice

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Opinion piece questioning whether audit improves care and whether it is a secure basis for clinical governance.

result.setting: Respiratory sleep service, district general hospital, Nottingham

cycle1.result: At 12 months 33 assigned nCPAP (81% compliance, 20% dissatisfied), 25 ENT surgery (only half operated, 42% awaiting and dissatisfied), 37 simple measures (no improvement, 33% dissatisfied); interspecialty referral delay mean 16 weeks.

result.other_findings: Referral letters were unhelpful for directing initial referral; coordination between respiratory and ENT recommended.

result.setting: Regional Cancer Registry, Trent

cycle1.result: 96% could be staged by registry clerical staff but none were staged by clinicians; tumour extent based only on DRE in 45% and not assessed in 32%; 81% had no nodal investigation; 61% had no investigation for metastases.

result.other_findings: Survival analysis supported validity of registry-based staging.

result.topic: Prostate cancer diagnosis and treatment documentation
result.setting: Regional Cancer Registry, Trent

cycle1.result: 81% histologically proven; 76% had a PSA test; 29% of histologically proven cases had a Gleason grade; none staged by clinicians; 39% drug treatment alone and 37% no active treatment in six months after diagnosis.

result.other_findings: Need for standardised pathology reports and treatment protocols.

result.setting: 15 UK hospitals (Myocardial Infarction Audit Group)

cycle1.result: In 1993, 28.2% given thrombolysis within 90 minutes of calling for help; 42.6% called for help within 30 minutes; 4.4% treated in emergency departments, median door to needle there 53 min.

cycle2.result: In 1997, 39.1% given thrombolysis within 90 minutes of call (difference 10.9%, 95% CI 7.2% to 14.7%); 36.0% called within 30 minutes; 17.3% treated in emergency departments, median delay 36 min; CCU delay fell from 63 to 54 min.

result.other_findings: Observational trend study; direct use of emergency services rose by 18.9% but longer patient delays offset some gains.

result.setting: North Hertfordshire NHS Trust, Stevenage

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Introduction of a nurse-led leg ulcer clinic.
result.other_findings: Abstract gives no audit methods or results.

result.setting: Transfusion laboratory, Bishop Auckland General Hospital (district hospital)
result.standard: Error rates reported in the transfusion literature

cycle1.result: Most errors were preanalytical (incomplete sample or request form data) and corrected before action; main analytical errors were transcription of patient identification and incorrect blood group testing; main postanalytical error was nurses not following blood component collection procedures.

result.other_findings: No serious consequences; a standard UK method for calculating error rates is recommended.

result.setting: Seven partner general practice (14,000 patients), Bournemouth
result.standard: 48 hour target for processing repeat prescription requests

cycle1.result: Turnaround within 48 hours 95%; prescriptions needing records checked 18%.

result.intervention: PDSA cycles: synchronising repeat medications and recording drugs prescribed on visits, prioritising prescription signing at an agreed time, and moving prescription printing to reception.

cycle2.result: Turnaround within 48 hours 99%; prescriptions needing records checked 8.6%.

result.other_findings: Saved at least one working day of receptionist time per month, at reduced cost, with better staff satisfaction.

result.setting: UK laboratories submitting to PHLS Mycobacterium Reference Unit, regional centres and Scottish Mycobacteria Reference Laboratory

cycle1.result: Response 67.2%; only 3.3% of primary samples produced a mycobacterial culture; 62.9% used liquid media; few used molecular methods; reference services rated very good or good by 85.6%.

result.intervention: Rapid molecular diagnostic services established at PHLS MRU for rifampicin resistance and tuberculous meningitis.
result.other_findings: Most laboratories were CPA accredited and in NEQAS.

result.setting: All 16 NHS histopathology laboratories in Wales
result.standard: Minimum dataset (tumour type, depth of invasion, lymph node involvement, completeness of excision) and best practice reporting

cycle1.result: Minimum standards met in 77% of gastric (156/203) and 53% of oesophageal (42/79) resection reports; best practice in 20% of gastric and 18% of oesophageal reports.

result.other_findings: Omission of completeness of excision or circumferential margin statement was the commonest failure; template proforma reporting proposed.

result.setting: Combined paediatric plastic surgery and burns unit, Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle upon Tyne

cycle1.result: No evidence of cross-infection between burns patients and other patients on the ward.

result.other_findings: Screening swabs detected carriers, who were more at risk themselves than a risk to others.

result.setting: Teaching hospital gastroenterology unit, Imperial College, London

cycle1.result: 94% had upper GI endoscopy (yield 54%, including 4 malignancies); 84% had lower GI investigation by colonoscopy or barium enema (yield 37%). Combined endoscopic and barium examinations gave a diagnosis in 69%; overall an underlying diagnosis was made in 92%.

result.other_findings: 12.2% had significant co-existent upper and lower GI pathology. 33 patients had visceral angiography, with a bleeding source found in 27 (yield 82%).

result.setting: 18 UK nuclear medicine centres (BNCS/BNMS collaborative audit programme)
result.standard: Expert panel scoring of six parameters (stress technique, radiopharmaceutical usage, image acquisition, processing, report images, report text) as good (2), adequate (1) or poor (0)

cycle1.result: Stress technique inadequate in 10 (11%) studies; radiopharmaceutical usage and acquisition inadequate in 5 (6%); processing inadequate in 8 (10%); report images inadequate in 2 (3%); report text inadequate in 21 of 66 (32%). Mean quality score 1.3 (range 0.5-2.0); 17 of 88 (19%) scored below 1.0.

result.other_findings: Of the 21 inadequate reports, 11 (52%) were incorrect and 10 (48%) were essentially correct but misleading because of poor phrasing. Centres received quality scores and a consensus report as feedback.

result.setting: 187 dermatology centres across the UK (British Association of Dermatologists national audit, phase 1)
result.standard: Recommended outpatient facilities for atopic eczema; 100% working standard for each criterion

cycle1.result: No criterion reached the 100% standard. About half the recommended items (e.g. height and weight measurement, dietician access, patch testing, photochemotherapy) were reported in over 90% of centres. Appointment letters asking patients to bring treatment details were issued by 52% of centres; access to dermatology-experienced nurses on paediatric wards in 57%.

result.other_findings: Response rate 98%. Access to counselling services varied widely by region (33-94% of centres).

result.topic: Evidence use in student audit projects
result.setting: Department of General Practice, University of Glasgow; final-year medical students

cycle1.result: Quantity and quality of reference citation in student audit projects increased over 3 years, alongside the introduction of an evidence-based medicine session into audit teaching.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Royal Belfast Hospital for Sick Children

cycle1.result: Conversion rate 8%; median opiate requirement 1 day (range 1-5); median post-operative stay 2 days (range 2-15); operative morbidity 8%; recurrence rate 6%. Median follow-up 31.8 months.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Department of Otolaryngology, Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester

cycle1.result: Around 75% of patients seen at the new weekday-morning open access clinic were suitable for waiting until the next day.

result.other_findings: The clinic was judged to benefit GP access, routine clinics, junior doctor teaching and concentration of aural toilet cases under expert nurse care.

result.topic: Short-course preoperative radiotherapy for rectal cancer outcomes
result.setting: Two radiotherapy centres, Sheffield

cycle1.result: Time from referral to radiotherapy 33 (11-74) days; radiotherapy to operation 5 (1-42) days. Anastomotic leak rate 15% and perineal wound infection rate 18%, higher than expected.

result.other_findings: Perineal wound breakdown was more common in patients waiting more than 7 days: 15% (n = 39) versus 30% (n = 10).

result.topic: Intraoperative TOE in paediatric cardiac surgery
result.setting: Royal Alexandra Hospital for Children, Westmead, Sydney

cycle1.result: Probe insertion complications prevented full study in 11 (5.5%). Preoperative diagnosis confirmed in 176 of 189 (93%). Moderate or severe residual defects in 21 (11%); 10 (5.3%) returned to bypass, 6 prompted by TOE alone.

result.other_findings: Probe insertion complications were airway obstruction (6), inability to pass the probe (4) and vascular compression (1).

result.topic: Antenatal thalassaemia screening and informed choice
result.setting: UK Confidential Enquiry into Counselling for Genetic Disorders, thalassaemia module (national)
result.standard: Antenatal screening and counselling for haemoglobin disorders as standard UK practice; offer of prenatal diagnosis

cycle1.result: Risk detected by screening before or during first pregnancy in 49% (68/138) of couples. Prenatal diagnosis offered in 69% (274/400) of pregnancies; uptake 80% (216/274). Demonstrable service failure in 28% (110/400) of pregnancies.

result.other_findings: Offer of prenatal diagnosis ranged from 94% (122/130) for British Cypriots to 54% (80/149) for British Pakistanis, and from 90% in the south east of England to 39% in the West Midlands.

result.setting: Inner city palliative care centre, central London (Royal Marsden Hospital)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Records of patients staying more than 28 days were reviewed to identify features of long-stay patients for admission planning; no results given in the abstract.

result.setting: Doncaster Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Overall rate of clinically apparent hospital-acquired thromboembolic complications 0.4% (n = 35); 2.1% (n = 17) in the high-risk group. Prophylaxis did not appear to reduce incidence, even when stratified by risk.

result.other_findings: A high-risk subgroup was followed up for up to 42 days after discharge.

result.topic: GCS scoring in sedated patients for APACHE
result.setting: 22 general adult intensive care units in Scotland (Scottish Intensive Care Society Audit Group)

cycle1.result: 50% of patients were sedated and 22% had scores altered. Using the pre-sedation GCS improved discrimination of APACHE II and III and calibration of APACHE III; APACHE II calibration deteriorated overall.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Genito-urinary medicine outpatient clinic, Central Middlesex Hospital (district general hospital), London

cycle1.result: All patients eligible under BHIVA guidelines were being offered triple therapy. Viral load undetectable in 75% of 20 patients on their first established regimen and 36% of 14 patients who had failed at least one drug.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 19 randomly selected hospital dermatology departments across the UK (British Association of Dermatologists national audit, phase 2)
result.standard: Completeness of clinic letters and case-note recording; 100% working standard

cycle1.result: Clinic letters to GPs recording diagnosis, treatment and follow-up approached the 100% standard. Site and severity of eczema recorded in 83% and 74%, asthma in 53%, sleep loss in 21% and effect on school, work or social life in 6%. On average only 51% of all audit measures were recorded (range 41-61% between centres).

result.other_findings: The centre with the best recording used a purpose-designed data sheet for new atopic eczema patients.

result.setting: ENT surgeons, Freeman Hospital, Newcastle

cycle1.result: 196 percutaneous and 102 open tracheostomies. Complication rate 10% for percutaneous and 8% for open (chi 2 = 0.279, P = 0.598).

result.other_findings: Percutaneous tracheostomy was mainly used for respiratory support in intensive care, while most open tracheostomies were done in theatre.

result.topic: Breast cancer management against regional guidelines
result.setting: North Thames (East) Health region: 21 acute hospitals and 16 specialist surgeons treating breast cancer (Thames Cancer Registry)
result.standard: Regional evidence-based breast cancer clinical guidelines and guideline targets

cycle1.result: Chemotherapy use 17% and axillary surgery 46% (previous studies in this population).

cycle2.result: Chemotherapy use rose to 23% and axillary surgery to 76%.

result.other_findings: The audit sample was 28% of breast cancers diagnosed in the region in 1992; the pilot led to prospective audit of all regional breast cancers and a 15-fold increase in high-quality clinical information.

result.topic: Staging CT in prostate cancer radiotherapy
result.setting: Centre for Cancer Treatment, Mount Vernon Hospital, Middlesex

cycle1.result: All 97 had a planning CT; 85 also had a diagnostic staging CT, 51 (60%) with pelvic and abdominal imaging. 20 abnormalities were found in 19 patients; 13 were considered metastatic but only 4 altered treatment intent. Overall 4% were denied radical treatment on CT findings.

result.other_findings: Malignant intra-abdominal disease was not found without metastatic disease in the pelvis.

result.setting: Burns unit, Glasgow Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Patients recorded worst pain as none or mild in 64% of procedures, whereas no surgeon and only one nurse rated pain as none or mild.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Cancer units and centres in the West Midlands (West Midlands Gynaecological Oncology Group)
result.standard: 15 regional standards for uterine malignancy management

cycle1.result: Of 15 standards, 11 were met by at least one hospital; no hospital met all standards. Standards on initial referral and diagnostic intervals were universally failed. Outpatient diagnosis in only 30%. Surgery was usually within six weeks of diagnosis.

result.setting: Accident and Emergency Department and aeromedical service, Royal London Hospital
result.standard: Audit filter set at the upper quartile of emergency call to operating room time; comparison with national trauma database

cycle1.result: Median emergency call to operation 127 min (140 blunt, 86 penetrating); emergency department arrival to theatre 54 min. Audit filter selected 21 patients, with five correctable delays identified.

result.topic: Breast-conserving surgery rate in early breast cancer
result.setting: St Vincent's Public and Private Hospitals, Sydney (teaching hospital)
result.standard: Comparison with published Australian breast-conserving surgery rates

cycle1.result: Breast-conserving surgery rate 33% in 1990 and 36% in 1994, lower than expected.

result.other_findings: Rates varied widely between surgeons and for the same surgeon between years.

result.setting: 15 radiation oncology centres in Australia and New Zealand (TROG 96.01 quality assurance audit)
result.standard: Technical adherence to the trial protocol

cycle1.result: Unacceptable protocol violation rate 10%.

result.intervention: Improved audit design, staff education and increased data management resources.

cycle2.result: Unacceptable protocol violation rate fell to 4%, with improved data quality and quantity.

result.other_findings: The earlier measurement was from a different trial (head and neck TROG 91.01). A budget of $100 per patient was proposed for similar technical audits.

result.setting: 29 randomly selected hospital dermatology departments across the UK (British Association of Dermatologists national audit, phase 3)
result.standard: Eight working standards for service outcome (e.g. 60% relative DLQI improvement, 70% improvement in sleep loss, 80% improvement in worst aspect, 80% return to work or school)

cycle1.result: Mean DLQI 12.5 falling to 9.7 at 6 weeks (P = 0.001); mean CDLQI 10.5 falling to 8.7. Sleep loss improved in 44% of adults and 47% of children (standard 70%); worst aspect improved in 61% of adults and 59% of children (standard 80%). Return to work/school 70% of adults and 87.5% of children (standard 80%). Only one of eight standards met nationally.

result.other_findings: 235 (67%) returned the 6-week questionnaire. Most standards were met by at least one of the 11 NHS administrative areas.

result.setting: ENT consultants throughout England and Wales (Royal College of Surgeons of England Comparative Audit Service)

cycle1.result: Two-thirds had tonsillectomy for recurrent acute tonsillitis; 3% were day cases. Return to theatre for haemorrhage 0.75%; readmission almost 7%. 92% felt their throat was better and 88% were pleased they had the operation.

result.other_findings: 114 consultants returned the management questionnaire and 1408 patients returned postoperative questionnaires.

result.topic: Assault patient data collection in A&E

cycle1.result: Collecting information on the circumstances of violence was straightforward; questions on motive and on the relationship with the assailant were problematic. Receptionists were the most appropriate staff to record the information.

result.setting: Eight palliative care centres in England and Scotland (inpatient, outpatient, day, home and primary care)

cycle1.result: Staff and patient ratings agreed acceptably for 8 of 10 items; construct validity Spearman rho 0.43 to 0.80; test-retest reliability acceptable for seven items; Cronbach's alpha 0.65 (patients) and 0.70 (staff).

result.other_findings: 337 patients were assessed by staff and 148 completed the patient questionnaire; completion took no more than 10 minutes.

result.topic: Risk-stratified mortality in adult cardiac surgery

cycle1.result: Operative mortality 3.5% (95% CI 3.1% to 3.9%), range 2.7% to 3.8% across centres. Parsonnet score AUC 0.74; mean score 7.0, giving an observed to expected mortality ratio of 0.51 (range 0.4 to 0.64).

result.other_findings: Data collection was complete; validation of a random 10% of cases found discrepancy rates of 0% to 13% across risk factors. A new nine-factor model was derived.

result.topic: Missed myocardial damage in discharged chest pain patients

result.setting: General dental practitioners and vocational dental practitioners, NHS Trent Region

result.topic: Postoperative nausea and vomiting after breast surgery
result.setting: Department of Surgery, Withington Hospital, Manchester

cycle1.result: Postoperative nausea 56% and vomiting 41%, significantly associated with length of procedure and morphine use.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Wolfson Unit for Endoscopy, St Mark's Hospital, London; day-case colonoscopy

cycle1.result: Looping occurred in 91% (N-sigmoid 79%, deep transverse 34%); 69% of loops were incorrectly diagnosed. Tip location correct 85% overall. Abdominal pressure effective 54 of 145 times (37%) versus position change 95 of 144 (66%).

result.topic: Fever and neutropenia management in children
result.setting: Paediatric oncology unit, Royal Liverpool Children's Hospital
result.standard: Local standards set from neutropenia guidelines

cycle1.result: Retrospective notes review of care before the pathway; results not given in the abstract.

result.setting: 61 paediatric rheumatology units in the UK and Eire (British Paediatric Rheumatology Group postal survey)

cycle1.result: 18% of units (n = 9) had a dedicated adolescent clinic. Seven clinics had a standardised transfer process, first discussed at a median age of 13 years, but none provided literature or pre-visits. Generic health issues were addressed by only two clinics.

result.setting: Radiation Oncology Department, Liverpool Hospital, Sydney

cycle1.result: 998 new patients (74%) had radiotherapy, 57% radically. 40 (4%) did not complete treatment as planned and 89 (9%) were retreated.

result.topic: Cyclosporin use in inflammatory bowel disease

result.topic: Audit Commission district audit of family planning services
result.setting: Family planning service, Saltergate Health Centre, Chesterfield

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Descriptive account of an Audit Commission district audit; a national system (DATIS) compares family planning expenditure per thousand patients.

result.standard: MR imaging and reporting requirements for staging musculoskeletal tumours (e.g. whole-bone imaging for skip metastases)

result.setting: 91 general practices (Bridge Medical Centre, Crawley)
result.standard: Practice policy to step PPI therapy down to low-dose cost-effective therapy, or to antacids, H2 receptor antagonists or no treatment where PPI not needed

result.other_findings: Extrapolated savings of up to 50,000 pounds per 10,000-patient practice.

result.topic: Incomplete excision of basal cell carcinoma

cycle1.result: 41 of 879 lesions (4.7%) were incompletely excised in 754 patients; 16 were re-excised and the rest followed up.

result.standard: Comparison with the National Cataract Surgery Survey (RCO 1993)

result.topic: Diabetes as a risk factor for glaucoma
