result.topic: Radiological review of emergency department radiographs
result.setting: Accident and emergency department and radiology, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford (teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: 684 actual or suspected A&E interpretation errors flagged; 351 missed or strongly suspected fractures (mainly ankle, finger and elbow), 11 missed chest abnormalities and 24 A&E false positives. Further A&E action was taken in 286 (42.6%).

result.other_findings: Radiologists in training had an 18% false-positive rate against the musculoskeletal radiologist; no missed diagnosis needed surgery.

result.setting: Nottingham Paediatric Cochlear Implant Programme, Queen's Medical Centre

cycle1.result: 43.3% had no electrode faults; 23.3% had potential faults on both behavioural and integrity testing; 13.3% on behavioural testing only; 13.3% on integrity testing only; 6.7% were difficult to assess.

result.other_findings: Routine 5-year integrity testing affected management in 30% of patients.

result.setting: Department of Otolaryngology, Arrowe Park Hospital, Wirral

cycle1.dates: Year before the change in practice
cycle1.result: 8 patients had surgery (septoplasty, nasal packing, external carotid ligation); mean post-operative stay 3.9 days (range 3-6).

result.intervention: Endoscopic sphenopalatine artery diathermy, with or without anterior ethmoid artery diathermy, offered instead of conventional surgery.

cycle2.result: 10 patients (7%) needed surgery, all endoscopic sphenopalatine artery diathermy; mean post-operative stay 2.1 days (range 1-3); one recurrence managed conservatively and no surgical complications.

result.other_findings: Mean follow-up 10 months.

result.topic: Clinical audit and peer review for dental CPD
result.setting: General dental practice (discussion paper, University of Birmingham)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Discussion paper arguing that anonymised collaborative audit and peer review could inform continuing professional development provision.

result.topic: Cost of multidisciplinary head and neck cancer care
result.setting: Oxford Centre for Head and Neck Oncology, Radcliffe Infirmary

cycle1.result: Prospective audit quantified the cost of input from all team members in inpatient care; figures not given in the abstract.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: UK national lung transplant cohort (UK Cardiothoracic Transplant Audit, Royal College of Surgeons of England)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Presents current lung transplant results from a validated national database; no figures in the abstract.

result.setting: Six units in each of two health districts (psychiatry of old age services), County Durham

cycle1.result: Baseline mapping highlighted limited staff-client interaction and a need for a wider range of activities to promote person-centred care.

result.other_findings: High dependency did not automatically mean lower quality of person-centred care.

result.setting: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, University College Hospital, Galway
result.standard: RCOG 1995 guidelines for thromboprophylaxis following caesarean section

cycle1.result: 62.9% were moderate and 20.4% high risk. Overall 34 (17%) of 200 eligible women received thromboprophylaxis.

result.other_findings: Emergency caesarean section was associated with no thromboprophylaxis (OR 2.6, 95% CI 1.2-5.9) compared with elective.

result.setting: All liver transplant centres in the UK and Ireland (UK Liver Transplantation Audit, Royal College of Surgeons)

cycle1.result: 87% were first transplants; mean age 42 years. Lower graft and patient survival was associated with acute disease, transplantation from hospital and pre-operative renal or ventilatory support.

result.other_findings: 1-year graft and patient survival were consistent with the European Liver Transplant Registry.

result.topic: Follow-up of abnormal liver function tests in primary care
result.setting: University hospital and surrounding general practices, Nottingham (population about 330,000)

cycle1.result: Follow-up data in 873 (94%); 531 already under hospital review. Of 157 suitable for investigation, no further tests were requested in 91 (58%); in seven, results suggesting treatable chronic liver disease had not been followed up. On investigation 97 (62%) had a diagnosis needing hospital intervention or follow-up.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Urban mental health service, South Eastern Sydney Area Health Service

cycle1.result: Clinical file audits showed non-English-speaking patients received more pharmacological treatment and less cognitive behavioural therapy than English-speaking patients.

result.intervention: Planned cross-cultural training, revised policies and procedures, and revised roles for bilingual counsellors as cultural consultants.
result.other_findings: The programme also used a staff survey, workshops and a consumer and carer focus group.

result.setting: All 22 consultant-led maternity units in Scotland (national audit)
result.standard: National clinical guideline on management of diabetes in pregnancy (criterion-based audit)

cycle1.result: Antenatal care was organised in line with guideline recommendations, but formal prepregnancy care provision was lower and pregnancy planning and periconceptual care fell short of recommendations; care during pregnancy was meticulous.

result.other_findings: Adverse pregnancy outcomes remained commoner than in non-diabetic pregnancies.

result.topic: Information giving for depot antipsychotic medication
result.setting: Single community mental health team, Wales

cycle1.result: Case notes were examined for the type, nature and frequency of information given to patients on depot neuroleptics; results not given in the abstract.

result.other_findings: Evidence-based service guidelines for depot neuroleptic medication were produced.

result.setting: Mater Hospital, Belfast
result.standard: Department of Health and Social Services (March 1998) prescribing guidelines for drugs for dementia

cycle1.result: Guidelines generally followed; 3 patients prescribed drugs outside the guidelines; most failures (10) were due to poor recording of data in the clinical record.

result.intervention: Changes made to documentation of patient assessments; suggestions made to review CREST guidelines.
result.other_findings: No agreed shared care protocols had been implemented despite DHSS recommendation, but this did not seem to affect access to the drugs.

result.setting: 53 of 55 UK radiotherapy departments treating gynaecological malignancy (national study)

cycle1.result: Crude late severe complication rate 6.1% (actuarial 8%) at 5 years; 5-year overall survival 47%; 58.5% of surgery plus radiotherapy patients had Wertheim's procedure.

result.other_findings: Only FIGO stage was significantly associated with mortality; survival lower than European FIGO 1990-92 data.

result.setting: British general practice (descriptive review)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes what significant event auditing is and how it is done; appears a useful adjunct to clinical audit where a positive team culture exists.

result.setting: 59 neonatal units in North and South Thames regions (postal questionnaire)

cycle1.result: 42 of 59 questionnaires returned (71%); mean accurate identification of cerebral abnormalities 59% (range 45-71%); only 44% of neonatal registrars had formal training in cranial ultrasonography.

result.other_findings: 56% of those interpreting scans were neonatal registrars; authors recommend formal training, supervision and more formal reporting.

result.setting: Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, North Staffordshire Hospital, and local general dental practitioners
result.standard: Local guidelines for management of impacted third molars issued to general dental practitioners (April 1998)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Distribution of third molar referral guidelines to local general dental practitioners in April 1998.
result.other_findings: Authors conclude referral guidelines are an effective means of changing general dental practitioners' referral practice; no figures given in the abstract.

result.topic: Palliative chemotherapy in recurrent cervical cancer
result.setting: Gynaecological Oncology Unit, Royal Marsden Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Objective response rate 11.8%; symptomatic response in 8 patients (24%); 25 failed to complete 6 cycles, 11 due to toxicity (7 encephalopathy).

result.other_findings: Ifosfamide judged to have unacceptable toxicity and insufficient symptomatic efficacy.

result.topic: Lung cancer care pathway audit tool
result.setting: Multisite cancer unit (University of Sheffield study)

cycle1.result: Paper-based forms representing key steps in the lung cancer care pathway were found acceptable to users.

result.other_findings: Describes development of a tool to audit key standards within a lung cancer care pathway, with recommendations for an electronic record.

result.topic: Prostate cancer management and staging documentation
result.setting: National population-based study, Scottish Cancer Registry

cycle1.result: 8% managed by both a urologist and a clinical oncologist within a year of diagnosis; 14% managed by clinical oncologists in first year; documentation of staging information was poor.

cycle2.result: 13% managed by both a urologist and a clinical oncologist; 20% managed by clinical oncologists in first year.

result.other_findings: Two separate cohorts rather than a re-audit after an intervention; considerable inconsistency in management found.

result.setting: Neurosurgical units in the UK and Ireland (prospective multicentre audit)

cycle1.result: 70 (50%) shunt revisions over 5 years; 24 (18%) shunt infections; 36 (27%) shunts removed; favourable Glasgow Outcome Scale in 64% at 5 years.

result.other_findings: Headache improved after reprogramming in 27 of 38 (71%) patients with refractory headache; 49 (36%) valves never reprogrammed.

result.topic: Bloodborne virus testing and hepatitis B immunisation in injecting drug users
result.setting: Single general practice (Muirhouse Medical Group), Edinburgh

cycle1.result: Of 115 studied: 71 tested for HBV (44% previous infection), 75 tested for hepatitis C antibodies (72% positive), 80 tested for HIV (33% positive).

result.intervention: Attempts to improve testing and HBV immunisation; an abbreviated immunisation protocol was devised including post-vaccination checks and boosting; hepatitis C testing offered after counselling.

cycle2.result: 99 tested for HBV (40% previous infection), 108 tested for hepatitis C antibodies (68% positive), 105 tested for HIV (25% positive).

result.other_findings: Large numbers of injecting drug users were not immune to hepatitis B and required immunisation.

result.setting: Community dental services, two large Trusts in Wales
result.standard: Research evidence on best practice in restorative techniques (stainless steel crowns)

cycle1.result: No dental officers were using stainless steel crowns routinely for restoring primary molars; all 18 used glass ionomer cement and amalgam; 6 used GIC exclusively; 11 used stainless steel crowns only with pulpotomy.

result.other_findings: Baseline survey; a hands-on postgraduate training course was considered the most effective way of teaching restorative techniques.

result.topic: Laser Doppler imaging for burn depth
result.setting: Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle upon Tyne (burns service)

cycle1.result: Accuracy of LDI in assessing burn depth 97%, compared with 60-80% for established clinical methods.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend LDI for all burns of intermediate depth.

result.setting: Children's hospital (Alder Hey Children's Hospital, Liverpool), 10-year retrospective review

cycle1.result: 22 of 93 boys with HSP (24%) had scrotal involvement; 3/22 (14%) investigated radiologically; 8/22 (36%) had surgical exploration; none had testicular torsion.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest a conservative approach supported by colour Doppler sonography when the diagnosis is unequivocal.

result.setting: 177 hospitals in the UK and Ireland (Vascular Anaesthesia Society multicentre prospective audit)

cycle1.result: Overall in-hospital mortality 7.3%.

result.other_findings: Risk of death increased up to fivefold with age over 74, urgent surgery, occlusive disease, limited exercise capacity, severe angina or cardiac failure, ventricular ectopics and ischaemic ECG changes.

result.topic: GP radiology referrals for lumbar spine and knee radiographs
result.setting: Six radiology departments and 244 general practices (cluster randomised trial)
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists' guidelines on lumbar spine and knee radiographs

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Audit and feedback (6-monthly) and educational reminder messages attached to radiograph reports.
result.other_findings: Educational reminders reduced requests by about 20% (absolute change -1.53 per 1000 per year lumbar spine, -1.61 knee); audit and feedback had no effect (about 1%).

result.setting: Oncology Centre, Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists calculation of 10 minutes per follow-up consultation

cycle1.result: 848 consultations in 81 clinics; of 67 clinics with finish time recorded, 19 (28%) finished on time and 48 (72%) were late by a mean of 49 minutes; follow-up consultations averaged 21 minutes.

result.other_findings: Consultants spent mean 37, 21 and 22 minutes with new, follow-up and chemotherapy patients; multidisciplinary clinics overran more (59 vs 31 minutes).

result.topic: Cardiac arrest team emergency drug availability
result.setting: Adult cardiac arrest teams in all acute hospitals in Wales
result.standard: Resuscitation Council (UK) recommendations and international resuscitation guidelines

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Drugs supplied to cardiac arrest teams varied greatly between hospitals; authors propose a simplified two-box emergency drug list.

result.setting: The Dorset Cleft Centre, Poole Hospital

cycle1.result: Good early facial growth with dental arch relationships appropriate for age; only minor speech discrepancies; no patients required pharyngoplasty.

result.other_findings: Single-surgeon series managed by a multidisciplinary team under a strict protocol.

result.setting: 121 British and Irish vascular surgeons (national study)

cycle1.result: P-POSSUM using POSSUM data items alone predicted mortality and morbidity after arterial surgery; extra items did not significantly improve prediction.

result.other_findings: 1480 records collected; 1313 retained after checks. POSSUM physiology scores alone gave accurate models.

result.setting: General dental practice, Glasgow

cycle1.result: Majority of patients failing to attend were unemployed.

result.intervention: Changes to recall letters and appointment cards (new methods of patient information) in two target groups.

cycle2.result: Statistically significant reduction in failed appointments.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 38 UK hospitals (Royal College of Physicians national audit)

cycle1.result: FEV1 recorded in 53%; arterial blood gases in 79% (range 40-100%); oxygen formally prescribed in 64% (range 9-94%); 35% of acidotic hypercapnic cases had no repeat blood gas and 13% received ventilatory support; smoking cessation advice documented in 30% of current smokers.

result.other_findings: Of 246 severely hypoxic cases, two-thirds had no confirmation of oxygen recovery above LTOT thresholds; performance lowest in patients not under respiratory specialists.

result.setting: North Western Medical Physics, Christie Hospital, Manchester (single institution evaluation)

cycle1.result: Phantom and water tank calibration agreed within 0.5%; measured dose within 2% of planned dose at all selected points.

result.other_findings: Phantom design for multi-institutional technique audit of prostate radiotherapy.

result.setting: Large university-associated teaching hospital (Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Birmingham); specialist multidisciplinary clinic versus other clinics
result.standard: Points of good practice from published guidelines and reviews (adequacy of surgery, T4/TSH suppression, thyroglobulin monitoring, radioiodine ablation)

cycle1.result: Inadequate surgery and inadequate TSH suppression in approximately one-fifth of cases; ablative radioiodine not given despite being indicated in 11.7%; thyroglobulin monitoring and action inadequate in some cases.

result.other_findings: Inadequate surgery and failure to give radioiodine were less common in the specialist clinic group (n = 134) than other clinics (n = 71).

result.setting: Faculty of Public Health Medicine members registered for CPD and specialist registrars (questionnaire)
result.standard: Model answers agreed by experts (no pass mark)

cycle1.result: Median uncorrected score 44 out of 80; no negative scores; highest scores on communicable disease and critical appraisal, lowest on Primary Care Trusts.

result.other_findings: Some participants felt the exercise was too general.

result.setting: General practice of 6,700 patients, north-west London

cycle1.result: Referrals to acute physiotherapy fell by 86% and to outpatient rheumatology by 51%.

result.intervention: Introduction of microacupuncture in standard consultations and modification of the computer system to record treatments.
result.other_findings: Likely considerable cost saving to the NHS.

result.setting: Group of general practices (University of Leicester study)

cycle1.result: Practices initiated an average of 3.5 (range 1-7) audits in 2 years, of which 0.9 (range 0-3) were completed.

result.other_findings: Ten of 16 completed audits were externally funded or facilitated.

result.topic: Paediatric anaesthesia for bone-anchored hearing aids
result.setting: Birmingham Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: 102 anaesthetics in 43 children; intra-operative complications 5.9% (airway-related); postoperative complications 17.6% (mainly nausea and vomiting); 71% day case.

result.other_findings: 16 patients were grade 3 or 4 intubations; laryngeal mask and propofol use increased over the 7 years.

result.setting: Four district hospitals in Ghana and Jamaica
result.standard: 31 criterion-based audit criteria for good quality care of haemorrhage, eclampsia, genital tract infection, obstructed labour and uterine rupture

cycle1.result: Many common areas for improvement identified across the four hospitals.

result.intervention: Feedback of findings and target setting; clinical protocols, reviews of staffing and training workshops.

cycle2.result: Some aspects of clinical monitoring, drug use and record keeping improved significantly.

result.other_findings: Criterion-based audit judged feasible and acceptable in developing country district hospitals.

result.topic: Gonad shielding in paediatric pelvic radiographs
result.setting: South Cleveland Hospital, Middlesbrough (radiology, radiography, orthopaedics and medical physics)
result.standard: Gonad shield present, appropriate and correctly positioned where one should have been

cycle1.result: Gonad shield present in 77.9% of boys' films and 76% of girls' films where one should have been.

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary team formed; radiographer training and introduction of digital fluoroscopy for follow-up patients.

cycle2.result: Gonad shield present in 85.2% of boys' films and 85.4% of girls' films.

result.other_findings: Three rounds of data collection (1997, 1998, 1999); audit helped obtain resources to improve technique and reduce radiation dose.

result.topic: Peripherally inserted central lines in surgical neonates
result.setting: Regional neonatal centre, Diana, Princess of Wales Children's Hospital, Birmingham

cycle1.result: Insertion failed in 13 of 125 babies; mean complication-free duration 22.4 days; lines inserted in theatre had fewer complications than those on the ward (P < 0.05).

result.other_findings: No significant increase in complications for lines used over 4 weeks.

result.setting: Archived insurance claims after motor vehicle accidents, New South Wales

cycle1.result: Treating practitioners wrote less complete reports than plaintiff or defendant experts; plaintiffs' experts more often diagnosed PTSD and depression, defendants' experts more often found no disorder.

result.other_findings: Completeness rather than quality was measured using a novel rating scale.

result.setting: Vascular Medicine Unit, James Connolly Memorial Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 100 proximal DVTs in 89 patients; one-year mortality 14%, 3% from pulmonary embolism; most treated with anticoagulants for six months.

result.other_findings: Patient mobility not considered in choice of heparin; asymptomatic events given little consideration.

result.topic: Lymphoma survival in a cancer unit
result.setting: Medical oncology unit, Bradford Royal Infirmary (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 5-year actuarial survival 72.7% for Hodgkin's disease and 55.7% for non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.

result.other_findings: Age and stage were the only predictors of survival; survival comparable with national and European figures.

result.setting: Paediatric otolaryngology pre-admission clinic, Sunderland Royal Hospital

cycle1.result: Clinic attendance 97%; 90% of attenders had their operation as planned; complications 2.9%; operation delayed in 20 patients, with no cause documented in 11.

result.intervention: Senior House Officer now sees the patient on the day of admission rather than in the nurse-staffed pre-admission clinic.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 175 general dental practitioners, North West of England
result.standard: Antibiotic prescribing guidelines issued as part of the audit

cycle1.result: 2316 antibiotic prescriptions issued; 81% for therapeutic reasons; amoxycillin most commonly prescribed (57.6% overall).

result.intervention: Audit with an educational component and issuing of guidelines.

cycle2.result: Prescriptions reduced by 42.5% to 1330; antibiotic regimens significantly changed.

result.other_findings: Sample sizes are numbers of prescriptions from 175 practitioners; other common drugs were metronidazole (23.8%), penicillin (9.3%) and erythromycin (4.8%).

result.topic: Montelukast in nasal polyposis with asthma
result.setting: Royal National Throat, Nose and Ear Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Subjective improvement in nasal polyposis in 64% of aspirin-tolerant patients; asthma improvement in 87% of aspirin-tolerant and 61% of aspirin-sensitive patients.

result.other_findings: Open treatment study; response not related to aspirin sensitivity.

result.topic: Sedation and analgesia for oocyte retrieval
result.setting: Reproductive Medicine Unit, Liverpool Women's Hospital

cycle1.result: Many women found single-dose intramuscular pethidine and prochlorperazine unsatisfactory and requested general anaesthesia for subsequent retrievals.

result.intervention: Intravenous sedation and analgesia with midazolam and fentanyl introduced from June 1999.
result.other_findings: Study describes patient acceptability, safety and cost of the new regimen; no figures in the abstract.

result.topic: Lacrimal fossa block for endoscopic DCR
result.setting: Pain Management Unit, Ipswich Hospital

cycle1.result: Block with intranasal local anaesthesia gave good intraoperative analgesia, minimal diplopia and high patient acceptability.

result.other_findings: Technique description with cadaveric study.

result.setting: National audit: 50 UK hospitals in first audit, 23 of the same hospitals in second (National Blood Service with Royal Colleges and Societies)
result.standard: Standard procedures for administration of blood and national transfusion guidelines

cycle1.result: Over 20% of hospitals had no Hospital Transfusion Committee; only one-third trained doctors in blood sampling; considerable variation in performance of standard procedures for administration of blood.

cycle2.result: Little change in practice between the two audits.

result.other_findings: Audit tools were developed and published and fed into national guidelines on administration of blood; sample sizes are numbers of hospitals.

result.setting: Large district general hospital (Bradford Royal Infirmary)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Maximum blood order schedule implemented and continuously revised; review by hospital transfusion committee; usage reported by site, procedure and individual consultant.
result.other_findings: Four audits over 10 years; strategies to improve usage gave encouraging results, but no figures in the abstract.

result.topic: Psychosocial assessment after deliberate self harm
result.setting: Accident and emergency department (Leicester General Hospital area)
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists' standards for general hospital management of adult deliberate self harm

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Simple service developments, including encouraging staff to use a comprehensive checklist.

cycle2.result: Recording of information in case notes significantly improved in all areas of the psychosocial assessment.

result.other_findings: The checklist proved particularly beneficial.

result.setting: Department of Dermatology, Singleton Hospital, Swansea

cycle1.result: Three melanomas identified (yield 1:277).

result.other_findings: Participant satisfaction audited by postal questionnaire at 1 year; authors suggest GP triage may be more cost and time effective.

result.setting: Casualty units of nine community hospitals, Grampian
result.standard: Assessment and treatment protocols for nurse-led minor injury treatment

cycle1.result: Baseline results reported but not given in the abstract.

result.other_findings: Describes methods for auditing use of new protocols.

result.setting: The Roald Dahl EEG Unit, Alder Hey Children's Hospital, Liverpool

cycle1.result: 31 of 54 children had a typical episode during recording; results helpful to management in 17 (31%).

result.other_findings: Stricter clinical criteria for ambulatory recordings are recommended.

result.topic: Barium enema detection of colorectal cancer
result.setting: Department of Radiology, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford

cycle1.result: 74 true positives, 4 false positives and 8 false negatives; sensitivity 90.2%, specificity 99.5%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: General practices and receiving hospitals in Mersey region

cycle1.result: 105 (78%) presented to their GP within four weeks of symptoms; 99 (73%) referred within four weeks; 95 (70%) seen within two weeks of referral.

result.other_findings: No evidence that referral delays affected 18-month survival; stage III or more was the most important adverse factor.

result.setting: General dental practice (five dentists)

cycle1.result: 533 of 580 (91.9%) administrations successful; facial palsy 0.3%.

result.other_findings: Only the practitioner affected success, and only borderline significantly.

result.setting: Shackleton Department of Anaesthetics, Southampton General Hospital (vitreoretinal unit)
result.standard: Surgical standards and patient acceptability not compromised (no numeric target stated)

cycle1.result: 135 (76%) had local anaesthesia alone, 13 (7%) local with sedation, 29 (16%) general anaesthesia; 96.4% of patients compliant; 98.8% of operating conditions good or excellent; mean perioperative pain score 0.1 (range 0-1); 97% would choose local anaesthesia again.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Ophthalmic accident and emergency department, Royal Victoria Eye and Ear Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 54% self-referrals; 17% GP referrals; 56% discharged at first visit; waiting times 30 minutes to five hours (mean two hours); non-urgent problems 60-70% of visits.

result.other_findings: Recommends GP ophthalmic training, an ophthalmic triage system and expanded outpatient services.

result.setting: 38 acute UK hospitals (1997 BTS/RCP national COPD audit)

cycle1.result: 14% died within 3 months (hospital range 0-50%); 34% readmitted (range 5-65%); median length of stay 8 days.

result.other_findings: Poor performance status, acidosis and leg oedema were the best independent predictors of death.

result.setting: One NHS trust (Southmead Hospital, Bristol)

cycle1.result: All-silicone catheters appeared to have a higher incidence of reported removal problems.

result.other_findings: Cuff formation when the balloon fails to deflate was investigated as a factor; actions taken when nurses could not remove a catheter were examined.

result.setting: Milton Keynes General Hospital

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: A telephone call after day-case surgery appeared to give parents effective support; children had few problems immediately after surgery.

result.setting: Large general hospital (Sunderland Royal Hospital); trained and untrained nurses and medical staff

cycle1.result: Overall deficit in knowledge of pulse oximetry; medical staff showed no greater knowledge than many trained nurses.

result.other_findings: Recommended improved education and training of all staff.

result.setting: 62 UK intensive care units (ICNARC)

cycle1.result: All but 50 (0.2%) admissions coded within 24 h; 96.1% coded at all levels of the hierarchy.

result.other_findings: Five conditions accounted for 19.4% of primary reasons for admission.

result.setting: Psychiatric unit (Millbrook Unit, Macclesfield): two acute wards, an elderly assessment unit and a secure high dependency unit

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Audit of documentation of special observations with literature review; no results given in the abstract.

result.setting: 12 dementia units (6 day units, 6 inpatient units)
result.standard: Dementia care mapping (well-being values and Dementia Care Index)

cycle1.result: Results gave some idea of quality of care and identified where improvement and staff development were needed; no figures in the abstract.

result.other_findings: Five patients mapped per day on each unit.

result.setting: Paediatric surgical wards, St James's University Hospital, Leeds

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Introduction of a paediatric anaesthesia information leaflet.

cycle2.result: Parents who received the leaflet reported greater satisfaction with information provision than a control group; many perceived lower preoperative anxiety.

result.other_findings: Routine use of the leaflet continued; leaflets should not replace verbal communication.

result.setting: Endoscopy Unit, Basildon Hospital
result.standard: UK Health Department two week cancer wait initiative

cycle1.result: 84 gastroscoped the same day and 11 had an ultrasound scan; inappropriate tests avoided in 16%; 70% dealt with at a single attendance; waiting time rose progressively over the first six months.

result.intervention: Introduction of a one-stop dyspepsia clinic with a nurse endoscopist and a purpose-designed referral form.
result.other_findings: Six oesophageal or gastric cancers found, all advanced; only 12% of patients with alarm symptoms had cancer.

result.topic: Open chest cardiac compression after cardiac surgery
result.setting: Two specialist cardiothoracic hospitals, Royal Brompton and Harefield NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 33 (46%) initially survived and 12 (17%) survived to discharge.

result.other_findings: Authors propose an adapted ERC algorithm with resternotomy after 5 min of unsuccessful conventional CPR.

result.topic: Cervical cancer radiotherapy morbidity league tables
result.setting: UK national audit of radiotherapy centres treating cervical cancer in 1993

cycle1.result: Complication rate per centre ranged from 0 to 67%; differences consistent with sampling variability.

result.other_findings: Authors argue it is premature to use complication rates for league tables.

result.topic: Weight gain during breast cancer chemotherapy
result.setting: The Mount Vernon Centre for Cancer Treatment, Mount Vernon Hospital, Northwood, Middlesex

cycle1.result: Mean weight change +3.68 kg (P<0.001); 64% gained more than 2 kg, 31% stable (within 2 kg), 5 patients lost more than 2 kg; 33 gained more than 5 kg and 6 gained more than 10 kg.

result.other_findings: 85% received steroids as antiemetics but steroid dose, tamoxifen use (37%) and menopausal status showed no significant effect on weight change.

result.topic: Reasons for placement and replacement of dental restorations
result.setting: A general dental practice

cycle1.result: 779 restorations placed: 364 (47%) initial placements and 415 (53%) replacements; primary fractured teeth 16%, marginal fracture/degradation 31%, non-carious defects 13%, primary and secondary caries 9%.

result.other_findings: The proportion of glass-ionomer restorations increased with patient age while amalgams and composites decreased.

result.topic: HRT and fracture prevention advice after hysterectomy
result.setting: General practice pilot audit
result.standard: Offer of appropriate information on fracture prevention (advice and HRT) to hysterectomised women aged 25-64 years

cycle1.result: 2888 (50%) ever-users of HRT; 2083 (36%) current users (both ovaries removed 53%, one ovary removed 40%, both conserved 30%); 80% of those given HRT reported some advice, 77% of those not given HRT had received no advice.

result.setting: General practice acupuncture clinics held two evenings a week

cycle1.result: Overall improvement of 73%, with 61% classified as significant improvement or cure.

result.other_findings: Retained needles and forgotten patients were the most concerning adverse effects and led to practice changes after critical incident meetings.

result.setting: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Glenfield Hospital, Leicester; single surgeon

cycle1.result: 81 patients underwent pneumonectomy and 38 avoided pneumonectomy by bronchoplastic with or without angioplastic procedures; pneumonectomy rate decreased significantly with experience (R2=0.98).

result.other_findings: Pneumonectomy could be avoided in a large proportion of main stem bronchus tumours without adversely affecting outcome.

result.setting: Hospital palliative care, Newark Hospital (central England)
result.standard: Oral care practice (assessment, implementation, prescribing, evaluation) and staff knowledge

cycle1.result: Baseline audit of oral care practice and nursing knowledge; numbers not reported.

result.intervention: Oral care guidelines and a programme of ward-based teaching were introduced.

cycle2.result: Improvement in all aspects of oral care and staff knowledge (numbers not reported).

result.other_findings: Additional benefits included improved professional relationships and promotion of further palliative care audits.

result.topic: Barium enema colorectal cancer miss rate
result.setting: Department of Clinical Radiology, Bristol Royal Infirmary, large teaching hospital
result.standard: Miss rate compared with previous studies (15-24%) where double reporting was not used

cycle1.result: Of 70 patients with colorectal cancer who had a DCBE within 5 years, cancer was not diagnosed on DCBE in 5 (7%); 64 diagnosed on DCBE and 1 as a sessile polyp.

result.other_findings: Of the 5 missed cases, 3 lesions were visible retrospectively, 1 was not visible and 1 examination was incomplete; 169 patients had colorectal cancer in the year.

result.topic: Health needs of homeless families in temporary accommodation
result.setting: Three council-run hostels in Hinckley, Leicestershire

cycle1.result: Residents had a range of health problems similar to those described in the literature about the homeless; families lived in cramped conditions with shared facilities and no safe play areas.

result.other_findings: Recommendations were made regarding an on-site health visiting service.

result.topic: Dietetic referrals for autistic spectrum disorder
result.setting: Dietetic service, Gwent Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: Draft protocol agreed within the dietetic profession

cycle1.result: Requests for gluten-free and casein-free dietary advice and/or management of food selectivity and dysfunctional feeding behaviour made up the majority of referrals.

result.other_findings: The management of these referrals was highly complex.

result.topic: Benzodiazepine treatment of convulsive status epilepticus in children
result.setting: Accident and Emergency, Birmingham Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: IV diazepam used in 17 of 26 patients; seizure controlled within 15 minutes of cannula siting in 11 (65%), median 3 minutes.

result.intervention: Change of first-line treatment from IV diazepam to IV lorazepam.

cycle2.result: IV lorazepam used in 31 of 59; seizure controlled within 15 minutes in 20 (65%), median 5 minutes.

result.other_findings: Comparative audit of two treatments rather than compliance with a standard; no differences in age, sex or seizure type between groups.

result.setting: Acute general medical wards, Sunderland Royal Hospital

cycle1.result: Less than a fifth of patients receiving oxygen had a prescription written in their medical notes.

result.other_findings: Authors highlight possible legal implications and the need for nurse vigilance.

result.topic: Management of severe hypertension in pregnancy
result.setting: 21 maternity units in the West Midlands region (85,658 births)
result.standard: Standard of care for acute-onset hypertension in pregnancy (not specified)

cycle1.result: 81% severe pre-eclampsia, 14% HELLP syndrome, 5% eclampsia; 7% admitted to intensive therapy unit; 70% of births preterm and 62% low birth weight.

result.other_findings: The audit highlighted areas where standards of care can be improved.

result.setting: Child and Family Therapy Service, Nottinghamshire Healthcare Trust
result.standard: New local standards set from the literature evidence

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Practice refined and new ways of assessment implemented.
result.other_findings: Authors state the audit cycle needs to be revisited.

result.setting: Inpatient Unit, St Margaret's Somerset Hospice, specialist palliative care unit
result.standard: Pressure ulcer incidence; Waterlow risk assessment

cycle1.result: 26.1% admitted with pressure ulcers and 12.0% developed pressure damage during stay; 95.3% accurately assessed at high or very high risk on Waterlow; 89.2% of ulcers Grade 1 or 2.

result.other_findings: 78.4% of developing ulcers were sacral; superficial ulcers often developed in the last days of life.

result.setting: Paediatric HIV in South London Network (PHILS-NET)

cycle1.result: 91 (83%) received 166 regimens; 60% triple therapy; changes due to virological failure in 60% and toxicity in 10%; 46% on first line and 37% on second line achieved undetectable viral load.

result.other_findings: Retrospective cohort outcome study; surrogate outcomes similar to clinical trials.

result.setting: Adult ICU, Royal Liverpool University Hospital

cycle1.result: 124 (39.1%) of 317 admissions had definite alcohol consumption; Group 1 (89, directly alcohol associated) median APACHE II 19 and mortality 41.6% vs 18.4% in non-drinkers.

result.other_findings: Authors note the small sample size.

result.setting: ENT Department, district general hospital, Gloucester
result.standard: Incidence of secondary haemorrhage after tonsillectomy

cycle1.dates: 6-week period after introduction of single-use instruments
cycle1.result: 9.5% re-admitted with secondary haemorrhage and 4% required emergency surgery; with single-use bipolar forceps (57%), 16.8% re-admitted and 7% needed surgery; none of the 43% with ties re-admitted.

result.intervention: Single-use bipolar diathermy forceps replaced by a new design.

cycle2.result: Significant reduction in postoperative morbidity (numbers not reported).

result.other_findings: Complications of new instruments can be identified by repeated audit cycles.

result.topic: Clinical governance implementation in primary care
result.setting: Twelve primary care groups/trusts in England

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews: PCG/Ts focus on supporting practices in quality improvement and setting up monitoring systems.

result.other_findings: Barriers were structural, resource and cultural.

result.topic: Prescribing indicators in primary care groups
result.setting: 145 PCGs in London and South-East NHS regions

cycle1.result: 121 of 145 (83%) replied; generic prescribing monitored by 106 of 121 (88%); antibiotics 76%, gastrointestinal 68%, NSAIDs 37%, cardiovascular 32%.

result.other_findings: Only 33 (23%) disseminated all prescribing indicator information on a named basis.

result.setting: Maternity units of eight district general hospitals in one health region (Wessex)
result.standard: Antenatal detection of Down's syndrome before 24 weeks' gestation

cycle1.result: 335 cases identified, 171 detected antenatally; detection 57% with serum screening, 52% with maternal age plus serum or nuchal translucency, 54% with maternal age 35+ and anomaly scans; least successful district 31%.

result.other_findings: 15% of women were 35 or over at delivery and 58% of Down's syndrome infants were born to them.

result.setting: Twenty randomly selected UK maternity units
result.standard: Evidence-based recommendations: steroids in preterm delivery, antibiotics at Caesarean section, ventouse as first-choice instrument, PGA sutures for perineal repair

cycle1.result: Median unit rates: ventouse first choice 8%, PGA sutures 0%, steroids in preterm delivery 0%, antibiotics at Caesarean section 7%.

result.intervention: No specific intervention; change over time assessed.

cycle2.result: Ventouse 64% (range 0-98%), PGA sutures 72% (0-100%), steroids 82% (63-95%), antibiotics at Caesarean section 84% (10-100%).

result.other_findings: 50 consecutive cases per procedure per unit per period; no relation between compliance and unit size, facilities or attitudes, but a positive correlation with Cochrane availability.

result.setting: Scottish lung cancer audit, all patients diagnosed in Scotland

cycle1.result: 1118 (30.8%) of 3855 patients received thoracic radiotherapy.

result.other_findings: In non-small cell cancer, diagnosis by a lung cancer specialist, disease extent and microscopic verification predicted receiving radiotherapy.

result.setting: Fifteen general practices in Sandwell
result.standard: Sandwell's published angina audit criteria and local clinical guidelines

cycle1.result: Aspirin 66.5%, short-acting nitrates 62.1%, beta-blockers 58.4%; smoking advice 83.5%, weight 75.1%, alcohol 75.1%, exercise 64.5%; BP check 77.4%, cholesterol 40.5%, glucose 33.5%; none of the standards met.

result.other_findings: Non-white patients were significantly less likely to receive nitrates, advice and BP checks; women less likely to receive beta-blockers.

result.setting: Elderly Mental Health Services, North Dorset Primary Care NHS Trust
result.standard: Formal falls risk assessment for older patients

cycle1.result: There was no formal means of assessing falls risk before the audit.

result.intervention: Staff awareness raised and a specific falls-risk assessment developed.

cycle2.result: Follow-up audits showed a change in practice, with the assessment widely used (numbers not reported).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Palliative care unit

cycle1.result: Action research study: STAS audit fully integrated into unit work.

result.other_findings: Teamwork, an external facilitator, management relationships and prompt feedback were key to implementation.

result.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit, Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children
result.standard: Practice standards for peripheral intravenous catheters

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Audit identified insertion practices, duration of therapy and complications to provide benchmarks.

result.setting: Department of Microbiology, North Middlesex Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Acceptable turnaround times for mycobacterial processing

cycle1.result: Median time to identification 21.5 days and to antibiotic susceptibility results 35 days.

result.other_findings: Liquid culture systems make acceptable turnaround times achievable.

result.topic: Dentist experience of antibiotic prescribing audit
result.setting: General dental practitioners in the North West of England

cycle1.result: 141 (80.5%) evaluation forms returned; over 90% found the audit easily understood and about 69% felt it helped change their prescribing.

result.other_findings: Qualitative evaluation; GDPs highlighted need for continuing education in antibiotic prescribing.

result.setting: Myocardial Infarction National Audit Project (MINAP)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Discussion paper on IT systems for audit.

result.setting: Cardiology outpatient department, Glasgow Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Of 774 patients on treatment, 15% attended with their tablets, 28% with a note, 40% empty handed but confident and 17% empty handed and unsure.

result.intervention: Appointment cards stamped with the request to bring medications to the cardiology clinic.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Department of Ophthalmology, Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle upon Tyne

cycle1.result: Primary reattachment 67%, final success 84%; vitrectomies 1.5%, open conventional procedures 78%; visual acuity 6/12 or better 55%.

result.intervention: Increasing subspecialisation and organisational changes; shift in operative technique.

cycle2.result: Primary reattachment 87% (P = 0.0004), final success 97% (P = 0.0003); vitrectomies 48%; visual acuity 6/12 or better 49% (P = 0.34).

result.other_findings: Three audit cycles over 10 years; the 100% reattachment goal was still not attained and functional outcomes did not improve in step.

result.setting: Tertiary referral epilepsy centre, National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, London

cycle1.dates: follow-up at 6-monthly intervals for at least 18 months
cycle1.result: 20% had significant visual field constriction (monocular MRD 30 degrees or less); acuity and colour vision stable.

result.other_findings: No progression or resolution of field defects on discontinuing the drug and no relationship with dose history; males more severely affected.

result.topic: Outpatient management of pelvic inflammatory disease
result.setting: Department of Genitourinary Medicine, General Infirmary at Leeds
result.standard: Current standard of care for PID

cycle1.result: Chlamydia 30%, gonorrhoea 4%; with oral doxycycline and metronidazole, symptoms resolved in 57%, 18% persistent, 25% did not attend follow-up; partner notification discussed in 87%.

result.intervention: Antibiotic regimen for PID changed in the department.
result.other_findings: Treatment failure rate of 18% prompted the change of regimen.

result.setting: Group of hospitals in South West UK (radiotherapy physics)
result.standard: Detection of dosimetric errors greater than 5%

cycle1.result: No dose discrepancies greater than 5% detected.

result.other_findings: Differences correlated with complexity in some situations.

result.setting: Papworth Hospital, cardio-thoracic hospital

cycle1.result: Survival to discharge 20/79 (25%); ICU arrests 19/58 (33%) vs outside ICU 1/21 (5%); within 24 h of surgery 15/40 (38%) vs 5/39; reopened within 10 min 14/29 (48%) vs 6/50 (12%).

result.other_findings: All 12 patients reopened on the ward died; 818 confirmed in-hospital arrests overall.

result.topic: Lingual nerve injury after wisdom tooth removal
result.setting: High street dental practice
result.standard: Established lingual nerve injury rates reported elsewhere

cycle1.result: Low incidence of lingual nerve trauma, comparable with that reported elsewhere (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: District nursing practice
result.standard: UKCC Guidelines for Records and Record Keeping (1998)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Discussion article suggesting audit of nursing documentation.

result.setting: ENT Department, Poole Hospital NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Recurrent bleed rate 33% after SPA ligation/diathermy, higher than published results; mean stay 3.3 days.

result.other_findings: 563 patients admitted with epistaxis over two years; failures corrected with anterior ethmoidal ligation or embolisation.

result.setting: Oncology unit, University Hospitals of Leicester, large teaching hospital
result.standard: Mouth care practice and staff knowledge

cycle1.result: Oral problems common but under-reported, underdiagnosed, inadequately treated and inadequately documented; nursing knowledge deficits.

result.intervention: Oral care guidelines, patient information leaflets, posters and staff education programme.

cycle2.result: Significant improvements in diagnosis and treatment of oral problems and increased patient reporting (numbers not reported).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Dermatology beds in Greater Manchester

cycle1.result: 90% admitted for disease severity; inability to cope 40%, investigation or observation 33%, coexisting medical factors 17%; 87% benefited and DLQI improved by 42%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Department of Otolaryngology, Royal Hospital for Sick Children, Edinburgh
result.standard: SIGN guidelines (January 1999) on indications for tonsillectomy

cycle1.result: Documentation of number of tonsillitis attacks 30%; adherence to SIGN in documented cases 75%.

result.intervention: Publication of SIGN guidelines, then presentation of the results of cohorts 1 and 2.
result.other_findings: Second cohort after SIGN showed documentation 74% and adherence 80%.

result.setting: Two teaching hospitals of the Nottingham Cancer Centre

cycle1.result: Of 186 patients, 52 had cancer pain and 47 assessed; more than half had unrelieved pain that was severe at worst.

result.other_findings: Uncontrolled pain was associated with no formal assessment, no pain-care plan and not being seen by the palliative care team.

result.setting: District nursing, Southmead Hospital, Bristol

cycle1.result: 22 (14%) reported catheter removal problems in the previous year, 15 (68%) with all-silicone and 15 (68%) with suprapubic catheters; cuff formation noted in 60%.

result.other_findings: In vitro study confirmed increased withdrawal resistance from cuff formation with all-silicone catheters.

result.setting: Specialist cancer hospital, St Luke's Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Referral of dying inpatients to the palliative care service

cycle1.result: Relatively few dying patients were referred to the palliative care team.

result.intervention: Audit data presented on several occasions to nursing and medical staff.
result.other_findings: Many final admissions were for active anti-cancer treatment and short.

result.setting: Department of Anaesthesia, The New Children's Hospital, Sydney

cycle1.result: Postoperative vomiting 15.6%; 2 overnight admissions; 1 readmission on day 4 for haemorrhage.

result.other_findings: 80% of parents satisfied with day stay; about three-quarters rated pain moderate or severe at some stage.

result.setting: Wards of a non-specialist hospital, Altnagelvin Hospital, Londonderry
result.standard: Standard of current practice in syringe driver use (MDA 1998 concerns)

cycle1.result: Many areas of unregulated practice in setting up, monitoring and maintaining syringe drivers; drug choice, doses, evaluation and review of treatment were also of concern.

result.other_findings: Guidelines for syringe driver use in non-specialist hospitals were proposed.

result.topic: Specialist nurse intervention for poor glycaemic control
result.setting: Department of Diabetes and Endocrinology, University Hospital Aintree, Liverpool

cycle1.result: 63% achieved improvement in HbA1c with no increase in weight or hypoglycaemia; the 37% non-improvers showed a mean deterioration in HbA1c.

result.other_findings: Intervention involved re-education, dietary advice and insulin adjustment; outcome evaluation rather than audit against a standard.

result.setting: Department of Genitourinary Medicine, Derriford Hospital, Plymouth

cycle1.result: Outcome known in 137; 83 (61%) clear at three months (single procedures 57%, repeat 78%); recurrence 33 (24%).

result.other_findings: No difference in outcome between smokers and non-smokers.

result.setting: National UK study of NHS consultants performing retinal detachment surgery (Royal College of Ophthalmologists)

cycle1.result: Methods paper: 256/671 (38%) responding consultants performed retinal detachment surgery; 768 patients from 167 consultants recruited.

result.other_findings: Validation suggested no significant selection or reporting bias.

result.setting: National UK study, 167 consultant ophthalmologists (Royal College of Ophthalmologists)

cycle1.result: Overall single-procedure reattachment 77% (95% CI 73.9-80.2); specialists 82% vs non-specialists 71%.

result.other_findings: For grade 2 detachments, specialists 87% vs non-specialists 70% after case-mix adjustment; the study offers standards for surgeons to audit against.

result.topic: Audit activity in palliative care services
result.setting: Hospice and palliative care services in the UK and Republic of Ireland

cycle1.result: Response rate 60%; 73% audit their services and 79% of these changed services; physical care audited 61%, bereavement 17%, training 13%, psychological and spiritual care 12%.

result.other_findings: Barriers were lack of time, expertise and measurement tools.

result.setting: Department of Respiratory Medicine, Birmingham Heartlands Hospital; pre-hospital and hospital emergency care
result.standard: National COPD guidelines: initial FiO2 no more than 0.28

cycle1.result: Oxygen with FiO2 above 0.28 was common and predominantly initiated in the ambulance (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Patient awareness, disease identification aids and ambulance protocols suggested for improvement.

result.topic: Contraceptive service provision in general practice
result.setting: North Lambeth Primary Care Commissioning Group general practices, London
result.standard: Literature-derived factors for effective, acceptable, accessible and equitable contraceptive services

cycle1.result: Scope for development in all key areas; practice leaflet and waiting area information on contraceptive services generally limited.

result.other_findings: Recommendations covered information provision, staff training and confidential access.

result.setting: Saint James's Hospital, Dublin, 650-bed tertiary referral hospital
result.standard: Comparison with trial evidence and 1992 figures

cycle1.result: Revascularisation 72% (thrombolysis 67%, primary angioplasty 5%) vs 35% in 1992; aspirin or warfarin 99%, beta-blockers 67%, ACE inhibitors 34%, statins 28%; case fatality 16%.

result.other_findings: Mean 178 transmural infarctions a year; late presentation (15%) was the main reason for no thrombolysis.

result.topic: POSSUM in head and neck surgery
result.setting: Department of ENT, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff

cycle1.result: POSSUM valid for morbidity but more accurate for high-risk groups; neither POSSUM nor P-POSSUM accurately predicted mortality.

result.other_findings: Radiotherapy (P = 0.002) and previous surgery (P = 0.007) were significant for postoperative complications.

result.setting: Teaching hospital and community, Llandough Hospital, Cardiff
result.standard: National Service Framework for coronary heart disease: 80-90% prescribed appropriate secondary prevention by April 2002

cycle1.result: At discharge, unless contraindicated: aspirin 100%, beta-blockers 84%, statin and/or dietetic advice 66%, ACE inhibitors in heart failure 97%.

result.other_findings: At 1-2 years, cholesterol remained above 5.0 mmol/l in 25%, 24% had stopped beta-blockers and ACE inhibitors stayed at low dose in half.

result.setting: Irish psychiatric service, University College Hospital Galway

cycle1.result: 33 of 69 eligible entered switch study; 23 of 33 still on risperidone at 6 months, 19 at 12 months and 13 at 2 years.

result.other_findings: At 2 years, 19 of 32 surviving switchers had clinically detrimental events vs none of 33 non-consenters.

result.setting: Two general practices

cycle1.result: Reanalysis with Shewhart control charts distinguished low prescribers (common cause variation) and high prescribers, one affected by special cause variation.

result.other_findings: Original improvement effort produced only modest improvements; different actions were needed for high and low prescribers.

result.topic: Two-week wait referral for suspected colorectal cancer
result.setting: Rapid access colorectal clinic, Darlington Memorial Hospital and Bishop Auckland General Hospital, South Durham Health Care Trust
result.standard: Department of Health two week rule: suspected colorectal cancer seen within two weeks of GP referral; referral guideline criteria

cycle1.result: 96.2% given appointments within two weeks; 97.4% of referrals incomplete and 37.6% did not comply with the guidelines.

result.other_findings: 21 colorectal cancers (8.9%) diagnosed; early cancer detection rate 4.6%; guideline compliance was associated with higher cancer detection.

result.setting: District general hospital, Kingsmill Hospital, Sutton-in-Ashfield

cycle1.result: 301 (30.1%) did not meet accepted guidelines; no malignancy would have been missed if guidelines applied; malignancy in 17 patients, all died.

result.other_findings: Waiting time 18 weeks; normal endoscopy in 32.3%; no significant difference in pathology detection between groups once malignancy excluded.

result.topic: Pressure ulcer risk assessment and prevention
result.setting: RCN national pilot audit project across recruited sites
result.standard: RCN clinical guideline on pressure ulcer risk assessment and prevention

cycle1.result: Baseline audit provisional results reported; no figures given in abstract.

result.intervention: Tailored, evidence-based dissemination and implementation strategy with implementation resources and local initiatives.
result.other_findings: Project due for completion at the end of 2002, with final results to be published later.

result.setting: NHS Breast Screening Programme units, national annual audit (BASO-NHSBSP)
result.standard: NHSBSP clinical outcome measures defined by surgeons, radiologists and pathologists; preoperative diagnosis rate minimum standard 70 per cent or more

cycle1.result: Preoperative diagnosis rate 63 per cent; lymph node status recorded in 81 per cent.

result.intervention: Feedback of results and dissemination of good practice at local and national level.

cycle2.result: Preoperative diagnosis rate 87 per cent; lymph node status recorded in 93 per cent.

result.other_findings: Use of core biopsy increased over fine-needle cytology. No significant change in the number of women treated by low case-load surgeons, and waiting times for surgery increased.

result.setting: 21 maternity units in the West Midlands Region, multicentre cyclical criterion audit
result.standard: Audit standards for care of severe hypertensive illness in pregnancy (not detailed in abstract)

cycle1.result: Baseline compliance with audit standards measured; figures not given in abstract.

result.intervention: Feedback of baseline results to each hospital, a high risk monitoring chart and an eclampsia treatment pack.

cycle2.result: Compliance increased in all but one standard; figures not given in abstract.

result.other_findings: Authors state further improvements in quality of care are still needed.

result.topic: External cephalic version for breech presentation
result.setting: Royal Hampshire County Hospital, Winchester

cycle1.result: 102 breech presentations at term; 47 women had ECV with 55% success and no adverse outcomes; only 49% of women with uncomplicated breech agreed to ECV.

result.other_findings: Parity, non-extended breech and posterior placenta were independently associated with higher success; authors suggest a basic ultrasound scan should form part of the procedure.

result.setting: Prospective regional audit, South and West of England
result.standard: Basic staging procedures for endometrial cancer (minimum data set defined)

cycle1.result: Only one-third of patients had basic staging procedures performed fully.

result.other_findings: Limited tertiary referral to a gynaecological oncologist.

result.topic: Outpatient parenteral antibiotic therapy for bone and joint infection
result.setting: Infection and Immunodeficiency Unit (Tayside), ambulatory and home setting

cycle1.result: Mean cost per episode £1749.15 ambulatory teicoplanin vs £11 400 inpatient vs £2546 hypothetical oral linezolid at home.

result.other_findings: Teicoplanin therapeutic drug monitoring appeared valuable and serum levels appeared to correlate with good clinical outcomes.

result.setting: Hospital-based consultant orthodontists, UK-wide audit
result.standard: Audit used to establish a benchmark outcome standard for consultant fixed appliance treatment

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Paper describes how a treatment outcome standard was developed from the audit; findings not given in abstract.

result.setting: UK radiotherapy practitioners, national survey

cycle1.result: 15 used MRI to set GTV; 12 added 1 cm PTV margin; 9 used CT planning; 14 gave 50-55 Gy with 8 different dose/fractionation schedules; 2 centres gave written side-effect information.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest developing a national treatment protocol.

result.topic: Case identification for myocardial infarction audit
result.setting: 20 hospitals across the Yorkshire region

cycle1.result: Hospital coding identified 1668 (77.5%) AMI cases, missing 22.5%; 30-day mortality 15.9% for WHO-criteria patients (n=1391) vs 24.2% for the total cohort.

result.other_findings: Biochemistry and coronary care registers had lower sensitivity and positive predictive value than coding; multiple methods of case identification recommended.

result.topic: Basal cell carcinoma incomplete excision rate
result.setting: Department of Plastic Surgery, Mater Misericordiae Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 10 of 126 lesions showed incomplete excision on histology.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Hepatitis B vaccination status of healthcare staff
result.setting: General dental practices in two health authorities in Lancashire, postal questionnaire
result.standard: British Dental Association recommendations on vaccination against hepatitis B

cycle1.result: Vaccinated: 98.9% of dentists, 96.7% of nurses, 72.7% of non-clinical staff. Written evidence of immune status: 46.5% of dentists, 51.0% of nurses, 62.5% of non-clinical staff.

result.other_findings: 85% of practices responded (187 dentists, 270 nurses, 132 non-clinical staff); fewer had a blood test in the past five years.

result.topic: First-line neuroimaging in suspected acute stroke
result.setting: Stoke Mandeville Hospital, district general hospital, in-patients
result.standard: Local policy of diffusion-weighted MRI as first-line neuroimaging for suspected acute stroke

cycle1.result: Audit standard achieved in 88 (73.9%) of 119 MRI-safe patients; 31 had CT first because of lack of MRI capacity.

result.other_findings: Repeat neuroimaging in 16 (12.9%); mean study time 13 min for MRI vs 11 min for CT.

result.setting: St Thomas' Hospital, London, single centre

cycle1.result: 39% extubated within 6 h, 89% within 24 h and 95% within 48 h.

result.other_findings: Delayed extubation associated with poor left ventricular, renal and pulmonary function, high Euroscore, and type, duration and urgency of surgery.

result.setting: Arrowe Park Hospital, Wirral, large district general hospital
result.standard: Recently published recommendations and guidelines for open access echocardiography (not specified)

cycle1.result: Waiting time for open access echo shorter than for outpatient clinic; numeric compliance not reported in abstract.

result.other_findings: Echo for LV systolic function should be done only if the ECG is abnormal; ECG interpretation in primary care was unreliable.

result.setting: GP non-principals in the West of Scotland, postal questionnaire

cycle1.result: 79% response; 83% involved in three or fewer audits; 48% of 378 claimed audits not completed; 68% no audit as non-principal; 64% need training in audit method.

result.other_findings: 71% said they were not expected to take part in audit in their non-principal post.

result.topic: Incident monitoring versus chart review in intensive care
result.setting: Tertiary 12-bed closed adult and paediatric ICU, John Hunter Hospital, Newcastle, NSW

cycle1.result: Facilitated incident monitoring: 100 reports identifying 221 incidents, 84% preventable. Medical chart review: 132 adverse events in 48% of charts, 20% preventable.

result.other_findings: Incident monitoring identified few iatrogenic infections, pain management problems or problems leading to ICU admission; system causation evident in 41% of chart review adverse events.

result.topic: Radiotherapy treatment interruptions and waiting times
result.setting: All UK radiotherapy centres, national audit of head and neck cancer radiotherapy
result.standard: Published guidelines on compensation for treatment gaps and national waiting time targets

cycle1.result: 55 of 56 centres returned data. 1467 (55%) had one or more interruptions; of these 56% still completed on time but 32% had no attempted compensation. Seven centres had no interruption policy. Mean time from first clinic visit to radiotherapy 40 days; six centres averaged under 28 days.

result.other_findings: Centres whose policies included treatment on bank holidays achieved higher compliance and fewer prolonged cases.

result.topic: Radiotherapy treatment interruptions and waiting times
result.setting: Oncology Centre, Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge, plus survey of 62 UK oncology departments

cycle1.result: 22% completed EBRT without interruption; median overall treatment time 49 days; median wait to start radiotherapy 14 days.

cycle2.result: 94% completed EBRT without interruption (P = 0.0009); median overall treatment time 39 days (P = 0.001); median wait increased to 35 days (P = 0.007).

result.other_findings: 1998 data: 67% uninterrupted, median treatment time 42 days, median wait 18 days. Modelling suggested gains in tumour control from shorter treatment could be offset by longer waits.

result.topic: Thrombolysis call to needle time in myocardial infarction
result.setting: Letterkenny General Hospital, Donegal, district general hospital
result.standard: Cardiovascular Health Strategy: thrombolysis within ninety minutes of alerting medical or ambulance services

cycle1.result: Thrombolysis given in 31%; median call to needle time 200 minutes (rural median 227.5 minutes, n = 64; urban median 175 minutes, n = 37). Median arrival to CCU 90 minutes.

result.other_findings: Median time from symptom onset to calling for help was 119 minutes; 29% were more than 30 miles from the hospital.

result.topic: Child protection procedures in the emergency department
result.setting: English emergency departments with at least 18 000 child attenders per year, telephone questionnaire
result.standard: Two official 1999 documents on child protection procedures and staffing in emergency departments

cycle1.result: Many standards met; figures not given in abstract.

result.other_findings: Improvement needed in access to child protection registers, communication with school nurses, formal staff training and awareness of named professionals; more paediatric EM consultants and children's nurses needed.

result.setting: Orthodontic Department, Good Hope Hospital, Sutton Coldfield, multioperator unit

cycle1.result: Average PAR improvement 77.5% for the unit; clinician A marginally better than clinician B.

result.other_findings: Less improvement in right than left molar relationship, especially for clinician B (about 10% improvement). Paper mainly describes the COMP audit software.

result.topic: Alcohol screening tools in older people
result.setting: Old age psychiatry service, Maudsley Hospital, London

cycle1.result: AUROC 0.961 AUDIT, 0.964 AUDIT-5, 0.780 CAGE; AUDIT-5 at 4/5 cut-point sensitivity 75.0%, specificity 97.2%, PPV 83.3%.

result.other_findings: Diagnostic validity study; 'AUDIT' refers to the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test, not clinical audit.

result.topic: Out of hours interventional radiology workload
result.setting: Vascular unit, St James's University Hospital, Leeds
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists 1996 guidelines that units should regularly assess their out of hours workload

cycle1.result: 1093 (57%) under vascular surgeons; only 17 (1.6%) of these investigated out of hours; 13/17 (76%) had intervention within 24 h.

result.other_findings: 5/17 (29%) received thrombolysis, 7/17 (41%) angioplasty or stent; only 2/17 (12%) were referred from outside the trust.

result.topic: Laboratory interpretation of growth hormone stimulation tests
result.setting: UK NEQAS for Peptide Hormones, participating laboratories
result.standard: Consensus cut-off concentrations for GH response in insulin stress test

cycle1.result: A number of laboratories used out-of-consensus cut-offs; five laboratories (9.6%) reported equivocal results for specimens not indicative of GH deficiency.

result.other_findings: Some cut-offs were unrelated to the bias of the laboratory's GH assay.

result.setting: Hospitals in the South East of England, retrospective note audit and interviews
result.standard: National guidance on gynaecological cancer management (centre/unit requirements, FIGO stage-based management)

cycle1.result: Ovarian cancer: stage recorded in 53% (262/492); 81% (169/209) managed per guidelines. Cervical cancer: stage recorded in 60% (188/315); 76% (142/188) managed per guidelines; 40% (127/315) not assessable.

result.other_findings: Only one site met criteria for a cancer centre; most sites could not assemble a team including radiologist, pathologist and oncology nurse.

result.setting: Urban general practice with 9,463 registered patients, Glasgow
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists referral guidelines, including six weeks' delay after onset of chest wall pain

cycle1.result: 569 CXRs in 482 patients; 30% assessed as not indicated.

result.other_findings: Many chest pain patients were X-rayed before six weeks and most films were normal; follow-up films at under three weeks often showed incomplete resolution.

result.setting: Hairmyres Hospital, district general hospital, Lanarkshire
result.standard: Scottish Cancer Therapy Network (SCTN) minimum data set for breast cancer

cycle1.result: Minimum data set identified outliers from the normal range of process indicators; no figures given in abstract.

result.other_findings: Further local examination of outliers by clinicians under way; additional fields identified to refine the data set.

result.setting: Four tertiary referral centres in Scotland (Glasgow, Edinburgh, Dundee, Aberdeen)

cycle1.result: Annual GH recipients ranged 296-393, peaking in 1994; 296 in 1999, a 19% decrease since 1990, against CRAG projections of 500 in 1995 and 600 by 2000.

result.other_findings: Fivefold fall in familial short stature patients after trials ended; 98% of GH prescribed by general practitioners.

result.setting: Lothian Health Board, general practitioners of splenectomised patients
result.standard: Department of Health guidelines on post-splenectomy vaccination and antibiotic prophylaxis

cycle1.result: Vaccinated against S. pneumoniae 80.6%, H. influenzae 65.9%, N. meningitidis 48.2%; 74.8% on long-term prophylaxis; only 37.4% both vaccinated and on prophylaxis as recommended.

result.other_findings: Some of the highest-risk patients were neither vaccinated nor on prophylaxis.

result.setting: Stobhill NHS Trust, Glasgow, emergency medical admissions

cycle1.result: Cardiac 27% and respiratory 22% diagnoses; 67% received help from carers or family and only 7 (3%) reported less input before admission; 45% had seen a GP within the prior month.

result.other_findings: No breakdown in social or family support was found before admission.

result.setting: Department of Clinical Oncology, Western General Hospital, Edinburgh

cycle1.result: 5-year survival 2.6% radiotherapy, 0% chemotherapy alone, 5.1% chemoradiotherapy; radical radiotherapy 12.8% (median 58 weeks) vs palliative 2.1% (median 31.5 weeks), P < 0.001.

result.other_findings: Lymph node status influenced survival (median 37 vs 24.5 weeks, P < 0.01); gender and age did not.

result.topic: Organisation of head and neck cancer services
result.setting: UK head and neck oncology teams identified via 49 radiotherapy centres, questionnaire

cycle1.result: 90% of 108 teams and 45% of 11 sole practitioners responded; 335 surgical consultants treated 7500 cases per annum; 58% used the BAHNO basic dataset but only 32% could deliver workload information.

result.other_findings: Mean outpatient consultation time was 11 min; large variation in catchment populations.

result.topic: Chemotherapy nursing care in colorectal cancer
result.setting: European Oncology Nursing Society Nursing in Colorectal Cancer Initiative (NICCI)
result.standard: NICCI hallmarks and standards of colorectal cancer nursing care

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes establishing content validity of the audit tool through three stages of expert panel review.

result.topic: Chemotherapy nursing care in colorectal cancer
result.setting: European Oncology Nursing Society Nursing in Colorectal Cancer Initiative (NICCI)
result.standard: NICCI hallmarks and standards of colorectal cancer nursing care

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes development of the audit tool using the structure-process-outcome triad and the TELER system of audit.

result.topic: Patient concerns checklist in oncology outpatients
result.setting: Plymouth Oncology Centre, Derriford Hospital, outpatient department

cycle1.result: Patients found completing the concerns checklist an improvement, helpful for communication, information and staff-patient relationships.

result.intervention: Introduction of a patient 'concerns checklist' for follow-up visits.
result.other_findings: Pilot feasibility project evaluated by questionnaires to patients and staff.

result.setting: Vascular Surgical Society of Great Britain and Ireland National Vascular Database

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Opinion piece arguing for surgeon-led risk-adjusted outcome data collection.

result.setting: Consultant-led infertility clinic, Chelsea and Westminster Hospital, London
result.standard: RCOG evidence-based guidelines on initial investigation of the infertile couple

cycle1.result: Mid-luteal progesterone and semen analysis performed correctly with results available in only 33% and 2% of occasions; many patients lacked clearly documented advice.

result.other_findings: Some areas were adhered to efficiently; authors recommend a primary care infertility referral form.

result.topic: Dual diagnosis interventions in mental health
result.setting: Acute psychiatric unit, mental health nurses
result.standard: Key standards for dual diagnosis care based on national and local recommendations

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Training programme on dual diagnosis for mental health nurses.

cycle2.result: Improvement observed in standards of care; figures not given in abstract.

result.other_findings: Sample size small and statistical significance not determined.

result.topic: Team climate and quality of care in primary care
result.setting: 42 primary care practices

cycle1.result: Higher team climate scores associated with better diabetes care, patient evaluations and self-reported innovation; longer booking intervals associated with better chronic disease management.

result.other_findings: Team climate was better in singlehanded practices than partnerships.

result.setting: 23 adult intensive care units in Scotland, national audit of intensive care

cycle1.result: ARDS in 8.1% of ICU patients; incidence 16.0 per 100,000 per year; ICU mortality 53.1%, hospital mortality 60.9%; APACHE II SMR 0.99.

result.other_findings: Mortality higher than recent other series.

result.setting: The Cardiothoracic Centre-Liverpool, coronary artery bypass surgery

cycle1.result: 47.4% of patients received red blood cell transfusion.

result.intervention: Transfusion database built from patient administration system and blood transfusion service data allowing continuous audit.

cycle2.result: 31.6% of patients received red blood cell transfusion.

result.other_findings: Paper mainly describes the audit database methodology; p value truncated in abstract.

result.setting: Rochdale Infirmary obstetric unit, district general hospital
result.standard: RCOG Clinical Audit and Effectiveness Support Unit guidelines on female sterilisation

cycle1.result: Gaps between rhetoric and reality in many standards; figures not given in abstract.

result.other_findings: 134 of 655 sterilisations in 1997-2001 (20.5%) were at caesarean section.

result.setting: Saint Mary's Hospital, Portsmouth
result.standard: Two RCOG Clinical Audit Unit auditable standards for women labouring with a previous caesarean section

cycle1.result: Documented discussion of delivery options in 98% of notes; successful vaginal delivery 36/60 (60%) excluding those declining trial of labour.

result.other_findings: One in three suitable women declined a trial of vaginal delivery; one (1%) confirmed scar rupture.

result.topic: Palliative care access for ethnic minority patients
result.setting: Hospital palliative care team, Bradford teaching hospitals

cycle1.result: Bilingual health-care worker involved in 41% of referrals from ethnic minorities.

result.intervention: Appointment of a bilingual health-care worker in May 2000.
result.other_findings: Worker also provided a community-hospital link and bereavement and family support.

result.setting: A&E department, Crosshouse Hospital, Kilmarnock

cycle1.result: 238 of 1858 children (12.8%) had sports injuries; football 39%; soft tissue injuries 61%; upper limb 46%; 71% discharged, 26% clinic review, 3% admitted.

result.other_findings: Wrist injuries were most frequent (30 fractures and 30 soft tissue injuries); no children referred for physiotherapy.

result.setting: South Glamorgan Ambulance Service, extended trained crews, mixed urban and semi-rural area
result.standard: Agreed resuscitation protocols for ventricular fibrillation and asystole/EMD

cycle1.result: Deviations from the VF protocol in 27 cases (27.5%) and from the asystole protocol in 27 cases (16.0%). VF: 26 admitted, 17 discharged; asystole/EMD: 11 admitted, 1 discharged.

result.other_findings: Intubation successful in 94.7% and cannulation in 87.7%; most survivors were in VF responding to defibrillation alone (13 survivors).

result.setting: Mount Vernon Centre for Cancer Treatment, Northwood
