cycle1.result: 110 (45%) treated by radiotherapy alone: median survival 8.2 months; dysphagia improved in 77.3% with median relief 24 weeks, maintained until death in 40%.

result.other_findings: Radical regimens gave significantly better dysphagia relief than less than radical regimens.

result.topic: Management of high grade superficial bladder cancer
result.setting: Urology department, Southmead Hospital, Bristol, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Average delay 4.2 months from symptom onset to first cystoscopy; over 50% of high grade tumours invasive at presentation; aggressive treatment strongly associated with higher survival.

result.other_findings: A more standard treatment regime was advocated and a randomised controlled trial planned.

result.setting: South Tyneside District General Hospital, single surgeon

cycle1.result: 30-day hospital mortality 10.1%; crude survival 34% at 1 and 3 years after study; only 51% operated with reasonable prospect of cure.

result.other_findings: Authors attribute reduced mortality to improved surgical treatment, particularly in acute cases.

result.setting: Specialist respiratory unit, King's Cross Hospital, Dundee
result.standard: British Thoracic Society acute asthma guidelines

cycle1.result: PEFR recorded 52%, blood gases 72%, speech 27%, air entry 58%, exhaustion 4%; 93% of severe cases given corticosteroids but none given more than 35% oxygen; chest radiograph 87%, serum potassium 56%.

result.intervention: Severity marker stamp for case notes and treatment guidelines implemented.
result.other_findings: 78% had at least three of five objective markers of acute severe asthma.

result.topic: Management of high grade superficial bladder cancer
result.setting: Department of Urology, Southmead Hospital, Bristol, three consultants

cycle1.result: Recurrence at the original tumour site 60%; poor prognosis of grade 3 T1 tumours with or without CIS.

result.other_findings: Delays in diagnosis support a haematuria clinic; a structured follow-up and surveillance protocol is suggested.

result.setting: Adult urology unit, Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge, teaching hospital

cycle1.result: Total cost £147,796 for 159 admissions, 738 inpatient days, 131 operations and 615 outpatient visits; uncomplicated TURP £1140; diagnostic cystoscopy £130 outpatient, £240 day surgery, £430 inpatient.

result.other_findings: Hospital charges did not reflect individual treatment costs.

result.setting: Royal College of Surgeons of England Confidential Comparative Audit Service, national

cycle1.result: 160 surgeons returned data; mortality 0 to 5 per cent and morbidity 0 to 22 per cent; laparoscopic cholecystectomy had one-quarter the mortality and two-thirds the morbidity of open.

result.intervention: Confidential feedback of comparative results to surgeons.
result.other_findings: Of 33 surgeons surveyed after feedback, 39 per cent had performed further analyses and 15 per cent had changed practice.

result.setting: Beaumont Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Normal appendicectomy rate 22.8% (women 31%, men 15%); gangrenous or perforated 20%; mean assessment-surgery interval 16.7 hours.

result.other_findings: Considerable variation in antibiotic use; many investigations did not improve diagnostic accuracy.

result.setting: Meath Hospital ICU, Dublin

cycle1.result: Mean APACHE II 16; mean stay 5.2 days; ICU mortality 34 (13.4%); hospital mortality 20%.

result.other_findings: Continuous audit proved feasible and data collection became routine.

result.setting: Dermatology department, Royal Liverpool University Hospital

cycle1.result: Reasons for non-attendance included illness (28%) and problems related to appointments (33%).

result.other_findings: Authors suggest stricter follow-up of non-attenders including informing the GP.

result.setting: Mersey Regional Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, Liverpool Maternity Hospital

cycle1.result: Risk of major cerebral haemorrhage, VP shunt and NEC unchanged despite improved survival; recent reduction in pneumothorax and persistent arterial duct.

result.other_findings: Increased risk of chronic lung disease explained by survival; increased infection risk unexplained.

result.setting: Department of Anaesthetics, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes a bar code based hand-held computerised anaesthetic audit system (AxAudit).

result.setting: Large haematology unit, University College and Middlesex School of Medicine, London
result.standard: Threshold platelet count for prophylactic transfusion of 20 x 10(9)/l

cycle1.result: Lack of adherence to the threshold, with transfusions at higher platelet counts; major bleeding occurred above threshold when additional clinical factors present.

result.intervention: A lower transfusion threshold was recommended and instituted.

cycle2.result: 20% reduction in use of platelet concentrates with no increase in major bleeding episodes.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Department of Clinical Oncology, Western General Hospital, Edinburgh

cycle1.result: Crude 5-year survival 72%, cause-specific 78%, local control 72%; no significant difference between surgery and radiotherapy.

result.other_findings: Late bladder and bowel morbidity significantly worse in irradiated patients; bulky irradiated tumours fared worse.

result.setting: Ravenswood Medium and Low Secure Hospital, 5 secure forensic psychiatric wards
result.standard: NICE NG28, European Association for the Study of Diabetes and Southern Health NHS Foundation Trust guidelines (e.g. 2.31 CBG measurements per day; 70% of CBG readings in target range; ketone test after hyperglycaemia 100%)

cycle1.result: Non-compliance with diabetic monitoring 19%; 1.17 CBG measurements per day; 39% of CBG readings in target range; novorapid after hyperglycaemia 67%; ketone test offered 7%

result.intervention: Feedback sessions of audit findings with the MDT, information sessions on monitoring guidelines and dietary posters in patient areas

cycle2.result: Non-compliance with monitoring 9%; 1.32 CBG measurements per day; 31% of CBG readings in target range; novorapid after hyperglycaemia 68%; ketone test offered 37%

result.other_findings: Diabetic control worsened despite better monitoring. Between cycles 56% of patients had their diabetic care plan reviewed by a doctor and 25% were discussed with diabetes specialist services.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Birkdale Ward, secure inpatient unit, Mersey Care NHS Trust
result.standard: Trust standard operating procedure for prevention and management of VTE (August 2023) and NICE guidance that all admitted patients have a VTE risk assessment

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 0%; 68% appropriately assessed at all trigger points, 38% required an up-to-date VTE assessment

result.intervention: All patients needing an assessment received one and the SOP was disseminated to ward staff; SOP to be amended before re-audit
result.other_findings: The audit tool was adapted for long secure admissions and a defined data collection time frame was needed. Concerns were raised about the applicability of the SOP in acute and secure settings.

result.setting: Salford CAMHS, child and adolescent mental health service
result.standard: NICE CG155: height, weight, waist circumference, pulse, blood pressure, blood tests and ECG at baseline, 12 weeks and 6 months; 100% compliance expected

cycle1.result: Compliance below 50% for all standards; weight at baseline and 12 weeks 47.8%; blood tests 26% and ECG 35% at baseline; waist circumference 0% at any time point

result.intervention: Planned antipsychotic monitoring checklist with consent form and a running tab for physical health parameters in the electronic notes; re-audit planned in 12 months
result.other_findings: Cases dated from 2015 to 2023 and only 9 of 23 started antipsychotics in the last 12 months. In 30% there was documentation of non-compliance due to complex needs.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: 8 acute inpatient mental health wards, Sherwood Oaks and Millbrook Unit, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust policy 02.21: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission; NICE NG89 (stated as NG82) 2019: assess all acute psychiatric patients as soon as possible after admission or by first consultant review

cycle1.result: 69.3% assessed on admission (50% within 24 hours); 30.7% not assessed during admission

result.other_findings: Using Wells scoring, all assessed patients in cycle 2 were low risk (80.5%), with 19.5% of unknown risk because they were not assessed.

result.setting: Two Mental Health Services for Older People (MHSOP) inpatient wards, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE 2022 vitamin D guidance: all patients tested on admission; all with level 50 or below prescribed vitamin D; calcium replaced if also deficient; specialist referral if eGFR <30, hypercalcaemia or granulomatous conditions

cycle1.result: 30/34 (88%) tested on admission or had a recent level; 9 of 15 (60%) with insufficient or deficient levels prescribed vitamin D; 1 patient needing specialist referral not referred

result.intervention: Vitamin D awareness poster on wards, meetings with the ward pharmacist and presentation at the local MHSOP clinical effectiveness meeting

cycle2.result: 31/33 (94%) tested on admission; 9 of 12 (75%) requiring prescription were prescribed vitamin D

result.other_findings: Ongoing communication with pharmacists and rotating resident doctors was felt to be needed to sustain awareness.

result.topic: Physical health checks on psychiatric admission
result.setting: Battersea Bridge House Hospital, 22-bed acute mental health facility with three wards
result.standard: Local and trust admission protocol: clerking, mental state examination, physical examination, ECG and routine bloods all completed within 72 hours of admission

cycle1.result: 27 patients (62.8%) completed all five criteria within 72 hours; 14 (33.6%) delayed; 2 (4.7%) refused blood tests

result.intervention: Active physical health handover to the physical health nurse and junior doctors, with ECG available on the ward (details limited)

cycle2.result: Overall compliance for physical health checks increased from 62.4% to 96.6% after intervention

result.other_findings: Delays were mainly due to agitation, refusal of bloods or ECG and delayed consent; reasons were not documented for 2 patients. Laboratory result delays were also noted.

result.setting: Keats Ward, Meadowbrook Unit, adult female acute psychiatric inpatient unit, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Five key carer engagement domains agreed with patient groups and carer representatives (carer notified of admission, carer care plan, collateral history from carer, carer notified of discharge)

cycle1.result: Carer notified of admission 30%; documented carer care plan 50%; collateral information from carer 30%; carer notified of discharge 40%

result.intervention: Standardised Carer Contact Form introduced over several PDSA cycles, with staff training and competency assessments for nursing assistants

cycle2.dates: November 2024 to July 2025 (re-audit after nine months)
cycle2.result: Carer notified of admission 87%; documented carer care plan 60%; collateral information 87%; carer notified of discharge 80%

result.other_findings: Staff reported greater confidence engaging with carers and there were fewer complaints from families. Other wards in the unit adopted the form.

result.setting: Psychiatric outpatient clinics, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE NG225 and local trust standards for suicide risk assessment documentation

cycle1.result: Consent and confidentiality 4%; history of self-harm 28%; protective factors 52%; risk formulation 62%; plan and intent in those with suicidal ideation 0%; access to means 6%; shared decision-making 98%

result.intervention: Audit findings summarised and fed back to clinicians

cycle2.result: Consent and confidentiality 76%; history of self-harm 76%; protective factors 78%; risk formulation 82%; plan and intent 84%; access to means 14%; shared decision-making 84%

result.other_findings: Exploration of access to means stayed low and shared decision-making documentation fell. Suicidal ideation was present in 28% at baseline and 50% at re-audit.

result.setting: Centenary House community CAMHS, Sheffield
result.standard: Community CAMHS Physical Health Standard Operating Procedure for antipsychotic monitoring

cycle1.result: Blood tests 77% (10/13); ECG 85% (11/13); height and weight 62% (8/13); blood pressure and heart rate 62% (8/13); allergy status 62% (8/13); neurological examination for EPSEs 0%; only 6 patients had all parameters documented

result.intervention: Proposed electronic reminders, structured antipsychotic monitoring template, teaching for medical staff and re-audit in 6 to 12 months
result.other_findings: Prolactin monitoring was absent in the single patient prescribed risperidone.

result.setting: 8-bed Psychiatry of Old Age inpatient unit, Dublin
result.standard: NICE CG161: falls risk assessment within 24 hours of admission with interventions for identified risks

cycle1.result: 4 of 5 patients (80%) assessed within 24 hours with risks addressed within 48 hours; clinical documentation present for all (100%); 4 falls recorded, all documented (100%)

result.intervention: Education for team members on timely and accurate falls risk assessment
result.other_findings: Cycle one was judged compliant, but documentation quality and consistency needed improvement. Cycle 2 data collection was under way.

result.setting: Swallownest Court general adult psychiatry inpatient wards, Rotherham Doncaster and South Humber NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines and Ronaldson algorithm: baseline and weekly troponin and CRP during the first four weeks of clozapine titration

cycle1.result: Baseline troponin and CRP documented in 80%, baseline ECG in 90%; 5 (50%) had mildly raised troponin (>3 but <13 ng/L), 80% of these had repeat troponin testing; no suspected myocarditis

result.intervention: Recommendations to align local practice with Ronaldson and Maudsley protocols using locally agreed reference ranges, to be added to local policy; re-audit planned
result.other_findings: Repeat troponin tests were often triggered by acute coronary syndrome reference ranges rather than myocarditis thresholds. CRP rose in four patients, two from non-cardiac causes.

result.setting: Bradgate Mental Health Unit, acute psychiatric unit, Leicester
result.standard: Pregnancy test and gynaecological history for female admissions of reproductive age within the first 2 weeks of admission

cycle1.result: Pregnancy test within 2 weeks 14.3% (4/28); asked about chance of pregnancy 7.14% (1/28); last menstrual period asked in 1 patient; contraception and sexual activity asked in none; cervical screening up to date 53.57% (15/28)

result.intervention: Proposed posters, presentations and changes to prescribing software; re-audit planned
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Forget Me Not Unit, specialist dementia intensive care unit, Worthing
result.standard: Trust and Maudsley prescribing guidelines for indication, dose titration and physical health monitoring; target at least 90% adherence per domain

cycle1.result: 7/20 (35%) candidates for inpatient-initiated anti-dementia medication; of 6 offered, 5 clearly indicated (83%); all titrated per guideline; physical health monitoring completed in 5 (83%)

result.intervention: Raising staff awareness, disseminating results and visible audit reminders on ward lists

cycle2.result: 6 (30%) candidates, only 4 prescribed an indicated drug (67%); all inpatient-initiated medications titrated and monitored to standard

result.other_findings: The target was met in two of three domains by cycle 2 but indication remained below standard. Pre-admission anti-dementia prescriptions were 65% and 55%.

result.topic: Menstrual health screening in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Female inpatient psychiatric wards, Lambeth Hospital, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Active screening of menstrual and menopausal health during admission

cycle1.result: 3/44 (7%) actively screened; 8/44 (18%) had appropriate menstrual health intervention

result.intervention: Staff training, patient information materials and updated clerking prompts

cycle2.result: 28/45 (62%) actively screened; 33/45 (73%) had appropriate menstrual health intervention

result.other_findings: Symptoms such as dysmenorrhoea, menorrhagia, perimenopausal changes and amenorrhoea were more consistently identified after the changes.

result.topic: Mental health liaison response time breach documentation
result.setting: Mental Health Liaison Team at a medium-sized district general hospital A&E, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Core-24 one-hour response target; breach reason documented for referrals breaching the target

cycle1.result: 32 of 97 referrals breached the one-hour target (33%); 10 recorded a breach reason (30%)

result.intervention: Team-agreed breach codes added to the A&E assessment proforma, emailed to all staff, with posters in the team office

cycle2.result: 20 of 44 referrals breached (45.5%); 9 recorded reasons (45%): staffing 67%, multiple referrals 11%, patient left 11%, other 11%

result.other_findings: Documentation stayed low, and half as many referrals were accepted in the re-audit period, possibly because of Christmas and New Year.

result.topic: Social media enquiry in self-harm assessment
result.setting: CAMHS crisis team
result.standard: NICE 2022 self-harm guideline: psychosocial assessment includes enquiry about social media, its use to connect with others and its effect on mental health

cycle1.result: Social media enquiry 72%; social media used to connect with others 14%; impact on mental health 8%

result.intervention: Planned presentation of results, training and re-audit
result.other_findings: Of those asked, 97% used social media and all 4 asked about impact reported a negative effect on mental health. Self-poisoning was the commonest type of self-harm (48%).

result.topic: Insomnia management in community mental health
result.setting: Community general adult mental health team, South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: National guidance on insomnia management (Donaldson et al. 2009; NICE CKS 2025): sleep hygiene, CBT-i and appropriate hypnotic use

cycle1.dates: Patients seen over the previous five months
cycle1.result: Insomnia prevalence 58%; sleep hygiene advice 36% of relevant patients; CBT-i strategies 11%; combination hypnotics 15%

result.intervention: Education programme for the clinical team on sleep physiology, guidelines and CBT-i, plus a simplified sleep management algorithm

cycle2.result: Insomnia prevalence 63%; sleep hygiene advice 45%; CBT-i strategies 27%; combination hypnotics 8%

result.other_findings: CBT-i remained underused despite being first line. Zopiclone and promethazine were the most used hypnotics.

result.setting: ICU, Royal Liverpool University Hospital
result.standard: 100% of clinicians aware of location and contents of the difficult airway trolley; 100% of anaesthetists trained in difficult airway equipment

cycle1.result: 100% aware of the trolley; 35% had read the contents folder; 90% could name the equipment; 70% confident to use it unaided; 28% not airway trained

result.intervention: Designated consultant teaching at quarterly induction, simulation and mannequin training, case-based teaching and airway proficiency assessments at induction

cycle2.result: 100% aware of the equipment; 60% confident in its use; 100% airway trained

result.other_findings: Requests for an ODP at unplanned intubations rose from 50% to 80%.

result.setting: Critical care unit, University College Hospital London
result.standard: Intensive Care Society standards: cooling to 32 to 34°C for 12 to 24 hours after ROSC

cycle1.result: Effectively cooled within 4 hours 33%; maintained in target range over 24 hours 57%; mean CPC at ICU discharge 3.4

result.intervention: Introduction of an external noninvasive cooling device (CritiCool)

cycle2.result: Effectively cooled within 4 hours 57%; maintained in target range 70%; mean CPC 2.3

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: University Hospitals Southampton NHS Foundation Trust, large teaching hospital
result.standard: New local guideline allowing thrombolysis for massive and submassive PE

cycle1.result: Previous guidelines suggested considering thrombolysis in only seven patients in 6 months

result.intervention: New local guideline for thrombolysis of submassive and massive PE introduced March 2013

cycle2.result: 46 patients with massive or submassive PE (32% of all PEs); thrombolysis given to 2, but 6 had no contraindications

result.other_findings: Barriers were late recognition of submassive PE and poor awareness of the guideline change.

result.setting: ITU, Northampton General Hospital
result.standard: NICE clinical guidelines 50 and 83 domains for discharge summaries

cycle1.result: Frequent omissions: patient demographics (10%), doctor's designation (8%), bleep number (68%), plain-English summary for relatives (18%), relevant investigations (35%), monitoring plan on the ward (45%)

result.intervention: Electronic discharge summary template with mandatory NICE-based headings and prompts

cycle2.result: Legal aspects almost 100% compliant; reason for admission 99%; diagnosis 85%

result.other_findings: Pending investigations, nutrition plan, infection status, limitations of treatment and information for relatives now appear on summaries.

result.setting: Mid Essex ECT clinic, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: ECTAS guidelines: legal status, consent forms, memory assessment and MADRS documentation

cycle1.result: Legal status 5%; written consent/form 5 95%; Mini-ACE 5%; MADRS 0%

result.intervention: ECT discharge summaries introduced from November 2021, following earlier checklists and assessments

cycle2.result: Legal status, written consent, Mini-ACE and MADRS all 100% (excluding patients who did not complete treatment)

result.other_findings: The discharge summary improved communication with out-of-area referring clinicians and patient and carer satisfaction.

result.setting: Regional hypoglycaemia screen (hypopack) service across A&E departments, children's wards and neonatal units, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust (meeting abstract)
result.standard: Regional hypopack protocol: samples analysed and reported, taken while the patient is hypoglycaemic and before dextrose, and reports filed in charts

cycle1.result: 35% of patients hypoglycaemic (<2.6 mmol/L) when sampled; 54% sampled before dextrose; 35% of laboratory reports missing from charts

result.intervention: Redesigned request form, updated protocol and a summative report, introduced April 2006 with presentations to regional centres

cycle2.result: 49% hypoglycaemic when sampled; 64% sampled before dextrose; 21% of insulin samples rejected as haemolysed; 35% of reports still missing from charts

result.other_findings: The record is a meeting programme with several other abstracts, including a congenital heart disease delivery audit and a fluid electrolyte audit. Intrauterine growth restriction and fasting due to gastroenteritis were the commonest causes of hypoglycaemia.

result.setting: Altnagelvin Area Hospital, Londonderry, and Cancer Centre, Belfast City Hospital (meeting abstract)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: The record is a meeting programme whose matching abstract is a case report of thyrotoxicosis from testicular choriocarcinoma. It also includes a gout management audit and an ICU discharge review re-audit from other units.

result.setting: Departments of Endocrinology and Clinical Biochemistry, Ulster Hospital, Dundonald (meeting abstract)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Matching abstract is a case review: 12 of 16 (75%) patients with incongruent thyroid function tests had normal results on a different immunoassay. The meeting record also includes other audits (readmissions, documentation after death checklist, electrolyte supplements).

result.setting: Department of Pediatric Allergy, GATA School of Medicine, Ankara (meeting abstract book)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: The record is the 4th Pediatric Allergy and Asthma Meeting abstract book; the lead abstract reports two children with solitary mastocytoma presenting as bullous lesions. A few other abstracts in the book are allergy audits.

result.topic: Nomograms for axillary node metastasis prediction
result.setting: The Breast Centre, University Hospital of Llandough, Cardiff (meeting abstract book)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: The record is the British Society of Breast Radiology 2016 abstract book; the lead abstract compares MSKCC and Evidencio nomograms with post-operative nodal status and found both correlated with node status.

result.topic: Human factors and adverse events in theatre
result.setting: Cardiothoracic Department, Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Editorial proposing the RECORD model (report, evaluate, centralise, observe, record with video, plus audit and questionnaires) for studying adverse events in cardiac theatre; enrolment of 100 CABG cases had started but no results are reported.

result.topic: Soft tissue tumour referral diagnostic discrepancy
result.setting: Sarcoma Unit, Department of Histopathology, The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust, tertiary cancer centre
result.standard: NICE and RCPath recommendation that suspected soft tissue sarcomas are referred for specialist pathology review; discrepancy rates compared with the unit's 2005 audit

cycle1.result: Diagnostic agreement 73.4%; discrepancy 27.5% (15.7% minor, 10.9% major); 5% of discrepant cases benign-malignant discordances

result.intervention: No local intervention; in the interval referral guidance was widely adopted and ancillary molecular testing became routine

cycle2.result: Diagnostic agreement 250 (71.8%); 57 (16.4%) major and 41 (11.8%) minor discrepancies; 23 benign-malignant discrepancies (23.5% of discrepancies)

result.other_findings: Molecular tests contributed to only 3 major and 4 minor discrepancies; most discrepancies were interpretational. The authors support national guidance that all suspected soft tissue tumours are referred to a specialist unit.

result.topic: Heart failure management in primary care
result.setting: General practices in north-west England, Greater Manchester Heart Failure Investigation Tool (GM-HFIT) programme

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Qualitative process evaluation of facilitation of an audit-and-feedback heart failure programme; themes were macro and micro agendas, forming a facilitative unit and maintaining momentum. No audit results are reported.

result.setting: Department of general medicine, acute teaching hospital, Brighton and Sussex University Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians handover guidance (minimum of 3 patient identifiers, ceiling of care, task urgency, assigned team member)

cycle1.result: 12 different pro formas in use; 87% had 3 patient identifiers; 1% documented ceiling of care; 0% documented task urgency; 63% had a named team member for the task

result.intervention: Standardised weekend handover pro forma based on RCP guidance, launched with a teaching session, trust email and ward visits

cycle2.result: 100% uptake of the single pro forma; 98% had 3 patient identifiers; 60% documented ceiling of care; 88% documented task urgency; 100% had a named team member

result.other_findings: At 4 weeks (76 patients): 95% identifiers, 45% ceiling of care, 67% urgency, 97% team member. 88% of surveyed doctors felt the new pro forma improved safety; electronic handover software and handover teaching at induction followed.

result.setting: Combined Assessment Unit and surgical ward, Perth Royal Infirmary, district general hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines on surgical patient handover (minimum data set)

cycle1.result: 15% of patients handed over from CAU to ward FY1; 0% of handovers included the full RCSEng minimum data set

result.intervention: Handover tool based on RCSEng guidance attached to the notes and signed by both FY1s, policy that handover occurs after senior review, a named ward FY1 for new admissions, and teaching

cycle2.result: 45% of patients handed over; 100% of handovers contained all recommended information

result.other_findings: At baseline FY1s first learnt of 48% of new admissions on the ward round, and 60% of patients whose SEWS score rose between CAU and the ward were not handed over.

result.setting: University teaching hospital (inpatient notes; presented at the Nordic Orthopaedic Federation)
result.standard: NHS Litigation Authority record keeping standards, CQC essential standards and Oxford University Hospitals documentation guidelines (VTE assessment within 6 hours, clear plan, postoperative instructions, senior present documented, contemporaneous entries)

cycle1.result: VTE assessment within 6 hours 80% (available in 100%); plan and postoperative instructions 100%; contemporaneous entries 75%; consultant presence documented 80%

result.intervention: Findings presented at the departmental audit meeting to raise awareness of contemporaneous documentation and recording the most senior person present
result.other_findings: Second cycle at 6 months: contemporaneous entries 80%, consultant presence 90%. Junior doctor presence was hard to establish and EPR timestamps make contemporaneous entry hard to judge.

result.setting: Medical wards, Broomfield Hospital, Mid Essex Hospital Services NHS Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians medical handover guidelines

cycle1.result: Doctor survey: 12% used the electronic system for weekend handover; 89% found sorting jobs time consuming; 67% handed jobs meant for another grade; 41% knew who to hand weekend discharges to; safety score 3.18/5

result.intervention: New dedicated electronic handover database with a proforma, earlier structured Friday handover meeting chaired by a registrar with SBAR and a register, plus teaching, grand round and email from the medical director

cycle2.result: 100% used the electronic system; 47% found sorting jobs time consuming; 37% handed jobs for another grade; 89% knew who to hand discharges to; safety score 3.84/5

result.other_findings: Measures were from doctor questionnaires. Registrar attendance at the meeting and inappropriate or poorly explained jobs remained problems.

result.setting: General adult critical care unit, Manchester Royal Infirmary
result.standard: NICE CG103 delirium guidance; delirium rate compared with PRE-DELIRIC predicted rate (39%)

cycle1.result: Level 3 ICU patients: delirium at first assessment 65%, at any time 70% (16/23); 87% exposed to deliriogenic drugs

result.intervention: Two PDSA programmes: delirium teaching, lighter sedation with short-acting agents and daily sedation breaks, redesigned drug booklets and charts, then unit refurbishment with more natural light and clocks, dexmedetomidine and chart prompts for delirium assessment

cycle2.result: Delirium at first assessment 15%, at any time 29% (predicted 39%); 70% exposed to deliriogenic drugs

result.other_findings: After the first PDSA cycle (85 patients) delirium was 16% at first assessment and 44% at any time; the second cycle added less, suggesting a plateau.

result.setting: Acute surgical receiving ward, Hairmyres Hospital, NHS Lanarkshire, district general hospital
result.standard: NICE and Scottish Patient Safety Programme: 95% of patients to have medicines reconciliation within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: 46% reconciled on admission and 77% within 24 hours (abstract states 49% and 75%)

result.intervention: Emergency Care Summary access for junior doctors plus lunchtime teaching and email reinforcement

cycle2.result: Third cycle: 57% completed on admission and 84% at 24 hours; 89% had a complete medication history

result.other_findings: Second cycle showed 62% on admission and 86% at 24 hours with 93% accurate history; performance slipped at the third cycle and never reached 95%. Six patients were lost to follow up and three discharged within 24 hours at baseline.

result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, King's College Hospital, major trauma centre, London
result.standard: GMC and BMA/NPSA safe handover guidance: unstable patients known to seniors, tasks prioritised and unstable patients reviewed

cycle1.result: FY1 questionnaire: 38.5% felt handover was safe; 7.1% had sufficient time to complete the ward round; 15.4% could identify and prioritise unwell patients; 30.8% could identify outstanding jobs

result.intervention: Traffic light prioritisation categories (including weekend discharge and weekend admissions) added to the electronic weekend handover on EPR, publicised by posters, email and FY1 induction

cycle2.result: Improvement sustained across all parameters but smaller than immediately after the change (detailed figures only in supplementary table)

result.other_findings: Immediately after the change (8 responders): safe handover 100%, time to complete ward round 50%, time for bleeps 100%, prioritising unwell patients 100%, identifying outstanding jobs 87.5%. Measures were FY1 opinions from questionnaires.

result.topic: Neonatal cranial ultrasound scheduling and documentation
result.setting: Tertiary neonatal intensive care unit, Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth
result.standard: Consultant-agreed scanning schedule and local documentation standards; 100% of infants scanned to schedule and 100% of key documentation fields completed

cycle1.result: 52% of preterm (93 scans) and 44% of term (9 scans) scans performed to schedule; preterm reports with time documented 75% and scanning doctor's name 92%; no comment on IVH in 16% of preterm scans

result.intervention: Departmental audit meeting education (PDSA 1, no real improvement), then a local cranial ultrasound guideline, a documentation template in every set of notes, posters, email and a one-minute-wonder board (PDSA 2)

cycle2.result: 74% of preterm and 100% of term scans performed to schedule; 100% had doctor's name and time of scan documented; 100% of preterm reports documented IVH

result.other_findings: Documentation of when the next scan was due stayed poor (missing in 37% of preterm and 20% of term scans) and signature rates fell because the template lacked a signature box.

result.setting: Liaison psychiatry service at King's College Hospital, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Locally agreed minimum handover data set (patient identifiers, location, referrer, reason for referral, priority, risk, pending tasks, clinician name and signature)

cycle1.result: Overall completeness 40%; hospital number 2%; risk 22%; priority of task 13%; clinician name 29%; signature 15%

result.intervention: Education and a written handout at induction (no consistent improvement), then a handover proforma sticker, later a printed handover book

cycle2.result: Overall completeness 78%; hospital number 48%; risk 53%; priority 59%; pending tasks 100%; clinician name 97%; signature 97%

result.other_findings: After education alone completeness was 34% to 46%; immediately after the proforma it was 71% and 72% at two months. Recording of risk and contact numbers stayed relatively poor.

result.setting: Vascular surgery ward, large tertiary referral centre, Barts Health NHS Trust
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians 2009 standards for admission clerking documentation

cycle1.result: Presenting complaint absent in 19%; past surgical history absent in 45%; drug history 72%, doses and frequency 41%, allergy status 75%; family history 19%; systems enquiry 12%; vascular examination 59%, pulses 46%; observations 31%; VTE assessment 73%

result.intervention: Clerking pro forma based on RCP guidance (with AMTS, VTE, ABPI, investigations and nil-by-mouth sections), junior doctor education and a named FY1 lead per cohort

cycle2.result: Sustained improvement in record keeping; observations recorded in 62% (significant increase); non-significant improvements in nil-by-mouth status and prior investigations

result.other_findings: At PDSA 1 (30 clerkings, 28 on the pro forma) most domains improved significantly (p <0.05), but observations were 42% and nil-by-mouth documentation fell. A later check of 23 acute-take clerkings not using the pro forma was as poor as baseline.

result.topic: Cognitive screening on admission in older patients
result.setting: Acute Surgical Receiving Unit, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee, tertiary centre
result.standard: Mental Status Questionnaire completed on admission for 95% of patients aged 75 or over (project target)

cycle1.result: MSQ completion 14.99% (16.6% and 13.3% in the two five-day periods); no patient had a formal delirium diagnosis despite a mean of 5.4 of 12 risk factors

result.intervention: Sticker listing all 10 MSQ questions in the admission document, with signage, email to junior doctors and advanced nurse practitioners briefing new staff

cycle2.result: Average MSQ completion 81.33%; 100% on two days; 40% on the first day

result.other_findings: Compliance dipped at the weekend and with junior doctor rotation; there was no clear pathway for patients with low MSQ scores.

result.setting: Endoscopy unit, University Hospital Llandough, Cardiff and Vale University Health Board
result.standard: JAG/BCSP: excellent or adequate bowel preparation in more than 90% of colonoscopies

cycle1.result: 490 (80%) adequate preparation; 118 (19%) inadequate; 14 (2.24%) needed repeat investigation; 100% PEG preparations

result.intervention: Patient information leaflets with diet and medication advice, algorithm-based choice of bowel preparation triaged by consultants, and cheaper postage in padded envelopes

cycle2.result: 93 (93%) adequate preparation; 7% inadequate; no repeat investigations; PEG use 58.82%

result.other_findings: An interim re-audit of 873 patients at 3 months showed 83.5% adequate and 2.29% repeats. Estimated annual savings were £23,265 from postage, £12,000 from prescribing and about £150,000 from fewer repeat procedures.

result.topic: Fluid balance monitoring and AKI prevention
result.setting: Acute orthopaedic trauma ward, regional trauma centre, North Bristol NHS Trust
result.standard: Completion of six key fluid balance chart components (patient details, weight, running hourly input, 6-hourly input and output subtotals, 24-hour total); project aim of a 50% reduction in monthly AKI alerts

cycle1.result: Patient details 100%; weight 8%; running 1-hour input 80%; 6-hour input 83%; 6-hour urine output 36%; 24-hour balance 12%; mean 47 AKI alerts per month (October 2015 to January 2016)

result.intervention: Redesigned fluid balance chart, posters of correct and incorrect charts, handover scenario training, three-level e-learning modules, patient leaflets and regular feedback of AKI rates to junior doctors

cycle2.result: Running 1-hour total 96%; 6-hourly output 68%; weight 16% (after peaking at 80%); 24-hour running total 32% (after peaking at 72%); monthly AKI alerts fell from 50 (January 2016) to 19 (November 2016), mean down 33% to 31 (P<0.001)

result.other_findings: An interim re-audit was done in March 2016. Weights and 24-hour totals fell back after early gains, and staff found adding up the 24-hour totals difficult.

result.setting: Transplant Unit, Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, Cambridge
result.standard: Warfarin with target INR 2.5 (acceptable range 2.0 to 3.0); time in therapeutic range by Rosendaal method

cycle1.result: 0.38 INR measurements per patient-week; mean INR 2.46±0.59; time in therapeutic range 67.96%; 36 episodes out of range

result.intervention: Home point-of-care INR testing for all patients with results by email, a networked electronic INR and dosing database, and a dedicated daily VAD coordinator session for anticoagulation

cycle2.result: 1.24 INR measurements per patient-week; mean INR 2.48±0.6; time in therapeutic range 76.56% (not significant)

result.other_findings: Second cycle (January 2015): 0.9 measurements per patient-week (p=0.006) and 77.97% time in range. A small number of patients were out of range for long periods.

result.topic: Regional anaesthesia block room patient flow
result.setting: Regional anaesthesia block room, University Hospital, London Health Sciences Centre, tertiary academic centre, London, Ontario
result.standard: Locally set targets: 90% of patients in block room 60 min before OR start; 90% arrive within 15 min of calling the surgical preparation unit; 90% enter OR within 10 min of scheduled start

cycle1.result: 31% arrived in the block room 60 min before OR start; 69% arrived within 15 min of the call; 52% entered OR within 10 min of scheduled start

result.intervention: Audit feedback to stakeholders, preparing flagged patients in the block room with a dedicated prep nurse, a structured OR-block room communication loop and consistent block room nursing staff

cycle2.dates: Re-measurement 1 month after PDSA cycles (project September 2016 to June 2017)
cycle2.result: 53% arrived 60 min before OR start (p=0.04); 98% within 15 min of the call (p<0.001); 65% entered OR on time (p=0.03)

result.other_findings: Two targets remained well below 90%. Day-to-day variation in case mix and staffing limited flow, and the work supported extra staffing and IT tracking tools.

result.topic: Daily sedation holds in ventilated patients
result.setting: 10-bed combined ICU/HDU, Hairmyres Hospital, NHS Lanarkshire, district general hospital
result.standard: Critical care guidelines recommending light sedation with a daily sedation hold (spontaneous awakening trial); project target 80% of eligible patients

cycle1.result: Median 47% of SAT-eligible patients received a sedation hold; mean RASS -2.3; 7 ventilated days and 10 unit days on average

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary sedation hold protocol based on the 'Wake up and breathe' guidelines, tested in PDSA cycles, with staff education, consultant prompting and a daily audit form

cycle2.result: 96% of SAT-eligible patients received a sedation break; ventilation 5.5 days and unit stay 8 days; no adverse events

result.other_findings: During PDSA testing 65% then 79% received holds. Average RASS did not improve (-2.4), and medical staff were less aware of the protocol than nurses.

result.setting: ENT outpatient department, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Iterative restructuring: five ring-fenced aerosol-generating procedure rooms, PPE and powered respirator availability, nurse training and clinic template changes
result.other_findings: Iterative service evaluation, not an audit against a standard (the authors say so). In-person attendances rose four-fold (25 to 100) and mean aerosol-generating procedure time fell from 37 to 16.2 minutes; 20 of 33 recommendations were achieved.

result.setting: St Peter's Hospital, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (weekend handover lists and three random wards on an electronic SBAR platform)
result.standard: National handover guidance (RCP Acute Care Toolkit) SBAR components on a local proforma: admission date, estimated discharge date, presenting complaint, past medical and social history, escalation status, issues, updates and plans

cycle1.result: Admission date 51%; estimated discharge date 60%; presenting complaint 100%; social history 82%; escalation status 20%; issues 12%; important updates 71%; plans 100%

result.intervention: Teaching for foundation doctors, posters of the proforma, ward 'Careflow champions' and re-education at mandatory teaching

cycle2.result: Admission date 58% (+13.7%); estimated discharge date 80% (+33.3%); social history 92%; escalation status 67% (+335%); issues 29% (+242%); important updates 96%; plans 100%

result.other_findings: 710 handovers were assessed over four PDSA cycles. Admission date completion fell from 94% to 58% in the last cycle with junior doctor rotation and the COVID surge rota.

result.setting: Acute surgical unit, North Devon District Hospital

cycle1.result: Median blood test time to result 329 min (IQR 271-391.8)

result.intervention: Phlebotomy round re-routed to prioritise the acute surgical unit and other acute wards, with doctors asked to have request forms ready by 0800

cycle2.result: Median time to result 210 min (IQR 186-240), p<0.001

result.other_findings: The phlebotomy route had been set by hospital geography rather than clinical need. The effect on non-acute wards was not measured.

result.topic: Time to senior review in paediatric admissions
result.setting: Paediatric Assessment Unit, Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, teaching hospital
result.standard: RCPCH Facing the Future: tier two doctor review within 4 hours and consultant review within 14 hours of admission

cycle1.result: 92% (24/26) seen by a registrar or above within 4 hours; mean wait 104.2 min; consultant review not measured

result.intervention: Extended weekend consultant on-site cover, flagging patients awaiting consultant review on the handover sheet, and a tier two roster with at least two doctors on at all times

cycle2.result: 96.2% seen by a tier two doctor within 4 hours (from 82.9% in cycle 3, p=0.028)

result.other_findings: Consultant review within 14 hours rose from 53.3% (cycle 2) to 95% (cycle 3, p=0.005). Length of stay rose from 229 to 329 min despite earlier review; 177 of 288 data sets were complete.

result.setting: Emergency department, London district general hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists iRefer guidelines (2017) for plain abdominal radiography

cycle1.result: 79% of requests had at least one indication meeting iRefer guidance; 27% of radiographs diagnostic; 50% aided clinical management

result.intervention: Teaching session for ED clinicians on iRefer guidance and radiation dose, plus posters in the department and on the shared drive

cycle2.result: 87% met iRefer guidance; 47% diagnostic; 70% aided clinical management; 15% fewer radiographs

result.other_findings: Over half of studies needed more than one image. Constipation was a common indication even though a radiograph does not diagnose constipation.

result.topic: Infant pain practice change eHealth tool usability
result.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit, The Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto (single paediatric hospital)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Mixed-methods usability study of the ImPaC Resource (which includes a 10-chart pain audit and re-audit); median System Usability Scale rose from 73.75 to 88.75 and acceptability from 24 to 27.5 over three phases.

result.setting: Pulmonary hypertension shared care centre, Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Diagnostic accuracy study: the BSE/ESC echo probability algorithm had sensitivity 89% and specificity 68%, and 36% of low-probability patients had PH at right heart catheterisation; adding RV strain, RVFAC and IVRT (IMPULSE algorithm) cut false negatives by 29%.

result.setting: Renal transplant unit, The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: No published standard; unit guideline introduced after cycle 1 that all incidentally enlarged iliac lymph nodes are biopsied

cycle1.result: 11 (14.47%) had incidentally enlarged iliac lymph nodes biopsied at the surgeon's discretion; all showed reactive changes only

result.intervention: Unit guideline that all incidentally enlarged iliac lymph nodes at transplantation undergo histological assessment regardless of size

cycle2.result: 8 (4.85%) had enlarged nodes, all biopsied: 5 reactive, 2 with no nodal tissue, 1 chronic lymphocytic leukaemia

result.other_findings: The CLL diagnosis led to reduced immunosuppression. The authors recommend histology for incidental nodes with suspicious features or over 10 mm (positive yield 1 in 19, 5.26%).

result.topic: Pregnancy outcomes in rare inherited coagulation disorders
result.setting: Tertiary obstetric-haematology unit, university hospital trust, Leeds

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Retrospective service evaluation of 29 pregnancies: primary PPH in 38% (mostly caesarean births), antepartum haemorrhage 3%, no secondary PPH; vitamin K was documented for only about 60% of neonates.

result.topic: Liposomal bupivacaine versus rectus sheath catheters after laparotomy
result.setting: Colorectal service, English university teaching hospital, Royal Devon and Exeter

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Single-shot intraoperative liposomal bupivacaine (EXPAREL) instead of bupivacaine boluses via rectus sheath catheters, introduced March 2022 by early-adopter surgeons
result.other_findings: Outcome comparison rather than audit against a standard: median total PCA 270 mg OME with liposomal bupivacaine versus 396 mg with catheters (p=0.54) and length of stay 15.5 versus 16 days, with no loss of control on SPC charts; each catheter top-up took about 30 minutes of nursing time.

result.setting: Department of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery, University Hospital Galway, tertiary centre
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland Code of Practice for Surgeons (2018) operative note content

cycle1.result: Time of procedure 0%; elective/emergency 9.4%; anaesthetist 59%; complications 25%; additional procedures 12.5%; blood loss 0%; antibiotic prophylaxis 0%; closure technique 59.4%; uploaded to EVOLVE 28.1%

result.intervention: Theatre checklist poster, scanner in theatre with instruction poster and video for uploading notes, individual scanner accounts and staff education at M&M meetings

cycle2.dates: Third cycle, about six months after baseline
cycle2.result: Time 6.25%; elective/emergency 50%; anaesthetist 90.6%; complications 90.6%; additional procedures 75%; blood loss 9.3%; antibiotics 28.1%; closure technique 100%; uploaded to EVOLVE 90.6%

result.other_findings: Time, blood loss and antibiotic prophylaxis improved in the second cycle (28.1%, 34.3%, 43.7%) but fell again in the third. All notes were handwritten.

result.topic: Chest wall injury diagnosis in older fallers
result.setting: Emergency department, William Harvey Hospital, district general hospital and trauma unit, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Project SMART aim: 90% of chest wall injuries diagnosed at the initial ED assessment (informed by London Major Trauma System 2018 guidance on elderly trauma)

cycle1.result: 61% of chest wall injuries diagnosed at the initial ED encounter (30 of 77 missed; text also reports 61% missed); mean time from attendance to first CT 477 minutes

result.intervention: Thoracic trauma proforma with a modified PIC score and CT criteria, updated trust chest trauma pathway allowing contrast CT, a resus drawer for the proforma, and teaching, posters and email reminders

cycle2.result: 91% diagnosed at initial ED assessment (3 missed); time to first CT 169 minutes; proforma completed in 9 cases

result.other_findings: Modified PIC score use reached 26% of chest wall injury cases. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted teaching and the electronic record change prevented a digital proforma.

result.topic: Long-term outcomes after infant liver transplantation
result.setting: The Liver Unit, Birmingham Women's and Children's Hospital, and adult transition clinic

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Registered as an audit but reports outcomes only: mean IQ 91.13 after transplant versus 85.7 before (not significant); 31% had depression and 56% anxiety; 15 of 16 (94%) were in work or education.

result.topic: Paediatric and adolescent gynaecology congress abstracts
result.setting: 16th European Congress of Paediatric and Adolescent Gynaecology (abstract book; organisers from Athens, Ioannina, Bratislava and Belgrade)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Congress abstract collection, mostly case reports and studies. One abstract (P15, Rotunda Hospital, Dublin) is a teen pregnancy contraception re-audit: antenatal counselling 100% and discharge with contraception up from 22% to 58% (n=50).

result.setting: Community child health services, Middlesbrough and Redcar & Cleveland boroughs
result.standard: Local population immunisation rates / national immunisation schedule

cycle1.result: Children in public care had lower immunisation rates and more incomplete schedules than the local population (no figures given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Accurate assessment needed all the child's health records; some children thought incomplete were complete and vice versa.

result.topic: Audit teaching in academic general practice departments
result.setting: Academic departments of general practice

cycle1.result: 30 of 31 departments responded; 11/27 undergraduate departments provided formal teaching on audit.

result.other_findings: Survey: 11 of 27 responding undergraduate departments gave formal audit teaching; all 29 UK departments sat on medical audit advisory groups.

result.topic: Two-week wait suspected cancer referral compliance
result.setting: Department of Urology, St Helier Hospital, Carshalton
result.standard: UK Government 2-week rule for suspected cancer referrals (seen within 2 weeks); regional tumour working group referral criteria

cycle1.result: 82/234 GP referrals met regional suspected cancer criteria; 13% clearly marked urgent/cancer; 23% had no implication of cancer; 72% seen in haematuria clinic with median 56.5 days and none within 2 weeks; others median 21 days with 34% compliance.

result.other_findings: DoH figures recorded only 18 referrals over 3 months with 89% compliance, grossly underestimating the true workload.

result.setting: Paediatric Neurology Service outpatients, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff

cycle1.result: Of 27 children given topiramate, 6 had MAE; 5 improved after titration.

result.other_findings: Retrospective outcome review: 5 of 6 children with MAE improved on adjunctive topiramate; 3 had over 80% reduction in atonic seizures.

result.topic: Post-operative nausea and vomiting after cardiac surgery
result.setting: Cardiac intensive care, Bristol Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Nausea and vomiting in 67% of patients after cardiac surgery.

result.other_findings: Incidence audit without a standard: 67% had nausea and vomiting, mostly on day 1; 7% had it for up to a quarter of their post-operative course.

result.topic: Criteria based audit training in maternity care
result.setting: Makerere University Medical School, Mulago Hospital Kampala and Mpigi District health centres
result.standard: Criteria based audit standards of maternity care set locally

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Didactic teaching on criteria based audit, practical work in own units, ongoing support and follow-up workshops

cycle2.result: Improvements were seen in many standards of care (no figures in abstract).

result.other_findings: Staff were enthusiastic and produced simple cost-free improvements; follow-up needed to prevent waning enthusiasm.

result.topic: Adjuvant breast cancer treatment guideline compliance
result.setting: North Trent Cancer Network cancer units and cancer centre
result.standard: North Trent Cancer Network Breast Group adjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy guidelines (revised 1998)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 82% (chemotherapy 90%, radiotherapy 74%), similar across the network; compliance undetermined in 5%.

result.other_findings: On case review 22% of non-compliant incidents were justified and 16% reflected variation in guideline interpretation.

result.topic: Empirical antibiotic policy adherence in bacteraemia
result.setting: Aberdeen Royal Infirmary, large teaching hospital
result.standard: Hospital antibiotic policy for empirical therapy

cycle1.result: Poor use of the antibiotic policy, with inadequate (P=0.005) or excessive (P<0.00001) antibiotic treatment and a trend to increased mortality.

result.other_findings: 87% of blood cultures were Gram-stain positive within 24 h, but streamlined therapy was still judged excessive in 27%.

result.setting: Maternity department of a district general hospital, inner London
result.standard: Departmental antenatal action protocols triggered by booking risk factors

cycle1.result: 3673 of 15,658 protocol-dictated actions (23.5%) performed; actions rated clinically important by consultants 28.3% vs 18.6% for less important.

result.other_findings: Protocols were more often followed in early bookers, older mothers, black women and those with uncertain gestational age, despite a computer system and protocol manual.

result.setting: 12 referral hospitals in Benin, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana and Morocco
result.country: Benin, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana and Morocco

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Feasibility of near-miss audit; most successful in first referral level hospitals; ownership, leadership and senior staff involvement key; case note quality poor.

result.topic: Moving to paperless records in general practice
result.setting: Large multi-site general practice (Student Health Centre, University of Surrey, Guildford)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Case study: paperless working achieved in about two years; audit and quality improvement activity increased.

result.topic: Colorectal cancer histopathology reporting and lymph node yield
result.setting: Former South Western Health region hospitals, with a reference hospital
result.standard: Completeness of histopathology reports (nodes examined, nodes positive, Dukes stage, ICD9 code)

cycle1.result: Incomplete reports: 4.3% at reference hospital (629 reports) vs 36.1% elsewhere (918); mean nodes examined 18.81 vs 6.41.

result.other_findings: Dukes C ascertainment was related to nodes examined, optimal with at least 10 and fewer than 15 nodes.

result.topic: Cancer pain management in the community
result.setting: Community/primary care teams in Lanarkshire
result.standard: Scottish Cancer Pain Audit prescribing standards

cycle1.result: Pain scores recorded in 90% of 3259 visits; specific gaps in prescribing identified; 88% of practices submitted forms.

result.intervention: Results fed back to prescribers and used for a primary care education programme
result.other_findings: Continuous audit was achievable within normal care; stakeholder engagement was key.

result.topic: Shared care for long-term mental illness
result.setting: General practices and community mental health teams, Southeast London

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Development of the Mental Health Link facilitated quality improvement programme; not an audit against a standard.

result.setting: Action research project, Bloomsbury and Islington College of Nursing and Midwifery

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Discussion of Phaneuf's Nursing Audit tool, which had more disadvantages than advantages.

result.topic: Criteria based audit training in maternity care
result.setting: Makerere University Medical School, Mulago Hospital Kampala and Mpigi District health centres
result.standard: Criteria based audit standards of maternity care set locally

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Didactic teaching on criteria based audit, practical work in own units, ongoing support and follow-up workshops

cycle2.result: Improvements were seen in many standards of care (no figures in abstract).

result.other_findings: Same abstract as the BMJ report; follow-up needed to prevent waning enthusiasm.

result.setting: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Basildon Hospital

cycle1.result: VBAC achieved in 33.5% of women with one previous caesarean.
