result.other_findings: Colorectal surgeons appeared more conservative with fewer recurrences, without difference in postoperative incontinence; numbers too small for conclusions.

result.setting: Medical, surgical and orthopaedic wards of one acute hospital (Chesterfield Royal Hospital)
result.standard: Standard sepsis definitions and Surviving Sepsis Campaign management guidelines

cycle1.result: Some ward nurses appeared to have poor knowledge of the signs and symptoms of sepsis, severe sepsis/septic shock and some aspects of initial management (no figures in abstract).

result.intervention: Educational initiatives introduced to raise awareness of sepsis definitions and Surviving Sepsis guidelines.
result.other_findings: No re-audit reported after the education.

result.topic: Congenital heart surgery mortality data quality
result.setting: Congenital heart surgery centres in the UK (11 English centres in HES; 13 UK centres in CCAD)

cycle1.result: HES omitted 5% to 38% of infants operated on per centre, with a median 40% (range 0-73%) shortfall in deaths; 30-day mortality 4% by HES vs 8% by CCAD.

result.other_findings: CCAD had 1% to 23% missing outcomes in nine of 11 English centres. Oxford infant mortality (10%) was not statistically different from the UK mean (8%).

result.topic: Deaths within 7 days of ED admission
result.setting: Emergency department, Peterborough District Hospital

cycle1.result: Of 3521 ED admissions, 95 (2.69%) died within 7 days; 78 (82.1%) appropriately diagnosed and managed; 17 (17.87%) had deficiencies; 3 (3.15%) definitely, 3 (3.15%) probably and 6 (6.31%) possibly preventable deaths.

result.other_findings: 5 (5.26%) deaths unpreventable despite deficient ED care. New sepsis and undifferentiated presentation guidelines were being introduced with a planned re-audit.

result.topic: Vascular surgery process and outcome database
result.setting: Three health authorities (interdistrict audit, Brighton)

cycle1.result: 28% of initial assessment patients had an arteriogram, 9% were admitted immediately and 7% discharged to the GP; at follow-up main symptom cured in 38%, unchanged in 27%, worse in 5%.

result.other_findings: Preliminary results; paper also discusses practical difficulties of proforma data collection.

result.setting: ENT emergency clinic, Leicester Royal Infirmary
result.standard: All ENT emergency clinic patients should have a summary letter sent to their GP

cycle1.result: Only 7% of responding GPs had previously received regular correspondence from the clinic.

cycle2.result: Letter sent to 100% of patients' GPs; 97% of GPs valued it (mean satisfaction 8.4/10); 86% would not prefer a dictated letter.

result.other_findings: 72 of 100 GPs responded to the questionnaire.

result.setting: Waiting List Initiative clinics, large district general hospital (Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth)
result.standard: Local protocols guiding primary care referral of common paediatric orthopaedic problems

cycle1.result: Few examples of inappropriate referrals; variations of normal development were the commonest complaint, with most discharged after the first consultation.

result.other_findings: Audit also quantified extra workload for other specialties generated by the clinics.

result.setting: Paediatric intensive care unit, St Mary's Hospital (Imperial College), London
result.standard: Previously achieved blind bedside placement success of 96%

cycle1.result: Nasojejunal route used in 19%; placement success 94.5-95%.

result.intervention: Training programme: one-to-one training of key nurses and supervised placement with senior nurse or dietitian.
result.other_findings: Parenteral feeding 1% in 2001 and 3% in 2004; gastric feeding 80% and 79%.

result.setting: Emergency ambulance services and admitting hospitals in England and Wales (MINAP registry)

cycle1.result: Re-infarction recorded for 22 391 (63.3%), of whom 1460 (6.5%) re-infarcted; higher after pre-hospital tenecteplase than reteplase (9.6% vs 6.6%, p = 0.005).

result.other_findings: With more than 30 minutes from pre-hospital treatment to arrival, re-infarction was 12.5% for reteplase and 11.4% for tenecteplase.

result.topic: Radiotherapy planning for Hodgkin lymphoma trial QA
result.setting: 42 UK radiotherapy centres in the Stanford V vs ABVD trial
result.standard: Trial quality assurance programme (no target stated)

cycle1.result: One-third plan with CT alone, one-third with simulator only; 11 centres calculate a dose distribution per patient; in vivo dosimetry in 7 centres; treatment verification in 24.

result.other_findings: Questionnaire-based; practice varies across the country, with a move towards CT planning and virtual simulation.

result.setting: Emergency ophthalmology, North Middlesex University Hospital, London
result.standard: Published evidence level (Medline, Cochrane) for each diagnosis-intervention pair

cycle1.result: 71% of interventions evidence based; 36% at evidence levels 1-3; 29% no or contrary evidence.

cycle2.result: 82% evidence based (P=0.04); levels 1-3 in 60% (P=0.02); no or contrary evidence fell to 18% (P=0.04).

result.other_findings: Re-attendances were also reduced.

result.setting: District general hospital (Frimley Park Hospital)

cycle1.result: 19% (n=24) had post-operative bleeding; 10% (n=13) returned and were admitted.

result.other_findings: Authors conclude re-admission is an unreliable measure of secondary haemorrhage rate.

result.setting: Paediatric department, large inner-city district general hospital (Birmingham Heartlands Hospital)
result.standard: Trust Intranet Medical Dictionary (TID) and Mosby's Medical Dictionary (MMD)

cycle1.result: 25 handover sheets: 2286 abbreviations (221 different), 14% recognised by TID and 20% by MMD; 168 sets of notes: 3668 abbreviations (479 different), 15% TID and 17% MMD.

result.other_findings: Paediatric doctors recognised 56-94% of selected abbreviations and other healthcare professionals 31-63%; some abbreviations had multiple meanings (e.g. TOF).

result.topic: Antibiotic duration in paediatric septic arthritis
result.setting: Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre, Oxford

cycle1.result: Clinical improvement was most marked in the first two weeks with no significant change after six weeks; radiological bone changes in 21 by two weeks and a further 10 by six weeks.

result.other_findings: Haematological indices continued to improve after antibiotics stopped; no new radiological changes after six weeks, so six weeks of antibiotics recommended.

result.topic: Delayed discharge due to warfarin initiation in AF
result.setting: Three acute medical wards (96 beds), district general hospital (Rotherham General Hospital)

cycle1.result: 7 (30%) had delayed discharges solely due to warfarin initiation; 36 of 217 bed days (17%) were delayed; only 10 (43%) discharged with INR in target range 2 to 3.

result.other_findings: No difference between delayed and non-delayed patients in age, comorbidity, Barthel score or loading regimen; outpatient initiation suggested.

result.setting: 12 NHS Trusts using electronic patient record systems (Cataract National Dataset)
result.standard: Benchmark standards from the 1997-1998 UK National Cataract Survey

cycle1.result: Posterior capsule rupture and/or vitreous loss 1.92%; zonule dialysis 0.46%; retained lens fragments 0.18%; postoperative VA 6/12 or better in 91.0% (6/6 or better 45.9%).

result.other_findings: Phacoemulsification in 99.7%, local anaesthesia in 95.5%, trainees performed 33.9%; PCR/vitreous loss halved compared with the 1997-1998 survey.

result.topic: Neonatal and paediatric transport service satisfaction
result.setting: NSW Neonatal and Paediatric Transport Service (NETS), Children's Hospital at Westmead

cycle1.result: Referring doctors (288): over 90% positive about communication; parents (152): over 98% found team helpful; receiving doctors (218): 93% thought referral appropriate, 98% advice carried out correctly, 90% needs reported accurately.

result.other_findings: Parents travelled with their child 60% of the time. A minority of retrievals raised important concerns about ventilation, sedation and assessment.

result.topic: Self-harm management in the emergency department
result.setting: A&E department, Ysbyty Glan Clwyd, Conwy & Denbighshire NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE 2004 self-harm guideline audit criteria (psychosocial assessment, staff training, patient satisfaction)

cycle1.result: Generally high standards of psychosocial assessment; ambulance involvement information often unclear; staff training questionnaire response 44% with wide variation between staff groups.

result.other_findings: Proposed self-harm training for all staff likely to meet it and a practical self-harm pathway; no re-audit reported.

result.setting: Accident and emergency department resuscitation room, Leicester Royal Infirmary
result.standard: TRISS predicted survival and peer review

cycle1.result: Mortality 33%; 18 (51%) of 35 deaths were unexpected by TRISS (Z = 5.74, P < 0.001); peer review judged 11 deaths preventable.

result.other_findings: Lack of an on-site neurosurgical service may have affected outcome.

result.setting: All acute hospitals in England and Wales (MINAP database)

cycle1.result: Inpatient mortality 10.6%; acute aspirin and out-of-hospital thrombolysis each associated with over 50% mortality risk reduction; 14-predictor model C index 0.82.

result.other_findings: A 10-year age increase doubled mortality risk; cerebrovascular disease increased it by 1.7.

result.setting: Neurosurgical inpatient beds, Essex Centre for Neurosciences, Queen's Hospital, Romford
result.standard: Inappropriate delay defined as an action taking more than 24 h from initiation to completion

cycle1.result: 482 of 1665 bed days (29%) due to delays; 92.5% of wasted days in emergency admissions; delays due to transfer back (46%), operative (26%), radiological (19%).

result.other_findings: Eliminating delays would free the equivalent of 10.7 of 37 beds; own hospital had the longest transfer delays (6.3 days/patient vs average 2.8).

result.topic: Barthel Index use in palliative care
result.setting: Inpatient intermediate care unit (Wyre Forest PCT and Kemp Hospice)

cycle1.result: Low Barthel score on admission, or a drop of ten or more per week, predicted a short prognosis.

result.other_findings: Authors suggest the Index could aid discharge planning and prevent inappropriate admissions.

result.topic: Intermittent pneumatic compression DVT prophylaxis in theatre
result.setting: All theatre staff in one NHS trust (Derby Hospitals NHS Trust)
result.standard: Existing baseline standard for IPC use in DVT prophylaxis (not detailed)

cycle1.result: Performance against the standard good: IPC is the perioperative DVT prophylaxis of choice and is used frequently on most patients.

result.other_findings: Highlighted need for local DVT risk assessment guidelines so prophylaxis targets at-risk groups.

result.setting: Specialist high-risk antenatal clinic, Unified Maternity Services, Cork

cycle1.result: Caesarean section rate 41%; perinatal mortality 67 per 1000 (uncorrected); 20% of neonates needed NICU; average gestation 35.9 weeks, birth weight 2598 g.

result.other_findings: Risk categories: maternal medical disease 62%, multiple pregnancy 11%, poor obstetric history 10%, fetal anomaly 8%.

result.setting: Department of Radiodiagnosis, Bristol Royal Infirmary
result.standard: 26-item quality score across request card, films, report and film packets with a predetermined acceptable range

cycle1.result: Several problem areas identified (no figures in abstract).

result.intervention: Steps taken to improve items with scores outside the predetermined range.
result.other_findings: Pilot of a simple scoring system proposed for routine departmental use.

result.setting: Cancer patients in primary and secondary care, north Durham (specialist pharmacist)
result.standard: Evidence-based or best-practice standardised management strategies

cycle1.result: 119 active symptoms in 23 patients; median eight drugs prescribed; dry mouth in 21 (91%) and constipation in 12 (52%); many symptoms unmanaged by medication.

result.other_findings: The specialist pharmacist made 89 recommended medication changes, mostly for dry mouth and prokinetic antiemetics.

result.topic: Antiplatelet and anticoagulant use in cataract surgery
result.setting: 12 NHS Trusts using electronic patient records (Cataract National Dataset); eight centres recording drug history

cycle1.result: 28.1% taking aspirin, 5.1% warfarin, 1.9% clopidogrel, 1.0% dipyridamole; any local anaesthetic block complication recorded in 8.0% of clopidogrel users.

result.other_findings: Clopidogrel or warfarin use was associated with more minor anaesthetic complications but not with sight-threatening haemorrhagic complications.

result.setting: 30 maternity units in north-west England (North West Diabetic Pregnancy Audit)
result.standard: Regionally agreed standards (1999) in line with the St Vincent Declaration and Diabetes National Service Framework

cycle1.result: Funnel plots and tables highlight large differences between hospitals in booking and outcome measures (no figures in abstract).

result.other_findings: Describes the audit methodology: monthly data collection with individualised annual hospital reports.

result.setting: Bristol Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Adverse events in 50/104 on dual therapy vs 29/95 on azathioprine monotherapy (chi=6.4, P=0.05); adverse events in 26% on 2 mg/kg or more vs 54% on less than 2 mg/kg.

result.other_findings: No relationship between TPMT activity and adverse events; dual therapy patients were more likely to relapse.

result.setting: Specialist tertiary psychiatric inpatient unit (St Andrew's Healthcare, Northampton)
result.standard: Standards derived from two UK dementia guidelines

cycle1.result: Of 60 patients with dementia, 50 (83%) had BPSD and 28 (56%) of these received antipsychotics; results generally satisfactory.

result.other_findings: Room for improvement in documenting off-label use, screening for cerebrovascular risk factors, consulting relatives and using low starting doses with slow titration.

result.setting: 26 health centres in Cuba, Peru and Bolivia
result.standard: WHO and national TB programme guidelines on use of microscopy, culture and radiology

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Introduction of clinical audit with at least two audit cycles over 2 years.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in 11 of 13 criteria in Cuba, 2 of 6 in Bolivia and 2 of 5 in Peru; 12 of 24 criteria reached the agreed standards.

result.other_findings: Barriers included conflicting objectives between clinicians and TB programmes, poor health system coordination and patient attitudes.

result.topic: Equine colic surgery audit database feasibility
result.setting: Equine surgeons (ACVS/ECVS diplomates), international

cycle1.result: 30 interviews and 43/98 (44%) questionnaires returned; high interest in a large colic surgery database, with concerns about data collection time and confidentiality.

result.other_findings: A minority of surgeons were monitoring colic surgery results in their hospitals.

result.topic: GP referral patterns for hernia repair
result.setting: GPs in South East Wales referring to Royal Gwent Hospital

cycle1.result: 84% referred to a general surgeon or as open referral; only 14% referred directly to a hernia specialist; none regularly referred to a laparoscopic surgeon.

result.other_findings: 86 of 120 questionnaires returned; further GP education recommended.

result.setting: Busy ENT unit, Ipswich Hospital
result.standard: Current recommendations that patients have time to consider surgery before giving written consent

cycle1.result: 15% of patients gave written consent on the day of their operation.

result.intervention: Simple change in departmental consent policy.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Risk stratification for posterior capsule rupture in cataract surgery
result.setting: 12 NHS Trusts using an electronic patient record system (Cataract National Dataset)

cycle1.result: Overall PCR or VL or both 1.92% (95% CI 1.81-2.04%); predicted probability ranged from less than 0.75% to more than 75% by risk profile.

result.other_findings: Risk indicators included age, male sex, glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, brunescent/white cataract, small pupil, axial length 26.0 mm or more, doxazosin, inability to lie flat and trainee surgeon.

result.setting: 12 NHS Trusts using the same electronic patient record system (Cataract National Dataset)

cycle1.result: Local anaesthesia in 95.5% (topical 22.3%, subtenons 46.9%, peribulbar 19.5%, retrobulbar 0.5%); minor complications in 4.3% of 38,058 blocks, 2.3 times more common with subtenons.

result.other_findings: Wide variation by site; serious complications significantly more likely with sharp needle than subtenons anaesthesia.

result.setting: Primary care trust older people's services, West Dorset
result.standard: NICE 2004 falls guideline recommendation on education and information-giving

cycle1.result: Staff are beginning to meet the NICE education recommendation (no figures in abstract).

result.intervention: Local falls champions and a three-tier education approach.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 7 endoscopy units, Kent and Medway Strategic Health Authority
result.standard: National standards: total colonoscopy in at least 90%; BSG sedation guidelines; more than 100 colonoscopies per year

cycle1.result: 39 of 55 colonoscopists (71%) achieved total colonoscopy in at least 90%; 12 (22%) in 80-89%; 4 (7%) in 79% or less; 79% sedated per BSG guidelines; 22 of 55 (40%) performed more than 100 colonoscopies.

result.other_findings: Complications below expected levels; seven doctors stopped performing colonoscopy during the study.

result.setting: East Kent NHS Hospitals Trust (William Harvey Hospital, Ashford)
result.standard: RCOG ectopic pregnancy guidelines, local guidelines and NCEPOD recommendations

cycle1.result: 90.19% of procedures in working hours; 86.7% of non-sensitised Rhesus negative women received anti-D; 96% diagnosed within 96 h; betahCG available within 24 h in 80%.

result.other_findings: Consultant performed 51.13% of procedures; only 26% of ectopics were successfully treated laparoscopically.

result.topic: Chronic disease management in primary care
result.setting: Primary care (systematic review, Australian policy context)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Systematic review: self-management support via GP and practice nurse education and care plans with multidisciplinary support were most likely effective; registers recommended to facilitate audit.

result.topic: Skeletal survey quality in suspected non-accidental injury
result.setting: Skeletal surveys from across England and Wales sent for second opinion to a single children's hospital (Birmingham Children's Hospital)
result.standard: British Society of Paediatric Radiology guidelines: 20 recommended views per skeletal survey; technical quality score out of 11

cycle1.result: Mean 16.5 (range 5-20) of 20 recommended views covered per survey; 15% of surveys included all 20 views (previously 0% in an earlier study before the guideline). Mean technical score 9.7/11 (88%).

result.other_findings: 62% of surveys were digitally acquired and 59% included a head CT. Comparison was with an earlier published study done before the guideline; further publicity of the guidelines was recommended.

result.topic: Falls and bone health service organisation
result.setting: National organisational audit of trusts in England (Royal College of Physicians)
result.standard: Requirement to implement an integrated falls service for older people by April 2005

cycle1.result: Each site received a report of local results against the national picture with an organisational score and section scores; numbers not reported in abstract.

result.intervention: Site reports with scoring, action planning workshops learning from high performers, and chief executives asked to provide action plans.
result.other_findings: Some sites clearly used their audit results and scores to draw up immediate action plans.

result.topic: Acute coronary syndrome risk score performance
result.setting: All acute hospitals in England and Wales (MINAP national registry)

cycle1.result: C-indexes: PURSUIT 0.79, GUSTO-1 0.80, GRACE in-hospital 0.80, GRACE 6-month 0.80, SRI 0.79, EMMACE 0.78.

result.other_findings: Discriminative performance of all models was reduced in patients with diabetes, chronic renal failure or angina.

result.setting: University teaching hospital, Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Trust (Freeman Hospital)
result.standard: NCEPOD guidelines for urgent surgery: fully staffed emergency theatre and after-midnight operating restricted to immediate life-, limb- or organ-threatening conditions; classification of delays developed from existing guidelines

cycle1.result: Urgent cases continued to be delayed unnecessarily; incidence of delays audited (figures not given in abstract).

result.intervention: Audit results disseminated to the involved perioperative and surgical directorates.

cycle2.result: Significant decrease in delays (p = 0.001), significant increase in surgeon availability (p = 0.001) and significant decrease in median waiting time for urgent surgery compared with the first cycle and a previous standard (p < 0.01).

result.other_findings: An earlier audit had shown shorter waits and more senior care after overnight preoperative assessment by anaesthetic trainees.

result.setting: UK-wide annual audit of children over 1 year admitted with acute wheeze/asthma, 53-67 centres per year

cycle1.result: In 1998, 7% of admitted children received bronchodilators exclusively by spacer and 24% were discharged with a written asthma plan.

cycle2.result: By 2005, 44% received bronchodilators exclusively by spacer and 41% were discharged with a written asthma plan.

result.other_findings: 9429 admissions over 8 annual audits; around 90% received systemic steroids and wide variation between centres in chest x-rays and written plans. Children under respiratory specialists more often had documented asthma education, plans and inhaler technique checks.

result.topic: Perinatal care planning in severe mental illness
result.setting: New perinatal mental health service, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Recommendation that high-risk pregnant women are referred to perinatal mental health services with individualised care plans before delivery

cycle1.result: 39 women (87%) were seen for assessment; all women seen antenatally had care plans written addressing the high risk of postpartum relapse.

result.other_findings: 10 (26%) had psychiatric admissions during pregnancy and 15 (38%) relapsed or were admitted in the first postpartum year; at 1 year 74% had care of their children.

result.setting: West of Scotland radiotherapy planning (Department of Clinical Physics and Bio-engineering, Glasgow)
result.standard: Calculated delivered dose compared with prescribed dose; errors greater than 5% flagged

cycle1.result: 14 errors in excess of 5% discovered and corrected, approximately 0.5% of all plans checked.

result.other_findings: Describes an audit system for checking treatment planning dose delivery.

result.topic: Use of Mental Health Act section 5(2)
result.setting: Psychiatric hospital, Hull
result.standard: Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice standards for section 5(2)

cycle1.result: 75% of patients were assessed by the RMO within 48 hours; 41% regraded to informal, 32% placed on section 3 and 27% on section 2.

result.other_findings: Most section 5(2) uses were out of hours; the higher conversion rate to section 2/3 than similar studies suggested appropriate use.

result.setting: Ocular Oncology Service, St Paul's Eye Unit, Royal Liverpool University Hospital

cycle1.result: 40 previously untreated patients: all eyes conserved; invasive conjunctival recurrence in 6, more likely with medial tumours (P=0.004) and without radiotherapy (P=0.03); 4 died of metastases.

result.other_findings: Of 36 referred for salvage therapy after surgery elsewhere, 5 died, all referred with recurrent invasive tumour.

result.topic: Sedation for dental treatment in learning disability
result.setting: Multicentre dental services in Canterbury, Warwick, Dorset and Cardiff

cycle1.result: Of 222 sedation episodes, 128 (57.65%) accepted treatment well, 75 (33.78%) had slight problems not compromising treatment, and 19 (8.55%) could not be treated and were referred for general anaesthesia.

result.other_findings: A range of treatments including advanced restorative care was delivered with combined intranasal/intravenous midazolam.

result.setting: Acute children's services in two district general hospitals and child and adolescent mental health service, Hertfordshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Working together to safeguard children (HM Government 2006)

cycle1.result: Knowledge about information sharing was good; only 41% of staff gave an acceptable response on parental responsibility.

result.other_findings: Gaps also found in knowledge of legal orders, particularly emergency protection orders and police protection powers; training needs identified.

result.topic: Regional anaesthesia failure at Caesarean section
result.setting: Department of Anaesthesia, St Michael's Hospital, Bristol
result.standard: Royal College of Anaesthetists targets for conversion of regional to general anaesthesia: 1% for elective and 3% for emergency Caesarean section

cycle1.result: Conversion of regional to general anaesthesia 0.8% for elective and 4.9% for emergency Caesarean section; 20% in category 1 Caesarean section. 8% of women had general anaesthesia overall (primary plus conversion).

result.other_findings: Failure to achieve a pain-free operation was 6% with spinals, 24% with epidural top-up and 18% with combined spinal-epidural. Serious adverse incidents were 1:126 with general and 1:501 with regional anaesthesia.

result.topic: Relaxation therapy in oncology and palliative care
result.setting: Occupational Therapy Department, The Royal Marsden Hospital, Sutton

cycle1.result: Breast cancer was the most frequent primary diagnosis and age 50-59 the largest group; guided visualisation was the most used technique, with very little change in perceived tension across techniques.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Intravenous fluid prescribing and electrolyte monitoring in children
result.setting: Specialist children's hospital, Royal Hospital for Sick Children, Yorkhill, Glasgow
result.standard: National Patient Safety Agency guidance NPSA/2007/22 (March 2007) on intravenous fluids in children

cycle1.result: Hypotonic maintenance fluid prescribed for 94% before surgery and 92% after surgery; all maintenance volumes correctly calculated by weight; boluses isotonic on 128/129 occasions; no patient had daily plasma electrolytes while on i.v. fluids; 27 patients had recorded hyponatraemia.

result.other_findings: Practice before the NPSA guidance did not fully meet recommended standards; nasogastric losses were replaced with 0.9% sodium chloride.

result.setting: Neonatal Unit, University Hospital of North Staffordshire, Stoke-on-Trent
result.standard: 11 infection control and four routine care standards (random safety audits based on a Vermont-Oxford Network concept)

cycle1.result: Median compliance with infection control standards 70% (range 20%-100%).

result.intervention: Random safety audits during the weekly grand round with immediate feedback.

cycle2.result: Median compliance with infection control standards 95% (range 66%-100%).

result.other_findings: Three cycles of 15 audits each were completed in 6 months (complete results for 14 audits); routine care standards results were more variable.

result.setting: English NHS hospitals (Hospital Episode Statistics and National Prospective Tonsillectomy Audit)

cycle1.result: Haemorrhage rate within 28 days rose 0.5% per year from 2002, reaching 6.4% when NICE guidance was published, then fell immediately to 5.7% (difference 0.7%, 95% CI -1.3% to 0.0%).

result.other_findings: The fall coincided with a shift in surgical technique consistent with the NICE guidance.

result.setting: Breast cancer follow-up clinics in Cornwall

cycle1.result: Only 15% (10) of local recurrences were detected at routine follow-up; 48% were first noticed by patients and 37% detected at routine mammography.

result.other_findings: Six weekly follow-up clinics took about 20 h per week at around 4857 pounds per week (252,564 pounds per year); alternative follow-up methods were recommended.

result.topic: Procedural sedation in the emergency department
result.setting: Department of Emergency Medicine, Hairmyres Hospital, East Kilbride

cycle1.result: 85 (40%) given ketamine, 107 (51%) midazolam, 18 (9%) propofol; complications in 15.9% overall (14.6% ketamine, 15.8% midazolam, 22.2% propofol). Median time to full orientation 25 min ketamine, 30 min midazolam, 10 min propofol.

result.other_findings: 19.5% of ketamine patients had re-emergence phenomenon but no psychological sequelae.

result.topic: Preoperative group and save in elective surgery
result.setting: Department of Surgery, Royal Bolton Hospital
result.standard: Hospital blood ordering guidelines requiring group, screen and save for all elective breast cancer surgery

cycle1.result: 438 (88.1%) had group-and-save; only 19 (3.82%) received a transfusion: 9 (1.81%) of 447 mastectomy or wide local excision patients and 10 (20%) of 50 immediate reconstructions.

result.other_findings: Routine preoperative group-and-save was judged not justified for breast surgery without reconstruction.

result.topic: Home alcohol and drug detoxification outcomes
result.setting: Community drug and alcohol service, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Of 154 referrals, 59 commenced home detoxification and 95 did not; 96.6% of those who commenced completed the programme.

result.other_findings: Absence of a suitable carer and pre-existing medical-psychiatric conditions were the main reasons for unsuitability.

result.topic: Oral mucositis after autologous stem cell transplant
result.setting: 25 European transplant centres

cycle1.result: Severe oral mucositis in 44%; it increased TPN use by 2.7 days (P<0.001), opioids by 4.6 days (P<0.001) and antibiotics by 2.4 days (P=0.045).

result.other_findings: Severe oral mucositis prolonged hospital stay by 2.3 days (P=0.013) in myeloma but not lymphoma patients.

result.setting: Survey of Scotland's 18 consultant-led maternity units

cycle1.result: 2 of 18 maternity units used cell salvage; only 4/15 anaesthetists saw safety concerns as a barrier.

result.other_findings: Perceived barriers were lack of machine, insufficient cases and lack of familiarity with the technology.

result.setting: Hospital orthodontic departments in the East of England
result.standard: British Cardiac Society and Royal College of Physicians 2004 infective endocarditis prophylaxis guidelines; standards agreed at a regional audit meeting

cycle1.result: Significant deficiencies in knowledge of which dental procedures did or did not need antibiotic prophylaxis (14 consultants and 9 trainees).

result.intervention: Survey results discussed at a regional audit meeting and standards agreed.

cycle2.result: Knowledge improved to a variable extent (13 consultants and 8 trainees), with persistent confusion about multiple conflicting guidelines.

result.other_findings: Re-audit coincided with new British Society for Antimicrobial Chemotherapy guidance; the authors note NICE issued a single guideline in March 2008. No written departmental policy data reported in abstract.

result.setting: Six general dental practices in Scotland (nine dentists)

cycle1.result: Four agents routinely used (Duraphat, Duraphat and Sensodyne, Sensodyne, Seal and Protect); all produced statistically significant improvement (details truncated in abstract).

result.intervention: The most successful treatment (Seal and Protect) was adopted by all participating dentists.

cycle2.result: Seal and Protect was found to be reliable and predictable when used by all dentists (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: A four-point categorical ranking scale provided a simple and reliable measure of dentine hypersensitivity.

result.topic: Emergency obstetric care availability and quality
result.setting: 73 health facilities (13 hospitals and 60 health centres) in three districts in Malawi
result.standard: Criterion-based clinical audit of emergency obstetric care

cycle1.result: Baseline emergency obstetric care availability, utilisation and quality (details not given in abstract).

result.intervention: Facility-based maternal death reviews and criterion-based clinical audit with feedback introduced in 2006.

cycle2.result: Number of comprehensive and basic EmOC facilities did not change over 3 years (p for trend=1.000); institutional delivery rate increased overall over 3 years.

result.other_findings: 2006 data included 43,729 women, when the institutional delivery rate dipped; the abstract is truncated for further results.

result.setting: Intensive Care Unit, Hope Hospital, Salford

cycle1.result: Pretraining prescriptions with errors: 25%, 19% (one missing data point) across 3-month cycles.

result.intervention: Prescriber education in tutorials and ward-based teaching with feedback of individual and anonymised peer error rates, in 3-monthly cycles for each new trainee group.

cycle2.result: Final audit after 6 weeks: prescriptions with errors 7%, 3%, 5% across cycles.

result.other_findings: Post-training error rates were 23%, 6% and 11% across the cycles.

result.setting: Department of Anaesthetics, Royal Prince Alfred Hospital, Sydney

cycle1.result: 25 (56%) received intraoperative morphine (mean 9 mg); 43 (96%) had regular postoperative paracetamol; 36 (80%) needed additional postoperative opioid, mean 14.5 mg parenteral morphine equivalents.

result.other_findings: 39 received intraoperative hyoscine butylbromide and 14 received antiemetics; simple analgesic regimens appeared adequate.

result.topic: ECG interpretation in the emergency department
result.setting: Accident and Emergency Department, Ulster Hospital, Dundonald, Belfast

cycle1.result: SHOs correctly interpreted 90% of normal and 57% of abnormal ECGs compared with a consultant cardiologist; 96.5% of patients were considered correctly managed.

result.other_findings: Audit of all A&E ECGs by an experienced reader and ECG training for new staff were recommended.

result.setting: Palliative care service (St Christopher's Hospice, London) with 48 beds, over 600 home care and 100 day care patients

cycle1.dates: Two years after introduction of an adult protection policy
cycle1.result: 20 safeguarding cases identified, involving institutional, physical, verbal and financial abuse and neglect.

result.other_findings: Difficult family relationships, sometimes with substance misuse or mental illness, often exacerbated caring stresses leading to abuse concerns.

result.setting: A&E department of a district general hospital (Kent and Sussex Hospital, Tunbridge Wells)
result.standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 6-hour resuscitation care bundle

cycle1.result: Overall compliance with the 6-hour bundle 19%; arterial lactate done 100% of the time; only just over half received an appropriate fluid challenge; antibiotic administration very slow.

result.other_findings: Recommendations included improving the A&E track and trigger system, the prescribing doctor administering antibiotics, and staff education.

result.topic: Tumour bed clip placement after breast conserving surgery
result.setting: Cambridge Breast Unit, Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (IMPORT trial)
result.standard: 5/6 pairs of clips identified on RT planning CT - 100%; possible clip migration: 50%

cycle1.result: Five or six pairs of clips identified in all 30 cases (100%); no evidence of clip migration. Tumour bed identifiable by seroma alone in only 8/30 (27%); clips essential in 22/30 (73%).

result.other_findings: Tumour bed localisation modified radiotherapy field borders in 18/30 (60%), with clips alone responsible in 13/30 (43%).

result.setting: Department of Urology, The Adelaide and Meath Hospital, Tallaght, Dublin

cycle1.result: Mean hospital stay 14.3 days; early morbidity in 26 and late in 13; no mortality; 95% complete remission after RPLND (mean follow-up 30 months).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Bristol Urological Institute, Southmead Hospital, Bristol

cycle1.result: Successful videocystometry in 39 (81%); 97% of written reports contained adequate information. Of 33 returned questionnaires (85%), 30 (91%) said the result directly influenced management.

result.other_findings: Areas for improvement were highlighted and reported as addressed, but no re-audit is described.

result.setting: Ambulance service and emergency department 'majors' section of a university hospital (Salford Royal)
result.standard: Joint Royal Colleges Ambulance Liaison Committee (JRCALC) guidance on oxygen use

cycle1.result: SpO2 recorded for 90% of patients (remainder of results truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Baseline audit before new national emergency oxygen guidelines; oxygen use was suboptimal, especially in COPD.

result.topic: Obstetric anal sphincter injury repair training
result.setting: Structured hands-on OASIS repair course (Mayday University Hospital, Croydon)

cycle1.result: Participants had performed on average 14 OASIS repairs independently; only 13% were satisfied with their experience before their first unsupervised repair. 60% identified and repaired the internal sphincter.

result.intervention: Structured hands-on course using models and cadaveric pig anal sphincters.

cycle2.result: 63% returned the questionnaire; identifying and repairing the internal sphincter rose to 90% (P < 0.0001).

result.other_findings: Participants classified OASIS more accurately after the course.

result.setting: Neonatal networks in England (National Neonatal Audit Programme database; 18 of 24 networks)
result.standard: National Audit Office recommended maximum of 5% of transfers out of network

cycle1.result: 91 infants (18.8%) were transferred out of network or to a more distant centre than appropriate, compared with 3.6% for all network patients.

result.other_findings: Only one network used a single surgical centre; median number of surgical units accessed per network was 3 (range 1-8).

result.setting: NHS Education for Scotland peer assessment system for GP clinical audit

cycle1.result: 12 significant event analysis reports and 12 criterion audit projects assessed by 11 GP assessors and 10 NHS audit specialists; score differences truncated in abstract.

result.other_findings: NHS clinical audit specialists gave numerically accurate feedback scores compared with established peer assessors.

result.setting: Six-doctor general practice in south London with 11,500 patients (Sydenham Green Health Centre)
result.standard: Practice-set goals for immunisation, abnormal smear follow-up, blood pressure and smoking recording, over-75 screening, diabetes and serious mental illness care, antenatal care, workload and appointment availability

cycle1.result: The receptionist audited all these tasks in four hours a week; attainment figures not given in abstract.

result.other_findings: Supervision of about 30 minutes a week in year one and 30 minutes a fortnight in year two was needed; the receptionist's job satisfaction increased.

result.setting: Acute surgical admissions, district general hospital (Hinchingbrooke NHS Trust Hospital, Huntingdon)
result.standard: Local guidelines derived from American College of Chest Physicians (ACCP) criteria for VTE prophylaxis

cycle1.result: Only 19/51 (37%) received appropriate VTE prophylaxis; 18/29 high risk and 4/10 medium risk patients were not adequately protected.

result.intervention: VTE prevention protocol with risk assessment and decision support nested within a new clerking proforma for acute surgical admissions.
result.other_findings: Over half of patients were at high risk for VTE.

result.topic: Paediatric diabetes care processes and glycaemic control
result.setting: 16 paediatric diabetes units in Yorkshire (Yorkshire Register of Diabetes in Children and Young People)

cycle1.result: An HbA1c measure was recorded for 91.6% of patients (proportion meeting target truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Poor diabetes control was associated with higher deprivation.

result.topic: Automated versus manual audit of paediatric clinical indicators
result.setting: Emergency department, single centre (Tamworth, New South Wales)
result.standard: 16 clinical indicators for croup, asthma, bronchiolitis, head injury and gastroenteritis

cycle1.result: Manual audit showed overall agreement with clinical indicators of 73.5%, versus 90.6% from automated TELEform data (available for only 24 patients), an overestimate of 17%.

result.other_findings: Compliance was 92.5% when the guideline was incorporated into the clinical record versus 51.3% when it was not.

result.topic: CT colonography versus barium enema for colorectal cancer detection
result.setting: Department of Radiology, Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 2520 DCBEs and 604 CTCs: DCBE detected 21 of 33 cancers (sensitivity 63.7%); CTC detected 32 of 33 (sensitivity 97.7%).

result.other_findings: DCBE sensitivity declined after CTC introduction.

result.setting: Sickle cell patients living in Coventry (Department of Haematology, University Hospital, Coventry)

cycle1.result: Children (n=25): 14 (56%) completely immunised against pneumococcus, Hib and MenC, 8 (32%) partial, 3 (12%) none. Adults (n=33): 4 (12%) complete; pneumococcus 21%, Hib 18%, MenC 15%. Influenza within last year 12% of adults and 8% of children.

result.other_findings: Rates were similar to other UK studies; haemoglobinopathy nurse specialists and a national database were suggested to improve coverage.

result.setting: Six health districts in the south of England (Oxford record linkage study)

cycle1.result: Inpatient episodes increased by 23.5% and day cases by 13.1%; emergency readmissions rose by an average of 2.7% a year; length of stay fell consistently.

result.other_findings: About 90% of the increase was due to more people treated and 10% to readmissions.

result.topic: Outcomes of gynaecology referrals for menstrual problems
result.setting: General practices in the Oxford Regional Health Authority area referring to 19 gynaecology clinics

cycle1.result: Over 5 years, 167 (81%) admitted to hospital, 91 (44%) had a hysterectomy (87 (60%) of 145 referred for menorrhagia), 98 (48%) had D&C, 25 (12%) drug therapy only and 10 (5%) no active treatment.

result.other_findings: Of 18,754 referrals, 2513 (13%) went to gynaecology, 21% of which were for menstrual disorders, with more than three-fold variation between practices.

result.setting: 100 dermatology units in the UK (British Association of Dermatologists audit)
result.standard: British Association of Dermatologists guidelines and standards for psoriasis care

cycle1.result: 18% (18/98) of units had fewer than 2.0 WTE consultants and 20% had no specialist nurse; only 21% had dedicated psoriasis clinics; 55% had no systemic drug monitoring clinic. Of 73 units prescribing biologics, 88% (64/73) followed BAD biologics guidelines. Quality-of-life score inadequately or never recorded in 81% of units' outpatient records; PASI inadequately or never recorded in 79% of outpatient records.

result.other_findings: 56% lacked adult clinical psychology and 59% (55/93) lacked child psychology services; 39% of biologic prescribers were restricted by finance.

result.setting: Colorectal Services, Addenbrookes Hospital, Cambridge (nurse-led follow-up)

cycle1.result: 95% of patients were very or fairly happy with the current follow-up service.

result.intervention: Follow-up phone calls post-diagnosis and 48 hours after discharge introduced after the audit.
result.other_findings: Patients wanted a follow-up phone call post-diagnosis and 48 hours post-discharge.

result.setting: 17 UK paediatric intensive care units and two PICU transport services
result.standard: 2002 American College of Critical Care Medicine/Pediatric Advanced Life Support (ACCM-PALS) guideline

cycle1.result: 34/200 (17%) children died after referral; most children received inadequate fluid resuscitation and inotropic support in the first hours after presentation.

result.other_findings: Shock at PICU admission was associated with increased risk of death.

result.setting: District general hospital intensive care unit, Cheltenham General Hospital

cycle1.result: 258 echocardiograms in 217 patients (224 (86.8%) by intensive care consultants; 187 TTE, 71 TOE); management changed directly in 51.2% of studies.

result.other_findings: TTE gave diagnostic images in 91.3% of spontaneously breathing and 84.2% of ventilated patients.

result.setting: Oral and maxillofacial surgery units across the UK (BAOMS national audit)

cycle1.result: 56.4% registered with a GDP; 140 (52.6%) sought primary dental care and only 20 failed to obtain treatment; 66% were prescribed oral antibiotics only without operative intervention by primary dental care; 81% required admission and 46% surgery under general anaesthesia.

result.other_findings: 50% were referred by A&E; 89% made a full recovery and there were no deaths. Intended as a benchmark for future comparison.

result.setting: All hospitals in Wales: ambulance, A&E, medical admission units and inpatient care

cycle1.result: BTS/SIGN severity assessment rarely performed; monitoring of progress and discharge process disappointing. 30% of patients appeared mild and 19% severe/acute severe.

result.other_findings: Major incompatibilities found between BTS/SIGN guidelines and the Welsh Ambulance Service protocol and the BAEM protocol for moderate asthma.

result.topic: Dental management of patients on warfarin
result.setting: General dental practitioners in South West Wales (questionnaire)
result.standard: Current guidelines, including new recommendations produced in 2001, on dental management of patients on warfarin

cycle1.result: Results of the first audit not given in abstract.

cycle2.result: 332/447 (74%) returned; 278 (84%) would check INR before treatment, 214 (65%) within 24 hours; none would advise reducing warfarin dose and 1% would stop warfarin without medical opinion; 206 (63%) would seek medical advice for high risk procedures.

result.other_findings: Safe upper INR limits cited varied widely (34% chose 2.5, 30% chose 3, 10% each chose 3.5 and 4); authors reported a broad change towards the 2001 recommendations but further education is needed.

result.setting: Department of Vascular Surgery, St Vincent's Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Predicted vs observed morbidity 41% vs 35.8% (P = 0.066); POSSUM over-predicted mortality at 9.7% vs observed 5.7% (P = 0.021).

result.other_findings: POSSUM scores were strongly associated with mortality (area under ROC curve 0.97250) but discriminated morbidity poorly.

result.setting: University Department of Head and Neck Surgery, Manchester Royal Infirmary (tertiary referral centre)
result.standard: Correct OPCS procedure coding reflective of work undertaken

cycle1.result: 47 of 99 (47.4%) original procedure codes were incorrect (revised coding generated 146 codes); HRG unchanged in 19 of 34 cases (55.9%); six cases never coded, equating to a 15,300 pound loss.

result.other_findings: The coding system was found complicated, ambiguous and inaccurate, resulting in lost remuneration.

result.topic: Two-week wait referrals for suspected testicular cancer
result.setting: Department of Urology, Royal Cornwall Hospital, Truro
result.standard: Two-week wait referral guidelines for suspected testicular cancer

cycle1.result: Referral-to-treatment journey for 42 testicular tumour cases before the two-week wait system (interval figures not given in abstract).

result.intervention: Introduction of the two-week wait referral system.

cycle2.result: Testicular cancer found in only 8% of two-week wait referrals; 48% of referrals judged inappropriate; 78% required no surgery. Average GP referral to urology clinic time improved by 9 days; other intervals unchanged.

result.other_findings: GP examination of scrotal swellings and use of the guidelines was very poor; ultrasound within 2 weeks was proposed instead of clinic appointments.

result.setting: Gondar University Hospital, referral hospital, all departments
result.standard: Agreed local clinical guidelines by topic

cycle1.result: 20 audits commenced: 7 completed, 11 in progress, 2 awaiting analysis; good practice in treating common paediatric emergencies and record documentation; glucose testing on the children's ward needed improvement.

result.intervention: Lead clinician nominated, audit clerk appointed, staff training and local guidelines written.
result.other_findings: Topics included obstructed labour, acute diarrhoea in children and medical record-keeping.

result.setting: 29 UK medical schools and one Irish medical school (questionnaire to dermatology teaching leads)
result.standard: British Association of Dermatologists recommendations for a core undergraduate dermatology curriculum; all curricula should include the essential clinical skills learning outcomes

cycle1.result: Replies from 29 of 30 schools; dermatological history taking and skin examination were included in most but not all curricula; some omissions such as diagnosis of meningococcaemia.

result.other_findings: Knowledge-based assessments were used by 27 schools; results are intended as a baseline for future audits.

result.setting: Review of criterion-based clinical audit in developing countries (Immpact, University of Aberdeen)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Summarises practical steps in applying criterion-based clinical audit and lessons from low-income countries.

result.setting: Four-partner general practice (Department of Primary Medical Care, University of Southampton)

cycle1.result: 818 GP consultations for the asthmatic patients.

result.intervention: Introduction of a nurse-run asthma clinic.

cycle2.dates: First 12 months after the clinic started
cycle2.result: GP consultations fell to 414 (P less than 0.001), offset by 496 nurse consultations; significant reductions (P less than 0.01) in oral steroid courses, acute nebulisations and days lost from work or school.

result.other_findings: 80% of patients had medication modified; prescribing costs remained stable.

result.setting: Radiology Department, Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital (university teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: 1338 of 15,095 films (8.86%) rejected (range 7.69% to 13.82%); causes: radiographer faults 547 (40.88%), equipment faults 255 (19.06%), patient faults 250 (18.90%).

result.other_findings: Highest reject rate was for spine films (13.82%); 885 (76.89%) of patients needing repeats required at least one extra hospital visit.

result.topic: Self-harm assessment in the emergency department
result.setting: Accident and emergency department, Leicester Royal Infirmary
result.standard: Adequacy of psychiatric and social assessment by the A&E doctor, scored over 10 headings (no named guideline or target)

cycle1.result: 210 adolescents attended after deliberate self poisoning; records available for 200. 89 admitted (mean score 5.1), 80 discharged without psychiatric consultation or follow up (mean score 5.4), 31 discharged with consultation or follow up (mean score 9.1). Adequate or better assessment across 10 headings ranged 0%-40%, 0%-50% and 0%-61% by group. Documentation of suicidal state inadequate in 49% (54/111) of those discharged.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend A&E doctors liaise with child psychiatrists before discharging adolescent self-harm patients.

result.topic: Mode of delivery after previous caesarean section
result.setting: 17 obstetric units in North West Thames region; regional obstetric database

cycle1.result: 395 (37%) had elective repeat caesarean section and 664 (63%) were allowed a trial of labour; 471 (71%) of those allowed to labour achieved vaginal delivery.

result.other_findings: Postnatal infection higher after elective and intrapartum caesarean section than vaginal delivery (14.7% and 16.0% v 3.4%); trend to greater success in units allowing longer labour (p less than 0.05).

result.topic: Nasal injury referral from the emergency department
result.setting: ENT outpatients receiving A&E nasal injury referrals, University Hospital of North Staffordshire
result.standard: Local nasal injury management guideline (refer only patients with deformity after swelling subsides)

cycle1.result: Nasal injury referrals seen in ENT outpatients before the guideline, including those not requiring ENT treatment (figures not reported in abstract).

result.intervention: Introduction of a nasal injury management guideline for A&E

cycle2.result: Proportion of patients seen in ENT outpatients not requiring any ENT treatment was reduced (figures not reported in abstract).

result.other_findings: Authors suggest the guideline may also prevent delayed ENT input for new onset nasal deformity.

result.setting: Urology department, Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley; large teaching hospital
result.standard: Department of Health two-week wait referral guidelines for suspected urological cancer

cycle1.result: 42 (11%) referrals were inappropriate. Cancer found in 90 of 400 (23%); detection ranged from 50 of 122 (41%) for elevated PSA to 2 of 56 (4%) for scrotal lumps.

result.other_findings: Most inappropriate referrals were for long-standing symptoms and non-specific testicular or scrotal symptoms; authors suggest GP access to fast-track scrotal ultrasound.

result.setting: Large teaching hospital; Department of Colorectal Surgery, Beaumont Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Normal appendicectomy rate 10.2%, compared with 22.8% in a prior 1988 study at the same hospital.

result.other_findings: Normal appendicectomy rate was twice as high in women of reproductive age as in men.

result.setting: Audiology department, Ealing Hospital, London; patients referred from ENT for tinnitus counselling

cycle1.result: After reading the educational poster, 42% chose counselling, 9% chose to ignore tinnitus, 26% a sound generator and 24% hearing aids.

result.intervention: Patient-centred tinnitus management tool (educational poster) offering treatment options
result.other_findings: The tool reduced the number who would otherwise have been referred for tinnitus counselling by 58%, shortening the waiting list.

result.setting: Radiology department requests; Department of Otolaryngology, Hope Hospital, Salford
result.standard: Current best practice guidelines (chronic rhinosinusitis diagnosed on history and nasendoscopy; sinus x-rays not indicated)

cycle1.result: Sinus x-rays still being requested, particularly by primary care physicians (figures not reported).

result.intervention: Informing GPs of current best practice guidelines
result.other_findings: Authors state the rate of sinus x-rays can be reduced by informing GPs of guidelines; no figures given.

result.setting: North East Deputising Service (urban co-operative deputising service), Glasgow
result.standard: Diagnosis-based classification of calls as emergency, reasonable or unnecessary

cycle1.result: 6834 calls from 37,300 population (183 per 1000 patients per year). In a sample of 468 (7%) calls, 23% were unnecessary, 65% reasonable and 12% emergencies. Only 1% ended with telephone advice; 5% waited more than two hours.

result.other_findings: People in deprived areas were more likely to call and to make inappropriate calls.

result.setting: Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 94 (39%) scans positive for hernia; 62 operated with four false positives (PPV 94% in operated patients). 143 negative; none of those discharged returned with related complaints.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Surgical site infection rates by surgeon
result.setting: General surgical inpatients, West Dorset district (Dorset County Hospital)

cycle1.result: 79 infections, overall rate 7.3%; individual surgeon rates 3.9 to 14.6% (P less than 0.005) and 2.9 to 20.0% for clean operations (P less than 0.0005).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Dermatology Department, Leeds General Infirmary

cycle1.result: Employment of the nurse specialist was associated with fewer hospital admissions and a positive impact on waiting lists (figures not reported).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Cervical screening history in invasive cervical cancer
result.setting: Southampton and South West Hampshire population

cycle1.result: Interval cancers rose from 31.5% of all cancers in 1985-87 to 48.6% in 1994-96 (P= 0.002), while their incidence fell from 20.1 to 10.9 per 100 000 screened women (P= 0.008).

result.other_findings: Factors other than previous negative smears were recorded in 50.9% of interval cancers.

result.setting: Kent and Medway Cancer Network: seven hospitals across four NHS trusts

cycle1.result: Around 22% (n = 664) of surveillance referrals were in line with guidelines, 51% (n = 1540) could be cancelled and 27% (n = 816) could be given a new date. Average wait for diagnostic colonoscopy 76.8 days.

result.intervention: Non-compliant surveillance referrals adjusted (cancelled or re-dated) to match the guidelines
