result.other_findings: Referral rate ranged 3.7 to 24.0 per 1000 per year; many referrals outside guidelines still had cancer (urological 15.9%, lung 8.8%).

result.setting: One UK mental health trust (Leicestershire Partnership NHS Trust); questionnaire to all 24 non-medical prescribers
result.standard: UK Standards for non-medical prescribing adopted by the mental health service

cycle1.result: 83% of non-medical prescribers responded; UK Standards were met by the majority, but there was a shortfall in uptake of training and supervision.

result.other_findings: Concerns about training, supervision and experience of some prescribers; conflict with psychiatrists was reported but their availability for support was valued.

result.setting: Rural regional mental health service, East Galway (St Brigid's Hospital, Ballinasloe)

cycle1.result: Most had an annual documented medical review and prescription; injection site condition documented in 5 (8%); site alternation in 28 (47%); no written consent to treatment in any; no information on depot and side effects documented in 57 (95%).

result.intervention: A standardised checklist was developed to be introduced by all teams (not yet re-audited).
result.other_findings: 60 case files were 31% of the 181 service users on depots; failure to monitor some blood tests was partly due to unclear responsibility.

result.setting: UK policy and practice discussion paper

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Discussion paper on translating falls prevention evidence into practice; no audit data reported.

result.setting: Four CT scanners, Hull and East Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Diagnostic reference levels; validated against the 'gold standard' standard-sized patient dose audit

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Validation of a large-scale dose audit technique using radiology information system data; results equivalent to the standard-sized patient could be inferred.

result.setting: Point prevalence survey in four acute teaching hospitals using the ESAC audit tool
result.standard: Hospital antibiotic guidelines; ESAC quality indicators (indication recorded, surgical prophylaxis duration)

cycle1.result: 52.4% of antibiotics compliant with hospital guidelines; indication recorded in 84.3% of prescribing episodes; 3.9% of surgical prophylaxis prescriptions were for >24 h.

result.other_findings: Most used antibiotics were penicillin/beta-lactamase inhibitor combinations (33.6%), metronidazole (9.1%) and macrolides (8.1%).

result.setting: Primary Care Department, Bristol Dental Hospital
result.standard: Departmental guidelines: drainage plus three-day standard-dose antibiotic course

cycle1.result: Review obtained for 80.3%; when departmental guidelines were followed all reviewed patients had a successful outcome; overall antibiotic prescribing rate 2.9% for adults attending emergency department in pain.

result.other_findings: Outcome audit of the effectiveness of a three-day antibiotic regime.

result.setting: Southampton Vascular Unit, Royal South Hampshire Hospital

cycle1.result: Marked discrepancies from national workload figures; all reconstructive surgery except emergency aortic aneurysm grafting performed more often than expected.

result.other_findings: Mortality was appreciable in all major vascular procedures, usually cardiac or renal related.

result.setting: One thoracic surgery operating theatre, Royal Devon and Exeter NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Extended surgical time out checklist including VTE prophylaxis

cycle1.result: Time out performed in 959 of 990 (96.8%); errors captured: VTE prophylaxis n=53 (6%), blood products n=11, clerical n=5, imaging n=2, miscellaneous n=2.

result.intervention: Human factors training, introduction of debriefing and escalation of VTE prophylaxis to regular departmental meetings.

cycle2.result: VTE prophylaxis errors substantially reduced (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Time out performance was consistent over time.

result.topic: Antiplatelet and anticoagulation after cardiac surgery
result.setting: National telephone survey of on-call registrars in all 37 NHS adult cardiac surgery centres
result.standard: EACTS guideline on antiplatelet and anticoagulation management in cardiac surgery (aspirin 150-300 mg, loading within 24 h)

cycle1.result: 20 (54%) hospitals had a unit protocol; 23 (62.2%) registrars aware of EACTS guidelines; aspirin loading within 24 h followed by 60.7% of surgeons; low-dose aspirin commonly used.

result.other_findings: Little deviation from the guideline for anticoagulation therapy.

result.setting: Intermediate minor oral surgery (IMOS) service, Croydon PCT primary care

cycle1.result: 99% treated in IMOS practices, only three (<1%) referred on to hospital; 72 (13%) teeth removed were simple extractions without medical complications.

result.other_findings: Commonest referrals were teeth of special difficulty (237; 40%) and lower third molars (154; 26%); standards set for future audits.

result.setting: Outpatient radiology, Children's University Hospital, Temple Street, Dublin

cycle1.result: 42% given a reduced initial dose; augmentation required in 10.9% overall (15.7% >1 year vs 5.7% infants).

result.other_findings: Reduced initial dose had no negative effect on outcome (P = 0.19) or time to sedation; no significant complications.

result.setting: 2008 UK national COPD audit; 98% of acute UK trusts
result.standard: British Thoracic Society guidelines on supported discharge programmes

cycle1.result: SDPs available in 142 of 239 (59%) units; 1630 of 8971 (18%) patients treated within SDPs.

result.other_findings: Median stay 3 (1-6) days in SDPs vs 6 (3-11) days (p<0.001); 90-day mortality 4.3% vs 6.7%.

result.setting: University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Intermittent compression devices caused pressure sores in selected women undergoing long operations.

cycle2.result: Reduced risk of pressure sores without increased VTE risk (figures not given).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Day case colonoscopy, district general hospital (Antrim Area Hospital)

cycle1.result: 91 KleanPrep, 86 Moviprep, 81 Senna/Citramag; more patients unable to take the full KleanPrep dose (19.6%).

result.other_findings: Moviprep and Senna/Citramag better tolerated than large-volume PEG; Senna/Citramag gave superior cleansing.

result.topic: Nurse prescribing in critical care outreach
result.setting: Critical care outreach team, Royal Berkshire NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Wide range of medications prescribed; prescribing decisions increased over time; most prescriptions written out of hours.

result.other_findings: Descriptive audit of two independent non-medical prescribers.

result.setting: National Lung Cancer Audit; hospitals in England, Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Jersey
result.standard: National Lung Cancer Audit process and outcome measures

cycle1.dates: Start of the five-year audit period
cycle1.result: Histological confirmation 64%; MDT discussion 78%; anti-cancer treatment 43%; surgical resection 9%; small cell chemotherapy 58%.

result.intervention: Continuous national audit with feedback over five years.

cycle2.result: Histological confirmation 76%; MDT discussion 94%; anti-cancer treatment 59%; surgical resection 14%; small cell chemotherapy 66%.

result.other_findings: Audit captures approximately 100% of expected incident cases; national averages hide wide variation between hospitals not explained by casemix.

result.topic: MRI staging accuracy in endometrial cancer
result.setting: National audit; 37 of 87 UK radiology departments performing MRI staging of endometrial cancer
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists target accuracies: myometrial invasion 85%, cervical extension 86%, nodal spread 70%

cycle1.result: National accuracy: myometrial invasion 82%, cervical extension 90%, pelvic nodes 94%; centres meeting target: 13/37 (35%) myometrial invasion, 31/36 (86%) cervical extension, 31/34 (91%) nodes.

result.other_findings: No significant difference with intravenous contrast; some evidence of better myometrial invasion accuracy with higher caseload.

result.setting: Emergency department of a metropolitan teaching hospital, Melbourne
result.standard: Paper-based cTnI ordering guideline incorporated into computerised order entry decision support

cycle1.result: cTnI tests ordered in 7.3% of chest pain presentations; mean cost $A9.28 per presentation.

result.intervention: Quality improvement initiative (paper guideline, education, audit and feedback) plus electronic decision support in 2003-4; decision support modified in 2005-7 to allow bypassing the full guideline.

cycle2.result: 4.1% in 2003-4 and 2.8% in 2005-7; mean cost $A8.54 then $A8.18; saving of $A13,251 since 2003.

result.other_findings: Longitudinal linked-data study of decision support impact and sustainability.

result.topic: Respiratory diagnostic accuracy in primary care
result.setting: Community Respiratory Assessment Unit, Charing Cross Hospital, London, for GP referrals

cycle1.result: 666 referred for five common reasons; COPD commonest (445/666, 66.8%) but 161/445 (36%) GP COPD diagnoses were incorrect.

result.other_findings: Restrictive defects (56/666, 8%) were overlooked and often mistaken for obstructive disease; misdiagnosis led to inappropriate inhaled therapy.

result.setting: Cataract National Dataset electronic audit; 406 surgeons in 12 NHS Trusts

cycle1.result: Preoperative VA known for 55,528 (99.9%) and postoperative VA for 40,758 (73.3%) operations.

result.other_findings: Posterior capsule rupture was the only modifiable risk indicator and was strongly associated with VA loss (OR=5.74).

result.setting: Questionnaire to GPs served by five HPA laboratories in South West England

cycle1.result: 70% would only give oral antifungals after sending a sample, yet 27% never waited for a microscopy report before prescribing.

result.other_findings: Questionnaire sent to 2420 GPs; terbinafine (86%) and amorolfine (53%) preferred.

result.topic: General anaesthesia safety for paediatric cardiac MRI
result.setting: Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children, London

cycle1.result: 71% without significant incident; minor incidents in 32 patients (mostly mild hypotension); one major event (cardiac arrest, resuscitated).

result.other_findings: Complication rate higher than in the general paediatric population.

result.setting: Long-term forensic psychiatric inpatient population, GP with special interest service, East London
result.standard: UK primary care Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF) local and national benchmarks (2005-2006)

cycle1.result: QOF was a useful assessment tool; increased prevalence of all QOF-assessed long-term conditions compared with local and national populations (figures not given).

result.other_findings: Suggests QOF can be used to commission and monitor physical healthcare for inpatient psychiatric and prison populations.

result.topic: Depression case management in primary care
result.setting: Depression case-management clinics run by practice nurses in general practice (Tees Esk and Wear Valleys)

cycle1.result: Mean PHQ9 change 9.07 (SD 6.67, 95% CI 7.93-10.22, P < 0.001); shift from moderate-severe to mild depression.

result.other_findings: Patients 'very satisfied'; mean practice nurse time cost £45 per patient.

result.topic: Two-week wait referral for suspected cancer
result.setting: OMFS department, Newcastle General Hospital, then oral surgery and oral medicine, Newcastle Dental Hospital
result.standard: Department of Health two-week rule referral guidelines

cycle1.result: 57 (90%) seen within time; 60 (95%) conformed to guidelines; cancer detection rate 11% (7/63).

result.intervention: Repeat identical audit in a different department; no intervention described.

cycle2.result: 43/49 (88%) seen within time; 39 (80%) compliant with guidelines; detection rate 7%.

result.other_findings: All patients with cancer had guideline-compliant referrals; further education of referrers recommended.

result.setting: Seven family-based child weight management programmes, West Midlands

cycle1.result: None of the programmes provided all essential measures; weight change from +0.4 kg to -0.9 kg; BMI SD fell 0.1-0.2 in four programmes and was unchanged in two.

result.other_findings: Four programmes collected 6-month follow-up, limited by dropout.

result.setting: Population-based record linkage, Tayside

cycle1.result: 96.9% had at least one TSH assay during or just before pregnancy; 81.2% in the first trimester; thyroxine increased in 60.0%.

result.other_findings: 60% had at least one elevated TSH during pregnancy (55% in first trimester).

result.topic: Primary bone tumours of the thoracic skeleton
result.setting: Leeds regional bone tumour registry

cycle1.result: 90 of 2004 registry cases (4.5%) were thoracic; ribs 37%, scapulae 32%, thoracic vertebrae 11%, sternum 11%, clavicles 9%; 54 malignant v 36 benign.

result.other_findings: Presenting symptoms poorly predicted malignancy; few correct preoperative diagnoses, supporting early biopsy.

result.topic: Inpatient care for children with diabetes
result.setting: 27 children's diabetes services in three regional networks, southern England
result.standard: Department of Health Children's Diabetes Working Group care standards

cycle1.result: 70% of wards had all four protocols (52% of EDs); trained children's nurses every shift on wards 100% vs EDs 33%; dietetic advice on wards 37%; diabetes team informed within 2 h in daytime 26%.

result.other_findings: Half of centres reported insulin errors; only 11% would contact the diabetes consultant overnight for PICU/HDU admissions.

result.topic: Surgical site infection and antibiotic prophylaxis
result.setting: One consultant surgeon, district general hospital (Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester)
result.standard: Annual review of wound infection rate

cycle1.result: Wound infection 43% in colorectal surgery in 1976 with no prophylaxis; 12% in biliary surgery 1981-7 with no prophylaxis.

result.intervention: Serial changes in prophylaxis: single intravenous metronidazole and cefuroxime intraoperatively plus peritoneal and wound lavage with 0.1% tetracycline.

cycle2.result: Colorectal wound infection 1%; biliary 2% after tetracycline lavage.

result.other_findings: 400 colorectal resections (1976-89) and 500 cholecystectomies (1981-9); multiple annual audit rounds.

result.setting: Department of General Surgery, Scarborough General Hospital; questionnaire to on-call surgical trainees
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons handover guidelines (satisfactory compliance >80% of sessions)

cycle1.result: Satisfactory compliance for only five of nine components; 95% at a designated place; none had formal handover training; 48% (n=20) aware of guidelines.

result.other_findings: Computer-generated handover sheet most common (57%, n=24); 21% dissatisfied with current handover.

result.setting: Department of Otolaryngology, Royal Blackburn Hospital
result.standard: ENTUK and SIGN criteria: five or more disabling sore throat episodes per year for at least a year

cycle1.result: All 17 tonsillectomies justified but only two (11.8 per cent) had documented indications.

result.intervention: Surgeons agreed to list specified criteria when scheduling; pro forma reminder distributed to all clinics.

cycle2.result: 85 per cent had all essential criteria documented in the listing letter.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: National BSCCP questionnaire to UK lead colposcopists

cycle1.result: 110 of 210 (52%) responded; all discuss stage IA cancer at gynaecological MDT; conservatively managed women followed up for at least 5 years.

result.other_findings: Wide variation in management of LVSI and stage IA2; national guidance recommended.

result.setting: National colonoscopy audit; 302 NHS units, 2681 colonoscopists
result.standard: National colonoscopy standards (caecal intubation, polyp detection, retrieval, comfort)

cycle1.result: Unadjusted caecal intubation rate 92.3% (adjusted 95.8%); polyp detection rate 32.1%; 92.3% of resected polyps retrieved; 90.2% acceptable comfort.

result.other_findings: Eight perforations and 52 significant haemorrhages; improvement from CIR 76.9% in the study seven years earlier; performance above national standards.

result.topic: Use of routine data for obstetric audit
result.setting: Maternity department, regional referral hospital, Oxford (John Radcliffe Hospital)
result.standard: Principles of clinical audit (comparison with agreed standards)

cycle1.result: 130 special inquiries based on computerised data; most were descriptive; genuine clinical audit was rare.

result.other_findings: Simple audits (e.g. induction after term) could be supported by routine data, but detailed audits needed supplementary data.

result.topic: ICU mortality against APACHE II prediction
result.setting: Intensive care unit, Belfast City Hospital

cycle1.result: Mortality 15.5% vs predicted 18.8%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 11 UK general practices and 442 THIN practices

cycle1.result: 8.4 children per 1000 child years with at least one maltreatment-related code (8.0/1000 in THIN); of 25 patients with known maltreatment, six had no maltreatment codes.

result.intervention: Consensus recommendations to code 'child is cause for concern' and use a code list around four clinical concepts with an optional templated form (not re-audited).
result.other_findings: GPs cited harm to patient relationship, uncertainty about codes and family information as reasons for undercoding.

result.setting: 54 NHS mental health trusts in the POMH-UK quality improvement programme; older people's services
result.standard: POMH-UK practice standards for antipsychotic prescribing in dementia (including 6-monthly review)

cycle1.result: 1620 (16%) without psychotic illness prescribed an antipsychotic; of 1001 (62%) treated >6 months, only three-quarters had a documented review in the previous 6 months.

result.other_findings: Good practice in considering alternatives and documenting target symptoms; younger age, care home/inpatient setting, vascular or Parkinson's dementia and severity predicted prescribing.

result.setting: Breast Cancer Audit Database of the Society of Breast Surgeons of Australia and New Zealand

cycle1.result: 2.3% synchronous bilateral cancers; disease-specific survival did not differ (p=0.206); adjusted relative risk of death 1.17 (95% CL 0.91, 1.51).

result.other_findings: SBBC rose from 1.4% under 40 years to 4.1% at 80 years or over.

result.setting: 34 general practices (St George's Hospital Medical School, London)
result.standard: Inhaler technique scoring system (good 4/4, adequate 3-4, inadequate 2 or less)

cycle1.result: 25% had inadequate technique; good technique 78% with Turbohaler and 45% with metered dose inhalers.

result.other_findings: 63% used metered dose inhalers, 15% Rotahalers, 9% spacers.

result.topic: Anaesthetic technique and recovery after orthognathic surgery
result.setting: Single centre, Heatherwood and Wexham Park Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Propofol-remifentanil (n = 21) had higher pain scores in first 4 hours than volatile with longer-acting opioids (n = 30) (P = .016).

result.other_findings: No differences in opioid use, haemodynamics or PONV; non-significant trend to shorter recovery with TIVA.

result.setting: Somerset Court Advice and Assessment Service, first year
result.standard: Six objectives in the Service Level Agreement

cycle1.result: Service met all six Service Level Agreement objectives.

result.other_findings: Self-harm/suicidal ideation and mood disorders were the main referral reasons; electronic patient records helped provide timely information to court.

result.setting: Four Birmingham primary care practices
result.standard: National guidelines (2008): ask two screening questions about work effect

cycle1.result: Occupation recorded in 55/396 (14%); 9 (2%) had any work-effect enquiry; 4 had enquiry at diagnosis among 117 with traceable notes.

result.intervention: Suggested modifying asthma review electronic templates (not implemented).
result.other_findings: Occupational asthma prevalence in working-age asthmatics 0.3%, suggesting under-diagnosis.

result.topic: Colonoscopic surveillance after colorectal cancer resection
result.setting: Derriford Hospital, Plymouth

cycle1.result: Colonoscopic follow-up by 2 years 32.8%; 63.5% by 5 years.

result.other_findings: Significant neoplasia and resectable recurrences found before 2 years; interval of no more than 2 years recommended.

result.setting: Belfast Dental School compared with UK and Republic of Ireland dental schools

cycle1.result: Three main differences: other schools used irrigants besides sodium hypochlorite, different intracanal medicaments and higher NaOCl concentrations.

result.intervention: New evidence-based protocols introduced for primary and secondary cases.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Intensive care unit, Barnet General Hospital, London
result.standard: Royal College of Anaesthetists NAP4 recommendations for advanced airway management

cycle1.result: Local practice benchmarked against NAP4 national standards (figures not given).

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary training, improved resources, new working practices and a new departmental training programme.

cycle2.result: Improved endotracheal intubation technique and embedded new practice (figures not given).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Chest reopening after cardiac arrest on cardiac surgical wards
result.setting: Cardiac surgical wards, Papworth Hospital, Cambridge

cycle1.result: Survival to discharge 53.6% (52 of 97) and at 1 year 44.3%; 21 (21.6%) underwent scoop and run; 5 of 12 daytime vs none of 9 night-time scoop and runs survived.

result.other_findings: All five survivors were neurologically intact despite median 22 min to chest opening; scoop and run should be restricted to witnessed arrests.

result.topic: Technical quality of root canal treatment
result.setting: Undergraduate endodontic competence cases, Dublin Dental University Hospital
result.standard: European guidelines for technical quality of root canal treatment (obturation within 2 mm of apex, no voids or errors)

cycle1.result: Acceptable: 49% of single-rooted and 17% of multi-rooted teeth; voids in 36% (single) and 38% (multi); within 2 mm of apex 69% and 60%.

result.other_findings: 119 canals in 78 teeth selected; five teeth excluded for missing or non-diagnostic radiographs; results similar to previous undergraduate studies.

result.topic: Reasons for pulmonary function test referral
result.setting: Four adult lung function laboratories (3 public, 1 private)

cycle1.result: Identifiable reason for referral in 83%; follow-up of known respiratory disease 53%, specific symptoms 18%, possible specific lung disease 13%.

result.other_findings: Testing in known disease or for change was the primary reason in 60% of tests.

result.setting: Single psychiatric outpatient clinic (University of Cambridge)

cycle1.result: No significant effect of antipsychotic class or diagnosis on diabetes prevalence; prevalence not significantly different from the national average.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 56 residential aged care facilities

cycle1.result: Purpose-built units (24) scored significantly higher than non-purpose-built (32) on nine of 10 EAT subscales and overall.

result.other_findings: Validation study of the Environmental Audit Tool.

result.setting: Acutely unwell adult medical inpatients, London trust
result.standard: Trust IV fluid guideline based on British consensus guidelines; seven local standards forming a prescribing bundle

cycle1.result: 3.8% met the IV fluid prescribing bundle; legibility 28.3%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: UK Renal Registry national PD access audit; England, Northern Ireland and Wales
result.standard: 2009 Renal Association working party recommended PD access outcome measures

cycle1.result: 43 of 63 centres returned data on 863 PD catheter placements, 225 with missing insertion date; outcome results not yet available.

result.other_findings: Data completeness and ambiguities were noted as problems.

result.setting: MINAP; 215 acute hospitals in England and Wales

cycle1.result: Adjusted mini-GRACE calibration better than mini-GRACE (Hosmer-Lemeshow p=0.33).

result.other_findings: Both scores performed well but less well in higher-risk subgroups; AMG use may be limited by missing predictors.

result.setting: Iron deficiency anaemia pathway, Derriford Hospital, Plymouth
result.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for initial investigation

cycle1.result: Initial diagnosis in 266 (42%); GI luminal neoplasm in 124 (19%), 54 (8%) malignant; of 373 without initial cause, 6 (2%) later had GI luminal malignancy and 18 (5%) other malignancy.

result.other_findings: 143 (22%) did not have confirmed iron deficiency; normal-ferritin patients had as many GI malignancies as low-ferritin patients.

result.topic: Salvage therapy after failed endoscopic haemostasis
result.setting: UK national audit of upper GI bleeding; 212 centres

cycle1.result: 533 (11.9 per cent) had further bleeding; 163 (30.6 per cent) had salvage surgery (97), TAE (60) or both (6); mortality 29 per cent after surgery and 10 per cent after TAE.

result.other_findings: Consultant surgeon present in 89 per cent of operations; coagulopathy (OR 3.27) and haemoglobin 10 g/dl or less predicted endoscopic failure.

result.setting: UK Central Cardiac Audit Database (Great Ormond Street Hospital)

cycle1.result: Commonest diagnoses: VSD 13%, PDA 10.4%, tetralogy of Fallot 9.5%; biventricular without aortic obstruction 64.2%.

result.other_findings: Of operations classed 'not a specific procedure', 97.1% had a diagnosis identified in Scheme 1.

result.setting: Neonatal Unit, Royal Children's Hospital, Melbourne
result.standard: Study site's recommended chloral hydrate dosing range

cycle1.result: 238 doses to 32 patients; 84% ordered as repeating doses; median repetitive dose above the recommended range; distress assessment accompanied about half of doses.

result.other_findings: No recognisable pattern of sedation maintenance or weaning.

result.setting: Survey of 3rd-year medical students on O&G placements (Sheffield)

cycle1.result: Students rated the RCOG standards as highly appropriate.

result.other_findings: Significant gender differences in clinical exposure and career intentions; greater interest in O&G than previously documented.

result.setting: Wales-Trent Bowel Cancer Audit 1993 and Welsh Bowel Cancer Audit 2007-2008

cycle1.result: Surgical treatment in 93%.

result.other_findings: Demographics and ASA unchanged; less frequent surgery contributed to lower 30-day operative mortality.

result.topic: Intradural and subdural haemorrhage at paediatric autopsy
result.setting: Two paediatric pathology referral centres (Barts Health NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: In fetuses, SDH with IDH was present in 22%, IDH alone in 31% and no or minimal haemorrhage in 47%; in infants and children SDH with IDH was present in 19%, IDH alone in 32% and no or minimal haemorrhage in 49%.

result.other_findings: SDH was significantly associated with hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (P < 0.001) and with age (P < 0.0001), being more common in infants 1 month or younger corrected age.

result.topic: Blood transfusion in head and neck surgery
result.setting: ENT Department, Dudley Road Hospital, Birmingham

cycle1.result: Retrospective review of 100 records found transfusion practice lacked standardisation on a scientific basis and represented resource over-utilisation.

result.intervention: A new transfusion policy for head and neck surgery was proposed; no re-audit reported.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Khartoum Teaching Hospital, 1,000-bed tertiary hospital, elective surgery
result.standard: International standards for surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (choice, dose, timing, duration)

cycle1.result: 99.4% (1,758) received prophylactic antibiotics; prophylaxis was recommended in 74.5% (1,288) of cases. Among recommended cases, 56.3% received a broad-spectrum antibiotic or unnecessary combination, 70.9% a sub-therapeutic dose, 9.3% (120) the first dose within the proper time window, and 97% (1,250) an extended duration. Compliance with all criteria was 2.7% (47).

result.intervention: Development and implementation of local guidelines recommended; no re-audit reported.
result.other_findings: 25.5% (442) received antibiotics that were not recommended; 1,814 procedures, 70.4% clean-contaminated.

result.topic: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting management in children
result.setting: National paediatric cancer unit, Our Lady's Children's Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Anti-emetic prescribing proportional to emetogenic potential of chemotherapy (evidence-based practice)

cycle1.result: Anti-emetic prescription was unrelated to the emetogenic potential of chemotherapy; dexamethasone was used in only 1 case; 20 children took no anti-emetics after discharge, of whom 11 had delayed vomiting.

result.intervention: Evidence-based guidelines established with anti-emetic prescription proportional to emetogenic potential; education of staff, patients and families recommended. No re-audit reported.
result.other_findings: 50 patient episodes in 25 children.

result.topic: Type 2 diabetes prescribing in primary care
result.setting: Primary care (University of East Anglia School of Pharmacy)

cycle1.result: All anti-hyperglycaemic prescribing was within guidance; 87.4% of patients on an anti-hypertensive were prescribed an ACE inhibitor or equivalent.

result.other_findings: A large number of patients remained uncontrolled for blood glucose or blood pressure, suggesting a role for pharmacists in optimisation and adherence.

result.setting: 215 hospitals in England and Wales (MINAP registry)

cycle1.result: 30-day mortality fell from 10.7% (10.6 to 10.9%) in 2004/5 to 8.4% (8.3 to 8.6%) in 2008/9; median hospital opportunity-based composite score rose from 87.3 to 90.3.

result.other_findings: Improvements in 30-day mortality differed by age and sex; young males had plateaued while other groups were still improving.

result.setting: Department of Breast Radiology, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 4.1% of 855 breast ultrasounds were in patients under 25; 20 had features of fibroadenoma, confirmed histologically in 15.

result.other_findings: Five patients were not biopsied due to young age or bilateral fibroadenoma; authors conclude typical fibroadenoma under 25 does not need biopsy.

result.topic: Anaphylaxis management in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency department, Royal Liverpool and Broadgreen University Hospitals

cycle1.result: Widespread inconsistencies in diagnosis and treatment of anaphylaxis (no figures given in abstract).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Single general surgical department (University of Limerick)
result.standard: Health Service Executive generic prescription policy

cycle1.result: 51% of prescriptions were trade-name where an appropriate generic equivalent existed.

result.other_findings: Cost implications were greatly affected by hospital pharmacy substitution policies.

result.topic: Lung cancer diagnosis in primary care (significant event audit)
result.setting: 92 general practices, North of England Cancer Network

cycle1.result: Most significant event audits showed timely recognition and referral; delays often had reasonable explanations such as normal or benign chest X-ray reports, patient factors and comorbidity.

result.other_findings: Lessons included limitations of chest X-ray, vigilance in patients with comorbidity and the importance of safety-netting.

result.topic: Mental health team working audit tool validation
result.setting: Community mental health teams (HSE West, Roscommon)

cycle1.result: The 25-item Mental Health Team Development Audit Tool showed good face validity and internal reliability, with three internally consistent subscales.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis in mandibular fracture fixation
result.setting: Five maxillofacial units in the Yorkshire region
result.standard: Infection rate after ORIF of mandibular fractures compared with other centres

cycle1.result: Wide range of antimicrobial prophylaxis used across units; infection rate 10.3%.

result.intervention: A common perioperative antimicrobial protocol was implemented in all units: amoxicillin or clarithromycin plus metronidazole IV from admission with 2 postoperative doses.

cycle2.result: Infection rate 8.9% (vs 10.3%; χ2=0.051, df=1, p=0.83, not significant).

result.other_findings: Authors recommend short perioperative prophylaxis with a maximum of 2 postoperative doses.

result.topic: Health equity in chronic disease management
result.setting: 38 general practices, Tower Hamlets primary care trust, east London
result.standard: Key process and outcome indicators for CHD, type 2 diabetes and COPD by ethnicity, age and gender

cycle1.result: Baseline inequalities were found in each condition across the three east London PCTs.

result.intervention: Practice-level health equity audit reports disseminated to practices with facilitation sessions.

cycle2.result: Performance on physician-driven indicators (cholesterol in CHD, blood pressure and HbA1c in diabetes) improved, but smoking rates in COPD remained static; all ethnic groups improved without reduction in differences between them.

result.other_findings: Reductions in gender and age group differences were seen in diabetes and CHD; changes could not be attributed to the audits.

result.setting: Elective surgery (University of Nottingham/Sherwood Forest Hospitals)
result.standard: Royal College of Nursing (2005) preoperative fasting guidelines

cycle1.result: Results upheld previous studies showing prolonged preoperative starving periods (no figures given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Excessively starved patients reported hunger, distress and nausea.

result.setting: Inpatient echocardiography, John Hunter Hospital, Newcastle, New South Wales

cycle1.result: Significant pulmonary hypertension documented in 4.6% of patients referred for inpatient echocardiography.

result.other_findings: Pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease was the most common aetiology.

result.setting: Acute pain service, major abdominal surgery (Manchester)
result.standard: Reduction in percentage of patients with an epidural in severe pain

cycle1.result: Baseline mean pain score (VNRS) was 4; 57% of patients were hypotensive on the first postoperative day.

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary group used statistical process control charts to identify variation and introduce quality improvement interventions.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in epidural failure rate (no figures given in abstract).

result.other_findings: No special cause variation by surgeon, clinical area or prior pain; the work led to a national pain registry.

result.setting: ICNARC Case Mix Programme database (critical care units)

cycle1.result: The clinical obstetric early warning score had AUROC 0.957 (95% CI 0.923-0.991) and the statistical score 0.995 (0.992-0.998) in the validation set (n = 2200).

result.other_findings: Comparators: MEOWS 0.955, CEMACH obstetric score 0.937, NEWS 0.973.

result.setting: Department of Dermatology, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee
result.standard: Proposed BSDS minimum dataset and audit standards for UK Mohs centres

cycle1.result: Primary BCC recurrence rate 0.3% at both 2 and 5 years.

result.intervention: Local Mohs database modified in response to repeated audit cycles; minimum dataset developed.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Nurse-led telephone follow-up for oral chemotherapy
result.setting: Christie Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, Manchester

cycle1.result: Nurse-led telephone follow-up was associated with reduced toxicity (chest pain, vomiting, oral mucositis, nausea, insomnia) versus historical standard care (n = 81).

result.other_findings: Telephone follow-up was similar to home care for vomiting and mucositis but less effective for diarrhoea and insomnia.

result.topic: Head injury CT imaging guideline adherence
result.setting: Emergency department of a major UK trauma hospital
result.standard: NICE CG56 head injury guideline criteria for head CT

cycle1.result: 73% of CG56 criteria were documented; 32% of patients had head CT, 24% (37) of these with pathology; 24 patients (5%) had CT without documented clinical justification, none with pathology.

result.intervention: Further education and awareness of head injury guidelines suggested; no re-audit reported.
result.other_findings: Least documented criteria were signs of basal skull fracture and amnesia of events.

result.setting: Three maxillofacial units (multicentre, including University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff)
result.standard: BOS/BAOMS minimum dataset for orthognathic clinical records

cycle1.result: Compliance varied between units; documentation of altered sensation was consistently poor and too many unnecessary radiographs were taken.

result.intervention: Recirculation of the guidelines suggested; no re-audit reported.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Triple assessment in male breast disease
result.setting: Cambridge Breast Unit, Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local age-related triple assessment protocol (mammography in men 35 years or older)

cycle1.result: Sensitivity was 64.0% for clinical examination, 77.8% for mammography and 92.0% for ultrasound; 25 cancers were diagnosed, 24 in men over 40.

result.other_findings: Two cancers presented with nipple discharge; bloody nipple discharge is a suspicious sign.

result.setting: Three intensive care units, NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: Prescription accuracy (patient data, dose, concentration, rate, frequency, legibility, signature)

cycle1.dates: 7 rolling days over 7 weeks, September and October 2011
cycle1.result: 40 errors in 1418 prescriptions (2.8%): advanced nurse practitioners 2 in 388 (0.6%), trainee medical staff 33 in 984 (3.4%), consultants 5 in 73 (6.8%).

result.other_findings: Error rates differed significantly between prescribing groups; 77 patient prescription Cardexes reviewed.

result.topic: Early mortality after lung cancer resection
result.setting: English National Lung Cancer Audit

cycle1.result: 3% (334) died within 30 days and 5.9% (647) within 90 days of surgery for NSCLC.

result.other_findings: Age was the strongest predictor of early death (adjusted OR within 90 days 1.46 for 80-84 vs 70-74 years); performance status, lung function, stage and procedure also predicted death.

result.setting: UK intensive care units in the ICNARC database (16 neurosciences units, 48 and 138 general ICUs)

cycle1.result: Intracerebral haemorrhage: ICU mortality 42.4% and acute hospital mortality 62.1%; lower mortality in specialist neurocritical care units.

result.other_findings: Myasthenia gravis (n = 1,064) ICU/hospital mortality 8.7%/22%; Guillain-Barre syndrome (n = 1,906) 7.7%/16.7%, not decreasing over time.

result.setting: Neonatal unit (University of Strathclyde, Glasgow)
result.standard: ESPGHAN recommended phosphate intake of 184-230 mg/kg/day

cycle1.result: A majority of infants under 32 weeks did not achieve the recommended phosphate intake in the first week; mean plasma phosphate was 2.10 (0.38) mM/L with oral supplementation versus 1.92 (0.50) mM/L without.

result.other_findings: Despite recommended intake from week 3, many infants had plasma phosphate below the normal range.

result.topic: Day case versus overnight paediatric tonsillectomy pain
result.setting: Department of Anaesthesia, James Cook University Hospital, Middlesbrough

cycle1.result: Small but significant greater baseline pain scores in day case group (n = 32) versus overnight stay (n = 28) in the first 24 h; no difference in worst pain at 24 h or pain at 7 days.

result.other_findings: No difference in vomiting, healthcare consultation, readmission or satisfaction.

result.setting: North Cork area, HSE South orthodontic service (Cork University Dental School and Hospital)
result.standard: HSE eligibility criteria based on modified IOTN

cycle1.result: 61% of patients were IOTN grade 5 and 36% grade 4; records verified patients satisfied HSE eligibility criteria.

result.other_findings: 57% female; Class II division 1 was the commonest malocclusion (40%), Class III 18%.

result.setting: 384 hospitals in 13 European countries

cycle1.result: Adherence to the 10 key recommendations varied between hospitals and countries (no figures given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Lack of available spirometry and variable use of oxygen and NIV were high-impact areas for improvement.

result.setting: 30 acute medical units (Society for Acute Medicine national audit)
result.standard: Society for Acute Medicine common standards, including timing of junior and senior review; high reliability defined as over 90% compliance

cycle1.result: Compliance with timing of junior and senior review was highly variable; for almost all other standards only a small number of units achieved over 90% compliance.

result.other_findings: Mean 36 (SD 14) admissions per unit; annual audit suggested.

result.setting: Ten cancer centres (national rotational radiotherapy audit)

cycle1.result: 2D-array detector measurements agreed closely with ion chamber and alanine measurements (concordance correlation coefficient >0.998).

result.other_findings: A commercial detector array was found suitable for dosimetry audit in place of standard systems.

result.topic: Early intervention in psychosis discharge outcomes
result.setting: North Derbyshire Early Intervention in Psychosis Service
result.standard: Standards based on international and national early intervention guidelines

cycle1.result: 55% were transferred back to primary care; 69% did not require inpatient admission; almost half were in education, training or employment at discharge.

result.other_findings: Most had psychological, pharmacological and physical health needs addressed but there was room for improvement against standards.

result.setting: UK Renal Registry multisite audit, 43 of 65 centres in England, Northern Ireland and Wales
result.standard: Aim to identify an appropriate standard of PD catheter function

cycle1.result: 917 PD catheter placements reported from 43 centres; percutaneous insertion was associated with higher early (under 2 weeks) peritonitis and more flow problems.

result.other_findings: Wide variation between centres in PD catheter use for late presenters; diabetes was not associated with more catheter failure or early peritonitis.

result.topic: Osteoporosis screening and treatment in primary care
result.setting: Rural medical centre, 10 general practitioners (New South Wales)
result.standard: Royal Australian College of General Practitioners osteoporosis guidelines

cycle1.result: Only 35% had been scanned for osteoporosis; 66% with osteopenia and 26% with osteoporosis were receiving no treatment; 48% with previous low BMD had not had recommended follow-up scans.

result.other_findings: Scanning rates varied with age, gender and number and type of risk factors; active surveillance with PENCAT suggested.

result.topic: Bone protection in patients on anti-epileptic drugs
result.setting: General practices in Ellesmere Port and Neston (13) and Chester area (26)
result.standard: NICE epilepsy guidelines and QOF (calcium and vitamin D supplementation for patients on long-term AEDs)

cycle1.result: Clinical notes review of 414 patients in 2009 with written recommendations for supplementation where appropriate (baseline figures not given in abstract).

result.intervention: Individualised written recommendations after a notes review, plus a computer message added to relevant prescriptions recommending supplements.

cycle2.result: Significant increase in repeat prescriptions of calcium and vitamin D, most marked where both written recommendations and computer message were used compared with computer message only.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: All interventional radiology units in Scotland (Scottish Audit of Surgical Mortality pilot)

cycle1.result: 95 forms sent, 71 returned and 46 completed the full process; 10 areas for consideration or concern were attributed.

result.intervention: Anonymised case vignettes and reports used as educational tools.
result.other_findings: Most areas of concern involved percutaneous biliary interventions.

result.setting: 170 consultant-led maternity units in England (postal questionnaire)
result.standard: NICE and RCOG guidance on information about caesarean section complications

cycle1.result: Response rate 84.11% (143/170); 50/143 (34.97%) units used risk stickers, pre-typed or standard checklist forms, while 92/143 (64.34%) relied on information given from doctors' memory.

result.other_findings: Subgroup analysis of 23 hospitals showed large heterogeneity in information given; standardised written information recommended.

result.topic: Colorectal cancer referral pathway and GP communication
result.setting: Surgeons from three Australian states

cycle1.result: Median time from colonoscopy to first surgical consultation was 10 days, with 19% waiting more than 28 days; a report back to the GP was found in 78% of records.

result.other_findings: 33 surgeons participated; no surgeon characteristics explained variation in GP feedback.

result.setting: Rapid access prostate assessment clinic, Galway University Hospital

cycle1.result: Average wait to first visit 18 days (12-39); 503 (45.5%) diagnosed with prostate cancer on TRUS biopsy.

result.other_findings: 71 (14.1%) had radical prostatectomy, 67 (13.3%) active monitoring, 235 external beam radiotherapy and 68 (13.5%) brachytherapy.

result.topic: Left ventricular function quantification in myocardial perfusion imaging
result.setting: 58 nuclear medicine institutions across the UK

cycle1.result: Mean ejection fraction 58.5±3%, end-diastolic volume 114±12 ml and end-systolic volume 54±6 ml across centres.

result.other_findings: Results were affected by frames per cycle and software package but not by reconstruction filter.

result.setting: Royal Devon and Exeter Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 1605 elective laparoscopic cholecystectomies performed by 8 surgeons (conversion figures truncated in abstract).

result.intervention: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy practice restricted to surgeons with interest and commitment to the service.

cycle2.result: Concentrating expertise led to standardisation and reduced conversion rates (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Correlation found between surgical volume and outcomes.

result.setting: National audit (Better Blood Transfusion, National Services Scotland)
result.standard: Best practice for patient identification and monitoring during transfusion

cycle1.result: Most patients received safe transfusion with adequate identity checks and monitoring, but some lacked an identity wristband or monitoring (no figures given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Continued improving trend compared with previous audits.

result.topic: Multiple psychiatric diagnoses in community mental health team
result.setting: Community mental health team, Bedford
result.standard: Every patient should have only one mental health diagnosis where possible

cycle1.result: 23.2% of patients had multiple diagnoses.

result.intervention: No intervention; repeated measurements in June 2011 and February 2013.
result.other_findings: Proportion was 25.2% in June 2011.

result.setting: Bedford adult working age community mental health team

cycle1.result: Case descriptions of patients assessed for Parkinson's disease; many were started on Parkinson's medication (no figures given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Patients often needed to stay on an atypical antipsychotic.

result.setting: Bedford East Community Mental Health Team

cycle1.result: Patients with each psychiatric condition had a higher than expected prevalence of autoimmune conditions overall.

result.other_findings: Hypothyroidism was more common than expected in almost every psychiatric condition.

result.topic: Acute severe ulcerative colitis rescue therapy outcomes
result.setting: UK IBD audit, 209 (2008) and 198 (2010) hospital sites

cycle1.result: ASUC in-hospital mortality 1.2% in 2008 and 0.7% in 2010 (P = 0.22); response to first-line steroids 61% and 58%.

result.other_findings: Mortality was higher in steroid non-responders (2008: 2.9% (9/315) vs 0.19% (1/537)); ciclosporin response rates were relatively low.

result.setting: UK/US Role 3 medical treatment facility, Camp Bastion, Afghanistan
result.standard: UK published guidance and the deployed antimicrobial formulary

cycle1.result: 84.8% (212/250) were prescribed antimicrobials in line with the formulary: 93.5% (130/139) in battle injury versus 73.9% (82/111) in disease and non-battle injury.

result.other_findings: 475 case notes reviewed; co-amoxiclav was used in 74% (185/250) of patients.

result.setting: Three PCI centres in Northern Ireland

cycle1.result: 30-day MACE rate 0.85% with sub-acute stent thrombosis 0.4%; no MACE from discharge to 24 hours.

result.other_findings: 72.3% elective and 27.7% ACS; radial access in 98%; 40.8% of lesions high risk.

result.topic: Aged care nursing documentation quality instrument
result.setting: Australian aged care (University of Wollongong)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: The 34-question QANDAC instrument showed satisfactory validity and inter-rater reliability.

result.topic: Cardiac implantable device management in radiotherapy
result.setting: UK radiotherapy departments (national policy audit)
result.standard: Current gold-standard evidence-based guidelines for managing cardiac implantable electronic devices during radiotherapy

cycle1.result: 31/45 (69%) policies defined pacemaker tolerance dose and 14/45 (31%) the monitoring procedure in line with best practice; only 5/45 (11%) defined ICD tolerance dose and 12/45 (27%) ICD monitoring in line with best practice.

result.other_findings: 47/67 (70%) departments responded; policies were based on 1994 AAPM research.

result.setting: All seven UK intraoperative radiotherapy sites

cycle1.result: Mean difference between measured and planned dose was -3.2±2.7%; isotropy within ±3% laterally and +11±4% forward; depth doses within 5±2% of calibration values.

result.other_findings: Agreement within measurement uncertainty for all parameters except forward anisotropy.

result.setting: Medical Physics and Bioengineering Department, St James's Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Maximum velocity accuracy was consistently overestimated by 12% to 56% across tested systems; repeatability 18 ± 3.3% (MVA) and 19 ± 3.5% (ISB).

result.other_findings: MVA errors ranged 12.3-20.8% for linear, 32.3-53.8% for curvilinear and 27-40.7% for phased array probes.

result.topic: Acute myocardial infarction composite quality indicators
result.setting: 199 hospitals in the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project

cycle1.result: Median (IQR) composite scores: OBCS 95.0% (3.5), WOBCS 94.7% (0.8), ANCS 80.9% (11.8); each 1% increase was associated with 1 to 3% and 4% reductions in 6-month and 1-year mortality.

result.other_findings: The aggregation method changed hospital rank and the proportion of outliers; ANCS had no significant association with 30-day mortality.

result.setting: 33 general practices (pathology codes) and 2 practices (record review)

cycle1.result: Strong agreement between manual audit and tool for all variables except chronic kidney disease diagnoses, due to a programming error.

result.other_findings: Four of nine pathology companies used incorrect codes for albuminuria tests.

result.topic: Cystogram after bladder repair in colorectal surgery
result.setting: Department of General Surgery, Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital

cycle1.result: All patients had at least one postoperative cystogram; only 46% had cystogram instructions documented in the operation note; 4 (7%) showed a leak.

result.other_findings: Repeat cystography in the four leaks showed no or smaller leak and no further procedures were needed.

result.topic: Prenatal detection of congenital heart disease
result.setting: One congenital cardiac centre with 3 prospective and 16 retrospective maternity hospitals, London

cycle1.result: 385 major CHD cases (3.2/1000); relative detection performance hospital A 1.68, B 0.70, C 0.65.

result.other_findings: Standardised prenatal detection across 19 hospitals was 37% for TGA and 34% for coarctation, with wide variation.

result.setting: Diabetes and Endocrine Center, Bahrain Defence Forces Hospital
result.standard: Recognised standards for diabetes process and outcome measures

cycle1.result: HbA1c, blood pressure, lipids, creatinine and weight recorded in over 90%; smoking recorded in 8% and BMI in 19%; retinal screening 42%, foot inspection 22%, microalbuminuria 23%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Pain control after third molar surgery
result.setting: Department of Oral Surgery, King's College Dental Hospital, London
result.standard: Adequate postoperative pain control with the departmental analgesic protocol

cycle1.result: 53% of patients experienced moderate to severe pain.

result.intervention: Written patient instructions on postoperative analgesic use introduced, then postoperative ibuprofen dose increased from 400 mg to 600 mg.

cycle2.result: 96% of patients had satisfactory pain control at the third audit.

result.other_findings: At the second audit (after written instructions) 86% had pain managed successfully.

result.setting: Orthodontic Unit, Cork University Dental School and Hospital (HSE South referral centre)

cycle1.result: 83 (29%) new referrals were eligible for treatment under HSE guidelines.

result.other_findings: Commonest eligible traits were crossbite with >2 mm discrepancy (24) and overjet >9 mm (21).

result.setting: HSE orthodontic service, Dublin Mid-Leinster region (St James's Hospital)
result.standard: HSE national orthodontic referral protocol (2007); audit standard 75% of referrals with correct IOTN classification

cycle1.result: Referral to assessment within three to six months: 85-80% compliance for IOTN 5 and 4; 60% of referrals had correct IOTN classification.

result.intervention: No intervention; repeat audit to assess effect of HSE austerity measures.

cycle2.result: Compliance fell to 26-4% for IOTN 5 and 4 within three to six months; 51% correct IOTN classification (below 75% standard).

result.other_findings: Only 5a (overjet >9 mm), 5i (impacted teeth) and 5h (extensive hypodontia) met the standard for identification.

result.setting: Regional audit of Genitourinary Medicine services in the north east of England
result.standard: British Association of Sexual Health and HIV guidelines on managing syphilis in pregnancy, plus locally developed standards on multidisciplinary working and communication

cycle1.result: 69% treated according to national guidance; all cases completed treatment. Local standards on multidisciplinary working and communication were met less well.

result.intervention: A regional good practice guide was developed and implemented to address standards not met.
result.other_findings: Documentation of pregnancy outcomes in GUM records and communication between specialities were particular problems.

result.setting: Multicentre point-incident collaborative audit (East and South East England Specialist Pharmacy Services)
result.standard: National Patient Safety Agency Rapid Response Report (2010) on reducing harm from omitted and delayed medicines

cycle1.result: 21,825 antimicrobial doses reviewed; 13% were affected by omitted doses.

result.other_findings: Some omissions were in patients' best interests; the authors call for targeting omissions with no acceptable reason.

result.setting: UK central cardiac audit database, national PCI procedures

cycle1.result: 2152 patients (0.97%) underwent rotational atherectomy; they were older (71.7 vs 64.1 years) and had worse medium-term survival, which persisted after adjustment.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Analgesia for adenotonsillectomy in children with obstructive sleep apnoea
result.setting: Department of Paediatric Anaesthesia, Royal Manchester Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: Major and minor respiratory complications 1.6% and 27%; primary/secondary haemorrhage 0.4%/1.2%; postoperative nausea and vomiting 4.4%.

result.other_findings: Complications were associated with younger age (p=0.0078), lower SpO2 low (p=0.004) and higher ODI4%.

result.topic: Clinical risk assessment documentation in mental health
result.setting: Eight-bed psychiatric intensive care unit in a regional mental health facility (Hunter New England)

cycle1.result: Varying quality of clinical risk assessment documentation (no figures in abstract).

result.intervention: Care zoning model introduced for three months, assigning patients to one of three risk zones with targeted interventions.

cycle2.dates: Weekly file audits during the three-month trial
cycle2.result: Improved quality of mental state documentation and more accurate identification of clinical risk information.

result.other_findings: Limited improvement in care planning and documentation of clinical interventions; staff acceptance improved.

result.setting: Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project, 247 hospitals in England and Wales

cycle1.result: For STEMI, six-month relative survival rose for ages 65-80 (84.8% to 89.2%) and over 80 (68.0% to 71.8%); improvements in survival were seen in older but not younger patients.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Private psychiatric hospital, Sydney

cycle1.result: None of the 60 audited files recorded waist circumference.

result.intervention: Single nurse-education session (25 nurses) and change in assessment-form design.

cycle2.result: 25 of 60 files (42%) recorded waist circumference (35 of 60, 58%, at 3 months).

result.other_findings: Only 19% had a healthy BMI, 37% smoked and 31% were hypertensive; only two patients refused measurement.

result.topic: Upper GI cancer registry data items
result.setting: Seven European oesophagogastric cancer surgery registries (EURECCA Upper GI)
result.country: Denmark, France, Ireland, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, United Kingdom

cycle1.result: Registered items ranged from 40 (Poland) to 650 (Ireland); 46 items were shared by at least six of seven registries.

result.other_findings: Information on non-surgical treatment was available in only 4 registries.

result.setting: 11 Irish hospitals in the European Respiratory Society COPD audit

cycle1.result: 35% received high-flow oxygen before admission; 18% cared for on a dedicated respiratory ward; 23% needed ventilatory support; median stay 7 days; 41% readmitted; 89% alive at 90 days.

result.topic: Unplanned PICU and HDU admission after surgery
result.setting: Paediatric hospital HDU and PICU after noncardiac surgery (University of Glasgow)
result.standard: Unplanned admission to intensive care after surgery as a recommended clinical indicator of perioperative safety

cycle1.result: 319 unplanned admissions to HDU/PICU (0.6%); 108 (34%) related to anaesthetic complications, a rate of 0.2%.

result.other_findings: Emergency procedures and shared airway procedures were particular risk factors.

result.setting: Multicentre clinical audit in 212 UK hospitals

cycle1.result: 66% had endoscopy within 24 h; 64% received endoscopic therapy; before endoscopy 57% received PPIs, 44% vasopressors and 27% antibiotics; 26% rebled and 15% died by day 30.

result.other_findings: Transfusion thresholds varied widely; the authors note deficiencies in use of vasopressors and endoscopic therapy.

result.setting: Three wards in a large university teaching hospital (University Hospitals of Leicester)
result.standard: Dementia CQUIN: screening for memory problems in patients over 75 admitted as emergencies

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Improvements to the screening process (details not given in abstract).
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Multicentre, multivendor audit in 16 UK nuclear medicine centres

cycle1.result: Eight centres had few clinically relevant discrepancies between half-count and full-count reports; eight had an unacceptably high number.

result.other_findings: Centres with many discrepancies were more likely to perform both rest and stress scans on normal studies.

result.setting: Teaching hospital with electronic prescribing, Sydney

cycle1.result: 0% compliant with the antibiotic policy.

result.intervention: Individualised feedback letters on policy compliance emailed to 36 prescribers.
result.other_findings: Problems with the policy and approval process made compliance hard to assess and achieve.

result.setting: UK National Lung Cancer Audit

cycle1.result: 19% of NSCLC patients were referred non-electively; this was associated with advanced stage and poorer survival.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Inner city NHS maternity unit with 6,000 births per year (University College London Hospitals)

cycle1.result: All 31 multiparous women delivered vaginally; of 16 nulliparous women, 6 planned caesarean, 4 vaginal, 4 instrumental and 2 emergency caesarean.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: National Audit of Schizophrenia, Mental Health Trusts and Health Boards, community patients
result.standard: Six prescribing standards from the national clinical guidelines for schizophrenia

cycle1.result: 15.9% prescribed two or more antipsychotics; 10.1% prescribed above recommended limits; 23.7% receiving clozapine; 430/1073 (40.1%) with treatment resistance had no documented reason for no clozapine trial.

result.standard: ICGP referral guidelines and standardised referral form (maximum 37 points)

cycle1.result: Average score 16/37; referrer details 75.42% (paediatric) and 72.9% (adult); clinical information 34% and 35%; only 32 letters mentioned examination findings.

result.topic: Latent tuberculosis management in renal transplant
result.setting: 23 UK renal transplant units (self-completed questionnaire)

cycle1.result: Three-quarters had a management protocol but only one-third of these were in line with guidance; almost half prescribed treatment at the wrong dose or duration.

result.setting: Single surgeon, regional university hospital (Cork University Hospital)

cycle1.result: 126 procedures in under-16s (22.8% of all operations); 56 emergency (44.4%) and 70 elective (55.5%).

result.setting: 10 Scottish health boards reporting colorectal cancer resections
result.standard: Royal College of Pathologists (2007) standards and NHS Quality Improvement Scotland standards

cycle1.result: Only three units met RCPath standards for rectal cancer reporting; non-proforma units failed minimum standards for serosal involvement (6%) and EMVI (24%); rectal cases with mean node count of 12 or more 56% (non-proforma) vs 81% (proforma).

result.setting: Royal Brompton Hospital, London (paediatric permanent pacemaker insertion)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Significant reduction in the number of children receiving no analgesia (figures not given).

result.other_findings: The audit cycle was repeated five times; no further adverse event forms were submitted.

result.topic: Acute coronary syndrome care in older people
result.setting: Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project, England and Wales

cycle1.result: Older patients were less likely to receive secondary prevention and intensive management; in STEMI patients aged 85 or over, 55% received reperfusion vs 84% of younger patients.

result.setting: Single maternity unit, Northwick Park Hospital
result.standard: All patients in the four SAFE categories (Sick, At-risk, Follow-ups, Epidurals) should be handed over

result.standard: NICE Clinical Guideline 148 (lower urinary tract symptoms in neurogenic bladder dysfunction)

cycle1.result: 21 of 118 patients had abnormal urine dipsticks; methylprednisolone was delayed pending culture and, if infected, until antibiotics were completed.

result.setting: UK National Cardiac Arrest Audit, 144 acute hospitals

cycle1.result: Incidence 1.6 per 1000 admissions; survival to discharge 18.4% (49.0% shockable, 10.5% non-shockable rhythms).

cycle1.result: 4 of 6 localities had a heavy workload index; patient acuity and dependency were high.

result.setting: UK radiotherapy centres, public and private (radiography and physics staff)

cycle1.result: 36% satisfied, 11% dissatisfied, 53% ambivalent; 37.5% of clinical staff had high emotional exhaustion; 42.4% reported presenteeism.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Pilot by 25 volunteer dentists on recall patients (Denplan)

cycle1.result: Mean oral health status score 79.5 +/- 10.8 (100 = perfect); mean age 53.

result.topic: Urinary catheter use at end of life

cycle1.result: 63% had an indwelling catheter; catheter insertion and care documentation present in 75%; 75% had continence screening on admission.
