result.topic: Neonatal surgical unit admissions and mortality
result.setting: Dan Young Neonatal Surgical Unit, Royal Hospital for Sick Children, Yorkhill, Glasgow

cycle1.result: Death rate 1.8% in 2012, 2.9% in 2013 and 2.6% in 2014; total and miscellaneous admissions increased since the 2008 amalgamation.

result.other_findings: No clinically significant change in index surgical case numbers or ISC deaths.

result.topic: GP involvement in community mental health care
result.setting: Community mental health centre, Eastern Suburbs Mental Health Service, Sydney
result.standard: Guidelines suggesting collaboration between GPs and mental health services for physical health in serious mental illness

cycle1.result: 98 of 191 (51%) patients had a GP documented in their records; no significant difference in metabolic screening rates between those with and without a GP.

result.other_findings: Patients with a GP had more medical diagnoses and took more psychiatric medications.

result.topic: Antithrombotic therapy guidelines in suspected acute coronary syndrome
result.setting: Western Infirmary Glasgow

cycle1.result: Full antithrombotic therapy recommended in 91 (45%) by the NHS GG&C guideline, 37 (18%) by SIGN and 30 (15%) by the proposed guideline; final diagnosis ACS in 39 (19%).

result.other_findings: Local guideline sensitivity 80%, specificity 63% (AUROC 0.71) versus SIGN 62%, 92% (0.77) and proposed guideline 54%, 94% (0.74).

result.topic: Diagnostic workup of paediatric inflammatory bowel disease
result.setting: 52 centres across 20 European countries and Israel (EUROKIDS registry)
result.standard: Complete diagnostic workup defined as full endoscopy plus small bowel radiology

cycle1.result: IBD-U was the provisional diagnosis in 265 of 3461 children (7.7%); only 48% had complete diagnostic workup, mainly lacking small bowel radiology.

result.other_findings: After reinvestigation over median 5.7 years, diagnosis changed to Crohn's disease (12%) or ulcerative colitis (20%), reducing the IBD-U rate to 5.6%.

result.topic: Persistent foramen ovale closure in divers
result.setting: Bristol Heart Institute, Bristol Royal Infirmary (single cardiologist)

cycle1.result: 105 divers had 107 procedures with a low complication rate; 81 of 95 with follow-up bubble echocardiography returned to unrestricted diving.

result.other_findings: Two needed treatment for AF, two needed a second procedure for residual shunt, and 16 had minor symptoms.

result.setting: Royal Shrewsbury Hospital

cycle1.result: 211 of 238 (88.7%) specimens showed appendicitis; negative appendicectomy rate 11.3%; 1.7% had other abnormal pathology.

result.other_findings: Females accounted for 59.1% of negative appendicectomies.

result.topic: Clinical value of medical liver biopsy reporting
result.setting: Department of Cellular Pathology, Oxford University Hospitals NHS Trust (regional centre)

cycle1.result: Hepatologists rated 96% of reports clinically useful; 56% confirmed diagnoses, 46% differentiated between and 42% excluded diagnoses; 74% changed management; 27% gave an unsuspected diagnosis.

result.other_findings: Pilot of a questionnaire-based clinico-pathological audit template.

result.topic: Preoperative tattooing for laparoscopic colorectal surgery
result.setting: Northampton General Hospital
result.standard: Recommendation of at least three tattoo spots one mucosal fold distal to the lesion, with tattoo site documented in the endoscopy report

cycle1.result: Only 59% had a visible and accurate tattoo; 17% documented but not visible, 4% visible but inaccurate, 20% had no tattoo.

result.intervention: Standardised departmental tattooing protocol recommended (not re-audited)
result.other_findings: Absent tattoos required on-table endoscopy and intraoperative specimen analysis.

result.topic: Audit and feedback target selection in cardiac rehabilitation
result.setting: Web-based audit and feedback intervention for cardiac rehabilitation (laboratory study)

cycle1.result: Indicators with more room for improvement were more likely to be selected; in more than a quarter of cases participants' choices did not match the colour-coded recommendation.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 32 of 33 Irish hospitals admitting acute medical patients
result.standard: National performance framework benchmarks mirroring the model of care

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Model of care with four clinical pathways through acute medical assessment units, patient flow modelling, and performance feedback to hospitals

cycle2.result: Average length of stay fell by 1.6 days nationally between 2010 and 2013.

result.other_findings: Achieved despite a 25% increase in hospital discharges.

result.topic: Implementation of national major trauma audit
result.setting: 27 trauma receiving hospitals (National Office of Clinical Audit)

cycle1.result: 25 of 27 hospitals now collect data using the TARN platform, with clinical leads and data co-ordinators.

result.other_findings: Hospitals incorporated MTA reports into governance meetings and broadly accepted the escalation policy.

result.setting: Leicester General Hospital, University Hospitals of Leicester

cycle1.result: Therapeutic failure 10%; no analgesic failure over 48 hours in 39% and fewer than 5 episodes in 57%.

result.other_findings: Surgical incision was within the dermatomal limit of the block in 70% (88/124).

result.setting: Eight paediatric cardiac intensive care centres (PC4 registry)
result.standard: Predefined major and minor discrepancy definitions; case submission within 1 month of discharge

cycle1.result: 434 encounters and 29,476 fields audited; overall accuracy 99.1% and major discrepancy rate 0.62%; seven of eight hospitals submitted >90% of cases within 1 month.

result.other_findings: Accuracy ranged from 96.3 to 99.5% across hospitals; no evidence of selective case omission.

result.topic: Stunting in children with congenital heart disease
result.setting: Regional paediatric cardiology service, University Hospital Southampton

cycle1.result: 28.2% of infants were stunted (z-score <-2).

result.other_findings: Severity of surgery score was not associated with length of stay.

result.setting: All tuberculosis diagnostic and treatment centres in Fiji (national programme data)

cycle1.result: Of 690 smear-positive TB patients diagnosed in the laboratory, 579 (84%) started treatment; pre-treatment loss to follow-up 111 (16%).

result.other_findings: Western Division had 33% pre-treatment loss to follow-up, over five times the risk of the Central Division (OR 5.2, 95% CI 3.1-8.9); peaks in 2003, 2004 and 2010.

result.topic: Retreatment tuberculosis sputum culture and drug susceptibility testing
result.setting: One reference and three zonal laboratories and 500 health facilities managing retreatment TB, Tanzania
result.standard: National Tuberculosis and Leprosy Programme requirement that all notified retreatment TB cases have sputum sent for culture and drug susceptibility testing

cycle1.result: Of 40 940 notified retreatment patients, 3871 (10%) had sputum received at reference/zonal laboratories; 3761 (97%) cultured, 1589 (42%) culture-positive, 1415 (89%) had DST.

result.other_findings: There was a >90% shortfall between notified retreatment cases and samples received, cultured and tested.

result.topic: Body mass index and ICU outcome
result.setting: 730 ICUs in 84 countries (Intensive Care Over Nations audit substudy)

cycle1.result: Underweight was independently associated with higher hazard of 60-day in-hospital death and overweight with lower hazard; overweight and obese patients had longer hospital stays (10 and 11 vs 9 days).

result.other_findings: No BMI category was independently associated with increased hazard of ICU-acquired infection.

result.topic: Blinded independent central review bias assessment
result.setting: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Statistical methods paper applying a hazard ratio ratio approach to a completed phase III colorectal cancer trial.

result.setting: 148 surgeons in 86 UK centres (BAUS national nephrectomy audit)

cycle1.result: 1 044 nephron-sparing procedures; median volume 4 (1-39) per consultant and 8 (1-59) per centre; 42% minimally invasive, 58% open, 4% conversions; histology malignant 80%, benign 18%.

result.other_findings: 36 surgeons and 10 centres reported only one partial nephrectomy; indication unknown in 11%.

result.topic: Adverse event surveillance in veterinary anaesthesia
result.setting: Queen's Veterinary School Hospital, University of Cambridge (university teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: Forms completed for 1114 anaesthetics (80.4% compliance) with 1001 adverse events in 572 patients; commonest were arousal/breakthrough pain (14.9%), hypoventilation (13.5%) and hypotension (10.3%).

result.other_findings: Canine anaesthetics (57.3%) were more likely to involve adverse events than feline (35.5%).

result.setting: Hospitals in 13 European countries (European COPD Audit)

cycle1.result: On admission only 49.7% had spirometry results available and 81.6% had blood gases taken; age, acidotic respiratory failure, ventilatory support and comorbidity predicted mortality.

result.other_findings: More respiratory specialists per 1000 beds was the only resource factor that reduced post-discharge mortality.

result.setting: Primary care referral pathways, Sheffield

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Mandated referral pathway changes: a one-sided referral proforma, bounce back of inappropriate referrals to physiotherapy-led teams, and the STarT tool as a decision aid in primary care.
result.other_findings: Abstract reports data on quality of care and patient flows before and after the changes but gives no figures.

result.setting: Birmingham Women's NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Resistance to co-amoxiclav and ciprofloxacin increased since 2009; ciprofloxacin resistance rose from 1% to 8%; nitrofurantoin and gentamicin resistance remained low.

result.intervention: In 2010 hospital advice changed to reduce cephalosporins in favour of penicillins, in line with national guidance.
result.other_findings: Results fed back to commissioners and used in guideline updating; authors suggest meropenem and ciprofloxacin be reserved for proven resistance.

result.setting: RANZCR-accredited radiology training departments in Australia and New Zealand

cycle1.dates: Four nights between August and December 2013, compared with 2012 and 2011
cycle1.result: 14 of 32 sites provided data; ED CTs rose 15.7% (1700-2200 h) and 16.8% (2201-0730 h) between 2011 and 2013, versus 6.9% growth in ED presentations; CT images rose 23%.

result.other_findings: Category 1 and 2 ED presentations rose 26% over the same period.

result.setting: UK National Adult Cardiac Surgery Audit registry, England and Wales

cycle1.result: 16 (0.47%) in-hospital deaths; 5-year survival 93.1% on-pump and 93.4% off-pump; adjusted HR for on-pump 1.15 (95% CI 0.89-1.49; P = 0.28).

result.other_findings: Off-pump surgery by surgeons preferring off-pump had better survival than on-pump by on-pump-preferring surgeons (HR 1.72; P = 0.004).

result.setting: 111 Belgian hospitals (administrative discharge data)

cycle1.result: Five hospitals identified as possibly better and six as possibly worse outliers for standardised CAP mortality, with 18 others having possible quality weaknesses or strengths.

result.other_findings: Old age, comorbidity and mechanical ventilation were the main individual predictors of death.

result.setting: UK specialist vulval clinics (national survey of BSSVD and BSCCP members)
result.standard: British Society for the Study of Vulval Disease 'Standards of care for women with vulval conditions' (2013)

cycle1.result: The majority of specialist vulval clinics were non-compliant with the standards.

result.other_findings: Improvements needed in patient information, guidelines, access to multidisciplinary services, MDT processes and data recording; most clinicians supported clinical nurse specialists.

result.setting: Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital and Derriford Hospital

cycle1.result: Of 22 patients meeting FTD criteria, 6 original reports gave a full and accurate description of findings and 2 gave a fully accurate interpretation.

result.other_findings: Authors propose joint clinician-radiologist review and standardised scales for dementia MRI reporting.

result.topic: Liver cancer diagnostic intervals in primary care
result.setting: UK primary care (National Audit of Cancer Diagnosis in Primary Care)

cycle1.result: Median patient interval 9 days (IQR 0-31) and primary-care interval 11 days (IQR 0-40); 21 (23.3%) had three or more GP consultations before referral.

result.other_findings: Commonest presentations were right upper quadrant pain (11%) and decompensated liver failure (9%); 12% were found via incidental abnormal liver function tests.

result.topic: Dermatological conditions in paediatric intensive care
result.setting: UK and Ireland paediatric intensive care units (PICANet national audit database)

cycle1.result: 999 admissions of 882 children with dermatological conditions (0.8% of PICU admissions); 52 deaths (5.2%).

result.other_findings: Dermatological diagnosis was the reason for admission in 28%, a manifestation of systemic disease in 35% and incidental in 37%; mortality was higher with vascular/haematological conditions.

result.topic: Patient experience on acute medical units
result.setting: 55 acute medical units in the UK (SAMBA 2015)

cycle1.result: 824 of 945 patients (87.2%) would be extremely likely or likely to recommend the acute medical unit.

result.other_findings: Patients under 50 were less likely to recommend the unit.

result.setting: UK radiology departments (national questionnaire to audit leads)
result.standard: National Patient Safety Agency and Royal College of Radiologists guidance on communication of critical, urgent and unexpected significant radiological findings

cycle1.result: 154 of 229 departments (67%) responded; 88% had a policy, 34% had an automated electronic alert system and 17% had service-wide electronic tracking of reports.

result.other_findings: Only 11 departments with an electronic acknowledgement system regularly monitored the read rate.

result.setting: 66 acute medical units in the UK (SAMBA 2014)
result.standard: Society for Acute Medicine clinical quality indicators and Royal College of Physicians standards (early warning score within 30 minutes, competent decision maker within 4 hours, timely consultant review)

cycle1.result: 84% had an early warning score within 30 minutes, 81% were seen by a competent decision maker within 4 hours and 73% saw a consultant in time; only 56% met all three standards.

result.other_findings: No relation was found between unit characteristics or staffing and performance.

result.setting: 121 randomly selected wards in 24 NHS trusts in England
result.standard: Gold-standard pressure ulcer prevalence methods used to assess Safety Thermometer, incident reporting and STEIS

cycle1.result: Wound audit found 160 (7.1%) patients with an existing pressure ulcer versus 105 (4.7%) on Safety Thermometer (sensitivity 48.2%); incident reporting sensitivity 53.4%.

result.other_findings: Only 8 of 83 (9.6%) patients with a potentially serious pressure ulcer were reported on STEIS, showing high under-reporting.

result.setting: Mortimer Market Centre, large urban HIV clinic, London
result.standard: British HIV Association 2011 guidelines on routine tuberculosis screening in HIV

cycle1.result: Of 165 new attendees in whom screening was recommended, 6.1% had a completed electronic TB screening prompt and 12.1% underwent routine TB screening.

result.other_findings: An electronic screening prompt already in place for new attendees was ineffective; reasons were unclear.

result.topic: Use of national clinical audit feedback
result.setting: Local audit leads for four national cancer audits in English NHS trusts

cycle1.result: 274 of 607 audit leads (45%) completed the questionnaire; over 90% found findings relevant, 42% had changed clinical practice and 56% had implemented service improvements.

result.other_findings: Barriers were data quality and the need for clear presentation of benchmarked local data.

result.setting: Dedicated ENT emergency department, Royal Victoria Eye and Ear Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 945 consultations from 887 patients (1990: 1167 from 779); 57% new patients; 56% GP-referred and 38% self-referred.

result.other_findings: Commonest diagnoses were otitis externa (24%) and cerumen (20%); four new head and neck cancers were seen.

result.setting: Hospitals across the North Western Deanery (region-wide trainee audit)
result.standard: National guidance on management of adults with diabetes undergoing surgery (2011)

cycle1.result: HbA1c recorded preoperatively in 71%; VRIII not used when indicated in 11%; only 8% received recommended substrate fluid; hourly intra-operative CBG in 56%; CBG in recovery in 73%.

result.other_findings: Mean fasting time was 12:20 h; 9% with abnormal HbA1c were not known to the diabetes team; WHO checklist used in 95%.

result.setting: Colposcopy department, Wexford General Hospital
result.standard: Majority of LLETZ procedures should be performed under local anaesthesia in an outpatient setting

cycle1.result: 829 (85.5%) under local anaesthesia and 141 (14.5%) under general anaesthesia; GA indications: associated pathology 33.8%, anticipated difficulty 41.2%, patient request 25%.

result.other_findings: GA rate fell from 19.4% to 10% during the study owing to fewer anticipated-difficulty cases; authors propose a categorisation audit tool.

result.setting: Referral hospital in rural Tanzania
result.standard: Audit criteria for caesarean section based on literature and national/international guidelines

cycle1.result: Of 82 CS among women with severe maternal morbidity or death, 36 (44.0%) met criteria without delay, 20 (24.4%) had correct indication but significant delay, and 16 (19.5%) did not meet criteria.

result.other_findings: CS was more often correctly indicated during office hours (60.0% vs 36.0%).

result.setting: GP minor surgeons in three settings (enhanced service GPs, GPs with a special interest, Model 2 GPs)

cycle1.result: 6138 procedures; 88.8% of samples expected to go to histology were sent; malignant diagnosis correct in 69% (ESGPs), 93% (GPwSIs) and 91% (Model 2 GPs).

result.other_findings: Incomplete excision was significantly more frequent for enhanced service GPs (17%).

result.setting: European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Quality Improvement Initiative

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Position paper describing development of ESGE key performance measures and recommending local audit and feedback.

result.setting: 12 UK cardiac surgical centres (Association of Cardiothoracic Anaesthetists national audit)

cycle1.result: 5895 (31%) had preoperative anaemia (centre range 23% to 45%); anaemia was independently associated with transfusion (OR 2.75) and mortality (OR 1.42).

result.other_findings: Regional variation in anaemia and transfusion remained after adjustment.

result.topic: Laser therapy outcomes for twin-twin transfusion syndrome
result.setting: NSW Fetal Therapy Centre, Sydney

cycle1.result: Survival of at least one baby 85.6% and dual survival 52.5%; median gestation at delivery 32.6 weeks.

result.other_findings: Outcomes were comparable with the international literature; proportion treated at stage II increased over time.

result.topic: Response to audit and feedback in cardiac rehabilitation
result.setting: Laboratory experiment and 18 cardiac rehabilitation centres in a cluster-randomised trial

cycle1.result: Each 10% decrease in performance score increased the odds of an indicator being selected for improvement (OR 1.54 laboratory; OR 1.25 field study).

result.other_findings: Participants ignored benchmarks in 34% (laboratory) and 48% (field) of selections.

result.setting: Northumbria Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust (Sentinel Stroke National Audit Programme data)

cycle1.result: Patients receiving thrombolysis were more likely to have atrial fibrillation or die at discharge and had poorer modified Rankin scores; no difference at 6 months.

result.other_findings: Patients aged 80 and over were less likely to receive thrombolysis.

result.setting: Three tertiary paediatric hospitals in New South Wales

cycle1.result: 30 cases identified; ICD-10 code D14.1 had a PPV of 98.1%; median age at onset 36 months; estimated national prevalence 0.81 per 100 000.

result.other_findings: One patient died; median treatment duration 36 months.

result.topic: Coronary heart disease risk factor recording and control
result.setting: 79 centres in 11 countries in Europe, Asia and the Middle East (SURF international audit)

cycle1.result: Smoking was recorded in over 98%, but about 20% lacked relevant laboratory measurements; 16% smoked, 29% were obese and 46% had abdominal obesity.

result.other_findings: Risk factor control was poor with substantial variation between countries.

result.topic: Insulin therapy in acute coronary syndrome
result.setting: Two UK hospitals (North Bristol NHS Trust)
result.standard: Normoglycaemia (4-8 mmol/l) for a consecutive six-hour period with a low-dose insulin regimen

cycle1.result: Normoglycaemia for six consecutive hours achieved in 72% of patients within a median of 13 hours.

result.intervention: New low-dose intravenous insulin regimen for ACS with left ventricular failure, introduced after local audit showed more hypoglycaemia in this group.
result.other_findings: The audit reported here measured practice after the new regimen; earlier local audit data are not given numerically.

result.setting: English National Lung Cancer Audit linked to LCNS workforce census
result.standard: NICE recommendation that all lung cancer patients have access to a lung cancer nurse specialist

cycle1.result: LCNS assessment recorded as yes in 62%, no in 6% and missing in 32%.

result.other_findings: Assessment was lower in older, frailer patients and in high-volume trusts (OR 0.58), and higher where band 8 nurses did most work (OR 2.22).

result.setting: Department of Paediatric Cardiothoracic Anaesthesia, Freeman Hospital, Newcastle

cycle1.result: 64 (77.1%) had good, 17 (20.5%) moderate and 2 (2.4%) poor quality analgesia.

result.other_findings: Mean paravertebral bupivacaine dose was 0.29 mg/kg/h with intravenous morphine 20 micrograms/kg/h.

result.topic: CT chest surveillance after oral cancer
result.setting: Merseyside and Cheshire Regional Surgical Head and Neck Unit, University Hospital Aintree
result.standard: Recommended follow-up interval CT for indeterminate chest nodules

cycle1.result: Of 49 patients recommended interval scans, only 20 (41%) had them; 11 had further pathological findings (5 metastatic disease, 4 primary lung tumours).

result.intervention: Changed the process for booking CT surveillance scans with periodic checks that they are done.
result.other_findings: 324 of 413 patients (78%) had staging chest CT at diagnosis; re-audit planned to include other head and neck sites.

result.setting: Cork University Hospital

cycle1.result: Of 131 PICC placements, 28.2% (37) had complications leading to removal: thrombosis 14.5% (19) and infection 13.7% (18).

result.other_findings: 6-French PICCs needed removal more often than 5-French (79.2% vs 30%); diagnosis was associated with complications (p=0.019).

result.setting: Medway Maritime Hospital, Kent

cycle1.result: Incidence of third/fourth degree tears 4.7%.

result.intervention: STOMP (Stop Traumatic OASIS Morbidity Project): a series of clinical measures adopted by all staff with workshops and a publicity campaign.

cycle2.result: Incidence of third/fourth degree tears fell to 2.2% (significant decrease).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 28 Australian general practitioners (Weigh Forward audit)

cycle1.result: 147 (57%) retained to 24 weeks; completers lost mean 6.1% body weight and 27.2% lost at least 10%.

result.other_findings: Practitioners were hesitant to intensify treatment and set high goals (mean 17.3% weight loss).

result.setting: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Development of an outdoor environment audit checklist from walk-along interviews with older fallers.

result.topic: Hairy cell leukaemia diagnosis and response assessment
result.setting: Haematology Department, University Hospital Galway
result.standard: British Committee for Standards in Haematology revised guidelines for hairy cell leukaemia

cycle1.result: Blood film in 100%; flow cytometry in 89% (16), of which only 31% (5) included all four markers; no trephine analysed DBA44; post-treatment bone marrow biopsy in 65% (11) of treated patients.

result.other_findings: All initial trephine biopsies included CD20.

result.setting: Royal Prince Alfred Hospital emergency department, Sydney
result.standard: Authors' nine-item checklist and NSW Agency for Clinical Innovation referral template (2013)

cycle1.result: Over 60% completion in 80.9% of letters against the authors' checklist and 6.3% against the ACI checklist.

result.other_findings: Handwritten letters (11.9%) were poorer; fewer than half included results, psychosocial or vaccination history.

result.setting: 199 hospitals in a multicentre quality improvement collaborative (Vermont Oxford Network)

cycle1.result: Mean 3.7 of 6 NAS-focused guidelines in place.

result.intervention: Multicentre, multistate quality improvement collaborative to standardise NAS policies and care.

cycle2.result: Mean 5.1 of 6 NAS-focused guidelines in place.

result.other_findings: Participation was associated with decreased health care utilisation (length of treatment and stay).

result.setting: Twelve healthcare teams in prisons, young offender institutions and immigration removal centres, London
result.standard: NICE standards for tuberculosis best practice

cycle1.result: No provider with a digital X-ray machine was doing active case finding in new prisoners and none routinely did latent TB testing and preventive treatment.

result.other_findings: Barriers included staff skills and skill mix, structural and technical barriers, and custodial and health service demands.

result.setting: Oral and maxillofacial surgery department, Oxford University Hospitals

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Launch of a daytime adult treatment clinic for semi-urgent OMFS referrals from cross-covering junior doctors.
result.other_findings: Authors report the clinic was an effective, safe and supervised route for review; no figures given.

result.setting: Rheumatology services in the national audit for rheumatoid and early inflammatory arthritis
result.standard: NICE quality standards for rheumatoid arthritis

cycle1.dates: First 3 months of follow-up from first presentation
cycle1.result: Delays in referral and access to specialist care, and need for improvement in treating to target, suppressing high disease activity and supporting self-care.

result.other_findings: Patient-reported outcomes improved within 3 months with high satisfaction, but response rates were low.

result.setting: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Discussion paper on the relationship between quality assessment, audit and research in nursing.

result.setting: Metropolitan comprehensive stroke centre, Melbourne
result.standard: Inclusion of known CT predictors of ICH outcome in reports (dimensions, volume, location, hydrocephalus, shape, density, CTA spot sign)

cycle1.result: At least one ICH dimension in 90%, three dimensions missing in 39%, volume reported in 6%; CTA spot sign reported in 14 of 58 (24%) CTAs.

result.other_findings: Reporting of other features exceeded 95% except density and shape; routine ABC/2 volume reporting recommended.

result.setting: General dental practices in Wales
result.standard: Scottish Dental Clinical Effectiveness Programme (SDCEP) prescribing guidelines

cycle1.result: Of patients given antibiotics only 37.2% had spreading infection or systemic involvement recorded and 31.2% received no dental treatment; 79.2% of antibiotic, 69.4% of antifungal and 57.6% of antiviral preparations met dose, frequency and duration standards.

result.other_findings: 279 dentists took part and 5782 antimicrobials were prescribed; this is the first cycle.

result.topic: Rectal cancer MRI staging report quality
result.setting: 15 centres in Australia and New Zealand (PETACC-6 trial substudy)
result.standard: Minimum rectal MRI sequences and inclusion of relevant staging findings in reports

cycle1.result: 82% performed minimum T2 sequences; 31% of reports included T stage with substage, N stage and CRM, and 17% also included EMVI.

result.other_findings: Agreement with central reporters was T stage 76%, N stage 70%, CRM 57% and EMVI 16%; template reports included the three findings in 82%.

result.setting: Specialist secure mental health service (St Andrew's Healthcare, Northampton)
result.standard: Prevention and management of violence and aggression care plan in place for all patients

cycle1.result: No care plan in place at 151 of 539 incidents (72% compliance); 40% of patients documented as contributing to their care plan.

result.other_findings: Adherence to de-escalation elements was documented in 58% of incidents; some care plans listed coercive strategies as de-escalation.

result.setting: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust and Royal Bournemouth Hospital

cycle1.result: Interobserver agreement for residual cancer burden was good (kappa 0.775; Spearman 0.9497).

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 185 hospitals in England and Wales (National Heart Failure Audit)
result.standard: Key performance measures: ACE inhibitor/ARB and beta-blocker on discharge and referral to specialist follow-up

cycle1.result: Hospital adherence to composite KPM ranged from 50% to 97% (median 79%); only 8% of variation was attributable to hospital features.

result.other_findings: Specialist follow-up referral varied more (median 81%, range 20% to 100%), with 26% attributable to hospital differences.

result.setting: Paediatric medical and surgical wards and PICU, St George's Hospital, London (teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: Baseline audit identified a high prescribing error rate.

result.intervention: Multi-professional prescribing champions, workshops and a prescribing test, feedback of weekly sampling and a star chart game.

cycle2.result: Initial improvement in prescribing errors which was not sustained.

result.other_findings: Qualitative feedback showed increased knowledge and empowerment of stakeholders.

result.setting: UK intensive care units (national surveys of nurse leads and ICS linkmen)
result.standard: Department of Health (2012) ventilator care bundle high impact intervention

cycle1.result: Over 95% worked in units using a ventilator bundle; compliance with each component exceeded 85% except subglottic secretion drainage (47-53% of units).

result.other_findings: Lack of suitable endotracheal tubes meant some patients were re-intubated to allow subglottic secretion drainage; second survey had 77 responses.

result.setting: UK hospitals (British Thoracic Society national CAP audit)

cycle1.result: 30-day inpatient mortality fell over 6 years (2014 vs 2009 adjusted OR 0.86; p for trend 0.004); chest X-ray and first antibiotic within 4 hours of admission increased by 3.7% and 11.5%.

result.other_findings: Authors expect further gains from the 2016 NICE pneumonia quality standard.

result.setting: Paediatric patients, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: New paediatric vancomycin guideline; six standards with 100% target

cycle1.result: Three of six standards met: 100% correct starting dose; 90% of levels taken at correct time; 93% of actions on out-of-range levels correct; only 33% had initial level in range.

result.other_findings: Two standards could not be assessed (no neonates or renal impairment); authors suggest four times daily dosing or continuous infusion.

result.setting: Paediatric wards excluding intensive care and day surgery, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: Locally developed standards: timely analgesia and reassessment after pain score in 80%; 4-hourly pain scores on regular analgesia in 80%; naloxone co-prescribed with strong opioids in 90%

cycle1.result: Analgesia given in the same hour for 58% (34/59) severe and 30% (28/92) mild/moderate pain scores; reassessment within 60 minutes after 52% (37/71) and 34% (31/92) of doses; 83% (15/18) on regular analgesia assessed 4-hourly; 45% on strong opioids had no naloxone.

result.other_findings: Only hourly pain score documentation was seen; revised guideline and medical and nurse training are planned.

result.setting: Paediatric wards, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: Local paediatric empiric anti-infective guidelines and drug dose table: 90% adherence to empirical guidelines; 90% indication recorded; 90% duration/review date recorded; 95% initial doses adhere to dose table

cycle1.result: 40/41 (98%) adhered to empirical guidelines; 40/42 (95%) had indication stated; 26/42 (62%) had duration/review date recorded; 67/69 (97%) initial doses adhered to dose table.

result.intervention: Proposed only: present results to stewardship and pharmacy teams, electronic prescribing with mandatory fields, update antibiotic smartphone app, compulsory junior doctor education.
result.other_findings: Previous audit in 2013 showed 72% guideline adherence, 16% indication recording and 14% duration recording, so all improved; duration documentation still failed the standard.

result.setting: Paediatric critical care unit, Royal London Hospital, Barts Health NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Handwritten continuous infusion prescriptions had a 30.7% error rate.

result.intervention: Electronic (Excel) continuous infusion prescription chart with validated automatic dose and rate calculations, introduced April 2015 after a 4-week trial.

cycle2.result: Electronic charts had a 0.7% error rate (p value not given in text); the one error was due to incorrect data input.

result.other_findings: Parameters audited were dose, infusion rate, concentration, route, legibility and patient details; formula discrepancies were found during validation and the trial period.

result.topic: Paediatric paracetamol dosing by ideal body weight
result.setting: Paediatric surgical inpatients and discharges, Cardiff and Vale UHB
result.standard: Local peri-operative paediatric pain guidelines (2012): 100% weight and height documented; dosing by ideal body weight in overweight/obese children; IV route prescribed separately from oral/rectal; IV paracetamol reviewed at 48 hours for oral switch

cycle1.result: Weight documented in 84% of inpatient and 94% of discharge prescriptions; height documented for no patient; IV/PO combined prescribing in 32 inpatients; of 52 on IV paracetamol, 20 not reviewed at 48 hours (only 3 appropriate).

result.intervention: Local guidelines amended in 2015 to dose obese children on lean body mass/ideal weight for height and reduce maximum daily dose to 75 mg/kg/day; education of prescribers recommended.
result.other_findings: 100 inpatient and 35 discharge prescriptions; overweight/obese children received doses up to 30 mg/kg (oral inpatient) and 33 mg/kg (discharge) based on ideal body weight.

result.setting: Children's warfarin clinic (pharmacist-led telephone service), Leeds Children's Hospital
result.standard: NPSA safety standards for warfarin dosing

cycle1.result: Previous ward-based paper system: 44 patients, 1289 INRs; 11 patients (25%) lost to follow-up.

result.intervention: Pharmacist-led telephone warfarin service using a computerised documentation system replaced ward-based junior doctor dosing on paper.

cycle2.result: 73 patients, 1547 INRs; fully compliant with NPSA standards; no patients lost to follow-up; no significant difference in safety indicators versus the original service.

result.other_findings: No inappropriate target INRs in either service; 38/53 (72%) parents returned the satisfaction survey and 28 (78%) rated the clinic excellent.

result.setting: Acute oncology service admissions unit, St James's Institute of Oncology, Leeds

cycle1.result: 26% of admitted patients triaged via the telephone triage system; 133 triage forms completed; 52% of triaged patients admitted.

cycle2.result: 49% of admitted patients triaged; 264 triage forms completed; 49% of triaged patients admitted.

result.other_findings: Patients (n = 40) reported high satisfaction, but 56% delayed 2 days or more before contacting the unit.

result.setting: Hospital Authority neurosurgical centres, Hong Kong (multicentre)
result.standard: International standards for shunt infection rate (value not stated)

cycle1.result: Shunt infection rate 7% (n=36); reinsertion rate 16% (n=87); 30-day mortality 6%; infection rate met international standards.

result.other_findings: Independent predictors of infection: traumatic brain injury (aOR 6.2), emergency shunting (2.3) and vancomycin as sole prophylactic antibiotic (3.4).

result.topic: Response to antenatal booking risk factors
result.setting: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, St James's University Hospital, Leeds
result.standard: Appropriate medical response to 22 risk factors recorded at midwife booking

cycle1.result: Medical staff recognised 69% of booking risk factors and responded appropriately to 82% of these.

result.other_findings: Standard of care improved over the period studied; duplicate assessment with third-assessor arbitration improved accuracy.

result.topic: Test result audit and feedback in GP training
result.setting: General practice training (supervisor workshop), Valley to Coast, New South Wales

cycle1.result: 79.6% of supervisors used test result audit and feedback after the workshop.

result.intervention: Workshop for general practice supervisors on test result audit and feedback.
result.other_findings: Participants rated the method highly for clinical reasoning, test ordering quality and patient safety.

result.setting: Regional Hepato-Pancreato-Biliary Unit, Manchester Royal Infirmary (tertiary centre)
result.standard: IAP/APA guidelines: no routine intravenous antibiotic prophylaxis in acute pancreatitis

cycle1.result: 65 (58.5%) received antibiotics; mean antibiotic use 23.9 (sd 29.7) person-days; tertiary transfers 40.9 (sd 37.1) vs index admissions 10.2 (sd 8.9) days.

result.other_findings: 31 (28%) were tertiary transfers, who received antibiotics significantly more often; over-use seen in mild acute pancreatitis.

result.setting: A general practice in England

cycle1.result: Coverage significantly lower in Traveller children (n = 214) than non-Traveller children (n = 776) for all routine vaccinations and for schedule completion at all time points.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend GPs target Traveller children for catch-up vaccination.

result.setting: Perinatal psychiatric clinic, Camden and Islington NHS Foundation Trust, London
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists and NICE recommendations (details not stated)

cycle1.result: Previous audit showed the pilot clinic failed to capture predicted numbers of women with severe and enduring mental illness.

result.intervention: A more comprehensive perinatal psychiatric service was developed.

cycle2.result: Higher rate of referrals of pregnant women with severe and enduring mental illness (numbers not stated).

result.other_findings: Most referrals continued to come from midwifery.

result.topic: Early inflammatory arthritis NICE quality standards
result.setting: Rheumatology services in England and Wales (national audit)
result.standard: Six NICE quality standards for early inflammatory arthritis (e.g. GP referral within 3 days, specialist assessment within 3 weeks, DMARD within 6 weeks)

cycle1.result: GP referral within 3 days 17%; specialist assessment within 3 weeks 38%; DMARD within 6 weeks in RA 53%; structured education within 1 month 59%; treatment target set 91%, achieved within 3 months 27%; helpline available in 96% of trusts.

result.other_findings: 97% of trusts and health boards participated; substantial geographic variability; 36% received combination DMARDs and 82% steroids in the first 3 months.

result.topic: Radial versus femoral access in coronary angiography
result.setting: 286 hospitals in Australia and New Zealand (SNAPSHOT ACS audit)

cycle1.result: Femoral access in 1043 (63%), radial in 578 (36%); radial 73.7% in New Zealand vs 26.1% in Australia.

result.other_findings: No difference in in-hospital events or 18-month mortality by access site after adjustment; high PCI volume centres more likely to use radial access.

result.setting: Department of Radiation Oncology, Mid-North Coast Cancer Institute, Coffs Harbour
result.standard: Departmental protocol criteria for target and organ-at-risk doses

cycle1.result: Stage 2 template refinement and clinical audit in 20 patients (results not stated).

result.intervention: Stepwise refinement and review of a Monaco treatment planning template.

cycle2.result: Stage 4 template met clinical criteria in 82% of patients; minor changes in 13%, major changes in 4%, one not assessable; mean calculation time 13 minutes with seven mouse clicks.

result.other_findings: Template met criteria or needed only minor changes in 95% of prostate patients.

result.setting: Albany Hospital, regional cancer centre, Western Australia
result.standard: Guidelines: antibiotics within 60 minutes of arrival for neutropenic fever

cycle1.result: Antibiotics within 60 minutes in 73.68% of cases (14/19); neutropenic fever in 16/192 patients (8.33%) and 1.47% of cycles (19/1294); no deaths.

result.other_findings: Neutropenic fever rates were similar to other centres worldwide in this general physician-led rural model.

result.setting: Antenatal clinic and obstetric medicine clinic, Whittington Hospital, London
result.standard: Scottish Obstetric Group and Audit Project recommendations

cycle1.result: Obstetric medicine clinic: 14% documented preconception counselling, 58% on anti-epileptic drugs; antenatal clinic: 0% preconception counselling, 34% on anti-epileptic drugs.

cycle2.result: Obstetric medicine clinic: 37.5% preconception counselling, 84% on anti-epileptic drugs; antenatal clinic: 4.2% preconception counselling, 31% on anti-epileptic drugs.

result.other_findings: Care in the obstetric medicine clinic was more compliant; authors recommend all women with epilepsy be reviewed there.

result.topic: Electrochemotherapy for cutaneous breast cancer metastases
result.setting: Single centre, Cork (Cork University Hospital and Mercy University Hospital)

cycle1.result: Objective response in 161/202 lesions (79.7%), complete response in 130 (64.3%); 39 (19.3%) no response, 2 (1%) progressed.

result.other_findings: Smaller lesions were more likely to respond; 17 (73.9%) patients needed two or fewer treatments.

result.topic: Head and neck cancer surgery outcome risk adjustment
result.setting: Four UK head and neck cancer surgical centres

cycle1.result: 30-day complication rates varied from 34% to 51% between centres; risk score AUC 0.70; Brier score 0.19 for sites A-C and 0.23 with site D included.

result.other_findings: 1,218 operations in 1,075 patients; case mix did not explain all outcome differences between centres.

result.topic: Implementing audit and feedback in cardiac rehabilitation
result.setting: 18 Dutch cardiac rehabilitation centres

cycle1.result: 42 statements grouped into five clusters; QI team commitment rated most important, followed by organisational readiness, an adequate audit and feedback system, access to an external quality assessor and future system functions.

result.other_findings: Concept mapping study of professionals who used a web-based audit and feedback system during a trial.

result.setting: UK radiology departments registered with the Royal College of Radiologists (national audit)
result.standard: RCR audit standard for provisional report major discrepancy rates (target value truncated in abstract)

cycle1.result: 109/188 (58%) departments supplied data on 4,931 patients; the standard for provisional report major discrepancy was achieved for registrars (remaining figures truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Benefits shown for CT interpretation or review by on-site and more senior (consultant) radiologists; out-of-hours reporting needs improvement.

result.setting: Northern Ireland teaching hospital (Royal Victoria Hospital) and Northern Ireland hospitals
result.standard: CEPOD experience range; Royal College of Pathologists recommended pathologist staffing levels

cycle1.result: Overall necropsy rate 180/600 (30%); perioperative deaths 26/74 (35%), other surgical 16/72 (22%), medical 89/386 (23%); Northern Ireland overall 11.7%, and 8.2% outside Belfast teaching hospitals.

result.other_findings: Low peripheral necropsy rates reflected pathologist numbers below Royal College of Pathologists recommendations.

result.topic: Postmortem findings in paediatric congenital heart disease
result.setting: Paediatric cardiology unit, Bristol Royal Hospital for Sick Children

cycle1.result: Unsuspected abnormalities at necropsy in 80%; 29 cases had undiagnosed cardiac anomalies or surgical flaws, contributing to death in 13.

result.other_findings: Myocardial necrosis and pulmonary foreign body embolism were common findings.

result.setting: 15 UK hospitals (national audit)

cycle1.result: Median overall survival 8.5 months; Child-Pugh A 9.5 vs B 4.6 months; ALBI-1 12.9 vs ALBI-2 5.9 months; BCLC-B 13.0 vs BCLC-C 8.3 months.

result.other_findings: Trial-treated patients (n=109) had median survival of 8.1 months, not significantly different; median time on sorafenib 3.6 months.

result.setting: UK dermatology centres (British Association of Dermatologists national audit)
result.standard: Complete excision as the required surgical standard for nonmelanoma skin cancer

cycle1.result: Lateral and deep margins clear in 98.3% and 99.2% of BCCs and 98.4% and 97.1% of SCCs; clinical diagnosis confirmed in 94.4% of suspected BCCs and 66.8% of suspected SCCs; complication rate 3.4%.

result.other_findings: 227 responses from 135 centres; 58.3% of excisions on head and neck; complications may be under-reported as most patients were not followed up in secondary care.

result.setting: Five NHS hospitals and three independent sector providers, South Yorkshire

cycle1.result: 30-day readmission rate 4.7%, with 40% judged potentially avoidable, mostly due to pain and wound problems.

result.other_findings: Unavoidable readmissions correlated with centre workload (r = 0.63) and surgical complexity (r = 0.90); patient factors not associated.

result.setting: Adult critical care, Central Manchester University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (elective major surgery)

cycle1.result: Postoperative pulmonary complication rate 16/83 (19.3%).

result.intervention: ERAS+ peri-operative care model combining enhanced recovery with measures to reduce pulmonary complications, introduced June 2014 and fully implemented September 2014.

cycle2.result: Pulmonary complication rate 16/183 (8.7%); median length of stay improved from 12 to 9 days.

result.other_findings: During full implementation the complication rate was 24/228 (10.5%).

result.setting: 18 Scottish general surgery centres (elective and emergency admissions)
result.standard: Documentation of pregnancy status in women of reproductive age admitted to hospital

cycle1.result: Pregnancy status documented in 274 (51.7%): 52 (30.8%) elective and 222 (61.5%) emergency; possibility of pregnancy established in 237 (44.7%).

result.other_findings: Among emergency admissions with abdominal pain, 211 (65.1%) had documented pregnancy status; authors recommend electronic storage of results and including status in the pre-theatre brief and checklist.

result.setting: Nuclear medicine CT, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Proposed National Diagnostic Reference Levels for nuclear medicine CT

cycle1.result: For most examinations mean dose-length products did not exceed proposed national reference levels; bone SPECT/CT lumbar spine DLPs ranged from 51 ± 5 mGy cm (low dose) to 1086 ± 124 mGy cm (metal dose).

result.other_findings: The audit process was labour intensive because of limited CRIS data, reliance on paper records and small numbers after subdivision.

result.setting: UK hospitals (British Thoracic Society national community-acquired pneumonia audit)

cycle1.result: 1251 adults miscoded as pneumonia versus 6660 with CAP; miscoded patients were older (median 80 vs 78 years) with lower 30-day inpatient mortality (14.3% vs 17.0%, adjusted OR 0.75).

result.other_findings: Miscoded patients had more comorbidity, fewer respiratory symptoms and more constitutional symptoms such as falls.

result.setting: UK radiotherapy centres (national mail-based dosimetry audit)
result.standard: Planned and delivered dose agreement within ±3.0%

cycle1.result: Mean measured versus calculated dose difference 0.4±1.4% (alanine) and 1.4±3.4% (film) excluding pencil-beam; 25/27 SABR plans within ±3.0%.

result.other_findings: Pencil-beam algorithm differences were -6.1% and -12.9%; geometric accuracy was better for VMAT and Cyberknife than conformal techniques.

result.setting: ENT outpatient clinic, Tallaght Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Abstract states only the aim: to measure the percentage of GP-referred sore throat patients meeting HIQA criteria for tonsillectomy.

result.setting: Tertiary university hospital, University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Five or more episodes of severe pain in the first 72 hours in 133 patients; 82% (109/133) of these had persistent pain at 6 months; overall post-thoracotomy pain incidence 56% (mild 32%, moderate 18%, severe 6%).

result.other_findings: 306 of 364 survivors contacted; satisfaction with acute pain management excellent 36%, good 43%, fair or poor 21%.

result.topic: Rapid PCR for staphylococcal blood cultures
result.setting: Obstetric patients, Rotunda Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Pre-intervention median IV antimicrobial duration 55.5 h and median length of admission 66.5 h.

result.intervention: Introduction of the Xpert MRSA/SA blood culture PCR assay for positive blood cultures with Gram-positive cocci in clusters.

cycle2.result: Median IV antimicrobial duration 43.5 h (p = 0.46) and median length of admission 56 h (p = 0.15); all 22 positive cultures correctly identified.

result.other_findings: Reductions were not statistically significant; larger multicentre studies recommended.

result.setting: Five paediatric diabetes centres in Australia (Australasian Diabetes Data Network registry)
result.standard: National HbA1c target of less than 58 mmol/mol

cycle1.result: Mean HbA1c 67 mmol/mol (SD 15); only 27% achieved the target of less than 58 mmol/mol.

result.other_findings: 33% overweight or obese; 44% on CSII, 38% MDI, 18% twice-daily injections; mean HbA1c lower in under-6s (63) than adolescents (69 mmol/mol).

result.setting: Nine intensive care units, Wessex regional network
result.standard: UK best practice guidelines: transfusion threshold of 70 g/l in stable, non-bleeding critically ill patients

cycle1.result: Median pre-transfusion haemoglobin 73 (68-77) g/l; only 34% of transfusion episodes used the recommended threshold.

result.other_findings: 444 transfusions, 148 excluded; in patients without cardiac disease (n = 42) only 36% used the threshold; authors suggest electronic prompts or single-unit prescriptions.

result.setting: ENT Department, Medway Maritime Hospital
result.standard: Recording of essential operative details for tympanomastoid procedures

cycle1.result: Traditional handwritten recording: 50% of essential operative items recorded.

result.intervention: Standardised proforma with a diagrammatic template, first on paper and then as an all-electronic version.

cycle2.result: Electronic template with diagram: 81% of essential items recorded (p = 0.0004 vs handwritten).

result.other_findings: Third audit cycle of 95 cases in total; the intermediate non-electronic diagrammatic template recorded 78% (p = 0.3 vs electronic).

result.setting: Nominated specialist eye clinics in the UK (multicentre)

cycle1.result: 13% had received radioiodine; all with active disease received prophylactic steroids; 63% of current smokers offered smoking cessation advice; 54% unaware of their thyroid status.

result.other_findings: 60% were current or ex-smokers; 65% had active disease and 4% sight-threatening disease; mean 9.37 months from first doctor visit to diagnosis.

result.setting: Six sites across England (trainee research collaboratives)

cycle1.result: Feasibility pilot: questionnaires took an average of 5 minutes, data quality high with little missing data, site-lead satisfaction mean 4.83 out of 5.

result.other_findings: Pilot of a secure encrypted web-based data capture tool for a national trainee-led audit.

result.topic: Chronic kidney disease coding in primary care
result.setting: 915 GP practices in the UK National Chronic Kidney Disease Audit

cycle1.result: Practice prevalence of coded CKD stages 3-5 ranged from 0.04 to 7.8%; coding where CKD was indicated by testing ranged from 0 to 97%.

result.other_findings: Methodological paper showing overdispersion must be accounted for when identifying outlying practices.

result.setting: 8 Veterans Health Administration sites, New England (VISN 1)
result.standard: Time in therapeutic range; guideline-concordant INR target ranges and prompt follow-up after out-of-range INR

cycle1.result: Time in therapeutic range 66.4% (control sites 65.9%).

result.intervention: Process-of-care measurement system with targeted audit and feedback to sites.

cycle2.result: Time in therapeutic range 69.2% (control sites 66.4%); difference-in-differences 2.3%.

result.other_findings: Compared with 116 VA sites outside VISN 1; sample given as more than 5000 patients.

result.topic: Head and neck cancer surgery outcome risk adjustment
result.setting: Four UK cancer networks

cycle1.result: 30-day complication rates varied from 34% to 51% (rest truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: 1218 operations; logistic regression, decision tree, neural network and Naive Bayes models used for case-mix adjustment.

result.setting: New Zealand hospitals admitting acute coronary syndrome (national audits)
result.standard: Evidence-based guideline recommendations for STEMI management

cycle1.result: Primary PCI reperfusion in 3% of STEMI patients.

cycle2.result: Primary PCI reperfusion in 41% of STEMI patients (rest truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Intermediate 2007 audit showed 15% primary PCI; considerable room remains to improve timely reperfusion.

result.setting: UK urology units (BAUS National Nephrectomy Audit)

cycle1.result: Thirty-day mortality 110/21380 (0.5%): radical 0.6%, partial 0.1%, simple 0.4%, nephro-ureterectomy 0.9%.

result.other_findings: Novel risk factors were blood loss of 1-2 L and conversion from minimally invasive surgery (OR 2.53).

result.setting: UK nuclear medicine departments (national audit)
result.standard: British Nuclear Medicine Society practice guidelines

cycle1.result: Most centres had at least one noncompliance with BNMS guidelines, especially lack of injection-site imaging; coefficient of quartile deviation 0.03-0.13 for Tc uptake and 0.17-0.25 for I uptake.

result.other_findings: Median 50 scans per year per centre; Tc-based results reasonably consistent between sites.

result.setting: UK neonatal transport services (16 teams)

cycle1.result: Surgical diagnosis in 22% of cases; 7% had a condition where delay may have caused bowel loss.

result.other_findings: Teams treating these transfers as time-critical responded significantly faster; two infants with normal X-rays had surgical problems.

result.setting: Surgical ward inpatient pain service, University Hospitals of Leicester (tertiary centre)

cycle1.result: 36 patients diagnosed with abdominal myofascial pain syndrome; two-thirds of these discharged within 36 hours of trigger point injection.

result.intervention: Pathway of ultrasound-guided trigger point steroid injection within 48 hours of referral, with follow-up targeted somatic treatment.
result.other_findings: Four patients refused injection and three with active visceral disease had only a transient response; authors report reduced opioid use, length of stay and readmissions (figures not given).

result.topic: Psychiatric side effects of antiepileptic drugs
result.setting: Epilepsy Unit, West Glasgow Ambulatory Care Hospital

cycle1.result: Neuropsychiatric adverse effects led to withdrawal in 1.9-16.7% of patients; prior psychiatric history 22/209 (10.5%) vs 50/849 (5.9%) withdrew for psychiatric reasons (p=0.017).

result.other_findings: Sodium channel blockers had fewer intolerable psychiatric effects (1.9% vs 8.0%); depression was the commonest cause of discontinuation (2.8%).

result.setting: Mercy University Hospital, Cork (adult inpatients)
result.standard: Local antimicrobial guidelines for empiric CAP treatment based on CURB-65

cycle1.result: Guideline-concordant empiric antibiotics in 48% of cases; 100% concordance when CURB-65 was documented.

result.other_findings: Excessively broad-spectrum and inappropriate antibiotic use was a notable problem.

result.topic: Rapid PCR for staphylococcal blood cultures
result.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit, Rotunda Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Pre-intervention group of 42 neonates with staphylococcal positive blood cultures (outcome figures not stated).

result.intervention: Introduction of the Xpert MRSA/SA blood culture PCR test.

cycle2.result: Non-significant trend to shorter antimicrobial duration in term infants and shorter admission (p = 0.2); all 9 infants with significant bacteraemia changed to the optimal antimicrobial when the result was available.

result.other_findings: Pre-intervention group had higher birth weight and platelet count.

result.topic: Type 2 diabetes glycaemic control in primary care
result.setting: 4050 general practices (UK National Diabetes Audit)
result.standard: Total glycaemic control HbA1c ≤7.5% (58 mmol/mol); higher glycaemic risk HbA1c >10% (86 mmol/mol)

cycle1.result: 67.2% achieved total glycaemic control; 6.2% at higher glycaemic risk.

result.other_findings: Medication spending rose 8% annually without better outcomes; practices with better outcomes provided more effective services and spent less on prescribing.

result.topic: Antenatal care access for women with social complexity
result.setting: Three inner-city NHS maternity services, London
result.standard: NICE guidelines, local trust policy and national statistics (booking by 12 weeks; recommended number of antenatal appointments)

cycle1.result: Over 70% of non-English speaking women not booked by 12 weeks; on average 89% of primiparous women had fewer than the recommended antenatal appointments; no sample met the appointment criteria.

result.other_findings: Perinatal data management system data were largely incomplete and appeared unreliable.

result.setting: UK endoscopy units (2011 UK national colonoscopy audit)

cycle1.result: Composite indicator (caecal intubation with midazolam ≤2 mg and comfort score 1-3/5) achieved in 54.1% of procedures.

result.other_findings: Achieving the composite indicator was associated with higher polyp detection; unit accreditation and higher volume were associated with higher rates.

result.topic: Indigenous child health checks in primary care
result.setting: 59 Australian primary health-care centres serving Indigenous people
result.standard: Audit and Best Practice for Chronic Disease programme care items for children under 2 years

cycle1.result: Recall recorded in 84%; hearing assessment in 52%.

result.intervention: Participation in annual continuous quality improvement audit cycles.

cycle2.result: Recall recorded in 95% (OR 2.44); hearing assessment in 89% (OR 1.37).

result.other_findings: Improvement in anticipatory guidance, treatment and follow-up was almost universal; participating centres may be more committed to quality improvement.

result.topic: Routine data for inflammatory bowel disease audit
result.setting: NHS hospitals in England, Wales and Northern Ireland (UK IBD audit)

cycle1.result: Very high matching between audit and routine data for basic items (mortality, major surgery, dates, diagnoses); lower matching for admission source, reason, comorbidities and endoscopy.

result.other_findings: Routine data were much cheaper but did not cover most detailed audit items.

result.setting: Endoscopy training unit, Cheltenham General Hospital

cycle1.result: 19 (14%) repeat colonoscopies within 12 months had new findings, including one cancer; missed polyp rate 9%.

result.other_findings: 5747 colonoscopies performed; new findings more likely after non-consultant non-training grade endoscopists (23% vs 11%, p=0.09).

result.setting: UK acute NHS providers (Royal College of Radiologists national audit)
result.standard: Current UK guidelines for prevention, recognition and management of contrast-induced AKI

cycle1.result: Compliance with guidelines was poor with wide variation; clinically significant post-contrast AKI 0/3590 outpatients and 14/3569 (0.4%) inpatients; overall AKI incidence 0.9%.

result.other_findings: 89/172 (52%) providers responded; no change in median creatinine after contrast in high-risk patients.

result.topic: Rectal cancer MRI staging report quality
result.setting: 14 hospitals in the London Cancer Alliance
result.standard: London Cancer Alliance MRI reporting guidelines (standardised proforma)

cycle1.result: Key MRI metric completion 98% in proforma vs 73% in prose reports.

result.intervention: Incorporation of standardised proforma-based reporting into LCA guidelines.

cycle2.result: Uptake of proforma-based reporting improved and proforma reports captured more items than prose (figures truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Reporting of advanced cancers for beyond-TME surgery fell short of acceptable standards.

result.topic: Steroid excess in inflammatory bowel disease
result.setting: British IBD outpatient clinics (multicentre)

cycle1.result: 30% received steroids; 14.9% had steroid dependency or excess, avoidable in 49.1%; annual incidence of inappropriate steroid excess 7.1%.

result.other_findings: IBD multidisciplinary teams (CD) and dedicated IBD clinics (UC) were associated with less inappropriate steroid excess.

result.setting: UK dermatologists and GPs (national audit)
result.standard: British HIV Association guidelines on HIV testing in dermatology indicator diseases

cycle1.result: HIV testing in key indicator diseases remained below the national standard (figures not stated).

result.other_findings: GPs with a special interest in dermatology tested less and were less confident; many respondents wanted further training.

result.setting: All 19 maternity units in Ireland (national survey)

cycle1.result: All units recorded smoking at booking and gave verbal advice; 1 validated with CO breath test; 12 (63%) recorded cessation timing and gave written advice; 6 (32%) had all midwives trained; 5 (26%) revisited smoking status later.

result.other_findings: Smoking cessation services were judged inadequate with variation between hospitals.

result.topic: PRN medication prescribing and record keeping
result.setting: Two adolescent wards, St Andrew's Healthcare Hospital
result.standard: Local trust medicine policy standards for PRN prescribing, based on good clinical practice

cycle1.result: 36% of PRN medications were not cancelled despite not being used for >1 month; 23% did not have clear indications for use. Most other standards showed full compliance.

result.other_findings: Recommendations included screening tools (START/STOP) to alert the responsible clinician after a month, making indication an obligatory field, staff awareness and seasonal re-audits.

result.setting: Adolescent service, St Andrew's Hospital
result.standard: Hospital policy requiring completion of Glasgow Antipsychotic Side-Effect Scale (GASS) forms

cycle1.result: Only 31% of patients had completed GASS forms.

result.intervention: Remaining patients were supported to complete the forms.

cycle2.result: 92% of patients compliant with the policy.

result.other_findings: Suitability of the form for adolescents was questioned because of sensitive side-effect items; recommended completion on admission and at regular intervals.

result.setting: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust (emergency medicine, acute medicine and diabetes departments)
result.standard: Five specific targets: fluid prescription, fixed rate intravenous insulin infusion, glucose measurement, ketone measurement and specialist referral

cycle1.result: Baseline audit; mean average duration of DKA 22.0 hours.

result.intervention: Quality improvement using PDSA cycles, with interventions including monthly feedback of specific clinical criteria to emergency medicine, acute medicine and diabetes departments.

cycle2.result: Mean average duration of DKA reduced to 10.2 hours.

result.other_findings: Regular audit cycles were reported to give sustained improvement.

result.topic: Renal replacement therapy intensity in critical care
result.setting: Critical care units across the Scottish NHS (national audit)
result.standard: Intensity of renal replacement therapy compared with evidence from large randomised trials showing no benefit of high intensity

cycle1.result: Mean delivered effluent flow for CVVH 29.1 (SD 8.1) ml/kg/h (89% of prescribed); CVVHDF mean delivered dose 41.3 (7.9) ml/kg/h (88.4% of prescribed). Of 8 intermittent haemodialysis patients, 7 had daily treatments.

result.other_findings: Prescription and delivery were routinely at a higher intensity than necessary; avoiding excessive dose could save costs.

result.topic: Plasma and platelet transfusion before interventional procedures
result.setting: Single adult intensive care unit, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford
result.standard: Transfusion thresholds: prothrombin time 22 s for fresh frozen plasma; platelet count 50 × 10^9/l

cycle1.result: 8 (12.3%) patients received fresh frozen plasma before drain insertion despite prothrombin time below 22 s; one patient above the threshold received FFP; one received a double-dose platelet transfusion despite platelets above 50 × 10^9/l.

result.other_findings: 68 drain insertions in 54 patients. A national survey of interventional radiologists showed wide variation in safe thresholds and FFP use.

result.setting: Adult ICUs in England (national telephone audit)
result.standard: Intensive Care Society 1998 bereavement care recommendations (nine recommendations)

cycle1.result: 113 responses (78% of Trusts, 63% of ICUs). 96% had an information booklet; training (53%), auditing (19%) and adequate facilities (27%) did not meet the recommended standards.

result.other_findings: 144 Trusts (179 ICUs) were eligible; bereavement care was judged underdeveloped.

result.setting: 16 intensive care units in two regions of the UK (multicentre 24-hour audit)
result.standard: Low tidal volume ventilation ≤6.5 ml/kg predicted body weight; recommended PEEP levels

cycle1.result: Mean tidal volume 7.2 (±1.4) ml/kg PBW; compliance with low tidal volume ventilation 34%. Compliance with recommended PEEP 72%.

result.other_findings: Mean tidal volume 7.0 ml/kg with volume control vs 7.9 ml/kg with pressure control (P < 0.0001); significant regional and unit variation.

result.setting: 31 radiotherapy centres audited by IAEA QUATRO in the IAEA Europe Region
result.standard: IAEA QUATRO comprehensive quality audit methodology

cycle1.result: 759 recommendations and 600 commendations were given across 31 audit reports; 8 centres of competence had complete quality management systems and adequate staffing.

result.topic: Gleason score review of prostate biopsies

cycle1.result: 24 of 96 biopsies (25%) from 19 patients changed Gleason grade, with change in risk for 13 (68%); management plans could be affected for 9 (47%) and treatment options for 5 (26%).

result.setting: Bristol Royal Hospital for Children and Princess Margaret Hospital for Children, Perth

cycle1.result: Pain peaked on the day of or after surgery; median duration 5 days after open appendicectomy and 0-2 days for other procedures.

result.setting: Mona Vale Hospital, peripheral metropolitan hospital (ED and paediatric ward), Sydney
result.standard: Target to reduce paediatric respiratory viral swabs by 25% over 4 months

cycle2.result: 151 swabs (55% reduction); ED 82 (66% reduction); ED-discharged under 2s with a swab 3%.

result.other_findings: No increase in ward swabs; projected savings over $21 000 at 12 months.

result.setting: NHS Lothian sexual and reproductive health services with community pharmacies

cycle1.result: 56% of 549 vouchers were redeemed at a pharmacy within one week of issue.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Long-term mortality after acute coronary syndrome
result.setting: National New Zealand ACS audit cohort (2002)

cycle1.result: Only 23 of 42 (54.8%) coded deaths were confirmed AMI; excluding 22 incorrectly coded patients, 30-day mortality would fall from 9.87 to 4.14 per 100 cases.

result.topic: Blood transfusion consent and patient information

result.setting: National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation data

cycle1.result: Uptake of cardiac rehabilitation among patients with diabetes dropped by between 7% and 15% depending on age group.

result.setting: Intensive care unit, Palestinian Medical Complex, Ramallah

cycle1.result: Pre-ASP antimicrobial use 87.3 defined daily doses/100 beds.

cycle2.result: Antimicrobial use fell by 24.3% to 66.1 defined daily doses/100 beds; 176 interventions with 78.4% acceptance.

result.other_findings: Most accepted interventions were dose optimisation (87.0%) and culture-based de-escalation (84.4%); improvements in duration of therapy and length of stay.

result.setting: 24/7 Critical Care Outreach team, 600-bed district general hospital (Royal Berkshire NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: 8216 medication items prescribed by nine nurse prescribers, average 2.6 per shift; most commonly intravenous fluids and analgesia, mostly at night and weekends.

result.topic: Discharge to care home after stroke

cycle1.result: 203 (7.9%) were discharged to a care home for the first time; 401 (15.5%) died in hospital.

result.standard: Holistic nursing documentation, including WHO palliative care definition of assessment and management of symptoms

cycle2.result: Higher compliance with nursing assessments and more concise, comprehensive documentation of holistic care and patients' perspectives.

result.other_findings: Continuous education and organisational support were needed to sustain results and avoid a tick-box exercise.

result.topic: Intermittent hormone therapy in prostate cancer
result.setting: Whipps Cross University Hospital and Barts Institute of Cancer, London

cycle1.result: Overall survival 87%, 72% and 67% with intermittent anti-androgen and 73%, 56% and 43% with intermittent LHRH/MAB at 5, 8 and 10 years.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Mortality after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with acute coronary syndrome
result.setting: 239 UK hospitals (MINAP database)

cycle1.result: Overall hospital mortality 28.7%; ranged from 10.7% to 66.3% across 94 hospitals (median 28.6%).

result.setting: Single surgical team, St Thomas' Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Posterior capsule rupture 2.2% (ERM 1.7% vs MH 2.5%; P = 0.40); iatrogenic retinal tears 15.6% in MH vs 6.8% in ERM.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 131 NASBO participating units (consultant survey)

cycle1.result: 384 responses (29.2%). 88% would consider water-soluble contrast; 52.1% considered laparoscopy; oral supplements favoured in 67.4% for operated vs 48.4% for conservatively managed patients.

result.other_findings: Consensus on imaging and indications for early surgery, but variation in nutritional support.

result.setting: Sydney Adventist Hospital

cycle1.result: Overall clinical success in 102/115 (89%); heavy menstrual bleeding control 91/104 (88%); dysmenorrhoea relief 94/104 (90%).

result.setting: Mental health nursing settings in Ireland (questionnaire survey)

cycle1.result: Some areas reported no specific rapid tranquillisation policy; variation in post-intervention mental and physical health monitoring.

result.other_findings: Specific training and policy development were recommended.

result.setting: Hospitales Universitarios Puerta del Mar y Puerto Real, Cadiz
result.standard: Compared with EUREQUO (2013) and RCOphth NOD (2015) outcomes (postoperative VA ≤0.3 logMAR in 98% and 89%)

cycle1.result: Complication rate 6.7% (posterior capsule rupture 3.8%); 78.8% achieved postoperative VA ≤0.3 logMAR and 27.6% ≤0.0 logMAR.

result.topic: Acute myocardial infarction quality improvement toolkit
result.setting: 63 hospitals in Kerala (cluster randomised stepped-wedge trial)

cycle1.result: 30-day MACE 5.3% intervention vs 6.4% control; adjusted odds ratio 0.98 (95% CI 0.80-1.21), not significant.

result.setting: Orthopaedic surgery (joint replacement, hip fracture repair, ORIF), Beaumont Hospital, Dublin

result.topic: Did not wait rates and scheduled return clinics

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Advanced nurse practitioner-led scheduled return clinics.
result.other_findings: Abstract describes an audit of effectiveness but gives no figures.

cycle2.result: 83.4% of women wore wristbands; 495/535 (93%) correctly applied; forms recorded acuity colour 92%, working diagnosis 85%, plan 82%; median wait 29 (IQR 11-60) minutes.

result.topic: Potentially inappropriate medications in older people
result.setting: 4 rural community-based outpatient primary care clinics, Georgia Veterans Affairs

result.topic: Community-acquired pneumonia severity assessment and management

result.standard: NICE and American Thoracic Society guidelines for community-acquired pneumonia

cycle1.result: CURB-65 determined for 12 (12%); urea not documented in 48 (48%); respiratory rate not documented in 73 (73%); microbiology in 2 (2%); 81 (81%) received β-lactam plus macrolide.

result.standard: NICE CG32 standards 1.3.1 (indications for nutrition support) and 1.5.6 (monitoring); target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: Compliance with standard 1.3.1 was 46% and with standard 1.5.6 82%.

result.other_findings: 86% (n = 13) of patients reported satisfaction (target 90%); nationally 89% of dietitians used weight and 87% BMI as outcomes.

result.setting: Eastman Dental Hospital restorative dentistry referrals
result.standard: British Society of Periodontology referral criteria: all patients should have initial periodontal therapy before referral

cycle1.result: All 100 referrals incomplete; 12 had BPE scores matching those at consultation; 85 patients reported oral hygiene instruction and 91 root surface debridement before referral.

result.other_findings: Most referrers gave no diagnosis and used incorrect terminology; 25 dentists reported more initial therapy than patients did.

result.topic: Transfusion practice in sickle cell disease
result.setting: 84 hospitals in the UK and Republic of Ireland
result.standard: Standards and guidelines for transfusion services in sickle cell disease

cycle1.result: 4528 transfusion episodes, 84% elective; stroke prevention 42% of transfusions; 60% (732/1227) needed Rh CE negative blood; adults 50% automated red cell exchange, children 87% simple transfusion.

result.other_findings: Paucity of clinical management protocols, trained staff and network arrangements.

result.topic: Representativeness of cancer patient experience survey in lung cancer
result.setting: National Lung Cancer Audit population linked with the English Cancer Patient Experience Survey

cycle1.result: 15,967 (7%) were included in CPES; 96% of respondents received anti-cancer treatment vs 56% nationally (adjusted OR 10.3, 95% CI 9.4-11.2).

result.other_findings: CPES under-represented older, more deprived patients and those with worse performance status, comorbidity or emergency diagnosis.

result.setting: General internal medicine services at 3 academic hospitals (McMaster University, Hamilton, Ontario)
result.standard: Discharge medication reconciliation quality audit tool (Canadian Patient Safety Institute and ISMP Canada), modified

cycle1.result: Documentation of any discharge medication reconciliation for only 1 patient (3%); none carried out by pharmacists.

result.other_findings: Post-discharge interviews showed major communication gaps with community pharmacists and family physicians.

result.setting: 11 English sites across clinical settings

cycle1.result: Outcome measures (IPOS-Dem, Phase of Illness, AKPS, FAST) completed at first assessment for 225 people with dementia across nine sites.

result.other_findings: Recording non-physical symptoms by proxy was challenging.

result.setting: Tertiary urology department (Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: 334 of 2773 scheduled operations (12%) cancelled at the last minute.

result.intervention: Targeted interventions including a reminder telephone call covering admission instructions

cycle2.result: Modest reduction (0.2%) in the last-minute cancellation rate.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 85 UK radiology departments with an emergency department (major trauma centres, trauma units and others)
result.standard: National guidelines for imaging and reporting in major trauma

cycle1.result: 240 (11%) scans had a primary survey report documented, 53 (22%) of which were unavailable after 20 minutes; final consultant report within 1 hour for 1,033 (48%) and within 2 hours for a further 540 (25%).

result.other_findings: 63% of scans were out of hours; 40% of departments rely on registrars out of hours with consultant report next day.

result.setting: Ten hospitals in seven European nations (PaBloE working group)

cycle1.result: Almost all hospitals had preoperative anaemia pathways, but only two nations had national guidelines; anaesthetists organised management in six of ten hospitals; iron deficiency mostly treated with intravenous iron.

result.other_findings: Survey of organisation rather than audit of patient care.

result.setting: Seven hospitals in the East of England; elective day case general and vascular surgery
result.standard: National guidelines: all people with diabetes should have HbA1c within 6 months before surgery, below 69 mmol/mol if safe

cycle1.result: 86.7% (157/181) had HbA1c tested within 6 months; 8.9% (14/157) had HbA1c ≥ 69 mmol/mol and 85.7% (12/14) of these proceeded to surgery without optimisation.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: TURBT quality and bladder cancer guideline adherence
result.setting: Urology Department, The Pennine Acute Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Guidelines on management of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (single instillation chemotherapy, re-TUR timing)
