cycle1.result: Acute bed occupancy was high, frequently over 100%, and rose across the three years.

result.other_findings: Rising occupancy was associated with fewer acute and continuing care beds, more referrals and new long-stay patients.

result.setting: 15 hospitals (university, large and small district general hospitals) in England and Wales

cycle1.result: 32% of patients had moderate to severe pain at rest; 37% severe pain on movement; 41% moderate to severe pain on deep inspiration.

result.intervention: Staff and patient education, formal pain assessment and recording, and a standardised algorithm for intermittent intramuscular opioid prescription.

cycle2.result: Moderate to severe pain at rest fell to 12%; severe pain on movement to 13%; moderate to severe pain on deep inspiration to 22%.

result.other_findings: Nausea and vomiting fell similarly and postoperative complications fell slightly. Sample size 2738 is the total across both surveys.

result.setting: National Blood Service Transfusion Centre, North London, Colindale
result.standard: Published guidelines for blood products for neonatal exchange transfusion

cycle1.result: Only 42% of blood issued for exchange transfusion was used for that purpose; guidelines on blood specification were not adhered to.

result.other_findings: Substantial over-ordering by neonatologists meant expensive high-specification units were given to other patients.

result.topic: Antenatal ultrasound detection of renal anomalies
result.setting: North Tees NHS Trust, Stockton on Tees

cycle1.result: Renal tract anomaly suspected antenatally in 125 fetuses (5 per 1000 births); 107 live births.

result.other_findings: Of 78 fetuses with isolated pelvic distension, outcome was normal in 59% with unilateral and 48% with bilateral changes; no live birth in 14 pregnancies with oligohydramnios and no visible bladder.

result.setting: 20 primary health care teams in the Cambridge health district
result.standard: Palliative care standards developed with primary health care teams (Cambridge palliative audit schedule, CAMPAS)

cycle1.result: 876 contacts with 29 patients recorded; considerable inter- and intra-team variation in achievement of the standards.

result.other_findings: Main aim was developing the audit tool; future audit was planned to test whether care improved.

result.setting: Seven hospitals in south-east England; postal survey

cycle1.result: The 27-item Prostate Outcomes Questionnaire had a 95% response rate, Cronbach's alpha 0.82-0.93 and mean test-retest correlation 0.85.

result.other_findings: Development and validation of an audit instrument for outcomes after TURP for benign prostatic hyperplasia.

result.topic: Histopathological diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease
result.setting: Department of Histopathology, Royal Hallamshire Hospital, Sheffield

cycle1.result: Sensitivity of reports suggestive of Crohn's disease 50% and ulcerative colitis 62% (74% for both with active inflammation); PPV of highly suggestive diagnoses 100%; specificity of a normal diagnosis 96%.

result.other_findings: Results were proposed as achievable standards for non-specialist histopathology services.

result.setting: University Department of Paediatric Surgery, Royal Hospital for Sick Children, Yorkhill, Glasgow

cycle1.result: Operating shifted from many supervised cases to more major procedures, with more neonates and greater autonomy towards the end of training.

result.other_findings: Personal logbook audit of one higher surgical trainee; little operating in the research year.

result.topic: Axillary lymph node yield in breast cancer
result.setting: Leicestershire Breast Unit, Glenfield General Hospital, Leicester

cycle1.result: Median 8 nodes retrieved (range 0-30); fewer than 4 nodes in only 11 patients.

result.other_findings: Larger node yields were associated with more node-positive patients and more metastatic nodes identified.

result.topic: Barium enema detection of colorectal cancer
result.setting: Department of Radiology, Princess of Wales Hospital, Bridgend

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Retrospective comparison of pathology and radiology reports; the abstract gives no results.

result.setting: NHS hospitals in Scotland (Scottish Morbidity Record data)
result.standard: Scottish Office Clinical Outcome Indicator for emergency readmission within 28 days of appendicectomy

cycle1.result: 403 (4.6%) emergency readmissions within 28 days.

result.other_findings: Readmission was higher after removal of a normal appendix, interval, prophylactic and incidental appendicectomy, in higher-volume hospitals and in patients from more deprived areas.

result.topic: Nurse-led ward quality of care audit
result.setting: Residential sector of St George's Hospital, Morpeth, Northumberland (psychiatric wards)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes psychiatric nurses and a quality coordinator devising a ward audit of quality of care involving front-line staff.

result.setting: Scottish general practices using GPASS; University of Aberdeen

cycle1.result: Morbidity and prescribing data collected biannually from up to 2.4 million patients; continuous contact data from 52 practices (282,700 patients).

result.other_findings: Description of a national data resource rather than an audit against standards.

result.setting: Wessex Radiotherapy Centre, Royal South Hants Hospital, Southampton

cycle1.result: Anteroposterior bladder movement was <1 cm in 12 of 20 patients; target volume encompassed as planned in 16 patients; bladder dome rose out of the field in 2.

result.other_findings: Little left to right variation in bladder position was seen on serial CT.

result.setting: Department of Paediatric Neurology, Southampton General Hospital
result.standard: Agreed basic standards for correspondence quality, prescribing, drug monitoring, neuroimaging use and EEG requests

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Findings of the first audit were presented to staff.

cycle2.result: Prescribing practice and appropriateness of drug monitoring improved; quality of patient correspondence and EEG requests were unchanged.

result.other_findings: In both audits many parents were dissatisfied with the quality and amount of information about epilepsy.

result.setting: Single centre, Middlesex Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Metoclopramide and dexamethasone policy: 9 of 21 patients (43%) switched for nausea or vomiting; emesis in 15 of 66 (23%) CMF cycles.

result.intervention: Policy changed so that granisetron and dexamethasone were used for all patients.

cycle2.result: Granisetron and dexamethasone: 8 of 43 patients (19%) had emesis; emesis in 16 of 206 (8%) CMF cycles.

result.other_findings: The abstract states the second stage involved 28 patients but reports 8 of 43; a lower granisetron dose (1 mg) was suggested to reduce cost.

result.setting: University of Ulster, County Londonderry; hospital wards

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Development of an audit tool; preliminary findings showed wide variation in how far wards claiming primary nursing actually practised it.

result.setting: Adult general Intensive Care Unit, Queen's Medical Centre, Nottingham

cycle1.result: 72.6% of patients who died had treatment withdrawn; three organ failures were most often present at withdrawal.

result.other_findings: Involvement in withdrawal decisions varied between consultants.

result.setting: Unit of Paediatric Dentistry, University Dental Hospital of Manchester
result.standard: Agreed good-practice criteria for radiographic usage (pre-planned checklist)

cycle1.result: Clinical note-keeping to accompany radiographic examinations was the least satisfactory area of practice.

result.intervention: Areas for improvement identified in the initial audit were addressed before re-audit.
result.other_findings: Criterion-based audit run through six 1-hour audit group meetings of unit staff and postgraduate students.

result.setting: Theatres, University College London Hospitals (UCLH)
result.standard: LMA cuff pressure within the manufacturers' recommended limit of <60 cmH2O, measured by manometer

cycle1.result: Only 4 (5%) cuff pressures were within the recommended <60 cmH2O; 57 (63%) exceeded the manometer scale (>120 cmH2O); 25 (27%) reported sore throat.

result.intervention: Results presented to anaesthetists and anaesthetic assistants; manometers bought for every theatre; education and in-theatre demonstration for anaesthetic assistants on measuring and adjusting cuff pressure.

cycle2.result: LMA pressures within recommended limits rose to 43%; pressures exceeding the manometer fell to 16%; pharyngolaryngeal morbidity 11% in the 45 patients whose pressure was reduced to normal (P=0.001).

result.other_findings: Adherence remained suboptimal, with staff turnover and agency assistants cited as barriers; manometry was adopted as standard of care at University College Hospital.

result.setting: 130-bed district general hospital (ED and general wards), South Canterbury DHB
result.standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines and Sepsis Six bundle; antibiotics, IV fluids and oxygen within one hour of initial assessment

cycle1.result: 16 of 55 (29%) had antibiotics, IV fluids with or without oxygen within 1 hour; lactate measured in 10 (18%); blood cultures in 18 (33%); urine output monitoring in 15 (27%); 35% received 4-6 bundle elements.

result.intervention: Sepsis Six pathway and posters; education workshops for ED staff, junior doctors and ward nurses; designated sepsis assistants; laminated Sepsis Six photo on ED phlebotomy trolleys; request for an extra ED consultant.

cycle2.result: 25 of 40 (63%) had antibiotics, fluids with or without oxygen within 1 hour; lactate 10 (25%); blood cultures 25 (63%), 96% before antibiotics; urine output monitoring 17 (43%); 66% received 4-6 bundle elements.

result.other_findings: A 3-month re-audit (n = 71) showed 52% within 1 hour. Time to clinician review did not improve (47 to 44 minutes) and in-hospital mortality rose from 2% to 10%, possibly due to winter re-audits.

result.topic: Antenatal lifestyle risk factor screening and counselling
result.setting: 50 primary health care centres in predominantly Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities (ABCD National Research Partnership) across five Australian states and territories
result.standard: Australian Clinical Practice Guidelines for Antenatal Care: screening and counselling for smoking, alcohol, nutrition, physical activity and food security, and folate before 20 weeks

cycle1.result: Screened for cigarette use 73%; cessation advice 52%; screened for alcohol 65%; brief alcohol counselling 51%; nutrition counselling 41%; food security counselling 4.8%; physical activity counselling 20%; folate before 20 weeks 28%.

result.intervention: Continuous quality improvement cycles: systems assessment and health record audits, with each centre setting priorities and developing its own system improvement strategies, supported by One21seventy tools and facilitators.

cycle2.result: Screened for cigarette use 95% (OR 11); cessation advice 73%; screened for alcohol 83%; brief alcohol counselling 71%; nutrition counselling 65%; food security counselling 9.1%; physical activity counselling 15%; folate before 20 weeks 34%.

result.other_findings: After cycle 1 (n = 758) cigarette screening was 90%; four CQI cycles in total. Better self-rated organisational systems were associated with more alcohol screening, nutrition counselling and folate prescription; lifestyle counselling and folate remained poor.

result.setting: 20 acute care hospitals, Banner Health system, Arizona
result.standard: CMS sepsis bundle (SEP-1) compliance; aim to improve from 30% to 40% within 1 year

cycle1.result: Mean compliance 25.8% (monthly range 16-31%); baseline rate for SPC 28.5%.

result.intervention: Revised sepsis standardised clinical practice and system-wide education; computerised decision support to reflex-order repeat lactate and prompt lactate and blood cultures when antibiotics ordered; pharmacy made first-time IV antibiotic orders stat.

cycle2.result: Mean compliance 34.6% in the second 6 months (p<0.0001), peaking at 42%; 31.8% after CMS changed specifications in July 2016 (p<0.019 vs baseline).

result.other_findings: Most commonly missed elements were repeat lactate (30%), blood cultures (19%) and antibiotics (16%); the improvement was not sustained after the CMS specification change. Total denominator over 12 months was 1850 patients.

result.setting: Pediatric emergency department, Oregon Health and Science University academic medical centre
result.standard: Time to antibiotic administration <60 minutes; aim >80% of eligible patients within 60 minutes

cycle1.result: Mean time to antibiotics 64 minutes; 59% received antibiotics in <60 minutes.

result.intervention: PDSA cycles: target of antibiotic order within 13 minutes with abnormality tracker, emails and audit and feedback; revised order set with antibiotic flagged urgent and pharmacy prioritisation; EHR change allowing antibiotic ordering before patient arrival using most recent weight.

cycle2.result: Mean time to antibiotics 53 minutes; 84% received antibiotics in <60 minutes.

result.other_findings: Gains were sustained in the maintenance period (April 2016 to March 2017) with mean 44 minutes and 85% within 60 minutes; balancing measures (asthma bronchodilator and steroid times) did not worsen.

result.setting: Level 3 academic NICU (49 beds), University of California San Diego Jacobs Medical Center
result.standard: Targets: handoff data accuracy 80%, incorrectly listed medications reduced (0% target), verbal handoff time reduced by 20%, user satisfaction up 1 point on a 5-point Likert scale

cycle1.result: Composite accuracy of 16 patient data points 51% (demographics 37%, medical data 66%); patients with incorrect or incomplete medication lists 51%.

result.intervention: EHR-generated structured handoff tool with autopopulated fields (Epic SmartPhrases), developed through PDSA cycles with stakeholder feedback, tutorials and a pilot; went live February 2019.

cycle2.result: Composite accuracy 97% (demographics 100%, medical data 94%); incorrect medication lists 0%.

result.other_findings: Verbal handoff time did not change; user satisfaction appeared to increase (7 respondents per post-implementation survey). Handoffs were audited 4-5 times a month.

result.setting: Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre, large academic cardiac centre, Toronto
result.standard: Choosing Wisely and cardiology society guidance that troponin alone is the biomarker of choice for cardiac injury; target 50% reduction in CK tests and CK-to-troponin ratio of one-third or less

cycle1.result: 47,556 CK tests (mean 3963 per month); CK-to-troponin ratio 0.91; 72.8% of CK tests coupled with troponin.

result.intervention: Revised institutional testing guidelines; CK removed from ED triage, cardiology admission, cardiovascular surgery and ICU order sets; academic detailing and education; unit-level comparative feedback by email; reduced default intervals for recurring CK tests.

cycle2.result: 25,332 CK tests (mean 2111 per month), a 46.7% reduction (p<0.001); CK-to-troponin ratio 0.49; coupled tests 58.3% of CK orders.

result.other_findings: Troponin testing did not change; the reduction was sustained in January to March 2020 and projected annual savings were C$28,446. The 50% target was narrowly missed.

result.setting: Paediatric oncology ward, KK Women's and Children's Hospital Cancer Centre, Singapore
result.standard: Universal nutrition screening within 24 hours of admission (JCI accreditation); aim for timely dietitian referral of high-risk children within 48 hours of admission

cycle1.result: 4 of 11 (36.4%) high-risk patients referred to the dietitian; 16 of 30 (53.3%) seen within 48 hours; median time to dietitian 3 days (IQR 1-14); malnutrition at admission 45 of 258 (17.4%).

result.intervention: Validated cancer-specific screening tool (SCAN) with nurse champion training; mandatory SCAN template in the EMR with auto-populated weights; direct dietitian self-referral from a work board flag.

cycle2.result: 42 of 49 (85.7%) high-risk patients seen by the dietitian (p=0.005); 40 of 41 (97.6%) seen within 48 hours; median time to dietitian 1 day (p=0.010); malnutrition 17 of 260 (6.5%).

result.other_findings: Screening completion was 94.4% in PDSA cycle 1 but referral remained low (62.7%) until direct referral was introduced; early intervention was associated with better weight change at 3 months.

result.setting: Level 6 neonatal unit (14 NICU and 34 special care beds), Women's and Children's Hospital, North Adelaide
result.standard: Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute benchmark of 3% blood culture contamination; project aim to reduce contamination from 2.0% to 1.0% by March 2020

cycle1.result: 39 contaminants (2.0%); monthly rates varied 0.0-5.7%; compliance with standard bottle inoculation and skin preparation steps 50% each (observational audits, n = 20).

result.intervention: Four PDSA cycles: standardised bottle inoculation with a transfer device; standardised skin preparation for cannulation; aseptic technique education package; minimum 1 mL blood volume with a blood culture sticker and record book.

cycle2.result: 10 contaminants (0.90%); compliance with inoculation process 100% and skin preparation 95%; at least 1 mL collected in 94% of 450 collections.

result.other_findings: Aseptic technique test scores rose from 39% to 92% (n = 10, P < 0.001); no skin burns or unsuccessful sampling events occurred.

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infections
result.setting: 18 community-based outpatient clinics, VA Tennessee Valley Healthcare System
result.standard: Guidelines recommending no antibiotics for acute uncomplicated bronchitis; aim to reduce antibiotic prescribing from 65% to <32% by April 2020

cycle1.dates: July to December 2018 (6 months before intervention)
cycle1.result: Antibiotics prescribed in 314 of 486 (64.6%) acute bronchitis/URI encounters; 667 of 1054 (63%) over January to December 2018.

result.intervention: Seven PDSA cycles: provider needs-assessment interviews; CDC patient education materials and supportive care prescription pads; individual comparative feedback emails; individualised focused case reviews with high prescribers; primary care grand rounds.

cycle2.result: Antibiotics prescribed in 154 of 418 (36.8%) encounters (p=0.002 across periods).

result.other_findings: The target of <32% was not reached; feedback emails were high effort with low read rates, while case reviews of 14 high prescribers gave the largest reduction. No change in return visits or calls; VA clinics improved more than contract clinics.

result.setting: Obstetric emergency, Sub-District Hospital Ballabgarh (secondary care, AIIMS New Delhi rural health project)
result.standard: Completeness of 31 agreed data points on first information sheets (items based on hospital policy and Ministry of Health guidelines); aim >90% completeness

cycle1.result: Mean first information sheet completeness 73.95%; 1 of 12 (8.33%) fully complete.

result.intervention: PDSA cycles: education session for interns; wall notes of required data points; a printed antenatal care (ANC) admission checklist, then implemented with shift-wise training and nursing officers printing it each shift.

cycle2.result: Mean completeness 86.34% (p<0.001); 16 of 65 (24.62%) fully complete (p=0.2); ANC checklist used in 69.72% of sheets.

result.other_findings: Physical examination items improved most; high-risk pregnancy documentation rose from 0% to 56.66% (17/30). Sheets with the checklist were more complete than those without (87.74% vs 74.42%).

result.setting: Mother-baby unit, suburban community hospital in North Carolina (Duke University Health System)
result.standard: AAP Infant Safe Sleep guidelines; composite 'perfect sleep' measure; aim 70% within 1 year

cycle1.result: 41.9% of sleeping infants met 'perfect sleep'; 38.0% of sleep areas had extra items; 15.3% inappropriately bundled; 87.0% in a safe location; 90.3% on their back; 3.8% raised bassinette head.

result.intervention: Seven PDSA cycles: nursing education module; parent education with door hangers then crib cards; temporary then permanent supply of wearable blankets (sleep sacks) with laundering; reminder to labour ward nurses to give empty bassinettes; gifting sleep sacks to take home.

cycle2.result: 'Perfect sleep' rose to 67.3% (goal of 70% not met); extra items 20.2%; inappropriate bundling 3.8%; safe location 92.0%; back sleeping 98.1%.

result.other_findings: Improvements were sustained over 12 months after the last PDSA cycle; over 3100 observations were recorded in total. Extra items in the bassinette, often due to storage, remained the main cause of failure.

result.setting: Postnatal clinics, ESIC Medical College and Hospital, Faridabad (tertiary care hospital)
result.standard: SMART aim to increase centchroman acceptance as a postpartum contraceptive to at least 50%

cycle1.result: Baseline centchroman acceptance rate 2.9%.

result.intervention: Staff seminar, then three PDSA cycles: information charts in postnatal clinics; awareness sessions by nursing staff; counselling by resident doctors.

cycle2.result: Acceptance rose to 15.3%, 56.3% and 78.2% after PDSA cycles 1-3; overall acceptance 81.7% during 12-week follow-up.

result.other_findings: Continuation rates were 96.7%, 89.5% and 78.6% at 1, 3 and 6 months; discontinuation was mainly due to preference for IUDs or medroxyprogesterone injections.

result.setting: Tertiary care teaching hospital (ESIC Medical College and Hospital, Faridabad)
result.standard: Aim to increase postpartum tubal ligation among multiparous women by 50% from baseline

cycle1.result: Baseline prevalence of postpartum tubal ligation 30.2%.

result.intervention: Three PDSA cycles: modified consent form with a PPTL column and red sticker on antenatal cards plus provider counselling; group antenatal education for women; counselling of partners and birth attendants.

cycle2.result: PPTL rose to 49.5% after cycle 1, 68.8% after cycle 2 and 74.4% after cycle 3; continuation rate 72% at the end of follow-up.

result.other_findings: Six-monthly audits were proposed; women not wanting PPTL all opted for postpartum intrauterine devices.

result.topic: Early follow-up after heart failure discharge
result.setting: 13 hospitals in a Michigan quality improvement collaborative (I-MPACT, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan)

cycle1.result: 43% (n = 2,798) had a 7-day follow-up visit scheduled; 10% (n = 666) had an ED return within 30 days; early follow-up was associated with lower ED returns (aRR 0.85).

result.other_findings: Retrospective cohort study. Medicaid, dialysis, depression and opioids at discharge were linked to lower early follow-up, and three hospitals with few Black patients had lower follow-up rates for Black patients.

result.setting: Marshfield Clinic Health System, 20-county region of north-central Wisconsin

cycle1.result: 65 injured children in the in-farm group (4,730) and 378 in the out-farm group (93,420); in-farm injury rates ranged from 61.8 per 10,000 (2017) to 28.2 per 10,000 (2018) versus 10.7 to 16.8 per 10,000 in the out-farm group.

result.other_findings: Injury surveillance study; rates were about three times higher in farm residents and did not change significantly over 5 years. ATV injuries were common in both groups.

result.setting: Postgraduate prosthodontics (MClinDent) programme, Cardiff University Dental Hospital
result.standard: Standards set from a systematic review: implant success rate 90% and survival rate 95%

cycle1.result: 84 implants in 38 patients: success rate 90.5% (n = 76) and survival rate 100% (n = 84); both standards met.

result.other_findings: Eight implants (9.5%) failed on bone loss criteria; history of periodontitis and poor compliance with supportive periodontal therapy were risk factors. Written oral hygiene brochures were recommended.

result.topic: Patient-reported side effects and treatment continuation
result.setting: Direct-to-consumer telehealth platform (Roman Health Ventures) treating erectile dysfunction

cycle1.result: 71.1% of control patients refilled their prescription; 3.3% had medication adjusted.

result.intervention: Automated Rx Check-In questionnaire on satisfaction and side effects sent 14 days after starting treatment (randomised); later, standardised side-effect counselling message templates for providers.

cycle2.result: 75.2% of intervention patients refilled (log-rank p = 0.04); 5.4% had medication adjusted (p = 0.038).

result.other_findings: Randomised trial rather than an audit. In cycle 2, 96.7% of 396 patients counselled with templates continued treatment versus 90.2% of 358 without (p = 0.0005); questionnaire response rate was about 33%.

result.setting: Cardiac, thoracic and vascular surgery departments, RUDN University-affiliated teaching hospital, Moscow
result.standard: International (ASA/European Society of Anaesthesiology) and Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh fasting guidance: clear fluids until 2 hours and solids until 6 hours before surgery (morning list: solids to midnight, clear fluids to 06:30; afternoon list: breakfast before 07:00, clear fluids to 11:00)

cycle1.dates: September (baseline audit; year given as 2022 in methods and 2023 in abstract)
cycle1.result: 86 (95.6%) fasted >2 hours from clear fluids and 90 (100%) >6 hours from solid food; 18 (20.0%) fasted >12 hours from clear fluids; 48 (53.3%) received both verbal and written instructions.

result.intervention: Institutional action plan: explicit morning and afternoon fasting rules, fasting information at pre-hospitalisation and preoperative clinic visits, and explanatory leaflets for patients.

cycle2.dates: December (final monthly re-audit after October and November)
cycle2.result: 33 of 57 (57.9%) fasted >2 hours from clear fluids (p=0.021); 27 (47.4%) fasted >6-12 hours from solid food (p=0.005); 3 (5.3%) fasted >12 hours from clear fluids.

result.other_findings: Across all 306 patients median fasting was 4.5 hours for clear fluids and 14.5 hours for solids; afternoon-list patients fasted longer (clear fluids 6.2 vs 3.4 hours, p<0.001). Both instruction types were received by 70.3% after the action plan.

result.setting: 15-bed closed adult ICU, tertiary care hospital (Dr. S.N. Medical College, Jodhpur)
result.standard: Ventilator bundle compliance (all five components documented); aim >90% within 6 months

cycle1.result: Ventilator bundle compliance 40.7%, lowest for daily sedation vacation with SBT and thromboprophylaxis; VAP 62.4 per 1,000 ventilator days.

result.intervention: PDSA cycles: multidisciplinary educational boot camp with WhatsApp group; bundle checklist in ICU progress chart signed by nurses and residents and countersigned by consultants, random inspections and a placard; simulation and micro-scenarios to standardise technique, with coloured bed marks for head elevation.

cycle2.dates: September 2022 to August 2023 (6 months after compliance >90%)
cycle2.result: Compliance >70% after cycle 1 and >90% after cycle 2; VAP fell to 25.7 per 1,000 ventilator days (P=0.004; incidence rate ratio 2.34).

result.other_findings: Total ventilation days and ICU length of stay also fell significantly (P=0.007 and P=0.002).

result.setting: Sultan Bin Abdulaziz Humanitarian City, 511-bed rehabilitation facility, Riyadh
result.standard: CDC CAUTI prevention guidance, HOUDINI nurse-driven catheter removal protocol and CAUTI care bundle

cycle1.result: Mean CAUTI rate 1.28 per 1000 catheter days.

result.intervention: Three PDSA cycles: staff education, HOUDINI nurse-driven removal protocol with posters and a campaign; monitored HOUDINI and care bundle compliance; closed urinary drainage system introduced; external catheters as alternatives; internal audits with feedback; patient and family education and a urinary catheter passport.

cycle2.result: Mean CAUTI rate 0.42 per 1000 catheter days (p=0.04); eight consecutive points below the centre line from July 2023 to May 2024.

result.other_findings: Bundle and HOUDINI compliance were monitored but compliance figures were not reported; a sustainability plan included automating the HOUDINI tool.

result.topic: CT KUB scan cranial extent and radiation dose
result.setting: District general hospital, Doncaster Royal Infirmary
result.standard: IR(ME)R principle of minimising radiation; local protocol to start CT KUB at the T10-T12 vertebral level (no formal national guideline)

cycle1.result: 48% (n=49) of scans started above T10, 51% (n=52) from T10-T12 and 1% below T12; mean effective dose 6.37 mSv above T10 vs 4.56 mSv from T10-T12.

result.intervention: Findings presented to urology and radiology departments and a new protocol to commence CT KUB from T10-T12 devised.

cycle2.result: 21.9% (n=23) started above T10, 75.2% (n=79) from T10-T12 and 2.9% below T12; mean dose 6.76 mSv above T10 vs 4.12 mSv from T10-T12.

result.other_findings: Kidneys were fully visualised from T10 in 98.6% of all scans, but from T12 in only 79.2%, supporting T10 as the cranial limit.

result.topic: Mid-trimester fetal anomaly scan image quality
result.setting: 88 operators of the French college of fetal ultrasound (CFEF) in public and private hospitals and private practice across France
result.standard: CNEOF 2022 national mid-trimester ultrasound protocol (21 recommended and 3 additional standardised views) with a 73-criterion consensus quality assessment score

cycle1.result: 9028 of 9240 (97.8%) recommended images recorded; feasibility of recommended views 88.5-100% (>95% for 20 of 21); 319 of 440 (72.5%) scans had no recommended view missing; 64 of 73 (88%) conformity criteria met in over 90% of cases.

result.other_findings: Weakest criteria included adrenal gland visibility (63.7%), cavum septi pellucidi (85.4%) and cervix views (about 87%); self- and peer-assessment agreed well (AC1 >0.80 for 70 of 73 criteria). Shorter scans and BMI >30 were associated with more missing images.

result.setting: Emergency department, Eastern Regional Referral Hospital, Mongar
result.standard: Hospital transcription protocol; complete drug chart documentation to be maintained above 90%

cycle1.result: 44.9% (45%) of drug charts complete; adherence to standard charting practice 51%; transcriber signature/name recorded in 45%.

result.intervention: Four 2-week PDSA cycles: sensitisation teaching on medication errors and the transcription protocol; standardisation to a single drug chart; red pens at the nursing station for antibiotic charting; daily drug chart monitoring and feedback by pharmacy.

cycle2.result: 98% of drug charts complete; adherence to standard charting practice 98%; transcriber signature 95%.

result.other_findings: Completeness was 81% after cycle 1 and 88% after cycle 2, passing 90% after cycle 3; only 48% of staff were initially aware of the transcription protocol.

result.setting: King Abdullah Specialist Children's Hospital, academic tertiary paediatric hospital (about 220 beds), Riyadh
result.standard: Bedside PEWS protocol for scores of 5 and above: targets 95% for timely reassessment and rescoring, 100% for nurse escalation and 100% for timely physician review

cycle1.result: Compliance 84% in the pilot unit; in the first year compliance was below target for reassessment, escalation and physician review.

result.intervention: Electronic PEWS integrated into the EMR with an action plan; training of about 600 staff and at orientation; modified action plan with observation frequency; staged roll-out to wards, ER and PICU; unit-specific action plans; quarterly compliance audits with feedback.

cycle2.result: Reassessment and rescoring 95-100%, escalation 100% and physician review 100% over the past 6 years; pilot compliance rose to 96% after the action plan change.

result.other_findings: Unplanned PICU admissions fell by 25% in 2018 and 50% in 2019 versus baseline, unplanned HDU admissions fell by 42.9% by 2019 and LOS after unplanned PICU admission halved; cardiopulmonary arrests outside PICU were unchanged. Nurses reporting a negative response to escalation fell from 72% to 23%.

result.setting: Obstetric unit, Women's Hospital of Nanjing Medical University (Nanjing Maternity and Child Health Care Hospital)

cycle1.result: Routine care: symptomatic VTE 2.4 per 1000 deliveries (32 cases); 12.6% received mechanical and 0.2% pharmacological prophylaxis.

result.intervention: Nurse-assisted early warning intervention: multidisciplinary team, patient education manuals, nurse and junior doctor Caprini risk assessment on admission, daily and within 6 hours after caesarean, with warning flags in the nurse workstation.

cycle2.result: Symptomatic VTE 0.29 per 1000 deliveries (4 cases; P < 0.001); 19.8% received mechanical and 0.9% pharmacological prophylaxis.

result.other_findings: Prospective cohort comparison of two concurrent groups rather than an audit against a standard; no life-threatening bleeding occurred.

result.setting: Emergency department, Eastern Regional Referral Hospital, Mongar
result.standard: Complete documentation of all five initial vital signs; aim to improve from 40% to over 80% in 10 weeks

cycle1.result: 40% of records had all five vital signs documented; temperature 42%, respiratory rate 50%, SpO2 85%, pulse and BP 96% each.

result.intervention: Four PDSA cycles: sensitisation teaching on vital signs and triage; procurement of working monitors, BP cuffs and thermometers; a designated assessment area with redesigned patient flow; a vital signs stamp on walk-in and OPD records.

cycle2.result: 97% of records had complete vital signs; respiratory rate and temperature 97% each; SpO2 100%.

result.other_findings: Completion was 74% after cycle 1, fell to 62% by the end of cycle 2 and reached 90% after cycle 3.

result.topic: Endotracheal cuff pressure monitoring and ventilator-associated pneumonia
result.setting: Adult ICUs in eight tertiary hospitals

cycle1.result: Randomised trial: VAP incidence 16.2% (17/105) with continuous vs 17.6% (19/108) with intermittent cuff pressure monitoring (P = 0.79); cuff pressure within 25-30 cmH2O 96.9% vs 70.7%.

result.other_findings: Continuous monitoring cut cumulative 48 h cuff adjustment time (85 s vs 660 s); no difference in ventilation duration, ICU stay or mortality.

result.setting: Jamma Primary Hospital, war-affected primary hospital, Amhara region
result.standard: Ethiopian Ministry of Health clinical quality audit guideline seven-element first-visit ANC bundle; aim 0% to 100%

cycle1.result: 0% of pregnant mothers received all ANC bundle elements at first visit (378 attended; nothing beyond counselling).

result.intervention: ANC first-visit bundle checklist, client exit interviews, weekly laboratory test availability checks, backup generator funded by the community, respectful care training and psychosocial support for staff.

cycle2.dates: Implementation year and sustainability year to April 2024
cycle2.result: 94.5% of mothers received all ANC bundle elements at first visit (monthly sample of 19 charts); checklist use 100%.

result.other_findings: Client satisfaction rose from 40% to 100% and laboratory test availability from 0% to 85%.

result.topic: Delirium screening accuracy in intensive care
result.setting: Three adult medical ICUs (41 beds), 2600-bed tertiary medical centre (National Taiwan University Hospital)
result.standard: Agreement of bedside nurse ICDSC assessments with an expert nurse (kappa >0.8 benchmark)
result.intervention: Three-month multimodal education: didactic lectures, case discussions of difficult scenarios and one-to-one bedside mentoring by an expert nurse.
result.other_findings: Agreement stayed poor for patients over 85 and those physically restrained; psychomotor item kappa only 0.36 after training.

result.topic: Transfer of deteriorating outpatients to the emergency department
result.setting: Outpatient clinics, Aga Khan University Hospital, 710-bed tertiary hospital, Karachi
result.standard: Locally developed early warning criteria, transfer process and SBAR handoff tool; compliance defined as all SBAR components documented

cycle1.result: No baseline transfer data (inconsistent documentation and no tracking before the project).

result.intervention: Revised outpatient early warning signs, structured five-step transfer process with defined roles, SBAR handoff tool, emergency transfer kits and equipment checks, hospital-wide webinar and in-person training.

cycle2.result: Handoff tool completed for more than 70% of items in 65.67% (176/268) of transfers; ED stay >7 hours in 45.52%; in-hospital mortality 5.22% (14/268).

result.other_findings: Staff knowledge improved significantly on 8 of 10 items after training (n=40); no workflow delays or extra staff burden were reported.

result.topic: CT head imaging in head injury
result.setting: Emergency department, University Hospital of North Durham
result.standard: NICE 2023 head injury guideline: CT within 1 hour for high-risk features and within 8 hours for others; target 100%

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 29/37 (78.4%); one-hour CT completed 4/10 (40%); anticoagulated 19/19 (100%); amnesia/LOC within 8 hours 6/9 (66.7%).

result.intervention: Structured teaching for doctors and nurses, NICE summary posters in triage, ambulance handover and staff base, and a rapid assessment senior clinician overseeing injury presentations.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 46/52 (88.5%) (p = 0.32); one-hour CT completed 11/18 (61.1%); anticoagulated 22/22 (100%); amnesia/LOC 22/28 (78.6%).

result.other_findings: None of the improvements reached statistical significance.

result.topic: Aseptic non-touch technique for peripheral cannulation
result.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit, Combined Military Hospital Multan
result.standard: ANTT guidelines (six key actions); aim 80% adherence over 12 weeks

cycle1.result: Median ANTT adherence 66%; initial handwashing 50%; hand wash before unpacking 0%; before gloves 21%; tray cleaning before use 64%, after use 36%.

result.intervention: Education (presentations, video, hands-on training), posters and handouts, bedside printed checklists, ANTT link nurse cascade training, then targeted feedback and supervised morning cannulations.

cycle2.result: Median adherence 94% (89% after first PDSA cycle, n=15).

result.other_findings: After cycle 1, hand wash before unpacking reached 67% and tray cleaning after use 60%.

result.setting: WVU Medicine Golisano Children's Hospital, tertiary children's hospital, Morgantown, West Virginia
result.standard: Vizient national top-quartile benchmark seven-day revisit rate 2.17%; aim to reduce revisit rate by at least 1% by December 31, 2025

cycle1.result: Seven-day revisit rate 3.75% (39/1041); pain and dehydration main drivers.

result.intervention: Perioperative bundle: intraoperative crystalloid >=30 ml/kg, acetaminophen and dexamethasone; scheduled PACU ibuprofen; tolerance-based hydration readiness; standardised discharge packet with hydration checklist and dye-free medication calendar; surgical team PACU check-ins (three PDSA cycles).

cycle2.result: Seven-day revisit rate 2.16% (n = 15); by cycle: PDSA 1 2.83% (7/247), PDSA 2 1.65% (7/423), PDSA 3 0.75% (1/133).

result.other_findings: Pain remained the main reason for revisit after the interventions; no formal statistical analysis.

result.topic: Early mobility and therapy referral in neonatal intensive care
result.setting: Level IV NICU surgical service, Boston Children's Hospital
result.standard: Aim: >75% of eligible surgical infants (>=34 weeks PMA) receive PT and OT consults within 24 months (adapted PICU Up! programme)

cycle1.result: PT consults 25% (24.7%) and OT consults 22% (21.6%); mean time to consult 23 days for both.

result.intervention: Adapted PICU Up! guideline for infants, one-to-one education by champions, PICU Up! level field added to the EMR and nursing handoff sheet, prompts on rounds, monthly audit feedback emails.

cycle2.result: PT consults 95% (95.3%) and OT consults 95% (94.7%); time to PT consult 8 days and OT consult 9 days.

result.other_findings: No significant change in length of stay, time to first extubation, pressure injuries, fractures or unplanned extubations; 364 infants eligible across the whole study.

result.topic: Myopia progression prediction in school children
result.setting: Government and private schools across five districts of Bhopal division, Madhya Pradesh

cycle1.result: Study protocol only: planned cross-sectional survey of about 5,000 children and 2-year cohort of about 500 to build an AI prediction model; no results.

result.other_findings: Observational cohort protocol to develop an AI model and mobile application for myopia screening.

result.setting: Private and general wards, tertiary referral academic hospital (Sri Ramachandra Institute), Chennai

cycle1.result: CAUTI in 26%; open drainage (61.3% vs 10.1%), urobag above waist (71.43% vs 13.92%), tubing kinking (75% vs 10.53%), diabetes and catheter >7 days were associated with CAUTI; risk score AUC 0.94.

result.other_findings: Prospective observational study deriving a point-based CAUTI risk score; open drainage bags were used in 31 of 100 patients.

result.topic: Ultrasound documentation during central venous catheter insertion
result.setting: 48-bed quaternary paediatric ICU, Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center
result.standard: SMART aim: ultrasound image capture of correct guidewire position in 2 planes before vessel dilation from 0% to 90%; supported by ASA and Society of Hospital Medicine recommendations

cycle1.result: 0% (no standard process to document guidewire position).

result.intervention: Image capture and EHR upload workflow (laminated guide, later condensed to 1 page), image capture step and QR survey added to the central line observation guide, reminders and booster education, simulation in fellow boot camp, troubleshooting guide and visual aid on ultrasound machines.

cycle2.result: Successful image capture and upload 117/270 (44%) overall; monthly mean rose to 58%, peak 64%. DICOM order placement 194/270 (74%); mean 83%, peak 100%.

result.other_findings: Aim of 90% not achieved; new fellows trained on the workflow at induction reached 70% vs 37% in the prior class; only 3 survey responses said the process took too much time.

result.topic: Surgical site infection after paediatric cardiac surgery
result.setting: Newly established public-sector congenital cardiac surgery programme, Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation, Karachi
result.standard: International Quality Improvement Collaborative (IQIC) benchmark SSI rate of about 2.2%

cycle1.result: SSI rate 12 per 100 surgeries (initial 3-month rate 23%, 3/13); hand hygiene about 45%, environmental cleaning about 20%, wound documentation 0%.

result.intervention: Measurement dashboards; single-use sterile consumables and skin preparation bundle; preoperative SSI risk screening tool; nurse-led wound clinic with 30-day photo follow-up by messaging; aseptic technique and hand hygiene training with daily audits; infection prevention champions, huddles and checklists.

cycle2.result: SSI rate 5 per 100 surgeries (lowest 2 per 100, July to November 2024); overall 31 SSIs in 500 surgeries (6.2 per 100).

result.other_findings: Hand hygiene rose to 90% and environmental cleaning to 85%; SSI rate rose again to 6 per 100 before stabilising, and benchmark was not sustained.

result.topic: Infection prevention and disinfection in eye clinics
result.setting: Multispecialty ophthalmology clinics, Magrabi Hospital, Riyadh
result.standard: Hospital infection control standards in line with MOH and CBAHI frameworks; aim >90% compliance across all domains

cycle1.result: Staff self-report survey: aware of disinfection policy 87.5%; annual training 45.8%; staff wear masks 39.6%; disinfection logs maintained 75.0%; multidose drops used for one patient only 58.3%; high-touch surfaces cleaned after each patient 66.7%.

result.intervention: Revised guidelines with visual guides for infection protocols and hand hygiene, emphasis on mask use and log keeping, quality team reminders, online training for all clinical staff and training at induction.

cycle2.result: Aware of policy 93.2%; annual training 63.4%; masks 68.2% (p=0.01); logs maintained 95.4% (p=0.01); multidose drops single-patient use fell to 18.2% (p<0.01); high-touch cleaning 72.7%.

result.other_findings: Shared cleaning responsibility fell from 75.0% to 54.5% and disposable tonometer tip use stayed at 6.8%; data were self-reported rather than observed.

result.topic: Tele-ECG for myocardial infarction diagnosis in primary care
result.setting: Regional network of 12 public institutions (11 primary healthcare centres) led by Sanya People's Hospital

cycle1.result: Median clinical decision-making time for chest pain at primary care 10 min; primary care ECG diagnostic accuracy 82.30%.

result.intervention: AI-enabled regional tele-ECG cloud platform with centralised specialist review.

cycle2.result: Decision-making time 3 min (70.0% reduction); report turnaround 3.79 +/- 1.81 min; diagnostic accuracy 98.11%.

result.other_findings: Real-world evaluation with budget impact analysis; primary care subgroup had low statistical power (mean 32.4%).

result.topic: Emergency pathway for acute myocardial infarction
result.setting: Emergency department, Suzhou Municipal Hospital affiliated to Anhui Medical University

cycle1.result: Routine care: in-hospital survival 81.3% (52/64); first-aid time 75.70 +/- 4.50 min; door-to-balloon 92.4 +/- 15.6 min; door-to-needle 41.2 +/- 8.9 min.

result.intervention: Emergency procedural pathway with timed steps (10, 20, 30 min) plus three-tier triage and red/yellow/green zoning, with staff training.

cycle2.result: In-hospital survival 96.8% (60/62); first-aid time 67.30 +/- 3.90 min; door-to-balloon 78.5 +/- 12.3 min; door-to-needle 32.5 +/- 6.8 min.

result.other_findings: Quasi-experimental outcome study; MACE 6.5% vs 18.8% and satisfaction 87.1% vs 65.6%.

result.setting: In silico database analysis (University of Thessaly)

cycle1.result: Bioinformatic study: 63 extracellular asthma-associated miRNA candidates; six had exact mature-arm concordance in three published studies; one FDR-significant Reactome pathway.

result.other_findings: Laboratory/bioinformatic research, not a clinical audit.

result.topic: Asthma recognition in children with sickle cell disease
result.setting: Routine sickle cell follow-up, Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni and Kourou residents

cycle1.result: Reversible airflow obstruction in 43, normal spirometry in 25, 72 unclassified; prior clinical suspicion in 10/43 (23.3%) with reversible obstruction; sensitivity 23.3%, specificity 88.0%, kappa 0.090.

result.other_findings: Diagnostic agreement study; 33/43 (76.7%) children with reversible obstruction had no prior suspicion of asthma.

result.setting: Department of Pediatrics, The Third People's Hospital of Chengdu

cycle1.result: Retrospective machine learning cohort: TabPFN temporal validation AUROC 0.999 (95% CI 0.997-1.000), Brier score 0.013; sensitivity 1.000 and specificity 0.981 at threshold 0.538.

result.other_findings: Prediction model study, not an audit; leading predictors were maternal disease count, abortion or preterm history, postnatal abnormality and birth-weight category.

result.topic: Sleep clinic referral for obstructive sleep apnoea in pregnancy with obesity
result.setting: High-risk pregnancy clinic, Canberra Hospital

cycle1.result: Protocol only; initial data screening suggests referral rates to sleep clinic are low. No results reported.

result.other_findings: Study of factors associated with referral and OSA diagnosis; results pending at time of abstract.

result.topic: Volatile sedation in burns intensive care
result.setting: Burn intensive care unit
result.standard: Aim to reduce the number of continuous sedative infusions needed to maintain target sedation (SAS 2-4) by 25% in the 48 hours after starting isoflurane

cycle1.result: Local audit: 70% of mechanically ventilated patients in the burn centre were managed on 3 or more continuous sedative infusions.

result.intervention: Introduction of isoflurane sedation with multifaceted education for burn surgeons, respiratory therapists and nurses (self-directed modules, in-person learning, just-in-time training).

cycle2.result: Within 48 hours of isoflurane initiation, 50% (9/18) had a decrease in number of sedative infusions and 56% (10/18) reached optimal sedation on isoflurane and hydromorphone alone.

result.other_findings: Staff feedback was positive on ease of implementation and titration; limitations were specialised equipment and training.

result.topic: Vancomycin continuous infusion protocol adherence in ICU
result.setting: General ICU, St George's Hospital
result.standard: Local ICU vancomycin continuous infusion protocol; steady-state serum concentration target 20-25 mg/L with daily monitoring

cycle1.result: Per-protocol prescribing/administration of loading and maintenance doses with daily monitoring 39% (7/18); therapeutic concentrations within 48 h 3/9.

result.intervention: Protocol dosing revised (2 g loading dose for >90 kg, new renal function categories, higher maintenance dose for CLCR >90 mL/min); protocol made accessible via ePMA and CliniBee/Microguide app; protocol teaching added to medical and nursing induction.

cycle2.result: Per-protocol prescribing/administration with daily monitoring 68% (15/22); therapeutic concentrations within 48 h 54% (7/13).

result.other_findings: Paper drug charts recorded both loading and maintenance doses 38% (5/13) less often than ePMA; administration time differences >60 min in 38% (3/8) of loading and 31% (4/13) of maintenance doses. Staff turnover periods were linked to lower compliance.

result.topic: Mental Health Act documentation and patient rights
result.setting: In-patient psychiatric unit, Delfryn House, Cygnet Health Care
result.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice guiding principles

cycle1.result: Initial audit of MHA documentation, patients' legal rights, section 17 leave, capacity and treatment forms, tribunal reports, section 117 meetings and managers' hearings identified gaps (figures not reported).

result.intervention: Weekly email template for MHA actions, section paper scrutiny template, MHA actions added to morning handover and review form, easy-language leaflets, pharmacist and nurse discussion slots, nurse teaching on report writing and tribunals.

cycle2.result: 100% in capacity assessments, treatment certificates and timely reports; patient knowledge of rights and MHA improved by 68% on pre/post score.

result.other_findings: Organising managers' hearings before section renewal still needed improvement.

result.setting: Psychiatry services across three sites, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, North Wales
result.standard: Deanery/HEIW requirements for local postgraduate teaching and MRCPsych Handbook core trainee requirements

cycle1.result: Consistent formal teaching was not provided and the programme did not meet deanery criteria.

result.intervention: New postgraduate teaching programme developed through PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 31 consultants rated the new programme 4.23/5; 31 non-consultants rated it 3.68/4 and 95% said it covered core trainee requirements.

result.other_findings: Earlier audits suggested teaching had worsened over time before the new programme.

result.setting: Psychiatry services, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, North Wales

cycle1.result: Pre-intervention questionnaire to junior doctors; results not reported numerically.

result.intervention: New induction folder for psychiatry, refined over 3 PDSA cycles (added emergency medication, deanery contacts, updated trust contacts).

cycle2.result: Overwhelmingly positive response from new and old doctors (no figures given).

result.other_findings: Sustainability of the changes was uncertain.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring for antipsychotic prescribing
result.setting: Older Adult Community Mental Health Team, South Wales
result.standard: NICE and Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on physical health monitoring for antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Completed lifestyle advice 0%, physical observations 3%, blood tests 3%, ECG 3%; no patient (0%) had full monitoring; mean overall compliance per patient 9%.

result.intervention: Staff education, junior-doctor-led virtual physical health monitoring clinic, and phlebotomy/ECG pathway; local protocol developed.

cycle2.result: Mean overall compliance per patient 69% (vs 9%); 50% of patients had complete monitoring by January 2023; 67% had bloods and ECG done.

result.other_findings: Main reasons for poor baseline performance were no clear pathway and lack of prescriber awareness (>95%); trained staff reached 100%.

result.setting: Three community mental health teams, East of North Wales, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: RCPsych 'ADHD in adults: Good practice guidelines'

cycle1.result: ASRS documented in 34% of referrals, AQ-10 18%, W-FIRS 0%; 46% diagnosed with a standardised instrument over more than one session; baseline BP 58%, pulse 70%, weight 50%, height 44%.

result.other_findings: Functional impairment and comorbid anxiety, depression and substance use were documented in >90%; family and physical health history mostly below 50%.

result.setting: Medium secure hospital, Rowan View, Merseycare
result.standard: Maudsley 14th edition and Synnovis guidance: clozapine level 12 hours post dose

cycle1.result: Samples >15 hours post dose: OD 56.3% (31/55), BD am/nocte 12.9% (9/62), BD pm/night 25% (3/12), TDS 16.7% (2/12). Samples >12 hours: OD 63.6%, BD am/nocte 51.6%, BD pm 75%, TDS 41.7%.

result.other_findings: Timing was least accurate with bespoke regimes; actions planned were team feedback, education, guideline change with pharmacy and re-audit in 12 months.

result.topic: VTE risk assessment in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Older persons mental health inpatient units, 3 sites, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, North Wales
result.standard: NICE and Department of Health VTE guidance; target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: East: 6/9 forms filled; Central: 2 of 21 patients had a form, none filled; West: 3/11 had a filled form. No standard proforma in Central and West.

result.other_findings: VTE prophylaxis was inconsistently noted on medication charts; a trust-wide VTE risk assessment proforma adapted for psychiatry was recommended.

result.topic: Antimicrobial stewardship prospective audit and feedback
result.setting: Pediatric cardiovascular ICU, Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford

cycle1.result: Aggregate antimicrobial use 1,172 DOT/1000 patient-days.

result.intervention: Formal prospective audit and feedback programme by the antimicrobial stewardship pharmacist and medical director, communicated via the CVICU pharmacist.

cycle2.result: 995 DOT/1000 patient-days (15% reduction); 156 recommendations from 475 audits, 77% accepted.

result.other_findings: Broad-spectrum Gram-negative use fell 8.7% and Gram-positive use fell 27%; stopping the antimicrobial was the most common recommendation (53%).

result.topic: Antimicrobial stewardship prospective audit and feedback
result.setting: Internal medicine wards, 400-bed community hospital (St. Joseph's Health Centre, Toronto)

cycle1.result: 469 DDD/1000 patient-days.

result.intervention: High-intensity twice-weekly interdisciplinary rounds-based prospective audit and feedback replaced low-intensity pharmacist feedback.

cycle2.result: 435 DDD/1000 patient-days (non-significant drop); adjusted change -20.5 (95% CI -67.8 to 26.8).

result.other_findings: A delayed reduction was seen at 13-24 months (adjusted -82.7 DDD/1000 PD).

result.setting: Multi-state paediatric primary care network (Nemours)
result.standard: Published guidelines: amoxicillin first-line for CAP

cycle1.result: Randomised trial of 43 providers; 316 CAP cases (214 control, 102 intervention). Numerical results not given in abstract.

result.intervention: Personalised monthly audit and feedback to individual providers after baseline education.
result.other_findings: Personalised audit and feedback had a small but measurable effect on guideline adherence.

result.topic: Antimicrobial review prompting in critical care
result.setting: Critical care unit, North York General Hospital, Toronto

cycle1.result: Monthly antimicrobial DOT 804/1000 patient-days with a positive trend (7.3 DOT/1000PD).

result.intervention: Nurses prompted prescriber review of antimicrobials on rounds with a standardised script stating day of therapy; pharmacist reminders added through PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Significant reductions in antimicrobial utilisation reported (figures truncated in abstract).

result.other_findings: Controlled interrupted time series with proton-pump inhibitor use as control.

result.topic: Antimicrobial stewardship prospective audit and feedback
result.setting: 17-bed intensive care unit, Royal University Hospital, Saskatoon

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Collaborative prospective audit and feedback rounds three times a week.

cycle2.result: No significant change in overall use; broad-spectrum use fell 28.6% (P = 0.05) and narrow-spectrum use rose 50.0%; recommendation acceptance 92.0%.

result.other_findings: Commonest recommendations: duration optimisation (27.7%), de-escalation (25.9%), discontinuation (17.0%).

result.topic: Outpatient antibiotic prescribing for respiratory and urinary infections
result.setting: Outpatient primary care office, Mercy Health Saint Mary's, Grand Rapids
result.standard: ASP guidelines for URI and UTI treatment

cycle1.result: Fluoroquinolone prescribing for UTI 85%; median URI duration 10 days.

result.intervention: Education with pocket cards on URI and UTI guidelines, then weekly pharmacist audit of all antibiotics for URI/UTI with feedback to prescribers.

cycle2.result: Fluoroquinolone prescribing for UTI fell to 40% in month 1 and 11.7% over the next 6 months; median URI duration 7 days.

result.other_findings: Nitrofurantoin rose from 0.4% to 38.6% of UTI prescriptions; commonest feedback reasons were inappropriate agent (26.3%) and too long a duration (24.3%).

result.topic: Antimicrobial stewardship prospective audit and feedback
result.setting: 151-bed urban community hospital, Chicago

cycle1.result: 370 DOT/1,000 patient-days; oral antimicrobials 32%.

result.intervention: Comprehensive ASP with syndrome-based prospective audit and feedback by trained pharmacists overseen by an ID physician.

cycle2.result: 350 DOT/1,000 patient-days; oral antimicrobials 43%; antibiotic spend down 11%.

result.other_findings: Interventions occurred in 53% of cases; de-escalation was harder in critical care.

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing for acute respiratory infections
result.setting: Emergency department and primary care clinics, VA Medical Centers

cycle1.result: Antibiotic prescribing for uncomplicated ARI visits 53.8%.

result.intervention: Audit-feedback reports to providers with frequent ARI visits plus an academic detailing visit.

cycle2.result: Antibiotic prescribing 27.9%; OR 0.6 (95% CI 0.3, 0.9) in initiating facilities.

result.other_findings: Recurrent ARI visits (8.2% vs 8.6%) and adverse events (2.3% vs 2.1%) did not change.

result.setting: Singapore General Hospital

cycle1.result: Same-day intervention acceptance rate 19.3%.

result.intervention: Rapid notification system: electronic intervention note with immediate text-message alert to prescriber.
result.other_findings: Piperacillin-tazobactam was the commonest antibiotic (85.4%); discontinuation the commonest intervention (68.4%).

result.topic: Urinary catheter use and CAUTI reduction
result.setting: ICUs, Loyola University Medical Center
result.standard: AHRQ-based initiative and nursing decatheterisation protocol

cycle1.result: Urinary catheter standardised utilisation ratio 0.98.

result.intervention: Daily review of catheter indication by night-shift nurses and by Clinical Quality Improvement Specialists, with removal recommendations to care teams.

cycle2.result: Standardised utilisation ratio fell to 0.78; 211 catheters removed after nurse recommendations and 386 after specialist audits.

result.other_findings: Specialists identified many more removable catheters than nurses (888 vs 256).

result.setting: Community hospital, UPMC Altoona

cycle1.result: 51 patients and 30 providers per month using ertapenem.

result.intervention: Remote audit and feedback: central ID physician and pharmacist reviewed ertapenem orders by phone with a local non-ID pharmacist who intervened.

cycle2.result: Median ertapenem use fell 55%; 35 patients and 17 providers per month; acceptance rate 88%.

result.other_findings: Median purchasing cost fell 73%; no patient harm identified.

result.setting: 423 acute facilities in the Hospital National Antimicrobial Prescribing Survey (haematology/oncology vs other inpatients)

cycle1.result: 95809 prescriptions for 63668 adult inpatients (4097 haemonc); haemonc patients were more likely to receive appropriate antibacterials (adjusted OR 1.72, 95% CI 1.59-1.87).

result.other_findings: High vancomycin and amphotericin B use in haemonc; targets identified were prophylaxis, antimicrobial allergy labels, vancomycin and amphotericin B.

result.topic: Antimicrobial stewardship prospective audit and feedback
result.setting: Academic medical centre (University of Nebraska Medical Center / Nebraska Medicine), Omaha

cycle1.result: Survey of clinicians: 110/459 responded (24%); 74.5% said antibiotic overuse was a problem.

result.other_findings: Clinician survey of perceptions of the stewardship programme; improvements needed in communication, education and EMR order sets.

result.setting: 151-bed urban community hospital, Chicago

cycle1.result: SEP-1 success rate 44%.

result.intervention: Sepsis improvement team (ID physician and nurse) running prospective audit and feedback within 48 hours of admission, with education and corrective actions; order sets, checklists and EMR alerts already in place.
result.other_findings: Commonest failures in both groups were initial and repeat lactate.

result.topic: Antimicrobial stewardship prospective audit and feedback
result.setting: General internal medicine unit, urban teaching hospital (St. Michael's Hospital), Toronto

cycle1.result: Temporary suspensions of audit and feedback were associated with changes in antimicrobial use trends (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Greater sustained decreases in targeted antimicrobials were associated with active audit and feedback.

result.setting: AdventHealth Orlando, large health system

cycle1.result: Tier 3 and 4 antimicrobial use 89 DOT per 1,000 days present; cost $9.83 per adjusted patient-day.

result.intervention: Hospital-wide antimicrobial tier policy with criteria for use at order entry plus prospective audit and feedback by pharmacists and transformation medical directors; education September 2018.

cycle2.result: Tier 3 and 4 use 70 DOT per 1,000 days present (21.3% decrease, P = 0.001); cost $7.27 (26% decrease).

result.other_findings: Non-significant decline in hospital-acquired C. difficile.

result.topic: Postpartum and preconception counselling in pre-existing diabetes
result.setting: Diabetes in Pregnancy Clinic, Mount Sinai Hospital, Toronto
result.standard: 2018 Diabetes Canada Clinical Practice Guidelines on Diabetes in Pregnancy (6 counselling components)

cycle1.result: 42% (n=50) returned for the 6-week postpartum visit; less than 20% had documented counselling on two or more key components.

result.other_findings: A quality improvement project was planned to close the gap.

result.topic: Pharmacist medication review in older adults with cancer
result.setting: Cancer Aging and Resiliency (CARE) clinic, The James Cancer Hospital, Ohio State University
result.standard: Beers criteria used to identify potentially inappropriate medications

cycle1.result: Mean 13.1 medications per patient; 457 drug therapy problems (3.3 per patient) and 523 interventions; PIM 16.2%, drug-drug interaction 6.1%.

result.other_findings: Commonest interventions were patient education (31.7%), medication reconciliation (26.2%) and discontinuation (16.1%).

result.setting: Inner-city Veterans Affairs hospital (John D Dingell VA Medical Center), Detroit
result.standard: IDSA/ATS CAP guidelines: 5 days of therapy for clinically stable patients; aim to reduce median duration by at least 1 day in 5 months

cycle1.result: 5-day treatment course in 5.3%.

result.intervention: Chief Resident in Quality and Safety gave monthly education and daily audit and feedback with patient-specific duration recommendations.
result.other_findings: Total antibiotic duration and excess days fell without adverse effect on outcomes.

result.topic: Urinary tract infection diagnosis in the emergency department
result.setting: Quaternary paediatric emergency department, The Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto
result.standard: Aim to reduce UTI misdiagnosis by 50% over 24 months

cycle1.result: Median UTI misdiagnosis 52.5%; correct antibiotic duration 45.2%; patients contacted to stop antibiotics 0%.

result.intervention: UTI diagnostic algorithm embedded in the electronic record and a urine culture callback system (PDSA cycles).

cycle2.result: Median misdiagnosis 32.5%; correct antibiotic duration 75.1%; algorithm adherence 78.9%; mean patients contacted 76.8%; 1,678 antibiotic-days saved.

result.other_findings: Of 106 missed UTIs, 8 returned within 72 hours and 2 needed admission.

result.setting: Two community teaching hospitals (Mercy Health Saint Mary's), Michigan
result.standard: Targeted audit and feedback recommending 5 days for uncomplicated CAP

cycle1.result: Average prescribed duration: pre-TAF 7.0 days, pre-PCT 7.8 days.

result.intervention: Procalcitonin testing with routine audit and feedback at one site; targeted audit and feedback recommending 5 days at the other.
result.other_findings: Both strategies significantly shortened durations with no difference in outcomes.

result.topic: Central line bundle compliance and CLABSI
result.setting: COVID ICUs, Mount Sinai Beth Israel, 220-bed acute care hospital, New York

cycle1.result: Bundle compliance 13%; ICU CLABSI 3.3 per 1,000 central line days (April-May).

result.intervention: Infusion nurses performed daily intensive central line maintenance rounds for a month, educating ICU nurses and emailing daily reports to nursing leadership.

cycle2.result: Bundle compliance 88%; CLABSI rate fell to 0.

result.other_findings: Baseline problems included undated, bloody or non-intact dressings, misplaced CHG discs and missing alcohol caps.

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing in the emergency department
result.setting: 2 intervention and 2 control emergency departments, Veterans Health Administration
result.standard: Guideline-concordant management of 5 acute respiratory infections and cystitis

cycle1.result: Guideline-concordant management 52.1%.

result.intervention: One-to-one education and individualised quarterly feedback on antibiotic prescribing with peer comparison.

cycle2.result: Guideline-concordant management 72.2%; antibiotic use fell 8.9% vs 3.4% at control sites (RRR -3.3%, 95% CI -8.4 to +1.7).

result.other_findings: Overall antibiotic use did not fall significantly compared with control EDs.

result.topic: Outpatient antibiotic prescribing for urinary and skin infections
result.setting: Two primary care offices (Family Medicine and Internal Medicine), Mercy Health Saint Mary's, Michigan
result.standard: Institutional outpatient empiric antimicrobial guidelines (selection, dose, duration, indication)

cycle1.result: Total antibiotic appropriateness 27.5%.

result.intervention: Pharmacist-led audit and feedback of antibiotics prescribed for UTI and SSTI.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Geriatrics COVID-19 cohort ward, Whiston Hospital
result.standard: Documented oxygen therapy on observation charts (device, flow rate, target saturations)

cycle1.result: Baseline figures not reported.

result.intervention: Staff education session, bedside oxygen guideline posters, quiz and reminder lanyard cards over 4 PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 100% correct oxygen device and flow rate after the 2nd and 3rd PDSA cycles.

result.other_findings: All staff reported greater confidence in oxygen management after teaching.

result.setting: 83 ENT departments in all four UK nations (national prospective audit)
result.standard: March 2020 UK epistaxis guidelines (dissolvable products, discharge with non-dissolvable packs)

cycle1.result: Dissolvable product used in 34.7% (816/2,351); 54.6% discharged from ED; re-presentation within 10 days 19.5% for ED discharges and 9.9% for admissions.

result.other_findings: Predictors of re-presentation were no ED packing, antiplatelets, failed cautery and recent epistaxis treatment.

result.setting: Temporary surgical emergency department, Glan Clwyd Hospital
result.standard: 4-hour target for access to services, admission and discharge; 0% 4-hour breaches

cycle1.result: All category 2-4 patients accommodated; hospital services accessed in 771 (77.72%); 221 (22.27%) discharged without investigations within 4 hours.

result.other_findings: X-ray was the most used service (42.33%).

result.setting: District general hospital, Northampton General Hospital

cycle1.result: Mean compliance 4.91/7 (70%); no nasogastric tube 96%; opioid avoidance 8%; early IV fluid stop 61%; catheter removal 57%; oral intake by day 1 78%; mobilised by day 3 91%.

result.other_findings: Higher compliance was associated with shorter length of stay (p = 0.01).

result.setting: Wirral University Teaching Hospitals

cycle1.result: Non-COVID group: average time to surgery 47.4 days; 25 had surgery; 15 at index admission; length of stay 11.8 days.

cycle2.result: COVID group: average time to surgery 56.7 days; 9 had surgery; 3 at index admission; length of stay 8.8 days.

result.other_findings: Comparison of pre-COVID and COVID cohorts rather than a re-audit after change.

result.setting: Intensive therapy unit, Christian Medical College, Vellore

cycle1.result: Feedback forms showed positive feedback and improved understanding and confidence (no figures).

result.intervention: Five teaching sessions on respiratory illness, ventilation and ARDS.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: COVID-19 risk mitigation for elective surgery
result.setting: Royal Derby Hospital
result.standard: Green pathway standards: appropriately timed preoperative CT chest, COVID-19 swabs and shielding adherence

cycle1.result: All had a 2-week preoperative swab and shielded; 48/49 had a swab 2 days pre-op; CT chest in all.

result.other_findings: 4 (8%) had Clavien-Dindo grade 2 or above complications, none COVID related; 1 asymptomatic postoperative COVID positive.

result.topic: Antimicrobial stewardship prospective audit and feedback
result.setting: Large Canadian academic centre (University of Alberta Hospital), Edmonton

cycle1.result: Actionable feedback in 731 (39%); overall acceptance 82% (598/731); physician alone 88% (OR 1.85), pharmacist alone 82%, duo 79%, trainee 79%.

result.other_findings: 93% of audited antibiotics with feedback were carbapenems.

result.setting: Four healthcare sites: two hospitals, a long-term care facility and a community pharmacy (multi-site gap analysis)

cycle1.result: A standardised medication reconciliation process was not implemented at any of the observed sites; no designated team or training, discrepancies at discharge, no patient counselling on medicine changes, discharge report often not provided.

result.intervention: Development of a standardised medication reconciliation framework and auditing tool (not re-measured)
result.other_findings: Communication between community pharmacies and hospital physicians was unavailable or not easily accessible.

result.topic: Intravitreal anti-VEGF injection scheduling during COVID-19
result.setting: Tanta University Hospital, intravitreal injection service
result.standard: Hospital modified anti-VEGF injection protocol during the COVID-19 pandemic

cycle1.result: 83 patients screened, 40 included (deferred or deviated from protocol). Deferred subgroup (11 eyes): logMAR BCVA 1 ± 0.23 before vs 0.8 ± 0.22 on return (p = 0.27); CST 444.57 ± 200.1 vs 413.71 ± 237.7 µm (p = 0.12). 29 patients had a disturbed injection schedule.

result.other_findings: 18 patients skipped injection appointments because of fear of infection.

result.setting: Community-based nutrition programme in rural Guatemala (125 households at start)
result.standard: Delivery of evidence-based nutrition package components (growth monitoring, micronutrient supplements)

cycle1.result: Child stunting prevalence 42.4%; mean length/height-for-age Z-score -1.77.

result.intervention: Audit and feedback for frontline nutrition workers: electronic worklists, performance dashboards and one-to-one feedback sessions

cycle2.result: Stunting prevalence fell to 30.6% and mean Z-score rose to -1.47, both meeting criteria for special cause variation; marked improvements in growth monitoring and micronutrient supplement delivery.

result.other_findings: Results displayed on run charts and control charts.

result.setting: Department of Orthodontics, Dhulikhel Hospital, Kathmandu University (retrospective record review)

cycle1.result: Bracket failure rate 3.43%; 32% of patients had at least one bracket failure; no significant difference by gender (p =0.344), malocclusion type (p =0.191) or operator (p =0.188).

result.other_findings: Maxillary left quadrant was the commonest site of failure, followed by mandibular right.

result.setting: Gastroenterology department, Apollo Gleneagles Hospitals, Kolkata (tertiary care)

cycle1.result: 38 HCWs (32.48%) had evidence of COVID-19 (PCR 23.93%, IgG only 8.55%); endoscopy technicians 68.75% vs doctors 20.69% (P = 0.003); critical care staff 42.86%.

result.other_findings: None of the six HCWs with adequate hydroxychloroquine prophylaxis developed COVID-19; all recovered but many working days were lost.

result.setting: Walk for Life clubfoot project, community audit of families who dropped out of Ponseti care

cycle1.result: 309 families audited after six months' discontinued treatment; main reasons were family issues, brace difficulty, travel distance and poor understanding of bracing and follow-up. Overt relapse in 9% of children.

result.other_findings: Half of the children recommenced brace use after review; most families were of low affluence.

result.setting: Nursing home physicians receiving provincial MyPractice: Long-Term Care audit and feedback report (qualitative interviews)

cycle1.result: Qualitative interviews with 18 of 361 eligible physicians; professional role and identity influenced antibiotic initiation and response to the feedback report.

result.other_findings: Environmental context and resources was an overarching domain; findings used to inform future audit and feedback reports.

result.setting: Nationwide Children's Hospital, Columbus: primary care clinics, emergency departments, NICUs and inpatient units
result.standard: American Academy of Pediatrics-recommended safe sleep environment

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary safe sleep teams, standardised data tools and multiple PDSA cycles in each setting

cycle2.result: Significant increase in compliance with safe sleep practices in inpatient and NICU settings (P values not legible in abstract).

result.other_findings: Sleep-related deaths decreased in the primary care network; screening and education increased in clinics and EDs.

result.setting: 24-bed ICU, Apollo Hospitals, Chennai (tertiary care)

cycle1.result: 31.3% of patients mobilised; average mobility score 2; 16.7% of intubated patients achieved mobility score 3-5 (1,033 patient days).

result.intervention: Three-phase multidisciplinary QI project testing mobilisation interventions

cycle2.result: 57.9% of patients mobilised; average mobility score 3.4; 49.8% of intubated patients achieved mobility score 3-5 (932 patient days).

result.other_findings: Adverse events and barriers to mobilisation were also recorded.

result.topic: Antibiotic prescribing for childhood diarrhoea and pneumonia
result.setting: Paediatric outpatient clinics and hospitals in Bhopal (cross-sectional prescription audit over 4 months)

cycle1.result: 513 pneumonia prescriptions: signs recorded on 15.6%, 95.5% had antimicrobials; 417 diarrhoea prescriptions: 73% recorded no signs, around 64% had antibiotics; ORS and zinc prescribed in the majority.

result.other_findings: Prescriptions were often incomplete for clinical features, follow-up advice, dose and duration.

result.setting: Network of 9 hospitals in Mexico City using PAIN OUT audit and feedback
result.standard: PAIN OUT patient-reported outcome quality indicators; primary outcome proportion reporting worst pain ≥6/10

cycle1.result: Patients receiving information about pain treatment options 44% at baseline.

result.intervention: Locally adapted teaching and pain management resources (website, journal special issue), teaching for anaesthetists, surgeons, residents and nurses, and patient information

cycle2.result: Worst pain decreased significantly; information about pain treatment options increased to 77%.

result.other_findings: Pain interfering with movement, deep breathing/coughing and sleep also decreased.

result.setting: National Reproductive Age Mortality Survey, Georgia (deaths in 2012)

cycle1.result: 23 maternal deaths (15 early, 8 late); MMR 26.3 per 100 000 live births; improvements in care that would have changed outcome in 87% of early and 67% of late direct maternal deaths.

result.other_findings: Delayed recognition and inappropriate management of complications were common; leading causes were sepsis, haemorrhage, embolism and pregnancy-induced hypertension.

result.topic: Defunctioning ileostomy after rectal cancer surgery
result.setting: Binational Colorectal Cancer Audit database, Australia and New Zealand

cycle1.result: 2581 (89%) received a defunctioning stoma and 319 (11%) did not.

result.other_findings: A defunctioning stoma did not prevent anastomotic leak but was associated with fewer reoperations, more postoperative ileus and longer stay.

result.setting: Desktop review of the Uganda Atomic Energy Council equipment registry
result.standard: WHO recommended ratio of 20 pieces of imaging equipment per million population

cycle1.result: 625 pieces of equipment at 354 facilities: 397 plain X-ray, 120 dental X-ray, 3 radiotherapy machines; 0.1% non-functional; Uganda below the WHO ratio.

result.other_findings: Most equipment was in the central region and in private facilities.

result.topic: Patient-reported outcomes after abdominal cancer surgery
result.setting: 15 sites in the CHIR-Net SIGMA student-led network (prospective cohort)

cycle1.result: Poor appetite, fatigue, exhaustion and sleeping problems peaked 10-30 days after surgery; no PRO-CTCAE symptom differed from baseline at 3-6 months.
